title: 波麗安娜
author: Eleanor H. Porter 埃莉諾·H·波特
description: 《Pollyanna》(1913):小女孩波麗安娜用「高興遊戲」改變整個小鎮,語言淺白溫暖,適合初中程度學習英語。

chapters.title: Ch. I Miss Polly 第一章:波莉小姐

passages.original: CH Miss Polly Harrington entered her kitchen a little hurriedly this June morning.
passages.vernacular: 六月嘅呢天早晨,波莉小姐·哈林頓匆匆走進廚房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 六月的這天早晨,波莉小姐·哈林頓匆匆走進廚房。

passages.original: Miss Polly did not usually make hurried movements; she specially prided herself on her repose of manner.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐平時不匆忙行動;佢特別以自己舉止沉穩而自豪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐平時不匆忙行動;她特別以自己舉止沉穩而自豪。

passages.original: But to-day she was hurrying--actually hurrying.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日佢好匆忙——真嘅匆忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是今天她很匆忙——真的匆忙。

passages.original: Nancy, washing dishes at the sink, looked up in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 南希正在水槽邊洗碗,驚訝地抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希正在水槽邊洗碗,驚訝地抬起頭來。

passages.original: Nancy had been working in Miss Polly's kitchen only two months, but already she knew that her mistress did not usually hurry.
passages.vernacular: 南希喺波莉小姐嘅廚房裡才工作咗兩個月,但佢已經知道,佢嘅女主人平時不匆忙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希在波莉小姐的廚房裡才工作了兩個月,但她已經知道,她的女主人平時不匆忙。

passages.original: “Nancy!”
passages.vernacular: 「南希!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希!」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人。」

passages.original: Nancy answered cheerfully, but she still continued wiping the pitcher in her hand.
passages.vernacular: 南希愉快地回答,不過手裡仍然繼續擦住嗰隻水罐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希愉快地回答,可是手裡仍然繼續擦著那隻水罐。

passages.original: “Nancy,”--Miss Polly's voice was very stern now--“when I'm talking to you, I wish you to stop your work and listen to what I have to say.”
passages.vernacular: 「南希,」——波莉小姐嘅聲音而家好嚴厲——「我跟你講話嘅時候,我要你停下手裡嘅活,聽我要講嘅話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,」——波莉小姐的聲音現在非常嚴厲——「我跟你說話的時候,我要你停下手裡的活,聽我要說的話。」

passages.original: Nancy flushed miserably.
passages.vernacular: 南希難堪地臉紅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希難堪地臉紅了。

passages.original: She set the pitcher down at once, with the cloth still about it, thereby nearly tipping it over--which did not add to her composure.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻把水罐放下,布仲包喺上面,結果差點把佢碰倒——呢並冇畀佢增添鎮定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她馬上把水罐放下,布還包在上面,結果差點把它碰倒——這並沒有給她增添鎮定。

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am; I will, ma'am,” she stammered, righting the pitcher, and turning hastily.
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人;我聽,夫人,」佢結結巴巴地講,把水罐扶正,慌忙轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人;我聽,夫人,」她結結巴巴地說,把水罐扶正,慌忙轉過身。

passages.original: “I was only keepin' on with my work 'cause you specially told me this mornin' ter hurry with my dishes, ye know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我只係接住幹活,因為您今日早晨特意叫我趕緊洗碗,您知道嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是接著幹活,因為您今天早晨特意叫我趕緊洗碗,您知道的。」

passages.original: Her mistress frowned.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅女主人皺起眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的女主人皺起眉頭。

passages.original: “That will do, Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,南希。

passages.original: I did not ask for explanations.
passages.vernacular: 我冇要你解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有要你解釋。

passages.original: I asked for your attention.”
passages.vernacular: 我要嘅係你嘅注意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要的是你的注意。」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人。」

passages.original: Nancy stifled a sigh.
passages.vernacular: 南希壓住一聲嘆息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希壓住一聲嘆息。

passages.original: She was wondering if ever in any way she could please this woman.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺想,佢係咪有一天能以任何方式討好呢個女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在想,她是否有一天能以任何方式討好這個女人。

passages.original: Nancy had never “worked out” before; but a sick mother suddenly widowed and left with three younger children besides Nancy herself, had forced the girl into doing something toward their support, and she had been so pleased when she found a place in the kitchen of the great house on the hill--Nancy had come from “The Corners,” six miles away, and she knew Miss Polly Harrington only as the mistress of the old Harrington homestead, and one of the wealthiest residents of the town.
passages.vernacular: 南希以前從冇「出去做工」過;但係佢生病嘅母親突然守咗寡,除咗南希自己仲留下三個更小嘅細路,逼得呢女孩為佢哋嘅生計做點事,所以佢喺山上嗰座大宅嘅廚房裡找到一個位置時好高興——南希來自六英里外嘅「拐角村」,佢只知道波莉·哈林頓小姐係古老嘅哈林頓祖宅嘅女主人,係鎮上最富有嘅居民之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希以前從沒「出去做工」過;但是她生病的母親突然守了寡,除了南希自己還留下三個更小的孩子,逼得這女孩為他們的生計做點事,所以她在山上那座大宅的廚房裡找到一個位置時非常高興——南希來自六英里外的「拐角村」,她只知道波莉·哈林頓小姐是古老的哈林頓祖宅的女主人,是鎮上最富有的居民之一。

passages.original: That was two months before.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係兩個月前嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是兩個月前的事。

passages.original: She knew Miss Polly now as a stern, severe-faced woman who frowned if a knife clattered to the floor, or if a door banged--but who never thought to smile even when knives and doors were still.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家知道波莉小姐係個嚴厲、板住臉嘅女人,刀掉到地上哐啷一聲或門砰地一響佢就皺眉——可即使刀同門都靜靜嘅時候,佢都從唔想住笑一笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在知道波莉小姐是個嚴厲、板著臉的女人,刀掉到地上哐啷一聲或門砰地一響她就皺眉——可即使刀和門都靜靜的時候,她也從不想著笑一笑。

passages.original: “When you've finished your morning work, Nancy,” Miss Polly was saying now, “you may clear the little room at the head of the stairs in the attic, and make up the cot bed.
passages.vernacular: 「南希,你做完朝早嘅活之後,」波莉小姐呢陣講,「你可以收拾樓梯頂閣樓上嘅嗰間小屋,把嗰張行軍床鋪好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,你做完早上的活之後,」波莉小姐這時說,「你可以收拾樓梯頂閣樓上的那間小屋,把那張行軍床鋪好。

passages.original: Sweep the room and clean it, of course, after you clear out the trunks and boxes.”
passages.vernacular: 把箱子同盒子搬出去之後,當然要把房間掃乾淨、清理一遍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把箱子和盒子搬出去之後,當然要把房間掃乾淨、清理一遍。」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am.
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人。

passages.original: And where shall I put the things, please, that I take out?”
passages.vernacular: 請問我攞出嚟嘅嘢放喺邊度?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問我拿出來的東西放在哪裡?」

passages.original: “In the front attic.”
passages.vernacular: 「放喺前面嘅閣樓裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「放在前面的閣樓裡。」

passages.original: Miss Polly hesitated, then went on: “I suppose I may as well tell you now, Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐猶豫咗一下,然後接住講:「我想我而家不妨告訴你,南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐猶豫了一下,然後接著說:「我想我現在不妨告訴你,南希。

passages.original: My niece, Miss Pollyanna Whittier, is coming to live with me.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅外甥女,波麗安娜·惠蒂爾小姐,要嚟同我同住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的外甥女,波麗安娜·惠蒂爾小姐,要來和我同住。

passages.original: She is eleven years old, and will sleep in that room.”
passages.vernacular: 佢十一歲,就瞓喺嗰個房間。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她十一歲,就睡在那個房間。」

passages.original: “A little girl--coming here, Miss Harrington?
passages.vernacular: 「一個小女孩——要嚟呢度,哈林頓小姐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個小女孩——要來這裡,哈林頓小姐?

passages.original: Oh, won't that be nice!” cried Nancy, thinking of the sunshine her own little sisters made in the home at “The Corners.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,嗰多好啊!」南希喊道,想到佢自己嘅小妹妹哋畀「拐角村」嘅家帶嚟嘅陽光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,那多好啊!」南希喊道,想到她自己的小妹妹們給「拐角村」的家帶來的陽光。

passages.original: “Nice?
Well, that isn't exactly the word I should use,” rejoined Miss Polly, stiffly.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,嗰可不完全係我會用嘅字眼,」波莉小姐僵硬地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,那可不完全是我會用的字眼,」波莉小姐僵硬地回答。

passages.original: “However, I intend to make the best of it, of course.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,當然,我打算盡力而為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,當然,我打算盡力而為。

passages.original: I am a good woman, I hope; and I know my duty.”
passages.vernacular: 我但願我係個好女人,我都知道我嘅責任。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我但願我是個好女人,我也知道我的責任。」

passages.original: Nancy colored hotly.
passages.vernacular: 南希漲紅咗臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希漲紅了臉。

passages.original: “Of course, ma'am; it was only that I thought a little girl here might--might brighten things up for you,” she faltered.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,夫人;我只係覺得,一個小女孩喺呢度或者能——能畀您添點生氣,」佢怯怯地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,夫人;我只是覺得,一個小女孩在這裡也許能——能給您添點生氣,」她怯怯地說。

passages.original: “Thank you,” rejoined the lady, dryly.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,」嗰位女士冷冷地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,」那位女士冷冷地回答。

passages.original: “I can't say, however, that I see any immediate need for that.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我唔能夠講我睇出眼下有呢個需要。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我不能說我看出眼下有這個需要。」

passages.original: “But, of course, you--you'd want her, your sister's child,” ventured Nancy, vaguely feeling that somehow she must prepare a welcome for this lonely little stranger.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,當然,您——您會想要佢,您姐姐嘅細路,」南希大住膽子講,隱約覺得唔知怎嘅佢必須為呢個孤單嘅小陌生人準備一個歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,當然,您——您會想要她,您姐姐的孩子,」南希大著膽子說,隱約覺得不知怎的她必須為這個孤單的小陌生人準備一個歡迎。

passages.original: Miss Polly lifted her chin haughtily.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐傲慢地抬起下巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐傲慢地抬起下巴。

passages.original: “Well, really, Nancy, just because I happened to have a sister who was silly enough to marry and bring unnecessary children into a world that was already quite full enough, I can't see how I should particularly WANT to have the care of them myself.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,講真嘅,南希,僅僅因為我碰巧有一個傻到去結婚、畀已經夠擁擠嘅世界帶嚟唔使要細路嘅姐姐,我睇不出我有乜嘢特別嘅理由要照顧佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,說真的,南希,僅僅因為我碰巧有一個傻到去結婚、給已經夠擁擠的世界帶來不必要孩子的姐姐,我看不出我有什麼特別的理由要照顧他們。

passages.original: However, as I said before, I hope I know my duty.
passages.vernacular: 不過,我之前講喇,我希望我知道我嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我之前說了,我希望我知道我的責任。

passages.original: See that you clean the corners, Nancy,” she finished sharply, as she left the room.
passages.vernacular: 你要把角落打掃乾淨,南希,」佢尖聲結束,離開咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要把角落打掃乾淨,南希,」她尖聲結束,離開了房間。

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am,” sighed Nancy, picking up the half-dried pitcher--now so cold it must be rinsed again.
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人,」南希嘆息住,攞起半乾嘅水罐——而家涼得必須再沖一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人,」南希嘆息著,拿起半乾的水罐——現在涼得必須再沖一遍。

passages.original: In her own room, Miss Polly took out once more the letter which she had received two days before from the far-away Western town, and which had been so unpleasant a surprise to her.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢自己嘅房間裡,波莉小姐又一次攞出兩天前收到嘅嗰封信,嗰個係從遙遠嘅西部小鎮寄嚟嘅,畀佢帶嚟咗咁不愉快嘅驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她自己的房間裡,波莉小姐又一次拿出兩天前收到的那封信,那是從遙遠的西部小鎮寄來的,給她帶來了那麼不愉快的驚訝。

passages.original: The letter was addressed to Miss Polly Harrington, Beldingsville, Vermont; and it read as follows:
passages.vernacular: 信係寄畀佛蒙特州貝爾丁斯維爾嘅波莉·哈林頓小姐嘅,內容如下:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 信是寄給佛蒙特州貝爾丁斯維爾的波莉·哈林頓小姐的,內容如下:

passages.original: “Dear Madam:--I regret to inform you that the Rev. John Whittier died two weeks ago, leaving one child, a girl eleven years old.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅夫人:——我好遺憾地通知您,約翰·惠蒂爾牧師兩週前去世喇,留下一個細路,一個十一歲嘅女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的夫人:——我很遺憾地通知您,約翰·惠蒂爾牧師兩週前去世了,留下一個孩子,一個十一歲的女孩。

passages.original: He left practically nothing else save a few books; for, as you doubtless know, he was the pastor of this small mission church, and had a very meagre salary.
passages.vernacular: 佢除咗幾本書,幾乎冇留下別嘅嘢;因為,您無疑知道,佢係呢個小布道教堂嘅牧師,薪水好微薄。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他除了幾本書,幾乎沒有留下別的東西;因為,您無疑知道,他是這個小布道教堂的牧師,薪水非常微薄。

passages.original: “I believe he was your deceased sister's husband, but he gave me to understand the families were not on the best of terms.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信佢係您已故姐姐嘅丈夫,但佢讓我明白,兩家嘅關係並唔係最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信他是您已故姐姐的丈夫,但他讓我明白,兩家的關係並不是最好。

passages.original: He thought, however, that for your sister's sake you might wish to take the child and bring her up among her own people in the East.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢認為,為了您姐姐嘅緣故,您或者願意收養呢細路,把佢喺東部佢自己嘅親人中間養大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他認為,為了您姐姐的緣故,您也許願意收養這孩子,把她在東部她自己的親人中間養大。

passages.original: Hence I am writing to you.
passages.vernacular: 因此我寫信畀您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此我寫信給您。

passages.original: “The little girl will be all ready to start by the time you get this letter; and if you can take her, we would appreciate it very much if you would write that she might come at once, as there is a man and his wife here who are going East very soon, and they would take her with them to Boston, and put her on the Beldingsville train.
passages.vernacular: 「小女孩喺您收到呢封信嘅時候就會完全準備好出發;如果您能收留佢,我哋會好感激,如果您回信講佢可以即刻嚟,因為呢度有一對夫婦好快要去東部,佢哋可以帶佢到波士頓,送佢上貝爾丁斯維爾嘅火車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小女孩在您收到這封信的時候就會完全準備好出發;如果您能收留她,我們會非常感激,如果您回信說她可以馬上來,因為這裡有一對夫婦很快要去東部,他們可以帶她到波士頓,送她上貝爾丁斯維爾的火車。

passages.original: Of course you would be notified what day and train to expect Pollyanna on.
passages.vernacular: 當然,您會被通知波麗安娜邊天、坐邊班火車到達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,您會被通知波麗安娜哪天、坐哪班火車到達。

passages.original: “Hoping to hear favorably from you soon, I remain,
passages.vernacular: 「希望好快得到您嘅好消息,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「希望很快得到您的好消息,

passages.original: “Respectfully yours,
passages.vernacular: 「您恭敬嘅,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您恭敬的,

passages.original: “Jeremiah O. White.”
passages.vernacular: 「傑里邁亞·O·懷特。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「傑里邁亞·O·懷特。」

passages.original: With a frown Miss Polly folded the letter and tucked it into its envelope.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺住眉把信折好,塞進信封。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺著眉把信折好,塞進信封。

passages.original: She had answered it the day before, and she had said she would take the child, of course.
passages.vernacular: 佢尋日已經回咗信,講當然會收留呢細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她昨天已經回了信,說當然會收留這孩子。

passages.original: She HOPED she knew her duty well enough for that!--disagreeable as the task would be.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望佢足夠了解佢嘅責任,能做到呢啲!——儘管呢任務令人不快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她希望她足夠了解她的責任,能做到這一點!——儘管這任務令人不快。

passages.original: As she sat now, with the letter in her hands, her thoughts went back to her sister, Jennie, who had been this child's mother, and to the time when Jennie, as a girl of twenty, had insisted upon marrying the young minister, in spite of her family's remonstrances.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家坐住,手裡攞住嗰封信,思緒回到佢嘅姐姐珍妮,都就係呢細路嘅母親,回到珍妮二十歲時,不顧家人嘅反對,堅持要嫁畀嗰位年輕牧師嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在坐著,手裡拿著那封信,思緒回到她的姐姐珍妮,也就是這孩子的母親,回到珍妮二十歲時,不顧家人的反對,堅持要嫁給那位年輕牧師的時候。

passages.original: There had been a man of wealth who had wanted her--and the family had much preferred him to the minister; but Jennie had not.
passages.vernacular: 曾有一個有錢嘅人想娶佢——家裡比起牧師,更鍾意嗰個人;但珍妮不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曾有一個有錢的人想娶她——家裡比起牧師,更喜歡那個人;但珍妮不喜歡。

passages.original: The man of wealth had more years, as well as more money, to his credit, while the minister had only a young head full of youth's ideals and enthusiasm, and a heart full of love.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個有錢人,年齡同金錢都更多,而牧師只有一顆滿懷青春理想同熱情嘅年輕腦袋,同一顆充滿愛嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個有錢人,年齡和金錢都更多,而牧師只有一顆滿懷青春理想與熱情的年輕腦袋,和一顆充滿愛的心。

passages.original: Jennie had preferred these--quite naturally, perhaps; so she had married the minister, and had gone south with him as a home missionary's wife.
passages.vernacular: 珍妮鍾意後者——或者係好自然嘅;所以佢嫁咗牧師,隨佢到南方,當咗一名本土傳教士嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 珍妮喜歡後者——也許是很自然的;所以她嫁了牧師,隨他到南方,當了一名本土傳教士的妻子。

passages.original: The break had come then.
passages.vernacular: 決裂就係嗰時發生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 決裂就是那時發生的。

passages.original: Miss Polly remembered it well, though she had been but a girl of fifteen, the youngest, at the time.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐記得清清楚楚,雖然當時佢只係個十五歲嘅女孩,最小嘅一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐記得清清楚楚,雖然當時她只是個十五歲的女孩,最小的一個。

passages.original: The family had had little more to do with the missionary's wife.
passages.vernacular: 家裡同嗰位傳教士嘅妻子幾乎再無來往。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 家裡與那位傳教士的妻子幾乎再無來往。

passages.original: To be sure, Jennie herself had written, for a time, and had named her last baby “Pollyanna” for her two sisters, Polly and Anna--the other babies had all died.
passages.vernacular: 的確,珍妮自己寫過一陣信,並且把佢嘅最後一個細路取名為「波麗安娜」,取自佢嘅兩個妹妹波莉同安娜——其他嘅細路都夭折喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 的確,珍妮自己寫過一陣信,並且把她的最後一個孩子取名為「波麗安娜」,取自她的兩個妹妹波莉和安娜——其他的孩子都夭折了。

passages.original: This had been the last time that Jennie had written; and in a few years there had come the news of her death, told in a short, but heart-broken little note from the minister himself, dated at a little town in the West.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係珍妮最後一次寫信;幾年後傳嚟咗佢去世嘅消息,係嗰位牧師自己寫嘅一封簡短而令人心碎嘅小信,日期寫嘅係西部一個小鎮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是珍妮最後一次寫信;幾年後傳來了她去世的消息,是那位牧師自己寫的一封簡短而令人心碎的小信,日期寫的是西部一個小鎮。

passages.original: Meanwhile, time had not stood still for the occupants of the great house on the hill.
passages.vernacular: 同時,時間並冇為山上大宅嘅住戶哋停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,時間並沒有為山上大宅的住戶們停下。

passages.original: Miss Polly, looking out at the far-reaching valley below, thought of the changes those twenty-five years had brought to her.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐望住外面遠處嘅山谷,想住嗰二十五年畀佢帶嚟嘅變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐望著外面遠處的山谷,想著那二十五年給她帶來的變化。

passages.original: She was forty now, and quite alone in the world.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家四十歲喇,在世上孤身一人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在四十歲了,在世上孤身一人。

passages.original: Father, mother, sisters--all were dead.
passages.vernacular: 父親、母親、姐妹——全都死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 父親、母親、姐妹——全都死了。

passages.original: For years, now, she had been sole mistress of the house and of the thousands left her by her father.
passages.vernacular: 多年嚟,佢一直係呢座房子同佢父親留畀佢嘅數千英鎊嘅唯一主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多年來,她一直是這座房子和她父親留給她的數千英鎊的唯一主人。

passages.original: There were people who had openly pitied her lonely life, and who had urged her to have some friend or companion to live with her; but she had not welcomed either their sympathy or their advice.
passages.vernacular: 有人公開同情佢孤獨嘅生活,都勸佢找個朋友或同伴嚟同住;但佢既不歡迎佢哋嘅同情,都不歡迎佢哋嘅建議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人公開同情她孤獨的生活,也勸她找個朋友或同伴來同住;但她既不歡迎他們的同情,也不歡迎他們的建議。

passages.original: She was not lonely, she said.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢不孤獨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她不孤獨。

passages.original: She liked being by herself.
passages.vernacular: 佢鍾意一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喜歡一個人。

passages.original: She preferred quiet.
passages.vernacular: 佢鍾意安靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喜歡安靜。

passages.original: But now--
passages.vernacular: 不過而家——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是現在——

passages.original: Miss Polly rose with frowning face and closely-shut lips.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺住眉、緊閉住嘴唇站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺著眉、緊閉著嘴唇站起來。

passages.original: She was glad, of course, that she was a good woman, and that she not only knew her duty, but had sufficient strength of character to perform it.
passages.vernacular: 佢當然好高興佢係個好女人,不僅知道自己嘅責任,而且有足夠嘅品格力量去履行佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她當然很高興她是個好女人,不僅知道自己的責任,而且有足夠的品格力量去履行它。

passages.original: But--POLLYANNA!--what a ridiculous name!
passages.vernacular: 不過——波麗安娜!——多荒唐嘅名字!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是——波麗安娜!——多荒唐的名字!

chapters.title: Ch. II Old Tom and Nancy 第二章:老湯姆與南希

passages.original: CH In the little attic room Nancy swept and scrubbed vigorously, paying particular attention to the corners.
passages.vernacular: 喺小閣樓房間裡,南希又掃又擦,格外用心地打掃角落。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在小閣樓房間裡,南希又掃又擦,格外用心地打掃角落。

passages.original: There were times, indeed, when the vigor she put into her work was more of a relief to her feelings than it was an ardor to efface dirt--Nancy, in spite of her frightened submission to her mistress, was no saint.
passages.vernacular: 的確,有時佢下嘅勁,同其講係為了擦掉灰塵嘅熱情,不如講更係發洩情緒嘅解脫——南希雖然喺女主人面前戰戰兢兢地順從,卻絕非聖人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 的確,有時她下的勁,與其說是為了擦掉灰塵的熱情,不如說更是發洩情緒的解脫——南希雖然在女主人面前戰戰兢兢地順從,卻絕非聖人。

passages.original: “I--just--wish--I could--dig--out the corners--of--her--soul!” she muttered jerkily, punctuating her words with murderous jabs of her pointed cleaning-stick.
passages.vernacular: 「我——只係——希望——我能——挖出——佢——靈魂裡嘅——角落!」佢一邊斷斷續續地嘟囔,一邊用尖頭嘅清潔棒狠狠地戳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——只是——希望——我能——挖出——她——靈魂裡的——角落!」她一邊斷斷續續地嘟囔,一邊用尖頭的清潔棒狠狠地戳。

passages.original: “There's plenty of 'em needs cleanin' all right, all right!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰兒有嘅係角落需要清理,的確,的確!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那兒有的是角落需要清理,的確,的確!

passages.original: The idea of stickin' that blessed child 'way off up here in this hot little room--with no fire in the winter, too, and all this big house ter pick and choose from!
passages.vernacular: 竟然把嗰可愛嘅細路塞到呢遠離一切嘅地方——呢個熱烘烘嘅小房間——冬天仲冇火,而咁大嘅房子任佢挑選!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 竟然把那可愛的孩子塞到這遠離一切的地方——這個熱烘烘的小房間——冬天還沒有火,而這麼大的房子任她挑選!

passages.original: Unnecessary children, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 唔使要嘅細路,真係嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不必要的孩子,真是的!

passages.original: Humph!” snapped Nancy, wringing her rag so hard her fingers ached from the strain; “I guess it ain't CHILDREN what is MOST unnecessary just now, just now!”
passages.vernacular: 哼!」南希厲聲講,把抹布擰得咁用力,手指都疼喇;「我想而家最唔使要嘅唔係細路哋,唔係,唔係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哼!」南希厲聲說,把抹布擰得那麼用力,手指都疼了;「我想現在最不必要的不是孩子們,不是,不是!」

passages.original: For some time she worked in silence; then, her task finished, she looked about the bare little room in plain disgust.
passages.vernacular: 佢默默地幹咗一會兒活;然後,活幹完喇,佢厭惡地環顧呢間光禿禿嘅小屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她默默地幹了一會兒活;然後,活幹完了,她厭惡地環顧這間光禿禿的小屋。

passages.original: “Well, it's done--my part, anyhow,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「好,做完喇——我呢份,反正,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,做完了——我這份,反正,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “There ain't no dirt here--and there's mighty little else.
passages.vernacular: 「呢度啲灰都冇——都冇別嘅乜嘢嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡一點灰都沒有——也沒有別的什麼東西。

passages.original: Poor little soul!--a pretty place this is ter put a homesick, lonesome child into!” she finished, going out and closing the door with a bang, “Oh!” she ejaculated, biting her lip.
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅小嘢!——呢真係個好地方,放一個想家、孤單嘅細路!」佢結束時走出去,砰地關上咗門,「哎呀!」佢叫咗一聲,咬住嘴唇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的小東西!——這真是個好地方,放一個想家、孤單的孩子!」她結束時走出去,砰地關上了門,「哎呀!」她叫了一聲,咬著嘴唇。

passages.original: Then, doggedly: “Well, I don't care.
passages.vernacular: 然後固執地講:「哼,我不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後固執地說:「哼,我不在乎。

passages.original: I hope she did hear the bang,--I do, I do!”
passages.vernacular: 我希望佢聽見咗嗰聲關門,——我希望,我希望!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望她聽見了那聲關門,——我希望,我希望!」

passages.original: In the garden that afternoon, Nancy found a few minutes in which to interview Old Tom, who had pulled the weeds and shovelled the paths about the place for uncounted years.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天下午,喺花園裡,南希找到幾分鐘去問老湯姆,佢喺呢個地方拔草、鏟小路,已經唔知多少年喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天下午,在花園裡,南希找到幾分鐘去問老湯姆,他在這個地方拔草、鏟小路,已經不知多少年了。

passages.original: “Mr. Tom,” began Nancy, throwing a quick glance over her shoulder to make sure she was unobserved; “did you know a little girl was comin' here ter live with Miss Polly?”
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆先生,」南希開口,飛快地回頭瞥咗一眼,確認冇人睇見;「你知道有個小女孩要嚟呢度跟波莉小姐住嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆先生,」南希開口,飛快地回頭瞥了一眼,確認沒人看見;「你知道有個小女孩要來這裡跟波莉小姐住嗎?」

passages.original: “A--what?” demanded the old man, straightening his bent back with difficulty.
passages.vernacular: 「一個——乜嘢?」老人問,費力地直起彎住嘅背。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個——什麼?」老人問,費力地直起彎著的背。

passages.original: “A little girl--to live with Miss Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「一個小女孩——嚟跟波莉小姐住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一個小女孩——來跟波莉小姐住。」

passages.original: “Go on with yer jokin',” scoffed unbelieving Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「別開玩笑喇,」不信嘅湯姆嘲笑道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別開玩笑了,」不信的湯姆嘲笑道。

passages.original: “Why don't ye tell me the sun is a-goin' ter set in the east ter-morrer?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點不乾脆告訴我太陽聽日要從東邊落下?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你怎麼不乾脆告訴我太陽明天要從東邊落下?」

passages.original: “But it's true.
passages.vernacular: 「不過呢個係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是這是真的。

passages.original: She told me so herself,” maintained Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 佢親自告訴我嘅,」南希堅持講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她親自告訴我的,」南希堅持說。

passages.original: “It's her niece; and she's eleven years old.”
passages.vernacular: 「係佢嘅外甥女;十一歲喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是她的外甥女;十一歲了。」

passages.original: The man's jaw fell.
passages.vernacular: 老人嘅下巴掉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人的下巴掉了下來。

passages.original: “Sho!--I wonder, now,” he muttered; then a tender light came into his faded eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「嘿!——我真奇怪,」佢喃喃道;然後一種溫柔嘅光芒進入佢褪色嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嘿!——我真奇怪,」他喃喃道;然後一種溫柔的光芒進入他褪色的眼睛。

passages.original: “It ain't--but it must be--Miss Jennie's little gal!
passages.vernacular: 「唔係——不過肯定係——珍妮小姐嘅小女兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是——可是肯定是——珍妮小姐的小女兒!

passages.original: There wasn't none of the rest of 'em married.
passages.vernacular: 其餘嘅人都冇結婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其餘的人都沒結婚。

passages.original: Why, Nancy, it must be Miss Jennie's little gal.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,南希,肯定係珍妮小姐嘅小女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,南希,肯定是珍妮小姐的小女兒。

passages.original: Glory be ter praise! ter think of my old eyes a-seein' this!”
passages.vernacular: 謝天謝地!想唔到我呢雙老眼仲能睇到呢個!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝天謝地!想不到我這雙老眼還能看到這個!」

passages.original: “Who was Miss Jennie?”
passages.vernacular: 「珍妮小姐係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「珍妮小姐是誰?」

passages.original: “She was an angel straight out of Heaven,” breathed the man, fervently; “but the old master and missus knew her as their oldest daughter.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係從天堂直接下嚟嘅天使,」嗰人熱切地低聲講;「但老爺同太太知道佢係佢哋嘅大女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是從天堂直接下來的天使,」那人熱切地低聲說;「但老爺和太太知道她是他們的大女兒。

passages.original: She was twenty when she married and went away from here long years ago.
passages.vernacular: 佢二十歲時結婚離開呢度,係好多年前嘅事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她二十歲時結婚離開這裡,是很多年前的事了。

passages.original: Her babies all died, I heard, except the last one; and that must be the one what's a-comin'.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽講佢嘅細路都死喇,除咗最後一個;嗰一定就係而家要嚟嘅呢個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽說她的孩子都死了,除了最後一個;那一定就是現在要來的這個。」

passages.original: “She's eleven years old.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢十一歲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她十一歲。」

passages.original: “Yes, she might be,” nodded the old man.
passages.vernacular: 「係,可能,」老人點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,可能,」老人點頭。

passages.original: “And she's goin' ter sleep in the attic--more shame ter HER!” scolded Nancy, with another glance over her shoulder toward the house behind her.
passages.vernacular: 「而佢要瞓喺閣樓裡——真係佢嘅恥辱!」南希斥責道,又回頭瞥咗一眼身後嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而她要睡在閣樓裡——真是她的恥辱!」南希斥責道,又回頭瞥了一眼身後的房子。

passages.original: Old Tom frowned.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆皺咗皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆皺了皺眉。

passages.original: The next moment a curious smile curved his lips.
passages.vernacular: 接住,一絲古怪嘅笑浮上佢嘅嘴角。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著,一絲古怪的笑浮上他的嘴角。

passages.original: “I'm a-wonderin' what Miss Polly will do with a child in the house,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我喺納悶,波莉小姐要攞一個細路喺家裡點算,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我在納悶,波莉小姐要拿一個孩子在家裡怎麼辦,」他說。

passages.original: “Humph!
Well, I'm a-wonderin' what a child will do with Miss Polly in the house!” snapped Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 我喺納悶,一個細路要攞波莉小姐喺家裡點算!」南希厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在納悶,一個孩子要拿波莉小姐在家裡怎麼辦!」南希厲聲說。

passages.original: The old man laughed.
passages.vernacular: 老人笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人笑了。

passages.original: “I'm afraid you ain't fond of Miss Polly,” he grinned.
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕你不鍾意波莉小姐,」佢咧嘴笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕你不喜歡波莉小姐,」他咧嘴笑。

passages.original: “As if ever anybody could be fond of her!” scorned Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「好像有邊個能鍾意佢似嘅!」南希輕蔑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像有誰能喜歡她似的!」南希輕蔑地說。

passages.original: Old Tom smiled oddly.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆古怪地笑咗笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆古怪地笑了笑。

passages.original: He stooped and began to work again.
passages.vernacular: 佢彎下腰,又開始幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他彎下腰,又開始幹活。

passages.original: “I guess maybe you didn't know about Miss Polly's love affair,” he said slowly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你可能唔知道波莉小姐嘅戀愛,」佢慢慢地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你可能不知道波莉小姐的戀愛,」他慢慢地說。

passages.original: “Love affair--HER!
passages.vernacular: 「戀愛——佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「戀愛——她!

passages.original: No!--and I guess nobody else didn't, neither.”
passages.vernacular: 不!——我想別人都冇人知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不!——我想別人也沒人知道。」

passages.original: “Oh, yes they did,” nodded the old man.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢哋知道嘅,」老人點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他們知道的,」老人點頭。

passages.original: “And the feller's livin' ter-day--right in this town, too.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且嗰個人今日仲活住——就喺呢個鎮上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且那個人今天還活著——就在這個鎮上。」

passages.original: “Who is he?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是誰?」

passages.original: “I ain't a-tellin' that.
passages.vernacular: 「我不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不說。

passages.original: It ain't fit that I should.”
passages.vernacular: 我不該講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不該說。」

passages.original: The old man drew himself erect.
passages.vernacular: 老人挺直咗身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人挺直了身子。

passages.original: In his dim blue eyes, as he faced the house, there was the loyal servant's honest pride in the family he has served and loved for long years.
passages.vernacular: 佢面對房子時,暗淡嘅藍眼睛裡有忠實僕人為自己長久服侍、愛戴嘅家族而生嘅真誠驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他面對房子時,暗淡的藍眼睛裡有忠實僕人為自己長久服侍、愛戴的家族而生的真誠驕傲。

passages.original: “But it don't seem possible--her and a lover,” still maintained Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「不過似乎唔可能——佢同一個情人,」南希仍然堅持講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是似乎不可能——她和一個情人,」南希仍然堅持說。

passages.original: Old Tom shook his head.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆搖搖頭。

passages.original: “You didn't know Miss Polly as I did,” he argued.
passages.vernacular: 「你不像我嗰樣了解波莉小姐,」佢辯解講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不像我那樣了解波莉小姐,」他辯解講。

passages.original: “She used ter be real handsome--and she would be now, if she'd let herself be.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢過去真係漂亮——要係佢肯讓自己漂亮,而家都會嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她過去真是漂亮——要是她肯讓自己漂亮,現在也會的。」

passages.original: “Handsome!
passages.vernacular: 「漂亮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「漂亮!

passages.original: Miss Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐!」

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: If she'd just let that tight hair of hern all out loose and careless-like, as it used ter be, and wear the sort of bunnits with posies in 'em, and the kind o' dresses all lace and white things--you'd see she'd be handsome!
passages.vernacular: 要係佢讓佢嗰緊緊嘅頭髮全鬆下嚟,隨意些,像以前嗰樣,戴有花嘅帽子,穿滿係花邊同白色嘅衣服——你就會睇出佢會係漂亮嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是她讓她那緊緊的頭髮全鬆下來,隨意些,像以前那樣,戴有花的帽子,穿滿是花邊和白色的衣服——你就會看出她會是漂亮的!

passages.original: Miss Polly ain't old, Nancy.”
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐不老,南希。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐不老,南希。」

passages.original: “Ain't she, though?
passages.vernacular: 「佢不老?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她不老?

passages.original: Well, then she's got an awfully good imitation of it--she has, she has!” sniffed Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,嗰佢就係有個好好嘅仿冒品——係嘅,係嘅!」南希哼咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,那她就是有個非常好的仿冒品——是的,是的!」南希哼了一聲。

passages.original: “Yes, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「係,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,我知道。

passages.original: It begun then--at the time of the trouble with her lover,” nodded Old Tom; “and it seems as if she'd been feedin' on wormwood an' thistles ever since--she's that bitter an' prickly ter deal with.”
passages.vernacular: 係從嗰時開始嘅——同佢情人鬧矛盾嘅時候,」老湯姆點頭;「好像佢從嗰以後一直喺食苦艾同薊草——佢就係咁苦、咁扎人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是從那時開始的——和她情人鬧矛盾的時候,」老湯姆點頭;「好像她從那以後一直在吃苦艾和薊草——她就是那麼苦、那麼扎人。」

passages.original: “I should say she was,” declared Nancy, indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 「我該講係嘅,」南希憤慨地宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我該說是的,」南希憤慨地宣稱。

passages.original: “There's no pleasin' her, nohow, no matter how you try!
passages.vernacular: 「點都討好不咗佢,不管你點試!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼也討好不了她,不管你怎麼試!

passages.original: I wouldn't stay if 'twa'n't for the wages and the folks at home what's needin' 'em.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係為了工資同家裡需要呢工資嘅人,我才不待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是為了工資和家裡需要這工資的人,我才不待。

passages.original: But some day--some day I shall jest b'ile over; and when I do, of course it'll be good-by Nancy for me.
passages.vernacular: 但係總有一天——總有一天我會一下子爆發;到嗰時,當然就係我南希再見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是總有一天——總有一天我會一下子爆發;到那時,當然就是我南希再見了。

passages.original: It will, it will.”
passages.vernacular: 會嘅,會嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會的,會的。」

passages.original: Old Tom shook his head.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆搖搖頭。

passages.original: “I know.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。

passages.original: I've felt it.
passages.vernacular: 我都有過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也有過。

passages.original: It's nart'ral--but 'tain't best, child; 'tain't best.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係自然嘅——不過唔係最好,細路;唔係最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是自然的——可是不是最好,孩子;不是最好。

passages.original: Take my word for it, 'tain't best.”
passages.vernacular: 相信我嘅話,唔係最好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我的話,不是最好。」

passages.original: And again he bent his old head to the work before him.
passages.vernacular: 佢又低下佢嘅老頭,繼續面前嘅活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又低下他的老頭,繼續面前的活。

passages.original: “Nancy!” called a sharp voice.
passages.vernacular: 「南希!」一個尖厲嘅聲音喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希!」一個尖厲的聲音喊道。

passages.original: “Y-yes, ma'am,” stammered Nancy; and hurried toward the house.
passages.vernacular: 「係——係,夫人,」南希結結巴巴地講,匆忙朝房子走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是——是,夫人,」南希結結巴巴地說,匆忙朝房子走去。

chapters.title: Ch. III The Coming of Pollyanna 第三章:波麗安娜來了

passages.original: CH In due time came the telegram announcing that Pollyanna would arrive in Beldingsville the next day, the twenty-fifth of June, at four o'clock.
passages.vernacular: 電報喺適當嘅時候嚟喇,通知波麗安娜將於聽日,六月二十五日,下午四點鐘到達貝爾丁斯維爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 電報在適當的時候來了,通知波麗安娜將於明天,六月二十五日,下午四點鐘到達貝爾丁斯維爾。

passages.original: Miss Polly read the telegram, frowned, then climbed the stairs to the attic room.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐讀咗電報,皺咗皺眉,然後上樓走到閣樓房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐讀了電報,皺了皺眉,然後上樓走到閣樓房間。

passages.original: She still frowned as she looked about her.
passages.vernacular: 佢環顧四周時仍然皺住眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她環顧四周時仍然皺著眉。

passages.original: The room contained a small bed, neatly made, two straight-backed chairs, a washstand, a bureau--without any mirror--and a small table.
passages.vernacular: 房間裡有一張整潔鋪好嘅小床,兩把直背椅子,一個洗臉架,一個冇鏡子嘅五斗櫃,同一張小桌子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房間裡有一張整潔鋪好的小床,兩把直背椅子,一個洗臉架,一個沒有鏡子的五斗櫃,和一張小桌子。

passages.original: There were no drapery curtains at the dormer windows, no pictures on the wall.
passages.vernacular: 老虎窗上冇帷幔窗簾,牆上冇畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老虎窗上沒有帷幔窗簾,牆上沒有畫。

passages.original: All day the sun had been pouring down upon the roof, and the little room was like an oven for heat.
passages.vernacular: 整整一天,太陽直曬喺屋頂上,小房間熱得像個烤爐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整整一天,太陽直曬在屋頂上,小房間熱得像個烤爐。

passages.original: As there were no screens, the windows had not been raised.
passages.vernacular: 因為冇紗窗,窗子冇打開過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為沒有紗窗,窗子沒有打開過。

passages.original: A big fly was buzzing angrily at one of them now, up and down, up and down, trying to get out.
passages.vernacular: 一隻大蒼蠅正在其中一扇窗上憤怒地嗡嗡叫,上上下下,上上下下,想出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻大蒼蠅正在其中一扇窗上憤怒地嗡嗡叫,上上下下,上上下下,想出去。

passages.original: Miss Polly killed the fly, swept it through the window (raising the sash an inch for the purpose), straightened a chair, frowned again, and left the room.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐打死咗蒼蠅,把佢掃出窗子(為此把窗框抬高咗一英寸),扶正一把椅子,又皺咗皺眉,離開咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐打死了蒼蠅,把它掃出窗子(為此把窗框抬高了一英寸),扶正一把椅子,又皺了皺眉,離開了房間。

passages.original: “Nancy,” she said a few minutes later, at the kitchen door, “I found a fly up-stairs in Miss Pollyanna's room.
passages.vernacular: 「南希,」佢幾分鐘後喺廚房門口講,「我喺樓上波麗安娜小姐嘅房間裡發現一隻蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,」她幾分鐘後在廚房門口說,「我在樓上波麗安娜小姐的房間裡發現一隻蒼蠅。

passages.original: The window must have been raised at some time.
passages.vernacular: 窗子一定喺某個時候被打開過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗子一定在某個時候被打開過。

passages.original: I have ordered screens, but until they come I shall expect you to see that the windows remain closed.
passages.vernacular: 我已經訂咗紗窗,但喺佢哋到之前,我要你負責讓窗子一直關住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經訂了紗窗,但在它們到之前,我要你負責讓窗子一直關著。

passages.original: My niece will arrive to-morrow at four o'clock.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅外甥女聽日下午四點鐘到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的外甥女明天下午四點鐘到。

passages.original: I desire you to meet her at the station.
passages.vernacular: 我要你去車站接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要你去車站接她。

passages.original: Timothy will take the open buggy and drive you over.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西會套上敞篷馬車,送你過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西會套上敞篷馬車,送你過去。

passages.original: The telegram says 'light hair, red-checked gingham dress, and straw hat.'
passages.vernacular: 電報上講『淺色頭髮,紅格子棉布裙,草帽』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 電報上說『淺色頭髮,紅格子棉布裙,草帽』。

passages.original: That is all I know, but I think it is sufficient for your purpose.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我所知道嘅全部,但我想對你嘅目的來講已經足夠喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我所知道的全部,但我想對你的目的來說已經足夠了。」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am; but--you--”
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人;不過——您——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人;可是——您——」

passages.original: Miss Polly evidently read the pause aright, for she frowned and said crisply:
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐顯然讀懂咗呢個停頓,因為佢皺住眉乾脆地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐顯然讀懂了這個停頓,因為她皺著眉乾脆地說:

passages.original: “No, I shall not go.
passages.vernacular: 「不,我不去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,我不去。

passages.original: It is not necessary that I should, I think.
passages.vernacular: 我想我冇必要去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我沒有必要去。

passages.original: That is all.”
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣。」

passages.original: And she turned away--Miss Polly's arrangements for the comfort of her niece, Pollyanna, were complete.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉身走喇——波莉小姐為佢外甥女波麗安娜嘅舒適所做嘅安排都完成喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她轉身走了——波莉小姐為她外甥女波麗安娜的舒適所做的安排都完成了。

passages.original: In the kitchen, Nancy sent her flatiron with a vicious dig across the dish-towel she was ironing.
passages.vernacular: 喺廚房裡,南希用熨斗狠狠地喺佢正在燙嘅擦碗巾上戳咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在廚房裡,南希用熨斗狠狠地在她正在燙的擦碗巾上戳了一下。

passages.original: “'Light hair, red-checked gingham dress, and straw hat'--all she knows, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「『淺色頭髮,紅格子棉布裙,草帽』——佢知道嘅全部,真係嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『淺色頭髮,紅格子棉布裙,草帽』——她知道的全部,真是的!

passages.original: Well, I'd be ashamed ter own it up, that I would, I would--and her my onliest niece what was a-comin' from 'way across the continent!”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我會羞於承認,我會,我會——而佢係我唯一嘅外甥女,從大陸嘅嗰一頭嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我會羞於承認,我會,我會——而她是我唯一的外甥女,從大陸的那一頭來!」

passages.original: Promptly at twenty minutes to four the next afternoon Timothy and Nancy drove off in the open buggy to meet the expected guest.
passages.vernacular: 第二天下午差二好四點,蒂莫西同南希坐住敞篷馬車出發去接預期嘅客人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天下午差二十分四點,蒂莫西和南希坐著敞篷馬車出發去接預期的客人。

passages.original: Timothy was Old Tom's son.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西係老湯姆嘅兒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西是老湯姆的兒子。

passages.original: It was sometimes said in the town that if Old Tom was Miss Polly's right-hand man, Timothy was her left.
passages.vernacular: 鎮上有時有人講,如果老湯姆係波莉小姐嘅右手,蒂莫西就係佢嘅左手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鎮上有時有人說,如果老湯姆是波莉小姐的右手,蒂莫西就是她的左手。

passages.original: Timothy was a good-natured youth, and a good-looking one, as well.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西係個脾氣好嘅年輕人,都長得好睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西是個脾氣好的年輕人,也長得好看。

passages.original: Short as had been Nancy's stay at the house, the two were already good friends.
passages.vernacular: 南希喺呢座房子裡雖然時間不長,兩人已經係好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希在這座房子裡雖然時間不長,兩人已經是好朋友。

passages.original: To-day, however, Nancy was too full of her mission to be her usual talkative self; and almost in silence she took the drive to the station and alighted to wait for the train.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日,南希滿腦子係佢嘅任務,冇平日咁愛講話;佢哋幾乎一路沉默地駕車到車站,下車等火車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過今天,南希滿腦子是她的任務,沒有平日那麼愛說話;她們幾乎一路沉默地駕車到車站,下車等火車。

passages.original: Over and over in her mind she was saying it “light hair, red-checked dress, straw hat.”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺腦子裡一遍又一遍地念住「淺色頭髮,紅格子裙,草帽」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在腦子裡一遍又一遍地念著「淺色頭髮,紅格子裙,草帽」。

passages.original: Over and over again she was wondering just what sort of child this Pollyanna was, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 佢一遍又一遍地納悶,呢個波麗安娜到底係個乜嘢樣嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一遍又一遍地納悶,這個波麗安娜到底是個什麼樣的孩子。

passages.original: “I hope for her sake she's quiet and sensible, and don't drop knives nor bang doors,” she sighed to Timothy, who had sauntered up to her.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望為了佢好,佢安靜懂事,不摔刀子都不摔門,」佢對蒂莫西嘆道,佢已經溜達到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望為了她好,她安靜懂事,不摔刀子也不摔門,」她對蒂莫西嘆道,他已經溜達到她身邊。

passages.original: “Well, if she ain't, nobody knows what'll become of the rest of us,” grinned Timothy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,如果佢唔係,邊個知道我哋其他人會點樣,」蒂莫西咧嘴笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,如果她不是,誰知道我們其他人會怎樣,」蒂莫西咧嘴笑。

passages.original: “Imagine Miss Polly and a NOISY kid!
passages.vernacular: 「想像一下波莉小姐同一個吵鬧嘅小孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想像一下波莉小姐和一個吵鬧的小孩!

passages.original: Gorry! there goes the whistle now!”
passages.vernacular: 天呀!哨子響喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!哨子響了!」

passages.original: “Oh, Timothy, I--I think it was mean ter send me,” chattered the suddenly frightened Nancy, as she turned and hurried to a point where she could best watch the passengers alight at the little station.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,蒂莫西,我——我覺得派我嚟真卑鄙,」突然害怕起嚟嘅南希結結巴巴地講,佢轉身匆忙走到一個能最好地睇乘客喺小車站下車嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,蒂莫西,我——我覺得派我來真卑鄙,」突然害怕起來的南希結結巴巴地說,她轉身匆忙走到一個能最好地看乘客在小車站下車的地方。

passages.original: It was not long before Nancy saw her--the slender little girl in the red-checked gingham with two fat braids of flaxen hair hanging down her back.
passages.vernacular: 不久南希就睇見咗佢——穿住紅格子棉布裙嘅苗條小女孩,背後垂住兩條粗粗嘅亞麻色辮子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久南希就看見了她——穿著紅格子棉布裙的苗條小女孩,背後垂著兩條粗粗的亞麻色辮子。

passages.original: Beneath the straw hat, an eager, freckled little face turned to the right and to the left, plainly searching for some one.
passages.vernacular: 草帽下,一張熱切嘅、長住雀斑嘅小臉轉向左邊同右邊,顯然喺找人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 草帽下,一張熱切的、長著雀斑的小臉轉向左邊和右邊,顯然在找人。

passages.original: Nancy knew the child at once, but not for some time could she control her shaking knees sufficiently to go to her.
passages.vernacular: 南希即刻認出咗呢細路,卻過咗好一會兒才能控制住顫抖嘅膝蓋走向佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希立刻認出了這孩子,卻過了好一會兒才能控制住顫抖的膝蓋走向她。

passages.original: The little girl was standing quite by herself when Nancy finally did approach her.
passages.vernacular: 南希終於走近時,小女孩正獨自站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希終於走近時,小女孩正獨自站著。

passages.original: “Are you Miss--Pollyanna?” she faltered.
passages.vernacular: 「您係波——波麗安娜小姐嗎?」佢怯怯地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您是波——波麗安娜小姐嗎?」她怯怯地問。

passages.original: The next moment she found herself half smothered in the clasp of two gingham-clad arms.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢發現自己被兩條穿棉布衣袖嘅手臂緊緊摟住,幾乎窒息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻她發現自己被兩條穿棉布衣袖的手臂緊緊摟住,幾乎窒息。

passages.original: “Oh, I'm so glad, GLAD, GLAD to see you,” cried an eager voice in her ear.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興、高興、高興見到你喇,」一個熱切嘅聲音喺佢耳邊喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興、高興、高興見到你了,」一個熱切的聲音在她耳邊喊道。

passages.original: “Of course I'm Pollyanna, and I'm so glad you came to meet me!
passages.vernacular: 「我當然係波麗安娜,我太高興你嚟接我喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我當然是波麗安娜,我太高興你來接我了!

passages.original: I hoped you would.”
passages.vernacular: 我就希望你會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就希望你會。」

passages.original: “You--you did?” stammered Nancy, vaguely wondering how Pollyanna could possibly have known her--and wanted her.
passages.vernacular: 「你——你希望?」南希結結巴巴地講,隱約納悶波麗安娜點可能認得佢——仲想要佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你——你希望?」南希結結巴巴地說,隱約納悶波麗安娜怎麼可能認得她——還想要她。

passages.original: “You--you did?” she repeated, trying to straighten her hat.
passages.vernacular: 「你——你希望?」佢重複講,試圖把帽子扶正。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你——你希望?」她重複說,試圖把帽子扶正。

passages.original: “Oh, yes; and I've been wondering all the way here what you looked like,” cried the little girl, dancing on her toes, and sweeping the embarrassed Nancy from head to foot, with her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅;我一路都喺猜你長乜嘢樣,」小女孩喊道,踮住腳跳住,用眼睛把窘迫嘅南希從頭到腳掃咗一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的;我一路都在猜你長什麼樣,」小女孩喊道,踮著腳跳著,用眼睛把窘迫的南希從頭到腳掃了一遍。

passages.original: “And now I know, and I'm glad you look just like you do look.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家我知道喇,我好高興你嘅長相就係你而家嘅樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我知道了,我很高興你的長相就是你現在的樣子。」

passages.original: Nancy was relieved just then to have Timothy come up.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣蒂莫西走咗過嚟,南希鬆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時蒂莫西走了過來,南希鬆了口氣。

passages.original: Pollyanna's words had been most confusing.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅話讓人好困惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的話讓人非常困惑。

passages.original: “This is Timothy.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係蒂莫西。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是蒂莫西。

passages.original: Maybe you have a trunk,” she stammered.
passages.vernacular: 或者你有一隻箱子,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你有一隻箱子,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “Yes, I have,” nodded Pollyanna, importantly.
passages.vernacular: 「係,我有,」波麗安娜重要地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,我有,」波麗安娜重要地點頭。

passages.original: “I've got a brand-new one.
passages.vernacular: 「我有一個嶄新嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有一個嶄新的。

passages.original: The Ladies' Aid bought it for me--and wasn't it lovely of them, when they wanted the carpet so?
passages.vernacular: 係婦女互助會畀我買嘅——佢哋多好啊,佢哋咁想要地毯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是婦女互助會給我買的——他們多好啊,他們那麼想要地毯!

passages.original: Of course I don't know how much red carpet a trunk could buy, but it ought to buy some, anyhow--much as half an aisle, don't you think?
passages.vernacular: 當然我唔知道一隻箱子嘅錢能買多少紅地毯,但佢總該能買啲,至少像半條走道咁多,你不覺得嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我不知道一隻箱子的錢能買多少紅地毯,但它總該能買一些,至少像半條走道那麼多,你不覺得嗎?

passages.original: I've got a little thing here in my bag that Mr. Gray said was a check, and that I must give it to you before I could get my trunk.
passages.vernacular: 我袋子裡有一個小嘢,格雷先生講嗰個係個行李票,我必須把佢交畀你,才能攞到我嘅箱子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我袋子裡有一個小東西,格雷先生說那是個行李票,我必須把它交給你,才能拿到我的箱子。

passages.original: Mr. Gray is Mrs. Gray's husband.
passages.vernacular: 格雷先生係格雷太太嘅丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格雷先生是格雷太太的丈夫。

passages.original: They're cousins of Deacon Carr's wife.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋係執事卡爾太太嘅堂親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們是執事卡爾太太的堂親。

passages.original: I came East with them, and they're lovely!
passages.vernacular: 我跟佢哋一起嚟東部,佢哋好極喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟他們一起來東部,他們好極了!

passages.original: And--there, here 'tis,” she finished, producing the check after much fumbling in the bag she carried.
passages.vernacular: 仲有——哦,喺呢兒,」佢結束時講,喺佢攞住嘅袋子裡摸索咗好一陣後,攞出咗行李票。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有——哦,在這兒,」她結束時說,在她拿著的袋子裡摸索了好一陣後,拿出了行李票。

passages.original: Nancy drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 南希深吸咗一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希深吸了一口氣。

passages.original: Instinctively she felt that some one had to draw one--after that speech.
passages.vernacular: 佢本能地覺得,聽咗嗰番話,邊個都得吸一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本能地覺得,聽了那番話,誰都得吸一口氣。

passages.original: Then she stole a glance at Timothy.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢偷偷睇咗蒂莫西一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她偷偷看了蒂莫西一眼。

passages.original: Timothy's eyes were studiously turned away.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西嘅眼睛特意轉向別處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西的眼睛特意轉向別處。

passages.original: The three were off at last, with Pollyanna's trunk in behind, and Pollyanna herself snugly ensconced between Nancy and Timothy.
passages.vernacular: 三人終於出發喇,波麗安娜嘅箱子放喺後面,波麗安娜本人舒舒服服地坐喺南希同蒂莫西中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三人終於出發了,波麗安娜的箱子放在後面,波麗安娜本人舒舒服服地坐在南希和蒂莫西中間。

passages.original: During the whole process of getting started, the little girl had kept up an uninterrupted stream of comments and questions, until the somewhat dazed Nancy found herself quite out of breath trying to keep up with her.
passages.vernacular: 整個出發嘅過程中,小女孩一直不停地發表評論同提問,弄得有點發懵嘅南希上氣不接下氣地努力跟上佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個出發的過程中,小女孩一直不停地發表評論和提問,弄得有點發懵的南希上氣不接下氣地努力跟上她。

passages.original: “There!
passages.vernacular: 「好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了!

passages.original: Isn't this lovely?
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係好美嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是很美嗎?

passages.original: Is it far?
passages.vernacular: 遠嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 遠嗎?

passages.original: I hope 'tis--I love to ride,” sighed Pollyanna, as the wheels began to turn.
passages.vernacular: 我希望係——我愛坐車,」波麗安娜嘆道,車輪開始轉動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望是——我愛坐車,」波麗安娜嘆道,車輪開始轉動。

passages.original: “Of course, if 'tisn't far, I sha'n't mind, though, 'cause I'll be glad to get there all the sooner, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,如果不遠,我都不介意,因為我會更早到嗰兒就好高興,你知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,如果不遠,我也不介意,因為我會更早到那兒就很高興,你知道的。

passages.original: What a pretty street!
passages.vernacular: 幾咁漂亮嘅街啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多麼漂亮的街啊!

passages.original: I knew 'twas going to be pretty; father told me--”
passages.vernacular: 我就知道佢會好漂亮;爸爸告訴過我——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就知道它會很漂亮;爸爸告訴過我——」

passages.original: She stopped with a little choking breath.
passages.vernacular: 佢停住喇,帶住輕輕嘅哽咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她停住了,帶著輕輕的哽咽。

passages.original: Nancy, looking at her apprehensively, saw that her small chin was quivering, and that her eyes were full of tears.
passages.vernacular: 南希憂慮地睇住佢,睇見佢小小嘅下巴喺顫抖,眼睛裡滿係淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希憂慮地看著她,看見她小小的下巴在顫抖,眼睛裡滿是淚水。

passages.original: In a moment, however, she hurried on, with a brave lifting of her head.
passages.vernacular: 不過一會兒,佢勇敢地昂起頭,匆忙接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過一會兒,她勇敢地昂起頭,匆忙接著說。

passages.original: “Father told me all about it.
passages.vernacular: 「爸爸把一切都告訴我喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「爸爸把一切都告訴我了。

passages.original: He remembered.
passages.vernacular: 佢記得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他記得。

passages.original: And--and I ought to have explained before.
passages.vernacular: 而且——而且我應該早點解釋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且——而且我應該早點解釋的。

passages.original: Mrs. Gray told me to, at once--about this red gingham dress, you know, and why I'm not in black.
passages.vernacular: 格雷太太叫我即刻講——關於呢條紅格子裙子,你知道,以及我點解不穿黑嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格雷太太叫我馬上說——關於這條紅格子裙子,你知道,以及我為什麼不穿黑的。

passages.original: She said you'd think 'twas queer.
passages.vernacular: 佢講你會覺得奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說你會覺得奇怪。

passages.original: But there weren't any black things in the last missionary barrel, only a lady's velvet basque which Deacon Carr's wife said wasn't suitable for me at all; besides, it had white spots--worn, you know--on both elbows, and some other places.
passages.vernacular: 但係最後一個傳教士捐贈桶裡冇黑色嘅嘢,只有一件女士嘅天鵝絨緊身衣,執事卡爾太太講完全不適合我;而且,兩個肘部同其他啲地方都有白斑——磨嘅,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是最後一個傳教士捐贈桶裡沒有黑色的東西,只有一件女士的天鵝絨緊身衣,執事卡爾太太說完全不適合我;而且,兩個肘部和其他一些地方都有白斑——磨的,你知道。

passages.original: Part of the Ladies' Aid wanted to buy me a black dress and hat, but the other part thought the money ought to go toward the red carpet they're trying to get--for the church, you know.
passages.vernacular: 婦女互助會嘅一部分人想畀我買一條黑裙子同帽子,但另一部分人認為呢筆錢應該用喺佢哋正在努力買嘅紅地毯上——為教堂,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 婦女互助會的一部分人想給我買一條黑裙子和帽子,但另一部分人認為這筆錢應該用在他們正在努力買的紅地毯上——為教堂,你知道。

passages.original: Mrs. White said maybe it was just as well, anyway, for she didn't like children in black--that is, I mean, she liked the children, of course, but not the black part.”
passages.vernacular: 懷特太太講或者咁樣更好,反正佢不鍾意穿黑衣服嘅細路——就係,我嘅意思係,佢當然鍾意細路,不過不鍾意黑色嘅部分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懷特太太說也許這樣更好,反正她不喜歡穿黑衣服的孩子——就是,我的意思是,她當然喜歡孩子,不過不喜歡黑色的部分。」

passages.original: Pollyanna paused for breath, and Nancy managed to stammer:
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜停下嚟喘氣,南希勉強結結巴巴地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜停下來喘氣,南希勉強結結巴巴地說:

passages.original: “Well, I'm sure it--it'll be all right.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我肯定佢——佢會冇事嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我肯定它——它會沒事的。」

passages.original: “I'm glad you feel that way.
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興你咁覺得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興你這麼覺得。

passages.original: I do, too,” nodded Pollyanna, again with that choking little breath.
passages.vernacular: 我都係,」波麗安娜點點頭,又帶住嗰種輕輕嘅哽咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也是,」波麗安娜點點頭,又帶著那種輕輕的哽咽。

passages.original: “Of course, 'twould have been a good deal harder to be glad in black--”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,穿黑色要高興起嚟困難得多——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,穿黑色要高興起來困難得多——」

passages.original: “Glad!” gasped Nancy, surprised into an interruption.
passages.vernacular: 「高興!」南希喊道,驚訝得打斷咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興!」南希喊道,驚訝得打斷了她。

passages.original: “Yes--that father's gone to Heaven to be with mother and the rest of us, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——因為爸爸去天堂同媽媽以及我哋其他人喺一起喇,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——因為爸爸去天堂和媽媽以及我們其他人在一起了,你知道。

passages.original: He said I must be glad.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我必須高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說我必須高興。

passages.original: But it's been pretty hard to--to do it, even in red gingham, because I--I wanted him, so; and I couldn't help feeling I OUGHT to have him, specially as mother and the rest have God and all the angels, while I didn't have anybody but the Ladies' Aid.
passages.vernacular: 不過做到呢啲好難——即使穿住紅格子裙,因為我——我咁想要佢;我忍不住覺得我應該擁有佢,尤其係媽媽同其他人有上帝同所有天使,而我除咗婦女互助會邊個都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是做到這一點很難——即使穿著紅格子裙,因為我——我那麼想要他;我忍不住覺得我應該擁有他,尤其是媽媽和其他人有上帝和所有天使,而我除了婦女互助會誰也沒有。

passages.original: But now I'm sure it'll be easier because I've got you, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 但而家我肯定會容易些,因為我有咗你,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在我肯定會容易些,因為我有了你,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I'm so glad I've got you!”
passages.vernacular: 我太高興我有你喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興我有你了!」

passages.original: Nancy's aching sympathy for the poor little forlornness beside her turned suddenly into shocked terror.
passages.vernacular: 南希對身邊呢可憐小孤兒嘅痛惜同情,突然變成咗震驚嘅恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希對身邊這可憐小孤兒的痛惜同情,突然變成了震驚的恐懼。

passages.original: “Oh, but--but you've made an awful mistake, d-dear,” she faltered.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過——不過你弄錯喇,親——親愛嘅,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是——可是你弄錯了,親——親愛的,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “I'm only Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「我只係南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是南希。

passages.original: I ain't your Aunt Polly, at all!”
passages.vernacular: 我根本唔係你嘅波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我根本不是你的波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: “You--you AREN'T?” stammered the little girl, in plain dismay.
passages.vernacular: 「你——你唔係?」小女孩結結巴巴地講,顯然好沮喪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你——你不是?」小女孩結結巴巴地說,顯然很沮喪。

passages.original: “No. I'm only Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係。我只係南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是。我只是南希。

passages.original: I never thought of your takin' me for her.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇想到你會把我當成佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒想到你會把我當成她。

passages.original: We--we ain't a bit alike we ain't, we ain't!”
passages.vernacular: 我哋——我哋啲都不像,我哋不像,我哋不像!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們——我們一點也不像,我們不像,我們不像!」

passages.original: Timothy chuckled softly; but Nancy was too disturbed to answer the merry flash from his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西輕輕笑喇;但南希太慌亂,冇回應佢閃住快活嘅眼神。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西輕輕笑了;但南希太慌亂,沒回應他閃著快活的眼神。

passages.original: “But who ARE you?” questioned Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「不過你係邊個?」波麗安娜問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是你是誰?」波麗安娜問。

passages.original: “You don't look a bit like a Ladies' Aider!”
passages.vernacular: 「你啲都不像婦女互助會嘅人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你一點也不像婦女互助會的人!」

passages.original: Timothy laughed outright this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢次蒂莫西放聲大笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次蒂莫西放聲大笑。

passages.original: “I'm Nancy, the hired girl.
passages.vernacular: 「我係南希,女傭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是南希,女傭。

passages.original: I do all the work except the washin' an' hard ironin'.
passages.vernacular: 我做除咗洗衣同重熨燙之外嘅所有活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我做除了洗衣和重熨燙之外的所有活。

passages.original: Mis' Durgin does that.”
passages.vernacular: 杜爾金太太做嗰啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 杜爾金太太做那些。」

passages.original: “But there IS an Aunt Polly?” demanded the child, anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「不過有一位波莉姨媽吧?」細路焦急地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是有一位波莉姨媽吧?」孩子焦急地問。

passages.original: “You bet your life there is,” cut in Timothy.
passages.vernacular: 「當然有,你放心,」蒂莫西插話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然有,你放心,」蒂莫西插話。

passages.original: Pollyanna relaxed visibly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜明顯放鬆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜明顯放鬆了。

passages.original: “Oh, that's all right, then.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰就冇事喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那就沒事了。」

passages.original: There was a moment's silence, then she went on brightly: “And do you know?
passages.vernacular: 沉默咗片刻,然後佢愉快地接住講:「你知道嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默了片刻,然後她愉快地接著說:「你知道嗎?

passages.original: I'm glad, after all, that she didn't come to meet me; because now I've got HER still coming, and I've got you besides.”
passages.vernacular: 我反而高興,佢冇嚟接我;因為而家我仲有佢要嚟,仲有你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我反而高興,她沒有來接我;因為現在我還有她要來,還有你。」

passages.original: Nancy flushed.
passages.vernacular: 南希臉紅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希臉紅了。

passages.original: Timothy turned to her with a quizzical smile.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西帶住揶揄嘅笑轉向佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西帶著揶揄的笑轉向她。

passages.original: “I call that a pretty slick compliment,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我講呢個係相當漂亮嘅恭維,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說這是相當漂亮的恭維,」他說。

passages.original: “Why don't you thank the little lady?”
passages.vernacular: 「你點解不謝謝呢位小姐?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你為什麼不謝謝這位小姐?」

passages.original: “I--I was thinkin' about--Miss Polly,” faltered Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我喺想——波莉小姐,」南希結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我在想——波莉小姐,」南希結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: Pollyanna sighed contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜滿足地嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜滿足地嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “I was, too.
passages.vernacular: 「我都喺想佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也在想她。

passages.original: I'm so interested in her.
passages.vernacular: 我對佢太感興趣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對她太感興趣了。

passages.original: You know she's all the aunt I've got, and I didn't know I had her for ever so long.
passages.vernacular: 你知道,佢係我僅有嘅姨媽,我好久好久都唔知道我有佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,她是我僅有的姨媽,我很久很久都不知道我有她。

passages.original: Then father told me.
passages.vernacular: 後來爸爸告訴我喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來爸爸告訴我了。

passages.original: He said she lived in a lovely great big house 'way on top of a hill.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢住喺山頂上一座好大好美嘅房子裡。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說她住在山頂上一座很大很美的房子裡。」

passages.original: “She does.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是。

passages.original: You can see it now,” said Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 你而家就能睇見,」南希講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在就能看見,」南希說。

passages.original: “It's that big white one with the green blinds, 'way ahead.”
passages.vernacular: 「就係遠處嗰座有綠百葉窗嘅大白房子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是遠處那座有綠百葉窗的大白房子。」

passages.original: “Oh, how pretty!--and what a lot of trees and grass all around it!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,多漂亮!——周圍有咁多樹同草地!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,多漂亮!——周圍有那麼多樹和草地!

passages.original: I never saw such a lot of green grass, seems so, all at once.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇一下子見過咁多綠草,似乎係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒一下子見過這麼多綠草,似乎是這樣。

passages.original: Is my Aunt Polly rich, Nancy?”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅波莉姨媽有錢嗎,南希?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的波莉姨媽有錢嗎,南希?」

passages.original: “Yes, Miss.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,小姐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,小姐。」

passages.original: “I'm so glad.
passages.vernacular: 「我太高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我太高興了。

passages.original: It must be perfectly lovely to have lots of money.
passages.vernacular: 有好多錢一定好極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有很多錢一定好極了。

passages.original: I never knew any one that did have, only the Whites--they're some rich.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇認識有錢嘅人,只有懷特家——佢哋有點錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒認識有錢的人,只有懷特家——他們有點錢。

passages.original: They have carpets in every room and ice-cream Sundays.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋每個房間都有地毯,星期日仲有冰淇淋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們每個房間都有地毯,星期日還有冰淇淋。

passages.original: Does Aunt Polly have ice-cream Sundays?”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽家星期日有冰淇淋嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽家星期日有冰淇淋嗎?」

passages.original: Nancy shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 南希搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希搖搖頭。

passages.original: Her lips twitched.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅嘴唇抽動住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的嘴唇抽動著。

passages.original: She threw a merry look into Timothy's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢快活地睇咗蒂莫西一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她快活地看了蒂莫西一眼。

passages.original: “No, Miss.
passages.vernacular: 「冇,小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,小姐。

passages.original: Your aunt don't like ice-cream, I guess; leastways I never saw it on her table.”
passages.vernacular: 你姨媽不鍾意冰淇淋,我想;至少我從冇喺佢桌上見過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你姨媽不喜歡冰淇淋,我想;至少我從沒在她桌上見過。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's face fell.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅臉沉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的臉沉了下來。

passages.original: “Oh, doesn't she?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢不鍾意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她不喜歡嗎?

passages.original: I'm so sorry!
passages.vernacular: 我真遺憾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真遺憾!

passages.original: I don't see how she can help liking ice-cream.
passages.vernacular: 我不明白佢點會不鍾意冰淇淋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不明白她怎麼會不喜歡冰淇淋。

passages.original: But--anyhow, I can be kinder glad about that, 'cause the ice-cream you don't eat can't make your stomach ache like Mrs. White's did--that is, I ate hers, you know, lots of it.
passages.vernacular: 不過——不過,我可以有點高興呢個,因為你不食嘅冰淇淋唔會讓你肚子疼,像懷特太太嘅嗰樣——就係,我食咗佢嘅,你知道,食咗好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是——不過,我可以有點高興這個,因為你不吃的冰淇淋不會讓你肚子疼,像懷特太太的那樣——就是,我吃了她的,你知道,吃了很多。

passages.original: Maybe Aunt Polly has got the carpets, though.”
passages.vernacular: 不過波莉姨媽或者有地毯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過波莉姨媽也許有地毯。」

passages.original: “Yes, she's got the carpets.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢有地毯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,她有地毯。」

passages.original: “In every room?”
passages.vernacular: 「每個房間都有?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「每個房間都有?」

passages.original: “Well, in almost every room,” answered Nancy, frowning suddenly at the thought of that bare little attic room where there was no carpet.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,幾乎每個房間,」南希回答,一想到嗰個冇地毯嘅光禿禿嘅小閣樓,突然皺起咗眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,幾乎每個房間,」南希回答,一想到那個沒有地毯的光禿禿的小閣樓,突然皺起了眉頭。

passages.original: “Oh, I'm so glad,” exulted Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興喇,」波麗安娜歡呼道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興了,」波麗安娜歡呼道。

passages.original: “I love carpets.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛地毯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛地毯。

passages.original: We didn't have any, only two little rugs that came in a missionary barrel, and one of those had ink spots on it.
passages.vernacular: 我哋冇,只有兩塊小地墊係傳教士捐贈桶裡嚟嘅,其中一塊上有墨水漬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們沒有,只有兩塊小地墊是傳教士捐贈桶裡來的,其中一塊上有墨水漬。

passages.original: Mrs. White had pictures, too, perfectly beautiful ones of roses and little girls kneeling and a kitty and some lambs and a lion--not together, you know--the lambs and the lion.
passages.vernacular: 懷特太太仲有畫,好漂亮嘅畫,畫住玫瑰、跪住嘅小女孩、一隻小貓、啲羊羔同一頭獅子——你知道,不喺一起——羊羔同獅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懷特太太還有畫,非常漂亮的畫,畫著玫瑰、跪著的小女孩、一隻小貓、一些羊羔和一頭獅子——你知道,不在一起——羊羔和獅子。

passages.original: Oh, of course the Bible says they will sometime, but they haven't yet--that is, I mean Mrs. White's haven't.
passages.vernacular: 哦,當然聖經講佢哋有一天會,但而家仲冇——就係,我嘅意思係懷特太太嘅畫上冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,當然聖經說它們有一天會,但現在還沒有——就是,我的意思是懷特太太的畫上沒有。

passages.original: Don't you just love pictures?”
passages.vernacular: 你不愛畫嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不愛畫嗎?」

passages.original: “I--I don't know,” answered Nancy in a half-stifled voice.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我唔知道,」南希用半窒息嘅聲音回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我不知道,」南希用半窒息的聲音回答。

passages.original: “I do.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛。

passages.original: We didn't have any pictures.
passages.vernacular: 我哋冇任何畫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們沒有任何畫。

passages.original: They don't come in the barrels much, you know.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不常喺捐贈桶裡,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們不常在捐贈桶裡,你知道。

passages.original: There did two come once, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過有一次嚟咗兩幅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過有一次來了兩幅。

passages.original: But one was so good father sold it to get money to buy me some shoes with; and the other was so bad it fell to pieces just as soon as we hung it up.
passages.vernacular: 但其中一幅太好喇,爸爸把佢賣喇,畀我買鞋;另一幅太差喇,我哋一掛上去就散架喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但其中一幅太好了,爸爸把它賣了,給我買鞋;另一幅太差了,我們一掛上去就散架了。

passages.original: Glass--it broke, you know.
passages.vernacular: 玻璃——碎喇,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 玻璃——碎了,你知道。

passages.original: And I cried.
passages.vernacular: 我仲哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還哭了。

passages.original: But I'm glad now we didn't have any of those nice things, 'cause I shall like Aunt Polly's all the better--not being used to 'em, you see.
passages.vernacular: 但我而家高興我哋冇嗰啲好嘢,因為我會更鍾意波莉姨媽嘅——不習慣佢哋,你睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我現在高興我們沒有那些好東西,因為我會更喜歡波莉姨媽的——不習慣它們,你看。

passages.original: Just as it is when the PRETTY hair-ribbons come in the barrels after a lot of faded-out brown ones.
passages.vernacular: 就像漂亮嘅髮帶喺捐贈桶裡出而家一大堆褪色嘅棕色髮帶之後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像漂亮的髮帶在捐贈桶裡出現在一大堆褪色的棕色髮帶之後。

passages.original: My! but isn't this a perfectly beautiful house?” she broke off fervently, as they turned into the wide driveway.
passages.vernacular: 天呀!呢唔係一座絕對漂亮嘅房子嗎?」佢熱切地打斷自己,呢陣佢哋轉進咗寬闊嘅車道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!這不是一座絕對漂亮的房子嗎?」她熱切地打斷自己,這時他們轉進了寬闊的車道。

passages.original: It was when Timothy was unloading the trunk that Nancy found an opportunity to mutter low in his ear:
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西卸箱子時,南希找到機會低聲喺佢耳邊嘟囔:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西卸箱子時,南希找到機會低聲在他耳邊嘟囔:

passages.original: “Don't you never say nothin' ter me again about leavin', Timothy Durgin.
passages.vernacular: 「蒂莫西·杜爾金,你以後再都別對我講乜嘢離開嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「蒂莫西·杜爾金,你以後再也別對我說什麼離開的話。

passages.original: You couldn't HIRE me ter leave!”
passages.vernacular: 你就係雇我都雇不走!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你就是雇我也雇不走!」

passages.original: “Leave!
passages.vernacular: 「離開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「離開!

passages.original: I should say not,” grinned the youth.
passages.vernacular: 我該講唔會,」小夥子咧嘴笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該說不會,」小夥子咧嘴笑。

passages.original: “You couldn't drag me away.
passages.vernacular: 「你就係拖我都拖不走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你就是拖我也拖不走。

passages.original: It'll be more fun here now, with that kid 'round, than movin'-picture shows, every day!”
passages.vernacular: 而家有嗰細路喺周圍,比天天睇電影仲有趣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在有那孩子在周圍,比天天看電影還有趣!」

passages.original: “Fun!--fun!” repeated Nancy, indignantly, “I guess it'll be somethin' more than fun for that blessed child--when them two tries ter live tergether; and I guess she'll be a-needin' some rock ter fly to for refuge.
passages.vernacular: 「有趣!——有趣!」南希憤慨地重複,「我想對嗰可憐嘅細路來講,不只係有趣——當嗰兩個試住住喺一起嘅時候;我想佢會需要一塊岩石去避難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有趣!——有趣!」南希憤慨地重複,「我想對那可憐的孩子來說,不只是有趣——當那兩個試著住在一起的時候;我想她會需要一塊岩石去避難。

passages.original: Well, I'm a-goin' ter be that rock, Timothy; I am, I am!” she vowed, as she turned and led Pollyanna up the broad steps.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我要做嗰塊岩石,蒂莫西;我要,我要!」佢發誓講,轉身領波麗安娜走上寬寬嘅台階。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我要做那塊岩石,蒂莫西;我要,我要!」她發誓說,轉身領波麗安娜走上寬寬的台階。

chapters.title: Ch. IV The Little Attic Room 第四章:閣樓小房間

passages.original: CH Miss Polly Harrington did not rise to meet her niece.
passages.vernacular: 波莉·哈林頓小姐冇起身迎接佢嘅外甥女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉·哈林頓小姐沒有起身迎接她的外甥女。

passages.original: She looked up from her book, it is true, as Nancy and the little girl appeared in the sitting-room doorway, and she held out a hand with “duty” written large on every coldly extended finger.
passages.vernacular: 南希同小女孩出而家起居室門口時,佢確實從書上抬起咗頭,伸出一隻手,每根冷冷伸出嘅手指上都大大地寫住「責任」二字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希和小女孩出現在起居室門口時,她確實從書上抬起了頭,伸出一隻手,每根冷冷伸出的手指上都大大地寫著「責任」二字。

passages.original: “How do you do, Pollyanna?
passages.vernacular: 「你好嗎,波麗安娜?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你好嗎,波麗安娜?

passages.original: I--” She had no chance to say more.
passages.vernacular: 我——」佢冇機會再講下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——」她沒有機會再說下去。

passages.original: Pollyanna, had fairly flown across the room and flung herself into her aunt's scandalized, unyielding lap.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜簡直係飛過房間,撲進佢姨媽震驚而紋絲不動嘅膝上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜簡直是飛過房間,撲進她姨媽震驚而紋絲不動的膝上。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly, I don't know how to be glad enough that you let me come to live with you,” she was sobbing.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,我唔知道點樣才夠高興,你讓我嚟同你一起住,」佢抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,我不知道怎樣才夠高興,你讓我來和你一起住,」她抽泣著說。

passages.original: “You don't know how perfectly lovely it is to have you and Nancy and all this after you've had just the Ladies' Aid!”
passages.vernacular: 「你唔知道,喺只有婦女互助會之後,有你、有南希、有呢一切,係幾咁絕對地美好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不知道,在只有婦女互助會之後,有你、有南希、有這一切,是多麼絕對地美好!」

passages.original: “Very likely--though I've not had the pleasure of the Ladies' Aid's acquaintance,” rejoined Miss Polly, stiffly, trying to unclasp the small, clinging fingers, and turning frowning eyes on Nancy in the doorway.
passages.vernacular: 「好可能——雖然我仲冇榮幸認識婦女互助會,」波莉小姐僵硬地回答,試圖掰開嗰雙緊抓不放嘅小手指,並把皺住眉嘅眼睛轉向站喺門口嘅南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能——雖然我還沒有榮幸認識婦女互助會,」波莉小姐僵硬地回答,試圖掰開那雙緊抓不放的小手指,並把皺著眉的眼睛轉向站在門口的南希。

passages.original: “Nancy, that will do.
passages.vernacular: 「南希,夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,夠了。

passages.original: You may go.
passages.vernacular: 你可以走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以走了。

passages.original: Pollyanna, be good enough, please, to stand erect in a proper manner.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜,請好心地,規規矩矩地站直。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜,請好心地,規規矩矩地站直。

passages.original: I don't know yet what you look like.”
passages.vernacular: 我仲唔知道你長乜嘢樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還不知道你長什麼樣。」

passages.original: Pollyanna drew back at once, laughing a little hysterically.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜即刻退後,有點歇斯底里地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜立刻退後,有點歇斯底里地笑了。

passages.original: “No, I suppose you don't; but you see I'm not very much to look at, anyway, on account of the freckles.
passages.vernacular: 「係,我想你唔知道;不過你睇,反正我不太好睇,因為有雀斑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,我想你不知道;不過你看,反正我不太好看,因為有雀斑。

passages.original: Oh, and I ought to explain about the red gingham and the black velvet basque with white spots on the elbows.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我仲該解釋一下關於紅棉布裙同肘上有白斑嘅黑天鵝絨緊身衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我還該解釋一下關於紅棉布裙和肘上有白斑的黑天鵝絨緊身衣。

passages.original: I told Nancy how father said--”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴過南希爸爸點講——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴過南希爸爸怎麼說——」

passages.original: “Yes; well, never mind now what your father said,” interrupted Miss Polly, crisply.
passages.vernacular: 「係;好喇,而家唔使管你爸爸講咗乜嘢,」波莉小姐乾脆地打斷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是;好了,現在不用管你爸爸說了什麼,」波莉小姐乾脆地打斷道。

passages.original: “You had a trunk, I presume?”
passages.vernacular: 「你有一隻箱子,我想?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你有一隻箱子,我想?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, indeed, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,有嘅,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,有的,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I've got a beautiful trunk that the Ladies' Aid gave me.
passages.vernacular: 我有一隻漂亮嘅箱子,係婦女互助會畀我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一隻漂亮的箱子,是婦女互助會給我的。

passages.original: I haven't got so very much in it--of my own, I mean.
passages.vernacular: 裡面冇好多——我自己嘅嘢,我係講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 裡面沒有很多——我自己的東西,我是說。

passages.original: The barrels haven't had many clothes for little girls in them lately; but there were all father's books, and Mrs. White said she thought I ought to have those.
passages.vernacular: 捐贈桶裡最近冇太多小女孩嘅衣服;不過有爸爸所有嘅書,懷特太太講佢覺得我應該有嗰啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 捐贈桶裡最近沒有太多小女孩的衣服;不過有爸爸所有的書,懷特太太說她覺得我應該有那些。

passages.original: You see, father--”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,爸爸——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,爸爸——」

passages.original: “Pollyanna,” interrupted her aunt again, sharply, “there is one thing that might just as well be understood right away at once; and that is, I do not care to have you keep talking of your father to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,」佢姨媽又尖銳地打斷講,「有一件事最好即刻講清楚;就係,我唔想你一直對我談你嘅父親。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,」她姨媽又尖銳地打斷說,「有一件事最好立刻說清楚;就是,我不想你一直對我談你的父親。」

passages.original: The little girl drew in her breath tremulously.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩顫抖地吸咗一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩顫抖地吸了一口氣。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, you--you mean--” She hesitated, and her aunt filled the pause.
passages.vernacular: 「點解,波莉姨媽,你——你係講——」佢猶豫喇,佢姨媽接上咗呢停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼,波莉姨媽,你——你是說——」她猶豫了,她姨媽接上了這停頓。

passages.original: “We will go up-stairs to your room.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋上樓去你嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們上樓去你的房間。

passages.original: Your trunk is already there, I presume.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅箱子大概已經喺嗰度喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的箱子大概已經在那裡了。

passages.original: I told Timothy to take it up--if you had one.
passages.vernacular: 我叫蒂莫西把佢攞上去——如果你有一隻嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫蒂莫西把它拿上去——如果你有一隻的話。

passages.original: You may follow me, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 你跟我嚟,波麗安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你跟我來,波麗安娜。」

passages.original: Without speaking, Pollyanna turned and followed her aunt from the room.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜一言不發,轉身跟住姨媽離開咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜一言不發,轉身跟著姨媽離開了房間。

passages.original: Her eyes were brimming with tears, but her chin was bravely high.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛裡滿係淚水,但下巴勇敢地高抬住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛裡滿是淚水,但下巴勇敢地高抬著。

passages.original: “After all, I--I reckon I'm glad she doesn't want me to talk about father,” Pollyanna was thinking.
passages.vernacular: 「畢竟,我——我想我好高興佢唔好我談爸爸,」波麗安娜心想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「畢竟,我——我想我很高興她不要我談爸爸,」波麗安娜心想。

passages.original: “It'll be easier, maybe--if I don't talk about him.
passages.vernacular: 「或者會容易些——如果我不談佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許會容易些——如果我不談他。

passages.original: Probably, anyhow, that is why she told me not to talk about him.”
passages.vernacular: 反正,大概呢個就係佢叫我唔好談佢嘅原因。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正,大概這就是她叫我不要談他的原因。」

passages.original: And Pollyanna, convinced anew of her aunt's “kindness,” blinked off the tears and looked eagerly about her.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜再次確信咗佢姨媽嘅「善意」,眨掉眼淚,熱切地四處睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜再次確信了她姨媽的「善意」,眨掉眼淚,熱切地四處看。

passages.original: She was on the stairway now.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家喺樓梯上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在在樓梯上。

passages.original: Just ahead, her aunt's black silk skirt rustled luxuriously.
passages.vernacular: 就喺前面,佢姨媽嘅黑絲裙奢華地沙沙作響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在前面,她姨媽的黑絲裙奢華地沙沙作響。

passages.original: Behind her an open door allowed a glimpse of soft-tinted rugs and satin-covered chairs.
passages.vernacular: 佢身後一扇開住嘅門,讓人瞥見柔色嘅地毯同緞面包住嘅椅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她身後一扇開著的門,讓人瞥見柔色的地毯和緞面包著的椅子。

passages.original: Beneath her feet a marvellous carpet was like green moss to the tread.
passages.vernacular: 佢腳下一條美妙嘅地毯,踩上去像綠色嘅苔蘚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她腳下一條美妙的地毯,踩上去像綠色的苔蘚。

passages.original: On every side the gilt of picture frames or the glint of sunlight through the filmy mesh of lace curtains flashed in her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 四面八方,畫框嘅金色或陽光透過薄薄蕾絲窗簾網眼嘅閃光,喺佢眼裡閃爍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 四面八方,畫框的金色或陽光透過薄薄蕾絲窗簾網眼的閃光,在她眼裡閃爍。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly,” breathed the little girl, rapturously; “what a perfectly lovely, lovely house!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,」小女孩狂喜地低聲講;「幾咁絕對美好、美好嘅房子啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,」小女孩狂喜地低聲說;「多麼絕對美好、美好的房子啊!

passages.original: How awfully glad you must be you're so rich!”
passages.vernacular: 你能咁富有,一定高興極喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能這麼富有,一定高興極了!」

passages.original: “PollyANNA!” ejaculated her aunt, turning sharply about as she reached the head of the stairs.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜!」佢姨媽大聲講,喺樓梯頂轉身尖銳地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜!」她姨媽大聲說,在樓梯頂轉身尖銳地說。

passages.original: “I'm surprised at you--making a speech like that to me!”
passages.vernacular: 「我對你好食驚——對我講咁樣嘅話!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我對你很吃驚——對我說這樣的話!」

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, AREN'T you?” queried Pollyanna, in frank wonder.
passages.vernacular: 「點解,波莉姨媽,你不高興嗎?」波麗安娜直率地驚奇地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼,波莉姨媽,你不高興嗎?」波麗安娜直率地驚奇地問。

passages.original: “Certainly not, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「當然不,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不,波麗安娜。

passages.original: I hope I could not so far forget myself as to be sinfully proud of any gift the Lord has seen fit to bestow upon me,” declared the lady; “certainly not, of RICHES!”
passages.vernacular: 我希望我唔會忘咗自己到罪惡地為主認為適合賜畀我嘅任何禮物感到驕傲,」嗰位女士宣稱;「當然不,為財富!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望我不會忘了自己到罪惡地為主認為適合賜給我的任何禮物感到驕傲,」那位女士宣稱;「當然不,為財富!」

passages.original: Miss Polly turned and walked down the hall toward the attic stairway door.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐轉身沿走廊朝閣樓樓梯門走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐轉身沿走廊朝閣樓樓梯門走去。

passages.original: She was glad, now, that she had put the child in the attic room.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家好高興把呢細路安置喺閣樓房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在很高興把這孩子安置在閣樓房間。

passages.original: Her idea at first had been to get her niece as far away as possible from herself, and at the same time place her where her childish heedlessness would not destroy valuable furnishings.
passages.vernacular: 佢最初嘅想法係,把佢嘅外甥女弄得離自己盡可能遠,同時把佢安置喺佢細路氣嘅粗心唔會破壞貴重家具嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她最初的想法是,把她的外甥女弄得離自己盡可能遠,同時把她安置在她孩子氣的粗心不會破壞貴重家具的地方。

passages.original: Now--with this evident strain of vanity showing thus early--it was all the more fortunate that the room planned for her was plain and sensible, thought Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 而家——既然呢種虛榮嘅氣息咁早就顯露——計劃畀佢嘅房間簡樸而實用,就更加慶幸喇,波莉小姐想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在——既然這種虛榮的氣息這麼早就顯露——計劃給她的房間簡樸而實用,就更加慶幸了,波莉小姐想。

passages.original: Eagerly Pollyanna's small feet pattered behind her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅小腳熱切地啪嗒啪嗒跟喺佢姨媽身後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的小腳熱切地啪嗒啪嗒跟在她姨媽身後。

passages.original: Still more eagerly her big blue eyes tried to look in all directions at once, that no thing of beauty or interest in this wonderful house might be passed unseen.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅藍大眼睛更熱切地試圖同時睇向所有方向,不放過呢座奇妙房子裡任何美麗或有趣嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的藍大眼睛更熱切地試圖同時看向所有方向,不放過這座奇妙房子裡任何美麗或有趣的東西。

passages.original: Most eagerly of all her mind turned to the wondrously exciting problem about to be solved: behind which of all these fascinating doors was waiting now her room--the dear, beautiful room full of curtains, rugs, and pictures, that was to be her very own?
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅思緒最熱切地轉向即將解決嘅奇妙而激動人心嘅問題:喺所有呢啲迷人嘅門中,佢嘅房間喺邊一扇後面等待——嗰個親愛嘅、美麗嘅、滿係窗簾、地毯同畫嘅房間,將完全屬於佢自己?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的思緒最熱切地轉向即將解決的奇妙而激動人心的問題:在所有這些迷人的門中,她的房間在哪一扇後面等待——那個親愛的、美麗的、滿是窗簾、地毯和畫的房間,將完全屬於她自己?

passages.original: Then, abruptly, her aunt opened a door and ascended another stairway.
passages.vernacular: 然後,突然,佢姨媽打開一扇門,上咗另一道樓梯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,突然,她姨媽打開一扇門,上了另一道樓梯。

passages.original: There was little to be seen here.
passages.vernacular: 呢度冇乜嘢可睇嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡沒什麼可看的。

passages.original: A bare wall rose on either side.
passages.vernacular: 兩邊都係光禿禿嘅牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩邊都是光禿禿的牆。

passages.original: At the top of the stairs, wide reaches of shadowy space led to far corners where the roof came almost down to the floor, and where were stacked innumerable trunks and boxes.
passages.vernacular: 樓梯頂上,陰暗寬闊嘅空間延伸到屋頂幾乎壓到地板嘅遠處角落,嗰度堆住無數嘅箱子同盒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓梯頂上,陰暗寬闊的空間延伸到屋頂幾乎壓到地板的遠處角落,那裡堆著無數的箱子和盒子。

passages.original: It was hot and stifling, too.
passages.vernacular: 又熱又悶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又熱又悶。

passages.original: Unconsciously Pollyanna lifted her head higher--it seemed so hard to breathe.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜無意識地把頭抬得更高——似乎呼吸咁困難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜無意識地把頭抬得更高——似乎呼吸那麼困難。

passages.original: Then she saw that her aunt had thrown open a door at the right.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢睇見佢姨媽推開咗右邊嘅一扇門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她看見她姨媽推開了右邊的一扇門。

passages.original: “There, Pollyanna, here is your room, and your trunk is here, I see.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,波麗安娜,呢個係你嘅房間,我睇你嘅箱子喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,波麗安娜,這是你的房間,我看你的箱子在這裡。

passages.original: Have you your key?”
passages.vernacular: 你有鑰匙嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有鑰匙嗎?」

passages.original: Pollyanna nodded dumbly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜無聲地點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜無聲地點點頭。

passages.original: Her eyes were a little wide and frightened.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛有點睜大,有點害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛有點睜大,有點害怕。

passages.original: Her aunt frowned.
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她姨媽皺眉。
