passages.original: “When I ask a question, Pollyanna, I prefer that you should answer aloud not merely with your head.”
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,我問問題時,我希望你出聲回答,而不只係用頭。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,我問問題時,我希望你出聲回答,而不只是用頭。」

passages.original: “Yes, Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: “Thank you; that is better.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝;咁樣好些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝;這樣好些。

passages.original: I believe you have everything that you need here,” she added, glancing at the well-filled towel rack and water pitcher.
passages.vernacular: 我相信你喺呢度有需要嘅一切,」佢補充講,瞥咗一眼放滿毛巾嘅毛巾架同水壺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我相信你在這裡有需要的一切,」她補充說,瞥了一眼放滿毛巾的毛巾架和水壺。

passages.original: “I will send Nancy up to help you unpack.
passages.vernacular: 「我會叫南希上嚟幫你開箱子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會叫南希上來幫你開箱子。

passages.original: Supper is at six o'clock,” she finished, as she left the room and swept down-stairs.
passages.vernacular: 晚飯六點鐘,」佢結束時,走出房間,窸窣下樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚飯六點鐘,」她結束時,走出房間,窸窣下樓。

passages.original: For a moment after she had gone Pollyanna stood quite still, looking after her.
passages.vernacular: 佢走後嘅片刻,波麗安娜完全靜止地站住,目送佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走後的片刻,波麗安娜完全靜止地站著,目送她。

passages.original: Then she turned her wide eyes to the bare wall, the bare floor, the bare windows.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把睜大嘅眼睛轉向光禿禿嘅牆、光禿禿嘅地板、光禿禿嘅窗子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她把睜大的眼睛轉向光禿禿的牆、光禿禿的地板、光禿禿的窗子。

passages.original: She turned them last to the little trunk that had stood not so long before in her own little room in the far-away Western home.
passages.vernacular: 佢最後把目光轉向嗰隻小箱子,不久前佢仲放喺遙遠西部家裡佢自己嘅小房間裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她最後把目光轉向那隻小箱子,不久前它還放在遙遠西部家裡她自己的小房間裡。

passages.original: The next moment she stumbled blindly toward it and fell on her knees at its side, covering her face with her hands.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢跌跌撞撞地走向佢,喺佢旁邊跪下,雙手捂住臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻她跌跌撞撞地走向它,在它旁邊跪下,雙手捂住臉。

passages.original: Nancy found her there when she came up a few minutes later.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後南希上嚟,發現咗佢喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後南希上來,發現了她在那裡。

passages.original: “There, there, you poor lamb,” she crooned, dropping to the floor and drawing the little girl into her arms.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,你呢可憐嘅小羊羔,」佢輕輕哼住,蹲到地上,把小女孩摟進懷裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,你這可憐的小羊羔,」她輕輕哼著,蹲到地上,把小女孩摟進懷裡。

passages.original: “I was just a-fearin!
passages.vernacular: 「我就怕——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就怕——

passages.original: I'd find you like this, like this.”
passages.vernacular: 會睇到你咁樣,咁樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會看到你這樣,這樣。」

passages.original: Pollyanna shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜搖搖頭。

passages.original: “But I'm bad and wicked, Nancy--awful wicked,” she sobbed.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我壞,我邪惡,南希——好邪惡,」佢抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我壞,我邪惡,南希——非常邪惡,」她抽泣著說。

passages.original: “I just can't make myself understand that God and the angels needed my father more than I did.”
passages.vernacular: 「我就係冇法讓自己明白,上帝同天使比我更需要我父親。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就是沒法讓自己明白,上帝和天使比我更需要我父親。」

passages.original: “No more they did, neither,” declared Nancy, stoutly.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋都不需要,」南希堅決地宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們也不需要,」南希堅決地宣稱。

passages.original: “Oh-h!--NANCY!”
The burning horror in Pollyanna's eyes dried the tears.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜眼裡燃燒嘅恐懼止住咗淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜眼裡燃燒的恐懼止住了淚水。

passages.original: Nancy gave a shamefaced smile and rubbed her own eyes vigorously.
passages.vernacular: 南希羞愧地笑咗笑,用力擦咗擦自己嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希羞愧地笑了笑,用力擦了擦自己的眼睛。

passages.original: “There, there, child, I didn't mean it, of course,” she cried briskly.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,細路,當然我唔係嗰個意思,」佢活潑地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,孩子,當然我不是那個意思,」她活潑地喊道。

passages.original: “Come, let's have your key and we'll get inside this trunk and take out your dresses in no time, no time.”
passages.vernacular: 「嚟,畀我鑰匙,我哋好快就能打開呢隻箱子,把你嘅裙子攞出嚟,好快,好快。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來,給我鑰匙,我們很快就能打開這隻箱子,把你的裙子拿出來,很快,很快。」

passages.original: Somewhat tearfully Pollyanna produced the key.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜含住淚攞出鑰匙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜含著淚拿出鑰匙。

passages.original: “There aren't very many there, anyway,” she faltered.
passages.vernacular: 「反正嗰度面冇好多,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「反正那裡面沒有很多,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “Then they're all the sooner unpacked,” declared Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰佢哋就更快拆完喇,」南希宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那它們就更快拆完了,」南希宣稱。

passages.original: Pollyanna gave a sudden radiant smile.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜突然露出燦爛嘅笑容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜突然露出燦爛的笑容。

passages.original: “That's so!
passages.vernacular: 「呢倒係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這倒是!

passages.original: I can be glad of that, can't I?” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 我可以為此高興,係唔係?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以為此高興,是不是?」她喊道。

passages.original: Nancy stared.
passages.vernacular: 南希瞪住眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希瞪著眼。

passages.original: “Why, of--course,” she answered a little uncertainly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當——然,」佢有點不確定地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當——然,」她有點不確定地回答。

passages.original: Nancy's capable hands made short work of unpacking the books, the patched undergarments, and the few pitifully unattractive dresses.
passages.vernacular: 南希能幹嘅手好快攞出書、打補丁嘅內衣同幾件可憐而不起眼嘅裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希能幹的手很快拿出書、打補丁的內衣和幾件可憐而不起眼的裙子。

passages.original: Pollyanna, smiling bravely now, flew about, hanging the dresses in the closet, stacking the books on the table, and putting away the undergarments in the bureau drawers.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜而家勇敢地微笑住,飛快地到處跑,把裙子掛進衣櫃,把書堆喺桌上,把內衣放進五斗櫃抽屜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜現在勇敢地微笑著,飛快地到處跑,把裙子掛進衣櫃,把書堆在桌上,把內衣放進五斗櫃抽屜。

passages.original: “I'm sure it--it's going to be a very nice room.
passages.vernacular: 「我確信佢——佢會係一個好好嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確信它——它會是一個很好的房間。

passages.original: Don't you think so?” she stammered, after a while.
passages.vernacular: 你不咁想嗎?」過咗一會兒,佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不這麼想嗎?」過了一會兒,她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: There was no answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: Nancy was very busy, apparently, with her head in the trunk.
passages.vernacular: 南希顯然好忙,頭埋喺箱子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希顯然非常忙,頭埋在箱子裡。

passages.original: Pollyanna, standing at the bureau, gazed a little wistfully at the bare wall above.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜站喺五斗櫃旁,有點渴望地凝視上方光禿禿嘅牆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜站在五斗櫃旁,有點渴望地凝視上方光禿禿的牆。

passages.original: “And I can be glad there isn't any looking-glass here, too, 'cause where there ISN'T any glass I can't see my freckles.”
passages.vernacular: 「我仲可以高興呢度都冇鏡子,因為冇鏡子,我就睇唔見我嘅雀斑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還可以高興這裡也沒有鏡子,因為沒有鏡子,我就看不見我的雀斑。」

passages.original: Nancy made a sudden queer little sound with her mouth--but when Pollyanna turned, her head was in the trunk again.
passages.vernacular: 南希嘅嘴突然發出一個古怪嘅小聲音——不過波麗安娜轉身時,佢嘅頭又喺箱子裡喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希的嘴突然發出一個古怪的小聲音——可是波麗安娜轉身時,她的頭又在箱子裡了。

passages.original: At one of the windows, a few minutes later, Pollyanna gave a glad cry and clapped her hands joyously.
passages.vernacular: 幾分鐘後,喺一扇窗前,波麗安娜發出一聲歡呼,高興地拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾分鐘後,在一扇窗前,波麗安娜發出一聲歡呼,高興地拍手。

passages.original: “Oh, Nancy, I hadn't seen this before,” she breathed.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,南希,我以前冇睇到呢個,」佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,南希,我以前沒看到這個,」她低聲說。

passages.original: “Look--'way off there, with those trees and the houses and that lovely church spire, and the river shining just like silver.
passages.vernacular: 「睇——遠處嗰度,有嗰啲樹同房子,同嗰座可愛嘅教堂尖頂,仲有像銀子一樣閃閃發光嘅河。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看——遠處那裡,有那些樹和房子,和那座可愛的教堂尖頂,還有像銀子一樣閃閃發光的河。

passages.original: Why, Nancy, there doesn't anybody need any pictures with that to look at.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,南希,有嗰個可睇,邊個都不需要乜嘢畫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,南希,有那個可看,誰也不需要什麼畫了。

passages.original: Oh, I'm so glad now she let me have this room!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我而家太高興佢讓我住呢個房間喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我現在太高興她讓我住這個房間了!」

passages.original: To Pollyanna's surprise and dismay, Nancy burst into tears.
passages.vernacular: 令波麗安娜食驚同沮喪嘅係,南希突然哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令波麗安娜吃驚和沮喪的是,南希突然哭了。

passages.original: Pollyanna hurriedly crossed to her side.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜匆忙走到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜匆忙走到她身邊。

passages.original: “Why, Nancy, Nancy--what is it?” she cried; then, fearfully: “This wasn't--YOUR room, was it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,南希,南希——點喇?」佢喊道;然後害怕地講:「呢唔係——你嘅房間,係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,南希,南希——怎麼了?」她喊道;然後害怕地說:「這不是——你的房間,是嗎?」

passages.original: “My room!” stormed Nancy, hotly, choking back the tears.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅房間!」南希激烈地講,哽住眼淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的房間!」南希激烈地說,哽住眼淚。

passages.original: “If you ain't a little angel straight from Heaven, and if some folks don't eat dirt before--Oh, land! there's her bell!”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你唔係從天堂直接下嚟嘅小天使,如果有些人不喺——哎呀!佢嘅鈴響喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你不是從天堂直接下來的小天使,如果有些人不在——哎呀!她的鈴響了!」

passages.original: After which amazing speech, Nancy sprang to her feet, dashed out of the room, and went clattering down the stairs.
passages.vernacular: 講完呢番驚人嘅話,南希跳起嚟,衝出房間,嘩啦嘩啦地跑下樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說完這番驚人的話,南希跳起來,衝出房間,嘩啦嘩啦地跑下樓。

passages.original: Left alone, Pollyanna went back to her “picture,” as she mentally designated the beautiful view from the window.
passages.vernacular: 獨自留下嘅波麗安娜回到佢嘅「畫」前,佢喺心裡咁樣稱呼窗外嘅美景。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獨自留下的波麗安娜回到她的「畫」前,她在心裡這樣稱呼窗外的美景。

passages.original: After a time she touched the sash tentatively.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,佢試探地碰咗碰窗框。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,她試探地碰了碰窗框。

passages.original: It seemed as if no longer could she endure the stifling heat.
passages.vernacular: 似乎佢再都忍受不了悶熱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎她再也忍受不了悶熱。

passages.original: To her joy the sash moved under her fingers.
passages.vernacular: 令佢高興嘅係,窗框喺佢嘅手指下動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令她高興的是,窗框在她的手指下動了。

passages.original: The next moment the window was wide open, and Pollyanna was leaning far out, drinking in the fresh, sweet air.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻窗子大開,波麗安娜探出身子好遠,貪婪地吸住清新甜美嘅空氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻窗子大開,波麗安娜探出身子很遠,貪婪地吸著清新甜美的空氣。

passages.original: She ran then to the other window.
passages.vernacular: 佢然後跑到另一扇窗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她然後跑到另一扇窗。

passages.original: That, too, soon flew up under her eager hands.
passages.vernacular: 嗰扇都好快喺佢熱切嘅手下被推咗上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那扇也很快在她熱切的手下被推了上去。

passages.original: A big fly swept past her nose, and buzzed noisily about the room.
passages.vernacular: 一隻大蒼蠅從佢鼻子旁掠過,喺房間裡嗡嗡亂飛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻大蒼蠅從她鼻子旁掠過,在房間裡嗡嗡亂飛。

passages.original: Then another came, and another; but Pollyanna paid no heed.
passages.vernacular: 然後又嚟一隻,又一隻;但波麗安娜冇理會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後又來一隻,又一隻;但波麗安娜沒有理會。

passages.original: Pollyanna had made a wonderful discovery--against this window a huge tree flung great branches.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜有咗一個奇妙嘅發現——呢扇窗外,一棵巨大嘅樹伸出大樹枝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜有了一個奇妙的發現——這扇窗外,一棵巨大的樹伸出大樹枝。

passages.original: To Pollyanna they looked like arms outstretched, inviting her.
passages.vernacular: 喺波麗安娜睇來,佢哋像伸出嘅手臂,邀請佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在波麗安娜看來,它們像伸出的手臂,邀請她。

passages.original: Suddenly she laughed aloud.
passages.vernacular: 突然佢放聲大笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然她放聲大笑。

passages.original: “I believe I can do it,” she chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 「我相信我能做到,」佢咯咯笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我相信我能做到,」她咯咯笑著說。

passages.original: The next moment she had climbed nimbly to the window ledge.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢已敏捷地爬上窗台。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻她已敏捷地爬上窗台。

passages.original: From there it was an easy matter to step to the nearest tree-branch.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰度走到最近嘅樹枝上係件容易嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那裡走到最近的樹枝上是件容易的事。

passages.original: Then, clinging like a monkey, she swung herself from limb to limb until the lowest branch was reached.
passages.vernacular: 然後,像猴子一樣攀住,佢從一根樹枝盪到另一根,直到到達最低嘅樹枝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,像猴子一樣攀著,她從一根樹枝盪到另一根,直到到達最低的樹枝。

passages.original: The drop to the ground was--even for Pollyanna, who was used to climbing trees--a little fearsome.
passages.vernacular: 落到地上——即使對習慣爬樹嘅波麗安娜來講——都有點嚇人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 落到地上——即使對習慣爬樹的波麗安娜來說——也有點嚇人。

passages.original: She took it, however, with bated breath, swinging from her strong little arms, and landing on all fours in the soft grass.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢屏住呼吸做喇,用有力嘅小胳膊盪住,四肢住地落喺柔軟嘅草地上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她屏住呼吸做了,用有力的小胳膊盪著,四肢著地落在柔軟的草地上。

passages.original: Then she picked herself up and looked eagerly about her.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢爬起嚟,熱切地四處張望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她爬起來,熱切地四處張望。

passages.original: She was at the back of the house.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺房子後面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在房子後面。

passages.original: Before her lay a garden in which a bent old man was working.
passages.vernacular: 佢面前係一個花園,一個彎腰嘅老人正在嗰度幹活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她面前是一個花園,一個彎腰的老人正在那裡幹活。

passages.original: Beyond the garden a little path through an open field led up a steep hill, at the top of which a lone pine tree stood on guard beside the huge rock.
passages.vernacular: 花園嗰邊,一條穿過空曠田野嘅小路通向一座陡坡,坡頂有一棵孤零零嘅松樹守喺巨大嘅岩石旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 花園那邊,一條穿過空曠田野的小路通向一座陡坡,坡頂有一棵孤零零的松樹守在巨大的岩石旁。

passages.original: To Pollyanna, at the moment, there seemed to be just one place in the world worth being in--the top of that big rock.
passages.vernacular: 對波麗安娜來講,此刻世界上似乎只有一個值得待嘅地方——嗰塊大岩石嘅頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對波麗安娜來說,此刻世界上似乎只有一個值得待的地方——那塊大岩石的頂上。

passages.original: With a run and a skilful turn, Pollyanna skipped by the bent old man, threaded her way between the orderly rows of green growing things, and--a little out of breath--reached the path that ran through the open field.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜奔跑住,巧妙一轉,蹦跳住經過彎腰嘅老人,喺整齊嘅綠色生長物行列之間穿行,然後——有點上氣不接下氣地——到咗穿過空曠田野嘅小路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜奔跑著,巧妙一轉,蹦跳著經過彎腰的老人,在整齊的綠色生長物行列之間穿行,然後——有點上氣不接下氣地——到了穿過空曠田野的小路。

passages.original: Then, determinedly, she began to climb.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢堅定地開始攀爬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,她堅定地開始攀爬。

passages.original: Already, however, she was thinking what a long, long way off that rock must be, when back at the window it had looked so near!
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢已經喺想,嗰塊岩石一定遠得好,好遠,而從窗口睇時佢似乎咁近!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,她已經在想,那塊岩石一定遠得很,很遠,而從窗口看時它似乎那麼近!

passages.original: Fifteen minutes later the great clock in the hallway of the Harrington homestead struck six.
passages.vernacular: 十五分鐘後,哈林頓祖宅走廊裡嘅大鐘敲咗六點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十五分鐘後,哈林頓祖宅走廊裡的大鐘敲了六點。

passages.original: At precisely the last stroke Nancy sounded the bell for supper.
passages.vernacular: 喺最後一聲鐘響嘅同時,南希敲響咗晚飯鈴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在最後一聲鐘響的同時,南希敲響了晚飯鈴。

passages.original: One, two, three minutes passed.
passages.vernacular: 一分鐘,兩分鐘,三分鐘過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一分鐘,兩分鐘,三分鐘過去了。

passages.original: Miss Polly frowned and tapped the floor with her slipper.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺眉,用拖鞋輕敲地板。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺眉,用拖鞋輕敲地板。

passages.original: A little jerkily she rose to her feet, went into the hall, and looked up-stairs, plainly impatient.
passages.vernacular: 佢有點急促地站起嚟,走進走廊,向樓上睇,顯然不耐煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她有點急促地站起來,走進走廊,向樓上看,顯然不耐煩。

passages.original: For a minute she listened intently; then she turned and swept into the dining room.
passages.vernacular: 佢專注地聽咗一分鐘;然後轉身走進餐廳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她專注地聽了一分鐘;然後轉身走進餐廳。

passages.original: “Nancy,” she said with decision, as soon as the little serving-maid appeared; “my niece is late.
passages.vernacular: 「南希,」小女傭一出現,佢就果斷地講;「我嘅外甥女遲到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,」小女傭一出現,她就果斷地說;「我的外甥女遲到了。

passages.original: No, you need not call her,” she added severely, as Nancy made a move toward the hall door.
passages.vernacular: 不,你唔使去叫佢,」南希朝走廊門動咗一下時,佢嚴厲地補充。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,你不必去叫她,」南希朝走廊門動了一下時,她嚴厲地補充。

passages.original: “I told her what time supper was, and now she will have to suffer the consequences.
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴過佢晚飯係乜嘢時間,而家佢得承擔後果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴過她晚飯是什麼時間,現在她得承擔後果。

passages.original: She may as well begin at once to learn to be punctual.
passages.vernacular: 佢不妨即刻開始學守時。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不妨立刻開始學守時。

passages.original: When she comes down she may have bread and milk in the kitchen.”
passages.vernacular: 佢下嚟時可以喺廚房食麵包同牛奶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她下來時可以在廚房吃麵包和牛奶。」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人。」

passages.original: It was well, perhaps, that Miss Polly did not happen to be looking at Nancy's face just then.
passages.vernacular: 或者幸好波莉小姐嗰時冇碰巧睇南希嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許幸好波莉小姐那時沒有碰巧看南希的臉。

passages.original: At the earliest possible moment after supper, Nancy crept up the back stairs and thence to the attic room.
passages.vernacular: 晚飯後,南希一有可能嘅最早時刻,就爬上後樓梯,然後到閣樓房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚飯後,南希一有可能的最早時刻,就爬上後樓梯,然後到閣樓房間。

passages.original: “Bread and milk, indeed!--and when the poor lamb hain't only just cried herself to sleep,” she was muttering fiercely, as she softly pushed open the door.
passages.vernacular: 「麵包同牛奶,真係嘅!——而嗰可憐嘅小羊羔才剛哭住瞓住,」佢輕輕推開門時,凶狠地嘀咕住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「麵包和牛奶,真是的!——而那可憐的小羊羔才剛哭著睡著,」她輕輕推開門時,凶狠地嘀咕著。

passages.original: The next moment she gave a frightened cry.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻,佢驚恐地叫咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻,她驚恐地叫了一聲。

passages.original: “Where are you?
passages.vernacular: 「你喺邊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你在哪?

passages.original: Where've you gone?
passages.vernacular: 你去邊兒喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去哪兒了?

passages.original: Where HAVE you gone?” she panted, looking in the closet, under the bed, and even in the trunk and down the water pitcher.
passages.vernacular: 你去邊兒喇?」佢喘住氣,找遍衣櫃、床下,甚至箱子裡同水壺裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你去哪兒了?」她喘著氣,找遍衣櫃、床下,甚至箱子裡和水壺裡。

passages.original: Then she flew down-stairs and out to Old Tom in the garden.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢飛下樓,出去找花園裡嘅老湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她飛下樓,出去找花園裡的老湯姆。

passages.original: “Mr. Tom, Mr. Tom, that blessed child's gone,” she wailed.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆先生,湯姆先生,嗰可愛嘅細路唔見喇,」佢哀號。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆先生,湯姆先生,那可愛的孩子不見了,」她哀號。

passages.original: “She's vanished right up into Heaven where she come from, poor lamb--and me told ter give her bread and milk in the kitchen--her what's eatin' angel food this minute, I'll warrant, I'll warrant!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢直接消失到天堂去喇,佢嚟嘅地方,可憐嘅小羊羔——我仲被叫去喺廚房畀佢麵包同牛奶——佢呢會兒大概喺食天使嘅食物,我敢講,我敢講!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她直接消失到天堂去了,她來的地方,可憐的小羊羔——我還被叫去在廚房給她麵包和牛奶——她這會兒大概在吃天使的食物,我敢說,我敢說!」

passages.original: The old man straightened up.
passages.vernacular: 老人直起腰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人直起腰。

passages.original: “Gone?
passages.vernacular: 「唔見喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不見了?

passages.original: Heaven?” he repeated stupidly, unconsciously sweeping the brilliant sunset sky with his gaze.
passages.vernacular: 天堂?」佢傻乎乎地重複,無意識地用目光掃咗掃輝煌嘅日落天空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天堂?」他傻乎乎地重複,無意識地用目光掃了掃輝煌的日落天空。

passages.original: He stopped, stared a moment intently, then turned with a slow grin.
passages.vernacular: 佢停住喇,專注地凝視咗片刻,然後慢慢咧嘴笑住轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他停住了,專注地凝視了片刻,然後慢慢咧嘴笑著轉過身。

passages.original: “Well, Nancy, it do look like as if she'd tried ter get as nigh Heaven as she could, and that's a fact,” he agreed, pointing with a crooked finger to where, sharply outlined against the reddening sky, a slender, wind-blown figure was poised on top of a huge rock.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,南希,睇起嚟佢確實係想盡量靠近天堂,呢個係真嘅,」佢同意道,用彎曲嘅手指指住一個地方,喺漸紅嘅天空襯托下,有一個細長嘅、被風吹拂嘅身影,輪廓分明地站喺一塊巨石頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,南希,看起來她確實是想盡量靠近天堂,這是真的,」他同意道,用彎曲的手指指著一個地方,在漸紅的天空襯托下,有一個細長的、被風吹拂的身影,輪廓分明地站在一塊巨石頂上。

passages.original: “Well, she ain't goin' ter Heaven that way ter-night--not if I has my say,” declared Nancy, doggedly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,今晚佢唔能夠嗰樣去天堂——只要我講咗算,」南希固執地宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,今晚她不能那樣去天堂——只要我說了算,」南希固執地宣稱。

passages.original: “If the mistress asks, tell her I ain't furgettin' the dishes, but I gone on a stroll,” she flung back over her shoulder, as she sped toward the path that led through the open field.
passages.vernacular: 「如果女主人問,告訴佢我冇忘咗洗碗,我只係出去散步喇,」佢頭都不回地扔下呢句話,朝穿過空曠田野嘅小路飛奔而去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果女主人問,告訴她我沒忘了洗碗,我只是出去散步了,」她頭也不回地扔下這句話,朝穿過空曠田野的小路飛奔而去。

chapters.title: Ch. V The Game 第五章:遊戲

passages.original: CH “For the land's sake, Miss Pollyanna, what a scare you did give me,” panted Nancy, hurrying up to the big rock, down which Pollyanna had just regretfully slid.
passages.vernacular: 「睇喺老天嘅份上,波麗安娜小姐,你真把我嚇壞喇,」南希喘住氣,匆忙跑到大岩石旁,波麗安娜啱啱不情願地從上面滑下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看在老天的份上,波麗安娜小姐,你真把我嚇壞了,」南希喘著氣,匆忙跑到大岩石旁,波麗安娜剛剛不情願地從上面滑下來。

passages.original: “Scare?
passages.vernacular: 「嚇壞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嚇壞?

passages.original: Oh, I'm so sorry; but you mustn't, really, ever get scared about me, Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我好抱歉;不過你千萬別為我擔心,南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我很抱歉;不過你千萬別為我擔心,南希。

passages.original: Father and the Ladies' Aid used to do it, too, till they found I always came back all right.”
passages.vernacular: 爸爸同婦女互助會都曾經咁樣,直到佢哋發現我總是平安回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸和婦女互助會也曾經這樣,直到他們發現我總是平安回來。」

passages.original: “But I didn't even know you'd went,” cried Nancy, tucking the little girl's hand under her arm and hurrying her down the hill.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我連你走咗都唔知道,」南希喊道,把小女孩嘅手夾喺胳膊下,匆匆領佢下山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我連你走了都不知道,」南希喊道,把小女孩的手夾在胳膊下,匆匆領她下山。

passages.original: “I didn't see you go, and nobody didn't.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇睇見你走,都冇人睇見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒看見你走,也沒人看見。

passages.original: I guess you flew right up through the roof; I do, I do.”
passages.vernacular: 我想你係直接穿過屋頂飛出去嘅;我想係,我想係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你是直接穿過屋頂飛出去的;我想是,我想是。」

passages.original: Pollyanna skipped gleefully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜歡快地蹦跳住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜歡快地蹦跳著。

passages.original: “I did, 'most--only I flew down instead of up.
passages.vernacular: 「差不多,——只不過我係往下飛,而唔係往上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「差不多,——只不過我是往下飛,而不是往上。

passages.original: I came down the tree.”
passages.vernacular: 我係順住樹爬下嚟嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是順著樹爬下來的。」

passages.original: Nancy stopped short.
passages.vernacular: 南希猛地站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希猛地站住。

passages.original: “You did--what?”
“Came down the tree, outside my window.”
passages.vernacular: 「順住樹爬下嚟,喺我窗戶外面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「順著樹爬下來,在我窗戶外面。」

passages.original: “My stars and stockings!” gasped Nancy, hurrying on again.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅天呀!」南希倒抽一口氣,又匆匆走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的天哪!」南希倒抽一口氣,又匆匆走。

passages.original: “I'd like ter know what yer aunt would say ter that!”
passages.vernacular: 「我倒想知道你姨媽聽咗會講乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我倒想知道你姨媽聽了會說什麼!」

passages.original: “Would you?
passages.vernacular: 「你想知道嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想知道嗎?

passages.original: Well, I'll tell her, then, so you can find out,” promised the little girl, cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 嗰我告訴佢,你就能知道喇,」小女孩愉快地許諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我告訴她,你就能知道了,」小女孩愉快地許諾。

passages.original: “Mercy!” gasped Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」南希倒抽冷氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」南希倒抽冷氣。

passages.original: “No--no!”
“Why, you don't mean she'd CARE!” cried Pollyanna, plainly disturbed.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,你唔會係講佢在乎吧!」波麗安娜喊道,顯然不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,你不會是說她在乎吧!」波麗安娜喊道,顯然不安。

passages.original: “No--er--yes--well, never mind.
passages.vernacular: 「不——呃——係——嗯,算喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——呃——是——嗯,算了。

passages.original: I--I ain't so very particular about knowin' what she'd say, truly,” stammered Nancy, determined to keep one scolding from Pollyanna, if nothing more.
passages.vernacular: 我——我並唔係好想知道佢會講乜嘢,真嘅,」南希結結巴巴地講,決心至少要讓波麗安娜免受一頓責罵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——我並不是很想知道她會說什麼,真的,」南希結結巴巴地說,決心至少要讓波麗安娜免受一頓責罵。

passages.original: “But, say, we better hurry.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,聽住,我哋最好快點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,聽著,我們最好快點。

passages.original: I've got ter get them dishes done, ye know.”
passages.vernacular: 我得把嗰啲碗洗完,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得把那些碗洗完,你知道。」

passages.original: “I'll help,” promised Pollyanna, promptly.
passages.vernacular: 「我嚟幫忙,」波麗安娜即刻許諾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我來幫忙,」波麗安娜立刻許諾。

passages.original: “Oh, Miss Pollyanna!” demurred Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波麗安娜小姐!」南希推辭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波麗安娜小姐!」南希推辭說。

passages.original: For a moment there was silence.
passages.vernacular: 有咁片刻,冇人講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼片刻,沒有人說話。

passages.original: The sky was darkening fast.
passages.vernacular: 天空迅速暗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天空迅速暗下來。

passages.original: Pollyanna took a firmer hold of her friend's arm.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜更緊地抓住朋友嘅胳膊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜更緊地抓住朋友的胳膊。

passages.original: “I reckon I'm glad, after all, that you DID get scared--a little, 'cause then you came after me,” she shivered.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我定係高興你被嚇到喇——啲,因為嗰樣你就嚟找我喇,」佢打住寒顫講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我還是高興你被嚇到了——一點,因為那樣你就來找我了,」她打著寒顫說。

passages.original: “Poor little lamb!
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅小羊羔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的小羊羔!

passages.original: And you must be hungry, too.
passages.vernacular: 你一定都餓喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一定也餓了。

passages.original: I--I'm afraid you'll have ter have bread and milk in the kitchen with me.
passages.vernacular: 我——我怕你得喺廚房跟我一起食麵包同牛奶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——我怕你得在廚房跟我一起吃麵包和牛奶。

passages.original: Yer aunt didn't like it--because you didn't come down ter supper, ye know.”
passages.vernacular: 你姨媽不高興——因為你冇下嚟食晚飯,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你姨媽不高興——因為你沒下來吃晚飯,你知道。」

passages.original: “But I couldn't.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我不能。

passages.original: I was up here.”
passages.vernacular: 我喺上面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在上面。」

passages.original: “Yes; but--she didn't know that, you see!” observed Nancy, dryly, stifling a chuckle.
passages.vernacular: 「係,不過——佢唔知道,你睇!」南希乾巴巴地講,忍住一聲輕笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,可是——她不知道,你看!」南希乾巴巴地說,忍住一聲輕笑。

passages.original: “I'm sorry about the bread and milk; I am, I am.”
passages.vernacular: 「我為麵包同牛奶難過;我難過,我難過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為麵包和牛奶難過;我難過,我難過。」

passages.original: “Oh, I'm not.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我不難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我不難過。

passages.original: I'm glad.”
passages.vernacular: 我高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高興。」

passages.original: “Glad!
passages.vernacular: 「高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興!

passages.original: Why?”
passages.vernacular: 點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, I like bread and milk, and I'd like to eat with you.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我鍾意麵包同牛奶,我都願意跟你一起食。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我喜歡麵包和牛奶,我也願意跟你一起吃。

passages.original: I don't see any trouble about being glad about that.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇不出為呢個高興有乜嘢困難。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看不出為這個高興有什麼困難。」

passages.original: “You don't seem ter see any trouble bein' glad about everythin',” retorted Nancy, choking a little over her remembrance of Pollyanna's brave attempts to like the bare little attic room.
passages.vernacular: 「你好像睇不出點解事高興有乜嘢困難,」南希反駁,想起波麗安娜勇敢地試圖鍾意嗰個光禿禿嘅小閣樓,聲音有點哽咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你好像看不出為什麼事高興有什麼困難,」南希反駁,想起波麗安娜勇敢地試圖喜歡那個光禿禿的小閣樓,聲音有點哽咽。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed softly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜輕輕笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜輕輕笑了。

passages.original: “Well, that's the game, you know, anyway.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰個就係呢個遊戲,你知道嘅,反正。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那就是這個遊戲,你知道的,反正。」

passages.original: “The--GAME?”
“Yes; the 'just being glad' game.”
passages.vernacular: 「係;『只要高興』嘅遊戲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是;『只要高興』的遊戲。」

passages.original: “Whatever in the world are you talkin' about?”
passages.vernacular: 「你到底喺講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你到底在說什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, it's a game.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,呢個係個遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,這是個遊戲。

passages.original: Father told it to me, and it's lovely,” rejoined Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸告訴我嘅,可好玩喇,」波麗安娜回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸告訴我的,可好玩了,」波麗安娜回答。

passages.original: “We've played it always, ever since I was a little, little girl.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋一直玩佢,從我係小小嘅小女孩嘅時候起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們一直玩它,從我是小小的小女孩的時候起。

passages.original: I told the Ladies' Aid, and they played it--some of them.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴咗婦女互助會,佢哋都玩喇——其中啲人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴了婦女互助會,他們也玩了——其中一些人。」

passages.original: “What is it?
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼?

passages.original: I ain't much on games, though.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我不太會玩遊戲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我不太會玩遊戲。」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed again, but she sighed, too; and in the gathering twilight her face looked thin and wistful.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜又笑喇,但佢都嘆咗氣;喺漸暗嘅暮色中,佢嘅臉顯得消瘦而渴望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜又笑了,但她也嘆了氣;在漸暗的暮色中,她的臉顯得消瘦而渴望。

passages.original: “Why, we began it on some crutches that came in a missionary barrel.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我哋係從傳教士捐贈桶裡嚟嘅一副拐杖開始嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我們是從傳教士捐贈桶裡來的一副拐杖開始的。」

passages.original: “CRUTCHES!”
passages.vernacular: 「拐杖!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「拐杖!」

passages.original: “Yes.
You see I'd wanted a doll, and father had written them so; but when the barrel came the lady wrote that there hadn't any dolls come in, but the little crutches had.
passages.vernacular: 你睇我想要一個洋娃娃,爸爸咁寫信畀佢哋喇;不過桶嚟嘅時候,嗰位女士寫信講冇洋娃娃,但小拐杖嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看我想要一個洋娃娃,爸爸這麼寫信給他們了;可是桶來的時候,那位女士寫信說沒有洋娃娃,但小拐杖來了。

passages.original: So she sent 'em along as they might come in handy for some child, sometime.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢把佢哋送嚟,因為佢哋或者乜嘢時候對邊個細路有用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她把它們送來,因為它們也許什麼時候對哪個孩子有用。

passages.original: And that's when we began it.”
passages.vernacular: 就係嗰時我哋開始嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是那時我們開始的。」

passages.original: “Well, I must say I can't see any game about that, about that,” declared Nancy, almost irritably.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我得講我睇不出嗰有乜嘢遊戲,乜嘢遊戲,」南希幾乎煩躁地宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我得說我看不出那有什麼遊戲,什麼遊戲,」南希幾乎煩躁地宣稱。

passages.original: “Oh, yes; the game was to just find something about everything to be glad about--no matter what 'twas,” rejoined Pollyanna, earnestly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅;遊戲就係對每件事都找出啲值得高興嘅地方——不管係乜嘢,」波麗安娜誠懇地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的;遊戲就是對每件事都找出一點值得高興的地方——不管是什麼,」波麗安娜誠懇地回答。

passages.original: “And we began right then--on the crutches.”
passages.vernacular: 「我哋就從嗰時開始——從拐杖開始。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們就從那時開始——從拐杖開始。」

passages.original: “Well, goodness me!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!

passages.original: I can't see anythin' ter be glad about--gettin' a pair of crutches when you wanted a doll!”
passages.vernacular: 我睇不出有乜嘢可高興嘅——你想要洋娃娃卻得到一副拐杖!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看不出有什麼可高興的——你想要洋娃娃卻得到一副拐杖!」

passages.original: Pollyanna clapped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜拍手。

passages.original: “There is--there is,” she crowed.
passages.vernacular: 「有嘅——有嘅,」佢得意地叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有的——有的,」她得意地叫。

passages.original: “But I couldn't see it, either, Nancy, at first,” she added, with quick honesty.
passages.vernacular: 「不過一開始我都睇不出嚟,南希,」佢以迅速嘅誠實補充講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過一開始我也看不出來,南希,」她以迅速的誠實補充說。

passages.original: “Father had to tell it to me.”
passages.vernacular: 「係爸爸告訴我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是爸爸告訴我的。」

passages.original: “Well, then, suppose YOU tell ME,” almost snapped Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,咁,你告訴我吧,」南希幾乎厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那麼,你告訴我吧,」南希幾乎厲聲說。

passages.original: “Goosey!
passages.vernacular: 「傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「傻瓜!

passages.original: Why, just be glad because you don't--NEED--'EM!” exulted Pollyanna, triumphantly.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,就係因為你不——需要——佢哋而高興!」波麗安娜得意洋洋地歡呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,就是因為你不——需要——它們而高興!」波麗安娜得意洋洋地歡呼。

passages.original: “You see it's just as easy--when you know how!”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇呢個就係咁容易——只要你知道方法!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看這就是這麼容易——只要你知道方法!」

passages.original: “Well, of all the queer doin's!” breathed Nancy, regarding Pollyanna with almost fearful eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真係怪事!」南希低聲講,幾乎帶住害怕嘅眼神睇住波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真是怪事!」南希低聲說,幾乎帶著害怕的眼神看著波麗安娜。

passages.original: “Oh, but it isn't queer--it's lovely,” maintained Pollyanna enthusiastically.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,但呢不奇怪——呢個好好,」波麗安娜熱情地堅持。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,但這不奇怪——這很好,」波麗安娜熱情地堅持。

passages.original: “And we've played it ever since.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋從嗰以後一直喺玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們從那以後一直在玩。

passages.original: And the harder 'tis, the more fun 'tis to get 'em out; only--only sometimes it's almost too hard--like when your father goes to Heaven, and there isn't anybody but a Ladies' Aid left.”
passages.vernacular: 越難,把佢哋找出嚟就越好玩;只係——只係有時幾乎太難喇——比如你爸爸去咗天堂,剩下嘅除咗婦女互助會邊個都冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 越難,把它們找出來就越好玩;只是——只是有時幾乎太難了——比如你爸爸去了天堂,剩下的除了婦女互助會誰也沒有。」

passages.original: “Yes, or when you're put in a snippy little room 'way at the top of the house with nothin' in it,” growled Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,或者你被放喺房子最頂上一間小氣嘅小房間,裡面乜嘢都冇,」南希咆哮道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,或者你被放在房子最頂上一間小氣的小房間,裡面什麼也沒有,」南希咆哮道。

passages.original: Pollyanna sighed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜嘆氣。

passages.original: “That was a hard one, at first,” she admitted, “specially when I was so kind of lonesome.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係個難嘅,起初,」佢承認,「尤其係我當時咁孤單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是個難的,起初,」她承認,「尤其是我當時那麼孤單。

passages.original: I just didn't feel like playing the game, anyway, and I HAD been wanting pretty things, so!
passages.vernacular: 我就係唔想玩呢個遊戲,我確實一直想要漂亮嘢,所以!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是不想玩這個遊戲,我確實一直想要漂亮東西,所以!

passages.original: Then I happened to think how I hated to see my freckles in the looking-glass, and I saw that lovely picture out the window, too; so then I knew I'd found the things to be glad about.
passages.vernacular: 然後我碰巧想到我多討厭喺鏡子裡睇我嘅雀斑,而且我都從窗口睇見咗嗰幅可愛嘅畫;所以我就知道我找到咗值得高興嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我碰巧想到我多討厭在鏡子裡看我的雀斑,而且我也從窗口看見了那幅可愛的畫;所以我就知道我找到了值得高興的事。

passages.original: You see, when you're hunting for the glad things, you sort of forget the other kind--like the doll you wanted, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,當你喺尋找高興嘅事時,你就有點忘咗另一種——就像你想要嘅洋娃娃,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,當你在尋找高興的事時,你就有點忘了另一種——就像你想要的洋娃娃,你知道。」

passages.original: “Humph!” choked Nancy, trying to swallow the lump in her throat.
passages.vernacular: 「哼!」南希哽咽住,試住嚥下喉嚨裡嘅硬塊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼!」南希哽咽著,試著嚥下喉嚨裡的硬塊。

passages.original: “Most generally it doesn't take so long,” sighed Pollyanna; “and lots of times now I just think of them WITHOUT thinking, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「通常不需要咁久,」波麗安娜嘆氣;「而家好多時候我連想都唔想就想到佢哋喇,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「通常不需要那麼久,」波麗安娜嘆氣;「現在很多時候我連想都不想就想到它們了,你知道。

passages.original: I've got so used to playing it.
passages.vernacular: 我玩得太習慣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我玩得太習慣了。

passages.original: It's a lovely game.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個好玩嘅遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個好玩的遊戲。

passages.original: F-father and I used to like it so much,” she faltered.
passages.vernacular: 爸——爸爸同我過去咁鍾意佢,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸——爸爸和我過去那麼喜歡它,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “I suppose, though, it--it'll be a little harder now, as long as I haven't anybody to play it with.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,我想,佢——而家會難啲,因為我冇人陪我玩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,我想,它——現在會難一點,因為我沒有人陪我玩了。

passages.original: Maybe Aunt Polly will play it, though,” she added, as an after-thought.
passages.vernacular: 或者波莉姨媽會玩,」佢又補充,像係事後想起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許波莉姨媽會玩,」她又補充,像是事後想起。

passages.original: “My stars and stockings!--HER!” breathed Nancy, behind her teeth.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅天呀!——佢!」南希咬住牙低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的天哪!——她!」南希咬著牙低聲說。

passages.original: Then, aloud, she said doggedly: “See here, Miss Pollyanna, I ain't sayin' that I'll play it very well, and I ain't sayin' that I know how, anyway; but I'll play it with ye, after a fashion--I just will, I will!”
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢大聲固執地講:「聽住,波麗安娜小姐,我不講我會玩得好好,我都不講我知道點玩;不過我會跟你玩,以某種方式——我就會,我會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,她大聲固執地說:「聽著,波麗安娜小姐,我不說我會玩得很好,我也不說我知道怎麼玩;不過我會跟你玩,以某種方式——我就會,我會!」

passages.original: “Oh, Nancy!” exulted Pollyanna, giving her a rapturous hug.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,南希!」波麗安娜歡呼,狂喜地擁抱佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,南希!」波麗安娜歡呼,狂喜地擁抱她。

passages.original: “That'll be splendid!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰太棒喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那太棒了!

passages.original: Won't we have fun?”
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔會玩得好開心嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不會玩得很開心嗎?」

passages.original: “Er--maybe,” conceded Nancy, in open doubt.
passages.vernacular: 「呃——或者,」南希公開懷疑地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「呃——也許,」南希公開懷疑地承認。

passages.original: “But you mustn't count too much on me, ye know.
passages.vernacular: 「不過你別太指望我,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過你別太指望我,你知道。

passages.original: I never was no case fur games, but I'm a-goin' ter make a most awful old try on this one.
passages.vernacular: 我從來唔係玩遊戲嘅料,不過我要對呢個盡最大嘅努力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從來不是玩遊戲的料,不過我要對這個盡最大的努力。

passages.original: You're goin' ter have some one ter play it with, anyhow,” she finished, as they entered the kitchen together.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,你會有人陪你玩嘅,」佢結束時,佢哋一起走進廚房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,你會有人陪你玩的,」她結束時,她們一起走進廚房。

passages.original: Pollyanna ate her bread and milk with good appetite; then, at Nancy's suggestion, she went into the sitting room, where her aunt sat reading.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜胃口好好地食咗佢嘅麵包同牛奶;然後,喺南希嘅建議下,佢走進起居室,佢姨媽坐喺嗰度睇書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜胃口很好地吃了她的麵包和牛奶;然後,在南希的建議下,她走進起居室,她姨媽坐在那裡看書。

passages.original: Miss Polly looked up coldly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐冷冷地抬起頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐冷冷地抬起頭。

passages.original: “Have you had your supper, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 「你食過晚飯咗嗎,波麗安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你吃過晚飯了嗎,波麗安娜?」

passages.original: “Yes, Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「食喇,波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吃了,波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: “I'm very sorry, Pollyanna, to have been obliged so soon to send you into the kitchen to eat bread and milk.”
passages.vernacular: 「我好遺憾,波麗安娜,咁快就唔得不叫你到廚房食麵包同牛奶。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很遺憾,波麗安娜,這麼快就不得不叫你到廚房吃麵包和牛奶。」

passages.original: “But I was real glad you did it, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我真嘅好高興你咁做,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我真的很高興你這麼做,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I like bread and milk, and Nancy, too.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意麵包同牛奶,都鍾意南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡麵包和牛奶,也喜歡南希。

passages.original: You mustn't feel bad about that one bit.”
passages.vernacular: 你啲都唔使為呢個難過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你一點也不用為這個難過。」

passages.original: Aunt Polly sat suddenly a little more erect in her chair.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嘅椅子上,佢突然坐得更直咗些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽的椅子上,她突然坐得更直了些。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, it's quite time you were in bed.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你早該上床喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你早該上床了。

passages.original: You have had a hard day, and to-morrow we must plan your hours and go over your clothing to see what it is necessary to get for you.
passages.vernacular: 你今日辛苦喇,聽日我哋得安排你嘅作息,整理你嘅衣服,睇需要畀你添乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你今天辛苦了,明天我們得安排你的作息,整理你的衣服,看需要給你添什麼。

passages.original: Nancy will give you a candle.
passages.vernacular: 南希會畀你一支蠟燭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希會給你一支蠟燭。

passages.original: Be careful how you handle it.
passages.vernacular: 攞嘅時候要小心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿的時候要小心。

passages.original: Breakfast will be at half-past seven.
passages.vernacular: 早飯七點半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯七點半。

passages.original: See that you are down to that.
passages.vernacular: 你要下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要下來。

passages.original: Good-night.”
passages.vernacular: 晚安。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安。」

passages.original: Quite as a matter of course, Pollyanna came straight to her aunt's side and gave her an affectionate hug.
passages.vernacular: 好自然地,波麗安娜直接走到佢姨媽身邊,深情地擁抱咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很自然地,波麗安娜直接走到她姨媽身邊,深情地擁抱了她。

passages.original: “I've had such a beautiful time, so far,” she sighed happily.
passages.vernacular: 「到目前為止,我過得美極喇,」佢快樂地嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「到目前為止,我過得美極了,」她快樂地嘆道。

passages.original: “I know I'm going to just love living with you but then, I knew I should before I came.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道我會好愛住喺你呢度——不過,我嚟之前就知道我會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道我會非常愛住在你這裡——不過,我來之前就知道我會。

passages.original: Good-night,” she called cheerfully, as she ran from the room.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,」佢愉快地喊道,跑出咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,」她愉快地喊道,跑出了房間。

passages.original: “Well, upon my soul!” ejaculated Miss Polly, half aloud.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」波莉小姐半出聲地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」波莉小姐半出聲地說。

passages.original: “What a most extraordinary child!”
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁非凡嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼非凡的孩子!」

passages.original: Then she frowned.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢皺起眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她皺起眉。

passages.original: “She's 'glad' I punished her, and I 'mustn't feel bad one bit,' and she's going to 'love to live' with me!
passages.vernacular: 「佢『高興』我懲罰咗佢,我『啲都唔使難過』,佢仲要『愛住』喺我呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她『高興』我懲罰了她,我『一點也不用難過』,她還要『愛住』在我這裡!

passages.original: Well, upon my soul!” ejaculated Miss Polly again, as she took up her book.
passages.vernacular: 天呀!」波莉小姐又講,攞起咗佢嘅書。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!」波莉小姐又說,拿起了她的書。

passages.original: Fifteen minutes later, in the attic room, a lonely little girl sobbed into the tightly-clutched sheet:
passages.vernacular: 十五分鐘後,喺閣樓房間裡,一個孤單嘅小女孩對住緊緊抓住嘅床單抽泣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十五分鐘後,在閣樓房間裡,一個孤單的小女孩對著緊緊抓著的床單抽泣:

passages.original: “I know, father-among-the-angels, I'm not playing the game one bit now--not one bit; but I don't believe even you could find anything to be glad about sleeping all alone 'way off up here in the dark--like this.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,天使中嘅爸爸,我而家啲都冇喺玩呢個遊戲——啲都冇;但我不相信,即使係你,都能找到乜嘢值得高興嘅,獨自一個人瞓喺呢遠遠嘅上面,喺黑暗裡——像咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,天使中的爸爸,我現在一點也沒有在玩這個遊戲——一點也沒有;但我不相信,即使是你,也能找到什麼值得高興的,獨自一個人睡在這遠遠的上面,在黑暗裡——像這樣。

passages.original: If only I was near Nancy or Aunt Polly, or even a Ladies' Aider, it would be easier!”
passages.vernacular: 要係我離南希或波莉姨媽近些,或者甚至係一個婦女互助會嘅人,會容易些!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是我離南希或波莉姨媽近些,或者甚至是一個婦女互助會的人,會容易些!」

passages.original: Down-stairs in the kitchen, Nancy, hurrying with her belated work, jabbed her dish-mop into the milk pitcher, and muttered jerkily:
passages.vernacular: 樓下廚房裡,南希匆忙做佢被耽誤嘅活,把洗碗刷戳進牛奶壺,斷斷續續地嘀咕:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓下廚房裡,南希匆忙做她被耽誤的活,把洗碗刷戳進牛奶壺,斷斷續續地嘀咕:

passages.original: “If playin' a silly-fool game--about bein' glad you've got crutches when you want dolls--is got ter be--my way--o' bein' that rock o' refuge--why, I'm a-goin' ter play it--I am, I am!”
passages.vernacular: 「如果玩一個愚蠢嘅遊戲——關於你想要洋娃娃卻得到拐杖仲要高興——係要成為——我嘅——避難岩——嘅方式——咁,我就要玩——我要,我要!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果玩一個愚蠢的遊戲——關於你想要洋娃娃卻得到拐杖還要高興——是要成為——我的——避難岩——的方式——那麼,我就要玩——我要,我要!」

chapters.title: Ch. VI A Question of Duty 第六章:責任的問題

passages.original: CH It was nearly seven o'clock when Pollyanna awoke that first day after her arrival.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜抵達後嘅第一天,佢醒嚟時已近七點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜抵達後的第一天,她醒來時已近七點。

passages.original: Her windows faced the south and the west, so she could not see the sun yet; but she could see the hazy blue of the morning sky, and she knew that the day promised to be a fair one.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅窗子朝南同朝西,所以仲睇唔到太陽;但佢能睇到早晨天空朦朧嘅藍色,知道呢一天睇來會係個好天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的窗子朝南和朝西,所以還看不到太陽;但她能看到早晨天空朦朧的藍色,知道這一天看來會是個好天。

passages.original: The little room was cooler now, and the air blew in fresh and sweet.
passages.vernacular: 小房間而家涼快咗些,空氣清新甜美地吹進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小房間現在涼快了些,空氣清新甜美地吹進來。

passages.original: Outside, the birds were twittering joyously, and Pollyanna flew to the window to talk to them.
passages.vernacular: 外面,鳥兒歡快地啁啾,波麗安娜飛奔到窗口去同牠哋講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 外面,鳥兒歡快地啁啾,波麗安娜飛奔到窗口去同牠們說話。

passages.original: She saw then that down in the garden her aunt was already out among the rosebushes.
passages.vernacular: 佢呢陣睇見下面花園裡,佢姨媽已經出嚟喺玫瑰叢中喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她這時看見下面花園裡,她姨媽已經出來在玫瑰叢中了。

passages.original: With rapid fingers, therefore, she made herself ready to join her.
passages.vernacular: 於是,佢用飛快嘅手指準備好自己去找佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是,她用飛快的手指準備好自己去找她。

passages.original: Down the attic stairs sped Pollyanna, leaving both doors wide open.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜飛奔下閣樓樓梯,兩扇門都大開住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜飛奔下閣樓樓梯,兩扇門都大開著。

passages.original: Through the hall, down the next flight, then bang through the front screened-door and around to the garden, she ran.
passages.vernacular: 穿過走廊,下咗另一段樓梯,然後砰地穿過帶紗窗嘅前門,繞到花園,佢跑住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 穿過走廊,下了另一段樓梯,然後砰地穿過帶紗窗的前門,繞到花園,她跑著。

passages.original: Aunt Polly, with the bent old man, was leaning over a rose-bush when Pollyanna, gurgling with delight, flung herself upon her.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽同嗰個彎腰嘅老人正在一叢玫瑰上彎住身,波麗安娜咯咯地笑住喜悅地撲到佢身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽同那個彎腰的老人正在一叢玫瑰上彎著身,波麗安娜咯咯地笑著喜悅地撲到她身上。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly, I reckon I am glad this morning just to be alive!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,我想今日早晨我就為活住而高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,我想今天早晨我就為活著而高興!」

passages.original: “PollyANNA!” remonstrated the lady, sternly, pulling herself as erect as she could with a dragging weight of ninety pounds hanging about her neck.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜!」嗰位女士嚴厲地責備,盡可能把身子挺直,儘管脖子上掛住九十磅重嘅拖累。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜!」那位女士嚴厲地責備,盡可能把身子挺直,儘管脖子上掛著九十磅重的拖累。

passages.original: “Is this the usual way you say good morning?”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係你平常講早安嘅方式嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是你平常說早安的方式嗎?」

passages.original: The little girl dropped to her toes, and danced lightly up and down.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩落到腳尖上,輕輕地上上下下跳住舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩落到腳尖上,輕輕地上上下下跳著舞。

passages.original: “No, only when I love folks so I just can't help it!
passages.vernacular: 「不,只有當我愛人愛得忍不住嘅時候!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,只有當我愛人愛得忍不住的時候!

passages.original: I saw you from my window, Aunt Polly, and I got to thinking how you WEREN'T a Ladies' Aider, and you were my really truly aunt; and you looked so good I just had to come down and hug you!”
passages.vernacular: 我從窗子睇見你,波莉姨媽,我就想起你唔係婦女互助會嘅人,你係我真正嘅姨媽;你睇起嚟咁好,我就唔得不下嚟擁抱你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從窗子看見你,波莉姨媽,我就想起你不是婦女互助會的人,你是我真正的姨媽;你看起來那麼好,我就不得不下來擁抱你!」

passages.original: The bent old man turned his back suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個彎腰嘅老人突然轉過身去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個彎腰的老人突然轉過身去。

passages.original: Miss Polly attempted a frown--with not her usual success.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐試圖皺眉——不像平常咁成功。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐試圖皺眉——不像平常那麼成功。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, you--I Thomas, that will do for this morning.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你——湯瑪斯,今日早晨夠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你——湯瑪斯,今天早晨夠了。

passages.original: I think you understand--about those rose-bushes,” she said stiffly.
passages.vernacular: 我想你明白——關於嗰啲玫瑰叢,」佢僵硬地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你明白——關於那些玫瑰叢,」她僵硬地說。

passages.original: Then she turned and walked rapidly away.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢轉身快步走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她轉身快步走開。

passages.original: “Do you always work in the garden, Mr.--Man?” asked Pollyanna, interestedly.
passages.vernacular: 「你總是喺花園裡幹活嗎,先生——大叔?」波麗安娜感興趣地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你總是在花園裡幹活嗎,先生——大叔?」波麗安娜感興趣地問。

passages.original: The man turned.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人轉過身。

passages.original: His lips were twitching, but his eyes looked blurred as if with tears.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅嘴唇喺抽動,但眼睛睇起嚟模糊,像含住淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的嘴唇在抽動,但眼睛看起來模糊,像含著淚。

passages.original: “Yes, Miss.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,小姐。

passages.original: I'm Old Tom, the gardener,” he answered.
passages.vernacular: 我係老湯姆,園丁,」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是老湯姆,園丁,」他回答。

passages.original: Timidly, but as if impelled by an irresistible force, he reached out a shaking hand and let it rest for a moment on her bright hair.
passages.vernacular: 佢怯怯地,但像被一種不可抗拒嘅力量推動,伸出一隻顫抖嘅手,讓佢喺佢明亮嘅頭髮上停留咗片刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他怯怯地,但像被一種不可抗拒的力量推動,伸出一隻顫抖的手,讓它在她明亮的頭髮上停留了片刻。

passages.original: “You are so like your mother, little Miss!
passages.vernacular: 「你太像你母親喇,小姐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你太像你母親了,小姐!

passages.original: I used ter know her when she was even littler than you be.
passages.vernacular: 我認識佢嘅時候,佢比你仲小。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認識她的時候,她比你還小。

passages.original: You see, I used ter work in the garden--then.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,嗰時我就喺花園裡幹活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,那時我就在花園裡幹活。」

passages.original: Pollyanna caught her breath audibly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜明顯地倒抽咗一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜明顯地倒抽了一口氣。

passages.original: “You did?
passages.vernacular: 「你認識?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你認識?

passages.original: And you knew my mother, really--when she was just a little earth angel, and not a Heaven one?
passages.vernacular: 你真嘅認識我母親——當佢仲只係個地上嘅小天使,唔係天堂嘅天使嘅時候?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你真的認識我母親——當她還只是個地上的小天使,不是天堂的天使的時候?

passages.original: Oh, please tell me about her!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,請告訴我關於佢嘅事!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,請告訴我關於她的事!」

passages.original: And down plumped Pollyanna in the middle of the dirt path by the old man's side.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜喺老人身邊嘅泥土小路中間撲通坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜在老人身邊的泥土小路中間撲通坐下。

passages.original: A bell sounded from the house.
passages.vernacular: 房子嗰邊響起一聲鈴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子那邊響起一聲鈴。

passages.original: The next moment Nancy was seen flying out the back door.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻,睇見南希從後門飛奔出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻,看見南希從後門飛奔出來。

passages.original: “Miss Pollyanna, that bell means breakfast--mornin's,” she panted, pulling the little girl to her feet and hurrying her back to the house; “and other times it means other meals.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜小姐,嗰鈴意思係早飯——早晨嘅時候,」佢喘住氣,把小女孩拉起嚟,匆匆領回房子;「別嘅時候意思係別嘅飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜小姐,那鈴意思是早飯——早晨的時候,」她喘著氣,把小女孩拉起來,匆匆領回房子;「別的時候意思是別的飯。

passages.original: But it always means that you're ter run like time when ye hear it, no matter where ye be.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢總是意思係,聽見嘅時候,不管你喺邊兒,你都要像趕時間一樣跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過它總是意思是,聽見的時候,不管你在哪兒,你都要像趕時間一樣跑。

passages.original: If ye don't--well, it'll take somethin' smarter'n we be ter find ANYTHIN' ter be glad about in that!” she finished, shooing Pollyanna into the house as she would shoo an unruly chicken into a coop.
passages.vernacular: 如果你不——嗯,要喺嗰件事裡找出值得高興嘅事,得比我哋聰明才行!」佢結束時,把波麗安娜趕進屋裡,就像把不聽話嘅小雞趕進雞籠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你不——嗯,要在那件事裡找出值得高興的事,得比我們聰明才行!」她結束時,把波麗安娜趕進屋裡,就像把不聽話的小雞趕進雞籠。

passages.original: Breakfast, for the first five minutes, was a silent meal; then Miss Polly, her disapproving eyes following the airy wings of two flies darting here and there over the table, said sternly:
passages.vernacular: 早飯頭五分鐘係沉默嘅一餐;然後波莉小姐,不贊同嘅眼睛隨住兩隻喺桌上呢兒嗰兒飛嚟飛去嘅蒼蠅輕盈嘅翅膀,嚴厲地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯頭五分鐘是沉默的一餐;然後波莉小姐,不贊同的眼睛隨著兩隻在桌上這兒那兒飛來飛去的蒼蠅輕盈的翅膀,嚴厲地說:

passages.original: “Nancy, where did those flies come from?”
passages.vernacular: 「南希,嗰啲蒼蠅係邊度嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,那些蒼蠅是哪裡來的?」

passages.original: “I don't know, ma'am.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,夫人。

passages.original: There wasn't one in the kitchen.”
passages.vernacular: 廚房裡一隻都冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 廚房裡一隻也沒有。」

passages.original: Nancy had been too excited to notice Pollyanna's up-flung windows the afternoon before.
passages.vernacular: 南希前一天下午太興奮,冇注意到波麗安娜推高嘅窗子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希前一天下午太興奮,沒有注意到波麗安娜推高的窗子。

passages.original: “I reckon maybe they're my flies, Aunt Polly,” observed Pollyanna, amiably.
passages.vernacular: 「我想或者係我嘅蒼蠅,波莉姨媽,」波麗安娜和善地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也許是我的蒼蠅,波莉姨媽,」波麗安娜和善地說。

passages.original: “There were lots of them this morning having a beautiful time upstairs.”
passages.vernacular: 「今日早晨樓上有好多,玩得好開心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天早晨樓上有好多,玩得很開心。」

passages.original: Nancy left the room precipitately, though to do so she had to carry out the hot muffins she had just brought in.
passages.vernacular: 南希倉促地離開咗房間,雖然為此佢得把剛端進嚟嘅熱鬆餅攞出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希倉促地離開了房間,雖然為此她得把剛端進來的熱鬆餅拿出去。

passages.original: “Yours!” gasped Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅!」波莉小姐倒抽冷氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的!」波莉小姐倒抽冷氣。

passages.original: “What do you mean?
passages.vernacular: 「你乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你什麼意思?

passages.original: Where did they come from?”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋從邊兒嚟嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們從哪兒來的?」

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, they came from out of doors of course, through the windows.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,佢哋當然係從外面嚟嘅,通過窗子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,它們當然是從外面來的,通過窗子。

passages.original: I SAW some of them come in.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇見其中啲飛進嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看見其中一些飛進來。」

passages.original: “You saw them!
passages.vernacular: 「你睇見喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看見了!

passages.original: You mean you raised those windows without any screens?”
passages.vernacular: 你係講你喺冇紗窗嘅情況下抬起咗嗰啲窗子?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是說你在沒有紗窗的情況下抬起了那些窗子?」

passages.original: “Why, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是的。

passages.original: There weren't any screens there, Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰度冇紗窗,波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那裡沒有紗窗,波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: Nancy, at this moment, came in again with the muffins.
passages.vernacular: 南希呢陣端住鬆餅又進嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希這時端著鬆餅又進來了。

passages.original: Her face was grave, but very red.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉好嚴肅,但紅得厲害。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉很嚴肅,但紅得厲害。

passages.original: “Nancy,” directed her mistress, sharply, “you may set the muffins down and go at once to Miss Pollyanna's room and shut the windows.
passages.vernacular: 「南希,」佢嘅女主人尖銳地指示,「你可以把鬆餅放下,即刻到波麗安娜小姐嘅房間去把窗子關上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,」她的女主人尖銳地指示,「你可以把鬆餅放下,馬上到波麗安娜小姐的房間去把窗子關上。

passages.original: Shut the doors, also.
passages.vernacular: 把門都關上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把門也關上。

passages.original: Later, when your morning work is done, go through every room with the spatter.
passages.vernacular: 稍後,你朝早嘅活做完喇,攞住蒼蠅拍去每個房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後,你早上的活做完了,拿著蒼蠅拍去每個房間。

passages.original: See that you make a thorough search.”
passages.vernacular: 要徹底搜查。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要徹底搜查。」

passages.original: To her niece she said:
passages.vernacular: 佢對外甥女講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對外甥女說:

passages.original: “Pollyanna, I have ordered screens for those windows.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,我已經為嗰啲窗子訂咗紗窗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,我已經為那些窗子訂了紗窗。

passages.original: I knew, of course, that it was my duty to do that.
passages.vernacular: 我當然知道呢個係我嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當然知道這是我的責任。

passages.original: But it seems to me that you have quite forgotten YOUR duty.”
passages.vernacular: 不過喺我睇來,你已經完全忘記咗你嘅責任。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是在我看來,你已經完全忘記了你的責任。」

passages.original: “My--duty?”
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅——責任?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的——責任?」

passages.original: Pollyanna's eyes were wide with wonder.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅眼睛睜得大大嘅,滿係驚奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的眼睛睜得大大的,滿是驚奇。

passages.original: “Certainly.
passages.vernacular: 「當然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。

passages.original: I know it is warm, but I consider it your duty to keep your windows closed till those screens come.
passages.vernacular: 我知道天氣暖同,但我認為喺嗰啲紗窗到來之前,保持窗子關閉係你嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道天氣暖和,但我認為在那些紗窗到來之前,保持窗子關閉是你的責任。

passages.original: Flies, Pollyanna, are not only unclean and annoying, but very dangerous to health.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜,蒼蠅不但不乾淨、討人厭,而且對健康好危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜,蒼蠅不但不乾淨、討人厭,而且對健康非常危險。

passages.original: After breakfast I will give you a little pamphlet on this matter to read.”
passages.vernacular: 早飯後我會畀你一本關於呢個問題嘅小冊子讀。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早飯後我會給你一本關於這個問題的小冊子讀。」

passages.original: “To read?
Oh, thank you, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 哦,謝謝你,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,謝謝你,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I love to read!”
passages.vernacular: 我愛讀書!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛讀書!」

passages.original: Miss Polly drew in her breath audibly, then she shut her lips together hard.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐明顯地倒吸一口氣,然後把嘴唇緊緊閉住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐明顯地倒吸一口氣,然後把嘴唇緊緊閉住。

passages.original: Pollyanna, seeing her stern face, frowned a little thoughtfully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜睇見佢嚴厲嘅臉,若有所思地微微皺咗皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜看見她嚴厲的臉,若有所思地微微皺了皺眉。

passages.original: “Of course I'm sorry about the duty I forgot, Aunt Polly,” she apologized timidly.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,我為我忘記嘅責任感到抱歉,波莉姨媽,」佢怯怯地道歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,我為我忘記的責任感到抱歉,波莉姨媽,」她怯怯地道歉。

passages.original: “I won't raise the windows again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔會再抬起窗子喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不會再抬起窗子了。」

passages.original: Her aunt made no reply.
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她姨媽沒有回答。

passages.original: She did not speak, indeed, until the meal was over.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實在飯食完之前冇講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她確實在飯吃完之前沒有說話。

passages.original: Then she rose, went to the bookcase in the sitting room, took out a small paper booklet, and crossed the room to her niece's side.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢站起嚟,走到起居室嘅書架前,攞出一本小紙冊子,穿過房間走到佢外甥女身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她站起來,走到起居室的書架前,拿出一本小紙冊子,穿過房間走到她外甥女身邊。

passages.original: “This is the article I spoke of, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係我講嘅文章,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是我說的文章,波麗安娜。

passages.original: I desire you to go to your room at once and read it.
passages.vernacular: 我要你即刻回你嘅房間讀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要你馬上回你的房間讀它。

passages.original: I will be up in half an hour to look over your things.”
passages.vernacular: 半小時後我會上去檢查你嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 半小時後我會上去檢查你的東西。」

passages.original: Pollyanna, her eyes on the illustration of a fly's head, many times magnified, cried joyously:
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜眼睛盯住一張放大咗許多倍嘅蒼蠅頭嘅插圖,高興地喊道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜眼睛盯著一張放大了許多倍的蒼蠅頭的插圖,高興地喊道:

passages.original: “Oh, thank you, Aunt Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,謝謝你,波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,謝謝你,波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: The next moment she skipped merrily from the room, banging the door behind her.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻佢快樂地蹦跳住離開房間,身後砰地關上咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻她快樂地蹦跳著離開房間,身後砰地關上了門。

passages.original: Miss Polly frowned, hesitated, then crossed the room majestically and opened the door; but Pollyanna was already out of sight, clattering up the attic stairs.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺眉,猶豫,然後威嚴地穿過房間,打開門;但波麗安娜已經唔見喇,正嘩啦嘩啦地跑上閣樓樓梯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺眉,猶豫,然後威嚴地穿過房間,打開門;但波麗安娜已經不見了,正嘩啦嘩啦地跑上閣樓樓梯。

passages.original: Half an hour later when Miss Polly, her face expressing stern duty in every line, climbed those stairs and entered Pollyanna's room, she was greeted with a burst of eager enthusiasm.
passages.vernacular: 半小時後,波莉小姐臉上每一條線都表現出嚴厲嘅責任感,爬上嗰啲樓梯,走進波麗安娜嘅房間時,迎接佢嘅係一陣熱切嘅熱情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 半小時後,波莉小姐臉上每一條線都表現出嚴厲的責任感,爬上那些樓梯,走進波麗安娜的房間時,迎接她的是一陣熱切的熱情。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, I never saw anything so perfectly lovely and interesting in my life.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,我呢輩子從冇見過咁絕對美好、有趣嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,我這輩子從沒見過這麼絕對美好、有趣的東西。

passages.original: I'm so glad you gave me that book to read!
passages.vernacular: 我太高興你畀咗我嗰本書睇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興你給了我那本書看!

passages.original: Why, I didn't suppose flies could carry such a lot of things on their feet, and--”
passages.vernacular: 嗨,我冇想到蒼蠅腳上能帶咁多嘢,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,我沒想到蒼蠅腳上能帶那麼多東西,而且——」

passages.original: “That will do,” observed Aunt Polly, with dignity.
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,」波莉姨媽威嚴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,」波莉姨媽威嚴地說。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, you may bring out your clothes now, and I will look them over.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你而家把你嘅衣服攞出嚟,我嚟檢查。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你現在把你的衣服拿出來,我來檢查。

passages.original: What are not suitable for you I shall give to the Sullivans, of course.”
passages.vernacular: 不適合你嘅,我當然會送畀蘇利文家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不適合你的,我當然會送給蘇利文家。」

passages.original: With visible reluctance Pollyanna laid down the pamphlet and turned toward the closet.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜明顯不情願地放下小冊子,轉向衣櫃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜明顯不情願地放下小冊子,轉向衣櫃。

passages.original: “I'm afraid you'll think they're worse than the Ladies' Aid did--and THEY said they were shameful,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「我怕你會覺得佢哋比婦女互助會覺得嘅仲糟——而佢哋講佢哋不像話,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怕你會覺得它們比婦女互助會覺得的還糟——而她們說它們不像話,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “But there were mostly things for boys and older folks in the last two or three barrels; and--did you ever have a missionary barrel, Aunt Polly?”
passages.vernacular: 「但最後兩三個桶裡大多係男孩同老人嘅嘢;而且——你有過傳教士捐贈桶嗎,波莉姨媽?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但最後兩三個桶裡大多是男孩和老人的東西;而且——你有過傳教士捐贈桶嗎,波莉姨媽?」

passages.original: At her aunt's look of shocked anger, Pollyanna corrected herself at once.
passages.vernacular: 睇到佢姨媽震驚而憤怒嘅神情,波麗安娜即刻改口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看到她姨媽震驚而憤怒的神情,波麗安娜立刻改口。

passages.original: “Why, no, of course you didn't, Aunt Polly!” she hurried on, with a hot blush.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,不,當然你冇,波莉姨媽!」佢紅住臉匆忙繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,不,當然你沒有,波莉姨媽!」她紅著臉匆忙繼續說。

passages.original: “I forgot; rich folks never have to have them.
passages.vernacular: 「我忘喇;有錢人從來不需要嗰啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我忘了;有錢人從來不需要那些。

passages.original: But you see sometimes I kind of forget that you are rich--up here in this room, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 不過你睇,有時我有點忘咗你有錢——喺呢個房間裡,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是你看,有時我有點忘了你有錢——在這個房間裡,你知道。」

passages.original: Miss Polly's lips parted indignantly, but no words came.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅嘴唇憤慨地張開,但冇話講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的嘴唇憤慨地張開,但沒有話說出來。

passages.original: Pollyanna, plainly unaware that she had said anything in the least unpleasant, was hurrying on.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜顯然冇意識到佢講咗任何啲不愉快嘅話,匆忙地繼續。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜顯然沒意識到她說了任何一點不愉快的話,匆忙地繼續。

passages.original: “Well, as I was going to say, you can't tell a thing about missionary barrels--except that you won't find in 'em what you think you're going to--even when you think you won't.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我正要講,你對傳教士捐贈桶乜嘢都講不準——除咗你喺裡面找唔到你以為會找到嘅嘢——即使你以為你唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我正要說,你對傳教士捐贈桶什麼也說不準——除了你在裡面找不到你以為會找到的東西——即使你以為你不會。

passages.original: It was the barrels every time, too, that were hardest to play the game on, for father and--”
passages.vernacular: 每次最難玩呢遊戲嘅都係嗰啲桶,因為爸爸同——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每次最難玩這遊戲的也是那些桶,因為爸爸和——」

passages.original: Just in time Pollyanna remembered that she was not to talk of her father to her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜恰好及時記起,佢唔能夠對姨媽談佢嘅父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜恰好及時記起,她不能對姨媽談她的父親。

passages.original: She dived into her closet then, hurriedly, and brought out all the poor little dresses in both her arms.
passages.vernacular: 佢然後匆忙鑽進衣櫃,雙臂抱住所有可憐嘅小衣服出嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她然後匆忙鑽進衣櫃,雙臂抱著所有可憐的小衣服出來了。

passages.original: “They aren't nice, at all,” she choked, “and they'd been black if it hadn't been for the red carpet for the church; but they're all I've got.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋啲都不好,」佢哽咽住講,「如果唔係為了教堂嘅紅地毯,佢哋本來係黑嘅;但佢哋係我所有嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們一點也不好,」她哽咽著說,「如果不是為了教堂的紅地毯,它們本來是黑的;但它們是我所有的。」

passages.original: With the tips of her fingers Miss Polly turned over the conglomerate garments, so obviously made for anybody but Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐用指尖翻住嗰啲雜七雜八嘅衣服,顯然係為任何人而唔係波麗安娜做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐用指尖翻著那些雜七雜八的衣服,顯然是為任何人而不是波麗安娜做的。

passages.original: Next she bestowed frowning attention on the patched undergarments in the bureau drawers.
passages.vernacular: 接住佢皺眉關注五斗櫃抽屜裡打補丁嘅內衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著她皺眉關注五斗櫃抽屜裡打補丁的內衣。

passages.original: “I've got the best ones on,” confessed Pollyanna, anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「最好嘅穿喺身上喇,」波麗安娜焦急地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最好的穿在身上了,」波麗安娜焦急地承認。

passages.original: “The Ladies' Aid bought me one set straight through all whole.
passages.vernacular: 「婦女互助會畀我買咗一整套從頭到腳都完好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「婦女互助會給我買了一整套從頭到腳都完好的。

passages.original: Mrs. Jones--she's the president--told 'em I should have that if they had to clatter down bare aisles themselves the rest of their days.
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯太太——佢係會長——告訴佢哋我該有嗰個,即使佢哋自己喺以後嘅日子裡唔得不喺光禿禿嘅走道上哐啷哐啷地走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯太太——她是會長——告訴她們我該有那個,即使她們自己在以後的日子裡不得不在光禿禿的走道上哐啷哐啷地走。

passages.original: But they won't.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢哋唔會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她們不會的。

passages.original: Mr. White doesn't like the noise.
passages.vernacular: 懷特先生不鍾意噪音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懷特先生不喜歡噪音。

passages.original: He's got nerves, his wife says; but he's got money, too, and they expect he'll give a lot toward the carpet--on account of the nerves, you know.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅妻子講佢神經不好;但佢都有錢,佢哋期望佢會為地毯捐好多——因為神經,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的妻子說他神經不好;但他也有錢,她們期望他會為地毯捐很多——因為神經,你知道。

passages.original: I should think he'd be glad that if he did have the nerves he'd got money, too; shouldn't you?”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢應該高興,如果佢有神經,佢都有錢;你不覺得嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他應該高興,如果他有神經,他也有錢;你不覺得嗎?」

passages.original: Miss Polly did not seem to hear.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐似乎冇聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐似乎沒聽見。

passages.original: Her scrutiny of the undergarments finished, she turned to Pollyanna somewhat abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 佢檢查完內衣後,有點突兀地轉向波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她檢查完內衣後,有點突兀地轉向波麗安娜。

passages.original: “You have been to school, of course, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 「你當然上過學,波麗安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你當然上過學,波麗安娜?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: Besides, fath--I mean, I was taught at home some, too.”
passages.vernacular: 此外,爸——我係講,我喺家都學咗啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,爸——我是說,我在家也學了一些。」

passages.original: Miss Polly frowned.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺眉。

passages.original: “Very good.
passages.vernacular: 「好好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好。

passages.original: In the fall you will enter school here, of course.
passages.vernacular: 秋天你當然要喺呢度入學。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 秋天你當然要在這裡入學。

passages.original: Mr. Hall, the principal, will doubtless settle in which grade you belong.
passages.vernacular: 校長霍爾先生無疑會決定你屬於邊個年級。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 校長霍爾先生無疑會決定你屬於哪個年級。

passages.original: Meanwhile, I suppose I ought to hear you read aloud half an hour each day.”
passages.vernacular: 同時,我想我該每天聽你朗讀半小時。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,我想我該每天聽你朗讀半小時。」

passages.original: “I love to read; but if you don't want to hear me I'd be just glad to read to myself--truly, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛讀書;但如果你唔想聽我讀,我都好樂意自己讀——真嘅,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛讀書;但如果你不想聽我讀,我也很樂意自己讀——真的,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: And I wouldn't have to half try to be glad, either, for I like best to read to myself--on account of the big words, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 而且我都唔使勉強高興,因為我最鍾意自己讀——因為有大字,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我也不用勉強高興,因為我最喜歡自己讀——因為有大字,你知道。」

passages.original: “I don't doubt it,” rejoined Miss Polly, grimly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不懷疑,」波莉小姐冷冷地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不懷疑,」波莉小姐冷冷地回答。

passages.original: “Have you studied music?”
passages.vernacular: 「你學過音樂嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你學過音樂嗎?」

passages.original: “Not much.
passages.vernacular: 「不太多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不太多。

passages.original: I don't like my music--I like other people's, though.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意我嘅音樂——不過我鍾意別人嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡我的音樂——不過我喜歡別人的。

passages.original: I learned to play on the piano a little.
passages.vernacular: 我學過啲彈鋼琴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我學過一點彈鋼琴。

passages.original: Miss Gray--she plays for church--she taught me.
passages.vernacular: 格雷小姐——佢為教堂彈琴——教我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 格雷小姐——她為教堂彈琴——教我的。

passages.original: But I'd just as soon let that go as not, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 不過我寧願放棄,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我寧願放棄,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I'd rather, truly.”
passages.vernacular: 真嘅寧願。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的寧願。」

passages.original: “Very likely,” observed Aunt Polly, with slightly uplifted eyebrows.
passages.vernacular: 「好可能,」波莉姨媽講,眉毛微微上揚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能,」波莉姨媽說,眉毛微微上揚。

passages.original: “Nevertheless I think it is my duty to see that you are properly instructed in at least the rudiments of music.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我認為,確保你至少受到音樂基礎嘅適當教導係我嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我認為,確保你至少受到音樂基礎的適當教導是我的責任。

passages.original: You sew, of course.”
passages.vernacular: 你當然會縫紉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你當然會縫紉。」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,夫人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,夫人。」

passages.original: Pollyanna sighed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜嘆氣。

passages.original: “The Ladies' Aid taught me that.
passages.vernacular: 「係婦女互助會教我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是婦女互助會教我的。

passages.original: But I had an awful time.
passages.vernacular: 但我食咗大苦頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我吃了大苦頭。

passages.original: Mrs. Jones didn't believe in holding your needle like the rest of 'em did on buttonholing, and Mrs. White thought backstitching ought to be taught you before hemming (or else the other way), and Mrs. Harriman didn't believe in putting you on patchwork ever, at all.”
passages.vernacular: 瓊斯太太不相信像其他人嗰樣攞針鎖扣眼,懷特太太認為回針縫應該喺捲邊之前教畀你(或者反過嚟),而哈里曼太太根本不相信讓你做拼布。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓊斯太太不相信像其他人那樣拿針鎖扣眼,懷特太太認為回針縫應該在捲邊之前教給你(或者反過來),而哈里曼太太根本不相信讓你做拼布。」

passages.original: “Well, there will be no difficulty of that kind any longer, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,波麗安娜,從此再唔會有嗰類困難喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,波麗安娜,從此再不會有那類困難了。

passages.original: I shall teach you sewing myself, of course.
passages.vernacular: 我自己嚟教你縫紉,當然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己來教你縫紉,當然。

passages.original: You do not know how to cook, I presume.”
passages.vernacular: 我想你唔會做飯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你不會做飯。」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜突然笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜突然笑了。

passages.original: “They were just beginning to teach me that this summer, but I hadn't got far.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋今年夏天才剛開始教我嗰個,但我冇學多遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她們今年夏天才剛開始教我那個,但我沒學多遠。

passages.original: They were more divided up on that than they were on the sewing.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋喺呢上面比喺縫紉上更意見不一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們在這上面比在縫紉上更意見不一。

passages.original: They were GOING to begin on bread; but there wasn't two of 'em that made it alike, so after arguing it all one sewing-meeting, they decided to take turns at me one forenoon a week--in their own kitchens, you know.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋本來要從麵包開始;但冇兩個人做得一樣,所以喺整個縫紉會議上爭論之後,佢哋決定每週一個上午輪流教我——喺佢哋自己嘅廚房裡,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們本來要從麵包開始;但沒有兩個人做得一樣,所以在整個縫紉會議上爭論之後,她們決定每週一個上午輪流教我——在她們自己的廚房裡,你知道。

passages.original: I'd only learned chocolate fudge and fig cake, though, when--when I had to stop.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我只學會咗巧克力軟糖同無花果蛋糕,當——當我唔得不停下嚟嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我只學會了巧克力軟糖和無花果蛋糕,當——當我不得不停下來的時候。」

passages.original: Her voice broke.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音哽住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的聲音哽住了。

passages.original: “Chocolate fudge and fig cake, indeed!” scorned Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「巧克力軟糖同無花果蛋糕,真係嘅!」波莉小姐輕蔑地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「巧克力軟糖和無花果蛋糕,真是的!」波莉小姐輕蔑地說。

passages.original: “I think we can remedy that very soon.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我哋好快就能補救。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我們很快就能補救。」

passages.original: She paused in thought for a minute, then went on slowly: “At nine o'clock every morning you will read aloud one half-hour to me.
passages.vernacular: 佢思考咗一分鐘,然後慢慢地講:「每天早晨九點鐘,你要大聲念半小時畀我聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她思考了一分鐘,然後慢慢地說:「每天早晨九點鐘,你要大聲念半小時給我聽。

passages.original: Before that you will use the time to put this room in order.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰之前,你用呢個時間把呢個房間整理好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那之前,你用這個時間把這個房間整理好。

passages.original: Wednesday and Saturday forenoons, after half-past nine, you will spend with Nancy in the kitchen, learning to cook.
passages.vernacular: 星期三同星期六上午,九點半以後,你要同南希喺廚房裡學做飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期三和星期六上午,九點半以後,你要和南希在廚房裡學做飯。

passages.original: Other mornings you will sew with me.
passages.vernacular: 其他嘅早晨你同我一起縫紉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他的早晨你和我一起縫紉。

passages.original: That will leave the afternoons for your music.
passages.vernacular: 嗰樣下午就留畀你嘅音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那樣下午就留給你的音樂。

passages.original: I shall, of course, procure a teacher at once for you,” she finished decisively, as she arose from her chair.
passages.vernacular: 我當然會即刻畀你找個老師,」佢果斷地講完,從椅子上站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當然會馬上給你找個老師,」她果斷地說完,從椅子上站起來。

passages.original: Pollyanna cried out in dismay.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜沮喪地喊起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜沮喪地喊起來。

passages.original: “Oh, but Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly, you haven't left me any time at all just to--to live.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,你根本冇畀我留任何時間去——去生活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,你根本沒給我留任何時間去——去生活。」

passages.original: “To live, child!
passages.vernacular: 「去生活,細路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「去生活,孩子!

passages.original: What do you mean?
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼意思?

passages.original: As if you weren't living all the time!”
passages.vernacular: 好像你唔係一直喺生活似嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像你不是一直在生活似的!」

passages.original: “Oh, of course I'd be BREATHING all the time I was doing those things, Aunt Polly, but I wouldn't be living.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然,做嗰啲事嘅時候我一直喺呼吸,波莉姨媽,但我唔會係喺生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然,做那些事的時候我一直在呼吸,波莉姨媽,但我不會是在生活。

passages.original: You breathe all the time you're asleep, but you aren't living.
passages.vernacular: 你瞓住嘅時候都一直喺呼吸,但你唔係喺生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你睡著的時候也一直在呼吸,但你不是在生活。

passages.original: I mean living--doing the things you want to do: playing outdoors, reading (to myself, of course), climbing hills, talking to Mr. Tom in the garden, and Nancy, and finding out all about the houses and the people and everything everywhere all through the perfectly lovely streets I came through yesterday.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅意思係生活——做你想做嘅事:喺戶外玩耍,讀書(當然係自己讀),爬山,同湯姆先生喺花園裡講話,同南希講話,以及找出關於嗰啲房子、人哋,同我尋日經過嘅所有絕對漂亮嘅街道上到處一切嘅事情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的意思是生活——做你想做的事:在戶外玩耍,讀書(當然是自己讀),爬山,同湯姆先生在花園裡說話,同南希說話,以及找出關於那些房子、人們,和我昨天經過的所有絕對漂亮的街道上到處一切的事情。

passages.original: That's what I call living, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個就係我所講嘅生活,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就是我所說的生活,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: Just breathing isn't living!”
passages.vernacular: 只係呼吸唔係生活!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是呼吸不是生活!」

passages.original: Miss Polly lifted her head irritably.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐煩躁地抬起頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐煩躁地抬起頭。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, you ARE the most extraordinary child!
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你真係最非凡嘅細路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你真是最非凡的孩子!

passages.original: You will be allowed a proper amount of playtime, of course.
passages.vernacular: 當然,會允許你有適當嘅遊戲時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,會允許你有適當的遊戲時間。

passages.original: But, surely, it seems to me if I am willing to do my duty in seeing that you have proper care and instruction, YOU ought to be willing to do yours by seeing that that care and instruction are not ungratefully wasted.”
passages.vernacular: 但係,我覺得,如果我願意盡我嘅責任,確保你有適當嘅照顧同教導,你都應該願意盡你嘅責任,確保嗰種照顧同教導不被忘恩負義地浪費。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,我覺得,如果我願意盡我的責任,確保你有適當的照顧和教導,你也應該願意盡你的責任,確保那種照顧和教導不被忘恩負義地浪費。」

passages.original: Pollyanna looked shocked.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜顯得震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜顯得震驚。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, as if I ever could be ungrateful--to YOU!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,我點可能忘恩負義——對你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,我怎麼可能忘恩負義——對你!

passages.original: Why, I LOVE YOU--and you aren't even a Ladies' Aider; you're an aunt!”
passages.vernacular: 嗨,我愛你——而你甚至唔係婦女互助會嘅人;你係個姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,我愛你——而你甚至不是婦女互助會的人;你是個姨媽!」

passages.original: “Very well; then see that you don't act ungrateful,” vouchsafed Miss Polly, as she turned toward the door.
passages.vernacular: 「好好;咁注意你嘅行為別顯得忘恩負義,」波莉小姐賞賜般地講,轉向門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好;那麼注意你的行為別顯得忘恩負義,」波莉小姐賞賜般地說,轉向門口。

passages.original: She had gone halfway down the stairs when a small, unsteady voice called after her:
passages.vernacular: 佢走下樓梯一半時,一個小小嘅、不穩嘅聲音追住佢喊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走下樓梯一半時,一個小小的、不穩的聲音追著她喊:

passages.original: “Please, Aunt Polly, you didn't tell me which of my things you wanted to--to give away.”
passages.vernacular: 「請,波莉姨媽,你冇告訴我我嘅嘢邊啲你要——要送人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請,波莉姨媽,你沒告訴我我的東西哪些你要——要送人。」

passages.original: Aunt Polly emitted a tired sigh--a sigh that ascended straight to Pollyanna's ears.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽發出一聲疲倦嘅嘆息——一聲直接升到波麗安娜耳朵裡嘅嘆息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽發出一聲疲倦的嘆息——一聲直接升到波麗安娜耳朵裡的嘆息。

passages.original: “Oh, I forgot to tell you, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我忘咗告訴你,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我忘了告訴你,波麗安娜。

passages.original: Timothy will drive us into town at half-past one this afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西今日下午啲半送我哋進城。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西今天下午一點半送我們進城。

passages.original: Not one of your garments is fit for my niece to wear.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅衣服冇一件適合我嘅外甥女穿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的衣服沒有一件適合我的外甥女穿。

passages.original: Certainly I should be very far from doing my duty by you if I should let you appear out in any one of them.”
passages.vernacular: 如果我讓你穿住其中任何一件出去,我就遠遠冇盡到對你嘅責任。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我讓你穿著其中任何一件出去,我就遠遠沒有盡到對你的責任。」

passages.original: Pollyanna sighed now--she believed she was going to hate that word--duty.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜而家嘆氣——佢相信佢將會討厭嗰個詞——責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜現在嘆氣——她相信她將會討厭那個詞——責任。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, please,” she called wistfully, “isn't there ANY way you can be glad about all that--duty business?”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,請,」佢渴望地喊,「你有冇辦法對嗰整個責任嘅事感到高興?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,請,」她渴望地喊,「你有沒有辦法對那整個責任的事感到高興?」

passages.original: “What?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?」

passages.original: Miss Polly looked up in dazed surprise; then, suddenly, with very red cheeks, she turned and swept angrily down the stairs.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐驚訝茫然地抬頭睇;然後,突然,臉頰緋紅,佢轉身憤怒地衝下樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐驚訝茫然地抬頭看;然後,突然,臉頰緋紅,她轉身憤怒地衝下樓。

passages.original: “Don't be impertinent, Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「別無禮,波麗安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別無禮,波麗安娜!」

passages.original: In the hot little attic room Pollyanna dropped herself on to one of the straight-backed chairs.
passages.vernacular: 喺炎熱嘅小閣樓房間裡,波麗安娜一屁股坐到一張直背椅上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在炎熱的小閣樓房間裡,波麗安娜一屁股坐到一張直背椅上。
