passages.original: To her, existence loomed ahead one endless round of duty.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢睇來,前面嘅生活係一輪無盡嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她看來,前面的生活是一輪無盡的責任。

passages.original: “I don't see, really, what there was impertinent about that,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「我真嘅睇不出嗰有乜嘢無禮,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真的看不出那有什麼無禮,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “I was only asking her if she couldn't tell me something to be glad about in all that duty business.”
passages.vernacular: 「我只係問佢,能唔能夠告訴我,喺嗰整個責任嘅事裡有乜嘢值得高興嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是問她,能不能告訴我,在那整個責任的事裡有什麼值得高興的。」

passages.original: For several minutes Pollyanna sat in silence, her rueful eyes fixed on the forlorn heap of garments on the bed.
passages.vernacular: 有好幾分鐘,波麗安娜默默地坐住,佢懊悔嘅眼睛盯住床上嗰堆淒涼嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有好幾分鐘,波麗安娜默默地坐著,她懊悔的眼睛盯著床上那堆淒涼的衣服。

passages.original: Then, slowly, she rose and began to put away the dresses.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢慢慢地站起嚟,開始把裙子收起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,她慢慢地站起來,開始把裙子收起來。

passages.original: “There just isn't anything to be glad about, that I can see,” she said aloud; “unless--it's to be glad when the duty's done!”
passages.vernacular: 「就係冇乜嘢值得高興嘅,我睇不出嚟,」佢大聲講;「除非——責任完成咗就高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是沒有什麼值得高興的,我看不出來,」她大聲說;「除非——責任完成了就高興!」

passages.original: Whereupon she laughed suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 於是佢突然笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是她突然笑了。

chapters.title: Ch. VII Pollyanna and Punishments 第七章:波麗安娜與懲罰

passages.original: CH At half-past one o'clock Timothy drove Miss Polly and her niece to the four or five principal dry goods stores, which were about half a mile from the homestead.
passages.vernacular: 下午啲半,蒂莫西駕車送波莉小姐同佢外甥女去四五家主要嘅紡織品商店,離祖宅大約半英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下午一點半,蒂莫西駕車送波莉小姐和她外甥女去四五家主要的紡織品商店,離祖宅大約半英里。

passages.original: Fitting Pollyanna with a new wardrobe proved to be more or less of an exciting experience for all concerned.
passages.vernacular: 畀波麗安娜配置新衣櫃,對所有有關嘅人來講,或多或少成咗一次刺激嘅經歷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給波麗安娜配置新衣櫃,對所有有關的人來說,或多或少成了一次刺激的經歷。

passages.original: Miss Polly came out of it with the feeling of limp relaxation that one might have at finding oneself at last on solid earth after a perilous walk across the very thin crust of a volcano.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐出嚟時有一種癱軟放鬆嘅感覺,就像一個人喺火山嘅薄殼上危險地走咗一趟之後,終於發現自己到咗堅實嘅地面上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐出來時有一種癱軟放鬆的感覺,就像一個人在火山的薄殼上危險地走了一趟之後,終於發現自己到了堅實的地面上。

passages.original: The various clerks who had waited upon the pair came out of it with very red faces, and enough amusing stories of Pollyanna to keep their friends in gales of laughter the rest of the week.
passages.vernacular: 接待過佢哋兩個嘅各個店員出嚟時滿臉通紅,帶住足夠多關於波麗安娜嘅有趣故事,夠佢哋嘅朋友哋喺嗰個星期剩下嘅時間裡笑得前仰後合。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接待過她們兩個的各個店員出來時滿臉通紅,帶著足夠多關於波麗安娜的有趣故事,夠他們的朋友們在那個星期剩下的時間裡笑得前仰後合。

passages.original: Pollyanna herself came out of it with radiant smiles and a heart content; for, as she expressed it to one of the clerks: “When you haven't had anybody but missionary barrels and Ladies' Aiders to dress you, it IS perfectly lovely to just walk right in and buy clothes that are brand-new, and that don't have to be tucked up or let down because they don't fit!”
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜自己出嚟時笑容滿面,心滿意足;因為,佢向一個店員咁樣講:「當你只有傳教士捐贈桶同婦女互助會嘅人畀你穿衣服時,直接走進去買嶄新嘅、唔使因為不合身而收起或放長嘅衣服,真嘅絕對美好!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜自己出來時笑容滿面,心滿意足;因為,她向一個店員這樣說:「當你只有傳教士捐贈桶和婦女互助會的人給你穿衣服時,直接走進去買嶄新的、不用因為不合身而收起或放長的衣服,真的絕對美好!」

passages.original: The shopping expedition consumed the entire afternoon; then came supper and a delightful talk with Old Tom in the garden, and another with Nancy on the back porch, after the dishes were done, and while Aunt Polly paid a visit to a neighbor.
passages.vernacular: 購物之行用咗整個下午;然後係晚飯,以及同花園裡老湯姆愉快嘅談話,仲有碗洗完後喺後廊上同南希嘅另一次談話,嗰時波莉姨媽去拜訪鄰居喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 購物之行用了整個下午;然後是晚飯,以及同花園裡老湯姆愉快的談話,還有碗洗完後在後廊上同南希的另一次談話,那時波莉姨媽去拜訪鄰居了。

passages.original: Old Tom told Pollyanna wonderful things of her mother, that made her very happy indeed; and Nancy told her all about the little farm six miles away at “The Corners,” where lived her own dear mother, and her equally dear brother and sisters.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆告訴波麗安娜關於佢母親嘅奇妙事情,讓佢真嘅好高興;南希告訴佢六英里外「拐角村」嘅小農場嘅一切,佢親愛嘅母親、同樣親愛嘅弟弟妹妹就住喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆告訴波麗安娜關於她母親的奇妙事情,讓她真的非常高興;南希告訴她六英里外「拐角村」的小農場的一切,她親愛的母親、同樣親愛的弟弟妹妹就住在那裡。

passages.original: She promised, too, that sometime, if Miss Polly were willing, Pollyanna should be taken to see them.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲保證,如果波莉小姐同意,乜嘢時候會帶波麗安娜去睇佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還保證,如果波莉小姐同意,什麼時候會帶波麗安娜去看他們。

passages.original: “And THEY'VE got lovely names, too.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋都有好聽嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們也有好聽的名字。

passages.original: You'll like THEIR names,” sighed Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 你會鍾意佢哋嘅名字,」南希嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會喜歡他們的名字,」南希嘆道。

passages.original: “They're 'Algernon,' and 'Florabelle' and 'Estelle.'
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋叫『阿爾傑農』、『弗洛拉貝爾』同『埃斯泰爾』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們叫『阿爾傑農』、『弗洛拉貝爾』和『埃斯泰爾』。

passages.original: I--I just hate 'Nancy'!”
passages.vernacular: 我——我就係討厭『南希』!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——我就是討厭『南希』!」

passages.original: “Oh, Nancy, what a dreadful thing to say!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,南希,多可怕嘅話!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,南希,多可怕的話!

passages.original: Why?”
passages.vernacular: 點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼?」

passages.original: “Because it isn't pretty like the others.
passages.vernacular: 「因為佢不像別人嘅咁好聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為它不像別人的那麼好聽。

passages.original: You see, I was the first baby, and mother hadn't begun ter read so many stories with the pretty names in 'em, then.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,我係第一個細路,媽媽嗰時仲冇開始睇咁多有好聽名字嘅故事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,我是第一個孩子,媽媽那時還沒開始看那麼多有好聽名字的故事。」

passages.original: “But I love 'Nancy,' just because it's you,” declared Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我愛『南希』,就因為係你,」波麗安娜宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我愛『南希』,就因為是你,」波麗安娜宣稱。

passages.original: “Humph!
Well, I guess you could love 'Clarissa Mabelle' just as well,” retorted Nancy, “and it would be a heap happier for me.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我想你同樣可以愛『克拉麗莎·梅布爾』,」南希反駁,「嗰樣對我快樂得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我想你同樣可以愛『克拉麗莎·梅布爾』,」南希反駁,「那樣對我快樂得多。

passages.original: I think THAT name's just grand!”
passages.vernacular: 我覺得嗰名字簡直棒極喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得那名字簡直棒極了!」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: “Well, anyhow,” she chuckled, “you can be glad it isn't 'Hephzibah.'”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,不管點樣,」佢咯咯笑住講,「你可以高興佢唔係『海菲茲巴』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,不管怎樣,」她咯咯笑著說,「你可以高興它不是『海菲茲巴』。」

passages.original: “Hephzibah!”
passages.vernacular: 「海菲茲巴!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「海菲茲巴!」

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: Mrs. White's name is that.
passages.vernacular: 懷特太太就叫呢個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懷特太太就叫這個名字。

passages.original: Her husband calls her 'Hep,' and she doesn't like it.
passages.vernacular: 佢丈夫叫佢『海普』,佢不鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她丈夫叫她『海普』,她不喜歡。

passages.original: She says when he calls out 'Hep--Hep!' she feels just as if the next minute he was going to yell 'Hurrah!'
passages.vernacular: 佢講當佢喊『海普——海普!』時,佢覺得好像佢下一分鐘就要喊『萬歲!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說當他喊『海普——海普!』時,她覺得好像他下一分鐘就要喊『萬歲!』

passages.original: And she doesn't like to be hurrahed at.”
passages.vernacular: 佢不鍾意被人歡呼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不喜歡被人歡呼。」

passages.original: Nancy's gloomy face relaxed into a broad smile.
passages.vernacular: 南希陰沉嘅臉鬆開成咗一個大大嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希陰沉的臉鬆開成了一個大大的微笑。

passages.original: “Well, if you don't beat the Dutch!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,你真係咗唔得!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,你真是了不得!

passages.original: Say, do you know?--I sha'n't never hear 'Nancy' now that I don't think o' that 'Hep--Hep!' and giggle.
passages.vernacular: 我講,你知道嗎?——我以後再聽到『南希』,就唔會唔想起嗰個『海普——海普!』而咯咯笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說,你知道嗎?——我以後再聽到『南希』,就不會不想起那個『海普——海普!』而咯咯笑了。

passages.original: My, I guess I AM glad--” She stopped short and turned amazed eyes on the little girl.
passages.vernacular: 天呀,我想我係高興——」佢猛地停住,轉過食驚嘅眼睛睇住小女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪,我想我是高興——」她猛地停住,轉過吃驚的眼睛看著小女孩。

passages.original: “Say, Miss Pollyanna, do you mean--was you playin' that 'ere game THEN--about my bein' glad I wa'n't named Hephzibah'?”
passages.vernacular: 「講,波麗安娜小姐,你係講——你嗰時係喺玩嗰個遊戲——我高興我冇叫海菲茲巴?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說,波麗安娜小姐,你是說——你那時是在玩那個遊戲——我高興我沒有叫海菲茲巴?」

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned; then she laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜皺眉;然後笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜皺眉;然後笑了。

passages.original: “Why, Nancy, that's so!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,南希,真嘅係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,南希,真的是!

passages.original: I WAS playing the game--but that's one of the times I just did it without thinking, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 我係喺玩遊戲——但嗰個係我冇想就做咗嘅時候之一,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是在玩遊戲——但那是我沒想就做了的時候之一,我想。

passages.original: You see, you DO, lots of times; you get so used to it--looking for something to be glad about, you know.
passages.vernacular: 你睇,你確實常常咁樣;你習慣喇——尋找值得高興嘅事,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,你確實常常這樣;你習慣了——尋找值得高興的事,你知道。

passages.original: And most generally there is something about everything that you can be glad about, if you keep hunting long enough to find it.”
passages.vernacular: 而且大體上,只要你找得夠久,每件事裡面都有可以高興嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且大體上,只要你找得夠久,每件事裡面都有可以高興的事。」

passages.original: “Well, m-maybe,” granted Nancy, with open doubt.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,都——或者,」南希公開懷疑地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,也——也許,」南希公開懷疑地承認。

passages.original: At half-past eight Pollyanna went up to bed.
passages.vernacular: 八點半波麗安娜上樓瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 八點半波麗安娜上樓睡覺。

passages.original: The screens had not yet come, and the close little room was like an oven.
passages.vernacular: 紗窗仲冇到,悶熱嘅小房間像個烤爐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紗窗還沒到,悶熱的小房間像個烤爐。

passages.original: With longing eyes Pollyanna looked at the two fast-closed windows--but she did not raise them.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜用渴望嘅眼睛睇住嗰兩扇緊閉嘅窗子——但佢冇抬起佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜用渴望的眼睛看著那兩扇緊閉的窗子——但她沒有抬起它們。

passages.original: She undressed, folded her clothes neatly, said her prayers, blew out her candle and climbed into bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢脫咗衣服,整齊地疊好,做咗禱告,吹滅蠟燭,爬上床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她脫了衣服,整齊地疊好,做了禱告,吹滅蠟燭,爬上床。

passages.original: Just how long she lay in sleepless misery, tossing from side to side of the hot little cot, she did not know; but it seemed to her that it must have been hours before she finally slipped out of bed, felt her way across the room and opened her door.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺熱烘烘嘅小行軍床上,輾轉反側,瞓不住,痛苦地躺咗多久,佢唔知道;但佢覺得一定有好幾個小時,才終於滑下床,摸索住穿過房間,打開咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在熱烘烘的小行軍床上,輾轉反側,睡不著,痛苦地躺了多久,她不知道;但她覺得一定有好幾個小時,才終於滑下床,摸索著穿過房間,打開了門。

passages.original: Out in the main attic all was velvet blackness save where the moon flung a path of silver half-way across the floor from the east dormer window.
passages.vernacular: 外面嘅大閣樓裡,一片天鵝絨般嘅黑暗,只有月亮從東邊老虎窗投下一條銀色嘅路,延伸到地板中間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 外面的大閣樓裡,一片天鵝絨般的黑暗,只有月亮從東邊老虎窗投下一條銀色的路,延伸到地板中間。

passages.original: With a resolute ignoring of that fearsome darkness to the right and to the left, Pollyanna drew a quick breath and pattered straight into that silvery path, and on to the window.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜毅然無視左右兩邊嗰可怕嘅黑暗,倒吸一口氣,噠噠地徑直走進嗰條銀色嘅路,到咗窗前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜毅然無視左右兩邊那可怕的黑暗,倒吸一口氣,噠噠地徑直走進那條銀色的路,到了窗前。

passages.original: She had hoped, vaguely, that this window might have a screen, but it did not.
passages.vernacular: 佢隱約希望呢扇窗子有紗窗,但冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她隱約希望這扇窗子有紗窗,但沒有。

passages.original: Outside, however, there was a wide world of fairy-like beauty, and there was, too, she knew, fresh, sweet air that would feel so good to hot cheeks and hands!
passages.vernacular: 然而,外面係一個仙境般美麗嘅廣闊世界,佢知道,仲有清新甜美嘅空氣,對熱燙嘅臉頰同手幾咁舒服!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,外面是一個仙境般美麗的廣闊世界,她知道,還有清新甜美的空氣,對熱燙的臉頰和手多麼舒服!

passages.original: As she stepped nearer and peered longingly out, she saw something else: she saw, only a little way below the window, the wide, flat tin roof of Miss Polly's sun parlor built over the porte-cochere.
passages.vernacular: 佢走近一步,渴望地向外窺睇,佢睇見咗別嘅嘢:就喺窗子下面不遠,係波莉小姐建喺車門廊上嘅日光室嘅寬闊平坦嘅錫皮屋頂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她走近一步,渴望地向外窺看,她看見了別的東西:就在窗子下面不遠,是波莉小姐建在車門廊上的日光室的寬闊平坦的錫皮屋頂。

passages.original: The sight filled her with longing.
passages.vernacular: 呢景象讓佢心生渴望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這景象讓她心生渴望。

passages.original: If only, now, she were out there!
passages.vernacular: 要係而家佢喺外面該多好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是現在她在外面該多好!

passages.original: Fearfully she looked behind her.
passages.vernacular: 佢害怕地回頭睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她害怕地回頭看。

passages.original: Back there, somewhere, were her hot little room and her still hotter bed; but between her and them lay a horrid desert of blackness across which one must feel one's way with outstretched, shrinking arms; while before her, out on the sun-parlor roof, were the moonlight and the cool, sweet night air.
passages.vernacular: 嗰後面某處係佢嘅熱房間同更熱嘅床;但喺佢同佢哋之間,係一片可怕嘅黑暗沙漠,人必須伸出縮縮嘅雙臂摸索穿過;而喺佢前面,喺日光室屋頂上,係月光同涼爽甜美嘅夜晚空氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那後面某處是她的熱房間和更熱的床;但在她和它們之間,是一片可怕的黑暗沙漠,人必須伸出縮縮的雙臂摸索穿過;而在她前面,在日光室屋頂上,是月光和涼爽甜美的夜晚空氣。

passages.original: If only her bed were out there!
passages.vernacular: 要係佢嘅床喺外面該多好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是她的床在外面該多好!

passages.original: And folks did sleep out of doors.
passages.vernacular: 而且人哋確實瞓喺戶外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且人們確實睡在戶外。

passages.original: Joel Hartley at home, who was so sick with the consumption, HAD to sleep out of doors.
passages.vernacular: 家鄉嘅喬爾·哈特利,病得咁重嘅肺病患者,就必須瞓喺戶外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 家鄉的喬爾·哈特利,病得那麼重的肺病患者,就必須睡在戶外。

passages.original: Suddenly Pollyanna remembered that she had seen near this attic window a row of long white bags hanging from nails.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜突然想起,佢喺呢扇閣樓窗子附近睇見過一排掛喺釘子上嘅長白袋子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜突然想起,她在這扇閣樓窗子附近看見過一排掛在釘子上的長白袋子。

passages.original: Nancy had said that they contained the winter clothing, put away for the summer.
passages.vernacular: 南希講過,裡面裝住為夏天收起嚟嘅冬衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希說過,裡面裝著為夏天收起來的冬衣。

passages.original: A little fearfully now, Pollyanna felt her way to these bags, selected a nice fat soft one (it contained Miss Polly's sealskin coat) for a bed; and a thinner one to be doubled up for a pillow, and still another (which was so thin it seemed almost empty) for a covering.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜而家有點害怕地摸索到呢啲袋子旁,挑咗一個又胖又軟嘅(裡面裝住波莉小姐嘅海豹皮大衣)做床墊;一個較薄嘅折起嚟做枕頭,仲有一個(薄得好像幾乎空嘅)做被子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜現在有點害怕地摸索到這些袋子旁,挑了一個又胖又軟的(裡面裝著波莉小姐的海豹皮大衣)做床墊;一個較薄的折起來做枕頭,還有一個(薄得好像幾乎空的)做被子。

passages.original: Thus equipped, Pollyanna in high glee pattered to the moonlit window again, raised the sash, stuffed her burden through to the roof below, then let herself down after it, closing the window carefully behind her--Pollyanna had not forgotten those flies with the marvellous feet that carried things.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣裝備好後,波麗安娜好高興地噠噠回到月光照耀嘅窗前,抬起窗框,把佢嘅負擔塞出去到下面嘅屋頂上,然後自己順住放下去,小心地喺身後關上窗子——波麗安娜冇忘記嗰啲有奇妙嘅腳、能帶嘢嘅蒼蠅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣裝備好後,波麗安娜非常高興地噠噠回到月光照耀的窗前,抬起窗框,把她的負擔塞出去到下面的屋頂上,然後自己順著放下去,小心地在身後關上窗子——波麗安娜沒有忘記那些有奇妙的腳、能帶東西的蒼蠅。

passages.original: How deliciously cool it was!
passages.vernacular: 幾咁美妙嘅涼爽啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多麼美妙的涼爽啊!

passages.original: Pollyanna quite danced up and down with delight, drawing in long, full breaths of the refreshing air.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜高興得簡直跳起舞嚟,長長地深深地吸住清爽嘅空氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜高興得簡直跳起舞來,長長地深深地吸著清爽的空氣。

passages.original: The tin roof under her feet crackled with little resounding snaps that Pollyanna rather liked.
passages.vernacular: 佢腳下嘅錫皮屋頂發出一連串響亮嘅小啪聲,波麗安娜挺鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她腳下的錫皮屋頂發出一連串響亮的小啪聲,波麗安娜挺喜歡。

passages.original: She walked, indeed, two or three times back and forth from end to end--it gave her such a pleasant sensation of airy space after her hot little room; and the roof was so broad and flat that she had no fear of falling off.
passages.vernacular: 的確,佢從一頭到另一頭嚟回走咗兩三次——呢畀咗佢一種愉快嘅、經歷咗佢熱烘烘嘅小房間之後空曠通透嘅感覺;屋頂咁寬咁平,佢不怕掉下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 的確,她從一頭到另一頭來回走了兩三次——這給了她一種愉快的、經歷了她熱烘烘的小房間之後空曠通透的感覺;屋頂那麼寬那麼平,她不怕掉下去。

passages.original: Finally, with a sigh of content, she curled herself up on the sealskin-coat mattress, arranged one bag for a pillow and the other for a covering, and settled herself to sleep.
passages.vernacular: 最後,佢滿足地嘆咗口氣,蜷縮喺海豹皮大衣床墊上,把一個袋子當枕頭,另一個當被子,安頓下嚟瞓覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後,她滿足地嘆了口氣,蜷縮在海豹皮大衣床墊上,把一個袋子當枕頭,另一個當被子,安頓下來睡覺。

passages.original: “I'm so glad now that the screens didn't come,” she murmured, blinking up at the stars; “else I couldn't have had this!”
passages.vernacular: 「我而家太高興紗窗冇到喇,」佢對住星星眨住眼嘟囔;「否則我就得唔到呢個喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在太高興紗窗沒到了,」她對著星星眨著眼嘟囔;「否則我就得不到這個了!」

passages.original: Down-stairs in Miss Polly's room next the sun parlor, Miss Polly herself was hurrying into dressing gown and slippers, her face white and frightened.
passages.vernacular: 樓下,喺日光室旁邊波莉小姐嘅房間裡,波莉小姐自己正匆忙穿上晨衣同拖鞋,臉色蒼白而驚恐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓下,在日光室旁邊波莉小姐的房間裡,波莉小姐自己正匆忙穿上晨衣和拖鞋,臉色蒼白而驚恐。

passages.original: A minute before she had been telephoning in a shaking voice to Timothy:
passages.vernacular: 一分鐘前,佢用顫抖嘅聲音喺對蒂莫西打電話:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一分鐘前,她用顫抖的聲音在對蒂莫西打電話:

passages.original: “Come up quick!--you and your father.
passages.vernacular: 「快上嚟!——你同你父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「快上來!——你和你父親。

passages.original: Bring lanterns.
passages.vernacular: 帶上燈籠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶上燈籠。

passages.original: Somebody is on the roof of the sun parlor.
passages.vernacular: 有人喺日光室屋頂上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人在日光室屋頂上。

passages.original: He must have climbed up the rose-trellis or somewhere, and of course he can get right into the house through the east window in the attic.
passages.vernacular: 佢一定係爬咗玫瑰花架或別嘅地方,當然佢可以從閣樓東窗直接進入房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一定是爬了玫瑰花架或別的地方,當然他可以從閣樓東窗直接進入房子。

passages.original: I have locked the attic door down here--but hurry, quick!”
passages.vernacular: 我已經把樓下閣樓門鎖上喇——但快,快!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經把樓下閣樓門鎖上了——但快,快!」

passages.original: Some time later, Pollyanna, just dropping off to sleep, was startled by a lantern flash, and a trio of amazed ejaculations.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,波麗安娜剛要瞓住,被燈籠嘅閃光同三個食驚嘅叫聲驚醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,波麗安娜剛要睡著,被燈籠的閃光和三個吃驚的叫聲驚醒。

passages.original: She opened her eyes to find Timothy at the top of a ladder near her, Old Tom just getting through the window, and her aunt peering out at her from behind him.
passages.vernacular: 佢睜開眼睛,發現蒂莫西喺佢附近一個梯子頂上,老湯姆正從窗子鑽出嚟,佢姨媽喺佢後面向外窺睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她睜開眼睛,發現蒂莫西在她附近一個梯子頂上,老湯姆正從窗子鑽出來,她姨媽在他後面向外窺看她。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, what does this mean?” cried Aunt Polly then.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,呢個係乜嘢意思?」波莉姨媽然後喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,這是什麼意思?」波莉姨媽然後喊道。

passages.original: Pollyanna blinked sleepy eyes and sat up.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜眨住瞓眼惺忪嘅眼睛坐起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜眨著睡眼惺忪的眼睛坐起來。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Tom--Aunt Polly!” she stammered.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,湯姆先生——波莉姨媽!」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,湯姆先生——波莉姨媽!」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “Don't look so scared!
passages.vernacular: 「別咁害怕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別這麼害怕!

passages.original: It isn't that I've got the consumption, you know, like Joel Hartley.
passages.vernacular: 唔係我得咗肺病,你知道,像喬爾·哈特利嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是我得了肺病,你知道,像喬爾·哈特利那樣。

passages.original: It's only that I was so hot--in there.
passages.vernacular: 只係我喺裡面太熱喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是我在裡面太熱了。

passages.original: But I shut the window, Aunt Polly, so the flies couldn't carry those germ-things in.”
passages.vernacular: 但我關咗窗子,波莉姨媽,咁樣蒼蠅就帶不進嗰啲細菌嘅嘢喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我關了窗子,波莉姨媽,這樣蒼蠅就帶不進那些細菌的東西了。」

passages.original: Timothy disappeared suddenly down the ladder.
passages.vernacular: 蒂莫西突然沿住梯子消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 蒂莫西突然沿著梯子消失了。

passages.original: Old Tom, with almost equal precipitation, handed his lantern to Miss Polly, and followed his son.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆幾乎同樣倉促地把燈籠遞畀波莉小姐,跟住佢兒子走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆幾乎同樣倉促地把燈籠遞給波莉小姐,跟著他兒子走了。

passages.original: Miss Polly bit her lip hard--until the men were gone; then she said sternly:
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐使勁咬住嘴唇——直到嗰啲人都走喇;然後佢嚴厲地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐使勁咬著嘴唇——直到那些人都走了;然後她嚴厲地說:

passages.original: “Pollyanna, hand those things to me at once and come in here.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,即刻把嗰啲嘢遞畀我,進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,馬上把那些東西遞給我,進來。

passages.original: Of all the extraordinary children!” she ejaculated a little later, as, with Pollyanna by her side, and the lantern in her hand, she turned back into the attic.
passages.vernacular: 真係最非凡嘅細路!」佢稍後講,波麗安娜喺佢身邊,手裡提住燈籠,佢轉回閣樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真是最非凡的孩子!」她稍後說,波麗安娜在她身邊,手裡提著燈籠,她轉回閣樓。

passages.original: To Pollyanna the air was all the more stifling after that cool breath of the out of doors; but she did not complain.
passages.vernacular: 對波麗安娜來講,經歷咗戶外嗰一口涼爽嘅氣息之後,空氣更悶喇;但佢冇抱怨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對波麗安娜來說,經歷了戶外那一口涼爽的氣息之後,空氣更悶了;但她沒有抱怨。

passages.original: She only drew a long quivering sigh.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係長長地顫抖地嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只是長長地顫抖地嘆了口氣。

passages.original: At the top of the stairs Miss Polly jerked out crisply:
passages.vernacular: 喺樓梯頂,波莉小姐乾脆地冒出一句:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在樓梯頂,波莉小姐乾脆地冒出一句:

passages.original: “For the rest of the night, Pollyanna, you are to sleep in my bed with me.
passages.vernacular: 「喺剩下嘅夜裡,波麗安娜,你要同我瞓喺我嘅床上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在剩下的夜裡,波麗安娜,你要和我睡在我的床上。

passages.original: The screens will be here to-morrow, but until then I consider it my duty to keep you where I know where you are.”
passages.vernacular: 紗窗聽日到,但喺嗰之前,我認為我有責任把你放喺我知道你喺邊度嘅地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紗窗明天到,但在那之前,我認為我有責任把你放在我知道你在哪裡的地方。」

passages.original: Pollyanna drew in her breath.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜倒吸一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜倒吸一口氣。

passages.original: “With you?--in your bed?” she cried rapturously.
passages.vernacular: 「同你——瞓你嘅床?」佢狂喜地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「同你——睡你的床?」她狂喜地喊道。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly, how perfectly lovely of you!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,你幾咁絕對地好啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,你多麼絕對地好啊!

passages.original: And when I've so wanted to sleep with some one sometime--some one that belonged to me, you know; not a Ladies' Aider.
passages.vernacular: 而我一直咁想有一天同一個人瞓——屬於我嘅人,你知道;唔係婦女互助會嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我一直那麼想有一天同一個人睡——屬於我的人,你知道;不是婦女互助會的人。

passages.original: I've HAD them.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋我瞓過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們我睡過了。

passages.original: My!
passages.vernacular: 天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!

passages.original: I reckon I am glad now those screens didn't come!
passages.vernacular: 我想我而家高興紗窗冇到!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我現在高興紗窗沒到!

passages.original: Wouldn't you be?”
passages.vernacular: 你不高興嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不高興嗎?」

passages.original: There was no reply.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: Miss Polly was stalking on ahead.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐大步走喺前頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐大步走在前頭。

passages.original: Miss Polly, to tell the truth, was feeling curiously helpless.
passages.vernacular: 講實話,波莉小姐正覺得奇怪地無助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說實話,波莉小姐正覺得奇怪地無助。

passages.original: For the third time since Pollyanna's arrival, Miss Polly was punishing Pollyanna--and for the third time she was being confronted with the amazing fact that her punishment was being taken as a special reward of merit.
passages.vernacular: 自波麗安娜到來以來,波莉小姐第三次懲罰波麗安娜——第三次佢面對住令人驚異嘅事實:佢嘅懲罰被當成咗特別嘅獎賞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自波麗安娜到來以來,波莉小姐第三次懲罰波麗安娜——第三次她面對著令人驚異的事實:她的懲罰被當成了特別的獎賞。

passages.original: No wonder Miss Polly was feeling curiously helpless.
passages.vernacular: 難怪波莉小姐覺得奇怪地無助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪波莉小姐覺得奇怪地無助。

chapters.title: Ch. VIII Pollyanna Pays a Visit 第八章:波麗安娜出門拜訪

passages.original: CH It was not long before life at the Harrington homestead settled into something like order--though not exactly the order that Miss Polly had at first prescribed.
passages.vernacular: 冇過多久,哈林頓祖宅嘅生活就安定成咗某種秩序——雖然不完全係波莉小姐最初規定嘅嗰種秩序。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒過多久,哈林頓祖宅的生活就安定成了某種秩序——雖然不完全是波莉小姐最初規定的那種秩序。

passages.original: Pollyanna sewed, practised, read aloud, and studied cooking in the kitchen, it is true; but she did not give to any of these things quite so much time as had first been planned.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜確實縫紉、練琴、朗讀,並喺廚房學做飯;但佢冇畀呢啲事情花最初計劃嘅咁多時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜確實縫紉、練琴、朗讀,並在廚房學做飯;但她沒有給這些事情花最初計劃的那麼多時間。

passages.original: She had more time, also, to “just live,” as she expressed it, for almost all of every afternoon from two until six o'clock was hers to do with as she liked--provided she did not “like” to do certain things already prohibited by Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 佢都有更多時間「只係生活」,像佢講嘅,因為幾乎每個下午從兩點到六點全係佢自己嘅,愛點樣就點樣——只要佢不「鍾意」做波莉姨媽已經禁止嘅某些事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也有更多時間「只是生活」,像她說的,因為幾乎每個下午從兩點到六點全是她自己的,愛怎樣就怎樣——只要她不「喜歡」做波莉姨媽已經禁止的某些事。

passages.original: It is a question, perhaps, whether all this leisure time was given to the child as a relief to Pollyanna from work--or as a relief to Aunt Polly from Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 或者有個問題:畀細路咁多空閒時間,究竟係為了讓波麗安娜從工作中解脫——定係為了讓波莉姨媽從波麗安娜嗰度解脫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許有個問題:給孩子這麼多空閒時間,究竟是為了讓波麗安娜從工作中解脫——還是為了讓波莉姨媽從波麗安娜那裡解脫。

passages.original: Certainly, as those first July days passed, Miss Polly found occasion many times to ejaculate “What an extraordinary child!” and certainly the reading and sewing lessons found her at their conclusion each day somewhat dazed and wholly exhausted.
passages.vernacular: 可以肯定,隨住七月最初嘅日子過去,波莉小姐有好多次發現自己忍不住驚歎「幾咁非凡嘅細路!」,而且可以肯定,朗讀課同縫紉課每天結束時,都讓佢有點發懵、完全精疲力竭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以肯定,隨著七月最初的日子過去,波莉小姐有很多次發現自己忍不住驚歎「多麼非凡的孩子!」,而且可以肯定,朗讀課和縫紉課每天結束時,都讓她有點發懵、完全精疲力竭。

passages.original: Nancy, in the kitchen, fared better.
passages.vernacular: 廚房裡嘅南希過得好些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 廚房裡的南希過得好些。

passages.original: She was not dazed nor exhausted.
passages.vernacular: 佢既不發懵都不疲憊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她既不發懵也不疲憊。

passages.original: Wednesdays and Saturdays came to be, indeed, red-letter days to her.
passages.vernacular: 星期三同星期六對佢來講,確實成咗值得紀念嘅日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期三和星期六對她來說,確實成了值得紀念的日子。

passages.original: There were no children in the immediate neighborhood of the Harrington homestead for Pollyanna to play with.
passages.vernacular: 哈林頓祖宅嘅近鄰冇細路可以讓波麗安娜一起玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈林頓祖宅的近鄰沒有孩子可以讓波麗安娜一起玩。

passages.original: The house itself was on the outskirts of the village, and though there were other houses not far away, they did not chance to contain any boys or girls near Pollyanna's age.
passages.vernacular: 房子本身喺村子嘅邊緣,雖然不遠處有別嘅房子,佢哋碰巧都冇同波麗安娜年齡相近嘅男孩或女孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房子本身在村子的邊緣,雖然不遠處有別的房子,它們碰巧都沒有和波麗安娜年齡相近的男孩或女孩。

passages.original: This, however, did not seem to disturb Pollyanna in the least.
passages.vernacular: 不過,呢似乎啲都冇困擾波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,這似乎一點也沒困擾波麗安娜。

passages.original: “Oh, no, I don't mind it at all,” she explained to Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,我啲都不介意,」佢向南希解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,我一點也不介意,」她向南希解釋。

passages.original: “I'm happy just to walk around and see the streets and the houses and watch the people.
passages.vernacular: 「我就高興到處走走睇街道同房子,睇人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就高興到處走走看街道和房子,看人。

passages.original: I just love people.
passages.vernacular: 我就係愛人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是愛人。

passages.original: Don't you, Nancy?”
passages.vernacular: 你不愛嗎,南希?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不愛嗎,南希?」

passages.original: “Well, I can't say I do--all of 'em,” retorted Nancy, tersely.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔能夠講我愛——所有嘅,」南希簡短地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不能說我愛——所有的,」南希簡短地回答。

passages.original: Almost every pleasant afternoon found Pollyanna begging for “an errand to run,” so that she might be off for a walk in one direction or another; and it was on these walks that frequently she met the Man.
passages.vernacular: 幾乎每個晴朗嘅下午,波麗安娜都央求「跑個腿嘅差事」,好出去朝呢個嗰個方向散步;就喺呢啲散步中,佢常常遇到嗰個男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幾乎每個晴朗的下午,波麗安娜都央求「跑個腿的差事」,好出去朝這個那個方向散步;就在這些散步中,她常常遇到那個男人。

passages.original: To herself Pollyanna always called him “the Man,” no matter if she met a dozen other men the same day.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜喺心裡總叫佢「嗰個男人」,即使佢同一天碰到十幾個別嘅男人都一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜在心裡總叫他「那個男人」,即使她同一天碰到十幾個別的男人也一樣。

passages.original: The Man often wore a long black coat and a high silk hat--two things that the “just men” never wore.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個男人常穿一件黑色長大衣,戴一頂高高嘅絲帽——「公正嘅人」從不戴嘅兩樣嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個男人常穿一件黑色長大衣,戴一頂高高的絲帽——「公正的人」從不戴的兩樣東西。

passages.original: His face was clean shaven and rather pale, and his hair, showing below his hat, was somewhat gray.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉刮得乾乾淨淨,相當蒼白,帽子下露出嘅頭髮有點灰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的臉刮得乾乾淨淨,相當蒼白,帽子下露出的頭髮有點灰。

passages.original: He walked erect, and rather rapidly, and he was always alone, which made Pollyanna vaguely sorry for him.
passages.vernacular: 佢走路挺直,相當快,總是獨自一人,呢讓波麗安娜隱約為佢難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走路挺直,相當快,總是獨自一人,這讓波麗安娜隱約為他難過。

passages.original: Perhaps it was because of this that she one day spoke to him.
passages.vernacular: 或者正因如此,有一天佢同佢講咗話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許正因如此,有一天她同他說了話。

passages.original: “How do you do, sir?
passages.vernacular: 「您好,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您好,先生?

passages.original: Isn't this a nice day?” she called cheerily, as she approached him.
passages.vernacular: 今日天氣唔係好好嗎?」佢走近佢時愉快地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天天氣不是很好嗎?」她走近他時愉快地喊道。

passages.original: The man threw a hurried glance about him, then stopped uncertainly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人匆忙環顧四周,然後遲疑地停下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人匆忙環顧四周,然後遲疑地停下來。

passages.original: “Did you speak--to me?” he asked in a sharp voice.
passages.vernacular: 「你係對——我講話?」佢用尖銳嘅聲音問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是對——我說話?」他用尖銳的聲音問。

passages.original: “Yes, sir,” beamed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生,」波麗安娜笑容滿面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生,」波麗安娜笑容滿面。

passages.original: “I say, it's a nice day, isn't it?”
passages.vernacular: 「我講,今日天氣好好,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,今天天氣很好,是不是?」

passages.original: “Eh?
Oh!
passages.vernacular: 哦!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦!

passages.original: Humph!” he grunted; and strode on again.
passages.vernacular: 哼!」佢咕噥咗一聲;又大步走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哼!」他咕噥了一聲;又大步走開。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: He was such a funny man, she thought.
passages.vernacular: 佢想,佢係個咁滑稽嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想,他是個那麼滑稽的人。

passages.original: The next day she saw him again.
passages.vernacular: 第二天佢又睇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天她又看見他。

passages.original: “'Tisn't quite so nice as yesterday, but it's pretty nice,” she called out cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 「不像尋日咁好,但都挺好,」佢愉快地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不像昨天那麼好,但也挺好,」她愉快地喊道。

passages.original: “Eh?
Oh!
passages.vernacular: 哦!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦!

passages.original: Humph!” grunted the man as before; and once again Pollyanna laughed happily.
passages.vernacular: 哼!」嗰人像之前一樣咕噥;波麗安娜又快樂地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哼!」那人像之前一樣咕噥;波麗安娜又快樂地笑了。

passages.original: When for the third time Pollyanna accosted him in much the same manner, the man stopped abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜第三次用差不多嘅方式同佢搭話時,嗰人猛地停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜第三次用差不多的方式同他搭話時,那人猛地停下。

passages.original: “See here, child, who are you, and why are you speaking to me every day?”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,細路,你係邊個,點解每天都對我講話?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,孩子,你是誰,為什麼每天都對我說話?」

passages.original: “I'm Pollyanna Whittier, and I thought you looked lonesome.
passages.vernacular: 「我係波麗安娜·惠蒂爾,我覺得您睇起嚟好孤單。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是波麗安娜·惠蒂爾,我覺得您看起來很孤單。

passages.original: I'm so glad you stopped.
passages.vernacular: 我真高興您停下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真高興您停下來了。

passages.original: Now we're introduced--only I don't know your name yet.”
passages.vernacular: 而家我哋算係介紹過喇——只係我仲唔知道您嘅名字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我們算是介紹過了——只是我還不知道您的名字。」

passages.original: “Well, of all the--” The man did not finish his sentence, but strode on faster than ever.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真係——」嗰人冇講完,比以往更快地大步走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真是——」那人沒說完,比以往更快地大步走開了。

passages.original: Pollyanna looked after him with a disappointed droop to her usually smiling lips.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜帶住失望目送佢,平時微笑嘅嘴唇耷拉下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜帶著失望目送他,平時微笑的嘴唇耷拉下來。

passages.original: “Maybe he didn't understand--but that was only half an introduction.
passages.vernacular: 「或者佢冇聽懂——不過嗰只係半個介紹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許他沒聽懂——不過那只是半個介紹。

passages.original: I don't know HIS name, yet,” she murmured, as she proceeded on her way.
passages.vernacular: 我仲唔知道佢嘅名字,」佢繼續趕路時喃喃道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還不知道他的名字,」她繼續趕路時喃喃道。

passages.original: Pollyanna was carrying calf's-foot jelly to Mrs. Snow to-day.
passages.vernacular: 今日波麗安娜畀斯諾太太帶小牛腳凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天波麗安娜給斯諾太太帶小牛腳凍。

passages.original: Miss Polly Harrington always sent something to Mrs. Snow once a week.
passages.vernacular: 波莉·哈林頓小姐每週總畀斯諾太太送點嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉·哈林頓小姐每週總給斯諾太太送點東西。

passages.original: She said she thought that it was her duty, inasmuch as Mrs. Snow was poor, sick, and a member of her church--it was the duty of all the church members to look out for her, of course.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢認為呢個係佢嘅責任,因為斯諾太太貧窮、生病,又係佢教會嘅成員——照顧佢當然係所有教會成員嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她認為這是她的責任,因為斯諾太太貧窮、生病,又是她教會的成員——照顧她當然是所有教會成員的責任。

passages.original: Miss Polly did her duty by Mrs. Snow usually on Thursday afternoons--not personally, but through Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐通常喺星期四下午對斯諾太太盡責——唔係親自,而係通過南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐通常在星期四下午對斯諾太太盡責——不是親自,而是通過南希。

passages.original: To-day Pollyanna had begged the privilege, and Nancy had promptly given it to her in accordance with Miss Polly's orders.
passages.vernacular: 今日波麗安娜央求得到呢個差事,南希即刻按照波莉小姐嘅命令畀咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天波麗安娜央求得到這個差事,南希馬上按照波莉小姐的命令給了她。

passages.original: “And it's glad that I am ter get rid of it,” Nancy had declared in private afterwards to Pollyanna; “though it's a shame ter be tuckin' the job off on ter you, poor lamb, so it is, it is!”
passages.vernacular: 「我好高興能擺脫佢,」南希後來私下對波麗安娜宣稱;「雖然把呢活推畀你,可憐嘅小羊羔,好可恥,真嘅係,真嘅係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很高興能擺脫它,」南希後來私下對波麗安娜宣稱;「雖然把這活推給你,可憐的小羊羔,很可恥,真的是,真的是!」

passages.original: “But I'd love to do it, Nancy.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我好願意做,南希。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我很願意做,南希。」

passages.original: “Well, you won't--after you've done it once,” predicted Nancy, sourly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你做過一次之後就唔會喇,」南希酸溜溜地預言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你做過一次之後就不會了,」南希酸溜溜地預言。

passages.original: “Why not?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解不?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼不?」

passages.original: “Because nobody does.
passages.vernacular: 「因為冇人願意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為沒有人願意。

passages.original: If folks wa'n't sorry for her there wouldn't a soul go near her from mornin' till night, she's that cantankerous.
passages.vernacular: 如果人哋唔係可憐佢,就冇一個人會從早到晚靠近佢,佢咁難伺候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果人們不是可憐她,就沒有一個人會從早到晚靠近她,她那麼難伺候。

passages.original: All is, I pity her daughter what HAS ter take care of her.”
passages.vernacular: 我只可憐佢女兒,係佢得照顧佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只可憐她女兒,是她得照顧她。」

passages.original: “But, why, Nancy?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,點解,南希?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,為什麼,南希?」

passages.original: Nancy shrugged her shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 南希聳聳肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希聳聳肩。

passages.original: “Well, in plain words, it's just that nothin' what ever has happened, has happened right in Mis' Snow's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,直講吧,就係喺斯諾太太眼裡,從來冇發生過任何對嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,直說吧,就是在斯諾太太眼裡,從來沒有發生過任何對的事。

passages.original: Even the days of the week ain't run ter her mind.
passages.vernacular: 連一星期嘅日子都不合佢心意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連一星期的日子都不合她心意。

passages.original: If it's Monday she's bound ter say she wished 'twas Sunday; and if you take her jelly you're pretty sure ter hear she wanted chicken--but if you DID bring her chicken, she'd be jest hankerin' for lamb broth!”
passages.vernacular: 如果係星期一,佢一定講佢希望係星期日;你畀佢帶凍,你肯定會聽到佢想要雞肉——但如果你帶咗雞肉,佢又會渴望羊肉湯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是星期一,她一定說她希望是星期日;你給她帶凍,你肯定會聽到她想要雞肉——但如果你帶了雞肉,她又會渴望羊肉湯!」

passages.original: “Why, what a funny woman,” laughed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,多滑稽嘅女人,」波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,多滑稽的女人,」波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: “I think I shall like to go to see her.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我會鍾意去睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我會喜歡去看她。

passages.original: She must be so surprising and--and different.
passages.vernacular: 佢一定咁出人意料,而且——而且不同。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一定那麼出人意料,而且——而且不同。

passages.original: I love DIFFERENT folks.”
passages.vernacular: 我愛不同嘅人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛不同的人。」

passages.original: “Humph!
Well, Mis' Snow's 'different,' all right--I hope, for the sake of the rest of us!”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,斯諾太太當然『不同』——我希望,為了我哋其他人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,斯諾太太當然『不同』——我希望,為了我們其他人!」

passages.original: Nancy had finished grimly.
passages.vernacular: 南希陰沉地結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希陰沉地結束了。

passages.original: Pollyanna was thinking of these remarks to-day as she turned in at the gate of the shabby little cottage.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜今日轉進嗰座破舊小屋嘅柵門時,正在想呢啲話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜今天轉進那座破舊小屋的柵門時,正在想這些話。

passages.original: Her eyes were quite sparkling, indeed, at the prospect of meeting this “different” Mrs. Snow.
passages.vernacular: 確實,想到要見呢位「不同」嘅斯諾太太,佢嘅眼睛閃閃發光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,想到要見這位「不同」的斯諾太太,她的眼睛閃閃發光。

passages.original: A pale-faced, tired-looking young girl answered her knock at the door.
passages.vernacular: 一個臉色蒼白、疲憊嘅年輕女孩嚟應佢敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個臉色蒼白、疲憊的年輕女孩來應她敲門。

passages.original: “How do you do?” began Pollyanna politely.
passages.vernacular: 「您好?」波麗安娜有禮貌地開口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您好?」波麗安娜有禮貌地開口。

passages.original: “I'm from Miss Polly Harrington, and I'd like to see Mrs. Snow, please.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從波莉·哈林頓小姐嗰度嚟,我想見斯諾太太,請。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從波莉·哈林頓小姐那裡來,我想見斯諾太太,請。」

passages.original: “Well, if you would, you're the first one that ever 'liked' to see her,” muttered the girl under her breath; but Pollyanna did not hear this.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,如果你想,你係第一個『想』見佢嘅人,」女孩壓低聲音嘀咕;但波麗安娜冇聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,如果你想,你是第一個『想』見她的人,」女孩壓低聲音嘀咕;但波麗安娜沒聽見。

passages.original: The girl had turned and was leading the way through the hall to a door at the end of it.
passages.vernacular: 女孩轉身領路穿過走廊,走到盡頭嘅一扇門前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 女孩轉身領路穿過走廊,走到盡頭的一扇門前。

passages.original: In the sick-room, after the girl had ushered her in and closed the door, Pollyanna blinked a little before she could accustom her eyes to the gloom.
passages.vernacular: 喺病房裡,女孩領佢進嚟並關上門後,波麗安娜眨咗眨眼,才使眼睛適應昏暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在病房裡,女孩領她進來並關上門後,波麗安娜眨了眨眼,才使眼睛適應昏暗。

passages.original: Then she saw, dimly outlined, a woman half-sitting up in the bed across the room.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢睇見,隔住房間,喺床上半坐起嘅一個女人隱約嘅輪廓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她看見,隔著房間,在床上半坐起的一個女人隱約的輪廓。

passages.original: Pollyanna advanced at once.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜即刻走上前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜立刻走上前。

passages.original: “How do you do, Mrs. Snow?
passages.vernacular: 「您好,斯諾太太?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您好,斯諾太太?

passages.original: Aunt Polly says she hopes you are comfortable to-day, and she's sent you some calf's-foot jelly.”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽講佢希望您今日舒服,還畀您送嚟咗啲小牛腳凍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽說她希望您今天舒服,還給您送來了一些小牛腳凍。」

passages.original: “Dear me!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!

passages.original: Jelly?” murmured a fretful voice.
passages.vernacular: 凍?」一個煩躁嘅聲音喃喃道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凍?」一個煩躁的聲音喃喃道。

passages.original: “Of course I'm very much obliged, but I was hoping 'twould be lamb broth to-day.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然我好感激,但我本希望今日係羊肉湯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然我非常感激,但我本希望今天是羊肉湯。」

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned a little.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜微微皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜微微皺眉。

passages.original: “Why, I thought it was CHICKEN you wanted when folks brought you jelly,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我以為人哋畀您帶凍時,您要嘅係雞肉,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我以為人們給您帶凍時,您要的是雞肉,」她說。

passages.original: “What?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?」

passages.original: The sick woman turned sharply.
passages.vernacular: 病婦猛然轉過頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 病婦猛然轉過頭。

passages.original: “Why, nothing, much,” apologized Pollyanna, hurriedly; “and of course it doesn't really make any difference.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,冇乜嘢,」波麗安娜匆忙道歉;「當然呢其實冇乜嘢區別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,沒什麼,」波麗安娜匆忙道歉;「當然這其實沒什麼區別。

passages.original: It's only that Nancy said it was chicken you wanted when we brought jelly, and lamb broth when we brought chicken--but maybe 'twas the other way, and Nancy forgot.”
passages.vernacular: 只係南希講我哋帶凍時您要雞肉,帶雞肉時您要羊肉湯——但或者反過嚟,南希忘喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是南希說我們帶凍時您要雞肉,帶雞肉時您要羊肉湯——但也許反過來,南希忘了。」

passages.original: The sick woman pulled herself up till she sat erect in the bed--a most unusual thing for her to do, though Pollyanna did not know this.
passages.vernacular: 病婦撐起身子,喺床上坐直——對佢來講呢個係好不尋常嘅事,雖然波麗安娜唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 病婦撐起身子,在床上坐直——對她來說這是非常不尋常的事,雖然波麗安娜不知道。

passages.original: “Well, Miss Impertinence, who are you?” she demanded.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,無禮小姐,你係邊個?」佢質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,無禮小姐,你是誰?」她質問。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed gleefully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜高興地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜高興地笑了。

passages.original: “Oh, THAT isn't my name, Mrs. Snow--and I'm so glad 'tisn't, too!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰唔係我嘅名字,斯諾太太——我都好高興唔係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那不是我的名字,斯諾太太——我也很高興不是!

passages.original: That would be worse than 'Hephzibah,' wouldn't it?
passages.vernacular: 嗰比『海菲茲巴』仲糟,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那比『海菲茲巴』還糟,是不是?

passages.original: I'm Pollyanna Whittier, Miss Polly Harrington's niece, and I've come to live with her.
passages.vernacular: 我係波麗安娜·惠蒂爾,波莉·哈林頓小姐嘅外甥女,我嚟同佢住喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是波麗安娜·惠蒂爾,波莉·哈林頓小姐的外甥女,我來和她住在一起。

passages.original: That's why I'm here with the jelly this morning.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我今日早晨帶凍嚟呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我今天早晨帶凍來這裡。」

passages.original: All through the first part of this sentence, the sick woman had sat interestedly erect; but at the reference to the jelly she fell back on her pillow listlessly.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢句話嘅前半部分,病婦一直饒有興趣地坐直;但一提到凍,佢就無精打采地倒回枕頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這句話的前半部分,病婦一直饒有興趣地坐直;但一提到凍,她就無精打采地倒回枕頭上。

passages.original: “Very well; thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧;謝謝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧;謝謝。

passages.original: Your aunt is very kind, of course, but my appetite isn't very good this morning, and I was wanting lamb--” She stopped suddenly, then went on with an abrupt change of subject.
passages.vernacular: 你姨媽當然好好心,但我今日早晨胃口不太好,我一直想要羊肉——」佢突然停住,然後突兀地轉換咗話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你姨媽當然很好心,但我今天早晨胃口不太好,我一直想要羊肉——」她突然停住,然後突兀地轉換了話題。

passages.original: “I never slept a wink last night--not a wink!”
passages.vernacular: 「我琴晚一眼都冇瞓——一眼都冇瞓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我昨晚一眼也沒睡——一眼也沒睡!」

passages.original: “O dear, I wish I didn't,” sighed Pollyanna, placing the jelly on the little stand and seating herself comfortably in the nearest chair.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀,我希望我不瞓,」波麗安娜嘆氣,把凍放喺小桌上,舒適地坐進最近嘅椅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪,我希望我不睡,」波麗安娜嘆氣,把凍放在小桌上,舒適地坐進最近的椅子。

passages.original: “You lose such a lot of time just sleeping!
passages.vernacular: 「光係瞓覺要浪費多少時間啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「光是睡覺要浪費多少時間啊!

passages.original: Don't you think so?”
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得嗎?」

passages.original: “Lose time--sleeping!” exclaimed the sick woman.
passages.vernacular: 「浪費時間——瞓覺!」病婦喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「浪費時間——睡覺!」病婦喊道。

passages.original: “Yes, when you might be just living, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,本來你可以只係生活,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,本來你可以只是生活,你知道。

passages.original: It seems such a pity we can't live nights, too.”
passages.vernacular: 真可惜我哋夜裡唔能夠生活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真可惜我們夜裡不能生活。」

passages.original: Once again the woman pulled herself erect in her bed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰女人又一次撐直身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那女人又一次撐直身子。

passages.original: “Well, if you ain't the amazing young one!” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你真係個驚人嘅小傢伙!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你真是個驚人的小傢伙!」她喊道。

passages.original: “Here! do you go to that window and pull up the curtain,” she directed.
passages.vernacular: 「嚟!你去嗰扇窗子把窗簾拉起嚟,」佢命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「來!你去那扇窗子把窗簾拉起來,」她命令。

passages.original: “I should like to know what you look like!”
passages.vernacular: 「我想睇睇你長乜嘢樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想看看你長什麼樣!」

passages.original: Pollyanna rose to her feet, but she laughed a little ruefully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜站起嚟,但有點懊惱地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜站起來,但有點懊惱地笑了。

passages.original: “O dear! then you'll see my freckles, won't you?” she sighed, as she went to the window; “--and just when I was being so glad it was dark and you couldn't see 'em.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!嗰樣您就會睇見我嘅雀斑喇,係唔係?」佢嘆氣,走向窗子;「——而我頭先仲咁高興佢好暗,您睇唔見佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!那樣您就會看見我的雀斑了,是不是?」她嘆氣,走向窗子;「——而我剛才還那麼高興它很暗,您看不見它們。

passages.original: There!
passages.vernacular: 好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了!

passages.original: Now you can--oh!” she broke off excitedly, as she turned back to the bed; “I'm so glad you wanted to see me, because now I can see you!
passages.vernacular: 而家您能——哦!」佢興奮地打斷自己,轉身回到床邊;「我太高興您想睇我,因為而家我能睇見您喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在您能——哦!」她興奮地打斷自己,轉身回到床邊;「我太高興您想看我,因為現在我能看見您了!

passages.original: They didn't tell me you were so pretty!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇告訴我您咁漂亮!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沒告訴我您這麼漂亮!」

passages.original: “Me!--pretty!” scoffed the woman, bitterly.
passages.vernacular: 「我!——漂亮!」嗰女人苦澀地嘲笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我!——漂亮!」那女人苦澀地嘲笑。

passages.original: “Why, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是的。

passages.original: Didn't you know it?” cried Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 您唔知道嗎?」波麗安娜喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不知道嗎?」波麗安娜喊道。

passages.original: “Well, no, I didn't,” retorted Mrs. Snow, dryly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,唔知道,」斯諾太太冷冷地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,不知道,」斯諾太太冷冷地回答。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow had lived forty years, and for fifteen of those years she had been too busy wishing things were different to find much time to enjoy things as they were.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太已經活咗四十年,其中十五年裡佢忙住希望事物不一樣,以致冇乜嘢時間享受事物嘅本來面貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太已經活了四十年,其中十五年裡她忙著希望事物不一樣,以致沒什麼時間享受事物的本來面貌。

passages.original: “Oh, but your eyes are so big and dark, and your hair's all dark, too, and curly,” cooed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,但您嘅眼睛咁大咁黑,您嘅頭髮都全係黑嘅,而且捲曲,」波麗安娜柔聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,但您的眼睛那麼大那麼黑,您的頭髮也全是黑的,而且捲曲,」波麗安娜柔聲說。

passages.original: “I love black curls.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛黑色嘅卷髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛黑色的卷髮。

passages.original: (That's one of the things I'm going to have when I get to Heaven.)
passages.vernacular: (嗰個係我到咗天堂想要擁有嘅嘢之一。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: (那是我到了天堂想要擁有的東西之一。)

passages.original: And you've got two little red spots in your cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 而且您臉頰上有兩個小紅點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且您臉頰上有兩個小紅點。

passages.original: Why, Mrs. Snow, you ARE pretty!
passages.vernacular: 嗨,斯諾太太,您真漂亮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,斯諾太太,您真漂亮!

passages.original: I should think you'd know it when you looked at yourself in the glass.”
passages.vernacular: 我想您照鏡子時就該知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您照鏡子時就該知道。」

passages.original: “The glass!” snapped the sick woman, falling back on her pillow.
passages.vernacular: 「鏡子!」病婦厲聲講,倒回枕頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「鏡子!」病婦厲聲說,倒回枕頭上。

passages.original: “Yes, well, I hain't done much prinkin' before the mirror these days--and you wouldn't, if you was flat on your back as I am!”
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,嗯,呢啲日子我冇點對住鏡子打扮——要係你像我咁樣直挺挺躺住,你都唔會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,嗯,這些日子我沒怎麼對著鏡子打扮——要是你像我這樣直挺挺躺著,你也不會!」

passages.original: “Why, no, of course not,” agreed Pollyanna, sympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,唔會,當然不,」波麗安娜同情地同意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,不會,當然不,」波麗安娜同情地同意。

passages.original: “But wait--just let me show you,” she exclaimed, skipping over to the bureau and picking up a small hand-glass.
passages.vernacular: 「但等一下——讓我畀您睇睇,」佢喊道,蹦跳住走到五斗櫃旁,攞起一面小手鏡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但等一下——讓我給您看看,」她喊道,蹦跳著走到五斗櫃旁,拿起一面小手鏡。

passages.original: On the way back to the bed she stopped, eyeing the sick woman with a critical gaze.
passages.vernacular: 回到床邊嘅路上,佢停下嚟,用挑剔嘅目光打量病婦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回到床邊的路上,她停下來,用挑剔的目光打量病婦。

passages.original: “I reckon maybe, if you don't mind, I'd like to fix your hair just a little before I let you see it,” she proposed.
passages.vernacular: 「我想或者,如果您不介意,我想喺讓您睇之前,把您嘅頭髮稍微整理一下,」佢提議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也許,如果您不介意,我想在讓您看之前,把您的頭髮稍微整理一下,」她提議。

passages.original: “May I fix your hair, please?”
passages.vernacular: 「我可以畀您整理頭髮嗎,請?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我可以給您整理頭髮嗎,請?」

passages.original: “Why, I--suppose so, if you want to,” permitted Mrs. Snow, grudgingly; “but 'twon't stay, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我——想可以,如果你願意,」斯諾太太勉強地允許;「不過佢留不住,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我——想可以,如果你願意,」斯諾太太勉強地允許;「不過它留不住,你知道。」

passages.original: “Oh, thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,謝謝您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,謝謝您。

passages.original: I love to fix people's hair,” exulted Pollyanna, carefully laying down the hand-glass and reaching for a comb.
passages.vernacular: 我愛畀人整理頭髮,」波麗安娜歡呼,小心地放下手鏡,伸手去攞梳子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛給人整理頭髮,」波麗安娜歡呼,小心地放下手鏡,伸手去拿梳子。

passages.original: “I sha'n't do much to-day, of course--I'm in such a hurry for you to see how pretty you are; but some day I'm going to take it all down and have a perfectly lovely time with it,” she cried, touching with soft fingers the waving hair above the sick woman's forehead.
passages.vernacular: 「我今日唔會做太多,當然——我急住讓您睇到您多漂亮;但總有一天我要把佢全放下嚟,好好地玩個痛快,」佢喊道,用柔軟嘅手指碰住病婦額上波浪般嘅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我今天不會做太多,當然——我急著讓您看到您多漂亮;但總有一天我要把它全放下來,好好地玩個痛快,」她喊道,用柔軟的手指碰著病婦額上波浪般的頭髮。

passages.original: For five minutes Pollyanna worked swiftly, deftly, combing a refractory curl into fluffiness, perking up a drooping ruffle at the neck, or shaking a pillow into plumpness so that the head might have a better pose.
passages.vernacular: 有五分鐘,波麗安娜動作迅速而靈巧,把一綹不聽話嘅卷髮梳得蓬鬆,把脖子處垂下嘅荷葉邊撐起嚟,或者把枕頭拍鬆,好讓頭有更好嘅姿勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有五分鐘,波麗安娜動作迅速而靈巧,把一綹不聽話的卷髮梳得蓬鬆,把脖子處垂下的荷葉邊撐起來,或者把枕頭拍鬆,好讓頭有更好的姿勢。

passages.original: Meanwhile the sick woman, frowning prodigiously, and openly scoffing at the whole procedure, was, in spite of herself, beginning to tingle with a feeling perilously near to excitement.
passages.vernacular: 同此同時,病婦極度皺眉,公開嘲笑整個過程,卻不由自主地開始有一種危險地近乎興奮嘅感覺喺刺痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 與此同時,病婦極度皺眉,公開嘲笑整個過程,卻不由自主地開始有一種危險地近乎興奮的感覺在刺痛。

passages.original: “There!” panted Pollyanna, hastily plucking a pink from a vase near by and tucking it into the dark hair where it would give the best effect.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇!」波麗安娜喘住氣講,迅速從附近嘅花瓶裡摘咗一朵粉紅色嘅石竹,插進黑髮裡,效果最好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了!」波麗安娜喘著氣說,迅速從附近的花瓶裡摘了一朵粉紅色的石竹,插進黑髮裡,效果最好。

passages.original: “Now I reckon we're ready to be looked at!”
passages.vernacular: 「而家我想我哋可以被睇喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我想我們可以被看了!」

passages.original: And she held out the mirror in triumph.
passages.vernacular: 佢得意地舉起鏡子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她得意地舉起鏡子。

passages.original: “Humph!” grunted the sick woman, eyeing her reflection severely.
passages.vernacular: 「哼!」病婦咕噥,嚴厲地端詳鏡中嘅自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼!」病婦咕噥,嚴厲地端詳鏡中的自己。

passages.original: “I like red pinks better than pink ones; but then, it'll fade, anyhow, before night, so what's the difference!”
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意紅石竹勝過粉紅嘅;不過反正晚上前佢就謝喇,有乜嘢區別!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡紅石竹勝過粉紅的;不過反正晚上前它就謝了,有什麼區別!」

passages.original: “But I should think you'd be glad they did fade,” laughed Pollyanna, “'cause then you can have the fun of getting some more.
passages.vernacular: 「但我想您該高興佢哋謝喇,」波麗安娜笑道,「因為嗰樣您就有樂趣再弄啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我想您該高興它們謝了,」波麗安娜笑道,「因為那樣您就有樂趣再弄一些。

passages.original: I just love your hair fluffed out like that,” she finished with a satisfied gaze.
passages.vernacular: 我就愛您嘅頭髮蓬鬆成嗰樣,」佢帶住滿意嘅凝視結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就愛您的頭髮蓬鬆成那樣,」她帶著滿意的凝視結束。

passages.original: “Don't you?”
passages.vernacular: 「您不愛嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您不愛嗎?」

passages.original: “Hm-m; maybe.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯;或者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯;也許。

passages.original: Still--'twon't last, with me tossing back and forth on the pillow as I do.”
passages.vernacular: 不過——留不住,我喺枕頭上翻嚟翻去嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過——留不住,我在枕頭上翻來翻去的。」

passages.original: “Of course not--and I'm glad, too,” nodded Pollyanna, cheerfully, “because then I can fix it again.
passages.vernacular: 「當然留不住——我都高興,」波麗安娜愉快地點頭,「因為嗰樣我就可以再畀您整理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然留不住——我也高興,」波麗安娜愉快地點頭,「因為那樣我就可以再給您整理。

passages.original: Anyhow, I should think you'd be glad it's black--black shows up so much nicer on a pillow than yellow hair like mine does.”
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,我想您該高興佢係黑嘅——黑色喺枕頭上比像我咁樣嘅黃頭髮好睇得多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,我想您該高興它是黑的——黑色在枕頭上比像我這樣的黃頭髮好看得多。」

passages.original: “Maybe; but I never did set much store by black hair--shows gray too soon,” retorted Mrs. Snow.
passages.vernacular: 「或者;不過我從不太睇重黑頭髮——太快顯灰,」斯諾太太反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許;不過我從不太看重黑頭髮——太快顯灰,」斯諾太太反駁。

passages.original: She spoke fretfully, but she still held the mirror before her face.
passages.vernacular: 佢講得煩躁,但仍然把鏡子舉喺臉前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說得煩躁,但仍然把鏡子舉在臉前。

passages.original: “Oh, I love black hair!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我愛黑頭髮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我愛黑頭髮!

passages.original: I should be so glad if I only had it,” sighed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 要係我有佢我會太高興喇,」波麗安娜嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是我有它我會太高興了,」波麗安娜嘆道。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow dropped the mirror and turned irritably.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太放下鏡子,煩躁地轉身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太放下鏡子,煩躁地轉身。

passages.original: “Well, you wouldn't!--not if you were me.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你唔會!——如果你係我嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你不會!——如果你是我的話。

passages.original: You wouldn't be glad for black hair nor anything else--if you had to lie here all day as I do!”
passages.vernacular: 你唔會為黑頭髮或任何別嘅而高興——如果你得像我咁樣整天躺喺呢度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會為黑頭髮或任何別的而高興——如果你得像我這樣整天躺在這裡!」

passages.original: Pollyanna bent her brows in a thoughtful frown.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜若有所思地皺咗皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜若有所思地皺了皺眉。

passages.original: “Why, 'twould be kind of hard--to do it then, wouldn't it?” she mused aloud.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,嗰樣就有點難——去做,係唔係?」佢大聲沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,那樣就有點難——去做,是不是?」她大聲沉思。

passages.original: “Do what?”
passages.vernacular: 「做乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「做什麼?」

passages.original: “Be glad about things.”
passages.vernacular: 「為事情高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為事情高興。」

passages.original: “Be glad about things--when you're sick in bed all your days?
passages.vernacular: 「為事情高興——當你一輩子都病喺床上?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為事情高興——當你一輩子都病在床上?

passages.original: Well, I should say it would,” retorted Mrs. Snow.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我該講好難,」斯諾太太反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我該說很難,」斯諾太太反駁。

passages.original: “If you don't think so, just tell me something to be glad about; that's all!”
passages.vernacular: 「如果你不咁認為,就告訴我一件值得高興嘅事;就咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果你不這麼認為,就告訴我一件值得高興的事;就這樣!」

passages.original: To Mrs. Snow's unbounded amazement, Pollyanna sprang to her feet and clapped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 令斯諾太太極其驚訝嘅係,波麗安娜跳起嚟拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令斯諾太太極其驚訝的是,波麗安娜跳起來拍手。

passages.original: “Oh, goody!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,太好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,太好了!

passages.original: That'll be a hard one--won't it?
passages.vernacular: 嗰會係個難嘅——係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那會是個難的——是不是?

passages.original: I've got to go, now, but I'll think and think all the way home; and maybe the next time I come I can tell it to you.
passages.vernacular: 我而家得走喇,但我一路回家都會想啊想;或者下次我嚟時就能告訴您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在得走了,但我一路回家都會想啊想;也許下次我來時就能告訴您。

passages.original: Good-by.
passages.vernacular: 再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見。

passages.original: I've had a lovely time!
passages.vernacular: 我過得好極喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我過得好極了!

passages.original: Good-by,” she called again, as she tripped through the doorway.
passages.vernacular: 再見,」佢輕快地走出門口,又喊咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見,」她輕快地走出門口,又喊了一聲。

passages.original: “Well, I never!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我從冇見過!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我從沒見過!

passages.original: Now, what does she mean by that?” ejaculated Mrs. Snow, staring after her visitor.
passages.vernacular: 而家,佢嗰個係乜嘢意思?」斯諾太太大聲講,瞪住佢嘅訪客嘅背影。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,她那是什麼意思?」斯諾太太大聲說,瞪著她的訪客的背影。

passages.original: By and by she turned her head and picked up the mirror, eyeing her reflection critically.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢轉過頭,攞起鏡子,批判地端詳自己嘅映像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她轉過頭,拿起鏡子,批判地端詳自己的映像。

passages.original: “That little thing HAS got a knack with hair and no mistake,” she muttered under her breath.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰小嘢對頭髮確實有一手,毫無疑問,」佢低聲嘟囔。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那小東西對頭髮確實有一手,毫無疑問,」她低聲嘟囔。

passages.original: “I declare, I didn't know it could look so pretty.
passages.vernacular: 「我講,我唔知道佢能咁漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,我不知道它能這麼漂亮。

passages.original: But then, what's the use?” she sighed, dropping the little glass into the bedclothes, and rolling her head on the pillow fretfully.
passages.vernacular: 不過,有乜嘢用?」佢嘆氣,把小鏡子放進被褥裡,煩躁地喺枕頭上轉動腦袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,有什麼用?」她嘆氣,把小鏡子放進被褥裡,煩躁地在枕頭上轉動腦袋。

passages.original: A little later, when Milly, Mrs. Snow's daughter, came in, the mirror still lay among the bedclothes--thought it had been carefully hidden from sight.
passages.vernacular: 稍後,斯諾太太嘅女兒米莉進嚟時,鏡子仍躺喺被褥之間——雖然曾被小心地藏起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後,斯諾太太的女兒米莉進來時,鏡子仍躺在被褥之間——雖然曾被小心地藏起來。

passages.original: “Why, mother--the curtain is up!” cried Milly, dividing her amazed stare between the window and the pink in her mother's hair.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,媽媽——窗簾拉起嚟喇!」米莉喊道,把佢驚訝嘅目光分畀窗子同佢母親頭髮上嘅粉紅花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,媽媽——窗簾拉起來了!」米莉喊道,把她驚訝的目光分給窗子和她母親頭髮上的粉紅花。

passages.original: “Well, what if it is?” snapped the sick woman.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰又點樣?」病婦厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那又怎樣?」病婦厲聲說。

passages.original: “I needn't stay in the dark all my life, if I am sick, need I?”
passages.vernacular: 「就算我病喇,我都唔使一輩子待喺黑暗裡,係吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就算我病了,我也不必一輩子待在黑暗裡,是吧?」

passages.original: “Why, n-no, of course not,” rejoined Milly, in hasty conciliation, as she reached for the medicine bottle.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,不——當然唔係,」米莉匆忙安撫地回答,伸手去攞藥瓶。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,不——當然不是,」米莉匆忙安撫地回答,伸手去拿藥瓶。

passages.original: “It's only--well, you know very well that I've tried to get you to have a lighter room for ages and you wouldn't.”
passages.vernacular: 「只係——嗯,你好清楚我多年嚟一直想讓你搬到一間亮啲嘅房間,你就係唔肯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是——嗯,你很清楚我多年來一直想讓你搬到一間亮一點的房間,你就是不肯。」

passages.original: There was no reply to this.
passages.vernacular: 呢話冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這話沒有回答。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow was picking at the lace on her nightgown.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太正在扯佢瞓衣上嘅花邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太正在扯她睡衣上的花邊。

passages.original: At last she spoke fretfully.
passages.vernacular: 終於佢煩躁地開口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於她煩躁地開口。

passages.original: “I should think SOMEBODY might give me a new nightdress--instead of lamb broth, for a change!”
passages.vernacular: 「我想有人可以畀我一件新瞓衣——而唔係羊肉湯,換換花樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想有人可以給我一件新睡衣——而不是羊肉湯,換換花樣!」

passages.original: “Why--mother!”
No wonder Milly quite gasped aloud with bewilderment.
passages.vernacular: 難怪米莉驚訝得喘出聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪米莉驚訝得喘出聲。

passages.original: In the drawer behind her at that moment lay two new nightdresses that Milly for months had been vainly urging her mother to wear.
passages.vernacular: 佢身後嘅抽屜裡,此刻正放住兩件新瞓衣,米莉幾個月嚟一直徒勞地勸佢母親穿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她身後的抽屜裡,此刻正放著兩件新睡衣,米莉幾個月來一直徒勞地勸她母親穿。

chapters.title: Ch. IX Which Tells of the Man 第九章:那個男人的事

passages.original: CH It rained the next time Pollyanna saw the Man.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜下次見到嗰個男人時,下住雨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜下次見到那個男人時,下著雨。

passages.original: She greeted him, however, with a bright smile.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢仍然以燦爛嘅笑容向佢問候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她仍然以燦爛的笑容向他問候。

passages.original: “It isn't so nice to-day, is it?” she called blithesomely.
passages.vernacular: 「今日不太好,係吧?」佢輕快地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天不太好,是吧?」她輕快地喊道。

passages.original: “I'm glad it doesn't rain always, anyhow!”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我高興佢不總是下雨,無論如何!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我高興它不總是下雨,無論如何!」

passages.original: The man did not even grunt this time, nor turn his head.
passages.vernacular: 呢次嗰人連咕噥都冇,都冇轉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次那人連咕噥也沒有,也沒轉頭。

passages.original: Pollyanna decided that of course he did not hear her.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜斷定,佢當然冇聽見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜斷定,他當然沒聽見她。

passages.original: The next time, therefore (which happened to be the following day), she spoke up louder.
passages.vernacular: 因此,下一次(碰巧係第二天),佢講得更大聲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,下一次(碰巧是第二天),她說得更大聲了。

passages.original: She thought it particularly necessary to do this, anyway, for the Man was striding along, his hands behind his back, and his eyes on the ground--which seemed, to Pollyanna, preposterous in the face of the glorious sunshine and the freshly-washed morning air: Pollyanna, as a special treat, was on a morning errand to-day.
passages.vernacular: 反正佢覺得特別有必要咁樣做,因為嗰人正大步走住,雙手背喺身後,眼睛盯住地面——喺波麗安娜睇來,面對燦爛嘅陽光同剛被洗過嘅清晨空氣,呢個係荒謬嘅:波麗安娜今日作為特別嘅享受,正在做早晨嘅差事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正她覺得特別有必要這樣做,因為那人正大步走著,雙手背在身後,眼睛盯著地面——在波麗安娜看來,面對燦爛的陽光和剛被洗過的清晨空氣,這是荒謬的:波麗安娜今天作為特別的享受,正在做早晨的差事。

passages.original: “How do you do?” she chirped.
passages.vernacular: 「您好嗎?」佢嘰嘰喳喳地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您好嗎?」她嘰嘰喳喳地說。

passages.original: “I'm so glad it isn't yesterday, aren't you?”
passages.vernacular: 「我多高興今日唔係尋日,您不高興嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我多高興今天不是昨天,您不高興嗎?」

passages.original: The man stopped abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人突然停住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人突然停住。

passages.original: There was an angry scowl on his face.
passages.vernacular: 佢臉上帶住憤怒嘅怒容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他臉上帶著憤怒的怒容。

passages.original: “See here, little girl, we might just as well settle this thing right now, once for all,” he began testily.
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,小姑娘,我哋不妨而家就把呢事一次講清楚,」佢不耐煩地開口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,小姑娘,我們不妨現在就把這事一次說清楚,」他不耐煩地開口。

passages.original: “I've got something besides the weather to think of.
passages.vernacular: 「我除咗天氣仲有別嘅事要想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我除了天氣還有別的事要想。

passages.original: I don't know whether the sun shines or not.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道太陽出冇出嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道太陽出沒出來。」

passages.original: Pollyanna beamed joyously.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜高興得容光煥發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜高興得容光煥發。

passages.original: “No, sir; I thought you didn't.
passages.vernacular: 「係,先生;我想您唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,先生;我想您不知道。

passages.original: That's why I told you.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我才告訴您。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我才告訴您。」

passages.original: “Yes; well--Eh?
What?” he broke off sharply, in sudden understanding of her words.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢?」佢尖銳地打斷自己,突然明白咗佢嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼?」他尖銳地打斷自己,突然明白了她的話。

passages.original: “I say, that's why I told you--so you would notice it, you know--that the sun shines, and all that.
passages.vernacular: 「我講,所以我才告訴您——好讓您注意到,您知道——太陽出嚟喇,等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,所以我才告訴您——好讓您注意到,您知道——太陽出來了,等等。

passages.original: I knew you'd be glad it did if you only stopped to think of it--and you didn't look a bit as if you WERE thinking of it!”
passages.vernacular: 我知道您只要想一想就會高興——而您睇起嚟啲都不像喺想佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道您只要想一想就會高興——而您看起來一點也不像在想它!」

passages.original: “Well, of all the--” ejaculated the man, with an oddly impotent gesture.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真係——」嗰人講,帶住一個奇怪嘅無力手勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真是——」那人說,帶著一個奇怪的無力手勢。

passages.original: He started forward again, but after the second step he turned back, still frowning.
passages.vernacular: 佢又向前走,但走咗第二步後又轉咗回嚟,仍然皺住眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又向前走,但走了第二步後又轉了回來,仍然皺著眉。

passages.original: “See here, why don't you find some one your own age to talk to?”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,你點解不找個你自己年齡嘅人講話?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,你為什麼不找個你自己年齡的人說話?」

passages.original: “I'd like to, sir, but there aren't any 'round here, Nancy says.
passages.vernacular: 「我想,先生,但呢附近冇,南希講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想,先生,但這附近沒有,南希說。

passages.original: Still, I don't mind so very much.
passages.vernacular: 不過我不太介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我不太介意。

passages.original: I like old folks just as well, maybe better, sometimes--being used to the Ladies' Aid, so.”
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意老人,同樣鍾意,或者有時更鍾意——習慣咗婦女互助會,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡老人,同樣喜歡,也許有時更喜歡——習慣了婦女互助會,你知道。」

passages.original: “Humph!
The Ladies' Aid, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 婦女互助會,真係嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 婦女互助會,真是的!

passages.original: Is that what you took me for?”
passages.vernacular: 你把我當成嗰種人咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把我當成那種人了嗎?」

passages.original: The man's lips were threatening to smile, but the scowl above them was still trying to hold them grimly stern.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人嘅嘴唇快要笑出嚟喇,但上面嘅怒容仍試圖把佢哋嚴厲地繃住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人的嘴唇快要笑出來了,但上面的怒容仍試圖把它們嚴厲地繃住。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed gleefully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜高興地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜高興地笑了。

passages.original: “Oh, no, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唔係,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不是,先生。

passages.original: You don't look a mite like a Ladies' Aider--not but that you're just as good, of course--maybe better,” she added in hurried politeness.
passages.vernacular: 您啲都不像婦女互助會嘅人——唔係講您唔係一樣好,當然——或者更好,」佢匆忙禮貌地補充。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您一點也不像婦女互助會的人——不是說您不是一樣好,當然——也許更好,」她匆忙禮貌地補充。

passages.original: “You see, I'm sure you're much nicer than you look!”
passages.vernacular: 「您睇,我確信您比您睇起嚟好得多!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您看,我確信您比您看起來好得多!」

passages.original: The man made a queer noise in his throat.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人喉嚨裡發出一個古怪嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人喉嚨裡發出一個古怪的聲音。

passages.original: “Well, of all the--” he ejaculated again, as he turned and strode on as before.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真係——」佢又講,轉身像以前一樣大步走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真是——」他又說,轉身像以前一樣大步走開。

passages.original: The next time Pollyanna met the Man, his eyes were gazing straight into hers, with a quizzical directness that made his face look really pleasant, Pollyanna thought.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜下次遇到嗰人時,佢嘅眼睛直視佢嘅眼睛,帶住一種揶揄嘅直率,波麗安娜覺得,呢讓佢嘅臉睇起嚟真嘅好和藹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜下次遇到那人時,他的眼睛直視她的眼睛,帶著一種揶揄的直率,波麗安娜覺得,這讓他的臉看起來真的很和藹。

passages.original: “Good afternoon,” he greeted her a little stiffly.
passages.vernacular: 「下午好,」佢有點僵硬地問候佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「下午好,」他有點僵硬地問候她。

passages.original: “Perhaps I'd better say right away that I KNOW the sun is shining to-day.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者我最好即刻講我知道今日太陽出嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許我最好馬上說我知道今天太陽出來了。」

passages.original: “But you don't have to tell me,” nodded Pollyanna, brightly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過您唔使告訴我,」波麗安娜明快地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是您不必告訴我,」波麗安娜明快地點頭。

passages.original: “I KNEW you knew it just as soon as I saw you.”
passages.vernacular: 「我一睇見您就知道您知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一看見您就知道您知道。」

passages.original: “Oh, you did, did you?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你知道,係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你知道,是嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir; I saw it in your eyes, you know, and in your smile.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生;我從您嘅眼睛裡睇出嚟,你知道,仲有您嘅笑容。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生;我從您的眼睛裡看出來,你知道,還有您的笑容。」

passages.original: “Humph!” grunted the man, as he passed on.
passages.vernacular: 「哼!」嗰人咕噥住走過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼!」那人咕噥著走過去。

passages.original: The Man always spoke to Pollyanna after this, and frequently he spoke first, though usually he said little but “good afternoon.”
passages.vernacular: 從此以後,嗰個男人總是同波麗安娜講話,而且常常先開口,雖然通常除咗「下午好」講不咗幾個字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從此以後,那個男人總是和波麗安娜說話,而且常常先開口,雖然通常除了「下午好」說不了幾個字。

passages.original: Even that, however, was a great surprise to Nancy, who chanced to be with Pollyanna one day when the greeting was given.
passages.vernacular: 即使如此,都讓南希大為驚訝,有一天佢碰巧同波麗安娜喺一起,聽見嗰句問候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使如此,也讓南希大為驚訝,有一天她碰巧同波麗安娜在一起,聽見那句問候。

passages.original: “Sakes alive, Miss Pollyanna,” she gasped, “did that man SPEAK TO YOU?”
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,波麗安娜小姐,」佢倒抽氣,「嗰人同你講話咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,波麗安娜小姐,」她倒抽氣,「那人同你說話了嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, yes, he always does--now,” smiled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係啊,佢而家總是咁樣,」波麗安娜笑道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是啊,他現在總是這樣,」波麗安娜笑道。

passages.original: “'He always does'!
passages.vernacular: 「『佢總是咁樣』!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『他總是這樣』!

passages.original: Goodness!
passages.vernacular: 天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!

passages.original: Do you know who--he--is?” demanded Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 你知道佢係邊個嗎?」南希質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道他是誰嗎?」南希質問。

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned and shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜皺眉搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜皺眉搖頭。

passages.original: “I reckon he forgot to tell me one day.
passages.vernacular: 「我想佢有一天忘咗告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想他有一天忘了告訴我。

passages.original: You see, I did my part of the introducing, but he didn't.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,我做咗我嗰部分介紹,但佢冇做。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,我做了我那部分介紹,但他沒做。」

passages.original: Nancy's eyes widened.
passages.vernacular: 南希嘅眼睛睜大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希的眼睛睜大了。

passages.original: “But he never speaks ter anybody, child--he hain't for years, I guess, except when he just has to, for business, and all that.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢從不同任何人講話,細路——我想佢好多年都冇喇,除非佢唔得不,為了生意之類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是他從不同任何人說話,孩子——我想他好多年都沒有了,除非他不得不,為了生意之類。

passages.original: He's John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 佢係約翰·彭德爾頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是約翰·彭德爾頓。

passages.original: He lives all by himself in the big house on Pendleton Hill.
passages.vernacular: 佢獨自住喺彭德爾頓山嘅大房子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他獨自住在彭德爾頓山的大房子裡。

passages.original: He won't even have any one 'round ter cook for him--comes down ter the hotel for his meals three times a day.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至不讓有人喺周圍畀佢做飯——一天三次下嚟旅館食飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他甚至不讓有人在周圍給他做飯——一天三次下來旅館吃飯。

passages.original: I know Sally Miner, who waits on him, and she says he hardly opens his head enough ter tell what he wants ter eat.
passages.vernacular: 我認識畀佢上菜嘅莎莉·邁納,佢講佢幾乎不張嘴講佢要食乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認識給他上菜的莎莉·邁納,她說他幾乎不張嘴說他要吃什麼。

passages.original: She has ter guess it more'n half the time--only it'll be somethin' CHEAP!
passages.vernacular: 佢多半時候得猜——只係肯定係便宜嘅嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她多半時候得猜——只是肯定是便宜的東西!

passages.original: She knows that without no tellin'.”
passages.vernacular: 佢唔使講就知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不用說就知道。」

passages.original: Pollyanna nodded sympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜同情地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜同情地點頭。

passages.original: “I know.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。

passages.original: You have to look for cheap things when you're poor.
passages.vernacular: 你窮嘅時候得找便宜嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你窮的時候得找便宜的東西。

passages.original: Father and I took meals out a lot.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸同我常喺外面食飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸和我常在外面吃飯。

passages.original: We had beans and fish balls most generally.
passages.vernacular: 我哋通常食豆子同魚丸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們通常吃豆子和魚丸。

passages.original: We used to say how glad we were we liked beans--that is, we said it specially when we were looking at the roast turkey place, you know, that was sixty cents.
passages.vernacular: 我哋常講多高興我哋愛食豆子——就係,尤其係我哋睇住嗰個烤火雞嘅地方,你知道,要六十美分嘅時候咁樣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們常說多高興我們愛吃豆子——就是,尤其是我們看著那個烤火雞的地方,你知道,要六十美分的時候這樣說。

passages.original: Does Mr. Pendleton like beans?”
passages.vernacular: 彭德爾頓先生愛食豆子嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彭德爾頓先生愛吃豆子嗎?」

passages.original: “Like 'em!
passages.vernacular: 「愛食!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「愛吃!

passages.original: What if he does--or don't?
passages.vernacular: 佢愛不愛有乜嘢關係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他愛不愛有什麼關係?

passages.original: Why, Miss Pollyanna, he ain't poor.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,波麗安娜小姐,佢不窮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,波麗安娜小姐,他不窮。

passages.original: He's got loads of money, John Pendleton has--from his father.
passages.vernacular: 佢有好多錢,約翰·彭德爾頓,來自佢父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有好多錢,約翰·彭德爾頓,來自他父親。

passages.original: There ain't nobody in town as rich as he is.
passages.vernacular: 鎮上冇人像佢咁富有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鎮上沒有人像他那麼富有。

passages.original: He could eat dollar bills, if he wanted to--and not know it.”
passages.vernacular: 佢想食嘅話,可以食鈔票——仲唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想吃的話,可以吃鈔票——還不知道。」

passages.original: Pollyanna giggled.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜咯咯地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜咯咯地笑了。

passages.original: “As if anybody COULD eat dollar bills and not know it, Nancy, when they come to try to chew 'em!”
passages.vernacular: 「好像有人真能食鈔票卻唔知道似嘅,南希,當佢哋試住嚼佢哋嘅時候!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像有人真能吃鈔票卻不知道似的,南希,當他們試著嚼它們的時候!」

passages.original: “Ho!
I mean he's rich enough ter do it,” shrugged Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 我係講佢有錢到嗰個程度,」南希聳聳肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是說他有錢到那個程度,」南希聳聳肩。

passages.original: “He ain't spendin' his money, that's all.
passages.vernacular: 「佢不花錢,就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他不花錢,就是這樣。

passages.original: He's a-savin' of it.”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺存住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在存著。」

passages.original: “Oh, for the heathen,” surmised Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,為了異教徒,」波麗安娜猜道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,為了異教徒,」波麗安娜猜道。

passages.original: “How perfectly splendid!
passages.vernacular: 「幾咁絕對嘅好啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多麼絕對的好啊!

passages.original: That's denying yourself and taking up your cross.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個就係克己、背起自己嘅十字架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就是克己、背起自己的十字架。

passages.original: I know; father told me.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道;爸爸告訴過我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道;爸爸告訴過我。」

passages.original: Nancy's lips parted abruptly, as if there were angry words all ready to come; but her eyes, resting on Pollyanna's jubilantly trustful face, saw something that prevented the words being spoken.
passages.vernacular: 南希嘅嘴唇突然張開,好像有憤怒嘅話準備好要講出嚟;但佢嘅眼睛落喺波麗安娜歡欣信任嘅臉上,睇見咗某樣嘢,阻止咗話講出口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希的嘴唇突然張開,好像有憤怒的話準備好要說出來;但她的眼睛落在波麗安娜歡欣信任的臉上,看見了某樣東西,阻止了話說出口。

passages.original: “Humph!” she vouchsafed.
passages.vernacular: 「哼!」佢只賞咗一句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼!」她只賞了一句。

passages.original: Then, showing her old-time interest, she went on: “But, say, it is queer, his speakin' to you, honestly, Miss Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 然後,顯出佢嘅老興趣,佢繼續講:「不過,講真嘅,佢同你講話,波麗安娜小姐,確實奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,顯出她的老興趣,她繼續說:「不過,說真的,他同你說話,波麗安娜小姐,確實奇怪。

passages.original: He don't speak ter no one; and he lives all alone in a great big lovely house all full of jest grand things, they say.
passages.vernacular: 佢不同任何人講話;佢獨自住喺一座滿係華麗嘢嘅大大嘅漂亮房子裡,佢哋講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不同任何人說話;他獨自住在一座滿是華麗東西的大大的漂亮房子裡,他們說。

passages.original: Some says he's crazy, and some jest cross; and some says he's got a skeleton in his closet.”
passages.vernacular: 有人講佢瘋喇,有人講佢只係脾氣壞;仲有人講佢櫃子裡藏住個骷髏。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人說他瘋了,有人說他只是脾氣壞;還有人說他櫃子裡藏著個骷髏。」

passages.original: “Oh, Nancy!” shuddered Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,南希!」波麗安娜打咗個寒顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,南希!」波麗安娜打了個寒顫。

passages.original: “How can he keep such a dreadful thing?
passages.vernacular: 「佢點能留住咁可怕嘅嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他怎麼能留著這麼可怕的東西?

passages.original: I should think he'd throw it away!”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢會把佢扔掉!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他會把它扔掉!」

passages.original: Nancy chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 南希輕輕笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希輕輕笑了。

passages.original: That Pollyanna had taken the skeleton literally instead of figuratively, she knew very well; but, perversely, she refrained from correcting the mistake.
passages.vernacular: 佢好清楚波麗安娜把骷髏當成咗字面意思而唔係比喻;但佢任性地冇糾正呢個錯誤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她很清楚波麗安娜把骷髏當成了字面意思而不是比喻;但她任性地沒有糾正這個錯誤。

passages.original: “And EVERYBODY says he's mysterious,” she went on.
passages.vernacular: 「而且所有人都講佢神祕,」佢繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且所有人都說他神祕,」她繼續說。

passages.original: “Some years he jest travels, week in and week out, and it's always in heathen countries--Egypt and Asia and the Desert of Sarah, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「有些年佢就只係旅行,一個星期又一個星期,總是喺異教國家——埃及、亞洲同撒哈拉沙漠,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有些年他就只是旅行,一個星期又一個星期,總是在異教國家——埃及、亞洲和撒哈拉沙漠,你知道。」

passages.original: “Oh, a missionary,” nodded Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,傳教士,」波麗安娜點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,傳教士,」波麗安娜點頭。

passages.original: Nancy laughed oddly.
passages.vernacular: 南希古怪地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希古怪地笑了。

passages.original: “Well, I didn't say that, Miss Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我冇咁講,波麗安娜小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我沒這麼說,波麗安娜小姐。

passages.original: When he comes back he writes books--queer, odd books, they say, about some gimcrack he's found in them heathen countries.
passages.vernacular: 佢回嚟後寫書——古怪嘅、奇怪嘅書,佢哋講,關於佢喺嗰啲異教國家找到嘅啲小玩意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他回來後寫書——古怪的、奇怪的書,他們說,關於他在那些異教國家找到的一些小玩意。

passages.original: But he don't never seem ter want ter spend no money here--leastways, not for jest livin'.”
passages.vernacular: 但佢似乎從唔想喺呢度花錢——至少,唔係為了生活。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他似乎從不想在這裡花錢——至少,不是為了生活。」

passages.original: “Of course not--if he's saving it for the heathen,” declared Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「當然唔想——如果佢為異教徒存錢,」波麗安娜宣稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不想——如果他為異教徒存錢,」波麗安娜宣稱。

passages.original: “But he is a funny man, and he's different, too, just like Mrs. Snow, only he's a different different.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢係個滑稽嘅人,佢都係不同嘅,就像斯諾太太,只係佢係另一種不同。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過他是個滑稽的人,他也是不同的,就像斯諾太太,只是他是另一種不同。」

passages.original: “Well, I guess he is--rather,” chuckled Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想佢係——相當,」南希咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想他是——相當,」南希咯咯笑。

passages.original: “I'm gladder'n ever now, anyhow, that he speaks to me,” sighed Pollyanna contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 「無論如何,我而家比以往更高興佢同我講話,」波麗安娜滿足地嘆息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「無論如何,我現在比以往更高興他同我說話,」波麗安娜滿足地嘆息。

chapters.title: Ch. X A Surprise for Mrs. Snow 第十章:給斯諾太太的驚喜

passages.original: CH The next time Pollyanna went to see Mrs. Snow, she found that lady, as at first, in a darkened room.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜下次去睇斯諾太太時,發現嗰位女士仍像起初嗰樣,待喺暗住嘅房間裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜下次去看斯諾太太時,發現那位女士仍像起初那樣,待在暗著的房間裡。
