passages.original: “It's the little girl from Miss Polly's, mother,” announced Milly, in a tired manner; then Pollyanna found herself alone with the invalid.
passages.vernacular: 「係波莉小姐嗰邊嘅小女孩,媽媽,」米莉疲倦地通報;然後波麗安娜發現自己單獨同病人喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是波莉小姐那邊的小女孩,媽媽,」米莉疲倦地通報;然後波麗安娜發現自己單獨與病人在一起。

passages.original: “Oh, it's you, is it?” asked a fretful voice from the bed.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係你,係嗎?」床上傳嚟一個煩躁嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是你,是嗎?」床上傳來一個煩躁的聲音。

passages.original: “I remember you.
passages.vernacular: 「我記得你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我記得你。

passages.original: ANYbody'd remember you, I guess, if they saw you once.
passages.vernacular: 任何人見你一次都會記得你,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任何人見你一次都會記得你,我想。

passages.original: I wish you had come yesterday.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你尋日嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你昨天來。

passages.original: I WANTED you yesterday.”
passages.vernacular: 尋日我想要你嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 昨天我想要你來。」

passages.original: “Did you?
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?

passages.original: Well, I'm glad 'tisn't any farther away from yesterday than to-day is, then,” laughed Pollyanna, advancing cheerily into the room, and setting her basket carefully down on a chair.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,嗰我高興,離尋日並不比今日更遠,」波麗安娜笑住,愉快地走進房間,小心地把籃子放喺一張椅子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,那我高興,離昨天並不比今天更遠,」波麗安娜笑著,愉快地走進房間,小心地把籃子放在一張椅子上。

passages.original: “My! but aren't you dark here, though?
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!您呢度唔係好暗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!您這裡不是很暗嗎?

passages.original: I can't see you a bit,” she cried, unhesitatingly crossing to the window and pulling up the shade.
passages.vernacular: 我啲都睇唔見您,」佢喊道,毫不猶豫地走到窗邊,把百葉窗拉起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一點也看不見您,」她喊道,毫不猶豫地走到窗邊,把百葉窗拉起來。

passages.original: “I want to see if you've fixed your hair like I did--oh, you haven't!
passages.vernacular: 「我想睇睇您有冇像我嗰樣整理頭髮——哦,您冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想看看您有沒有像我那樣整理頭髮——哦,您沒有!

passages.original: But, never mind; I'm glad you haven't, after all, 'cause maybe you'll let me do it--later.
passages.vernacular: 不過,冇關係;畢竟我高興您冇整理,因為或者您會讓我嚟——以後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,沒關係;畢竟我高興您沒整理,因為也許您會讓我來——以後。

passages.original: But now I want you to see what I've brought you.”
passages.vernacular: 不過而家我想讓您睇睇我帶嚟咗乜嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在我想讓您看看我帶來了什麼。」

passages.original: The woman stirred restlessly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰女人不安地動咗動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那女人不安地動了動。

passages.original: “Just as if how it looks would make any difference in how it tastes,” she scoffed--but she turned her eyes toward the basket.
passages.vernacular: 「好像佢嘅樣子會對佢嘅味道有乜嘢影響似嘅,」佢嘲笑道——但佢把眼睛轉向咗籃子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像它的樣子會對它的味道有什麼影響似的,」她嘲笑道——但她把眼睛轉向了籃子。

passages.original: “Well, what is it?”
passages.vernacular: 「好,係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,是什麼?」

passages.original: “Guess!
What do you want?”
passages.vernacular: 您想要乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想要什麼?」

passages.original: Pollyanna had skipped back to the basket.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜蹦跳住回到籃子旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜蹦跳著回到籃子旁。

passages.original: Her face was alight.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉亮咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉亮了起來。

passages.original: The sick woman frowned.
passages.vernacular: 病婦皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 病婦皺眉。

passages.original: “Why, I don't WANT anything, as I know of,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我唔想要乜嘢,據我所知,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我不想要什麼,據我所知,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “After all, they all taste alike!”
passages.vernacular: 「反正佢哋嘗起嚟都一樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「反正它們嘗起來都一樣!」

passages.original: Pollyanna chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜咯咯笑。

passages.original: “This won't.
passages.vernacular: 「呢唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這不會。

passages.original: Guess!
passages.vernacular: 猜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猜!

passages.original: If you DID want something, what would it be?”
passages.vernacular: 如果您真想要乜嘢,會係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您真想要什麼,會是什麼?」

passages.original: The woman hesitated.
passages.vernacular: 嗰女人猶豫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那女人猶豫了。

passages.original: She did not realize it herself, but she had so long been accustomed to wanting what she did not have, that to state off-hand what she DID want seemed impossible--until she knew what she had.
passages.vernacular: 佢自己冇意識到,但佢長久以來習慣咗想要佢冇嘅嘢,以致要當場講出佢真正想要乜嘢似乎唔可能——除非佢知道佢有乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她自己沒意識到,但她長久以來習慣了想要她沒有的東西,以致要當場說出她真正想要什麼似乎不可能——除非她知道她有什麼。

passages.original: Obviously, however, she must say something.
passages.vernacular: 但顯然,佢必須講點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但顯然,她必須說點什麼。

passages.original: This extraordinary child was waiting.
passages.vernacular: 呢個非凡嘅細路正在等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個非凡的孩子正在等著。

passages.original: “Well, of course, there's lamb broth--”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當然,有羊肉湯——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當然,有羊肉湯——」

passages.original: “I've got it!” crowed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「我有!」波麗安娜歡叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有!」波麗安娜歡叫道。

passages.original: “But that's what I DIDN'T want,” sighed the sick woman, sure now of what her stomach craved.
passages.vernacular: 「可嗰個係我唔想要嘅,」病婦嘆氣,而家確定咗佢嘅胃渴望乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可那是我不想要的,」病婦嘆氣,現在確定了她的胃渴望什麼。

passages.original: “It was chicken I wanted.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想要嘅係雞肉。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想要的是雞肉。」

passages.original: “Oh, I've got that, too,” chuckled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我都有嗰個,」波麗安娜咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我也有那個,」波麗安娜咯咯笑。

passages.original: The woman turned in amazement.
passages.vernacular: 嗰女人驚訝地轉過頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那女人驚訝地轉過頭。

passages.original: “Both of them?” she demanded.
passages.vernacular: 「兩樣都有?」佢質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「兩樣都有?」她質問。

passages.original: “Yes--and calf's-foot jelly,” triumphed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——仲有小牛腳凍,」波麗安娜得意地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——還有小牛腳凍,」波麗安娜得意地說。

passages.original: “I was just bound you should have what you wanted for once; so Nancy and I fixed it.
passages.vernacular: 「我就係決心讓您呢次得到您想要嘅;所以南希同我一起準備喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就是決心讓您這次得到您想要的;所以南希和我一起準備了。

passages.original: Oh, of course, there's only a little of each--but there's some of all of 'em!
passages.vernacular: 哦,當然,每樣只有啲點——但每樣都有啲!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,當然,每樣只有一點點——但每樣都有一些!

passages.original: I'm so glad you did want chicken,” she went on contentedly, as she lifted the three little bowls from her basket.
passages.vernacular: 我太高興您確實想要雞肉喇,」佢滿足地繼續講,把三個小碗從籃子裡攞出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興您確實想要雞肉了,」她滿足地繼續說,把三個小碗從籃子裡拿出來。

passages.original: “You see, I got to thinking on the way here--what if you should say tripe, or onions, or something like that, that I didn't have!
passages.vernacular: 「您睇,我喺路上想啊想——如果您講嘅係牛肚,或洋蔥,或類似嗰樣我冇嘅嘢點算!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您看,我在路上想啊想——如果您說的是牛肚,或洋蔥,或類似那樣我沒有的東西怎麼辦!

passages.original: Wouldn't it have been a shame--when I'd tried so hard?” she laughed merrily.
passages.vernacular: 嗰唔係好可惜嗎——我咁努力地試過?」佢快樂地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那不是很可惜嗎——我那麼努力地試過?」她快樂地笑了。

passages.original: There was no reply.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: The sick woman seemed to be trying--mentally to find something she had lost.
passages.vernacular: 病婦似乎喺努力——喺心裡尋找佢丟失嘅乜嘢嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 病婦似乎在努力——在心裡尋找她丟失的什麼東西。

passages.original: “There!
passages.vernacular: 「好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了!

passages.original: I'm to leave them all,” announced Pollyanna, as she arranged the three bowls in a row on the table.
passages.vernacular: 我把佢哋都留下,」波麗安娜宣布,把三個碗喺桌上排成一排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把它們都留下,」波麗安娜宣布,把三個碗在桌上排成一排。

passages.original: “Like enough it'll be lamb broth you want to-morrow.
passages.vernacular: 「好可能聽日您想要嘅係羊肉湯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很可能明天您想要的是羊肉湯。

passages.original: How do you do to-day?” she finished in polite inquiry.
passages.vernacular: 您今日點樣?」佢以禮貌嘅詢問結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您今天怎麼樣?」她以禮貌的詢問結束。

passages.original: “Very poorly, thank you,” murmured Mrs. Snow, falling back into her usual listless attitude.
passages.vernacular: 「好糟,謝謝,」斯諾太太喃喃道,又倒回佢平時無精打采嘅姿態。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很糟,謝謝,」斯諾太太喃喃道,又倒回她平時無精打采的姿態。

passages.original: “I lost my nap this morning.
passages.vernacular: 「今日朝早我冇瞓成午覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天早上我沒睡成午覺。

passages.original: Nellie Higgins next door has begun music lessons, and her practising drives me nearly wild.
passages.vernacular: 隔壁嘅內莉·希金斯開始上音樂課,佢嘅練習幾乎把我逼瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隔壁的內莉·希金斯開始上音樂課,她的練習幾乎把我逼瘋。

passages.original: She was at it all the morning--every minute!
passages.vernacular: 佢整個上午都喺練——每一分鐘!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她整個上午都在練——每一分鐘!

passages.original: I'm sure, I don't know what I shall do!”
passages.vernacular: 我確信,我唔知道我該點算!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信,我不知道我該怎麼辦!」

passages.original: Polly nodded sympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜同情地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜同情地點頭。

passages.original: “I know.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。

passages.original: It IS awful!
passages.vernacular: 呢確實可怕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這確實可怕!

passages.original: Mrs. White had it once--one of my Ladies' Aiders, you know.
passages.vernacular: 懷特太太有一次都係——我嘅婦女互助會嘅人之一,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懷特太太有一次也是——我的婦女互助會的人之一,你知道。

passages.original: She had rheumatic fever, too, at the same time, so she couldn't thrash 'round.
passages.vernacular: 佢同時仲得咗風濕熱,所以佢冇法翻嚟覆去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她同時還得了風濕熱,所以她沒法翻來覆去。

passages.original: She said 'twould have been easier if she could have.
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果佢能,會容易些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說如果她能,會容易些。

passages.original: Can you?”
passages.vernacular: 您能嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您能嗎?」

passages.original: “Can I--what?”
passages.vernacular: 「我能——乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我能——什麼?」

passages.original: “Thrash 'round--move, you know, so as to change your position when the music gets too hard to stand.”
passages.vernacular: 「翻嚟覆去——動,你知道,咁樣音樂難以忍受嘅時候可以換個姿勢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「翻來覆去——動,你知道,這樣音樂難以忍受的時候可以換個姿勢。」

passages.original: Mrs. Snow stared a little.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太有點瞪眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太有點瞪眼。

passages.original: “Why, of course I can move--anywhere--in bed,” she rejoined a little irritably.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我當然能動——喺床上邊兒都行,」佢有點煩躁地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我當然能動——在床上哪兒都行,」她有點煩躁地回答。

passages.original: “Well, you can be glad of that, then, anyhow, can't you?” nodded Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰您至少可以為呢個高興,係唔係?」波麗安娜點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那您至少可以為這個高興,是不是?」波麗安娜點頭。

passages.original: “Mrs. White couldn't.
passages.vernacular: 「懷特太太唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「懷特太太不能。

passages.original: You can't thrash when you have rheumatic fever--though you want to something awful, Mrs. White says.
passages.vernacular: 您得風濕熱嘅時候唔能夠翻嚟覆去——雖然您想得要命,懷特太太講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您得風濕熱的時候不能翻來覆去——雖然您想得要命,懷特太太說。

passages.original: She told me afterwards she reckoned she'd have gone raving crazy if it hadn't been for Mr. White's sister's ears--being deaf, so.”
passages.vernacular: 佢後來告訴我,佢想如果唔係因為懷特先生嘅姐姐嘅耳朵——聾喇,所以——佢會發瘋嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她後來告訴我,她想如果不是因為懷特先生的姐姐的耳朵——聾了,所以——她會發瘋的。」

passages.original: “Sister's--EARS!
passages.vernacular: 「姐姐嘅——耳朵!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「姐姐的——耳朵!

passages.original: What do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼意思?」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: “Well, I reckon I didn't tell it all, and I forgot you didn't know Mrs. White.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想我冇講全,我忘咗您不認識懷特太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想我沒講全,我忘了您不認識懷特太太。

passages.original: You see, Miss White was deaf--awfully deaf; and she came to visit 'em and to help take care of Mrs. White and the house.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,懷特小姐係聾嘅——好聾;佢嚟睇望佢哋,並幫忙照顧懷特太太同房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,懷特小姐是聾的——非常聾;她來看望他們,並幫忙照顧懷特太太和房子。

passages.original: Well, they had such an awful time making her understand ANYTHING, that after that, every time the piano commenced to play across the street, Mrs. White felt so glad she COULD hear it, that she didn't mind so much that she DID hear it, 'cause she couldn't help thinking how awful 'twould be if she was deaf and couldn't hear anything, like her husband's sister.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,佢哋讓佢理解任何事都咁困難,所以後來,每當對面街上嘅鋼琴開始響,懷特太太就為佢能聽見而高興,咁佢就不咁介意佢確實聽見喇,因為佢禁不住想,如果佢像佢丈夫嘅姐姐嗰樣聾咗、乜嘢都聽唔見,嗰該多可怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,他們讓她理解任何事都那麼困難,所以後來,每當對面街上的鋼琴開始響,懷特太太就為她能聽見而高興,那麼她就不那麼介意她確實聽見了,因為她禁不住想,如果她像她丈夫的姐姐那樣聾了、什麼也聽不見,那該多可怕。

passages.original: You see, she was playing the game, too.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,佢都喺玩遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,她也在玩遊戲。

passages.original: I'd told her about it.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴過佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴過她。」

passages.original: “The--game?”
Pollyanna clapped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜拍手。

passages.original: “There!
passages.vernacular: 「對喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對了!

passages.original: I 'most forgot; but I've thought it up, Mrs. Snow--what you can be glad about.”
passages.vernacular: 我差點忘喇;不過我想出嚟喇,斯諾太太——您可以點解高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我差點忘了;不過我想出來了,斯諾太太——您可以為什麼高興。」

passages.original: “GLAD about!
passages.vernacular: 「高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興!

passages.original: What do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Why, I told you I would.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我講過我會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我說過我會的。

passages.original: Don't you remember?
passages.vernacular: 您不記得嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不記得嗎?

passages.original: You asked me to tell you something to be glad about--glad, you know, even though you did have to lie here abed all day.”
passages.vernacular: 您要我告訴您一件值得高興嘅事——高興,您知道,即使您得整天躺喺床上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您要我告訴您一件值得高興的事——高興,您知道,即使您得整天躺在床上。」

passages.original: “Oh!” scoffed the woman.
passages.vernacular: 「哦!」嗰女人嘲笑道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦!」那女人嘲笑道。

passages.original: “THAT?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個?

passages.original: Yes, I remember that; but I didn't suppose you were in earnest any more than I was.”
passages.vernacular: 係,我記得;不過我冇想到你比我更認真。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,我記得;不過我沒想到你比我更認真。」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, I was,” nodded Pollyanna, triumphantly; “and I found it, too.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,我認真喇,」波麗安娜得意地點頭;「我都找到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,我認真了,」波麗安娜得意地點頭;「我也找到了。

passages.original: But 'TWAS hard.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰確實難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那確實難。

passages.original: It's all the more fun, though, always, when 'tis hard.
passages.vernacular: 不過越難,總是越好玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過越難,總是越好玩。

passages.original: And I will own up, honest to true, that I couldn't think of anything for a while.
passages.vernacular: 我老實承認,有一陣子我乜嘢都想不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我老實承認,有一陣子我什麼也想不出來。

passages.original: Then I got it.”
passages.vernacular: 然後我想到喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我想到了。」

passages.original: “Did you, really?
passages.vernacular: 「你真嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真的?

passages.original: Well, what is it?”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,是什麼?」

passages.original: Mrs. Snow's voice was sarcastically polite.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太嘅聲音帶住諷刺嘅禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太的聲音帶著諷刺的禮貌。

passages.original: Pollyanna drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜深吸一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜深吸一口氣。

passages.original: “I thought--how glad you could be--that other folks weren't like you--all sick in bed like this, you know,” she announced impressively.
passages.vernacular: 「我想——您可以多高興——別人不像您——都病喺床上咁樣,你知道,」佢印象深刻地宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想——您可以多高興——別人不像您——都病在床上這樣,你知道,」她印象深刻地宣布。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow stared.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太瞪住眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太瞪著眼。

passages.original: Her eyes were angry.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛含住怒意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛含著怒意。

passages.original: “Well, really!” she ejaculated then, in not quite an agreeable tone of voice.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,真係!」佢然後用不太愉快嘅語氣喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,真是!」她然後用不太愉快的語氣喊道。

passages.original: “And now I'll tell you the game,” proposed Pollyanna, blithely confident.
passages.vernacular: 「而家我嚟告訴您呢個遊戲,」波麗安娜輕快而自信地提議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在我來告訴您這個遊戲,」波麗安娜輕快而自信地提議。

passages.original: “It'll be just lovely for you to play--it'll be so hard.
passages.vernacular: 「您玩會好玩極喇——佢會咁難。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您玩會好玩極了——它會那麼難。

passages.original: And there's so much more fun when it is hard!
passages.vernacular: 而難嘅時候好玩多喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而難的時候好玩多了!

passages.original: You see, it's like this.”
passages.vernacular: 您睇,係咁樣嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,是這樣的。」

passages.original: And she began to tell of the missionary barrel, the crutches, and the doll that did not come.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢開始講傳教士捐贈桶、拐杖同冇嚟嘅洋娃娃嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她開始講傳教士捐贈桶、拐杖和沒有來的洋娃娃的事。

passages.original: The story was just finished when Milly appeared at the door.
passages.vernacular: 故事剛講完,米莉出而家門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 故事剛講完,米莉出現在門口。

passages.original: “Your aunt is wanting you, Miss Pollyanna,” she said with dreary listlessness.
passages.vernacular: 「你姨媽喺找你,波麗安娜小姐,」佢帶住憂鬱嘅無精打采講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你姨媽在找你,波麗安娜小姐,」她帶著憂鬱的無精打采說。

passages.original: “She telephoned down to the Harlows' across the way.
passages.vernacular: 「佢打電話到對面嘅哈洛家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她打電話到對面的哈洛家。

passages.original: She says you're to hurry--that you've got some practising to make up before dark.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講你要快回去——天黑前你有些練習要補。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說你要快回去——天黑前你有些練習要補。」

passages.original: Pollyanna rose reluctantly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜不情願地站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜不情願地站起來。

passages.original: “All right,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “I'll hurry.”
passages.vernacular: 「我快點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我快點。」

passages.original: Suddenly she laughed.
passages.vernacular: 佢突然笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她突然笑了。

passages.original: “I suppose I ought to be glad I've got legs to hurry with, hadn't I, Mrs. Snow?”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我該高興我有腿可以快點,係唔係,斯諾太太?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我該高興我有腿可以快點,是不是,斯諾太太?」

passages.original: There was no answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow's eyes were closed.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太閉住眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太閉著眼睛。

passages.original: But Milly, whose eyes were wide open with surprise, saw that there were tears on the wasted cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 但米莉睜大咗驚訝嘅眼睛,睇到嗰消瘦嘅臉頰上有淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但米莉睜大了驚訝的眼睛,看到那消瘦的臉頰上有淚水。

passages.original: “Good-by,” flung Pollyanna over her shoulder, as she reached the door.
passages.vernacular: 「再見,」波麗安娜走到門口時,回頭喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見,」波麗安娜走到門口時,回頭喊道。

passages.original: “I'm awfully sorry about the hair--I wanted to do it.
passages.vernacular: 「我為頭髮抱歉得好——我本想弄嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為頭髮抱歉得很——我本想弄的。

passages.original: But maybe I can next time!”
passages.vernacular: 不過下次或者可以!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過下次也許可以!」

passages.original: One by one the July days passed.
passages.vernacular: 七月嘅日子一天一天過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 七月的日子一天一天過去。

passages.original: To Pollyanna, they were happy days, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 對波麗安娜來講,確實係快樂嘅日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對波麗安娜來說,確實是快樂的日子。

passages.original: She often told her aunt, joyously, how very happy they were.
passages.vernacular: 佢常高興地告訴佢姨媽佢哋幾咁快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她常高興地告訴她姨媽它們多麼快樂。

passages.original: Whereupon her aunt would usually reply, wearily:
passages.vernacular: 佢姨媽通常就疲倦地回答:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她姨媽通常就疲倦地回答:

passages.original: “Very well, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「好好,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,波麗安娜。

passages.original: I am gratified, of course, that they are happy; but I trust that they are profitable, as well--otherwise I should have failed signally in my duty.”
passages.vernacular: 我當然好高興佢哋快樂;但我相信佢哋都有益處——否則我就喺責任上明顯失敗喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當然很高興它們快樂;但我相信它們也有益處——否則我就在責任上明顯失敗了。」

passages.original: Generally Pollyanna would answer this with a hug and a kiss--a proceeding that was still always most disconcerting to Miss Polly; but one day she spoke.
passages.vernacular: 通常波麗安娜對此嘅回答係一個擁抱同一個吻——呢舉動總定係讓波莉小姐好侷促不安;但有一天佢講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 通常波麗安娜對此的回答是一個擁抱和一個吻——這舉動總還是讓波莉小姐非常侷促不安;但有一天她說話了。

passages.original: It was during the sewing hour.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係喺縫紉時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是在縫紉時間。

passages.original: “Do you mean that it wouldn't be enough then, Aunt Polly, that they should be just happy days?” she asked wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 「您嘅意思係講,波莉姨媽,嗰樣唔夠,只係快樂嘅日子嗎?」佢若有所思地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您的意思是說,波莉姨媽,那樣不夠,只是快樂的日子嗎?」她若有所思地問。

passages.original: “That is what I mean, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係我嘅意思,波麗安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是我的意思,波麗安娜。」

passages.original: “They must be pro-fi-ta-ble as well?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋仲必須有——益——處?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它們還必須有——益——處?」

passages.original: “Certainly.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。」

passages.original: “What is being pro-fi-ta-ble?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢係有——益——處?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼是有——益——處?」

passages.original: “Why, it--it's just being profitable--having profit, something to show for it, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,佢——佢就係有益處——有收益,有攞得出手嘅嘢,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,它——它就是有益處——有收益,有拿得出手的東西,波麗安娜。

passages.original: What an extraordinary child you are!”
passages.vernacular: 你真係個非凡嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你真是個非凡的孩子!」

passages.original: “Then just being glad isn't pro-fi-ta-ble?” questioned Pollyanna, a little anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 「咁只係高興就冇益處嗎?」波麗安娜有點焦慮地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼只是高興就沒益處嗎?」波麗安娜有點焦慮地問。

passages.original: “Certainly not.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然沒有。」

passages.original: “O dear!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪!

passages.original: Then you wouldn't like it, of course.
passages.vernacular: 嗰您當然唔會鍾意佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那您當然不會喜歡它了。

passages.original: I'm afraid, now, you won't ever play the game, Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 我怕您永遠唔會玩呢遊戲喇,波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕您永遠不會玩這遊戲了,波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: “Game?
passages.vernacular: 「遊戲?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「遊戲?

passages.original: What game?”
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢遊戲?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼遊戲?」

passages.original: “Why, that father--” Pollyanna clapped her hand to her lips.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,就係爸爸——」波麗安娜用手捂住嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,就是爸爸——」波麗安娜用手捂住嘴。

passages.original: “N-nothing,” she stammered.
passages.vernacular: 「冇——冇乜嘢,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒——沒什麼,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: Miss Polly frowned.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺眉。

passages.original: “That will do for this morning, Pollyanna,” she said tersely.
passages.vernacular: 「今日早晨到此為止,波麗安娜,」佢簡短地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今天早晨到此為止,波麗安娜,」她簡短地說。

passages.original: And the sewing lesson was over.
passages.vernacular: 縫紉課結束喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 縫紉課結束了。

passages.original: It was that afternoon that Pollyanna, coming down from her attic room, met her aunt on the stairway.
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰天下午,波麗安娜從閣樓房間下嚟,喺樓梯上遇到佢姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那天下午,波麗安娜從閣樓房間下來,在樓梯上遇到她姨媽。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, how perfectly lovely!” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,幾咁美好啊!」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,多麼美好啊!」她喊道。

passages.original: “You were coming up to see me!
passages.vernacular: 「您係嚟睇我嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您是來看我的!

passages.original: Come right in.
passages.vernacular: 快進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快進來。

passages.original: I love company,” she finished, scampering up the stairs and throwing her door wide open.
passages.vernacular: 我愛有人嚟,」佢蹦跳住上樓,把佢嘅門大大打開結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛有人來,」她蹦跳著上樓,把她的門大大打開結束。

passages.original: Now Miss Polly had not been intending to call on her niece.
passages.vernacular: 其實波莉小姐並冇打算拜訪佢嘅外甥女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其實波莉小姐並沒打算拜訪她的外甥女。

passages.original: She had been planning to look for a certain white wool shawl in the cedar chest near the east window.
passages.vernacular: 佢本來計劃喺東窗附近嘅雪松箱子裡找一條某條白羊毛披肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本來計劃在東窗附近的雪松箱子裡找一條某條白羊毛披肩。

passages.original: But to her unbounded surprise now, she found herself, not in the main attic before the cedar chest, but in Pollyanna's little room sitting in one of the straight-backed chairs--so many, many times since Pollyanna came, Miss Polly had found herself like this, doing some utterly unexpected, surprising thing, quite unlike the thing she had set out to do!
passages.vernacular: 但令佢大為驚訝嘅係,佢而家發現自己不喺大閣樓嘅雪松箱子前,而係喺波麗安娜嘅小房間裡,坐喺一張直背椅子上——自從波麗安娜嚟後,波莉小姐發現自己好多好多次係咁樣,做住某件完全出乎意料、令人驚訝嘅事,同佢出發要做嘅事完全不同!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但令她大為驚訝的是,她現在發現自己不在大閣樓的雪松箱子前,而是在波麗安娜的小房間裡,坐在一張直背椅子上——自從波麗安娜來後,波莉小姐發現自己很多很多次是這樣,做著某件完全出乎意料、令人驚訝的事,與她出發要做的事完全不同!

passages.original: “I love company,” said Pollyanna, again, flitting about as if she were dispensing the hospitality of a palace; “specially since I've had this room, all mine, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛有人嚟,」波麗安娜又講,飛嚟飛去,好像喺施展宮殿嘅款待;「尤其係我有咗呢個房間,完全屬於我嘅,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛有人來,」波麗安娜又說,飛來飛去,好像在施展宮殿的款待;「尤其是我有了這個房間,完全屬於我的,你知道。

passages.original: Oh, of course, I had a room, always, but 'twas a hired room, and hired rooms aren't half as nice as owned ones, are they?
passages.vernacular: 哦,當然我一直有房間,但嗰個係租嚟嘅房間,租嚟嘅房間不如自己嘅一半好,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,當然我一直有房間,但那是租來的房間,租來的房間不如自己的一半好,是不是?

passages.original: And of course I do own this one, don't I?”
passages.vernacular: 而且我當然擁有呢個,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我當然擁有這個,是不是?」

passages.original: “Why, y-yes, Pollyanna,” murmured Miss Polly, vaguely wondering why she did not get up at once and go to look for that shawl.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係——係嘅,波麗安娜,」波莉小姐喃喃道,隱約納悶自己點解不即刻站起嚟去找嗰條披肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是——是的,波麗安娜,」波莉小姐喃喃道,隱約納悶自己為什麼不馬上站起來去找那條披肩。

passages.original: “And of course NOW I just love this room, even if it hasn't got the carpets and curtains and pictures that I'd been want--” With a painful blush Pollyanna stopped short.
passages.vernacular: 「而且當然而家我就愛呢個房間,即使佢冇我一直想要嘅地毯、窗簾同畫——」波麗安娜痛苦地臉紅,突然停住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且當然現在我就愛這個房間,即使它沒有我一直想要的地毯、窗簾和畫——」波麗安娜痛苦地臉紅,突然停住。

passages.original: She was plunging into an entirely different sentence when her aunt interrupted her sharply.
passages.vernacular: 佢正衝進一個完全不同嘅句子,佢姨媽尖銳地打斷咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她正衝進一個完全不同的句子,她姨媽尖銳地打斷了她。

passages.original: “What's that, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係乜嘢,波麗安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是什麼,波麗安娜?」

passages.original: “N-nothing, Aunt Polly, truly.
passages.vernacular: 「冇——冇乜嘢,波莉姨媽,真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒——沒什麼,波莉姨媽,真的。

passages.original: I didn't mean to say it.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔想講嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想說的。」

passages.original: “Probably not,” returned Miss Polly, coldly; “but you did say it, so suppose we have the rest of it.”
passages.vernacular: 「可能唔想,」波莉小姐冷冷地回答;「但你講喇,所以讓我哋聽聽剩下嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可能不想,」波莉小姐冷冷地回答;「但你說了,所以讓我們聽聽剩下的。」

passages.original: “But it wasn't anything only that I'd been kind of planning on pretty carpets and lace curtains and things, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「可嗰冇乜嘢,只係我一直有點計劃要漂亮嘅地毯、蕾絲窗簾同嗰啲嘢,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可那沒什麼,只是我一直有點計劃要漂亮的地毯、蕾絲窗簾和那些東西,你知道。

passages.original: But, of course--”
passages.vernacular: 但係,當然——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,當然——」

passages.original: “PLANNING on them!” interrupted Miss Polly, sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「計劃要佢哋!」波莉小姐尖銳地打斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「計劃要它們!」波莉小姐尖銳地打斷。

passages.original: Pollyanna blushed still more painfully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜臉紅得更痛苦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜臉紅得更痛苦了。

passages.original: “I ought not to have, of course, Aunt Polly,” she apologized.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔應該該,當然,波莉姨媽,」佢道歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不應該,當然,波莉姨媽,」她道歉。

passages.original: “It was only because I'd always wanted them and hadn't had them, I suppose.
passages.vernacular: 「只係因為我一直想要佢哋卻冇,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是因為我一直想要它們卻沒有,我想。

passages.original: Oh, we'd had two rugs in the barrels, but they were little, you know, and one had ink spots, and the other holes; and there never were only those two pictures; the one fath--I mean the good one we sold, and the bad one that broke.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我哋桶裡有過兩塊地墊,但佢哋好小,你知道,一塊有墨水漬,另一塊有洞;而且只有過嗰兩幅畫;一幅爸——我係講好嘅我哋賣喇,壞嘅破喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我們桶裡有過兩塊地墊,但它們很小,你知道,一塊有墨水漬,另一塊有洞;而且只有過那兩幅畫;一幅爸——我是說好的我們賣了,壞的破了。

passages.original: Of course if it hadn't been for all that I shouldn't have wanted them, so--pretty things, I mean; and I shouldn't have got to planning all through the hall that first day how pretty mine would be here, and--and--but, truly, Aunt Polly, it wasn't but just a minute--I mean, a few minutes--before I was being glad that the bureau DIDN'T have a looking-glass, because it didn't show my freckles; and there couldn't be a nicer picture than the one out my window there; and you've been so good to me, that--”
passages.vernacular: 當然如果唔係因為呢一切,我就唔會想要佢哋,所以——我係講漂亮嘅嘢;我都唔會喺第一天一路走過走廊時,計劃我嘅喺呢度會多漂亮,仲有——仲有——不過,真嘅,波莉姨媽,只不過一分鐘——我係講,幾分鐘——我就高興呢個五斗櫃冇鏡子,因為佢照不出我嘅雀斑;而且冇比我窗外嗰幅更好嘅畫喇;仲有你一直對我咁好,所以——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然如果不是因為這一切,我就不會想要它們,所以——我是說漂亮的東西;我也不會在第一天一路走過走廊時,計劃我的在這裡會多漂亮,還有——還有——不過,真的,波莉姨媽,只不過一分鐘——我是說,幾分鐘——我就高興這個五斗櫃沒有鏡子,因為它照不出我的雀斑;而且沒有比我窗外那幅更好的畫了;還有你一直對我那麼好,所以——」

passages.original: Miss Polly rose suddenly to her feet.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐突然站起身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐突然站起身。

passages.original: Her face was very red.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉好紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉非常紅。

passages.original: “That will do, Pollyanna,” she said stiffly.
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,波麗安娜,」佢僵硬地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,波麗安娜,」她僵硬地說。

passages.original: “You have said quite enough, I'm sure.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確信你講得夠多喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確信你說得夠多了。」

passages.original: The next minute she had swept down the stairs--and not until she reached the first floor did it suddenly occur to her that she had gone up into the attic to find a white wool shawl in the cedar chest near the east window.
passages.vernacular: 下一分鐘佢已經走下咗樓——直到佢走到一樓,佢才突然想起,佢上閣樓係去東窗附近嘅雪松箱子裡找一條白羊毛披肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一分鐘她已經走下了樓——直到她走到一樓,她才突然想起,她上閣樓是去東窗附近的雪松箱子裡找一條白羊毛披肩。

passages.original: Less than twenty-four hours later, Miss Polly said to Nancy, crisply:
passages.vernacular: 唔到二十四小時後,波莉小姐乾脆地對南希講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不到二十四小時後,波莉小姐乾脆地對南希說:

passages.original: “Nancy, you may move Miss Pollyanna's things down-stairs this morning to the room directly beneath.
passages.vernacular: 「南希,今日早晨你可以把波麗安娜小姐嘅嘢搬到正下方嘅嗰間房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,今天早晨你可以把波麗安娜小姐的東西搬到正下方的那間房間。

passages.original: I have decided to have my niece sleep there for the present.”
passages.vernacular: 我決定暫時讓我嘅外甥女瞓嗰度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我決定暫時讓我的外甥女睡那裡。」

passages.original: “Yes, ma'am,” said Nancy aloud.
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人,」南希大聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人,」南希大聲說。

passages.original: “O glory!” said Nancy to herself.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,榮耀啊!」南希自言自語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,榮耀啊!」南希自言自語。

passages.original: To Pollyanna, a minute later, she cried joyously:
passages.vernacular: 一分鐘後,佢高興地對波麗安娜喊:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一分鐘後,她高興地對波麗安娜喊:

passages.original: “And won't ye jest be listenin' ter this, Miss Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「你聽聽呢個,波麗安娜小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你聽聽這個,波麗安娜小姐。

passages.original: You're ter sleep down-stairs in the room straight under this.
passages.vernacular: 你要瞓樓下喇,就喺呢間正下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要睡樓下了,就在這間正下面。

passages.original: You are--you are!”
passages.vernacular: 真嘅——真嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的——真的!」

passages.original: Pollyanna actually grew white.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜竟然白咗臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜竟然白了臉。

passages.original: “You mean--why, Nancy, not really--really and truly?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係講——嗨,南希,唔係真嘅——真真正正嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是說——嗨,南希,不是真的——真真正正的?」

passages.original: “I guess you'll think it's really and truly,” prophesied Nancy, exultingly, nodding her head to Pollyanna over the armful of dresses she had taken from the closet.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你會覺得係真真正正嘅,」南希得意地預言,朝波麗安娜點頭,懷裡抱住佢從衣櫃裡攞出嚟嘅一大堆裙子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你會覺得是真真正正的,」南希得意地預言,朝波麗安娜點頭,懷裡抱著她從衣櫃裡拿出來的一大堆裙子。

passages.original: “I'm told ter take down yer things, and I'm goin' ter take 'em, too, 'fore she gets a chance ter change her mind.”
passages.vernacular: 「我被告知要搬你嘅嘢下去,我都要搬,趁佢嚟得及改變主意之前。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我被告知要搬你的東西下去,我也要搬,趁她來得及改變主意之前。」

passages.original: Pollyanna did not stop to hear the end of this sentence.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜冇停下聽呢句話嘅結尾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜沒停下聽這句話的結尾。

passages.original: At the imminent risk of being dashed headlong, she was flying down-stairs, two steps at a time.
passages.vernacular: 冒住隨時被摔個頭朝下嘅危險,佢正飛快地跑下樓梯,一次兩級。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冒著隨時被摔個頭朝下的危險,她正飛快地跑下樓梯,一次兩級。

passages.original: Bang went two doors and a chair before Pollyanna at last reached her goal--Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 兩扇門同一把椅子砰砰響過,波麗安娜終於到達佢嘅目標——波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩扇門和一把椅子砰砰響過,波麗安娜終於到達她的目標——波莉姨媽。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly, did you mean it, really?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,您係認真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,您是認真的嗎?

passages.original: Why, that room's got EVERYTHING--the carpet and curtains and three pictures, besides the one outdoors, too, 'cause the windows look the same way.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,嗰個房間有一切——地毯、窗簾,三幅畫,仲有外面嗰幅,因為窗子朝同一個方向。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,那個房間有一切——地毯、窗簾,三幅畫,還有外面那幅,因為窗子朝同一個方向。

passages.original: Oh, Aunt Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: “Very well, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「好好,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,波麗安娜。

passages.original: I am gratified that you like the change, of course; but if you think so much of all those things, I trust you will take proper care of them; that's all.
passages.vernacular: 我當然好高興你鍾意呢個變化;不過如果你咁睇重呢啲嘢,我相信你會好好愛護佢哋;就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我當然很高興你喜歡這個變化;不過如果你這麼看重這些東西,我相信你會好好愛護它們;就是這樣。

passages.original: Pollyanna, please pick up that chair; and you have banged two doors in the last half-minute.”
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜,請把嗰把椅子扶起嚟;而且你喺過去半分鐘裡摔咗兩扇門。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜,請把那把椅子扶起來;而且你在過去半分鐘裡摔了兩扇門。」

passages.original: Miss Polly spoke sternly, all the more sternly because, for some inexplicable reason, she felt inclined to cry--and Miss Polly was not used to feeling inclined to cry.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐講得嚴厲,更嚴厲係因為,唔知乜嘢無法解釋嘅原因,佢覺得想哭——而波莉小姐係不習慣覺得想哭嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐說得嚴厲,更嚴厲是因為,不知什麼無法解釋的原因,她覺得想哭——而波莉小姐是不習慣覺得想哭的。

passages.original: Pollyanna picked up the chair.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜扶起椅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜扶起椅子。

passages.original: “Yes'm; I know I banged 'em--those doors,” she admitted cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人;我知道我摔咗佢哋——嗰啲門,」佢愉快地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人;我知道我摔了它們——那些門,」她愉快地承認。

passages.original: “You see I'd just found out about the room, and I reckon you'd have banged doors if--” Pollyanna stopped short and eyed her aunt with new interest.
passages.vernacular: 「您睇我剛知道房間嘅事,我想如果係您,您都會摔門嘅,如果——」波麗安娜突然停住,以新嘅興趣打量佢姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您看我剛知道房間的事,我想如果是您,您也會摔門的,如果——」波麗安娜突然停住,以新的興趣打量她姨媽。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, DID you ever bang doors?”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,您摔過門嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,您摔過門嗎?」

passages.original: “I hope--not, Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「我希望——冇,波麗安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望——沒有,波麗安娜!」

passages.original: Miss Polly's voice was properly shocked.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅聲音適當地顯得震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的聲音適當地顯得震驚。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, what a shame!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,真可惜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,真可惜!」

passages.original: Pollyanna's face expressed only concerned sympathy.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅臉上只表現出關切嘅同情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的臉上只表現出關切的同情。

passages.original: “A shame!” repeated Aunt Polly, too dazed to say more.
passages.vernacular: 「可惜!」波莉姨媽重複道,太發懵,講不出更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可惜!」波莉姨媽重複道,太發懵,說不出更多。

passages.original: “Why, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係啊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是啊。

passages.original: You see, if you'd felt like banging doors you'd have banged 'em, of course; and if you didn't, that must have meant that you weren't ever glad over anything--or you would have banged 'em.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,如果您想摔門,您當然就會摔;如果您冇,嗰一定意味住您從來冇為任何事高興過——否則您就會摔喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,如果您想摔門,您當然就會摔;如果您沒有,那一定意味著您從來沒有為任何事高興過——否則您就會摔了。

passages.original: You couldn't have helped it.
passages.vernacular: 您忍不住嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您忍不住的。

passages.original: And I'm so sorry you weren't ever glad over anything!”
passages.vernacular: 我太遺憾您從來冇為任何事高興過!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太遺憾您從來沒為任何事高興過!」

passages.original: “PollyANna!” gasped the lady; but Pollyanna was gone, and only the distant bang of the attic-stairway door answered for her.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜!」嗰位女士倒抽氣;但波麗安娜已經走喇,只有遠處閣樓樓梯門嘅砰一聲喺替佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜!」那位女士倒抽氣;但波麗安娜已經走了,只有遠處閣樓樓梯門的砰一聲在替她回答。

passages.original: Pollyanna had gone to help Nancy bring down “her things.”
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜去幫南希把「佢嘅嘢」搬下嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜去幫南希把「她的東西」搬下來了。

passages.original: Miss Polly, in the sitting room, felt vaguely disturbed;--but then, of course she HAD been glad--over some things!
passages.vernacular: 起居室裡嘅波莉小姐覺得隱隱不安;——不過,當然,佢確實高興過——為某些事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起居室裡的波莉小姐覺得隱隱不安;——可是,當然,她確實高興過——為某些事!

chapters.title: Ch. XI Introducing Jimmy 第十一章:認識吉米

passages.original: CH August came.
passages.vernacular: 八月到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 八月到了。

passages.original: August brought several surprises and some changes--none of which, however, were really a surprise to Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 八月帶嚟咗幾件驚訝同啲變化——不過其中冇一件對南希真係驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 八月帶來了幾件驚訝和一些變化——不過其中沒有一件對南希真是驚訝。

passages.original: Nancy, since Pollyanna's arrival, had come to look for surprises and changes.
passages.vernacular: 自波麗安娜到來以後,南希已經習慣咗期待驚訝同變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自波麗安娜到來以後,南希已經習慣了期待驚訝和變化。

passages.original: First there was the kitten.
passages.vernacular: 首先係小貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先是小貓。

passages.original: Pollyanna found the kitten mewing pitifully some distance down the road.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜喺離家有一段距離嘅路上發現咗可憐地喵喵叫嘅小貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜在離家有一段距離的路上發現了可憐地喵喵叫的小貓。

passages.original: When systematic questioning of the neighbors failed to find any one who claimed it, Pollyanna brought it home at once, as a matter of course.
passages.vernacular: 喺有系統地詢問鄰居哋,冇找到任何人認領之後,波麗安娜理所當然地即刻把佢帶回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在有系統地詢問鄰居們,沒找到任何人認領之後,波麗安娜理所當然地立刻把它帶回家。

passages.original: “And I was glad I didn't find any one who owned it, too,” she told her aunt in happy confidence; “'cause I wanted to bring it home all the time.
passages.vernacular: 「我都高興我冇找到任何主人,」佢快樂地信任地告訴佢姨媽;「因為我一直想把佢帶回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也高興我沒找到任何主人,」她快樂地信任地告訴她姨媽;「因為我一直想把它帶回家。

passages.original: I love kitties.
passages.vernacular: 我愛小貓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛小貓。

passages.original: I knew you'd be glad to let it live here.”
passages.vernacular: 我知道您會高興讓佢住喺呢度嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道您會高興讓它住在這裡的。」

passages.original: Miss Polly looked at the forlorn little gray bunch of neglected misery in Pollyanna's arms, and shivered: Miss Polly did not care for cats--not even pretty, healthy, clean ones.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐睇住波麗安娜懷裡嗰團無人照顧嘅、悲慘嘅小灰團,打咗個寒戰:波莉小姐不鍾意貓——邊怕係漂亮、健康、乾淨嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐看著波麗安娜懷裡那團無人照顧的、悲慘的小灰團,打了個寒戰:波莉小姐不喜歡貓——哪怕是漂亮、健康、乾淨的。

passages.original: “Ugh!
Pollyanna!
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜!

passages.original: What a dirty little beast!
passages.vernacular: 多髒嘅小畜生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多髒的小畜生!

passages.original: And it's sick, I'm sure, and all mangy and fleay.”
passages.vernacular: 我確信佢仲生病喇,全身長癬又長跳蚤。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信它還生病了,全身長癬又長跳蚤。」

passages.original: “I know it, poor little thing,” crooned Pollyanna, tenderly, looking into the little creature's frightened eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,可憐嘅小嘢,」波麗安娜溫柔地哼住,睇住小傢伙驚恐嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,可憐的小東西,」波麗安娜溫柔地哼著,看著小傢伙驚恐的眼睛。

passages.original: “And it's all trembly, too, it's so scared.
passages.vernacular: 「佢仲喺發抖呢,嚇壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它還在發抖呢,嚇壞了。

passages.original: You see it doesn't know, yet, that we're going to keep it, of course.”
passages.vernacular: 您睇佢仲唔知道,我哋會收養佢,當然。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看它還不知道,我們會收養它,當然。」

passages.original: “No--nor anybody else,” retorted Miss Polly, with meaning emphasis.
passages.vernacular: 「不——別人都唔知道,」波莉小姐有意強調地反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——別人也不知道,」波莉小姐有意強調地反駁。

passages.original: “Oh, yes, they do,” nodded Pollyanna, entirely misunderstanding her aunt's words.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢哋知道,」波麗安娜點頭,完全誤解咗佢姨媽嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他們知道,」波麗安娜點頭,完全誤解了她姨媽的話。

passages.original: “I told everybody we should keep it, if I didn't find where it belonged.
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴所有人我哋會養佢,如果我找唔到佢嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴所有人我們會養它,如果我找不到它的主人。

passages.original: I knew you'd be glad to have it--poor little lonesome thing!”
passages.vernacular: 我知道您會高興有佢——可憐孤單嘅小嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道您會高興有它——可憐孤單的小東西!」

passages.original: Miss Polly opened her lips and tried to speak; but in vain.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐張開嘴唇試圖講話;但徒勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐張開嘴唇試圖說話;但徒勞。

passages.original: The curious helpless feeling that had been hers so often since Pollyanna's arrival, had her now fast in its grip.
passages.vernacular: 自波麗安娜到來以來佢常有嘅嗰種奇怪嘅無助感,而家緊緊地攫住咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自波麗安娜到來以來她常有的那種奇怪的無助感,現在緊緊地攫住了她。

passages.original: “Of course I knew,” hurried on Pollyanna, gratefully, “that you wouldn't let a dear little lonesome kitty go hunting for a home when you'd just taken ME in; and I said so to Mrs. Ford when she asked if you'd let me keep it.
passages.vernacular: 「當然我知道,」波麗安娜感激地匆忙繼續,「您唔會讓一隻親愛嘅孤單小貓去找家,而您啱啱收留咗我;我都咁對福特太太講,佢問您係咪會讓我養佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然我知道,」波麗安娜感激地匆忙繼續,「您不會讓一隻親愛的孤單小貓去找家,而您剛剛收留了我;我也這麼對福特太太說,她問您是否會讓我養它。

passages.original: Why, I had the Ladies' Aid, you know, and kitty didn't have anybody.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,我有婦女互助會,您知道,而小貓乜嘢人都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,我有婦女互助會,您知道,而小貓什麼人也沒有。

passages.original: I knew you'd feel that way,” she nodded happily, as she ran from the room.
passages.vernacular: 我知道您會咁想,」佢高興地點頭,跑出咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道您會這麼想,」她高興地點頭,跑出了房間。

passages.original: “But, Pollyanna, Pollyanna,” remonstrated Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,波麗安娜,波麗安娜,」波莉小姐勸阻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,波麗安娜,波麗安娜,」波莉小姐勸阻。

passages.original: “I don't--” But Pollyanna was already halfway to the kitchen, calling:
passages.vernacular: 「我不——」但波麗安娜已經跑到廚房一半喇,喊住:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不——」但波麗安娜已經跑到廚房一半了,喊著:

passages.original: “Nancy, Nancy, just see this dear little kitty that Aunt Polly is going to bring up along with me!”
passages.vernacular: 「南希,南希,快睇呢隻親愛嘅小貓,波莉姨媽要同我一起養大佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,南希,快看這隻親愛的小貓,波莉姨媽要同我一起養大它!」

passages.original: And Aunt Polly, in the sitting room--who abhorred cats--fell back in her chair with a gasp of dismay, powerless to remonstrate.
passages.vernacular: 而起居室裡嘅波莉姨媽——佢憎惡貓——驚恐地喘住氣倒回椅子裡,無力勸阻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而起居室裡的波莉姨媽——她憎惡貓——驚恐地喘著氣倒回椅子裡,無力勸阻。

passages.original: The next day it was a dog, even dirtier and more forlorn, perhaps, than was the kitten; and again Miss Polly, to her dumfounded amazement, found herself figuring as a kind protector and an angel of mercy--a role that Pollyanna so unhesitatingly thrust upon her as a matter of course, that the woman--who abhorred dogs even more than she did cats, if possible--found herself as before, powerless to remonstrate.
passages.vernacular: 第二天係一隻狗,或者比小貓更髒更可憐;波莉小姐又一次驚駭地發現自己成咗一個仁慈嘅保護者同慈悲嘅天使——波麗安娜咁毫不猶豫、理所當然地把呢個角色強加畀佢,以致嗰個憎惡狗甚至比憎惡貓更甚嘅女人,又像之前一樣,無力勸阻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天是一隻狗,也許比小貓更髒更可憐;波莉小姐又一次驚駭地發現自己成了一個仁慈的保護者和慈悲的天使——波麗安娜那麼毫不猶豫、理所當然地把這個角色強加給她,以致那個憎惡狗甚至比憎惡貓更甚的女人,又像之前一樣,無力勸阻。

passages.original: When, in less than a week, however, Pollyanna brought home a small, ragged boy, and confidently claimed the same protection for him, Miss Polly did have something to say.
passages.vernacular: 然而,唔到一個星期,波麗安娜又帶回家一個衣衫襤褸嘅小男孩,並自信地為佢要求同樣嘅庇護時,波莉小姐確實有話要講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,不到一個星期,波麗安娜又帶回家一個衣衫襤褸的小男孩,並自信地為他要求同樣的庇護時,波莉小姐確實有話要說了。

passages.original: It happened after this wise.
passages.vernacular: 事情係咁樣發生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事情是這樣發生的。

passages.original: On a pleasant Thursday morning Pollyanna had been taking calf's-foot jelly again to Mrs. Snow.
passages.vernacular: 一個晴朗嘅星期四早晨,波麗安娜又畀斯諾太太帶小牛腳凍去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個晴朗的星期四早晨,波麗安娜又給斯諾太太帶小牛腳凍去。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow and Pollyanna were the best of friends now.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太同波麗安娜而家係最好嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太和波麗安娜現在是最好的朋友。

passages.original: Their friendship had started from the third visit Pollyanna had made, the one after she had told Mrs. Snow of the game.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋嘅友誼從波麗安娜第三次探訪開始,就係佢告訴斯諾太太遊戲之後嗰一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們的友誼從波麗安娜第三次探訪開始,就是她告訴斯諾太太遊戲之後那一次。

passages.original: Mrs. Snow herself was playing the game now, with Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 斯諾太太自己而家都喺同波麗安娜玩呢個遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斯諾太太自己現在也在同波麗安娜玩這個遊戲。

passages.original: To be sure, she was not playing it very well--she had been sorry for everything for so long, that it was not easy to be glad for anything now.
passages.vernacular: 的確,佢玩得不太好——佢為一切事感到遺憾已經咁久,而家要為任何事高興並唔容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 的確,她玩得不太好——她為一切事感到遺憾已經那麼久,現在要為任何事高興並不容易。

passages.original: But under Pollyanna's cheery instructions and merry laughter at her mistakes, she was learning fast.
passages.vernacular: 但喺波麗安娜愉快嘅指導同對佢錯誤嘅歡快笑聲下,佢進步好快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在波麗安娜愉快的指導和對她錯誤的歡快笑聲下,她進步很快。

passages.original: To-day, even, to Pollyanna's huge delight, she had said that she was glad Pollyanna brought calf's-foot jelly, because that was just what she had been wanting--she did not know that Milly, at the front door, had told Pollyanna that the minister's wife had already that day sent over a great bowlful of that same kind of jelly.
passages.vernacular: 今日,甚至令波麗安娜大喜過望嘅係,佢講佢高興波麗安娜帶嚟小牛腳凍,因為呢正是佢一直想要嘅——佢唔知道米莉喺前門告訴波麗安娜,牧師嘅妻子嗰天已經送嚟咗一大碗同樣嘅凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天,甚至令波麗安娜大喜過望的是,她說她高興波麗安娜帶來小牛腳凍,因為這正是她一直想要的——她不知道米莉在前門告訴波麗安娜,牧師的妻子那天已經送來了一大碗同樣的凍。

passages.original: Pollyanna was thinking of this now when suddenly she saw the boy.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜而家正想住呢個,忽然睇見咗嗰個男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜現在正想著這個,忽然看見了那個男孩。

passages.original: The boy was sitting in a disconsolate little heap by the roadside, whittling half-heartedly at a small stick.
passages.vernacular: 男孩坐喺路邊,蜷成沮喪嘅一小團,三心二意地削住一根小棍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩坐在路邊,蜷成沮喪的一小團,三心二意地削著一根小棍。

passages.original: “Hullo,” smiled Pollyanna, engagingly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,」波麗安娜迷人地微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,」波麗安娜迷人地微笑。

passages.original: The boy glanced up, but he looked away again, at once.
passages.vernacular: 男孩抬頭睇咗睇,但即刻又轉開視線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩抬頭看了看,但馬上又轉開視線。

passages.original: “Hullo yourself,” he mumbled.
passages.vernacular: 「你嗨,」佢咕噥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你嗨,」他咕噥。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: “Now you don't look as if you'd be glad even for calf's-foot jelly,” she chuckled, stopping before him.
passages.vernacular: 「而家你睇起嚟連小牛腳凍都唔會高興,」佢咯咯笑,喺佢面前停下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你看起來連小牛腳凍也不會高興,」她咯咯笑,在他面前停下。

passages.original: The boy stirred restlessly, gave her a surprised look, and began to whittle again at his stick, with the dull, broken-bladed knife in his hand.
passages.vernacular: 男孩不安地動咗動,驚訝地睇咗佢一眼,又開始用手裡嗰把鈍嘅、刀刃斷咗嘅小刀削佢嘅棍子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩不安地動了動,驚訝地看了她一眼,又開始用手裡那把鈍的、刀刃斷了的小刀削他的棍子。

passages.original: Pollyanna hesitated, then dropped herself comfortably down on the grass near him.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜遲疑咗一下,然後舒適地喺佢附近嘅草地上坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜遲疑了一下,然後舒適地在他附近的草地上坐下。

passages.original: In spite of Pollyanna's brave assertion that she was “used to Ladies' Aiders,” and “didn't mind,” she had sighed at times for some companion of her own age.
passages.vernacular: 儘管波麗安娜勇敢地聲稱佢「習慣咗婦女互助會嘅人」並且「不介意」,佢有時定係為了一個同齡嘅伴而嘆息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管波麗安娜勇敢地聲稱她「習慣了婦女互助會的人」並且「不介意」,她有時還是為了一個同齡的伴而嘆息。

passages.original: Hence her determination to make the most of this one.
passages.vernacular: 因此佢決心充分利用呢一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此她決心充分利用這一個。

passages.original: “My name's Pollyanna Whittier,” she began pleasantly.
passages.vernacular: 「我叫波麗安娜·惠蒂爾,」佢愉快地開口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我叫波麗安娜·惠蒂爾,」她愉快地開口。

passages.original: “What's yours?”
passages.vernacular: 「你叫乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你叫什麼?」

passages.original: Again the boy stirred restlessly.
passages.vernacular: 男孩又不安地動咗動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩又不安地動了動。

passages.original: He even almost got to his feet.
passages.vernacular: 佢甚至幾乎站起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他甚至幾乎站起來。

passages.original: But he settled back.
passages.vernacular: 但佢又坐咗回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他又坐了回去。

passages.original: “Jimmy Bean,” he grunted with ungracious indifference.
passages.vernacular: 「吉米·比恩,」佢不客氣地漠然咕噥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉米·比恩,」他不客氣地漠然咕噥。

passages.original: “Good!
Now we're introduced.
passages.vernacular: 而家我哋算介紹過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我們算介紹過了。

passages.original: I'm glad you did your part--some folks don't, you know.
passages.vernacular: 我高興你做咗你嗰部分——有些人不做,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高興你做了你那部分——有些人不做,你知道。

passages.original: I live at Miss Polly Harrington's house.
passages.vernacular: 我住喺波莉·哈林頓小姐家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我住在波莉·哈林頓小姐家。

passages.original: Where do you live?”
passages.vernacular: 你住邊?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你住哪?」

passages.original: “Nowhere.”
passages.vernacular: 「邊兒都冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪兒也沒有。」

passages.original: “Nowhere!
passages.vernacular: 「邊兒都冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哪兒也沒有!

passages.original: Why, you can't do that--everybody lives somewhere,” asserted Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,你唔能夠咁樣——每個人都住喺某個地方,」波麗安娜斷言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,你不能這樣——每個人都住在某個地方,」波麗安娜斷言。

passages.original: “Well, I don't--just now.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我不——而家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不——現在。

passages.original: I'm huntin' up a new place.”
passages.vernacular: 我喺找一個新地方。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在找一個新地方。」

passages.original: “Oh!
Where is it?”
passages.vernacular: 喺邊兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在哪兒?」

passages.original: The boy regarded her with scornful eyes.
passages.vernacular: 男孩用輕蔑嘅眼睛睇住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩用輕蔑的眼睛看著她。

passages.original: “Silly!
passages.vernacular: 「傻瓜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「傻瓜!

passages.original: As if I'd be a-huntin' for it--if I knew!”
passages.vernacular: 好像我知道嘅話仲會找佢似嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像我知道的話還會找它似的!」

passages.original: Pollyanna tossed her head a little.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜微微昂咗昂頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜微微昂了昂頭。

passages.original: This was not a nice boy, and she did not like to be called “silly.”
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係個好男孩,佢不鍾意被叫「傻瓜」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是個好男孩,她不喜歡被叫「傻瓜」。

passages.original: Still, he was somebody besides--old folks.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢係除咗老人以外嘅另一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,他是除了老人以外的另一個人。

passages.original: “Where did you live--before?” she queried.
passages.vernacular: 「你以前住邊?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你以前住哪?」她問。

passages.original: “Well, if you ain't the beat'em for askin' questions!” sighed the boy impatiently.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你真係問個冇完!」男孩不耐煩地嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你真是問個沒完!」男孩不耐煩地嘆道。

passages.original: “I have to be,” retorted Pollyanna calmly, “else I couldn't find out a thing about you.
passages.vernacular: 「我必須咁樣,」波麗安娜平靜地反駁,「否則我就唔能夠知道你嘅任何事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我必須這樣,」波麗安娜平靜地反駁,「否則我就不能知道你的任何事。

passages.original: If you'd talk more I wouldn't talk so much.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你多講話,我就唔使講咁多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你多說話,我就不用說那麼多。」

passages.original: The boy gave a short laugh.
passages.vernacular: 男孩短促地笑咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩短促地笑了一聲。

passages.original: It was a sheepish laugh, and not quite a willing one; but his face looked a little pleasanter when he spoke this time.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係羞澀嘅笑,唔係完全情願嘅;但佢呢次講話時,臉睇起嚟愉快咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是羞澀的笑,不是完全情願的;但他這次說話時,臉看起來愉快了一點。

passages.original: “All right then--here goes!
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,咁——講吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,那麼——說吧!

passages.original: I'm Jimmy Bean, and I'm ten years old goin' on eleven.
passages.vernacular: 我叫吉米·比恩,我十歲快十一歲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫吉米·比恩,我十歲快十一歲了。

passages.original: I come last year ter live at the Orphans' Home; but they've got so many kids there ain't much room for me, an' I wa'n't never wanted, anyhow, I don't believe.
passages.vernacular: 我去年嚟孤兒院住;但嗰度嘅細路太多,冇太多地方畀我,而且我想我從來就冇被需要過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去年來孤兒院住;但那裡的孩子太多,沒有太多地方給我,而且我想我從來就沒被需要過。

passages.original: So I've quit.
passages.vernacular: 所以我走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我走了。

passages.original: I'm goin' ter live somewheres else--but I hain't found the place, yet.
passages.vernacular: 我要去住別嘅地方——但我仲冇找到嗰地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要去住別的地方——但我還沒找到那地方。

passages.original: I'd LIKE a home--jest a common one, ye know, with a mother in it, instead of a Matron.
passages.vernacular: 我想要一個家——只係普通嘅,你知道,有媽媽嘅,而唔係舍監。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想要一個家——只是普通的,你知道,有媽媽的,而不是舍監。

passages.original: If ye has a home, ye has folks; an' I hain't had folks since--dad died.
passages.vernacular: 如果有家,就有親人;而我從爸爸死後就冇親人喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有家,就有親人;而我從爸爸死後就沒有親人了。

passages.original: So I'm a-huntin' now.
passages.vernacular: 所以我而家喺找。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我現在在找。

passages.original: I've tried four houses, but--they didn't want me--though I said I expected ter work, 'course.
passages.vernacular: 我試過四所房子,但——佢哋唔好我——雖然我講咗我當然準備工作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我試過四所房子,但——他們不要我——雖然我說了我當然準備工作。

passages.original: There!
passages.vernacular: 好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了!

passages.original: Is that all you want ter know?”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係你想知道嘅全部嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是你想知道的全部嗎?」

passages.original: The boy's voice had broken a little over the last two sentences.
passages.vernacular: 男孩嘅聲音喺最後兩句話上有點哽咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩的聲音在最後兩句話上有點哽咽。

passages.original: “Why, what a shame!” sympathized Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,真可憐!」波麗安娜同情地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,真可憐!」波麗安娜同情地說。

passages.original: “And didn't there anybody want you?
passages.vernacular: 「冇人要你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有人要你嗎?

passages.original: O dear!
passages.vernacular: 哦,天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,天哪!

passages.original: I know just how you feel, because after--after my father died, too, there wasn't anybody but the Ladies' Aid for me, until Aunt Polly said she'd take--” Pollyanna stopped abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 我完全知道你嘅感覺,因為喺——喺我父親死咗之後,我都除咗婦女互助會邊個都冇,直到波莉姨媽講佢會收——」波麗安娜突然停住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我完全知道你的感覺,因為在——在我父親死了之後,我也除了婦女互助會誰也沒有,直到波莉姨媽說她會收——」波麗安娜突然停住。

passages.original: The dawning of a wonderful idea began to show in her face.
passages.vernacular: 一個奇妙念頭嘅曙光開始喺佢臉上顯現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個奇妙念頭的曙光開始在她臉上顯現。

passages.original: “Oh, I know just the place for you,” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我知道正好適合你嘅地方,」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我知道正好適合你的地方,」她喊道。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly'll take you--I know she will!
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽會收你——我知道佢會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽會收你——我知道她會!

passages.original: Didn't she take me?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係收咗我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不是收了我嗎?

passages.original: And didn't she take Fluffy and Buffy, when they didn't have any one to love them, or any place to go?--and they're only cats and dogs.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係收咗毛毛同布布嗎,佢哋冇人愛,都冇地方去?——佢哋只係貓同狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不是收了毛毛和布布嗎,它們沒有人愛,也沒地方去?——它們只是貓和狗。

passages.original: Oh, come, I know Aunt Polly'll take you!
passages.vernacular: 哦,嚟吧,我知道波莉姨媽會收你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,來吧,我知道波莉姨媽會收你!

passages.original: You don't know how good and kind she is!”
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道佢多好多善良!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道她多好多善良!」

passages.original: Jimmy Bean's thin little face brightened.
passages.vernacular: 吉米·比恩瘦小嘅臉亮咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米·比恩瘦小的臉亮了起來。

passages.original: “Honest Injun?
passages.vernacular: 「講真嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說真的?

passages.original: Would she, now?
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅會?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她真的會?

passages.original: I'd work, ye know, an' I'm real strong!”
passages.vernacular: 我會工作嘅,你知道,我真嘅好強壯!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會工作的,你知道,我真的很強壯!」

passages.original: He bared a small, bony arm.
passages.vernacular: 佢露出一條瘦骨嶙峋嘅小胳膊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他露出一條瘦骨嶙峋的小胳膊。

passages.original: “Of course she would!
passages.vernacular: 「當然會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然會!

passages.original: Why, my Aunt Polly is the nicest lady in the world--now that my mama has gone to be a Heaven angel.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,我嘅波莉姨媽係世界上最好嘅女士——而家我媽媽去當天堂嘅天使喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,我的波莉姨媽是世界上最好的女士——現在我媽媽去當天堂的天使了。

passages.original: And there's rooms--heaps of 'em,” she continued, springing to her feet, and tugging at his arm.
passages.vernacular: 而且有房間——好多好多,」佢繼續講,跳起嚟拉住佢嘅胳膊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且有房間——好多好多,」她繼續說,跳起來拉著他的胳膊。

passages.original: “It's an awful big house.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係一座好大嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是一座非常大的房子。

passages.original: Maybe, though,” she added a little anxiously, as they hurried on, “maybe you'll have to sleep in the attic room.
passages.vernacular: 不過,或者,」佢喺佢哋匆忙往前走時,有點焦慮地補充,「或者你得瞓閣樓房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,也許,」她在他們匆忙往前走時,有點焦慮地補充,「也許你得睡閣樓房間。

passages.original: I did, at first.
passages.vernacular: 我起初就係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我起初就是。

passages.original: But there's screens there now, so 'twon't be so hot, and the flies can't get in, either, to bring in the germ-things on their feet.
passages.vernacular: 但而家嗰度有紗窗喇,所以唔會咁熱,蒼蠅都進不去,帶不進佢哋腳上嘅細菌嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但現在那裡有紗窗了,所以不會那麼熱,蒼蠅也進不去,帶不進它們腳上的細菌東西。

passages.original: Did you know about that?
passages.vernacular: 你知道嗰個嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道那個嗎?

passages.original: It's perfectly lovely!
passages.vernacular: 美極喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美極了!

passages.original: Maybe she'll let you read the book if you're good--I mean, if you're bad.
passages.vernacular: 如果你乖,或者佢會讓你讀嗰本書——我係講,如果你壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你乖,也許她會讓你讀那本書——我是說,如果你壞。

passages.original: And you've got freckles, too,”--with a critical glance--“so you'll be glad there isn't any looking-glass; and the outdoor picture is nicer than any wall-one could be, so you won't mind sleeping in that room at all, I'm sure,” panted Pollyanna, finding suddenly that she needed the rest of her breath for purposes other than talking.
passages.vernacular: 你都有雀斑,」——帶住挑剔嘅目光——「所以你會高興嗰度冇鏡子;而且窗外嘅畫比任何牆上嘅畫都好,所以我確信你啲都唔會介意瞓喺嗰個房間,」波麗安娜喘住氣講,突然發現佢需要留住剩下嘅呼吸做講話以外嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你也有雀斑,」——帶著挑剔的目光——「所以你會高興那裡沒有鏡子;而且窗外的畫比任何牆上的畫都好,所以我確信你一點也不會介意睡在那個房間,」波麗安娜喘著氣說,突然發現她需要留著剩下的呼吸做說話以外的事。

passages.original: “Gorry!” exclaimed Jimmy Bean tersely and uncomprehendingly, but admiringly.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀!」吉米·比恩簡短地、不明白但欽佩地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪!」吉米·比恩簡短地、不明白但欽佩地喊道。

passages.original: Then he added: “I shouldn't think anybody who could talk like that, runnin', would need ter ask no questions ter fill up time with!”
passages.vernacular: 然後佢補充講:「我想,講話像嗰樣,仲邊跑邊講嘅人,不需要問問題嚟湊時間!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他補充說:「我想,說話像那樣,還邊跑邊說的人,不需要問問題來湊時間!」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: “Well, anyhow, you can be glad of that,” she retorted; “for when I'm talking, YOU don't have to!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,不管點樣,你可以為此高興,」佢反駁;「因為我講話嘅時候,你就唔使講!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,不管怎樣,你可以為此高興,」她反駁;「因為我說話的時候,你就不用說!」

passages.original: When the house was reached, Pollyanna unhesitatingly piloted her companion straight into the presence of her amazed aunt.
passages.vernacular: 到咗房子,波麗安娜毫不猶豫地領住佢嘅同伴直接走到佢驚訝嘅姨媽面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了房子,波麗安娜毫不猶豫地領著她的同伴直接走到她驚訝的姨媽面前。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly,” she triumphed, “just look a-here!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,」佢得意地講,「睇呢兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,」她得意地說,「看這兒!

passages.original: I've got something ever so much nicer, even, than Fluffy and Buffy for you to bring up.
passages.vernacular: 我有比毛毛同布布更好得多嘅嘢要您收養。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有比毛毛和布布更好得多的東西要您收養。

passages.original: It's a real live boy.
passages.vernacular: 係個真正活住嘅男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是個真正活著的男孩。

passages.original: He won't mind a bit sleeping in the attic, at first, you know, and he says he'll work; but I shall need him the most of the time to play with, I reckon.”
passages.vernacular: 佢啲都不介意起初瞓喺閣樓裡,你知道,佢講佢會工作;但我想大部分時間我需要佢陪我玩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他一點也不介意起初睡在閣樓裡,你知道,他說他會工作;但我想大部分時間我需要他陪我玩。」

passages.original: Miss Polly grew white, then very red.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐臉色變白,然後變得好紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐臉色變白,然後變得很紅。

passages.original: She did not quite understand; but she thought she understood enough.
passages.vernacular: 佢不太明白;但佢覺得佢明白得夠多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不太明白;但她覺得她明白得夠多了。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, what does this mean?
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,呢個係乜嘢意思?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,這是什麼意思?

passages.original: Who is this dirty little boy?
passages.vernacular: 呢個髒兮兮嘅小男孩係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個髒兮兮的小男孩是誰?

passages.original: Where did you find him?” she demanded sharply.
passages.vernacular: 你喺邊度找到佢嘅?」佢尖銳地質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在哪裡找到他的?」她尖銳地質問。

passages.original: The “dirty little boy” fell back a step and looked toward the door.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個「髒兮兮嘅小男孩」後退一步,望向門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個「髒兮兮的小男孩」後退一步,望向門口。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed merrily.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜快樂地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜快樂地笑了。

passages.original: “There, if I didn't forget to tell you his name!
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,我忘咗告訴您佢嘅名字!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,我忘了告訴您他的名字!

passages.original: I'm as bad as the Man.
passages.vernacular: 我跟嗰個男人一樣糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟那個男人一樣糟。

passages.original: And he is dirty, too, isn't he?--I mean, the boy is--just like Fluffy and Buffy were when you took them in.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢係髒,係唔係?——我係講,男孩係——就像毛毛同布布被您收養時一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他是髒,是不是?——我是說,男孩是——就像毛毛和布布被您收養時一樣。

passages.original: But I reckon he'll improve all right by washing, just as they did, and--Oh, I 'most forgot again,” she broke off with a laugh.
passages.vernacular: 不過我想佢洗一洗就會好起嚟,就像佢哋嗰樣,而且——哦,我又差點忘喇,」佢笑住打斷自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想他洗一洗就會好起來,就像它們那樣,而且——哦,我又差點忘了,」她笑著打斷自己。

passages.original: “This is Jimmy Bean, Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個係吉米·比恩,波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這是吉米·比恩,波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: “Well, what is he doing here?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢喺呢度幹乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,他在這裡幹什麼?」

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, I just told you!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,我剛告訴您喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,我剛告訴您了!」

passages.original: Pollyanna's eyes were wide with surprise.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅眼睛驚訝得睜大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的眼睛驚訝得睜大。

passages.original: “He's for you.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係畀您嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是給您的。

passages.original: I brought him home--so he could live here, you know.
passages.vernacular: 我把佢帶回家——咁樣佢就能住喺呢度,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把他帶回家——這樣他就能住在這裡,你知道。

passages.original: He wants a home and folks.
passages.vernacular: 佢想要一個家同親人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想要一個家和親人。

passages.original: I told him how good you were to me, and to Fluffy and Buffy, and that I knew you would be to him, because of course he's even nicer than cats and dogs.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢您對我同毛毛、布布多好,我知道您對佢都會,因為佢當然比貓同狗更好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他您對我和毛毛、布布多好,我知道您對他也會,因為他當然比貓和狗更好。」

passages.original: Miss Polly dropped back in her chair and raised a shaking hand to her throat.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐癱回椅子,舉起一隻顫抖嘅手到喉嚨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐癱回椅子,舉起一隻顫抖的手到喉嚨。

passages.original: The old helplessness was threatening once more to overcome her.
passages.vernacular: 舊日嘅無助感又一次威脅住要壓倒佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 舊日的無助感又一次威脅著要壓倒她。

passages.original: With a visible struggle, however, Miss Polly pulled herself suddenly erect.
passages.vernacular: 然而,波莉小姐明顯掙扎咗一下,突然挺直身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,波莉小姐明顯掙扎了一下,突然挺直身子。

passages.original: “That will do, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,波麗安娜。

passages.original: This is a little the most absurd thing you've done yet.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係你到目前為止做嘅最荒唐嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是你到目前為止做的最荒唐的事。

passages.original: As if tramp cats and mangy dogs weren't bad enough but you must needs bring home ragged little beggars from the street, who--”
passages.vernacular: 好像流浪貓同長癬嘅狗仲唔夠糟,你仲非要從街上帶回衣衫襤褸嘅小乞丐,佢——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像流浪貓和長癬的狗還不夠糟,你還非要從街上帶回衣衫襤褸的小乞丐,他——」

passages.original: There was a sudden stir from the boy.
passages.vernacular: 男孩突然動喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩突然動了。

passages.original: His eyes flashed and his chin came up.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛閃光,下巴抬咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛閃光,下巴抬了起來。

passages.original: With two strides of his sturdy little legs he confronted Miss Polly fearlessly.
passages.vernacular: 佢邁住結實嘅小腿兩大步,無畏地面對波莉小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他邁著結實的小腿兩大步,無畏地面對波莉小姐。

passages.original: “I ain't a beggar, marm, an' I don't want nothin' o' you.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔係乞丐,太太,我都唔好你嘅任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不是乞丐,太太,我也不要你的任何東西。

passages.original: I was cal'latin' ter work, of course, fur my board an' keep.
passages.vernacular: 我打算工作,當然,換食宿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我打算工作,當然,換食宿。

passages.original: I wouldn't have come ter your old house, anyhow, if this 'ere girl hadn't 'a' made me, a-tellin' me how you was so good an' kind that you'd be jest dyin' ter take me in.
passages.vernacular: 要唔係呢個女孩逼我,告訴我你多好多善良,會巴唔得收留我,我才唔會嚟你呢座破房子呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要不是這個女孩逼我,告訴我你多好多善良,會巴不得收留我,我才不會來你這座破房子呢。

passages.original: So, there!”
passages.vernacular: 所以,就咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,就這樣!」

passages.original: And he wheeled about and stalked from the room with a dignity that would have been absurd had it not been so pitiful.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉身大步走出房間,嗰種尊嚴,若唔係咁可憐,簡直荒唐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他轉身大步走出房間,那種尊嚴,若不是那麼可憐,簡直荒唐。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly,” choked Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,」波麗安娜哽咽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,」波麗安娜哽咽。

passages.original: “Why, I thought you'd be GLAD to have him here!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我以為您會高興佢喺呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我以為您會高興他在這裡!

passages.original: I'm sure, I should think you'd be glad--”
passages.vernacular: 我確信,我想您會高興——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信,我想您會高興——」

passages.original: Miss Polly raised her hand with a peremptory gesture of silence.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐舉起手,做咗個唔容置疑嘅靜默手勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐舉起手,做了個不容置疑的靜默手勢。

passages.original: Miss Polly's nerves had snapped at last.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅神經終於崩斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的神經終於崩斷了。

passages.original: The “good and kind” of the boy's words were still ringing in her ears, and the old helplessness was almost upon her, she knew.
passages.vernacular: 男孩講嘅「好和善良」嘅話仍喺佢耳邊迴響,佢知道舊日嘅無助感幾乎要降臨喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩說的「好和善良」的話仍在她耳邊迴響,她知道舊日的無助感幾乎要降臨了。

passages.original: Yet she rallied her forces with the last atom of her will power.
passages.vernacular: 然而佢用最後啲意志力集結咗力量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而她用最後一點意志力集結了力量。

passages.original: “Pollyanna,” she cried sharply, “WILL you stop using that everlasting word 'glad'!
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,」佢尖銳地喊道,「你能唔能夠停止使用嗰個冇完冇咗嘅詞『高興』!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,」她尖銳地喊道,「你能不能停止使用那個沒完沒了的詞『高興』!

passages.original: It's 'glad'--'glad'--'glad' from morning till night until I think I shall grow wild!”
passages.vernacular: 從早到晚都係『高興』——『高興』——『高興』,我想我都要發瘋喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從早到晚都是『高興』——『高興』——『高興』,我想我都要發瘋了!」

passages.original: From sheer amazement Pollyanna's jaw dropped.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜驚訝得下巴掉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜驚訝得下巴掉了下來。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly,” she breathed, “I should think you'd be glad to have me gl--Oh!” she broke off, clapping her hand to her lips and hurrying blindly from the room.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,」佢倒抽氣,「我想您會高興我高——哦!」佢用手捂住嘴,盲目地匆忙離開房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,」她倒抽氣,「我想您會高興我高——哦!」她用手捂住嘴,盲目地匆忙離開房間。

passages.original: Before the boy had reached the end of the driveway, Pollyanna overtook him.
passages.vernacular: 男孩仲冇走到車道盡頭,波麗安娜就追上咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩還沒走到車道盡頭,波麗安娜就追上了他。

passages.original: “Boy!
passages.vernacular: 「男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男孩!

passages.original: Boy!
passages.vernacular: 男孩!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩!

passages.original: Jimmy Bean, I want you to know how--how sorry I am,” she panted, catching him with a detaining hand.
passages.vernacular: 吉米·比恩,我想讓你知道我幾咁——幾咁抱歉,」佢喘住氣,用手拽住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米·比恩,我想讓你知道我多麼——多麼抱歉,」她喘著氣,用手拽住他。

passages.original: “Sorry nothin'!
passages.vernacular: 「抱歉個啥!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「抱歉個啥!

passages.original: I ain't blamin' you,” retorted the boy, sullenly.
passages.vernacular: 我不怪你,」男孩悶悶地反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不怪你,」男孩悶悶地反駁。

passages.original: “But I ain't no beggar!” he added, with sudden spirit.
passages.vernacular: 「但我唔係乞丐!」佢突然有精神地補充。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我不是乞丐!」他突然有精神地補充。

passages.original: “Of course you aren't!
passages.vernacular: 「你當然唔係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你當然不是!

passages.original: But you mustn't blame auntie,” appealed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 但你唔好怪姨媽,」波麗安娜懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你不要怪姨媽,」波麗安娜懇求。

passages.original: “Probably I didn't do the introducing right, anyhow; and I reckon I didn't tell her much who you were.
passages.vernacular: 「可能我介紹得不對,反正;我想我冇告訴佢多少你係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可能我介紹得不對,反正;我想我沒告訴她多少你是誰。

passages.original: She is good and kind, really--she's always been; but I probably didn't explain it right.
passages.vernacular: 佢真嘅係好人又善良——佢一直係;但我可能冇解釋對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她真的是好人又善良——她一直是;但我可能沒解釋對。

passages.original: I do wish I could find some place for you, though!”
passages.vernacular: 我真希望我能為你找個地方!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望我能為你找個地方!」

passages.original: The boy shrugged his shoulders and half turned away.
passages.vernacular: 男孩聳聳肩,半轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩聳聳肩,半轉過身。

passages.original: “Never mind.
passages.vernacular: 「冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒關係。

passages.original: I guess I can find one myself.
passages.vernacular: 我想我自己能找到一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我自己能找到一個。

passages.original: I ain't no beggar, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔係乞丐,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是乞丐,你知道。」

passages.original: Pollyanna was frowning thoughtfully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜若有所思地皺住眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜若有所思地皺著眉。

passages.original: Of a sudden she turned, her face illumined.
passages.vernacular: 忽然佢轉身,臉上放出光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 忽然她轉身,臉上放出光彩。

passages.original: “Say, I'll tell you what I WILL do!
passages.vernacular: 「我講,我告訴你我要做乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,我告訴你我要做什麼!

passages.original: The Ladies' Aid meets this afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 婦女互助會今日下午開會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 婦女互助會今天下午開會。

passages.original: I heard Aunt Polly say so.
passages.vernacular: 我聽波莉姨媽講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽波莉姨媽說的。

passages.original: I'll lay your case before them.
passages.vernacular: 我會把你嘅情況提交畀佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會把你的情況提交給她們。

passages.original: That's what father always did, when he wanted anything--educating the heathen and new carpets, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 爸爸想要乜嘢嘅時候總是咁做——教化異教徒同新地毯,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸想要什麼的時候總是這麼做——教化異教徒和新地毯,你知道。」

passages.original: The boy turned fiercely.
passages.vernacular: 男孩凶狠地轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩凶狠地轉過身。

passages.original: “Well, I ain't a heathen or a new carpet.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔係異教徒,都唔係新地毯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不是異教徒,也不是新地毯。

passages.original: Besides--what is a Ladies' Aid?”
passages.vernacular: 再講——婦女互助會係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再說——婦女互助會是什麼?」

passages.original: Pollyanna stared in shocked disapproval.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜震驚而不贊成地瞪住眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜震驚而不贊成地瞪著眼。

passages.original: “Why, Jimmy Bean, wherever have you been brought up?--not to know what a Ladies' Aid is!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,吉米·比恩,你到底係喺邊兒長大嘅?——竟然唔知道婦女互助會係乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,吉米·比恩,你到底是在哪兒長大的?——竟然不知道婦女互助會是什麼!」

passages.original: “Oh, all right--if you ain't tellin',” grunted the boy, turning and beginning to walk away indifferently.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好吧——你不講就算喇,」男孩咕噥,轉身漠然地開始走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,好吧——你不說就算了,」男孩咕噥,轉身漠然地開始走開。

passages.original: Pollyanna sprang to his side at once.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜即刻跳到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜馬上跳到他身邊。

passages.original: “It's--it's--why, it's just a lot of ladies that meet and sew and give suppers and raise money and--and talk; that's what a Ladies' Aid is.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係——佢係——嗨,就係一群女士聚喺一起縫紉、辦晚飯、籌錢,仲有——仲有講話;婦女互助會就係呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「它是——它是——嗨,就是一群女士聚在一起縫紉、辦晚飯、籌錢,還有——還有說話;婦女互助會就是這個。

passages.original: They're awfully kind--that is, most of mine was, back home.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好善良——就係,我家鄉嘅大部分係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們非常善良——就是,我家鄉的大部分是。

passages.original: I haven't seen this one here, but they're always good, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 我仲冇見過呢度呢個,但佢哋總是好嘅,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還沒見過這裡這個,但她們總是好的,我想。

passages.original: I'm going to tell them about you this afternoon.”
passages.vernacular: 我今日下午要告訴佢哋你嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今天下午要告訴她們你的事。」

passages.original: Again the boy turned fiercely.
passages.vernacular: 男孩又凶狠地轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩又凶狠地轉過身。

passages.original: “Not much you will!
passages.vernacular: 「你敢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你敢!

passages.original: Maybe you think I'm goin' ter stand 'round an' hear a whole LOT o' women call me a beggar, instead of jest ONE!
passages.vernacular: 或者你以為我會站喺周圍聽一大群女人叫我乞丐,而唔係只有一個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你以為我會站在周圍聽一大群女人叫我乞丐,而不是只有一個!

passages.original: Not much!”
passages.vernacular: 冇門!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒門!」

passages.original: “Oh, but you wouldn't be there,” argued Pollyanna, quickly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,但你唔會喺嗰兒,」波麗安娜快速爭辯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,但你不會在那兒,」波麗安娜快速爭辯。

passages.original: “I'd go alone, of course, and tell them.”
passages.vernacular: 「我當然係自己去,告訴佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我當然是自己去,告訴她們。」

passages.original: “You would?”
passages.vernacular: 「你會?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會?」

passages.original: “Yes; and I'd tell it better this time,” hurried on Pollyanna, quick to see the signs of relenting in the boy's face.
passages.vernacular: 「會;而且呢次我會講得更好,」波麗安娜匆忙繼續,好快睇到男孩臉上有軟化嘅跡象。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「會;而且這次我會講得更好,」波麗安娜匆忙繼續,很快看到男孩臉上有軟化的跡象。

passages.original: “And there'd be some of 'em, I know, that would be glad to give you a home.”
passages.vernacular: 「我知道佢哋中會有人高興畀你一個家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道她們中會有人高興給你一個家。」

passages.original: “I'd work--don't forget ter say that,” cautioned the boy.
passages.vernacular: 「我會工作——別忘咗講呢個,」男孩提醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我會工作——別忘了說這個,」男孩提醒。

passages.original: “Of course not,” promised Pollyanna, happily, sure now that her point was gained.
passages.vernacular: 「當然唔會,」波麗安娜快樂地保證,而家確信佢嘅目的達到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不會,」波麗安娜快樂地保證,現在確信她的目的達到了。

passages.original: “Then I'll let you know to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我聽日讓你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我明天讓你知道。」

passages.original: “Where?”
passages.vernacular: 「喺邊兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在哪兒?」

passages.original: “By the road--where I found you to-day; near Mrs. Snow's house.”
passages.vernacular: 「路邊——我今日發現你嘅地方;喺斯諾太太嘅房子附近。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「路邊——我今天發現你的地方;在斯諾太太的房子附近。」

passages.original: “All right.
I'll be there.”
passages.vernacular: 我會喺嗰兒。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會在那兒。」

passages.original: The boy paused before he went on slowly: “Maybe I'd better go back, then, for ter-night, ter the Home.
passages.vernacular: 男孩停咗停,然後慢慢地繼續講:「或者我今晚最好回去,回孤兒院。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩停了停,然後慢慢地繼續說:「也許我今晚最好回去,回孤兒院。

passages.original: You see I hain't no other place ter stay; and--and I didn't leave till this mornin'.
passages.vernacular: 你睇我冇別嘅地方住;而且——而且我今日早晨才走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看我沒有別的地方住;而且——而且我今天早晨才走。

passages.original: I slipped out.
passages.vernacular: 我溜出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我溜出來的。

passages.original: I didn't tell 'em I wasn't comin' back, else they'd pretend I couldn't come--though I'm thinkin' they won't do no worryin' when I don't show up sometime.
passages.vernacular: 我冇告訴佢哋我不回去,否則佢哋會假裝我唔能夠走——不過我想佢哋有一天我唔見咗都唔會擔心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒告訴他們我不回去,否則他們會假裝我不能走——不過我想他們有一天我不見了也不會擔心。

passages.original: They ain't like FOLKS, ye know.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不像親人,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不像親人,你知道。

passages.original: They don't CARE!”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不在乎!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們不在乎!」

passages.original: “I know,” nodded Pollyanna, with understanding eyes.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」波麗安娜點頭,眼神充滿理解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」波麗安娜點頭,眼神充滿理解。

passages.original: “But I'm sure, when I see you to-morrow, I'll have just a common home and folks that do care all ready for you.
passages.vernacular: 「但我確信,聽日我見你時,我會有一個普通嘅家同真正在乎你嘅親人為你準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我確信,明天我見你時,我會有一個普通的家和真正在乎你的親人為你準備好。

passages.original: Good-by!” she called brightly, as she turned back toward the house.
passages.vernacular: 再見!」佢愉快地喊,轉身走回房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見!」她愉快地喊,轉身走回房子。

passages.original: In the sitting-room window at that moment, Miss Polly, who had been watching the two children, followed with sombre eyes the boy until a bend of the road hid him from sight.
passages.vernacular: 此刻,起居室嘅窗邊,一直睇住兩個細路嘅波莉小姐,用陰沉嘅眼睛跟隨嗰男孩,直到路嘅轉彎處把佢遮住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此刻,起居室的窗邊,一直看著兩個孩子的波莉小姐,用陰沉的眼睛跟隨那男孩,直到路的轉彎處把他遮住。

passages.original: Then she sighed, turned, and walked listlesly up-stairs--and Miss Polly did not usually move listlessly.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢嘆咗口氣,轉身,無精打采地走上樓——而波莉小姐通常唔會無精打采地走路。
