passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她嘆了口氣,轉身,無精打采地走上樓——而波莉小姐通常不會無精打采地走路。

passages.original: In her ears still was the boy's scornful “you was so good and kind.”
passages.vernacular: 男孩輕蔑嘅「你多好多善良」仍喺佢耳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 男孩輕蔑的「你多好多善良」仍在她耳邊。

passages.original: In her heart was a curious sense of desolation--as of something lost.
passages.vernacular: 佢心裡有一種奇怪嘅荒涼感——像丟失咗乜嘢嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她心裡有一種奇怪的荒涼感——像丟失了什麼東西。

chapters.title: Ch. XII Before the Ladies' Aid 第十二章:在濟貧會面前

passages.original: CH Dinner, which came at noon in the Harrington homestead, was a silent meal on the day of the Ladies' Aid meeting.
passages.vernacular: 婦女互助會開會嗰天,哈林頓祖宅中午嘅正餐係一頓沉默嘅飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 婦女互助會開會那天,哈林頓祖宅中午的正餐是一頓沉默的飯。

passages.original: Pollyanna, it is true, tried to talk; but she did not make a success of it, chiefly because four times she was obliged to break off a “glad” in the middle of it, much to her blushing discomfort.
passages.vernacular: 的確,波麗安娜試住講話;但冇成功,主要係因為佢四次唔得不把一個「高興」喺講到一半時斷開,令佢臉紅尷尬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 的確,波麗安娜試著說話;但沒有成功,主要是因為她四次不得不把一個「高興」在說到一半時斷開,令她臉紅尷尬。

passages.original: The fifth time it happened, Miss Polly moved her head wearily.
passages.vernacular: 第五次發生時,波莉小姐疲倦地動咗動頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第五次發生時,波莉小姐疲倦地動了動頭。

passages.original: “There, there, child, say it, if you want to,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,細路,你想講就講吧,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,孩子,你想說就說吧,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “I'm sure I'd rather you did than not if it's going to make all this fuss.”
passages.vernacular: 「我確信,如果要弄出咁多麻煩,我寧願你講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我確信,如果要弄出這麼多麻煩,我寧願你說。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's puckered little face cleared.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜皺住嘅小臉舒展喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜皺著的小臉舒展了。

passages.original: “Oh, thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,謝謝您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,謝謝您。

passages.original: I'm afraid it would be pretty hard--not to say it.
passages.vernacular: 我怕不講係好難嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕不說是很難的。

passages.original: You see I've played it so long.”
passages.vernacular: 您睇我玩咗咁久。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看我玩了那麼久。」

passages.original: “You've--what?” demanded Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「你——乜嘢?」波莉姨媽質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你——什麼?」波莉姨媽質問。

passages.original: “Played it--the game, you know, that father--” Pollyanna stopped with a painful blush at finding herself so soon again on forbidden ground.
passages.vernacular: 「玩——遊戲,您知道,爸爸——」波麗安娜痛苦地紅住臉停住,發現自己咁快又踏進咗禁區。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「玩——遊戲,您知道,爸爸——」波麗安娜痛苦地紅著臉停住,發現自己這麼快又踏進了禁區。

passages.original: Aunt Polly frowned and said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽皺眉,乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽皺眉,什麼也沒說。

passages.original: The rest of the meal was a silent one.
passages.vernacular: 飯嘅剩餘部分係沉默嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飯的剩餘部分是沉默的。

passages.original: Pollyanna was not sorry to hear Aunt Polly tell the minister's wife over the telephone, a little later, that she would not be at the Ladies' Aid meeting that afternoon, owing to a headache.
passages.vernacular: 稍後聽到波莉姨媽喺電話裡告訴牧師嘅妻子,佢因頭痛今日下午唔能夠去婦女互助會嘅會議,波麗安娜並不難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後聽到波莉姨媽在電話裡告訴牧師的妻子,她因頭痛今天下午不能去婦女互助會的會議,波麗安娜並不難過。

passages.original: When Aunt Polly went up-stairs to her room and closed the door, Pollyanna tried to be sorry for the headache; but she could not help feeling glad that her aunt was not to be present that afternoon when she laid the case of Jimmy Bean before the Ladies' Aid.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽上樓回房間關上門時,波麗安娜試住為頭痛難過;但佢禁不住高興,佢姨媽下午唔會在場,佢將喺婦女互助會面前提出吉米·比恩嘅案子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽上樓回房間關上門時,波麗安娜試著為頭痛難過;但她禁不住高興,她姨媽下午不會在場,她將在婦女互助會面前提出吉米·比恩的案子。

passages.original: She could not forget that Aunt Polly had called Jimmy Bean a little beggar; and she did not want Aunt Polly to call him that--before the Ladies' Aid.
passages.vernacular: 佢忘不咗波莉姨媽叫吉米·比恩小乞丐;佢唔想波莉姨媽嗰樣叫佢——喺婦女互助會面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她忘不了波莉姨媽叫吉米·比恩小乞丐;她不想波莉姨媽那樣叫他——在婦女互助會面前。

passages.original: Pollyanna knew that the Ladies' Aid met at two o'clock in the chapel next the church, not quite half a mile from home.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜知道婦女互助會兩點鐘喺教堂旁嘅小禮拜堂開會,離家唔到半英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜知道婦女互助會兩點鐘在教堂旁的小禮拜堂開會,離家不到半英里。

passages.original: She planned her going, therefore, so that she should get there a little before three.
passages.vernacular: 因此佢計劃出發嘅時間,好讓佢稍早於三點到達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此她計劃出發的時間,好讓她稍早於三點到達。

passages.original: “I want them all to be there,” she said to herself; “else the very one that wasn't there might be the one who would be wanting to give Jimmy Bean a home; and, of course, two o'clock always means three, really--to Ladies' Aiders.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想讓佢哋全都喺嗰兒,」佢對自己講;「否則冇到嘅嗰一個,可能正是想畀吉米·比恩一個家嘅人;而且,當然,兩點鐘對婦女互助會嘅人來講,總是意味住三點鐘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想讓她們全都在那兒,」她對自己說;「否則沒到的那一個,可能正是想給吉米·比恩一個家的人;而且,當然,兩點鐘對婦女互助會的人來說,總是意味著三點鐘。」

passages.original: Quietly, but with confident courage, Pollyanna ascended the chapel steps, pushed open the door and entered the vestibule.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜安靜地、但帶住自信嘅勇氣登上禮拜堂嘅台階,推開門,走進門廊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜安靜地、但帶著自信的勇氣登上禮拜堂的台階,推開門,走進門廊。

passages.original: A soft babel of feminine chatter and laughter came from the main room.
passages.vernacular: 大廳裡傳嚟女人哋嘅嘈雜低語同笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大廳裡傳來女人們的嘈雜低語和笑聲。

passages.original: Hesitating only a brief moment Pollyanna pushed open one of the inner doors.
passages.vernacular: 只遲疑咗片刻,波麗安娜推開咗一扇內門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只遲疑了片刻,波麗安娜推開了一扇內門。

passages.original: The chatter dropped to a surprised hush.
passages.vernacular: 交談聲降成咗驚訝嘅寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 交談聲降成了驚訝的寂靜。

passages.original: Pollyanna advanced a little timidly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜有點膽怯地走上前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜有點膽怯地走上前。

passages.original: Now that the time had come, she felt unwontedly shy.
passages.vernacular: 而家時刻到喇,佢感到異樣嘅羞怯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在時刻到了,她感到異樣的羞怯。

passages.original: After all, these half-strange, half-familiar faces about her were not her own dear Ladies' Aid.
passages.vernacular: 畢竟,佢周圍呢啲半陌生半熟悉嘅臉唔係佢自己親愛嘅婦女互助會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 畢竟,她周圍這些半陌生半熟悉的臉不是她自己親愛的婦女互助會。

passages.original: “How do you do, Ladies' Aiders?” she faltered politely.
passages.vernacular: 「您哋好,婦女互助會嘅各位?」佢禮貌地結結巴巴講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您們好,婦女互助會的各位?」她禮貌地結結巴巴說。

passages.original: “I'm Pollyanna Whittier.
passages.vernacular: 「我係波麗安娜·惠蒂爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是波麗安娜·惠蒂爾。

passages.original: I--I reckon some of you know me, maybe; anyway, I do YOU--only I don't know you all together this way.”
passages.vernacular: 我——我想你哋有些人或者認識我;反正,我認識你哋——只係我唔知道你哋咁樣全喺一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——我想你們有些人也許認識我;反正,我認識你們——只是我不知道你們這樣全在一起。」

passages.original: The silence could almost be felt now.
passages.vernacular: 寂靜而家幾乎能感覺到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 寂靜現在幾乎能感覺到了。

passages.original: Some of the ladies did know this rather extraordinary niece of their fellow-member, and nearly all had heard of her; but not one of them could think of anything to say, just then.
passages.vernacular: 有些女士確實認識佢哋會員嘅呢位相當非凡嘅外甥女,而且幾乎全都聽講過佢;但嗰時佢哋中冇一個人能想出講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些女士確實認識她們會員的這位相當非凡的外甥女,而且幾乎全都聽說過她;但那時她們中沒有一個人能想出說什麼。

passages.original: “I--I've come to--to lay the case before you,” stammered Pollyanna, after a moment, unconsciously falling into her father's familiar phraseology.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我嚟係要——要向你哋陳述一個案子,」波麗安娜過咗片刻結結巴巴地講,無意識地落入咗佢父親熟悉嘅措辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我來是要——要向你們陳述一個案子,」波麗安娜過了片刻結結巴巴地說,無意識地落入了她父親熟悉的措辭。

passages.original: There was a slight rustle.
passages.vernacular: 一陣輕微嘅沙沙聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣輕微的沙沙聲。

passages.original: “Did--did your aunt send you, my dear?” asked Mrs. Ford, the minister's wife.
passages.vernacular: 「你姨媽——派你嚟嘅嗎,親愛嘅?」牧師嘅妻子福特太太問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你姨媽——派你來的嗎,親愛的?」牧師的妻子福特太太問。

passages.original: Pollyanna colored a little.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜微微臉紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜微微臉紅。

passages.original: “Oh, no.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不。

passages.original: I came all by myself.
passages.vernacular: 我係自己嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是自己來的。

passages.original: You see, I'm used to Ladies' Aiders.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,我習慣咗婦女互助會嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,我習慣了婦女互助會的人。

passages.original: It was Ladies' Aiders that brought me up--with father.”
passages.vernacular: 係婦女互助會嘅人把我養大嘅——同爸爸一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是婦女互助會的人把我養大的——和爸爸一起。」

passages.original: Somebody tittered hysterically, and the minister's wife frowned.
passages.vernacular: 有人歇斯底里地咯咯笑,牧師嘅妻子皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人歇斯底里地咯咯笑,牧師的妻子皺眉。

passages.original: “Yes, dear.
passages.vernacular: 「係,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,親愛的。

passages.original: What is it?”
passages.vernacular: 係乜嘢事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是什麼事?」

passages.original: “Well, it--it's Jimmy Bean,” sighed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係——係吉米·比恩,」波麗安娜嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是——是吉米·比恩,」波麗安娜嘆氣。

passages.original: “He hasn't any home except the Orphan one, and they're full, and don't want him, anyhow, he thinks; so he wants another.
passages.vernacular: 「佢除咗孤兒院冇別嘅家,而且佢哋滿喇,唔好佢,佢咁樣認為;所以佢想要另一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他除了孤兒院沒有別的家,而且他們滿了,不要他,他這樣認為;所以他想要另一個。

passages.original: He wants one of the common kind, that has a mother instead of a Matron in it--folks, you know, that'll care.
passages.vernacular: 佢想要普通嘅嗰種,有媽媽而唔係舍監嘅——有親人,會關心佢嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想要普通的那種,有媽媽而不是舍監的——有親人,會關心他的。

passages.original: He's ten years old going on eleven.
passages.vernacular: 佢十歲快十一歲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他十歲快十一歲了。

passages.original: I thought some of you might like him--to live with you, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 我想你哋有些人或者鍾意佢——同你哋一起住,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你們有些人也許喜歡他——和你們一起住,你知道。」

passages.original: “Well, did you ever!” murmured a voice, breaking the dazed pause that followed Pollyanna's words.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你聽講過嗎!」一個聲音喃喃道,打破咗波麗安娜嘅話之後嗰陣發懵嘅停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你聽說過嗎!」一個聲音喃喃道,打破了波麗安娜的話之後那陣發懵的停頓。

passages.original: With anxious eyes Pollyanna swept the circle of faces about her.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜帶住焦慮嘅眼睛環視佢周圍一圈臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜帶著焦慮的眼睛環視她周圍一圈臉。

passages.original: “Oh, I forgot to say; he will work,” she supplemented eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我忘咗講;佢會工作,」佢熱切地補充。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我忘了說;他會工作,」她熱切地補充。

passages.original: Still there was silence; then, coldly, one or two women began to question her.
passages.vernacular: 仍然係寂靜;然後,冷冷地,一兩個女人開始問佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 仍然是寂靜;然後,冷冷地,一兩個女人開始問她。

passages.original: After a time they all had the story and began to talk among themselves, animatedly, not quite pleasantly.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一陣,佢哋都聽到咗呢個故事,開始彼此議論,活躍、但不太愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一陣,她們都聽到了這個故事,開始彼此議論,活躍、但不太愉快。

passages.original: Pollyanna listened with growing anxiety.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜聽住,越嚟越焦慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜聽著,越來越焦慮。

passages.original: Some of what was said she could not understand.
passages.vernacular: 所講嘅有些佢聽不懂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所說的有些她聽不懂。

passages.original: She did gather, after a time, however, that there was no woman there who had a home to give him, though every woman seemed to think that some of the others might take him, as there were several who had no little boys of their own already in their homes.
passages.vernacular: 不過過咗一會兒,佢確實聽出喇,嗰度冇一個女人有家可以畀佢,雖然每個女人似乎都認為別人可能會收留佢,因為有好幾個家裡仲冇自己嘅小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過過了一會兒,她確實聽出了,那裡沒有一個女人有家可以給他,雖然每個女人似乎都認為別人可能會收留他,因為有好幾個家裡還沒有自己的小男孩。

passages.original: But there was no one who agreed herself to take him.
passages.vernacular: 但冇一個人自己同意收留佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有一個人自己同意收留他。

passages.original: Then she heard the minister's wife suggest timidly that they, as a society, might perhaps assume his support and education instead of sending quite so much money this year to the little boys in far-away India.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢聽到牧師嘅妻子膽怯地建議,佢哋作為一個社團,或者可以承擔佢嘅撫養同教育,而唔係今年向遙遠印度嘅小男孩哋寄咁多錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她聽到牧師的妻子膽怯地建議,她們作為一個社團,也許可以承擔他的撫養和教育,而不是今年向遙遠印度的小男孩們寄那麼多錢。

passages.original: A great many ladies talked then, and several of them talked all at once, and even more loudly and more unpleasantly than before.
passages.vernacular: 然後許多女士講話喇,其中幾個同時講,聲音比之前更響、更不愉快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後許多女士說話了,其中幾個同時說,聲音比之前更響、更不愉快。

passages.original: It seemed that their society was famous for its offering to Hindu missions, and several said they should die of mortification if it should be less this year.
passages.vernacular: 似乎佢哋嘅社團以畀印度傳教站嘅捐款而出名,幾個人講如果今年少喇,佢哋會羞愧而死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎她們的社團以給印度傳教站的捐款而出名,幾個人說如果今年少了,她們會羞愧而死。

passages.original: Some of what was said at this time Pollyanna again thought she could not have understood, too, for it sounded almost as if they did not care at all what the money DID, so long as the sum opposite the name of their society in a certain “report” “headed the list”--and of course that could not be what they meant at all!
passages.vernacular: 此時所講嘅有些,波麗安娜又認為自己唔可能聽懂,因為聽起嚟幾乎像係,只要喺某份「報告」裡佢哋社團嘅名字旁邊嘅數目「居榜首」,佢哋根本不在乎錢用嚟做乜嘢——當然佢哋絕唔可能係呢個意思!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此時所說的有些,波麗安娜又認為自己不可能聽懂,因為聽起來幾乎像是,只要在某份「報告」裡她們社團的名字旁邊的數目「居榜首」,她們根本不在乎錢用來做什麼——當然她們絕不可能是這個意思!

passages.original: But it was all very confusing, and not quite pleasant, so that Pollyanna was glad, indeed, when at last she found herself outside in the hushed, sweet air--only she was very sorry, too: for she knew it was not going to be easy, or anything but sad, to tell Jimmy Bean to-morrow that the Ladies' Aid had decided that they would rather send all their money to bring up the little India boys than to save out enough to bring up one little boy in their own town, for which they would not get “a bit of credit in the report,” according to the tall lady who wore spectacles.
passages.vernacular: 但呢一切都好令人困惑,不太愉快,所以當佢終於發現自己喺外面寂靜甜美嘅空氣中時,波麗安娜確實好高興——但佢都好難過:因為佢知道,聽日要告訴吉米·比恩,婦女互助會決定寧可把所有嘅錢寄去撫養印度小男孩,都唔願省出足夠撫養自己鎮上一個小男孩嘅錢,嗰樣做喺報告上唔會「得到啲功勞」,戴眼鏡嘅高個子女士咁樣講,並唔容易,除咗悲傷乜嘢都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這一切都非常令人困惑,不太愉快,所以當她終於發現自己在外面寂靜甜美的空氣中時,波麗安娜確實很高興——但她也非常難過:因為她知道,明天要告訴吉米·比恩,婦女互助會決定寧可把所有的錢寄去撫養印度小男孩,也不願省出足夠撫養自己鎮上一個小男孩的錢,那樣做在報告上不會「得到一點功勞」,戴眼鏡的高個子女士這樣說,並不容易,除了悲傷什麼也不是。

passages.original: “Not but that it's good, of course, to send money to the heathen, and I shouldn't want 'em not to send SOME there,” sighed Pollyanna to herself, as she trudged sorrowfully along.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係講畀異教徒送錢不好,當然,我都不希望佢哋不送啲到嗰度,」波麗安娜悲傷地跋涉時對自己嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是說給異教徒送錢不好,當然,我也不希望她們不送一些到那裡,」波麗安娜悲傷地跋涉時對自己嘆道。

passages.original: “But they acted as if little boys HERE weren't any account--only little boys 'way off.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢哋表現得好像呢度嘅小男孩不算乜嘢——只有遠處嘅小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但她們表現得好像這裡的小男孩不算什麼——只有遠處的小男孩。

passages.original: I should THINK, though, they'd rather see Jimmy Bean grow--than just a report!”
passages.vernacular: 不過我認為佢哋寧可睇吉米·比恩長大——而唔係只睇一份報告!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我認為她們寧可看吉米·比恩長大——而不是只看一份報告!」

chapters.title: Ch. XIII In Pendleton Woods 第十三章:在潘德爾頓樹林裏

passages.original: CH Pollyanna had not turned her steps toward home, when she left the chapel.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜離開禮拜堂時,冇轉向回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜離開禮拜堂時,沒有轉向回家。

passages.original: She had turned them, instead, toward Pendleton Hill.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉向嘅係彭德爾頓山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她轉向的是彭德爾頓山。

passages.original: It had been a hard day, for all it had been a “vacation one” (as she termed the infrequent days when there was no sewing or cooking lesson), and Pollyanna was sure that nothing would do her quite so much good as a walk through the green quiet of Pendleton Woods.
passages.vernacular: 呢一天好艱難,儘管係個「假期」(呢個係佢對冇縫紉或烹飪課嘅稀少日子嘅稱呼),波麗安娜確信冇乜嘢比穿過彭德爾頓林地嘅綠色寧靜散步更對佢有益喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一天很艱難,儘管是個「假期」(這是她對沒有縫紉或烹飪課的稀少日子的稱呼),波麗安娜確信沒有什麼比穿過彭德爾頓林地的綠色寧靜散步更對她有益了。

passages.original: Up Pendleton Hill, therefore, she climbed steadily, in spite of the warm sun on her back.
passages.vernacular: 因此,儘管背上曬住暖陽,佢仍穩步爬上彭德爾頓山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,儘管背上曬著暖陽,她仍穩步爬上彭德爾頓山。

passages.original: “I don't have to get home till half-past five, anyway,” she was telling herself; “and it'll be so much nicer to go around by the way of the woods, even if I do have to climb to get there.”
passages.vernacular: 「反正我五點半才要回家,」佢對自己講;「繞住樹林走會好得多,即使我得爬上去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「反正我五點半才要回家,」她對自己說;「繞著樹林走會好得多,即使我得爬上去。」

passages.original: It was very beautiful in the Pendleton Woods, as Pollyanna knew by experience.
passages.vernacular: 彭德爾頓林地好美,波麗安娜從經驗中知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彭德爾頓林地非常美,波麗安娜從經驗中知道。

passages.original: But to-day it seemed even more delightful than ever, notwithstanding her disappointment over what she must tell Jimmy Bean to-morrow.
passages.vernacular: 但今日似乎比以往更令人愉快,儘管佢對聽日要告訴吉米·比恩嘅事感到失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但今天似乎比以往更令人愉快,儘管她對明天要告訴吉米·比恩的事感到失望。

passages.original: “I wish they were up here--all those ladies who talked so loud,” sighed Pollyanna to herself, raising her eyes to the patches of vivid blue between the sunlit green of the tree-tops.
passages.vernacular: 「我希望佢哋都喺呢度——所有嗰啲講話咁大聲嘅女士,」波麗安娜對自己嘆道,抬眼睇樹梢陽光照耀嘅綠色之間嘅一片片鮮藍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我希望她們都在這裡——所有那些說話那麼大聲的女士,」波麗安娜對自己嘆道,抬眼看樹梢陽光照耀的綠色之間的一片片鮮藍。

passages.original: “Anyhow, if they were up here, I just reckon they'd change and take Jimmy Bean for their little boy, all right,” she finished, secure in her conviction, but unable to give a reason for it, even to herself.
passages.vernacular: 「反正,如果佢哋喺呢度,我想佢哋肯定會改變,收留吉米·比恩做佢哋嘅小男孩,」佢確信地結束,堅信呢啲,卻連對自己都講不出理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「反正,如果她們在這裡,我想她們肯定會改變,收留吉米·比恩做她們的小男孩,」她確信地結束,堅信這一點,卻連對自己也說不出理由。

passages.original: Suddenly Pollyanna lifted her head and listened.
passages.vernacular: 突然波麗安娜抬起頭,傾聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 突然波麗安娜抬起頭,傾聽。

passages.original: A dog had barked some distance ahead.
passages.vernacular: 前面不遠處有一條狗叫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前面不遠處有一條狗叫了。

passages.original: A moment later he came dashing toward her, still barking.
passages.vernacular: 片刻後佢衝向佢,仍喺吠叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 片刻後它衝向她,仍在吠叫。

passages.original: “Hullo, doggie--hullo!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,小狗——嗨!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,小狗——嗨!」

passages.original: Pollyanna snapped her fingers at the dog and looked expectantly down the path.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜朝狗打咗個響指,期待地望住路下面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜朝狗打了個響指,期待地望著路下面。

passages.original: She had seen the dog once before, she was sure.
passages.vernacular: 佢確信佢以前見過呢條狗一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她確信她以前見過這條狗一次。

passages.original: He had been then with the Man, Mr. John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時佢同嗰個男人,約翰·彭德爾頓先生喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時它同那個男人,約翰·彭德爾頓先生在一起。

passages.original: She was looking now, hoping to see him.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家正望住,希望睇到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在正望著,希望看到他。

passages.original: For some minutes she watched eagerly, but he did not appear.
passages.vernacular: 佢熱切地睇咗幾分鐘,但佢冇出現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她熱切地看了幾分鐘,但他沒有出現。

passages.original: Then she turned her attention toward the dog.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把注意力轉向狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她把注意力轉向狗。

passages.original: The dog, as even Pollyanna could see, was acting strangely.
passages.vernacular: 狗,連波麗安娜都能睇出,行為古怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗,連波麗安娜都能看出,行為古怪。

passages.original: He was still barking--giving little short, sharp yelps, as if of alarm.
passages.vernacular: 佢仍喺吠叫——發出短促尖厲嘅叫聲,像係警報。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它仍在吠叫——發出短促尖厲的叫聲,像是警報。

passages.original: He was running back and forth, too, in the path ahead.
passages.vernacular: 佢都喺前面嘅路上嚟回跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它也在前面的路上來回跑。

passages.original: Soon they reached a side path, and down this the little dog fairly flew, only to come back at once, whining and barking.
passages.vernacular: 不久佢哋到咗一條小岔路,小狗幾乎飛一樣沿住佢衝下去,又即刻回嚟,嗚嗚叫住、吠住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久她們到了一條小岔路,小狗幾乎飛一樣沿著它衝下去,又馬上回來,嗚嗚叫著、吠著。

passages.original: “Ho!
That isn't the way home,” laughed Pollyanna, still keeping to the main path.
passages.vernacular: 嗰唔係回家嘅路,」波麗安娜笑住講,仍然走大路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那不是回家的路,」波麗安娜笑著說,仍然走大路。

passages.original: The little dog seemed frantic now.
passages.vernacular: 小狗而家似乎發狂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小狗現在似乎發狂了。

passages.original: Back and forth, back and forth, between Pollyanna and the side path he vibrated, barking and whining pitifully.
passages.vernacular: 喺波麗安娜同岔路之間嚟回、嚟回地跑,吠叫住、可憐地嗚咽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在波麗安娜和岔路之間來回、來回地跑,吠叫著、可憐地嗚咽著。

passages.original: Every quiver of his little brown body, and every glance from his beseeching brown eyes were eloquent with appeal--so eloquent that at last Pollyanna understood, turned, and followed him.
passages.vernacular: 佢棕色小身體嘅每一下顫抖,佢祈求嘅棕色眼睛嘅每一瞥,都充滿懇求嘅雄辯——雄辯到最後波麗安娜明白喇,轉身跟住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它棕色小身體的每一下顫抖,它祈求的棕色眼睛的每一瞥,都充滿懇求的雄辯——雄辯到最後波麗安娜明白了,轉身跟著它。

passages.original: Straight ahead, now, the little dog dashed madly; and it was not long before Pollyanna came upon the reason for it all: a man lying motionless at the foot of a steep, overhanging mass of rock a few yards from the side path.
passages.vernacular: 小狗而家瘋狂地直衝向前;不久波麗安娜就發現咗呢一切嘅原因:離岔路幾碼遠嘅一塊陡峭突出嘅岩石腳下,躺住一個一動不動嘅男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小狗現在瘋狂地直衝向前;不久波麗安娜就發現了這一切的原因:離岔路幾碼遠的一塊陡峭突出的岩石腳下,躺著一個一動不動的男人。

passages.original: A twig cracked sharply under Pollyanna's foot, and the man turned his head.
passages.vernacular: 一根細枝喺波麗安娜腳下尖銳地折斷,嗰男人轉過頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一根細枝在波麗安娜腳下尖銳地折斷,那男人轉過頭。

passages.original: With a cry of dismay Pollyanna ran to his side.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜驚叫一聲,跑到佢身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜驚叫一聲,跑到他身邊。

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton!
passages.vernacular: 「彭德爾頓先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「彭德爾頓先生!

passages.original: Oh, are you hurt?”
passages.vernacular: 哦,您受傷咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,您受傷了嗎?」

passages.original: “Hurt?
passages.vernacular: 「受傷?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「受傷?

passages.original: Oh, no!
passages.vernacular: 哦,冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,沒有!

passages.original: I'm just taking a siesta in the sunshine,” snapped the man irritably.
passages.vernacular: 我只係喺陽光下午瞓,」嗰人煩躁地厲聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是在陽光下午睡,」那人煩躁地厲聲說。

passages.original: “See here, how much do you know?
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,你知道多少?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,你知道多少?

passages.original: What can you do?
passages.vernacular: 你能做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能做什麼?

passages.original: Have you got any sense?”
passages.vernacular: 你有腦子嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有腦子嗎?」

passages.original: Pollyanna caught her breath with a little gasp, but--as was her habit--she answered the questions literally, one by one.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜輕輕倒抽咗一口氣,但——像佢嘅習慣——佢逐個字面地回答咗呢啲問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜輕輕倒抽了一口氣,但——像她的習慣——她逐個字面地回答了這些問題。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, I--I don't know so very much, and I can't do a great many things; but most of the Ladies' Aiders, except Mrs. Rawson, said I had real good sense.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,彭德爾頓先生,我——我知道嘅不多,都唔會做好多事;但婦女互助會嘅大部分人,除咗勞森太太,都講我真有腦子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,彭德爾頓先生,我——我知道的不多,也不會做很多事;但婦女互助會的大部分人,除了勞森太太,都說我真有腦子。

passages.original: I heard 'em say so one day--they didn't know I heard, though.”
passages.vernacular: 有一天我聽見佢哋咁講——不過佢哋唔知道我聽見喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天我聽見她們這麼說——不過她們不知道我聽見了。」

passages.original: The man smiled grimly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人嚴峻地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人嚴峻地笑了。

passages.original: “There, there, child, I beg your pardon, I'm sure; it's only this confounded leg of mine.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,細路,我道歉,我確信;只係呢條該死嘅腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,孩子,我道歉,我確信;只是這條該死的腿。

passages.original: Now listen.”
passages.vernacular: 而家聽住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在聽著。」

passages.original: He paused, and with some difficulty reached his hand into his trousers pocket and brought out a bunch of keys, singling out one between his thumb and forefinger.
passages.vernacular: 佢停咗停,費力地把手伸進褲兜,掏出一串鑰匙,用拇指同食指挑出一把。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他停了停,費力地把手伸進褲兜,掏出一串鑰匙,用拇指和食指挑出一把。

passages.original: “Straight through the path there, about five minutes' walk, is my house.
passages.vernacular: 「沿住嗰條小路直走,大約五分鐘嘅路,就係我嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沿著那條小路直走,大約五分鐘的路,就是我的房子。

passages.original: This key will admit you to the side door under the porte-cochere.
passages.vernacular: 呢把鑰匙能打開車門廊下嘅側門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這把鑰匙能打開車門廊下的側門。

passages.original: Do you know what a porte-cochere is?”
passages.vernacular: 你知道車門廊係乜嘢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道車門廊是什麼嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,知道,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,知道,先生。

passages.original: Auntie has one with a sun parlor over it.
passages.vernacular: 姨媽有一個,上面有日光室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 姨媽有一個,上面有日光室。

passages.original: That's the roof I slept on--only I didn't sleep, you know.
passages.vernacular: 我就瞓過嗰個屋頂——只不過我冇瞓成,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就睡過那個屋頂——只不過我沒睡成,你知道。

passages.original: They found me.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋找到咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們找到了我。」

passages.original: “Eh?
Oh!
passages.vernacular: 哦!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦!

passages.original: Well, when you get into the house, go straight through the vestibule and hall to the door at the end.
passages.vernacular: 好,你進咗房子,直穿門廊同大廳,到盡頭嘅門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你進了房子,直穿門廊和大廳,到盡頭的門。

passages.original: On the big, flat-topped desk in the middle of the room you'll find a telephone.
passages.vernacular: 房間中間嗰張大嘅平頂書桌上,你會找到一部電話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房間中間那張大的平頂書桌上,你會找到一部電話。

passages.original: Do you know how to use a telephone?”
passages.vernacular: 你知道點用電話嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道怎麼用電話嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, sir!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,知道,先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,知道,先生!

passages.original: Why, once when Aunt Polly--”
passages.vernacular: 嗨,有一次波莉姨媽——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,有一次波莉姨媽——」

passages.original: “Never mind Aunt Polly now,” cut in the man scowlingly, as he tried to move himself a little.
passages.vernacular: 「而家別管波莉姨媽,」嗰人皺住眉打斷,試住稍微挪動身體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在別管波莉姨媽,」那人皺著眉打斷,試著稍微挪動身體。

passages.original: “Hunt up Dr. Thomas Chilton's number on the card you'll find somewhere around there--it ought to be on the hook down at the side, but it probably won't be.
passages.vernacular: 「喺你會喺附近某處找到嘅卡片上,找托馬斯·奇爾頓醫生嘅號碼——佢應該掛喺旁邊嘅鉤子上,但可能不喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在你會在附近某處找到的卡片上,找托馬斯·奇爾頓醫生的號碼——它應該掛在旁邊的鉤子上,但可能不在。

passages.original: You know a telephone card, I suppose, when you see one!”
passages.vernacular: 我想你認識電話卡片,睇到時能認出嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你認識電話卡片,看到時能認出來!」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, sir!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,認識,先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,認識,先生!

passages.original: I just love Aunt Polly's.
passages.vernacular: 我太鍾意波莉姨媽嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太喜歡波莉姨媽的了。

passages.original: There's such a lot of queer names, and--”
passages.vernacular: 上面有咁多古怪嘅名字,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上面有那麼多古怪的名字,而且——」

passages.original: “Tell Dr. Chilton that John Pendleton is at the foot of Little Eagle Ledge in Pendleton Woods with a broken leg, and to come at once with a stretcher and two men.
passages.vernacular: 「告訴奇爾頓醫生,約翰·彭德爾頓喺彭德爾頓林地嘅小鷹岩腳下,腿斷喇,叫佢即刻帶擔架同兩個人嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴奇爾頓醫生,約翰·彭德爾頓在彭德爾頓林地的小鷹岩腳下,腿斷了,叫他馬上帶擔架和兩個人來。

passages.original: He'll know what to do besides that.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道除此以外該點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道除此以外該怎麼辦。

passages.original: Tell him to come by the path from the house.”
passages.vernacular: 叫佢從房子嗰邊嘅小路嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫他從房子那邊的小路來。」

passages.original: “A broken leg?
passages.vernacular: 「腿斷喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「腿斷了?

passages.original: Oh, Mr. Pendleton, how perfectly awful!” shuddered Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 哦,彭德爾頓先生,幾咁可怕!」波麗安娜打咗個寒顫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,彭德爾頓先生,多麼可怕!」波麗安娜打了個寒顫。

passages.original: “But I'm so glad I came!
passages.vernacular: 「但係我真高興我嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是我真高興我來了!

passages.original: Can't I do--”
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠做——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能做——」

passages.original: “Yes, you can--but evidently you won't!
passages.vernacular: 「能,你能——但顯然你唔肯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「能,你能——但顯然你不肯!

passages.original: WILL you go and do what I ask and stop talking,” moaned the man, faintly.
passages.vernacular: 你能唔能夠去做我叫你嘅,唔好講話,」嗰人虛弱地呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能不能去做我叫你的,別說話,」那人虛弱地呻吟。

passages.original: And, with a little sobbing cry, Pollyanna went.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜帶住一聲小小嘅抽泣去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜帶著一聲小小的抽泣去了。

passages.original: Pollyanna did not stop now to look up at the patches of blue between the sunlit tops of the trees.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜而家冇停下抬頭睇陽光照耀嘅樹梢間嗰一片片藍色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜現在沒有停下抬頭看陽光照耀的樹梢間那一片片藍色。

passages.original: She kept her eyes on the ground to make sure that no twig nor stone tripped her hurrying feet.
passages.vernacular: 佢眼睛盯住地面,確保冇細枝或石頭絆住佢匆忙嘅腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她眼睛盯著地面,確保沒有細枝或石頭絆住她匆忙的腳。

passages.original: It was not long before she came in sight of the house.
passages.vernacular: 冇過多久,佢就睇見咗房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒過多久,她就看見了房子。

passages.original: She had seen it before, though never so near as this.
passages.vernacular: 佢以前見過,雖然從冇離得咁近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她以前見過,雖然從沒離得這麼近。

passages.original: She was almost frightened now at the massiveness of the great pile of gray stone with its pillared verandas and its imposing entrance.
passages.vernacular: 面對嗰一大堆灰色石頭嘅龐大,以及佢有柱廊嘅陽台同宏偉嘅入口,佢而家幾乎害怕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 面對那一大堆灰色石頭的龐大,以及它有柱廊的陽台和宏偉的入口,她現在幾乎害怕了。

passages.original: Pausing only a moment, however, she sped across the big neglected lawn and around the house to the side door under the porte-cochere.
passages.vernacular: 不過只停咗片刻,佢就快步穿過巨大嘅荒廢草坪,繞過房子,到車門廊下嘅側門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過只停了片刻,她就快步穿過巨大的荒廢草坪,繞過房子,到車門廊下的側門。

passages.original: Her fingers, stiff from their tight clutch upon the keys, were anything but skilful in their efforts to turn the bolt in the lock; but at last the heavy, carved door swung slowly back on its hinges.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手指,因緊握鑰匙而僵硬,試圖轉動鎖栓時笨拙至極;但終於,沉重嘅雕花門慢慢轉開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的手指,因緊握鑰匙而僵硬,試圖轉動鎖栓時笨拙至極;但終於,沉重的雕花門慢慢轉開了。

passages.original: Pollyanna caught her breath.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜屏住咗呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜屏住了呼吸。

passages.original: In spite of her feeling of haste, she paused a moment and looked fearfully through the vestibule to the wide, sombre hall beyond, her thoughts in a whirl.
passages.vernacular: 儘管心急,佢定係停咗片刻,懼怕地穿過門廊望向對面寬闊陰沉嘅大廳,思緒如旋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管心急,她還是停了片刻,懼怕地穿過門廊望向對面寬闊陰沉的大廳,思緒如旋。

passages.original: This was John Pendleton's house; the house of mystery; the house into which no one but its master entered; the house which sheltered, somewhere--a skeleton.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係約翰·彭德爾頓嘅房子;神祕嘅房子;除咗主人無人進入嘅房子;某處藏住——骷髏嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是約翰·彭德爾頓的房子;神祕的房子;除了主人無人進入的房子;某處藏著——骷髏的房子。

passages.original: Yet she, Pollyanna, was expected to enter alone these fearsome rooms, and telephone the doctor that the master of the house lay now--
passages.vernacular: 然而佢,波麗安娜,被期望獨自進入呢啲可怕嘅房間,畀醫生打電話,講呢房子嘅主人而家躺喺——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而她,波麗安娜,被期望獨自進入這些可怕的房間,給醫生打電話,說這房子的主人現在躺在——

passages.original: With a little cry Pollyanna, looking neither to the right nor the left, fairly ran through the hall to the door at the end and opened it.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜輕叫一聲,左右都不睇,幾乎係跑住穿過大廳,到盡頭嘅門,把佢推開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜輕叫一聲,左右都不看,幾乎是跑著穿過大廳,到盡頭的門,把它推開。

passages.original: The room was large, and sombre with dark woods and hangings like the hall; but through the west window the sun threw a long shaft of gold across the floor, gleamed dully on the tarnished brass andirons in the fireplace, and touched the nickel of the telephone on the great desk in the middle of the room.
passages.vernacular: 房間好大,同大廳一樣,因深色木頭同帷幔而陰沉;但透過西窗,太陽喺地板上投下一道長長嘅金色光束,黯淡地照喺壁爐裡失去光澤嘅黃銅柴架上,觸到房間中央大書桌上電話嘅鎳鍍件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房間很大,同大廳一樣,因深色木頭和帷幔而陰沉;但透過西窗,太陽在地板上投下一道長長的金色光束,黯淡地照在壁爐裡失去光澤的黃銅柴架上,觸到房間中央大書桌上電話的鎳鍍件。

passages.original: It was toward this desk that Pollyanna hurriedly tiptoed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜匆忙地踮住腳尖朝呢張書桌走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜匆忙地踮著腳尖朝這張書桌走去。

passages.original: The telephone card was not on its hook; it was on the floor.
passages.vernacular: 電話卡片不喺佢嘅鉤子上;佢喺地板上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 電話卡片不在它的鉤子上;它在地板上。

passages.original: But Pollyanna found it, and ran her shaking forefinger down through the C's to “Chilton.”
passages.vernacular: 但波麗安娜找到咗佢,用顫抖嘅食指沿住C字頭往下找到「奇爾頓」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但波麗安娜找到了它,用顫抖的食指沿著C字頭往下找到「奇爾頓」。

passages.original: In due time she had Dr. Chilton himself at the other end of the wires, and was tremblingly delivering her message and answering the doctor's terse, pertinent questions.
passages.vernacular: 及時地,佢喺電話線另一頭接通咗奇爾頓醫生本人,顫抖地傳達佢嘅口信,並回答醫生簡短、切題嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 及時地,她在電話線另一頭接通了奇爾頓醫生本人,顫抖地傳達她的口信,並回答醫生簡短、切題的問題。

passages.original: This done, she hung up the receiver and drew a long breath of relief.
passages.vernacular: 做完呢啲,佢掛上聽筒,鬆咗一口長氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 做完這些,她掛上聽筒,鬆了一口長氣。

passages.original: Only a brief glance did Pollyanna give about her; then, with a confused vision in her eyes of crimson draperies, book-lined walls, a littered floor, an untidy desk, innumerable closed doors (any one of which might conceal a skeleton), and everywhere dust, dust, dust, she fled back through the hall to the great carved door, still half open as she had left it.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜只匆匆環顧咗一下周圍;然後,眼裡帶住模糊嘅景象:深紅色帷幔、滿係書嘅牆壁、雜亂嘅地板、凌亂嘅書桌、無數關住嘅門(其中任何一扇都可能藏住骷髏),以及到處係灰塵、灰塵、灰塵,佢逃回穿過大廳,到佢離開時半開住嘅大雕花門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜只匆匆環顧了一下周圍;然後,眼裡帶著模糊的景象:深紅色帷幔、滿是書的牆壁、雜亂的地板、凌亂的書桌、無數關著的門(其中任何一扇都可能藏著骷髏),以及到處是灰塵、灰塵、灰塵,她逃回穿過大廳,到她離開時半開著的大雕花門。

passages.original: In what seemed, even to the injured man, an incredibly short time, Pollyanna was back in the woods at the man's side.
passages.vernacular: 喺似乎連嗰受傷嘅人都覺得難以置信嘅短時間內,波麗安娜回到樹林裡嗰人嘅身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在似乎連那受傷的人也覺得難以置信的短時間內,波麗安娜回到樹林裡那人的身邊。

passages.original: “Well, what is the trouble?
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,有乜嘢問題?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,有什麼問題?

passages.original: Couldn't you get in?” he demanded.
passages.vernacular: 你進不去嗎?」佢質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你進不去嗎?」他質問。

passages.original: Pollyanna opened wide her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜睜大眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜睜大眼睛。

passages.original: “Why, of course I could!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,當然進得去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,當然進得去!

passages.original: I'm HERE,” she answered.
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢兒,」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這兒,」她回答。

passages.original: “As if I'd be here if I hadn't got in!
passages.vernacular: 「好像我冇進去仲會喺呢度似嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像我沒進去還會在這裡似的!

passages.original: And the doctor will be right up just as soon as possible with the men and things.
passages.vernacular: 醫生會盡快帶人同嘢上嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生會盡快帶人和東西上來。

passages.original: He said he knew just where you were, so I didn't stay to show him.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢知道您喺邊兒,所以我冇留下畀佢帶路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他知道您在哪兒,所以我沒留下給他帶路。

passages.original: I wanted to be with you.”
passages.vernacular: 我想同您喺一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想同您在一起。」

passages.original: “Did you?” smiled the man, grimly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?」嗰人嚴峻地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?」那人嚴峻地笑了。

passages.original: “Well, I can't say I admire your taste.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我唔能夠講我欣賞你嘅品味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不能說我欣賞你的品味。

passages.original: I should think you might find pleasanter companions.”
passages.vernacular: 我想你可以找到更愉快嘅伴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你可以找到更愉快的伴。」

passages.original: “Do you mean--because you're so--cross?”
passages.vernacular: 「您係講——因為您咁——兇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您是說——因為您那麼——兇?」

passages.original: “Thanks for your frankness.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你嘅坦率。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你的坦率。

passages.original: Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的。」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed softly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜輕輕笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜輕輕笑了。

passages.original: “But you're only cross OUTSIDE--You arn't cross inside a bit!”
passages.vernacular: 「但您只係外面兇——您裡面啲都不兇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但您只是外面兇——您裡面一點也不兇!」

passages.original: “Indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!

passages.original: How do you know that?” asked the man, trying to change the position of his head without moving the rest of his body.
passages.vernacular: 你點知道?」嗰人問,試圖喺不動身體其餘部分嘅情況下改變頭嘅位置。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼知道?」那人問,試圖在不動身體其餘部分的情況下改變頭的位置。

passages.original: “Oh, lots of ways; there--like that--the way you act with the dog,” she added, pointing to the long, slender hand that rested on the dog's sleek head near him.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,好多方式;瞧——像嗰樣——您對狗嘅樣子,」佢補充,指住佢身旁靠喺狗光滑頭上嘅嗰隻修長嘅手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,很多方式;瞧——像那樣——您對狗的樣子,」她補充,指著他身旁靠在狗光滑頭上的那隻修長的手。

passages.original: “It's funny how dogs and cats know the insides of folks better than other folks do, isn't it?
passages.vernacular: 「奇怪嘅係,狗同貓比別人更了解人嘅內心,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇怪的是,狗和貓比別人更了解人的內心,是不是?

passages.original: Say, I'm going to hold your head,” she finished abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 我講,我嚟托住您嘅頭,」佢突兀地結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說,我來托著您的頭,」她突兀地結束。

passages.original: The man winced several times and groaned once; softly while the change was being made; but in the end he found Pollyanna's lap a very welcome substitute for the rocky hollow in which his head had lain before.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人畏縮咗幾次,輕輕呻吟咗一聲,換位置嘅時候;但最後佢發現波麗安娜嘅膝蓋係佢之前頭躺嘅石頭凹處好受歡迎嘅替代物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人畏縮了幾次,輕輕呻吟了一聲,換位置的時候;但最後他發現波麗安娜的膝蓋是他之前頭躺的石頭凹處非常受歡迎的替代物。

passages.original: “Well, that is--better,” he murmured faintly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢——好些喇,」佢虛弱地喃喃道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這——好些了,」他虛弱地喃喃道。

passages.original: He did not speak again for some time.
passages.vernacular: 佢有好一陣冇再講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有好一陣沒再說話。

passages.original: Pollyanna, watching his face, wondered if he were asleep.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜睇住佢嘅臉,納悶佢係咪瞓住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜看著他的臉,納悶他是否睡著了。

passages.original: She did not think he was.
passages.vernacular: 佢不認為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不認為。

passages.original: He looked as if his lips were tight shut to keep back moans of pain.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟像係嘴唇緊閉,忍住痛苦嘅呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來像是嘴唇緊閉,忍住痛苦的呻吟。

passages.original: Pollyanna herself almost cried aloud as she looked at his great, strong body lying there so helpless.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜睇住佢巨大強壯嘅身體咁無助地躺喺嗰度,自己幾乎要哭出聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜看著他巨大強壯的身體那麼無助地躺在那裡,自己幾乎要哭出聲。

passages.original: One hand, with fingers tightly clenched, lay outflung, motionless.
passages.vernacular: 一隻手,手指緊握,伸展住,一動不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻手,手指緊握,伸展著,一動不動。

passages.original: The other, limply open, lay on the dog's head.
passages.vernacular: 另一隻,軟綿綿地張開,放喺狗嘅頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一隻,軟綿綿地張開,放在狗的頭上。

passages.original: The dog, his wistful, eager eyes on his master's face, was motionless, too.
passages.vernacular: 狗,用渴望而熱切嘅眼睛盯住主人嘅臉,都一動不動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 狗,用渴望而熱切的眼睛盯著主人的臉,也一動不動。

passages.original: Minute by minute the time passed.
passages.vernacular: 時間一分鐘一分鐘過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 時間一分鐘一分鐘過去。

passages.original: The sun dropped lower in the west and the shadows grew deeper under the trees.
passages.vernacular: 太陽喺西邊降低,樹下嘅影子變深喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 太陽在西邊降低,樹下的影子變深了。

passages.original: Pollyanna sat so still she hardly seemed to breathe.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜坐得咁靜,幾乎睇不出佢喺呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜坐得那麼靜,幾乎看不出她在呼吸。

passages.original: A bird alighted fearlessly within reach of her hand, and a squirrel whisked his bushy tail on a tree-branch almost under her nose--yet with his bright little eyes all the while on the motionless dog.
passages.vernacular: 一隻鳥毫無畏懼地落喺佢伸手可及處,一隻松鼠喺佢鼻子幾乎正下方嘅樹枝上甩住蓬鬆嘅尾巴——不過牠明亮嘅小眼睛始終盯住不動嘅狗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻鳥毫無畏懼地落在她伸手可及處,一隻松鼠在她鼻子幾乎正下方的樹枝上甩著蓬鬆的尾巴——可是牠明亮的小眼睛始終盯著不動的狗。

passages.original: At last the dog pricked up his ears and whined softly; then he gave a short, sharp bark.
passages.vernacular: 終於狗豎起耳朵,輕輕嗚咽;然後短促地尖叫咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 終於狗豎起耳朵,輕輕嗚咽;然後短促地尖叫了一聲。

passages.original: The next moment Pollyanna heard voices, and very soon their owners appeared three men carrying a stretcher and various other articles.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻波麗安娜聽見講話聲,好快佢哋嘅主人出現喇——三個男人抬住擔架同各種其他物件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻波麗安娜聽見說話聲,很快它們的主人出現了——三個男人抬著擔架和各種其他物件。

passages.original: The tallest of the party--a smooth-shaven, kind-eyed man whom Pollyanna knew by sight as “Dr. Chilton”--advanced cheerily.
passages.vernacular: 一行人中最高嘅——一個鬍子刮得光光嘅、眼神和善嘅人,波麗安娜認得係「奇爾頓醫生」——愉快地走上前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一行人中最高的——一個鬍子刮得光光的、眼神和善的人,波麗安娜認得是「奇爾頓醫生」——愉快地走上前。

passages.original: “Well, my little lady, playing nurse?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我嘅小女士,喺當護士?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我的小女士,在當護士?」

passages.original: “Oh, no, sir,” smiled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不,先生,」波麗安娜笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不,先生,」波麗安娜笑著說。

passages.original: “I've only held his head--I haven't given him a mite of medicine.
passages.vernacular: 「我只托住佢嘅頭——我啲藥都冇畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只托著他的頭——我一點藥也沒給他。

passages.original: But I'm glad I was here.”
passages.vernacular: 但我高興我喺呢度。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我高興我在這裡。」

passages.original: “So am I,” nodded the doctor, as he turned his absorbed attention to the injured man.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係,」醫生點頭,轉而專心照顧傷者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是,」醫生點頭,轉而專心照顧傷者。

chapters.title: Ch. XIV Just a Matter of Jelly 第十四章:只是果凍的事

passages.original: CH Pollyanna was a little late for supper on the night of the accident to John Pendleton; but, as it happened, she escaped without reproof.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·彭德爾頓出事故嘅嗰天晚上,波麗安娜晚飯遲到咗啲;但碰巧佢冇被責備就過去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·彭德爾頓出事故的那天晚上,波麗安娜晚飯遲到了一點;但碰巧她沒被責備就過去了。

passages.original: Nancy met her at the door.
passages.vernacular: 南希喺門口迎住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希在門口迎著她。

passages.original: “Well, if I ain't glad ter be settin' my two eyes on you,” she sighed in obvious relief.
passages.vernacular: 「哎,我真高興睇到你,」佢明顯鬆咗口氣地嘆息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎,我真高興看到你,」她明顯鬆了口氣地嘆息。

passages.original: “It's half-past six!”
passages.vernacular: 「已經六點半喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「已經六點半了!」

passages.original: “I know it,” admitted Pollyanna anxiously; “but I'm not to blame--truly I'm not.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,」波麗安娜焦慮地承認;「但呢不怪我——真嘅不怪我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,」波麗安娜焦慮地承認;「但這不怪我——真的不怪我。

passages.original: And I don't think even Aunt Polly will say I am, either.”
passages.vernacular: 而且我想連波莉姨媽都唔會講係我嘅錯。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我想連波莉姨媽也不會說是我的錯。」

passages.original: “She won't have the chance,” retorted Nancy, with huge satisfaction.
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇機會喇,」南希極為滿意地反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她沒機會了,」南希極為滿意地反駁。

passages.original: “She's gone.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她走了。」

passages.original: “Gone!” gasped Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「走喇!」波麗安娜倒抽氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「走了!」波麗安娜倒抽氣。

passages.original: “You don't mean that I've driven her away?”
passages.vernacular: 「你唔係講我把佢趕走咗吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不是說我把她趕走了吧?」

passages.original: Through Pollyanna's mind at the moment trooped remorseful memories of the morning with its unwanted boy, cat, and dog, and its unwelcome “glad” and forbidden “father” that would spring to her forgetful little tongue.
passages.vernacular: 此刻波麗安娜腦海裡湧現出悔恨嘅記憶:早晨嗰個不受歡迎嘅男孩、貓同狗,仲有佢健忘嘅小舌頭上冒出嚟嘅不受歡迎嘅「高興」同被禁止嘅「爸爸」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此刻波麗安娜腦海裡湧現出悔恨的記憶:早晨那個不受歡迎的男孩、貓和狗,還有她健忘的小舌頭上冒出來的不受歡迎的「高興」和被禁止的「爸爸」。

passages.original: “Oh, I DIDN'T drive her away?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我冇趕佢走吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我沒有趕她走吧?」

passages.original: “Not much you did,” scoffed Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「根本冇,」南希嘲笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「根本沒有,」南希嘲笑。

passages.original: “Her cousin died suddenly down to Boston, and she had ter go.
passages.vernacular: 「佢喺波士頓嘅表親突然死喇,佢得去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她在波士頓的表親突然死了,她得去。

passages.original: She had one o' them yeller telegram letters after you went away this afternoon, and she won't be back for three days.
passages.vernacular: 你今日下午走後,佢收到一封黃色嘅電報信,佢三天唔會回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你今天下午走後,她收到一封黃色的電報信,她三天不會回來。

passages.original: Now I guess we're glad all right.
passages.vernacular: 而家我想我哋可以高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我想我們可以高興了。

passages.original: We'll be keepin' house tergether, jest you and me, all that time.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會一起管家,就你同我,呢段時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會一起管家,就你和我,這段時間。

passages.original: We will, we will!”
passages.vernacular: 我哋會,我哋會!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會,我們會!」

passages.original: Pollyanna looked shocked.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜顯得震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜顯得震驚。

passages.original: “Glad!
passages.vernacular: 「高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興!

passages.original: Oh, Nancy, when it's a funeral?”
passages.vernacular: 哦,南希,呢不過葬禮?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,南希,這可是葬禮?」

passages.original: “Oh, but 'twa'n't the funeral I was glad for, Miss Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,可我高興嘅唔係葬禮,波麗安娜小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可我高興的不是葬禮,波麗安娜小姐。

passages.original: It was--” Nancy stopped abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 係——」南希突然停住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是——」南希突然停住。

passages.original: A shrewd twinkle came into her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢眼中閃出一絲狡黠嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她眼中閃出一絲狡黠的光。

passages.original: “Why, Miss Pollyanna, as if it wa'n't yerself that was teachin' me ter play the game,” she reproached her gravely.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波麗安娜小姐,好像唔係你自己教我玩呢個遊戲似嘅,」佢嚴肅地責備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波麗安娜小姐,好像不是你自己教我玩這個遊戲似的,」她嚴肅地責備。

passages.original: Pollyanna puckered her forehead into a troubled frown.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜把前額皺成憂心嘅皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜把前額皺成憂心的皺眉。

passages.original: “I can't help it, Nancy,” she argued with a shake of her head.
passages.vernacular: 「我冇辦法,南希,」佢搖住頭爭辯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒辦法,南希,」她搖著頭爭辯。

passages.original: “It must be that there are some things that 'tisn't right to play the game on--and I'm sure funerals is one of them.
passages.vernacular: 「一定有些事唔應該該玩呢個遊戲——我確信葬禮就係其中之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一定有些事不應該玩這個遊戲——我確信葬禮就是其中之一。

passages.original: There's nothing in a funeral to be glad about.”
passages.vernacular: 葬禮裡冇乜嘢值得高興嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葬禮裡沒有什麼值得高興的。」

passages.original: Nancy chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 南希咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希咯咯笑。

passages.original: “We can be glad 'tain't our'n,” she observed demurely.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋可以高興嗰唔係我哋嘅,」佢謙遜地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們可以高興那不是我們的,」她謙遜地說。

passages.original: But Pollyanna did not hear.
passages.vernacular: 但波麗安娜冇聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但波麗安娜沒聽見。

passages.original: She had begun to tell of the accident; and in a moment Nancy, open-mouthed, was listening.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經開始講嗰場事故;片刻後南希張住嘴聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她已經開始講那場事故;片刻後南希張著嘴聽著。

passages.original: At the appointed place the next afternoon, Pollyanna met Jimmy Bean according to agreement.
passages.vernacular: 第二天下午喺約定嘅地點,波麗安娜按約同吉米·比恩見面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天下午在約定的地點,波麗安娜按約同吉米·比恩見面。

passages.original: As was to be expected, of course, Jimmy showed keen disappointment that the Ladies' Aid preferred a little India boy to himself.
passages.vernacular: 可想而知,吉米顯然好失望,婦女互助會寧願要一個印度小男孩而唔好佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可想而知,吉米顯然很失望,婦女互助會寧願要一個印度小男孩而不要他。

passages.original: “Well, maybe 'tis natural,” he sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,或者呢個係自然嘅,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,也許這是自然的,」他嘆氣。

passages.original: “Of course things you don't know about are always nicer'n things you do, same as the pertater on 'tother side of the plate is always the biggest.
passages.vernacular: 「當然你唔知道嘅嘢總比你知道嘅更好,就像盤子另一邊嘅馬鈴薯總是最大嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然你不知道的東西總比你知道的更好,就像盤子另一邊的馬鈴薯總是最大的。

passages.original: But I wish I looked that way ter somebody 'way off.
passages.vernacular: 但我希望我喺遠處嘅某個人睇來係嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我希望我在遠處的某個人看來是那樣。

passages.original: Wouldn't it be jest great, now, if only somebody over in India wanted ME?”
passages.vernacular: 如果印度嗰邊有人要我,唔係好極咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果印度那邊有人要我,不是好極了嗎?」

passages.original: Pollyanna clapped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜拍手。

passages.original: “Why, of course!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,當然!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,當然!

passages.original: That's the very thing, Jimmy!
passages.vernacular: 吉米,就係呢個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米,就是這個!

passages.original: I'll write to my Ladies' Aiders about you.
passages.vernacular: 我畀我嘅婦女互助會嘅人寫信講你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給我的婦女互助會的人寫信說你。

passages.original: They aren't over in India; they're only out West--but that's awful far away, just the same.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋不喺印度;只喺西部——但同樣好遠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們不在印度;只在西部——但同樣很遠。

passages.original: I reckon you'd think so if you'd come all the way here as I did!”
passages.vernacular: 我想你像我咁樣一路嚟到呢度就會咁認為喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你像我這樣一路來到這裡就會這麼認為了!」

passages.original: Jimmy's face brightened.
passages.vernacular: 吉米嘅臉亮咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米的臉亮了起來。

passages.original: “Do you think they would--truly--take me?” he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你覺得佢哋會——真嘅——收留我嗎?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你覺得她們會——真的——收留我嗎?」他問。

passages.original: “Of course they would!
passages.vernacular: 「當然會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然會!

passages.original: Don't they take little boys in India to bring up?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋唔係收養印度嘅小男孩嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們不是收養印度的小男孩嗎?

passages.original: Well, they can just play you are the little India boy this time.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,呢次佢哋可以假裝你係嗰個印度小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,這次她們可以假裝你是那個印度小男孩。

passages.original: I reckon you're far enough away to make a report, all right.
passages.vernacular: 我想你離得夠遠,足夠做一份報告喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你離得夠遠,足夠做一份報告了。

passages.original: You wait.
passages.vernacular: 你等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你等著。

passages.original: I'll write 'em.
passages.vernacular: 我畀佢哋寫信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給她們寫信。

passages.original: I'll write Mrs. White.
passages.vernacular: 我寫畀懷特太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寫給懷特太太。

passages.original: No, I'll write Mrs. Jones.
passages.vernacular: 不,我寫畀瓊斯太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,我寫給瓊斯太太。

passages.original: Mrs. White has got the most money, but Mrs. Jones gives the most--which is kind of funny, isn't it?--when you think of it.
passages.vernacular: 懷特太太錢最多,但瓊斯太太畀得最多——呢有點滑稽,係唔係?——想想睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懷特太太錢最多,但瓊斯太太給得最多——這有點滑稽,是不是?——想想看。

passages.original: But I reckon some of the Aiders will take you.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我想互助會裡總有人會收留你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想互助會裡總有人會收留你。」

passages.original: “All right--but don't furgit ter say I'll work fur my board an' keep,” put in Jimmy.
passages.vernacular: 「好——但別忘咗講我會幹活換食宿,」吉米插嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——但別忘了說我會幹活換食宿,」吉米插嘴。

passages.original: “I ain't no beggar, an' biz'ness is biz'ness, even with Ladies' Aiders, I'm thinkin'.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔係乞丐,生意就係生意,即使係婦女互助會嘅人,我想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不是乞丐,生意就是生意,即使是婦女互助會的人,我想。」

passages.original: He hesitated, then added: “An' I s'pose I better stay where I be fur a spell yet--till you hear.”
passages.vernacular: 佢猶豫咗一下,然後補充:「我想我最好再喺原地待一陣——直到你有消息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他猶豫了一下,然後補充:「我想我最好再在原地待一陣——直到你有消息。」

passages.original: “Of course,” nodded Pollyanna emphatically.
passages.vernacular: 「當然,」波麗安娜強調地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,」波麗安娜強調地點頭。

passages.original: “Then I'll know just where to find you.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰樣我就知道喺邊兒找你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那樣我就知道在哪兒找你。

passages.original: And they'll take you--I'm sure you're far enough away for that.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋會收留你——我確信你離得夠遠喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們會收留你——我確信你離得夠遠了。

passages.original: Didn't Aunt Polly take--Say!” she broke off, suddenly, “DO you suppose I was Aunt Polly's little girl from India?”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽唔係收喇——講!」佢突然打斷自己,「你覺得我係波莉姨媽從印度嚟嘅小女孩嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽不是收了——說!」她突然打斷自己,「你覺得我是波莉姨媽從印度來的小女孩嗎?」

passages.original: “Well, if you ain't the queerest kid,” grinned Jimmy, as he turned away.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你真係最古怪嘅小孩,」吉米咧嘴笑,轉身走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你真是最古怪的小孩,」吉米咧嘴笑,轉身走開。

passages.original: It was about a week after the accident in Pendleton Woods that Pollyanna said to her aunt one morning:
passages.vernacular: 彭德爾頓林地事故大約一個星期後嘅一天早晨,波麗安娜對佢姨媽講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 彭德爾頓林地事故大約一個星期後的一天早晨,波麗安娜對她姨媽說:

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, please would you mind very much if I took Mrs. Snow's calf's-foot jelly this week to some one else?
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,請問,如果我呢個星期把斯諾太太嘅小牛腳凍送畀別人,您會好介意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,請問,如果我這個星期把斯諾太太的小牛腳凍送給別人,您會很介意嗎?

passages.original: I'm sure Mrs. Snow wouldn't--this once.”
passages.vernacular: 我確信斯諾太太唔會——就呢一次。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信斯諾太太不會——就這一次。」

passages.original: “Dear me, Pollyanna, what ARE you up to now?” sighed her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 「天呀,波麗安娜,你而家又喺搞乜嘢?」佢姨媽嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「天哪,波麗安娜,你現在又在搞什麼?」她姨媽嘆氣。

passages.original: “You ARE the most extraordinary child!”
passages.vernacular: 「你真係最非凡嘅細路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真是最非凡的孩子!」

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned a little anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜有點焦慮地皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜有點焦慮地皺眉。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, please, what is extraordinary?
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,請問,乜嘢係非凡?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,請問,什麼是非凡?

passages.original: If you're EXtraordinary you can't be ORdinary, can you?”
passages.vernacular: 如果你係非凡,就唔可能係平凡,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你是非凡,就不可能是平凡,是不是?」

passages.original: “You certainly can not.”
passages.vernacular: 「你當然唔可能。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你當然不可能。」

passages.original: “Oh, that's all right, then.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰就好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那就好了。

passages.original: I'm glad I'm EXtraordinary,” sighed Pollyanna, her face clearing.
passages.vernacular: 我高興我係非凡,」波麗安娜嘆氣,臉色放晴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我高興我是非凡,」波麗安娜嘆氣,臉色放晴。

passages.original: “You see, Mrs. White used to say Mrs. Rawson was a very ordinary woman--and she disliked Mrs. Rawson something awful.
passages.vernacular: 「您睇,懷特太太常講勞森太太係個好平凡嘅女人——而佢特別討厭勞森太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您看,懷特太太常說勞森太太是個非常平凡的女人——而她特別討厭勞森太太。

passages.original: They were always fight--I mean, father had--that is, I mean, WE had more trouble keeping peace between them than we did between any of the rest of the Aiders,” corrected Pollyanna, a little breathless from her efforts to steer between the Scylla of her father's past commands in regard to speaking of church quarrels, and the Charybdis of her aunt's present commands in regard to speaking of her father.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋總是打架——我係講,爸爸有——就係,我係講,我哋為保持佢哋之間嘅和平,比其他任何互助會嘅人之間都費更多麻煩,」波麗安娜糾正自己,因努力喺佢父親過去關於談論教會爭吵嘅指令之斯庫拉,同佢姨媽而家關於談論佢父親嘅命令之卡律布狄斯之間穿行,而有點喘不過氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她們總是打架——我是說,爸爸有——就是,我是說,我們為保持她們之間的和平,比其他任何互助會的人之間都費更多麻煩,」波麗安娜糾正自己,因努力在她父親過去關於談論教會爭吵的指令之斯庫拉,和她姨媽現在關於談論她父親的命令之卡律布狄斯之間穿行,而有點喘不過氣。

passages.original: “Yes, yes; well, never mind,” interposed Aunt Polly, a trifle impatiently.
passages.vernacular: 「係,係;好喇,唔使管,」波莉姨媽有點不耐煩地插話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是;好了,不用管,」波莉姨媽有點不耐煩地插話。

passages.original: “You do run on so, Pollyanna, and no matter what we're talking about you always bring up at those Ladies' Aiders!”
passages.vernacular: 「你講個冇完,波麗安娜,不管我哋談乜嘢,你總是扯到嗰啲婦女互助會嘅人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說個沒完,波麗安娜,不管我們談什麼,你總是扯到那些婦女互助會的人!」

passages.original: “Yes'm,” smiled Pollyanna, cheerfully, “I reckon I do, maybe.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」波麗安娜愉快地笑住講,「我想或者係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」波麗安娜愉快地笑著說,「我想也許是這樣。

passages.original: But you see they used to bring me up, and--”
passages.vernacular: 不過您睇佢哋把我養大,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過您看她們把我養大,而且——」

passages.original: “That will do, Pollyanna,” interrupted a cold voice.
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,波麗安娜,」一個冷冷嘅聲音打斷佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,波麗安娜,」一個冷冷的聲音打斷她。

passages.original: “Now what is it about this jelly?”
passages.vernacular: 「而家呢個凍係點回事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在這個凍是怎麼回事?」

passages.original: “Nothing, Aunt Polly, truly, that you would mind, I'm sure.
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢,波莉姨媽,真嘅,我確信您唔會介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒什麼,波莉姨媽,真的,我確信您不會介意。

passages.original: You let me take jelly to HER, so I thought you would to HIM--this once.
passages.vernacular: 您讓我畀佢帶凍,所以我想您都會讓我畀佢帶——就呢一次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您讓我給她帶凍,所以我想您也會讓我給他帶——就這一次。

passages.original: You see, broken legs aren't like--like lifelong invalids, so his won't last forever as Mrs. Snow's does, and she can have all the rest of the things after just once or twice.”
passages.vernacular: 您睇,斷腿不像——不像終身病人,所以佢嘅唔會永遠持續,像斯諾太太嘅嗰樣,而佢只一兩次後就能得到其他嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,斷腿不像——不像終身病人,所以他的不會永遠持續,像斯諾太太的那樣,而她只一兩次後就能得到其他東西。」

passages.original: “'Him'?
'He'?
'Broken leg'?
passages.vernacular: 『斷腿』?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 『斷腿』?

passages.original: What are you talking about, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 你喺講乜嘢,波麗安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在說什麼,波麗安娜?」

passages.original: Pollyanna stared; then her face relaxed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜瞪住眼;然後臉上放鬆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜瞪著眼;然後臉上放鬆了。

passages.original: “Oh, I forgot.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我忘了。

passages.original: I reckon you didn't know.
passages.vernacular: 我想您唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您不知道。

passages.original: You see, it happened while you were gone.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,係您不喺嘅時候發生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,是您不在的時候發生的。

passages.original: It was the very day you went that I found him in the woods, you know; and I had to unlock his house and telephone for the men and the doctor, and hold his head, and everything.
passages.vernacular: 正是您走嘅嗰天,我喺樹林裡發現咗佢,你知道;我唔得不打開佢嘅房子,打電話叫人同醫生,托住佢嘅頭,等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是您走的那天,我在樹林裡發現了他,你知道;我不得不打開他的房子,打電話叫人和醫生,托著他的頭,等等。

passages.original: And of course then I came away and haven't seen him since.
passages.vernacular: 當然然後我就走喇,此後冇見過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然然後我就走了,此後沒見過他。

passages.original: But when Nancy made the jelly for Mrs. Snow this week I thought how nice it would be if I could take it to him instead of her, just this once.
passages.vernacular: 但呢星期南希畀斯諾太太做凍時,我想如果我能把佢畀佢,而唔係畀佢,就呢一次,該多好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這星期南希給斯諾太太做凍時,我想如果我能把它給他,而不是給她,就這一次,該多好。

passages.original: Aunt Polly, may I?”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽,可以嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽,可以嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, yes, I suppose so,” acquiesced Miss Polly, a little wearily.
passages.vernacular: 「好,好,我想可以,」波莉小姐有點疲倦地默許。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好,好,我想可以,」波莉小姐有點疲倦地默許。

passages.original: “Who did you say he was?”
passages.vernacular: 「你講佢係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說他是誰?」

passages.original: “The Man.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個男人。

passages.original: I mean, Mr. John Pendleton.”
passages.vernacular: 我係講,約翰·彭德爾頓先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是說,約翰·彭德爾頓先生。」

passages.original: Miss Polly almost sprang from her chair.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐幾乎從椅子上跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐幾乎從椅子上跳起來。

passages.original: “JOHN PENDLETON!”
passages.vernacular: 「約翰·彭德爾頓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「約翰·彭德爾頓!」

passages.original: “Yes.
Nancy told me his name.
passages.vernacular: 南希告訴我佢嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希告訴我他的名字。

passages.original: Maybe you know him.”
passages.vernacular: 或者您認識佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許您認識他。」

passages.original: Miss Polly did not answer this.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐沒有回答。

passages.original: Instead she asked:
passages.vernacular: 相反,佢問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相反,她問:

passages.original: “Do YOU know him?”
passages.vernacular: 「你認識佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你認識他嗎?」

passages.original: Pollyanna nodded.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜點頭。

passages.original: “Oh, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,認識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,認識。

passages.original: He always speaks and smiles--now.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家總是打招呼、微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在總是打招呼、微笑。

passages.original: He's only cross OUTSIDE, you know.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係外面兇,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只是外面兇,您知道。

passages.original: I'll go and get the jelly.
passages.vernacular: 我去攞凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去拿凍。

passages.original: Nancy had it 'most fixed when I came in,” finished Pollyanna, already halfway across the room.
passages.vernacular: 我進嚟時南希快弄好喇,」波麗安娜講完,已經走到房間一半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我進來時南希快弄好了,」波麗安娜說完,已經走到房間一半。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, wait!
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,等一下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,等一下!

passages.original: Miss Polly's voice was suddenly very stern.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅聲音突然好嚴厲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的聲音突然非常嚴厲。

passages.original: I've changed my mind.
passages.vernacular: 我改變主意喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我改變主意了。

passages.original: I would prefer that Mrs. Snow had that jelly to-day--as usual.
passages.vernacular: 我寧願斯諾太太今日照常得到嗰份凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧願斯諾太太今天照常得到那份凍。

passages.original: That is all.
passages.vernacular: 就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是這樣。

passages.original: You may go now.”
passages.vernacular: 你可以走喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以走了。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's face fell.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅臉沉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的臉沉了下來。

passages.original: “Oh, but Aunt Polly, HERS will last.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過波莉姨媽,佢嘅會持續下去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是波莉姨媽,她的會持續下去。

passages.original: She can always be sick and have things, you know; but his is just a broken leg, and legs don't last--I mean, broken ones.
passages.vernacular: 佢可以一直病住、有嘢食,你知道;但佢嘅只係一條斷腿,腿唔會持續——我係講,斷咗嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她可以一直病著、有東西吃,你知道;但他的只是一條斷腿,腿不會持續——我是說,斷了的。

passages.original: He's had it a whole week now.”
passages.vernacular: 佢已經斷咗整整一個星期喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他已經斷了整整一個星期了。」

passages.original: “Yes, I remember.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我記得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我記得。

passages.original: I heard Mr. John Pendleton had met with an accident,” said Miss Polly, a little stiffly; “but--I do not care to be sending jelly to John Pendleton, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 我聽講約翰·彭德爾頓先生出咗事故,」波莉小姐有點僵硬地講;「但係——我唔想畀約翰·彭德爾頓送凍,波麗安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽說約翰·彭德爾頓先生出了事故,」波莉小姐有點僵硬地說;「但是——我不想給約翰·彭德爾頓送凍,波麗安娜。」

passages.original: “I know, he is cross--outside,” admitted Pollyanna, sadly, “so I suppose you don't like him.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道,佢兇——外面,」波麗安娜悲傷地承認,「所以我想您不鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道,他兇——外面,」波麗安娜悲傷地承認,「所以我想您不喜歡他。

passages.original: But I wouldn't say 'twas you sent it.
passages.vernacular: 但我唔會講係您送嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不會說是您送的。

passages.original: I'd say 'twas me.
passages.vernacular: 我會講係我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會說是我。

passages.original: I like him.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡他。

passages.original: I'd be glad to send him jelly.”
passages.vernacular: 我好樂意畀佢送凍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很樂意給他送凍。」

passages.original: Miss Polly began to shake her head again.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐又開始搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐又開始搖頭。

passages.original: Then, suddenly, she stopped, and asked in a curiously quiet voice:
passages.vernacular: 然後,突然,佢停住,用奇特安靜嘅聲音問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,突然,她停住,用奇特安靜的聲音問:

passages.original: “Does he know who you--are, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢知道你係——邊個嗎,波麗安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他知道你是——誰嗎,波麗安娜?」

passages.original: The little girl sighed.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩嘆氣。

passages.original: “I reckon not.
passages.vernacular: 「我想唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不知道。

passages.original: I told him my name, once, but he never calls me it--never.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴過佢我嘅名字一次,但佢從不叫我嘅名字——從不。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴過他我的名字一次,但他從不叫我的名字——從不。」

passages.original: “Does he know where you--live?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢知道你住喺邊兒嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他知道你住在哪兒嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, no.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不。

passages.original: I never told him that.”
passages.vernacular: 我從冇告訴過佢嗰個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒告訴過他那個。」

passages.original: “Then he doesn't know you're my--niece?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰佢唔知道你係我嘅——外甥女?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那他不知道你是我的——外甥女?」

passages.original: “I don't think so.”
passages.vernacular: 「我想唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想不知道。」

passages.original: For a moment there was silence.
passages.vernacular: 有一會兒沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一會兒沉默。

passages.original: Miss Polly was looking at Pollyanna with eyes that did not seem to see her at all.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐睇住波麗安娜,眼睛似乎根本冇睇見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐看著波麗安娜,眼睛似乎根本沒看見她。

passages.original: The little girl, shifting impatiently from one small foot to the other, sighed audibly.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩不耐煩地喺兩隻小腳之間挪動重心,明顯地嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩不耐煩地在兩隻小腳之間挪動重心,明顯地嘆了口氣。

passages.original: Then Miss Polly roused herself with a start.
passages.vernacular: 然後波莉小姐猛然驚醒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後波莉小姐猛然驚醒。

passages.original: “Very well, Pollyanna,” she said at last, still in that queer voice, so unlike her own; “you may you may take the jelly to Mr. Pendleton as your own gift.
passages.vernacular: 「好好,波麗安娜,」佢終於講,仍然用嗰種不像佢自己嘅古怪聲音;「你可以把凍作為你自己嘅禮物送畀彭德爾頓先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很好,波麗安娜,」她終於說,仍然用那種不像她自己的古怪聲音;「你可以把凍作為你自己的禮物送給彭德爾頓先生。

passages.original: But understand: I do not send it.
passages.vernacular: 但要明白:我不送。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但要明白:我不送。

passages.original: Be very sure that he does not think I do!”
passages.vernacular: 一定要確保佢不認為係我送嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一定要確保他不認為是我送的!」

passages.original: “Yes'm--no'm--thank you, Aunt Polly,” exulted Pollyanna, as she flew through the door.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,夫人——不,夫人——謝謝您,波莉姨媽,」波麗安娜歡呼,飛出門去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,夫人——不,夫人——謝謝您,波莉姨媽,」波麗安娜歡呼,飛出門去。

chapters.title: Ch. XV Dr. Chilton 第十五章:奇爾頓醫生

passages.original: CH The great gray pile of masonry looked very different to Pollyanna when she made her second visit to the house of Mr. John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜第二次去約翰·彭德爾頓先生嘅房子時,嗰座灰色嘅大石堆睇起嚟好不一樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜第二次去約翰·彭德爾頓先生的房子時,那座灰色的大石堆看起來很不一樣。

passages.original: Windows were open, an elderly woman was hanging out clothes in the back yard, and the doctor's gig stood under the porte-cochere.
passages.vernacular: 窗子開住,一個上咗年紀嘅女人喺後院晾衣服,醫生嘅輕便馬車停喺車門廊下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗子開著,一個上了年紀的女人在後院晾衣服,醫生的輕便馬車停在車門廊下。

passages.original: As before Pollyanna went to the side door.
passages.vernacular: 像上次一樣,波麗安娜走到側門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像上次一樣,波麗安娜走到側門。

passages.original: This time she rang the bell--her fingers were not stiff to-day from a tight clutch on a bunch of keys.
passages.vernacular: 呢次佢按咗鈴——佢嘅手指今日唔再因緊攥一串鑰匙而僵硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次她按了鈴——她的手指今天不再因緊攥一串鑰匙而僵硬。

passages.original: A familiar-looking small dog bounded up the steps to greet her, but there was a slight delay before the woman who had been hanging out the clothes opened the door.
passages.vernacular: 一條睇起嚟眼熟嘅小狗蹦跳住上咗台階迎接佢,但喺晾衣服嘅嗰個女人開門之前稍有耽擱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一條看起來眼熟的小狗蹦跳著上了台階迎接她,但在晾衣服的那個女人開門之前稍有耽擱。

passages.original: “If you please, I've brought some calf's-foot jelly for Mr. Pendleton,” smiled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「打擾喇,我畀彭德爾頓先生帶嚟咗啲小牛腳凍,」波麗安娜微笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「打擾了,我給彭德爾頓先生帶來了一些小牛腳凍,」波麗安娜微笑著說。

passages.original: “Thank you,” said the woman, reaching for the bowl in the little girl's hand.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你,」嗰女人講,伸手去攞小女孩手裡嘅碗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你,」那女人說,伸手去拿小女孩手裡的碗。

passages.original: “Who shall I say sent it?
passages.vernacular: 「我該講係邊個送嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我該說是誰送的?

passages.original: And it's calf's-foot jelly?”
passages.vernacular: 仲有,係小牛腳凍?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,是小牛腳凍?」

passages.original: The doctor, coming into the hall at that moment, heard the woman's words and saw the disappointed look on Pollyanna's face.
passages.vernacular: 醫生呢陣走進大廳,聽見嗰女人嘅話,睇見波麗安娜臉上失望嘅神色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生這時走進大廳,聽見那女人的話,看見波麗安娜臉上失望的神色。

passages.original: He stepped quickly forward.
passages.vernacular: 佢快步走上前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他快步走上前。

passages.original: “Ah!
Some calf's-foot jelly?” he asked genially.
passages.vernacular: 小牛腳凍?」佢和藹地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小牛腳凍?」他和藹地問。

passages.original: “That will be fine!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰太好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那太好了!

passages.original: Maybe you'd like to see our patient, eh?”
passages.vernacular: 或者你想睇睇我哋嘅病人,嗯?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你想看看我們的病人,嗯?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, sir,” beamed Pollyanna; and the woman, in obedience to a nod from the doctor, led the way down the hall at once, though plainly with vast surprise on her face.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,想,先生,」波麗安娜笑容滿面;嗰女人喺醫生點頭嘅指示下,即刻領路沿住大廳走,雖然臉上明顯帶住極大嘅驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,想,先生,」波麗安娜笑容滿面;那女人在醫生點頭的指示下,立刻領路沿著大廳走,雖然臉上明顯帶著極大的驚訝。

passages.original: Behind the doctor, a young man (a trained nurse from the nearest city) gave a disturbed exclamation.
passages.vernacular: 醫生身後,一個年輕人(從最近嘅城市嚟嘅受過訓練嘅護士)發出咗不安嘅驚呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生身後,一個年輕人(從最近的城市來的受過訓練的護士)發出了不安的驚呼。

passages.original: “But, Doctor, didn't Mr. Pendleton give orders not to admit--any one?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,醫生,彭德爾頓先生唔係下令不准接見——任何人嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,醫生,彭德爾頓先生不是下令不准接見——任何人嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes,” nodded the doctor, imperturbably.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」醫生泰然自若地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」醫生泰然自若地點頭。

passages.original: “But I'm giving orders now.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我而家下令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我現在下令。

passages.original: I'll take the risk.”
passages.vernacular: 我嚟承擔風險。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來承擔風險。」

passages.original: Then he added whimsically: “You don't know, of course; but that little girl is better than a six-quart bottle of tonic any day.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢古怪地補充:「你當然唔知道;但嗰個小女孩任何一天都勝過一大瓶六夸脫嘅補藥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他古怪地補充:「你當然不知道;但那個小女孩任何一天都勝過一大瓶六夸脫的補藥。

passages.original: If anything or anybody can take the grouch out of Pendleton this afternoon, she can.
passages.vernacular: 如果有乜嘢嘢或乜嘢人今日下午能治好彭德爾頓嘅壞脾氣,就係佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果有什麼東西或什麼人今天下午能治好彭德爾頓的壞脾氣,就是她。

passages.original: That's why I sent her in.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我讓佢進去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我讓她進去。」

passages.original: “Who is she?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是誰?」

passages.original: For one brief moment the doctor hesitated.
passages.vernacular: 有咁短暫嘅一刻,醫生遲疑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼短暫的一刻,醫生遲疑了。

passages.original: “She's the niece of one of our best known residents.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係我哋一位最有名嘅居民嘅外甥女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是我們一位最有名的居民的外甥女。

passages.original: Her name is Pollyanna Whittier.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字叫波麗安娜·惠蒂爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的名字叫波麗安娜·惠蒂爾。

passages.original: I--I don't happen to enjoy a very extensive personal acquaintance with the little lady as yet; but lots of my patients do--I'm thankful to say!”
passages.vernacular: 我——我碰巧仲冇多少同呢位小女士嘅私人交情;但我嘅好多病人有——我好感謝呢啲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——我碰巧還沒有多少與這位小女士的私人交情;但我的很多病人有——我很感謝這一點!」

passages.original: The nurse smiled.
passages.vernacular: 護士笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士笑了。

passages.original: “Indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的!

passages.original: And what are the special ingredients of this wonder-working--tonic of hers?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰佢呢種神奇嘅——補藥嘅特殊成分係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那她這種神奇的——補藥的特殊成分是什麼?」

passages.original: The doctor shook his head.
passages.vernacular: 醫生搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生搖搖頭。

passages.original: “I don't know.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。

passages.original: As near as I can find out it is an overwhelming, unquenchable gladness for everything that has happened or is going to happen.
passages.vernacular: 據我所能發現嘅,係對已經發生或將要發生嘅一切嘅一種壓倒性嘅、撲不滅嘅高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據我所能發現的,是對已經發生或將要發生的一切的一種壓倒性的、撲不滅的高興。

passages.original: At any rate, her quaint speeches are constantly being repeated to me, and, as near as I can make out, 'just being glad' is the tenor of most of them.
passages.vernacular: 總之,佢古怪嘅話不斷有人重複畀我聽,而據我所見,『只要高興』係其中大多數嘅主旨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,她古怪的話不斷有人重複給我聽,而據我所見,『只要高興』是其中大多數的主旨。

passages.original: All is,” he added, with another whimsical smile, as he stepped out on to the porch, “I wish I could prescribe her--and buy her--as I would a box of pills;--though if there gets to be many of her in the world, you and I might as well go to ribbon-selling and ditch-digging for all the money we'd get out of nursing and doctoring,” he laughed, picking up the reins and stepping into the gig.
passages.vernacular: 只係,」佢又帶住古怪嘅微笑補充,走到門廊上,「我希望我能像開一盒藥丸嗰樣開佢嘅處方——買到佢;——不過如果世上有許多像佢咁樣嘅人,你我不妨改行去賣緞帶同挖溝,因為護理同行醫賺唔到一分錢,」佢笑住講,攞起韁繩,上咗輕便馬車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是,」他又帶著古怪的微笑補充,走到門廊上,「我希望我能像開一盒藥丸那樣開她的處方——買到她;——不過如果世上有許多像她這樣的人,你我不妨改行去賣緞帶和挖溝,因為護理和行醫賺不到一分錢,」他笑著說,拿起韁繩,上了輕便馬車。

passages.original: Pollyanna, meanwhile, in accordance with the doctor's orders, was being escorted to John Pendleton's rooms.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜呢陣按醫生嘅吩咐,被護送到約翰·彭德爾頓嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜這時按醫生的吩咐,被護送到約翰·彭德爾頓的房間。

passages.original: Her way led through the great library at the end of the hall, and, rapid as was her progress through it, Pollyanna saw at once that great changes had taken place.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅路穿過走廊盡頭嘅大圖書室,儘管佢走得飛快,波麗安娜即刻睇出發生咗好大嘅變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的路穿過走廊盡頭的大圖書室,儘管她走得飛快,波麗安娜立刻看出發生了很大的變化。

passages.original: The book-lined walls and the crimson curtains were the same; but there was no litter on the floor, no untidiness on the desk, and not so much as a grain of dust in sight.
passages.vernacular: 滿係書嘅牆壁同深紅色嘅窗簾仍然係原樣;但地板上冇雜物,書桌上冇凌亂,視線裡連一粒灰塵都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滿是書的牆壁和深紅色的窗簾仍然是原樣;但地板上沒有雜物,書桌上沒有凌亂,視線裡連一粒灰塵都沒有。

passages.original: The telephone card hung in its proper place, and the brass andirons had been polished.
passages.vernacular: 電話卡掛喺佢應有嘅位置上,黃銅柴架被擦亮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 電話卡掛在它應有的位置上,黃銅柴架被擦亮了。

passages.original: One of the mysterious doors was open, and it was toward this that the maid led the way.
passages.vernacular: 其中一扇神祕嘅門開住,女傭向佢領路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一扇神祕的門開著,女傭向它領路。

passages.original: A moment later Pollyanna found herself in a sumptuously furnished bedroom while the maid was saying in a frightened voice:
passages.vernacular: 片刻後,波麗安娜發現自己喺一間陳設豪華嘅臥室裡,女傭用害怕嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 片刻後,波麗安娜發現自己在一間陳設豪華的臥室裡,女傭用害怕的聲音說:

passages.original: “If you please, sir, here--here's a little girl with some jelly.
passages.vernacular: 「請原諒,先生,呢——呢兒有個小女孩帶住啲凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請原諒,先生,這——這兒有個小女孩帶著一些凍。

passages.original: The doctor said I was to--to bring her in.”
passages.vernacular: 醫生講我要——要帶佢進嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生說我要——要帶她進來。」

passages.original: The next moment Pollyanna found herself alone with a very cross-looking man lying flat on his back in bed.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻,波麗安娜發現自己同一個睇起嚟好暴躁嘅、直挺挺躺喺床上嘅男人獨自在一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻,波麗安娜發現自己同一個看起來非常暴躁的、直挺挺躺在床上的男人獨自在一起。

passages.original: “See here, didn't I say--” began an angry voice.
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,我唔係講過——」一個憤怒嘅聲音開始講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,我不是說過——」一個憤怒的聲音開始說。

passages.original: “Oh, it's you!” it broke off not very graciously, as Pollyanna advanced toward the bed.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係你!」當波麗安娜朝床走去,佢不太客氣地打斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是你!」當波麗安娜朝床走去,它不太客氣地打斷了。

passages.original: “Yes, sir,” smiled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生,」波麗安娜微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生,」波麗安娜微笑。

passages.original: “Oh, I'm so glad they let me in!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興佢哋讓我進嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興他們讓我進來了!

passages.original: You see, at first the lady 'most took my jelly, and I was so afraid I wasn't going to see you at all.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,起初嗰位女士差點就攞走咗我嘅凍,我咁怕我根本見唔到您。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,起初那位女士差點就拿走了我的凍,我那麼怕我根本見不到您。

passages.original: Then the doctor came, and he said I might.
passages.vernacular: 然後醫生來喇,佢講我可以。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後醫生來了,他說我可以。

passages.original: Wasn't he lovely to let me see you?”
passages.vernacular: 佢讓我見您,唔係好好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他讓我見您,不是很好嗎?」

passages.original: In spite of himself the man's lips twitched into a smile; but all he said was “Humph!”
passages.vernacular: 儘管佢自己唔願意,嗰人嘅嘴唇定係抽動成咗一個微笑;但佢只講咗聲「哼!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管他自己不願意,那人的嘴唇還是抽動成了一個微笑;但他只說了聲「哼!」

passages.original: “And I've brought you some jelly,” resumed Pollyanna; “--calf's-foot.
passages.vernacular: 「我畀您帶咗啲凍,」波麗安娜繼續講;「——小牛腳凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給您帶了一些凍,」波麗安娜繼續說;「——小牛腳凍。

passages.original: I hope you like it?”
passages.vernacular: 我希望您鍾意?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望您喜歡?」

passages.original: There was a rising inflection in her voice.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅聲音有上揚嘅語調。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的聲音有上揚的語調。

passages.original: “Never ate it.”
passages.vernacular: 「從冇食過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從沒吃過。」

passages.original: The fleeting smile had gone, and the scowl had come back to the man's face.
passages.vernacular: 嗰轉瞬即逝嘅微笑消失喇,怒容回到嗰人嘅臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那轉瞬即逝的微笑消失了,怒容回到那人的臉上。

passages.original: For a brief instant Pollyanna's countenance showed disappointment; but it cleared as she set the bowl of jelly down.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜嘅臉上有片刻顯出失望;但佢放下嗰碗凍時又放晴喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜的臉上有片刻顯出失望;但她放下那碗凍時又放晴了。

passages.original: “Didn't you?
passages.vernacular: 「冇食過嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒吃過嗎?

passages.original: Well, if you didn't, then you can't know you DON'T like it, anyhow, can you?
passages.vernacular: 嗯,如果您冇食過,嗰您反正唔知道您不鍾意佢,係唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,如果您沒吃過,那您反正不知道您不喜歡它,是不是?

passages.original: So I reckon I'm glad you haven't, after all.
passages.vernacular: 所以我想我反而高興您冇食過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我想我反而高興您沒吃過。

passages.original: Now, if you knew--”
passages.vernacular: 而家,如果您知道——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,如果您知道——」

passages.original: “Yes, yes; well, there's one thing I know all right, and that is that I'm flat on my back right here this minute, and that I'm liable to stay here--till doomsday, I guess.”
passages.vernacular: 「係,係;嗯,有一件事我確實知道,就係呢一刻我直挺挺地躺喺呢兒,而且我可能要一直躺喺呢兒——直到世界末日,我想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,是;嗯,有一件事我確實知道,就是這一刻我直挺挺地躺在這兒,而且我可能要一直躺在這兒——直到世界末日,我想。」

passages.original: Pollyanna looked shocked.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜顯得震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜顯得震驚。

passages.original: “Oh, no!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不!
