passages.original: It couldn't be till doomsday, you know, when the angel Gabriel blows his trumpet, unless it should come quicker than we think it will--oh, of course, I know the Bible says it may come quicker than we think, but I don't think it will--that is, of course I believe the Bible; but I mean I don't think it will come as much quicker as it would if it should come now, and--”
passages.vernacular: 唔可能直到世界末日,您知道,就係天使加百列吹號角嘅時候,除非佢嚟得比我哋想嘅更快——哦,當然,我知道聖經講佢可能比我哋想嘅嚟得更快,但我不認為會——就係,當然我相信聖經;但我嘅意思係,我不認為佢會比而家嚟得更快——如果佢而家嚟嘅話,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能直到世界末日,您知道,就是天使加百列吹號角的時候,除非它來得比我們想的更快——哦,當然,我知道聖經說它可能比我們想的來得更快,但我不認為會——就是,當然我相信聖經;但我的意思是,我不認為它會比現在來得更快——如果它現在來的話,而且——」

passages.original: John Pendleton laughed suddenly--and aloud.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·彭德爾頓突然笑喇——仲笑出咗聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·彭德爾頓突然笑了——還笑出了聲。

passages.original: The nurse, coming in at that moment, heard the laugh, and beat a hurried--but a very silent--retreat.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣走進嚟嘅護士聽見笑聲,匆忙但極其安靜地退咗出去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時走進來的護士聽見笑聲,匆忙但極其安靜地退了出去。

passages.original: He had the air of a frightened cook who, seeing the danger of a breath of cold air striking a half-done cake, hastily shuts the oven door.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅神態像一個受驚嘅廚子,睇到一股冷風可能吹到半熟嘅蛋糕,趕緊關上烤箱門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的神態像一個受驚的廚子,看到一股冷風可能吹到半熟的蛋糕,趕緊關上烤箱門。

passages.original: “Aren't you getting a little mixed?” asked John Pendleton of Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「你係唔係有點糊塗喇?」約翰·彭德爾頓問波麗安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是不是有點糊塗了?」約翰·彭德爾頓問波麗安娜。

passages.original: The little girl laughed.
passages.vernacular: 小女孩笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小女孩笑了。

passages.original: “Maybe.
passages.vernacular: 「或者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許。

passages.original: But what I mean is, that legs don't last--broken ones, you know--like lifelong invalids, same as Mrs. Snow has got.
passages.vernacular: 但我嘅意思係,腿唔會持續——我係講斷咗嘅——像終身病人,就像斯諾太太嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我的意思是,腿不會持續——我是說斷了的——像終身病人,就像斯諾太太那樣。

passages.original: So yours won't last till doomsday at all.
passages.vernacular: 所以您嘅根本唔會持續到世界末日。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以您的根本不會持續到世界末日。

passages.original: I should think you could be glad of that.”
passages.vernacular: 我想您可以為此高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您可以為此高興。」

passages.original: “Oh, I am,” retorted the man grimly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我係,」嗰人嚴峻地反駁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我是,」那人嚴峻地反駁。

passages.original: “And you didn't break but one.
passages.vernacular: 「而且您只斷咗一條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且您只斷了一條。

passages.original: You can be glad 'twasn't two.”
passages.vernacular: 您可以高興唔係兩條。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您可以高興不是兩條。」

passages.original: Pollyanna was warming to her task.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜喺佢嘅任務中越嚟越起勁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜在她的任務中越來越起勁。

passages.original: “Of course!
passages.vernacular: 「當然!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然!

passages.original: So fortunate,” sniffed the man, with uplifted eyebrows; “looking at it from that standpoint, I suppose I might be glad I wasn't a centipede and didn't break fifty!”
passages.vernacular: 多幸運啊,」嗰人哼咗一聲,挑起眉毛;「從嗰個角度睇,我想我可以高興我唔係蜈蚣,冇斷五十條!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多幸運啊,」那人哼了一聲,挑起眉毛;「從那個角度看,我想我可以高興我不是蜈蚣,沒斷五十條!」

passages.original: Pollyanna chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜咯咯笑。

passages.original: “Oh, that's the best yet,” she crowed.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,呢個係目前最好嘅,」佢歡叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這是目前最好的,」她歡叫。

passages.original: “I know what a centipede is; they've got lots of legs.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道蜈蚣係乜嘢;佢哋有好多腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道蜈蚣是什麼;它們有很多腿。

passages.original: And you can be glad--”
passages.vernacular: 而您可以高興——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而您可以高興——」

passages.original: “Oh, of course,” interrupted the man, sharply, all the old bitterness coming back to his voice; “I can be glad, too, for all the rest, I suppose--the nurse, and the doctor, and that confounded woman in the kitchen!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,當然,」嗰人尖銳地打斷,所有舊日嘅苦澀回到佢嘅聲音裡;「我想我仲可以為其餘嘅一切高興——護士、醫生,同廚房裡嗰個該死嘅女人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,當然,」那人尖銳地打斷,所有舊日的苦澀回到他的聲音裡;「我想我還可以為其餘的一切高興——護士、醫生,和廚房裡那個該死的女人!」

passages.original: “Why, yes, sir--only think how bad 'twould be if you DIDN'T have them!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係嘅,先生——想想如果您冇佢哋,該多糟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是的,先生——想想如果您沒有他們,該多糟!」

passages.original: “Well, I--eh?” he demanded sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我——嗯?」佢尖銳地質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我——嗯?」他尖銳地質問。

passages.original: “Why, I say, only think how bad it would be if you didn't have 'em--and you lying here like this!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我講,想想如果您冇佢哋——而您像咁樣躺喺呢度,該多糟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我說,想想如果您沒有他們——而您像這樣躺在這裡,該多糟!」

passages.original: “As if that wasn't the very thing that was at the bottom of the whole matter,” retorted the man, testily, “because I am lying here like this!
passages.vernacular: 「好像嗰不正是整件事嘅根源似嘅,」嗰人急躁地反駁,「因為我像咁樣躺喺呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像那不正是整件事的根源似的,」那人急躁地反駁,「因為我像這樣躺在這裡!

passages.original: And yet you expect me to say I'm glad because of a fool woman who disarranges the whole house and calls it 'regulating,' and a man who aids and abets her in it, and calls it 'nursing,' to say nothing of the doctor who eggs 'em both on--and the whole bunch of them, meanwhile, expecting me to pay them for it, and pay them well, too!”
passages.vernacular: 而你仲期望我講我高興,因為一個蠢女人把整座房子弄得亂七八糟,仲叫佢『整頓』,仲有一個男人幫佢出主意,叫佢『護理』,更別提煽動佢哋倆嘅醫生——而佢哋呢一夥,同時仲期望我為此付錢,而且付得好高!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你還期望我說我高興,因為一個蠢女人把整座房子弄得亂七八糟,還叫它『整頓』,還有一個男人幫她出主意,叫它『護理』,更別提煽動他們倆的醫生——而他們這一夥,同時還期望我為此付錢,而且付得很高!」

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned sympathetically.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜同情地皺眉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜同情地皺眉。

passages.original: “Yes, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「係,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,我知道。

passages.original: THAT part is too bad--about the money--when you've been saving it, too, all this time.”
passages.vernacular: 嗰部分太糟喇——關於錢——當您一直喺存佢嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那部分太糟了——關於錢——當您一直在存它的時候。」

passages.original: “When--eh?”
“Saving it--buying beans and fish balls, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「存錢——買豆子同魚丸,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「存錢——買豆子和魚丸,您知道。

passages.original: Say, DO you like beans?--or do you like turkey better, only on account of the sixty cents?”
passages.vernacular: 講,您鍾意豆子嗎?——定係您更鍾意火雞,只係因為嗰六十美分?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說,您喜歡豆子嗎?——還是您更喜歡火雞,只是因為那六十美分?」

passages.original: “Look a-here, child, what are you talking about?”
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,細路,你喺講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,孩子,你在說什麼?」

passages.original: Pollyanna smiled radiantly.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑得燦爛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑得燦爛。

passages.original: “About your money, you know--denying yourself, and saving it for the heathen.
passages.vernacular: 「關於您嘅錢,您知道——克己,把佢存畀異教徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「關於您的錢,您知道——克己,把它存給異教徒。

passages.original: You see, I found out about it.
passages.vernacular: 您睇,我知道喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,我知道了。

passages.original: Why, Mr. Pendleton, that's one of the ways I knew you weren't cross inside.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,彭德爾頓先生,呢個係我知道您裡面不兇嘅方式之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,彭德爾頓先生,這是我知道您裡面不兇的方式之一。

passages.original: Nancy told me.”
passages.vernacular: 係南希告訴我嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是南希告訴我的。」

passages.original: The man's jaw dropped.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人嘅下巴掉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人的下巴掉了下來。

passages.original: “Nancy told you I was saving money for the--Well, may I inquire who Nancy is?”
passages.vernacular: 「南希告訴你我喺存錢畀——好吧,我能問問南希係邊個嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希告訴你我在存錢給——好吧,我能問問南希是誰嗎?」

passages.original: “Our Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋嘅南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們的南希。

passages.original: She works for Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 佢為波莉姨媽工作。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她為波莉姨媽工作。」

passages.original: “Aunt Polly!
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽!

passages.original: Well, who is Aunt Polly?”
passages.vernacular: 好吧,波莉姨媽係邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,波莉姨媽是誰?」

passages.original: “She's Miss Polly Harrington.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係波莉·哈林頓小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是波莉·哈林頓小姐。

passages.original: I live with her.”
passages.vernacular: 我同佢住喺一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和她住在一起。」

passages.original: The man made a sudden movement.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人突然動咗動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人突然動了動。

passages.original: “Miss--Polly--Harrington!” he breathed.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉——哈林頓——小姐!」佢低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉——哈林頓——小姐!」他低聲說。

passages.original: “You live with--HER!”
passages.vernacular: 「你同——佢住喺一起!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你同——她住在一起!」

passages.original: “Yes; I'm her niece.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;我係佢嘅外甥女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;我是她的外甥女。

passages.original: She's taken me to bring up--on account of my mother, you know,” faltered Pollyanna, in a low voice.
passages.vernacular: 佢收我撫養——因為我嘅媽媽,您知道,」波麗安娜低聲結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她收我撫養——因為我的媽媽,您知道,」波麗安娜低聲結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “She was her sister.
passages.vernacular: 「佢係佢嘅姐姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是她的姐姐。

passages.original: And after father--went to be with her and the rest of us in Heaven, there wasn't any one left for me down here but the Ladies' Aid; so she took me.”
passages.vernacular: 喺爸爸去同佢同我哋其他人喺天堂之後,下面呢度冇人畀我,只有婦女互助會;所以佢收咗我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在爸爸去同她和我們其他人在天堂之後,下面這裡沒有人給我,只有婦女互助會;所以她收了我。」

passages.original: The man did not answer.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人沒有回答。

passages.original: His face, as he lay back on the pillow now, was very white--so white that Pollyanna was frightened.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家向後靠喺枕頭上,臉好白——白得讓波麗安娜害怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在向後靠在枕頭上,臉很白——白得讓波麗安娜害怕。

passages.original: She rose uncertainly to her feet.
passages.vernacular: 佢猶豫地站起身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她猶豫地站起身。

passages.original: “I reckon maybe I'd better go now,” she proposed.
passages.vernacular: 「我想或者我最好而家走喇,」佢提議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也許我最好現在走了,」她提議。

passages.original: “I--I hope you'll like--the jelly.”
passages.vernacular: 「我——我希望您鍾意——呢個凍。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我希望您喜歡——這個凍。」

passages.original: The man turned his head suddenly, and opened his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人突然轉過頭,睜開眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人突然轉過頭,睜開眼睛。

passages.original: There was a curious longing in their dark depths which even Pollyanna saw, and at which she marvelled.
passages.vernacular: 佢深色嘅眼睛深處有一種奇怪嘅渴望,連波麗安娜都睇出嚟喇,並為之驚奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他深色的眼睛深處有一種奇怪的渴望,連波麗安娜也看出來了,並為之驚奇。

passages.original: “And so you are--Miss Polly Harrington's niece,” he said gently.
passages.vernacular: 「咁講你係——波莉·哈林頓小姐嘅外甥女,」佢輕聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說你是——波莉·哈林頓小姐的外甥女,」他輕聲說。

passages.original: “Yes, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。」

passages.original: Still the man's dark eyes lingered on her face, until Pollyanna, feeling vaguely restless, murmured:
passages.vernacular: 嗰人嘅深色眼睛仍然停留喺佢臉上,直到波麗安娜隱約感到不安,低聲講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人的深色眼睛仍然停留在她臉上,直到波麗安娜隱約感到不安,低聲說:

passages.original: “I--I suppose you know--her.”
passages.vernacular: 「我——我想您認識——佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我想您認識——她。」

passages.original: John Pendleton's lips curved in an odd smile.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·彭德爾頓嘅嘴唇彎成一個奇怪嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·彭德爾頓的嘴唇彎成一個奇怪的微笑。

passages.original: “Oh, yes; I know her.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅;我認識佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的;我認識她。」

passages.original: He hesitated, then went on, still with that curious smile.
passages.vernacular: 佢猶豫喇,然後繼續,仍帶住嗰種奇怪嘅微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他猶豫了,然後繼續,仍帶著那種奇怪的微笑。

passages.original: “But--you don't mean--you can't mean that it was Miss Polly Harrington who sent that jelly--to me?” he said slowly.
passages.vernacular: 「但係——你唔係講——你唔可能係講,係波莉·哈林頓小姐把嗰個凍送畀——我嘅?」佢慢慢地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是——你不是說——你不可能是說,是波莉·哈林頓小姐把那個凍送給——我的?」他慢慢地說。

passages.original: Pollyanna looked distressed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜顯得苦惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜顯得苦惱。

passages.original: “N-no, sir: she didn't.
passages.vernacular: 「不——不,先生;佢冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不——不,先生;她沒有。

passages.original: She said I must be very sure not to let you think she did send it.
passages.vernacular: 佢講我必須確保不讓您以為係佢送嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說我必須確保不讓您以為是她送的。

passages.original: But I--”
passages.vernacular: 不過我——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我——」

passages.original: “I thought as much,” vouchsafed the man, shortly, turning away his head.
passages.vernacular: 「我想都係,」嗰人簡短地講,把頭轉開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也是,」那人簡短地說,把頭轉開。

passages.original: And Pollyanna, still more distressed, tiptoed from the room.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜更加苦惱,踮住腳尖離開咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜更加苦惱,踮著腳尖離開了房間。

passages.original: Under the porte-cochere she found the doctor waiting in his gig.
passages.vernacular: 喺車門廊下,佢發現醫生坐喺輕便馬車裡等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在車門廊下,她發現醫生坐在輕便馬車裡等著。

passages.original: The nurse stood on the steps.
passages.vernacular: 護士站喺台階上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士站在台階上。

passages.original: “Well, Miss Pollyanna, may I have the pleasure of seeing you home?” asked the doctor smilingly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,波麗安娜小姐,我可以有幸送你回家嗎?」醫生微笑住問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,波麗安娜小姐,我可以有幸送你回家嗎?」醫生微笑著問。

passages.original: “I started to drive on a few minutes ago; then it occurred to me that I'd wait for you.”
passages.vernacular: 「幾分鐘前我開始要走喇;然後想到我該等你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「幾分鐘前我開始要走了;然後想到我該等你。」

passages.original: “Thank you, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝您,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝您,先生。

passages.original: I'm glad you did.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興您等喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興您等了。

passages.original: I just love to ride,” beamed Pollyanna, as he reached out his hand to help her in.
passages.vernacular: 我太愛坐車喇,」波麗安娜笑容滿面,佢伸出手扶佢上車。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太愛坐車了,」波麗安娜笑容滿面,他伸出手扶她上車。

passages.original: “Do you?” smiled the doctor, nodding his head in farewell to the young man on the steps.
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?」醫生微笑住講,朝台階上嘅年輕人點頭告別。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?」醫生微笑著說,朝台階上的年輕人點頭告別。

passages.original: “Well, as near as I can judge, there are a good many things you 'love' to do--eh?” he added, as they drove briskly away.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,據我所能判斷,有好多事你『愛』做——對吧?」佢補充講,佢哋輕快地駛走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,據我所能判斷,有很多事你『愛』做——對吧?」他補充說,他們輕快地駛走。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜笑了。

passages.original: “Why, I don't know.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,我唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,我不知道。

passages.original: I reckon perhaps there are,” she admitted.
passages.vernacular: 我想或者有,」佢承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想也許有,」她承認。

passages.original: “I like to do 'most everything that's LIVING.
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意做幾乎所有『生活』嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡做幾乎所有『生活』的事。

passages.original: Of course I don't like the other things very well--sewing, and reading out loud, and all that.
passages.vernacular: 當然我不太鍾意別嘅事——縫紉、大聲朗讀,等等。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然我不太喜歡別的事——縫紉、大聲朗讀,等等。

passages.original: But THEY aren't LIVING.”
passages.vernacular: 但嗰啲唔係『生活』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那些不是『生活』。」

passages.original: “No?
passages.vernacular: 「唔係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是?

passages.original: What are they, then?”
passages.vernacular: 嗰佢哋係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那它們是什麼?」

passages.original: “Aunt Polly says they're 'learning to live,'” sighed Pollyanna, with a rueful smile.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽講佢哋係『學習生活』,」波麗安娜帶住懊惱嘅微笑嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽說它們是『學習生活』,」波麗安娜帶著懊惱的微笑嘆氣。

passages.original: The doctor smiled now--a little queerly.
passages.vernacular: 醫生呢陣笑喇——有點古怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生這時笑了——有點古怪。

passages.original: “Does she?
passages.vernacular: 「佢咁講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她這麼說?

passages.original: Well, I should think she might say--just that.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我想佢可能會講——正是嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我想她可能會說——正是那樣。」

passages.original: “Yes,” responded Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係,」波麗安娜回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,」波麗安娜回答。

passages.original: “But I don't see it that way at all.
passages.vernacular: 「但我根本唔係咁睇嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我根本不是那麼看的。

passages.original: I don't think you have to LEARN how to live.
passages.vernacular: 我不認為你需要學點生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不認為你需要學怎麼生活。

passages.original: I didn't, anyhow.”
passages.vernacular: 反正我冇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正我沒有。」

passages.original: The doctor drew a long sigh.
passages.vernacular: 醫生長長地嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生長長地嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “After all, I'm afraid some of us--do have to, little girl,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「畢竟,我怕我哋有些人確實需要,小姑娘,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「畢竟,我怕我們有些人確實需要,小姑娘,」他說。

passages.original: Then, for a time he was silent.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢沉默咗一陣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,他沉默了一陣。

passages.original: Pollyanna, stealing a glance at his face, felt vaguely sorry for him.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜偷偷睇咗一眼佢嘅臉,隱約為佢難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜偷偷看了一眼他的臉,隱約為他難過。

passages.original: He looked so sad.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟咁悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來那麼悲傷。

passages.original: She wished, uneasily, that she could “do something.”
passages.vernacular: 佢不安地希望佢能「做點乜嘢」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不安地希望她能「做點什麼」。

passages.original: It was this, perhaps, that caused her to say in a timid voice:
passages.vernacular: 或者正是呢個,使佢用膽怯嘅聲音講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許正是這個,使她用膽怯的聲音說:

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton, I should think being a doctor would, be the very gladdest kind of a business there was.”
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生,我想當醫生係世上最高興嘅行業喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生,我想當醫生是世上最高興的行業了。」

passages.original: The doctor turned in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 醫生驚訝地轉過頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生驚訝地轉過頭。

passages.original: “'Gladdest'!--when I see so much suffering always, everywhere I go?” he cried.
passages.vernacular: 「『最高興』!——當我無論去邊度都總是睇到咁多痛苦?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『最高興』!——當我無論去哪裡都總是看到這麼多痛苦?」他喊道。

passages.original: She nodded.
passages.vernacular: 佢點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她點頭。

passages.original: “I know; but you're HELPING it--don't you see?--and of course you're glad to help it!
passages.vernacular: 「我知道;但係您喺幫助緩解佢——您冇睇出嚟嗎?——當然您高興幫助緩解!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道;但是您在幫助緩解它——您沒看出來嗎?——當然您高興幫助緩解!

passages.original: And so that makes you the gladdest of any of us, all the time.”
passages.vernacular: 所以呢讓您始終係我哋所有人中最高興嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以這讓您始終是我們所有人中最高興的。」

passages.original: The doctor's eyes filled with sudden hot tears.
passages.vernacular: 醫生嘅眼裡突然湧滿熱淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生的眼裡突然湧滿熱淚。

passages.original: The doctor's life was a singularly lonely one.
passages.vernacular: 醫生嘅生活特別孤獨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生的生活特別孤獨。

passages.original: He had no wife and no home save his two-room office in a boarding house.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇妻子,冇家,只有寄宿公寓裡嘅兩間辦公室。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有妻子,沒有家,只有寄宿公寓裡的兩間辦公室。

passages.original: His profession was very dear to him.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅職業對佢好珍貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的職業對他非常珍貴。

passages.original: Looking now into Pollyanna's shining eyes, he felt as if a loving hand had been suddenly laid on his head in blessing.
passages.vernacular: 而家望住波麗安娜閃亮嘅眼睛,佢覺得好像有一隻慈愛嘅手突然放喺佢嘅頭上為佢祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在望著波麗安娜閃亮的眼睛,他覺得好像有一隻慈愛的手突然放在他的頭上為他祝福。

passages.original: He knew, too, that never again would a long day's work or a long night's weariness be quite without that new-found exaltation that had come to him through Pollyanna's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢都知道,今後漫長嘅一天工作或漫長嘅一夜疲倦,再唔會冇嗰種通過波麗安娜嘅眼睛得到嘅新發現嘅昂揚感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他也知道,今後漫長的一天工作或漫長的一夜疲倦,再不會沒有那種通過波麗安娜的眼睛得到的新發現的昂揚感。

passages.original: “God bless you, little girl,” he said unsteadily.
passages.vernacular: 「上帝保佑你,小姑娘,」佢不穩地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「上帝保佑你,小姑娘,」他不穩地說。

passages.original: Then, with the bright smile his patients knew and loved so well, he added: “And I'm thinking, after all, that it was the doctor, quite as much as his patients, that needed a draft of that tonic!”
passages.vernacular: 然後,帶住佢嘅病人哋都知道並喜愛嘅燦爛微笑,佢補充道:「我想,畢竟,需要飲一口嗰補藥嘅,同佢嘅病人一樣,係醫生!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,帶著他的病人們都知道並喜愛的燦爛微笑,他補充道:「我想,畢竟,需要喝一口那補藥的,和他的病人一樣,是醫生!」

passages.original: All of which puzzled Pollyanna very much--until a chipmunk, running across the road, drove the whole matter from her mind.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切讓波麗安娜好困惑——直到一隻花栗鼠跑過馬路,把整件事趕出咗佢嘅腦海。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切讓波麗安娜非常困惑——直到一隻花栗鼠跑過馬路,把整件事趕出了她的腦海。

passages.original: The doctor left Pollyanna at her own door, smiled at Nancy, who was sweeping off the front porch, then drove rapidly away.
passages.vernacular: 醫生把波麗安娜放喺佢自己家門口,對正在掃前廊嘅南希微笑,然後迅速駛走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生把波麗安娜放在她自己家門口,對正在掃前廊的南希微笑,然後迅速駛走。

passages.original: “I've had a perfectly beautiful ride with the doctor,” announced Pollyanna, bounding up the steps.
passages.vernacular: 「我同醫生坐咗一次絕對美好嘅車,」波麗安娜宣布,蹦跳住上台階。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我同醫生坐了一次絕對美好的車,」波麗安娜宣布,蹦跳著上台階。

passages.original: “He's lovely, Nancy!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢太好喇,南希!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他太好了,南希!」

passages.original: “Is he?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes.
And I told him I should think his business would be the very gladdest one there was.”
passages.vernacular: 我仲告訴佢,我想佢嘅行業係世上最高興嘅行業。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還告訴他,我想他的行業是世上最高興的行業。」

passages.original: “What!--goin' ter see sick folks--an' folks what ain't sick but thinks they is, which is worse?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢!——去睇病人——仲有唔係病人卻以為自己係嘅人,嗰仲更糟?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼!——去看病人——還有不是病人卻以為自己是的人,那還更糟?」

passages.original: Nancy's face showed open skepticism.
passages.vernacular: 南希嘅臉上露出公開嘅懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希的臉上露出公開的懷疑。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed gleefully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜高興地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜高興地笑了。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: That's 'most what he said, too; but there is a way to be glad, even then.
passages.vernacular: 佢差不多都咁講;但即使咁樣都有高興嘅方法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他差不多也這麼說;但即使這樣也有高興的方法。

passages.original: Guess!”
Nancy frowned in meditation.
passages.vernacular: 南希皺眉沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希皺眉沉思。

passages.original: Nancy was getting so she could play this game of “being glad” quite successfully, she thought.
passages.vernacular: 南希覺得自己玩呢個「高興」遊戲玩得相當成功喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希覺得自己玩這個「高興」遊戲玩得相當成功了。

passages.original: She rather enjoyed studying out Pollyanna's “posers,” too, as she called some of the little girl's questions.
passages.vernacular: 佢都相當鍾意琢磨波麗安娜嘅「難題」,佢咁樣稱呼小女孩嘅啲問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也相當喜歡琢磨波麗安娜的「難題」,她這樣稱呼小女孩的一些問題。

passages.original: “Oh, I know,” she chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我知道,」佢咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我知道,」她咯咯笑。

passages.original: “It's just the opposite from what you told Mis' Snow.”
passages.vernacular: 「正好同你對斯諾太太講嘅相反。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「正好和你對斯諾太太說的相反。」

passages.original: “Opposite?” repeated Pollyanna, obviously puzzled.
passages.vernacular: 「相反?」波麗安娜重複,明顯困惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「相反?」波麗安娜重複,明顯困惑。

passages.original: “Yes.
You told her she could be glad because other folks wasn't like her--all sick, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你告訴佢,佢可以高興係因為別人不像佢——全病住,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你告訴她,她可以高興是因為別人不像她——全病著,你知道。」

passages.original: “Yes,” nodded Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係,」波麗安娜點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,」波麗安娜點頭。

passages.original: “Well, the doctor can be glad because he isn't like other folks--the sick ones, I mean, what he doctors,” finished Nancy in triumph.
passages.vernacular: 「咁,醫生可以高興係因為佢不像別人——生病嘅,我係講,佢醫治嘅,」南希得意地結束。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼,醫生可以高興是因為他不像別人——生病的,我是說,他醫治的,」南希得意地結束。

passages.original: It was Pollyanna's turn to frown.
passages.vernacular: 輪到波麗安娜皺眉喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 輪到波麗安娜皺眉了。

passages.original: “Why, y-yes,” she admitted.
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,係——係嘅,」佢承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,是——是的,」她承認。

passages.original: “Of course that IS one way, but it isn't the way I said; and--someway, I don't seem to quite like the sound of it.
passages.vernacular: 「當然嗰個係一種方式,但唔係我講嘅方式;而且——唔知怎嘅,我似乎不太鍾意佢聽起嚟嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然那是一種方式,但不是我說的方式;而且——不知怎的,我似乎不太喜歡它聽起來的樣子。

passages.original: It isn't exactly as if he said he was glad they WERE sick, but--You do play the game so funny, sometimes Nancy,” she sighed, as she went into the house.
passages.vernacular: 呢不完全係佢講佢高興佢哋病喇,但係——你玩呢個遊戲有時玩得真滑稽,南希,」佢嘆氣,走進屋裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不完全是他說他高興他們病了,但是——你玩這個遊戲有時玩得真滑稽,南希,」她嘆氣,走進屋裡。

passages.original: Pollyanna found her aunt in the sitting room.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜喺起居室裡找到佢姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜在起居室裡找到她姨媽。

passages.original: “Who was that man--the one who drove into the yard, Pollyanna?” questioned the lady a little sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個人係邊個——嗰個駕車進院子嘅人,波麗安娜?」嗰位女士有點尖銳地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那個人是誰——那個駕車進院子的人,波麗安娜?」那位女士有點尖銳地問。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, that was Dr. Chilton!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,嗰個係奇爾頓醫生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,那是奇爾頓醫生!

passages.original: Don't you know him?”
passages.vernacular: 您不認識佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不認識他嗎?」

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton!
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生!

passages.original: What was he doing--here?”
passages.vernacular: 佢喺呢兒幹乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在這兒幹什麼?」

passages.original: “He drove me home.
passages.vernacular: 「佢送我回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他送我回家。

passages.original: Oh, and I gave the jelly to Mr. Pendleton, and--”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我把凍送畀彭德爾頓先生喇,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我把凍送給彭德爾頓先生了,而且——」

passages.original: Miss Polly lifted her head quickly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐迅速抬起頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐迅速抬起頭。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, he did not think I sent it?”
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,佢冇以為係我送嘅吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,他沒以為是我送的吧?」

passages.original: “Oh, no, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,冇,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,沒有,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I told him you didn't.”
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢您冇送。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴他您沒送。」

passages.original: Miss Polly grew a sudden vivid pink.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐突然變得鮮粉紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐突然變得鮮粉紅。

passages.original: “You TOLD him I didn't!”
passages.vernacular: 「你告訴佢我冇送!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你告訴他我沒送!」

passages.original: Pollyanna opened wide her eyes at the remonstrative dismay in her aunt's voice.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜對佢姨媽聲音中責備嘅驚慌睜大咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜對她姨媽聲音中責備的驚慌睜大了眼睛。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, you SAID to!”
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,您講嘅呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,您說的呀!」

passages.original: Aunt Polly sighed.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽嘆氣。

passages.original: “I SAID, Pollyanna, that I did not send it, and for you to be very sure that he did not think I DID!--which is a very different matter from TELLING him outright that I did not send it.”
passages.vernacular: 「我講,波麗安娜,我冇送佢,你要確保佢不以為我送喇!——呢同直接告訴佢我冇送係完全不同嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說,波麗安娜,我沒有送它,你要確保他不以為我送了!——這和直接告訴他我沒送是完全不同的事。」

passages.original: And she turned vexedly away.
passages.vernacular: 佢煩惱地轉身走開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她煩惱地轉身走開。

passages.original: “Dear me!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!

passages.original: Well, I don't see where the difference is,” sighed Pollyanna, as she went to hang her hat on the one particular hook in the house upon which Aunt Polly had said that it must be hung.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我睇不出區別喺邊度,」波麗安娜嘆氣,走去把帽子掛喺屋裡波莉姨媽講必須掛嘅嗰個特定嘅鉤子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我看不出區別在哪裡,」波麗安娜嘆氣,走去把帽子掛在屋裡波莉姨媽說必須掛的那個特定的鉤子上。

chapters.title: Ch. XVI A Red Rose and a Lace Shawl 第十六章:紅玫瑰與蕾絲披肩

passages.original: CH It was on a rainy day about a week after Pollyanna's visit to Mr. John Pendleton, that Miss Polly was driven by Timothy to an early afternoon committee meeting of the Ladies' Aid Society.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜拜訪約翰·彭德爾頓先生大約一個星期後嘅一個雨天,蒂莫西送波莉小姐去參加婦女互助會嘅一個下午早些時候嘅委員會會議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜拜訪約翰·彭德爾頓先生大約一個星期後的一個雨天,蒂莫西送波莉小姐去參加婦女互助會的一個下午早些時候的委員會會議。

passages.original: When she returned at three o'clock, her cheeks were a bright, pretty pink, and her hair, blown by the damp wind, had fluffed into kinks and curls wherever the loosened pins had given leave.
passages.vernacular: 佢三點鐘回嚟時,臉頰係鮮豔漂亮嘅粉紅色,佢嘅頭髮被潮濕嘅風吹住,喺鬆開嘅髮夾允許嘅任何地方蓬成咗捲曲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她三點鐘回來時,臉頰是鮮豔漂亮的粉紅色,她的頭髮被潮濕的風吹著,在鬆開的髮夾允許的任何地方蓬成了捲曲。

passages.original: Pollyanna had never before seen her aunt look like this.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜以前從冇見過佢姨媽呢個樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜以前從沒見過她姨媽這個樣子。

passages.original: “Oh--oh--oh!
Why, Aunt Polly, you've got 'em, too,” she cried rapturously, dancing round and round her aunt, as that lady entered the sitting room.
passages.vernacular: 嗨,波莉姨媽,你都有佢哋,」佢狂喜地喊道,喺佢姨媽走進起居室時,圍住佢轉圈跳舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,波莉姨媽,你也有它們,」她狂喜地喊道,在她姨媽走進起居室時,圍著她轉圈跳舞。

passages.original: “Got what, you impossible child?”
passages.vernacular: 「有乜嘢,你呢唔可能嘅細路?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有什麼,你這不可能的孩子?」

passages.original: Pollyanna was still revolving round and round her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜仍然繞住佢姨媽轉圈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜仍然繞著她姨媽轉圈。

passages.original: “And I never knew you had 'em!
passages.vernacular: 「我從唔知道你有佢哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從不知道你有它們!

passages.original: Can folks have 'em when you don't know they've got 'em?
passages.vernacular: 人哋可以有佢哋而自己唔知道嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們可以有它們而自己不知道嗎?

passages.original: DO you suppose I could?--'fore I get to Heaven, I mean,” she cried, pulling out with eager fingers the straight locks above her ears.
passages.vernacular: 你覺得我能嗎?——我係講,喺我去天堂之前,」佢喊道,用熱切嘅手指拉出耳朵上方嘅直髮綹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得我能嗎?——我是說,在我去天堂之前,」她喊道,用熱切的手指拉出耳朵上方的直髮綹。

passages.original: “But then, they wouldn't be black, if they did come.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,即使佢哋長出嚟,都唔會係黑嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,即使它們長出來,也不會是黑的。

passages.original: You can't hide the black part.”
passages.vernacular: 你藏不住黑嘅嗰部分。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你藏不住黑的那部分。」

passages.original: “Pollyanna, what does all this mean?” demanded Aunt Polly, hurriedly removing her hat, and trying to smooth back her disordered hair.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,呢一切係乜嘢意思?」波莉姨媽質問,匆忙摘下帽子,試圖把凌亂嘅頭髮撫平。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,這一切是什麼意思?」波莉姨媽質問,匆忙摘下帽子,試圖把凌亂的頭髮撫平。

passages.original: “No, no--please, Aunt Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 「不,不——請,波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,不——請,波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: Pollyanna's jubilant voice turned to one of distressed appeal.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜歡欣嘅聲音變成咗苦惱嘅懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜歡欣的聲音變成了苦惱的懇求。

passages.original: “Don't smooth 'em out!
passages.vernacular: 「別把佢哋弄平!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「別把它們弄平!

passages.original: It's those that I'm talking about--those darling little black curls.
passages.vernacular: 我講嘅就係佢哋——嗰啲可愛嘅小黑卷髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說的就是它們——那些可愛的小黑卷髮。

passages.original: Oh, Aunt Polly, they're so pretty!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉姨媽,佢哋咁漂亮!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉姨媽,它們那麼漂亮!」

passages.original: “Nonsense!
passages.vernacular: 「胡講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「胡說!

passages.original: What do you mean, Pollyanna, by going to the Ladies' Aid the other day in that absurd fashion about that beggar boy?”
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜,你嗰天為嗰個乞丐男孩以嗰種荒唐嘅方式去婦女互助會係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜,你那天為那個乞丐男孩以那種荒唐的方式去婦女互助會是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “But it isn't nonsense,” urged Pollyanna, answering only the first of her aunt's remarks.
passages.vernacular: 「但呢唔係胡講,」波麗安娜懇求,只回答咗佢姨媽話中嘅第一句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但這不是胡說,」波麗安娜懇求,只回答了她姨媽話中的第一句。

passages.original: “You don't know how pretty you look with your hair like that!
passages.vernacular: 「你唔知道您嘅頭髮咁樣多漂亮!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不知道您的頭髮這樣多漂亮!

passages.original: Oh, Aunt Polly, please, mayn't I do your hair like I did Mrs. Snow's, and put in a flower?
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉姨媽,請問,我可不可以像畀斯諾太太嗰樣畀您整理頭髮,別上一朵花?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉姨媽,請問,我可不可以像給斯諾太太那樣給您整理頭髮,別上一朵花?

passages.original: I'd so love to see you that way!
passages.vernacular: 我多想睇睇您嗰個樣子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我多想看看您那個樣子!

passages.original: Why, you'd be ever so much prettier than she was!”
passages.vernacular: 嗨,您會比佢漂亮得多!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,您會比她漂亮得多!」

passages.original: “Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜!」

passages.original: (Miss Polly spoke very sharply--all the more sharply because Pollyanna's words had given her an odd throb of joy: when before had anybody cared how she, or her hair looked?
passages.vernacular: (波莉小姐講得好尖銳——更尖銳係因為波麗安娜嘅話畀咗佢一陣奇特嘅歡喜悸動:以前乜嘢時候有人在乎過佢或佢嘅頭髮好不好睇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: (波莉小姐說得很尖銳——更尖銳是因為波麗安娜的話給了她一陣奇特的歡喜悸動:以前什麼時候有人在乎過她或她的頭髮好不好看?

passages.original: When before had anybody “loved” to see her “pretty”?)
passages.vernacular: 以前乜嘢時候有人「愛」睇佢「漂亮」?)
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以前什麼時候有人「愛」看她「漂亮」?)

passages.original: “Pollyanna, you did not answer my question.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你冇回答我嘅問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你沒有回答我的問題。

passages.original: Why did you go to the Ladies' Aid in that absurd fashion?”
passages.vernacular: 你點解以嗰種荒唐嘅方式去婦女互助會?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼以那種荒唐的方式去婦女互助會?」

passages.original: “Yes'm, I know; but, please, I didn't know it was absurd until I went and found out they'd rather see their report grow than Jimmy.
passages.vernacular: 「係,夫人,我知道;但係,請問,我唔知道嗰個係荒唐嘅,直到我去咗才發現佢哋寧可睇佢哋嘅報告增長,而唔係吉米。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,夫人,我知道;但是,請問,我不知道那是荒唐的,直到我去了才發現她們寧可看她們的報告增長,而不是吉米。

passages.original: So then I wrote to MY Ladies' Aiders--'cause Jimmy is far away from them, you know; and I thought maybe he could be their little India boy same as--Aunt Polly, WAS I your little India girl?
passages.vernacular: 於是我寫信畀我嘅婦女互助會嘅人——因為吉米離佢哋好遠,你知道;我想佢可以做佢哋嘅印度小男孩,就像——波莉姨媽,我係您嘅印度小女孩嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 於是我寫信給我的婦女互助會的人——因為吉米離她們很遠,你知道;我想他可以做她們的印度小男孩,就像——波莉姨媽,我是您的印度小女孩嗎?

passages.original: And, Aunt Polly, you WILL let me do your hair, won't you?”
passages.vernacular: 仲有,波莉姨媽,您會讓我整理您嘅頭髮嘅,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,波莉姨媽,您會讓我整理您的頭髮的,是不是?」

passages.original: Aunt Polly put her hand to her throat--the old, helpless feeling was upon her, she knew.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽把手放喺喉嚨上——佢知道,舊日嘅無助感又落喺佢身上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽把手放在喉嚨上——她知道,舊日的無助感又落在她身上了。

passages.original: “But, Pollyanna, when the ladies told me this afternoon how you came to them, I was so ashamed!
passages.vernacular: 「但係,波麗安娜,今日下午女士哋告訴我你係點去佢哋嗰度嘅,我羞愧極喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,波麗安娜,今天下午女士們告訴我你是怎麼去她們那裡的,我羞愧極了!

passages.original: Pollyanna began to dance up and down lightly on her toes.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜開始輕輕地喺腳尖上上下下跳舞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜開始輕輕地在腳尖上上下下跳舞。

passages.original: “You didn't!--You didn't say I COULDN'T do your hair,” she crowed triumphantly; “and so I'm sure it means just the other way 'round, sort of--like it did the other day about Mr. Pendleton's jelly that you didn't send, but didn't want me to say you didn't send, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「您冇講!——您冇講我唔能夠整理您嘅頭髮,」佢得意地歡叫;「所以我確信佢意思係正好相反,有點像——像嗰天彭德爾頓先生嘅凍嗰樣,您冇送,卻不希望我講您冇送,您知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您沒說!——您沒說我不能整理您的頭髮,」她得意地歡叫;「所以我確信它意思是正好相反,有點像——像那天彭德爾頓先生的凍那樣,您沒送,卻不希望我說您沒送,您知道。

passages.original: Now wait just where you are.
passages.vernacular: 而家就待喺嗰兒別動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在就待在那兒別動。

passages.original: I'll get a comb.”
passages.vernacular: 我去攞梳子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去拿梳子。」

passages.original: “But Pollyanna, Pollyanna,” remonstrated Aunt Polly, following the little girl from the room and panting up-stairs after her.
passages.vernacular: 「但係波麗安娜,波麗安娜,」波莉姨媽勸阻,跟住小女孩走出房間,氣喘吁吁地跟佢上樓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是波麗安娜,波麗安娜,」波莉姨媽勸阻,跟著小女孩走出房間,氣喘吁吁地跟她上樓。

passages.original: “Oh, did you come up here?”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你上嚟喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你上來了?」

passages.original: Pollyanna greeted her at the door of Miss Polly's own room.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜喺波莉小姐自己房間嘅門口迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜在波莉小姐自己房間的門口迎接她。

passages.original: “That'll be nicer yet!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰更好喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那更好了!

passages.original: I've got the comb.
passages.vernacular: 我攞到梳子喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我拿到梳子了。

passages.original: Now sit down, please, right here.
passages.vernacular: 而家請坐,就坐喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在請坐,就坐在這裡。

passages.original: Oh, I'm so glad you let me do it!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太高興您讓我弄喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太高興您讓我弄了!」

passages.original: “But, Pollyanna, I--I--”
passages.vernacular: 「但係,波麗安娜,我——我——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,波麗安娜,我——我——」

passages.original: Miss Polly did not finish her sentence.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐冇講完佢嘅句子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐沒有說完她的句子。

passages.original: To her helpless amazement she found herself in the low chair before the dressing table, with her hair already tumbling about her ears under ten eager, but very gentle fingers.
passages.vernacular: 令佢無助地驚訝嘅係,佢發現自己坐喺梳妝台前嘅矮椅子上,頭髮已經喺十隻熱切卻好輕柔嘅手指下散落喺耳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令她無助地驚訝的是,她發現自己坐在梳妝台前的矮椅子上,頭髮已經在十隻熱切卻非常輕柔的手指下散落在耳邊。

passages.original: “Oh, my! what pretty hair you've got,” prattled Pollyanna; “and there's so much more of it than Mrs. Snow has, too!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀!您嘅頭髮多漂亮,」波麗安娜嘰嘰喳喳;「而且比斯諾太太嘅多得多!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪!您的頭髮多漂亮,」波麗安娜嘰嘰喳喳;「而且比斯諾太太的多得多!

passages.original: But, of course, you need more, anyhow, because you're well and can go to places where folks can see it.
passages.vernacular: 不過,當然,您反正需要更多,因為您健康,可以去人哋睇得見佢嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,當然,您反正需要更多,因為您健康,可以去人們看得見它的地方。

passages.original: My!
passages.vernacular: 天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!

passages.original: I reckon folks'll be glad when they do see it--and surprised, too, 'cause you've hid it so long.
passages.vernacular: 我想人哋睇到時會高興——都驚訝,因為您把佢藏咗咁久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想人們看到時會高興——也驚訝,因為您把它藏了那麼久。

passages.original: Why, Aunt Polly, I'll make you so pretty everybody'll just love to look at you!”
passages.vernacular: 嗨,波莉姨媽,我會把您弄得咁漂亮,人人都愛睇您!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗨,波莉姨媽,我會把您弄得那麼漂亮,人人都愛看您!」

passages.original: “Pollyanna!” gasped a stifled but shocked voice from a veil of hair.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜!」一個被抑制但震驚嘅聲音從一簾頭髮裡傳嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜!」一個被抑制但震驚的聲音從一簾頭髮裡傳來。

passages.original: “I--I'm sure I don't know why I'm letting you do this silly thing.”
passages.vernacular: 「我——我確信我唔知道我點解讓你做呢蠢事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我確信我不知道我為什麼讓你做這蠢事。」

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, I should think you'd be glad to have folks like to look at you!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,我想您該高興人哋愛睇您!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,波莉姨媽,我想您該高興人們愛看您!

passages.original: Don't you like to look at pretty things?
passages.vernacular: 您不鍾意睇漂亮嘅嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不喜歡看漂亮的東西嗎?

passages.original: I'm ever so much happier when I look at pretty folks, 'cause when I look at the other kind I'm so sorry for them.”
passages.vernacular: 我睇漂亮嘅人時開心得多,因為睇另一種人時我就為佢哋難過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看漂亮的人時開心得多,因為看另一種人時我就為他們難過。」

passages.original: “But--but--”
passages.vernacular: 「但係——但係——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是——但是——」

passages.original: “And I just love to do folks' hair,” purred Pollyanna, contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 「我就愛畀人整理頭髮,」波麗安娜滿足地咕嚕住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就愛給人整理頭髮,」波麗安娜滿足地咕嚕著。

passages.original: “I did quite a lot of the Ladies' Aiders'--but there wasn't any of them so nice as yours.
passages.vernacular: 「我畀婦女互助會嘅人整理過好多——但冇一個像您嘅咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給婦女互助會的人整理過很多——但沒有一個像您的這麼好。

passages.original: Mrs. White's was pretty nice, though, and she looked just lovely one day when I dressed her up in--Oh, Aunt Polly, I've just happened to think of something!
passages.vernacular: 不過懷特太太嘅挺不錯嘅,有一天我畀佢打扮時,佢睇起嚟可愛極喇,穿住——哦,波莉姨媽,我啱啱想起咗一件事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過懷特太太的挺不錯的,有一天我給她打扮時,她看起來可愛極了,穿著——哦,波莉姨媽,我剛剛想起了一件事!

passages.original: But it's a secret, and I sha'n't tell.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢個係個祕密,我不講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這是個祕密,我不說。

passages.original: Now your hair is almost done, and pretty quick I'm going to leave you just a minute; and you must promise--promise--PROMISE not to stir nor peek, even, till I come back.
passages.vernacular: 而家您嘅頭髮快好喇,好快我就要離開您一小會兒;您必須答應——答應——答應喺我回嚟之前唔好動,甚至唔好偷睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在您的頭髮快好了,很快我就要離開您一小會兒;您必須答應——答應——答應在我回來之前不要動,甚至不要偷看。

passages.original: Now remember!” she finished, as she ran from the room.
passages.vernacular: 而家記住!」佢結束講,跑出咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在記住!」她結束說,跑出了房間。

passages.original: Aloud Miss Polly said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐冇大聲講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐沒有大聲說什麼。

passages.original: To herself she said that of course she should at once undo the absurd work of her niece's fingers, and put her hair up properly again.
passages.vernacular: 佢對自己講,當然佢要即刻拆掉外甥女手指嘅荒唐成果,把頭髮重新好好盤起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她對自己說,當然她要馬上拆掉外甥女手指的荒唐成果,把頭髮重新好好盤起來。

passages.original: As for “peeking” just as if she cared how--
passages.vernacular: 至於「偷睇」,好像佢在乎點樣——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於「偷看」,好像她在乎怎樣——

passages.original: At that moment--unaccountably--Miss Polly caught a glimpse of herself in the mirror of the dressing table.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣——莫名其妙地——波莉小姐瞥見咗梳妝台鏡子裡嘅自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時——莫名其妙地——波莉小姐瞥見了梳妝台鏡子裡的自己。

passages.original: And what she saw sent such a flush of rosy color to her cheeks that--she only flushed the more at the sight.
passages.vernacular: 佢所睇到嘅,使一陣玫瑰色嘅紅暈湧上臉頰,而——佢睇到呢個,反而臉更紅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她所看到的,使一陣玫瑰色的紅暈湧上臉頰,而——她看到這個,反而臉更紅了。

passages.original: She saw a face--not young, it is true--but just now alight with excitement and surprise.
passages.vernacular: 佢睇見一張臉——確實不年輕——但此刻因興奮同驚訝而發光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她看見一張臉——確實不年輕——但此刻因興奮和驚訝而發光。

passages.original: The cheeks were a pretty pink.
passages.vernacular: 臉頰係漂亮嘅粉紅色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 臉頰是漂亮的粉紅色。

passages.original: The eyes sparkled.
passages.vernacular: 眼睛閃閃發亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 眼睛閃閃發亮。

passages.original: The hair, dark, and still damp from the outdoor air, lay in loose waves about the forehead and curved back over the ears in wonderfully becoming lines, with softening little curls here and there.
passages.vernacular: 頭髮深色,仲帶住室外空氣嘅潮濕,鬆散嘅波浪散喺前額,喺耳後彎成好合適嘅線條,呢度嗰度有柔和嘅小卷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭髮深色,還帶著室外空氣的潮濕,鬆散的波浪散在前額,在耳後彎成非常合適的線條,這裡那裡有柔和的小卷。

passages.original: So amazed and so absorbed was Miss Polly with what she saw in the glass that she quite forgot her determination to do over her hair, until she heard Pollyanna enter the room again.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐被佢喺鏡中所見驚得咁出神,以致完全忘咗佢要重新梳頭嘅決心,直到佢聽見波麗安娜又進咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐被她在鏡中所見驚得那麼出神,以致完全忘了她要重新梳頭的決心,直到她聽見波麗安娜又進了房間。

passages.original: Before she could move, then, she felt a folded something slipped across her eyes and tied in the back.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲冇嚟得及動,就感到有一個折起嚟嘅嘢滑過佢嘅眼睛,喺後面系住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還沒來得及動,就感到有一個折起來的東西滑過她的眼睛,在後面系住。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, Pollyanna!
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,波麗安娜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,波麗安娜!

passages.original: What are you doing?” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 你喺幹乜嘢?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在幹什麼?」她喊道。

passages.original: Pollyanna chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜咯咯笑。

passages.original: “That's just what I don't want you to know, Aunt Polly, and I was afraid you WOULD peek, so I tied on the handkerchief.
passages.vernacular: 「呢正是我唔想讓您知道嘅,波莉姨媽,我怕您會偷睇,所以我蒙上咗手帕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這正是我不想讓您知道的,波莉姨媽,我怕您會偷看,所以我蒙上了手帕。

passages.original: Now sit still.
passages.vernacular: 而家坐住別動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在坐著別動。

passages.original: It won't take but just a minute, then I'll let you see.”
passages.vernacular: 只要一分鐘,然後我就讓您睇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只要一分鐘,然後我就讓您看。」

passages.original: “But, Pollyanna,” began Miss Polly, struggling blindly to her feet, “you must take this off!
passages.vernacular: 「但係,波麗安娜,」波莉小姐開口,盲目地掙扎住站起嚟,「你必須把呢個取下嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但是,波麗安娜,」波莉小姐開口,盲目地掙扎著站起來,「你必須把這個取下來!

passages.original: You--child, child! what ARE you doing?” she gasped, as she felt a soft something slipped about her shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 你——細路,細路!你喺幹乜嘢?」佢倒抽氣,感到有一樣柔軟嘅嘢披喺佢嘅肩上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你——孩子,孩子!你在幹什麼?」她倒抽氣,感到有一樣柔軟的東西披在她的肩上。

passages.original: Pollyanna only chuckled the more gleefully.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜只係更歡樂地咯咯笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜只是更歡樂地咯咯笑。

passages.original: With trembling fingers she was draping about her aunt's shoulders the fleecy folds of a beautiful lace shawl, yellowed from long years of packing away, and fragrant with lavender.
passages.vernacular: 佢用顫抖嘅手指,把一條美麗嘅蕾絲披肩蓬鬆嘅褶子披喺佢姨媽嘅肩上,披肩因長年收藏而發黃,散發住薰衣草嘅香味。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用顫抖的手指,把一條美麗的蕾絲披肩蓬鬆的褶子披在她姨媽的肩上,披肩因長年收藏而發黃,散發著薰衣草的香味。

passages.original: Pollyanna had found the shawl the week before when Nancy had been regulating the attic; and it had occurred to her to-day that there was no reason why her aunt, as well as Mrs. White of her Western home, should not be “dressed up.”
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜係上個星期南希整理閣樓時發現呢條披肩嘅;佢今日想到,冇理由佢姨媽唔能夠像佢西部家鄉嘅懷特太太一樣被「打扮」一番。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜是上個星期南希整理閣樓時發現這條披肩的;她今天想到,沒理由她姨媽不能像她西部家鄉的懷特太太一樣被「打扮」一番。

passages.original: Her task completed, Pollyanna surveyed her work with eyes that approved, but that saw yet one touch wanting.
passages.vernacular: 任務完成後,波麗安娜用讚許嘅眼睛審視佢嘅作品,卻睇出仲缺少啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 任務完成後,波麗安娜用讚許的眼睛審視她的作品,卻看出還缺少一點。

passages.original: Promptly, therefore, she pulled her aunt toward the sun parlor where she could see a belated red rose blooming on the trellis within reach of her hand.
passages.vernacular: 因此佢即刻把姨媽拉向日光室,喺嗰度佢睇見一朵遲開嘅紅玫瑰喺佢伸手可及嘅花架上盛開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此她立刻把姨媽拉向日光室,在那裡她看見一朵遲開的紅玫瑰在她伸手可及的花架上盛開。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, what are you doing?
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你喺幹乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你在幹什麼?

passages.original: Where are you taking me to?” recoiled Aunt Polly, vainly trying to hold herself back.
passages.vernacular: 你要帶我去邊?」波莉姨媽退縮,徒勞地試圖把自己拉住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要帶我去哪?」波莉姨媽退縮,徒勞地試圖把自己拉住。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, I shall not--”
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,我唔好——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,我不要——」

passages.original: “It's just to the sun parlor--only a minute!
passages.vernacular: 「只係到日光室——一會兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是到日光室——一會兒!

passages.original: I'll have you ready now quicker'n no time,” panted Pollyanna, reaching for the rose and thrusting it into the soft hair above Miss Polly's left ear.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻就讓您準備好,」波麗安娜喘住氣,伸手去夠玫瑰,把佢插進波莉小姐左耳上方柔軟嘅頭髮裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我立刻就讓您準備好,」波麗安娜喘著氣,伸手去夠玫瑰,把它插進波莉小姐左耳上方柔軟的頭髮裡。

passages.original: “There!” she exulted, untying the knot of the handkerchief and flinging the bit of linen far from her.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇!」佢得意地歡叫,解開手帕嘅結,把嗰塊亞麻布遠遠扔開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了!」她得意地歡叫,解開手帕的結,把那塊亞麻布遠遠扔開。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, now I reckon you'll be glad I dressed you up!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,而家我想您會高興我把您打扮喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,現在我想您會高興我把您打扮了!」

passages.original: For one dazed moment Miss Polly looked at her bedecked self, and at her surroundings; then she gave a low cry and fled to her room.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐發懵地睇咗片刻打扮好嘅自己同周圍嘅環境;然後佢輕呼一聲,逃回自己嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐發懵地看了片刻打扮好的自己和周圍的環境;然後她輕呼一聲,逃回自己的房間。

passages.original: Pollyanna, following the direction of her aunt's last dismayed gaze, saw, through the open windows of the sun parlor, the horse and gig turning into the driveway.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜順住佢姨媽最後驚慌嘅目光,透過日光室敞開嘅窗子,睇見馬同輕便馬車轉進車道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜順著她姨媽最後驚慌的目光,透過日光室敞開的窗子,看見馬和輕便馬車轉進車道。

passages.original: She recognized at once the man who held the reins.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻認出握住韁繩嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她立刻認出握著韁繩的人。

passages.original: Delightedly she leaned forward.
passages.vernacular: 佢高興地向前傾身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她高興地向前傾身。

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton, Dr. Chilton!
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生,奇爾頓醫生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生,奇爾頓醫生!

passages.original: Did you want to see me?
passages.vernacular: 您想見我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您想見我嗎?

passages.original: I'm up here.”
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢上面。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這上面。」

passages.original: “Yes,” smiled the doctor, a little gravely.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」醫生有點嚴肅地微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」醫生有點嚴肅地微笑。

passages.original: “Will you come down, please?”
passages.vernacular: 「請你下嚟好嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請你下來好嗎?」

passages.original: In the bedroom Pollyanna found a flushed-faced, angry-eyed woman plucking at the pins that held a lace shawl in place.
passages.vernacular: 喺臥室裡,波麗安娜發現一個臉色潮紅、眼睛含怒嘅女人,正在拔固定蕾絲披肩嘅別針。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在臥室裡,波麗安娜發現一個臉色潮紅、眼睛含怒的女人,正在拔固定蕾絲披肩的別針。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, how could you?” moaned the woman.
passages.vernacular: 「波麗安娜,你點能咁樣?」嗰女人呻吟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波麗安娜,你怎麼能這樣?」那女人呻吟。

passages.original: “To think of your rigging me up like this, and then letting me--BE SEEN!”
passages.vernacular: 「想想你把我打扮成咁樣,然後讓我——被人睇見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「想想你把我打扮成這樣,然後讓我——被人看見!」

passages.original: Pollyanna stopped in dismay.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜驚慌地停住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜驚慌地停住。

passages.original: “But you looked lovely--perfectly lovely, Aunt Polly; and--”
passages.vernacular: 「但您睇起嚟可愛極喇——絕對可愛,波莉姨媽;而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但您看起來可愛極了——絕對可愛,波莉姨媽;而且——」

passages.original: “'Lovely'!” scorned the woman, flinging the shawl to one side and attacking her hair with shaking fingers.
passages.vernacular: 「『可愛』!」嗰女人輕蔑地講,把披肩甩到一邊,用顫抖嘅手指攻擊佢嘅頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『可愛』!」那女人輕蔑地說,把披肩甩到一邊,用顫抖的手指攻擊她的頭髮。

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly, please, please let the hair stay!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽,請,請讓頭髮留住!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽,請,請讓頭髮留著!」

passages.original: “Stay?
passages.vernacular: 「留住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「留著?

passages.original: Like this?
passages.vernacular: 像咁樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像這樣?

passages.original: As if I would!”
passages.vernacular: 好像我會似嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像我會似的!」

passages.original: And Miss Polly pulled the locks so tightly back that the last curl lay stretched dead at the ends of her fingers.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐把髮綹拉得咁緊向後,最後一個卷死死地伸直喺佢指尖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐把髮綹拉得那麼緊向後,最後一個卷死死地伸直在她指尖。

passages.original: “O dear!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,天哪!

passages.original: And you did look so pretty,” almost sobbed Pollyanna, as she stumbled through the door.
passages.vernacular: 你睇起嚟咁漂亮,」波麗安娜幾乎哭出聲,跌跌撞撞地出咗門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看起來那麼漂亮,」波麗安娜幾乎哭出聲,跌跌撞撞地出了門。

passages.original: Down-stairs Pollyanna found the doctor waiting in his gig.
passages.vernacular: 樓下,波麗安娜發現醫生坐喺輕便馬車裡等住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樓下,波麗安娜發現醫生坐在輕便馬車裡等著。

passages.original: “I've prescribed you for a patient, and he's sent me to get the prescription filled,” announced the doctor.
passages.vernacular: 「我畀你開咗處方畀一個病人,佢派我嚟配藥,」醫生宣布。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我給你開了處方給一個病人,他派我來配藥,」醫生宣布。

passages.original: “Will you go?”
passages.vernacular: 「你去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你去嗎?」

passages.original: “You mean--an errand--to the drug store?” asked Pollyanna, a little uncertainly.
passages.vernacular: 「您係講——去藥店跑腿?」波麗安娜有點不確定地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「您是說——去藥店跑腿?」波麗安娜有點不確定地問。

passages.original: “I used to go some--for the Ladies' Aiders.”
passages.vernacular: 「我過去畀婦女互助會嘅人去過啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我過去給婦女互助會的人去過一些。」

passages.original: The doctor shook his head with a smile.
passages.vernacular: 醫生微笑搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生微笑搖頭。

passages.original: “Not exactly.
passages.vernacular: 「不完全係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不完全是。

passages.original: It's Mr. John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 係約翰·彭德爾頓先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是約翰·彭德爾頓先生。

passages.original: He would like to see you to-day, if you'll be so good as to come.
passages.vernacular: 佢今日想見你,如果你肯好心嚟嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他今天想見你,如果你肯好心來的話。

passages.original: It's stopped raining, so I drove down after you.
passages.vernacular: 雨停喇,所以我駕車下嚟找你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雨停了,所以我駕車下來找你。

passages.original: Will you come?
passages.vernacular: 你嚟嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你來嗎?

passages.original: I'll call for you and bring you back before six o'clock.”
passages.vernacular: 我會嚟接你,六點前送你回嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會來接你,六點前送你回來。」

passages.original: “I'd love to!” exclaimed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「我好願意!」波麗安娜喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很願意!」波麗安娜喊道。

passages.original: “Let me ask Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「讓我問問波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我問問波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: In a few moments she returned, hat in hand, but with rather a sober face.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,佢回嚟喇,手裡攞住帽子,神情卻相當嚴肅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,她回來了,手裡拿著帽子,神情卻相當嚴肅。

passages.original: “Didn't--your aunt want you to go?” asked the doctor, a little diffidently, as they drove away.
passages.vernacular: 「你姨媽——唔想讓你去嗎?」佢哋駛走時,醫生有點膽怯地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你姨媽——不想讓你去嗎?」他們駛走時,醫生有點膽怯地問。

passages.original: “Y-yes,” sighed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係——係嘅,」波麗安娜嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是——是的,」波麗安娜嘆氣。

passages.original: “She--she wanted me to go TOO much, I'm afraid.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢——佢太想讓我去喇,我怕。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她——她太想讓我去了,我怕。」

passages.original: “Wanted you to go TOO MUCH!”
passages.vernacular: 「太想讓你去喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太想讓你去了!」

passages.original: Pollyanna sighed again.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜又嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜又嘆氣。

passages.original: “Yes.
I reckon she meant she didn't want me there.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢嘅意思係佢唔想我喺嗰兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她的意思是她不想我在那兒。

passages.original: You see, she said: 'Yes, yes, run along, run along--do!
passages.vernacular: 您睇,佢講:『係,係,快走,快走——去吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看,她說:『是,是,快走,快走——去吧!

passages.original: I wish you'd gone before.'”
passages.vernacular: 我希望你早點走。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你早點走。』」

passages.original: The doctor smiled--but with his lips only.
passages.vernacular: 醫生笑喇——但只係嘴唇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生笑了——但只是嘴唇。

passages.original: His eyes were very grave.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛好嚴肅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛很嚴肅。

passages.original: For some time he said nothing; then, a little hesitatingly, he asked:
passages.vernacular: 有一陣子佢乜嘢都冇講;然後有點遲疑地問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一陣子他什麼也沒說;然後有點遲疑地問:

passages.original: “Wasn't it--your aunt I saw with you a few minutes ago--in the window of the sun parlor?”
passages.vernacular: 「我幾分鐘前睇見同你喺一起嘅——係你姨媽吧——喺日光室嘅窗口?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我幾分鐘前看見和你在一起的——是你姨媽吧——在日光室的窗口?」

passages.original: Pollyanna drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜深吸一口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜深吸一口氣。

passages.original: “Yes; that's what's the whole trouble, I suppose.
passages.vernacular: 「係;我想呢個就係全部麻煩喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是;我想這就是全部麻煩了。

passages.original: You see I'd dressed her up in a perfectly lovely lace shawl I found up-stairs, and I'd fixed her hair and put on a rose, and she looked so pretty.
passages.vernacular: 您睇我畀佢穿上咗我喺樓上找到嘅絕對可愛嘅蕾絲披肩,仲整理咗佢嘅頭髮,插咗一朵玫瑰,佢睇起嚟咁漂亮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看我給她穿上了我在樓上找到的絕對可愛的蕾絲披肩,還整理了她的頭髮,插了一朵玫瑰,她看起來那麼漂亮。

passages.original: Didn't YOU think she looked just lovely?”
passages.vernacular: 您不覺得佢睇起嚟可愛極咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您不覺得她看起來可愛極了嗎?」

passages.original: For a moment the doctor did not answer.
passages.vernacular: 有片刻,醫生冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有片刻,醫生沒有回答。

passages.original: When he did speak his voice was so low Pollyanna could but just hear the words.
passages.vernacular: 佢講話時,聲音咁低,波麗安娜幾乎聽唔到嗰啲話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說話時,聲音那麼低,波麗安娜幾乎聽不到那些話。

passages.original: “Yes, Pollyanna, I--I thought she did look--just lovely.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,波麗安娜,我——我覺得佢睇起嚟——可愛極喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,波麗安娜,我——我覺得她看起來——可愛極了。」

passages.original: “Did you?
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?

passages.original: I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 我太高興喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興了!

passages.original: I'll tell her,” nodded the little girl, contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴佢,」小女孩滿足地點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴她,」小女孩滿足地點頭。

passages.original: To her surprise the doctor gave a sudden exclamation.
passages.vernacular: 令佢食驚嘅係,醫生突然驚呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令她吃驚的是,醫生突然驚呼。

passages.original: “Never!
passages.vernacular: 「千萬別!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「千萬別!

passages.original: Pollyanna, I--I'm afraid I shall have to ask you not to tell her--that.”
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜,我——我怕我得請你唔好告訴佢——嗰個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜,我——我怕我得請你不要告訴她——那個。」

passages.original: “Why, Dr. Chilton!
passages.vernacular: 「嗨,奇爾頓醫生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗨,奇爾頓醫生!

passages.original: Why not?
passages.vernacular: 點解不?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼不?

passages.original: I should think you'd be glad--”
passages.vernacular: 我想您會高興——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想您會高興——」

passages.original: “But she might not be,” cut in the doctor.
passages.vernacular: 「但佢或者唔會,」醫生打斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但她也許不會,」醫生打斷。

passages.original: Pollyanna considered this for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 波麗安娜考慮咗片刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波麗安娜考慮了片刻。

passages.original: “That's so--maybe she wouldn't,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「呢倒係——或者佢唔會,」佢嘆氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這倒是——也許她不會,」她嘆氣。

passages.original: “I remember now; 'twas 'cause she saw you that she ran.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家記起喇;佢就係因為睇見您才跑嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在記起了;她就是因為看見您才跑的。

passages.original: And she--she spoke afterwards about her being seen in that rig.”
passages.vernacular: 而佢——佢後來講過佢被人睇見穿成嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而她——她後來說過她被人看見穿成那樣。」

passages.original: “I thought as much,” declared the doctor, under his breath.
passages.vernacular: 「我想都係,」醫生低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想也是,」醫生低聲說。

passages.original: “Still, I don't see why,” maintained Pollyanna, “--when she looked so pretty!”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我定係不明白點解,」波麗安娜堅持講,「——佢睇起嚟咁漂亮!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我還是不明白為什麼,」波麗安娜堅持說,「——她看起來那麼漂亮!」

passages.original: The doctor said nothing.
passages.vernacular: 醫生乜嘢都冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生什麼也沒說。

passages.original: He did not speak again, indeed, until they were almost to the great stone house in which John Pendleton lay with a broken leg.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實再冇講話,直到佢哋幾乎到咗約翰·彭德爾頓腿斷咗躺住嘅嗰座大石屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他確實再沒說話,直到他們幾乎到了約翰·彭德爾頓腿斷了躺著的那座大石屋。

chapters.title: Ch. XVII "Just Like a Book" 第十七章:「就像書裏一樣」

passages.original: CH John Pendleton greeted Pollyanna to-day with a smile.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓今日對波莉安娜露出咗笑容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓今天對波莉安娜露出了笑容。

passages.original: “Well, Miss Pollyanna, I'm thinking you must be a very forgiving little person, else you wouldn't have come to see me again to-day.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,波莉安娜小姐,我想你一定係個好寬容嘅小人兒,不然你今日就唔會再嚟睇我喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,波莉安娜小姐,我想你一定是個很寬容的小人兒,不然你今天就不會再來看我了。」

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, I was real glad to come, and I'm sure I don't see why I shouldn't be, either.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我係真心高興才嚟嘅,而且我真不明白我點解會不高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我是真心高興才來的,而且我真不明白我為什麼會不高興。」

passages.original: “Oh, well, you know, I was pretty cross with you, I'm afraid, both the other day when you so kindly brought me the jelly, and that time when you found me with the broken leg at first.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你知道,我恐怕對你相當兇,前幾天你好心畀我送果凍嚟嘅時候係咁樣,當初你發現我摔斷咗腿嘅嗰一次都係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你知道,我恐怕對你相當兇,前幾天你好心給我送果凍來的時候是這樣,當初你發現我摔斷了腿的那一次也是這樣。

passages.original: By the way, too, I don't think I've ever thanked you for that.
passages.vernacular: 順便講一句,我想我仲從來冇為嗰件事謝過你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 順便說一句,我想我還從來沒為那件事謝過你。

passages.original: Now I'm sure that even you would admit that you were very forgiving to come and see me, after such ungrateful treatment as that!”
passages.vernacular: 而家我敢講,就連你都得承認,受咗嗰樣忘恩負義嘅對待,你仲肯嚟睇我,真係太寬容喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我敢說,就連你也得承認,受了那樣忘恩負義的對待,你還肯來看我,真是太寬容了!」

passages.original: Pollyanna stirred uneasily.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜不安地動咗動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜不安地動了動。

passages.original: “But I was glad to find you--that is, I don't mean I was glad your leg was broken, of course,” she corrected hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我好高興能找到你——我係講,我當然唔係講我高興你嘅腿斷喇。」佢連忙更正道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我很高興能找到你——我是說,我當然不是說我高興你的腿斷了。」她連忙更正道。

passages.original: John Pendleton smiled.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓笑了。

passages.original: “I understand.
passages.vernacular: 「我明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明白。

passages.original: Your tongue does get away with you once in a while, doesn't it, Miss Pollyanna?
passages.vernacular: 你呢張嘴偶爾係會跑喺腦子前頭嘅,係唔係,波莉安娜小姐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這張嘴偶爾是會跑在腦子前頭的,是不是,波莉安娜小姐?

passages.original: I do thank you, however; and I consider you a very brave little girl to do what you did that day.
passages.vernacular: 不過我真嘅謝謝你;我覺得你嗰天嘅所作所為,係個好勇敢嘅小姑娘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我真的謝謝你;我覺得你那天的所作所為,是個非常勇敢的小姑娘。

passages.original: I thank you for the jelly, too,” he added in a lighter voice.
passages.vernacular: 果凍我都謝謝你。」佢用輕鬆些嘅語氣補充道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 果凍我也謝謝你。」他用輕鬆些的語氣補充道。

passages.original: “Did you like it?” asked Pollyanna with interest.
passages.vernacular: 「你鍾意食嗎?」波莉安娜興致勃勃地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你喜歡吃嗎?」波莉安娜興致勃勃地問。

passages.original: “Very much.
passages.vernacular: 「好鍾意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很喜歡。

passages.original: I suppose--there isn't any more to-day that--that Aunt Polly DIDN'T send, is there?” he asked with an odd smile.
passages.vernacular: 我想——今日冇乜嘢——波莉姨媽冇送嘅嘢吧?」佢帶住古怪嘅笑容問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想——今天沒有什麼——波莉姨媽沒送的東西吧?」他帶著古怪的笑容問。

passages.original: His visitor looked distressed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅小客人露出為難嘅神色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的小客人露出為難的神色。

passages.original: “N-no, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇、冇,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒、沒有,先生。」

passages.original: She hesitated, then went on with heightened color.
passages.vernacular: 佢遲疑咗一下,然後紅住臉接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她遲疑了一下,然後紅著臉接著說。

passages.original: “Please, Mr. Pendleton, I didn't mean to be rude the other day when I said Aunt Polly did NOT send the jelly.”
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓先生,請別見怪,前幾天我講波莉姨媽冇送果凍,我唔係故意要無禮嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓先生,請別見怪,前幾天我說波莉姨媽沒有送果凍,我不是故意要無禮的。」

passages.original: There was no answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: John Pendleton was not smiling now.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓而家已經不笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓現在已經不笑了。

passages.original: He was looking straight ahead of him with eyes that seemed to be gazing through and beyond the object before them.
passages.vernacular: 佢直直地望住前方,眼神仿佛穿透咗眼前嘅嘢,望向更遠嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他直直地望著前方,眼神仿佛穿透了眼前的東西,望向更遠的地方。

passages.original: After a time he drew a long sigh and turned to Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,佢長長嘆咗口氣,轉向波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,他長長嘆了口氣,轉向波莉安娜。

passages.original: When he spoke his voice carried the old nervous fretfulness.
passages.vernacular: 佢開口時,聲音裡又帶住往日嗰種神經質嘅煩躁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他開口時,聲音裡又帶著往日那種神經質的煩躁。

passages.original: “Well, well, this will never do at all!
passages.vernacular: 「好咗好喇,咁樣可不行!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了好了,這樣可不行!

passages.original: I didn't send for you to see me moping this time.
passages.vernacular: 我呢次叫你嚟,唔係要你睇我悶悶不樂嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這次叫你來,不是要你看我悶悶不樂的。

passages.original: Listen!
passages.vernacular: 聽住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽著!

passages.original: Out in the library--the big room where the telephone is, you know--you will find a carved box on the lower shelf of the big case with glass doors in the corner not far from the fireplace.
passages.vernacular: 到外面嘅書房——就係放電話嘅嗰間大屋子——你會喺靠近壁爐嘅角落,嗰個有玻璃門嘅大柜子下層架子上,找到一個雕花嘅盒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到外面的書房——就是放電話的那間大屋子——你會在靠近壁爐的角落,那個有玻璃門的大柜子下層架子上,找到一個雕花的盒子。

passages.original: That is, it'll be there if that confounded woman hasn't 'regulated' it to somewhere else!
passages.vernacular: 都就係講,要係嗰個討厭嘅女人冇把佢『整理』到別處去嘅話,佢就喺嗰兒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也就是說,要是那個討厭的女人沒有把它『整理』到別處去的話,它就在那兒!

passages.original: You may bring it to me.
passages.vernacular: 你把佢攞嚟畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你把它拿來給我。

passages.original: It is heavy, but not too heavy for you to carry, I think.”
passages.vernacular: 佢好重,不過我想仲不至于重得你搬不動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它很重,不過我想還不至于重得你搬不動。」

passages.original: “Oh, I'm awfully strong,” declared Pollyanna, cheerfully, as she sprang to her feet.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我力氣可大喇。」波莉安娜高高興興地講住,一下子跳咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我力氣可大了。」波莉安娜高高興興地說著,一下子跳了起來。

passages.original: In a minute she had returned with the box.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,佢就把盒子攞回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,她就把盒子拿回來了。

passages.original: It was a wonderful half-hour that Pollyanna spent then.
passages.vernacular: 接下嚟嘅半個鐘頭,對波莉安娜來講美妙極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接下來的半個鐘頭,對波莉安娜來說美妙極了。

passages.original: The box was full of treasures--curios that John Pendleton had picked up in years of travel--and concerning each there was some entertaining story, whether it were a set of exquisitely carved chessmen from China, or a little jade idol from India.
passages.vernacular: 盒子裡裝滿咗寶貝——都係約翰·潘德爾頓多年旅行中收集嚟嘅珍奇古玩——每一件都有一段有趣嘅故事,不管係一套來自中國、雕工精美嘅象棋子,定係一尊來自印度嘅小玉像。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盒子裡裝滿了寶貝——都是約翰·潘德爾頓多年旅行中收集來的珍奇古玩——每一件都有一段有趣的故事,不管是一套來自中國、雕工精美的象棋子,還是一尊來自印度的小玉像。

passages.original: It was after she had heard the story about the idol that Pollyanna murmured wistfully:
passages.vernacular: 聽完嗰尊玉像嘅故事後,波莉安娜若有所思地喃喃講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽完那尊玉像的故事後,波莉安娜若有所思地喃喃說:

passages.original: “Well, I suppose it WOULD be better to take a little boy in India to bring up--one that didn't know any more than to think that God was in that doll-thing--than it would be to take Jimmy Bean, a little boy who knows God is up in the sky.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想,領養一個印度嘅小男孩嚟教養,總比領養吉米·比恩要好——嗰個細路乜嘢都不懂,居然以為上帝就喺嗰個娃娃似嘅嘢裡面——而吉米·比恩係個知道上帝喺天上嘅小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想,領養一個印度的小男孩來教養,總比領養吉米·比恩要好——那個孩子什麼都不懂,居然以為上帝就在那個娃娃似的東西裡面——而吉米·比恩是個知道上帝在天上的小男孩。

passages.original: Still, I can't help wishing they had wanted Jimmy Bean, too, besides the India boys.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,我定係忍不住希望,佢哋除咗要印度嘅男孩之外,都能要吉米·比恩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,我還是忍不住希望,他們除了要印度的男孩之外,也能要吉米·比恩。」

passages.original: John Pendleton did not seem to hear.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓似乎冇聽見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓似乎沒有聽見。

passages.original: Again his, eyes were staring straight before him, looking at nothing.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛又直直地盯住前方,乜嘢都冇睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的眼睛又直直地盯著前方,什麼也沒看。

passages.original: But soon he had roused himself, and had picked up another curio to talk about.
passages.vernacular: 但好快佢就回過神嚟,又攞起另一件古玩講咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但很快他就回過神來,又拿起另一件古玩講了起來。

passages.original: The visit, certainly, was a delightful one, but before it was over, Pollyanna was realizing that they were talking about something besides the wonderful things in the beautiful carved box.
passages.vernacular: 呢次拜訪確實愉快,但喺結束之前,波莉安娜就發覺,佢哋談嘅已經不只係嗰隻漂亮雕花盒子裡嘅奇妙嘢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次拜訪確實愉快,但在結束之前,波莉安娜就發覺,他們談的已經不只是那隻漂亮雕花盒子裡的奇妙東西了。

passages.original: They were talking of herself, of Nancy, of Aunt Polly, and of her daily life.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋談起咗佢自己、南希、波莉姨媽,仲有佢嘅日常生活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們談起了她自己、南希、波莉姨媽,還有她的日常生活。

passages.original: They were talking, too, even of the life and home long ago in the far Western town.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋甚至仲談到咗好久以前喺遙遠西部小鎮上嘅生活同家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們甚至還談到了很久以前在遙遠西部小鎮上的生活和家。

passages.original: Not until it was nearly time for her to go, did the man say, in a voice Pollyanna had never before heard from stern John Pendleton:
passages.vernacular: 直到快要告辭嘅時候,呢個男人才用波莉安娜從未喺嚴厲嘅約翰·潘德爾頓口中聽過嘅語氣講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到快要告辭的時候,這個男人才用波莉安娜從未在嚴厲的約翰·潘德爾頓口中聽過的語氣說:

passages.original: “Little girl, I want you to come to see me often.
passages.vernacular: 「小姑娘,我希望你常嚟睇我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小姑娘,我希望你常來看我。

passages.original: Will you?
passages.vernacular: 你愿意嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你愿意嗎?

passages.original: I'm lonesome, and I need you.
passages.vernacular: 我好寂寞,我需要你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很寂寞,我需要你。

passages.original: There's another reason--and I'm going to tell you that, too.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一個原因——我都要告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一個原因——我也要告訴你。

passages.original: I thought, at first, after I found out who you were, the other day, that I didn't want you to come any more.
passages.vernacular: 前幾天我發現你係邊個以後,起初我想,我唔想你再嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前幾天我發現你是誰以後,起初我想,我不想你再來了。

passages.original: You reminded me of--of something I have tried for long years to forget.
passages.vernacular: 你讓我想起喇——想起咗一件我多年嚟一直想忘掉嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你讓我想起了——想起了一件我多年來一直想忘掉的事。

passages.original: So I said to myself that I never wanted to see you again; and every day, when the doctor asked if I wouldn't let him bring you to me, I said no.
passages.vernacular: 所以我對自己講,我再都唔想見你;每天醫生問我愿不愿意讓佢帶你嚟,我都講不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我對自己說,我再也不想見你;每天醫生問我愿不愿意讓他帶你來,我都說不。

passages.original: “But after a time I found I was wanting to see you so much that--that the fact that I WASN'T seeing you was making me remember all the more vividly the thing I was so wanting to forget.
passages.vernacular: 「不過過咗一陣子,我發現我咁想見你,以至于——以至于冇見到你呢件事,反而讓我對嗰件拼命想忘記嘅事記得更清楚喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是過了一陣子,我發現我那麼想見你,以至于——以至于沒見到你這件事,反而讓我對那件拼命想忘記的事記得更清楚了。

passages.original: So now I want you to come.
passages.vernacular: 所以而家我希望你嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以現在我希望你來。

passages.original: Will you--little girl?”
passages.vernacular: 你愿意嗎——小姑娘?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你愿意嗎——小姑娘?」

passages.original: “Why, yes, Mr. Pendleton,” breathed Pollyanna, her eyes luminous with sympathy for the sad-faced man lying back on the pillow before her.
passages.vernacular: 「當然愿意,潘德爾頓先生,」波莉安娜輕聲講,睇住躺喺枕頭上、面帶愁容嘅男人,眼裡滿係同情嘅光,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然愿意,潘德爾頓先生,」波莉安娜輕聲說,看著躺在枕頭上、面帶愁容的男人,眼裡滿是同情的光,

passages.original: “I'd love to come!”
passages.vernacular: 「我好樂意嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很樂意來!」

passages.original: “Thank you,” said John Pendleton, gently.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你。」約翰·潘德爾頓溫和地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你。」約翰·潘德爾頓溫和地說。

passages.original: After supper that evening, Pollyanna, sitting on the back porch, told Nancy all about Mr. John Pendleton's wonderful carved box, and the still more wonderful things it contained.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚飯後,波莉安娜坐喺後門廊上,把約翰·潘德爾頓先生嗰隻奇妙嘅雕花盒子,同裡面更奇妙嘅嘢,全都講畀南希聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚飯後,波莉安娜坐在後門廊上,把約翰·潘德爾頓先生那隻奇妙的雕花盒子,和裡面更奇妙的東西,全都講給南希聽。

passages.original: “And ter think,” sighed Nancy, “that he SHOWED ye all them things, and told ye about 'em like that--him that's so cross he never talks ter no one--no one!”
passages.vernacular: 「你想想睇,」南希嘆道,「佢居然讓你睇嗰啲嘢,仲像嗰樣畀你講——佢不過咁兇,從來不跟任何人講話嘅人——任何人都不理!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你想想看,」南希嘆道,「他居然讓你看那些東西,還像那樣給你講——他可是那麼兇,從來不跟任何人說話的人——任何人都不理!」

passages.original: “Oh, but he isn't cross, Nancy, only outside,” demurred Pollyanna, with quick loyalty.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過佢并不兇呀,南希,只係外表咁樣,」波莉安娜好快地為佢辯護,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是他并不兇呀,南希,只是外表這樣,」波莉安娜很快地為他辯護,

passages.original: “I don't see why everybody thinks he's so bad, either.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白點解大家都覺得佢咁壞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白為什麼大家都覺得他那麼壞。

passages.original: They wouldn't, if they knew him.
passages.vernacular: 要係佢哋認識佢,就唔會咁想喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是他們認識他,就不會這麼想了。

passages.original: But even Aunt Polly doesn't like him very well.
passages.vernacular: 不過就連波莉姨媽都不太鍾意佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過就連波莉姨媽也不太喜歡他。

passages.original: She wouldn't send the jelly to him, you know, and she was so afraid he'd think she did send it!”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,佢唔肯把果凍送畀佢,仲生怕佢以為係佢送嘅呢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,她不肯把果凍送給他,還生怕他以為是她送的呢!」

passages.original: “Probably she didn't call him no duty,” shrugged Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「大概佢覺得對佢冇乜嘢義務吧。」南希聳聳肩講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大概她覺得對他沒什麼義務吧。」南希聳聳肩說,

passages.original: “But what beats me is how he happened ter take ter you so, Miss Pollyanna--meanin' no offence ter you, of course--but he ain't the sort o' man what gen'rally takes ter kids; he ain't, he ain't.”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我想不通嘅係,佢點會咁鍾意你,波莉安娜小姐——我冇冒犯你嘅意思——可佢唔係嗰種一般會鍾意小孩嘅人;佢唔係,佢唔係啊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過我想不通的是,他怎麼會這麼喜歡你,波莉安娜小姐——我沒有冒犯你的意思——可他不是那種一般會喜歡小孩的人;他不是,他不是啊。」

passages.original: Pollyanna smiled happily.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜高興地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜高興地笑了。

passages.original: “But he did, Nancy,” she nodded, “only I reckon even he didn't want to--ALL the time.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢鍾意我呀,南希,」佢點點頭講,「不過我想就連佢都唔係一直都想見我——一直都想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是他喜歡我呀,南希,」她點點頭說,「不過我想就連他也不是一直都想見我——一直都想。

passages.original: Why, only to-day he owned up that one time he just felt he never wanted to see me again, because I reminded him of something he wanted to forget.
passages.vernacular: 你瞧,就喺今日佢仲承認,有一陣子佢覺得再都唔想見我,因為我讓佢想起咗一件佢想忘記嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瞧,就在今天他還承認,有一陣子他覺得再也不想見我,因為我讓他想起了一件他想忘記的事。

passages.original: But afterwards--”
passages.vernacular: 不過後來——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過後來——」

passages.original: “What's that?” interrupted Nancy, excitedly.
passages.vernacular: 「你講乜嘢?」南希激動地打斷佢,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說什麼?」南希激動地打斷她,

passages.original: “He said you reminded him of something he wanted to forget?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講你讓佢想起咗一件佢想忘記嘅事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說你讓他想起了一件他想忘記的事?」

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係呀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是呀。

passages.original: But afterwards--”
passages.vernacular: 不過後來——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過後來——」

passages.original: “What was it?”
passages.vernacular: 「係乜嘢事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是什麼事?」

passages.original: Nancy was eagerly insistent.
passages.vernacular: 南希急切地追問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希急切地追問。

passages.original: “He didn't tell me.
passages.vernacular: 「佢冇告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他沒告訴我。

passages.original: He just said it was something.”
passages.vernacular: 佢只講係一件事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只說是一件事。」

passages.original: “THE MYSTERY!” breathed Nancy, in an awestruck voice.
passages.vernacular: 「謎團啊!」南希用敬畏嘅聲音喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謎團啊!」南希用敬畏的聲音喘著氣說。

passages.original: “That's why he took to you in the first place.
passages.vernacular: 「所以佢起先才會鍾意上你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以他起先才會喜歡上你。

passages.original: Oh, Miss Pollyanna!
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉安娜小姐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉安娜小姐!

passages.original: Why, that's just like a book--I've read lots of 'em; 'Lady Maud's Secret,' and 'The Lost Heir,' and 'Hidden for Years'--all of 'em had mysteries and things just like this.
passages.vernacular: 呢簡直就像書裡寫嘅一樣——我睇過好多咁樣嘅書呢:《莫德夫人嘅秘密》、《失蹤嘅繼承人》、《隱藏多年》——全都有謎團,有咁樣嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這簡直就像書裡寫的一樣——我看過好多這樣的書呢:《莫德夫人的秘密》、《失蹤的繼承人》、《隱藏多年》——全都有謎團,有這樣的事。

passages.original: My stars and stockings!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的天哪!

passages.original: Just think of havin' a book lived right under yer nose like this an' me not knowin' it all this time!
passages.vernacular: 你想想,有一本書就活生生地喺咱哋眼皮底下,我卻一直都唔知道!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想想,有一本書就活生生地在咱們眼皮底下,我卻一直都不知道!

passages.original: Now tell me everythin'--everythin' he said, Miss Pollyanna, there's a dear!
passages.vernacular: 快告訴我所有嘅事——佢講嘅所有嘅事,波莉安娜小姐,好小姐!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快告訴我所有的事——他說的所有的事,波莉安娜小姐,好小姐!

passages.original: No wonder he took ter you; no wonder--no wonder!”
passages.vernacular: 難怪佢鍾意你;難怪——難怪啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難怪他喜歡你;難怪——難怪啊!」

passages.original: “But he didn't,” cried Pollyanna, “not till I talked to HIM, first.
passages.vernacular: 「可佢起先并不鍾意,」波莉安娜叫道,「要等我先跟佢講話,佢才鍾意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可他起先并不喜歡,」波莉安娜叫道,「要等我先跟他說話,他才喜歡的。

passages.original: And he didn't even know who I was till I took the calf's-foot jelly, and had to make him understand that Aunt Polly didn't send it, and--”
passages.vernacular: 而且佢起先連我係邊個都唔知道,直到我攞咗小牛腳凍去,仲得讓佢明白嗰個係波莉姨媽冇送嘅,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且他起先連我是誰都不知道,直到我拿了小牛腳凍去,還得讓他明白那是波莉姨媽沒送的,而且——」

passages.original: Nancy sprang to her feet and clasped her hands together suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 南希猛地跳起嚟,雙手一拍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希猛地跳起來,雙手一拍。

passages.original: “Oh, Miss Pollyanna, I know, I know--I KNOW I know!” she exulted rapturously.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉安娜小姐,我知道喇,我知道喇——我知道我知道喇!」佢欣喜若狂地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉安娜小姐,我知道了,我知道了——我知道我知道了!」她欣喜若狂地喊道。

passages.original: The next minute she was down at Pollyanna's side again.
passages.vernacular: 下一刻,佢又回到波莉安娜身邊坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一刻,她又回到波莉安娜身邊坐下。

passages.original: “Tell me--now think, and answer straight and true,” she urged excitedly.
passages.vernacular: 「告訴我——你仔細想想,老老實實回答,」佢激動地催促道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴我——你仔細想想,老老實實回答,」她激動地催促道,

passages.original: “It was after he found out you was Miss Polly's niece that he said he didn't ever want ter see ye again, wa'n't it?”
passages.vernacular: 「係佢知道你係波莉小姐嘅外甥女之後,才講再都唔想見你嘅,對不對?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是他知道你是波莉小姐的外甥女之後,才說再也不想見你的,對不對?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,對。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,對。

passages.original: I told him that the last time I saw him, and he told me this to-day.”
passages.vernacular: 我最後一次見佢時就告訴過佢呢啲,佢今日都咁對我講喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我最後一次見他時就告訴過他這一點,他今天也這麼對我說了。」

passages.original: “I thought as much,” triumphed Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「我就猜係咁樣,」南希得意地講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就猜是這樣,」南希得意地說,

passages.original: “And Miss Polly wouldn't send the jelly herself, would she?”
passages.vernacular: 「而且波莉小姐自己唔肯送果凍,對不對?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且波莉小姐自己不肯送果凍,對不對?」

passages.original: “No.”
“And you told him she didn't send it?”
passages.vernacular: 「你仲告訴佢佢冇送?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你還告訴他她沒送?」

passages.original: “Why, yes; I--”
“And he began ter act queer and cry out sudden after he found out you was her niece.
passages.vernacular: 「而且佢知道你係佢外甥女之後,就開始舉止古怪,仲突然叫出聲嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且他知道你是她外甥女之後,就開始舉止古怪,還突然叫出聲來。

passages.original: He did that, didn't he?”
passages.vernacular: 佢係咁樣嘅,對不對?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是這樣的,對不對?」

passages.original: “Why, y-yes; he did act a little queer--over that jelly,” admitted Pollyanna, with a thoughtful frown.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係、係嘅;佢確實有點古怪——就為了嗰果凍。」波莉安娜皺住眉頭,若有所思地承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是、是的;他確實有點古怪——就為了那果凍。」波莉安娜皺著眉頭,若有所思地承認。

passages.original: Nancy drew a long sigh.
passages.vernacular: 南希長長地吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希長長地吸了口氣。

passages.original: “Then I've got it, sure!
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我準係猜對喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我準是猜對了!

passages.original: Now listen.
passages.vernacular: 而家聽好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在聽好。
