passages.original: MR.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·

passages.original: JOHN PENDLETON WAS MISS POLLY HARRINGTON'S LOVER!” she announced impressively, but with a furtive glance over her shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 潘德爾頓先生就係波莉·哈靈頓小姐嘅情人!」佢一本正經地宣布,卻又心虛地回頭瞥咗一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潘德爾頓先生就是波莉·哈靈頓小姐的情人!」她一本正經地宣布,卻又心虛地回頭瞥了一眼。

passages.original: “Why, Nancy, he couldn't be!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,南希,唔可能!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,南希,不可能!

passages.original: She doesn't like him,” objected Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 佢不鍾意佢呀。」波莉安娜反駁道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不喜歡他呀。」波莉安娜反駁道。

passages.original: Nancy gave her a scornful glance.
passages.vernacular: 南希輕蔑地睇咗佢一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希輕蔑地看了她一眼。

passages.original: “Of course she don't!
passages.vernacular: 「佢當然不鍾意!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她當然不喜歡!

passages.original: THAT'S the quarrel!”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係佢哋吵架嘅緣故!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是他們吵架的緣故!」

passages.original: Pollyanna still looked incredulous, and with another long breath Nancy happily settled herself to tell the story.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜依然一臉不信,南希又深深吸咗口氣,開心地坐好,準備講呢個故事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜依然一臉不信,南希又深深吸了口氣,開心地坐好,準備講這個故事。

passages.original: “It's like this.
passages.vernacular: 「係咁樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是這樣的。

passages.original: Just before you come, Mr. Tom told me Miss Polly had had a lover once.
passages.vernacular: 就喺你嚟之前,湯姆先生告訴我,波莉小姐曾經有過一個情人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在你來之前,湯姆先生告訴我,波莉小姐曾經有過一個情人。

passages.original: I didn't believe it.
passages.vernacular: 我不信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不信。

passages.original: I couldn't--her and a lover!
passages.vernacular: 我點可能信——佢,仲有情人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怎麼可能信——她,還有情人!

passages.original: But Mr. Tom said she had, and that he was livin' now right in this town.
passages.vernacular: 可湯姆先生講佢有過,而且嗰個人而家就住喺呢個鎮上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可湯姆先生說她有過,而且那個人現在就住在這個鎮上。

passages.original: And NOW I know, of course.
passages.vernacular: 而家我當然明白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我當然明白了。

passages.original: It's John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 就係約翰·潘德爾頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是約翰·潘德爾頓。

passages.original: Hain't he got a mystery in his life?
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅生活裡唔係有個謎嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的生活裡不是有個謎嗎?

passages.original: Don't he shut himself up in that grand house alone, and never speak ter no one?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係一個人把自己關喺嗰座大房子裡,從不跟任何人講話嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是一個人把自己關在那座大房子裡,從不跟任何人說話嗎?

passages.original: Didn't he act queer when he found out you was Miss Polly's niece?
passages.vernacular: 佢知道你係波莉小姐嘅外甥女之後,唔係舉止古怪嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他知道你是波莉小姐的外甥女之後,不是舉止古怪嗎?

passages.original: And now hain't he owned up that you remind him of somethin' he wants ter forget?
passages.vernacular: 而家佢唔係都承認,你讓佢想起咗一件佢想忘記嘅事嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他不是也承認,你讓他想起了一件他想忘記的事嗎?

passages.original: Just as if ANYBODY couldn't see 'twas Miss Polly!--an' her sayin' she wouldn't send him no jelly, too.
passages.vernacular: 擺明了就係波莉小姐嘛,邊個睇不出嚟!——何況佢仲講唔肯畀佢送乜嘢果凍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 擺明了就是波莉小姐嘛,誰看不出來!——何況她還說不肯給他送什麼果凍。

passages.original: Why, Miss Pollyanna, it's as plain as the nose on yer face; it is, it is!”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉安娜小姐,呢明擺住嘅,就像你臉上嘅鼻子一樣明顯;就係咁樣,就係咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉安娜小姐,這明擺著的,就像你臉上的鼻子一樣明顯;就是這樣,就是這樣!」

passages.original: “Oh-h!” breathed Pollyanna, in wide-eyed amazement.
passages.vernacular: 「哦——!」波莉安娜睜大眼睛,驚訝地喘住氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——!」波莉安娜睜大眼睛,驚訝地喘著氣。

passages.original: “But, Nancy, I should think if they loved each other they'd make up some time.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,南希,我想佢哋要係互相愛住,總有一天會同好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,南希,我想他們要是互相愛著,總有一天會和好的。

passages.original: Both of 'em all alone, so, all these years.
passages.vernacular: 兩個人咁多年都孤零零嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個人這麼多年都孤零零的。

passages.original: I should think they'd be glad to make up!”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢哋應該好樂意同好才對呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他們應該很樂意和好才對呀!」

passages.original: Nancy sniffed disdainfully.
passages.vernacular: 南希不屑地哼咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希不屑地哼了一聲。

passages.original: “I guess maybe you don't know much about lovers, Miss Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「我睇你不大懂情人嘅事吧,波莉安娜小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我看你不大懂情人的事吧,波莉安娜小姐。

passages.original: You ain't big enough yet, anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 你呀,反正年紀仲唔夠大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你呀,反正年紀還不夠大。

passages.original: But if there IS a set o' folks in the world that wouldn't have no use for that 'ere 'glad game' o' your'n, it'd be a pair o' quarrellin' lovers; and that's what they be.
passages.vernacular: 不過要講世上有邊一類人用不上你嗰個『高興遊戲』,嗰個就係一對吵咗架嘅情人;佢哋就係嗰樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過要說世上有哪一類人用不上你那個『高興遊戲』,那就是一對吵了架的情人;他們就是那樣的。

passages.original: Ain't he cross as sticks, most gen'rally?--and ain't she--”
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係大多數時候都兇得像根棍子嗎?——佢不都係——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不是大多數時候都兇得像根棍子嗎?——她不也是——」

passages.original: Nancy stopped abruptly, remembering just in time to whom, and about whom, she was speaking.
passages.vernacular: 南希突然住咗口,及時想起咗自己喺對邊個講話、喺講邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希突然住了口,及時想起了自己在對誰說話、在說誰。

passages.original: Suddenly, however, she chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢隨即又咯咯笑咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,她隨即又咯咯笑了起來。

passages.original: “I ain't sayin', though, Miss Pollyanna, but what it would be a pretty slick piece of business if you could GET 'em ter playin' it--so they WOULD be glad ter make up.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,我可冇講,波莉安娜小姐,要係你能讓佢哋玩起呢個遊戲——讓佢哋愿意同好——嗰倒係樁挺漂亮嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過,我可沒說,波莉安娜小姐,要是你能讓他們玩起這個遊戲——讓他們愿意和好——那倒是樁挺漂亮的事。

passages.original: But, my land! wouldn't folks stare some--Miss Polly and him!
passages.vernacular: 不過,天呀!大伙兒唔得嚇一跳嗎——波莉小姐同佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,天哪!大伙兒不得嚇一跳嗎——波莉小姐和他!

passages.original: I guess, though, there ain't much chance, much chance!”
passages.vernacular: 不過我想啊,機會不大,機會不大!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我想啊,機會不大,機會不大!」

passages.original: Pollyanna said nothing; but when she went into the house a little later, her face was very thoughtful.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜冇講話;不過過咗一會兒佢走進屋裡嘅時候,臉上嘅神情好若有所思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜沒說話;可是過了一會兒她走進屋裡的時候,臉上的神情非常若有所思。

chapters.title: Ch. XVIII Prisms 第十八章:棱鏡

passages.original: CH As the warm August days passed, Pollyanna went very frequently to the great house on Pendleton Hill.
passages.vernacular: 八月裡暖同嘅日子一天天過去,波莉安娜常常到潘德爾頓山上嘅嗰座大房子去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 八月裡暖和的日子一天天過去,波莉安娜常常到潘德爾頓山上的那座大房子去。

passages.original: She did not feel, however, that her visits were really a success.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢并不覺得佢嘅拜訪真嘅成功喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是她并不覺得她的拜訪真的成功了。

passages.original: Not but that the man seemed to want her there--he sent for her, indeed, frequently; but that when she was there, he seemed scarcely any the happier for her presence--at least, so Pollyanna thought.
passages.vernacular: 并唔係講嗰個男人唔想要佢去——佢的確經常派人叫佢;只係佢去咗以後,佢似乎并冇因為佢在場就開心多少——至少波莉安娜係咁想嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 并不是說那個男人不想要她去——他的確經常派人叫她;只是她去了以後,他似乎并沒有因為她在場就開心多少——至少波莉安娜是這麼想的。

passages.original: He talked to her, it was true, and he showed her many strange and beautiful things--books, pictures, and curios.
passages.vernacular: 佢確實跟佢講話,都畀佢睇咗許多奇妙美麗嘅嘢——書、畫同珍奇古玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他確實跟她說話,也給她看了許多奇妙美麗的東西——書、畫和珍奇古玩。

passages.original: But he still fretted audibly over his own helplessness, and he chafed visibly under the rules and “regulatings” of the unwelcome members of his household.
passages.vernacular: 但佢仍舊對自己嘅無助抱怨個不停,仲對家裡嗰啲不受歡迎嘅人定下嘅規矩同「整理」公然表示不滿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但他仍舊對自己的無助抱怨個不停,還對家裡那些不受歡迎的人定下的規矩和「整理」公然表示不滿。

passages.original: He did, indeed, seem to like to hear Pollyanna talk, however, and Pollyanna talked, Pollyanna liked to talk--but she was never sure that she would not look up and find him lying back on his pillow with that white, hurt look that always pained her; and she was never sure which--if any--of her words had brought it there.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢確實似乎鍾意聽波莉安娜講話,而波莉安娜都愛講話——可佢總是講不準,抬頭會唔會又睇見佢仰躺喺枕頭上,帶住嗰種總讓佢難受嘅、蒼白而受傷嘅神情;而且佢從來唔知道,係自己嘅邊一句話——如果有嘅話——引出咗嗰副神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過他確實似乎喜歡聽波莉安娜說話,而波莉安娜也愛說話——可她總是說不準,抬頭會不會又看見他仰躺在枕頭上,帶著那種總讓她難受的、蒼白而受傷的神情;而且她從來不知道,是自己的哪一句話——如果有的話——引出了那副神情。

passages.original: As for telling him the “glad game,” and trying to get him to play it--Pollyanna had never seen the time yet when she thought he would care to hear about it.
passages.vernacular: 至于把「高興遊戲」講畀佢聽,并讓佢玩——波莉安娜從來冇碰到過一個時機,覺得佢會想聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至于把「高興遊戲」講給他聽,并讓他玩——波莉安娜從來沒碰到過一個時機,覺得他會想聽。

passages.original: She had twice tried to tell him; but neither time had she got beyond the beginning of what her father had said--John Pendleton had on each occasion turned the conversation abruptly to another subject.
passages.vernacular: 佢試過兩次要告訴佢;但兩次都冇講到佢父親講嘅話嘅開頭——兩次約翰·潘德爾頓都突然把話題轉到別處去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她試過兩次要告訴他;但兩次都沒講到她父親說的話的開頭——兩次約翰·潘德爾頓都突然把話題轉到別處去了。

passages.original: Pollyanna never doubted now that John Pendleton was her Aunt Polly's one-time lover; and with all the strength of her loving, loyal heart, she wished she could in some way bring happiness into their to her mind--miserably lonely lives.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜而家毫不懷疑,約翰·潘德爾頓就係佢波莉姨媽從前嘅情人;佢用盡佢充滿愛嘅忠誠嘅心嘅全部力量,希望能想辦法畀佢哋——喺佢睇來係嗰樣可憐孤單嘅兩個人——帶嚟幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜現在毫不懷疑,約翰·潘德爾頓就是她波莉姨媽從前的情人;她用盡她充滿愛的忠誠的心的全部力量,希望能想辦法給他們——在她看來是那樣可憐孤單的兩個人——帶來幸福。

passages.original: Just how she was to do this, however, she could not see.
passages.vernacular: 不過究竟該點做,佢卻睇不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是究竟該怎麼做,她卻看不出來。

passages.original: She talked to Mr. Pendleton about her aunt; and he listened, sometimes politely, sometimes irritably, frequently with a quizzical smile on his usually stern lips.
passages.vernacular: 佢跟潘德爾頓先生談起佢姨媽;佢聽住,有時客客氣氣,有時不耐煩,常常係嘴角掛住一絲嘲弄嘅微笑,而佢嗰嘴唇平時係好嚴厲嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她跟潘德爾頓先生談起她姨媽;他聽著,有時客客氣氣,有時不耐煩,常常是嘴角掛著一絲嘲弄的微笑,而他那嘴唇平時是很嚴厲的。

passages.original: She talked to her aunt about Mr. Pendleton--or rather, she tried to talk to her about him.
passages.vernacular: 佢又跟姨媽談起潘德爾頓先生——或者講,佢試住跟佢談起佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她又跟姨媽談起潘德爾頓先生——或者說,她試著跟她談起他。

passages.original: As a general thing, however, Miss Polly would not listen--long.
passages.vernacular: 不過一般來講,波莉小姐聽不咗多久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過一般來說,波莉小姐聽不了多久。

passages.original: She always found something else to talk about.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是找別嘅話題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她總是找別的話題。

passages.original: She frequently did that, however, when Pollyanna was talking of others--of Dr. Chilton, for instance.
passages.vernacular: 不過當波莉安娜談起別人嘅時候,佢都常常咁樣——比如談起奇爾頓醫生嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過當波莉安娜談起別人的時候,她也常常這樣——比如談起奇爾頓醫生的時候。

passages.original: Pollyanna laid this, though, to the fact that it had been Dr. Chilton who had seen her in the sun parlor with the rose in her hair and the lace shawl draped about her shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 不過波莉安娜把呢歸因于:當時係奇爾頓醫生睇見佢喺日光室裡頭上插住玫瑰、肩上披住蕾絲披肩嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過波莉安娜把這歸因于:當時是奇爾頓醫生看見她在日光室裡頭上插著玫瑰、肩上披著蕾絲披肩的樣子。

passages.original: Aunt Polly, indeed, seemed particularly bitter against Dr. Chilton, as Pollyanna found out one day when a hard cold shut her up in the house.
passages.vernacular: 姨媽似乎特別痛恨奇爾頓醫生,呢個係波莉安娜有一天重感冒被關喺家裡時發現嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 姨媽似乎特別痛恨奇爾頓醫生,這是波莉安娜有一天重感冒被關在家裡時發現的。

passages.original: “If you are not better by night I shall send for the doctor,” Aunt Polly said.
passages.vernacular: 「要係你到晚上仲唔見好,我就派人去請醫生。」波莉姨媽講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是你到晚上還不見好,我就派人去請醫生。」波莉姨媽說。

passages.original: “Shall you?
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的嗎?

passages.original: Then I'm going to be worse,” gurgled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 嗰我就要加重喇。」波莉安娜咯咯笑住講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我就要加重了。」波莉安娜咯咯笑著說,

passages.original: “I'd love to have Dr. Chilton come to see me!”
passages.vernacular: 「我好想讓奇爾頓醫生來睇我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很想讓奇爾頓醫生來看我!」

passages.original: She wondered, then, at the look that came to her aunt's face.
passages.vernacular: 接住佢奇怪地睇到姨媽臉上現出嘅神色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著她奇怪地看到姨媽臉上現出的神色。

passages.original: “It will not be Dr. Chilton, Pollyanna,” Miss Polly said sternly.
passages.vernacular: 「唔會係奇爾頓醫生,波莉安娜,」波莉小姐嚴厲地講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會是奇爾頓醫生,波莉安娜,」波莉小姐嚴厲地說,

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton is not our family physician.
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生唔係我哋家嘅家庭醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生不是我們家的家庭醫生。

passages.original: I shall send for Dr. Warren--if you are worse.”
passages.vernacular: 如果你病重喇,我會請沃倫醫生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你病重了,我會請沃倫醫生。」

passages.original: Pollyanna did not grow worse, however, and Dr. Warren was not summoned.
passages.vernacular: 不過波莉安娜并冇加重,沃倫醫生都冇被請嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過波莉安娜并沒有加重,沃倫醫生也沒有被請來。

passages.original: “And I'm so glad, too,” Pollyanna said to her aunt that evening.
passages.vernacular: 「我都真高興,」嗰天晚上波莉安娜對姨媽講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也真高興,」那天晚上波莉安娜對姨媽說,

passages.original: “Of course I like Dr. Warren, and all that; but I like Dr. Chilton better, and I'm afraid he'd feel hurt if I didn't have him.
passages.vernacular: 「當然我都鍾意沃倫醫生,呢啲都冇錯;可我更鍾意奇爾頓醫生,我怕要係我不請佢,佢會傷心嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然我也喜歡沃倫醫生,這些都沒錯;可我更喜歡奇爾頓醫生,我怕要是我不請他,他會傷心的。

passages.original: You see, he wasn't really to blame, after all, that he happened to see you when I'd dressed you up so pretty that day, Aunt Polly,” she finished wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 你知道,佢真嘅不該受責怪,波莉姨媽,佢只係碰巧喺嗰天睇見咗你,而當時係我把你打扮得咁漂亮。」佢惋惜地講完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,他真的不該受責怪,波莉姨媽,他只是碰巧在那天看見了你,而當時是我把你打扮得那麼漂亮。」她惋惜地說完。

passages.original: “That will do, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「夠喇,波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「夠了,波莉安娜。

passages.original: I really do not wish to discuss Dr. Chilton--or his feelings,” reproved Miss Polly, decisively.
passages.vernacular: 我真嘅唔想討論奇爾頓醫生——或者佢嘅感受。」波莉小姐斷然責備道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真的不想討論奇爾頓醫生——或者他的感受。」波莉小姐斷然責備道。

passages.original: Pollyanna looked at her for a moment with mournfully interested eyes; then she sighed:
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜帶住悲傷而感興趣嘅眼神睇咗佢一會兒;然後嘆咗口氣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜帶著悲傷而感興趣的眼神看了她一會兒;然後嘆了口氣:

passages.original: “I just love to see you when your cheeks are pink like that, Aunt Polly; but I would so like to fix your hair.
passages.vernacular: 「我真愛睇你臉頰像咁樣紅紅嘅樣子,波莉姨媽;我真想畀你梳頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真愛看你臉頰像這樣紅紅的樣子,波莉姨媽;我真想給你梳頭髮。

passages.original: If--Why, Aunt Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 要係——哎呀,波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是——哎呀,波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: But her aunt was already out of sight down the hall.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢姨媽已經走到走廊嗰頭睇唔見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是她姨媽已經走到走廊那頭看不見了。

passages.original: It was toward the end of August that Pollyanna, making an early morning call on John Pendleton, found the flaming band of blue and gold and green edged with red and violet lying across his pillow.
passages.vernacular: 八月快結束嘅時候,有一天清晨波莉安娜去睇約翰·潘德爾頓,發現一道火焰般嘅藍、金、綠、邊上帶住紅同紫嘅光帶,橫喺佢嘅枕頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 八月快結束的時候,有一天清晨波莉安娜去看約翰·潘德爾頓,發現一道火焰般的藍、金、綠、邊上帶著紅和紫的光帶,橫在他的枕頭上。

passages.original: She stopped short in awed delight.
passages.vernacular: 佢驚喜得愣住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她驚喜得愣住了。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, it's a baby rainbow--a real rainbow come in to pay you a visit!” she exclaimed, clapping her hands together softly.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,呢個係個小彩虹——一道真嘅彩虹嚟睇你啦!」佢輕輕拍著手叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,這是個小彩虹——一道真的彩虹來看你啦!」她輕輕拍著手叫道。

passages.original: “Oh--oh--oh, how pretty it is!
passages.vernacular: 「哦——哦——哦,多美呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——哦——哦,多美呀!

passages.original: But how DID it get in?” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 可佢係點進嚟嘅呢?」佢喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可它是怎麼進來的呢?」她喊道。

passages.original: The man laughed a little grimly: John Pendleton was particularly out of sorts with the world this morning.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人有點嚴峻地笑咗笑:約翰·潘德爾頓今日朝早特別跟全世界過不去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人有點嚴峻地笑了笑:約翰·潘德爾頓今天早上特別跟全世界過不去。

passages.original: “Well, I suppose it 'got in' through the bevelled edge of that glass thermometer in the window,” he said wearily.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我想係從窗臺上嗰支玻璃溫度計嘅斜面邊緣『進嚟』嘅吧。」佢疲倦地講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我想是從窗臺上那支玻璃溫度計的斜面邊緣『進來』的吧。」他疲倦地說,

passages.original: “The sun shouldn't strike it at all but it does in the morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「太陽本不該照到佢,可朝早就照到喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太陽本不該照到它,可早上就照到了。」

passages.original: “Oh, but it's so pretty, Mr. Pendleton!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過佢太美啦,潘德爾頓先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是它太美啦,潘德爾頓先生!

passages.original: And does just the sun do that?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係太陽做嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是太陽做的嗎?

passages.original: My! if it was mine I'd have it hang in the sun all day long!”
passages.vernacular: 天呀!要係佢係我嘅,我要讓佢整天掛喺太陽底下!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 天哪!要是它是我的,我要讓它整天掛在太陽底下!」

passages.original: “Lots of good you'd get out of the thermometer, then,” laughed the man.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你就唔會從溫度計嗰度得到乜嘢好處喇,」嗰人笑道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你就不會從溫度計那裡得到什麼好處了,」那人笑道,

passages.original: “How do you suppose you could tell how hot it was, or how cold it was, if the thermometer hung in the sun all day?”
passages.vernacular: 「要係溫度計整天掛喺太陽底下,你點知道係熱定係冷呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是溫度計整天掛在太陽底下,你怎麼知道是熱還是冷呢?」

passages.original: “I shouldn't care,” breathed Pollyanna, her fascinated eyes on the brilliant band of colors across the pillow.
passages.vernacular: 「我才不在乎呢。」波莉安娜講,著迷嘅眼睛盯住枕頭上嗰道燦爛嘅彩色光帶,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我才不在乎呢。」波莉安娜說,著迷的眼睛盯著枕頭上那道燦爛的彩色光帶,

passages.original: “Just as if anybody'd care when they were living all the time in a rainbow!”
passages.vernacular: 「要係整天都生活喺彩虹裡,邊個仲會在乎呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是整天都生活在彩虹裡,誰還會在乎呀!」

passages.original: The man laughed.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人笑了。

passages.original: He was watching Pollyanna's rapt face a little curiously.
passages.vernacular: 佢有點好奇地望住波莉安娜出神嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有點好奇地望著波莉安娜出神的臉。

passages.original: Suddenly a new thought came to him.
passages.vernacular: 忽然佢想到咗一個新點子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 忽然他想到了一個新點子。

passages.original: He touched the bell at his side.
passages.vernacular: 佢按咗一下身邊嘅鈴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他按了一下身邊的鈴。

passages.original: “Nora,” he said, when the elderly maid appeared at the door, “bring me one of the big brass candle-sticks from the mantel in the front drawing-room.”
passages.vernacular: 「諾拉,」當嗰個上咗年紀嘅女仆出而家門口時,佢講,「從前客廳壁爐臺上攞一個大嘅黃銅燭臺嚟畀我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「諾拉,」當那個上了年紀的女仆出現在門口時,他說,「從前客廳壁爐臺上拿一個大的黃銅燭臺來給我。」

passages.original: “Yes, sir,” murmured the woman, looking slightly dazed.
passages.vernacular: 「係,先生。」女仆喃喃道,顯得有點發懵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是,先生。」女仆喃喃道,顯得有點發懵。

passages.original: In a minute she had returned.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒佢就回嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒她就回來了。

passages.original: A musical tinkling entered the room with her as she advanced wonderingly toward the bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢朝床邊走嚟時,伴住一陣悅耳嘅叮當聲,令人好奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她朝床邊走來時,伴著一陣悅耳的叮當聲,令人好奇。

passages.original: It came from the prism pendants encircling the old-fashioned candelabrum in her hand.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係佢手裡嗰座老式燭臺四周嘅棱鏡吊墜發出嘅聲響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是她手裡那座老式燭臺四周的棱鏡吊墜發出的聲響。

passages.original: “Thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你。

passages.original: You may set it here on the stand,” directed the man.
passages.vernacular: 放喺呢個架子上吧。」嗰人吩咐道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 放在這個架子上吧。」那人吩咐道。

passages.original: “Now get a string and fasten it to the sash-curtain fixtures of that window there.
passages.vernacular: 「而家攞根繩子,繫喺嗰邊窗子嘅窗簾掛鉤上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在拿根繩子,繫在那邊窗子的窗簾掛鉤上。

passages.original: Take down the sash-curtain, and let the string reach straight across the window from side to side.
passages.vernacular: 把窗簾取下嚟,讓繩子橫住拉過窗子,從呢邊到嗰邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把窗簾取下來,讓繩子橫著拉過窗子,從這邊到那邊。

passages.original: That will be all.
passages.vernacular: 就呢啲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這些了。

passages.original: Thank you,” he said, when she had carried out his directions.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝你。」等佢照佢嘅吩咐做完,佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝你。」等她照他的吩咐做完,他說。

passages.original: As she left the room he turned smiling eyes toward the wondering Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 佢離開房間後,佢帶住微笑嘅眼睛轉向一臉疑惑嘅波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她離開房間後,他帶著微笑的眼睛轉向一臉疑惑的波莉安娜。

passages.original: “Bring me the candlestick now, please, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家請把燭臺攞畀我,波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在請把燭臺拿給我,波莉安娜。」

passages.original: With both hands she brought it; and in a moment he was slipping off the pendants, one by one, until they lay, a round dozen of them, side by side, on the bed.
passages.vernacular: 佢用雙手把燭臺捧過嚟;不一會兒,佢就把嗰啲吊墜一個個取咗下嚟,整整十二個,并排擺喺床上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用雙手把燭臺捧過來;不一會兒,他就把那些吊墜一個個取了下來,整整十二個,并排擺在床上。

passages.original: “Now, my dear, suppose you take them and hook them to that little string Nora fixed across the window.
passages.vernacular: 「而家,親愛嘅,你把佢哋攞去,掛喺諾拉繫喺窗子上嘅嗰根小繩子上吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在,親愛的,你把它們拿去,掛在諾拉繫在窗子上的那根小繩子上吧。

passages.original: If you really WANT to live in a rainbow--I don't see but we'll have to have a rainbow for you to live in!”
passages.vernacular: 要係你真嘅想住喺彩虹裡——嗰我睇我哋就得弄一道彩虹畀你住喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是你真的想住在彩虹裡——那我看我們就得弄一道彩虹給你住了!」

passages.original: Pollyanna had not hung up three of the pendants in the sunlit window before she saw a little of what was going to happen.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜喺灑滿陽光嘅窗前仲冇掛上三個吊墜,就已經睇出啲接下嚟會發生乜嘢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜在灑滿陽光的窗前還沒掛上三個吊墜,就已經看出一點接下來會發生什麼了。

passages.original: She was so excited then she could scarcely control her shaking fingers enough to hang up the rest.
passages.vernacular: 佢激動得連發抖嘅手指都幾乎控制不住,冇法把剩下嘅掛完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她激動得連發抖的手指都幾乎控制不住,沒法把剩下的掛完。

passages.original: But at last her task was finished, and she stepped back with a low cry of delight.
passages.vernacular: 不過終于,佢嘅任務完成喇,佢後退一步,發出一聲歡喜嘅低呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是終于,她的任務完成了,她後退一步,發出一聲歡喜的低呼。

passages.original: It had become a fairyland--that sumptuous, but dreary bedroom.
passages.vernacular: 嗰間華麗卻沉悶嘅臥室,變成咗仙境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那間華麗卻沉悶的臥室,變成了仙境。

passages.original: Everywhere were bits of dancing red and green, violet and orange, gold and blue.
passages.vernacular: 到處係跳動嘅碎片:紅嘅、綠嘅,紫嘅、橙嘅,金嘅、藍嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到處是跳動的碎片:紅的、綠的,紫的、橙的,金的、藍的。

passages.original: The wall, the floor, and the furniture, even to the bed itself, were aflame with shimmering bits of color.
passages.vernacular: 墻壁、地板同家具,甚至連床本身,都被閃爍嘅色彩點燃喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 墻壁、地板和家具,甚至連床本身,都被閃爍的色彩點燃了。

passages.original: “Oh, oh, oh, how lovely!” breathed Pollyanna; then she laughed suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,哦,哦,多可愛呀!」波莉安娜喘住氣講;接住佢忽然笑咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,哦,哦,多可愛呀!」波莉安娜喘著氣說;接著她忽然笑了起來。

passages.original: “I just reckon the sun himself is trying to play the game now, don't you?” she cried, forgetting for the moment that Mr. Pendleton could not know what she was talking about.
passages.vernacular: 「我想太陽自己而家都喺玩呢個遊戲喇,你講係唔係?」佢叫道,一時忘咗潘德爾頓先生唔可能知道佢喺講乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想太陽自己現在也在玩這個遊戲了,你說是不是?」她叫道,一時忘了潘德爾頓先生不可能知道她在說什麼。

passages.original: “Oh, how I wish I had a lot of those things!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我真希望我有好多好多咁樣嘅嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我真希望我有好多好多這樣的東西!

passages.original: How I would like to give them to Aunt Polly and Mrs. Snow and--lots of folks.
passages.vernacular: 我要把佢哋送畀波莉姨媽、斯諾太太,仲有——好多好多人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要把它們送給波莉姨媽、斯諾太太,還有——好多好多人。

passages.original: I reckon THEN they'd be glad all right!
passages.vernacular: 我想嗰樣佢哋準會高興起嚟嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想那樣他們準會高興起來的!

passages.original: Why, I think even Aunt Polly'd get so glad she couldn't help banging doors if she lived in a rainbow like that.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,我想就連波莉姨媽要係住喺咁樣嘅彩虹裡,都會高興得忍不住砰砰地摔門呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,我想就連波莉姨媽要是住在這樣的彩虹裡,也會高興得忍不住砰砰地摔門呢。

passages.original: Don't you?”
passages.vernacular: 你講係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說是不是?」

passages.original: Mr. Pendleton laughed.
passages.vernacular: 潘德爾頓先生笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潘德爾頓先生笑了。

passages.original: “Well, from my remembrance of your aunt, Miss Pollyanna, I must say I think it would take something more than a few prisms in the sunlight to--to make her bang many doors--for gladness.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,根據我對你姨媽嘅記憶,波莉安娜小姐,我得講,我覺得光靠陽光裡嘅幾塊棱鏡,係不足以讓佢——高興得去摔幾下門嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,根據我對你姨媽的記憶,波莉安娜小姐,我得說,我覺得光靠陽光裡的幾塊棱鏡,是不足以讓她——高興得去摔幾下門的。

passages.original: But come, now, really, what do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 不過講真嘅,你到底係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過說真的,你到底是什麼意思?」

passages.original: Pollyanna stared slightly; then she drew a long breath.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜略微愣咗一下;接住佢深深吸咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜略微愣了一下;接著她深深吸了口氣。

passages.original: “Oh, I forgot.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我忘喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我忘了。

passages.original: You don't know about the game.
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道呢個遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道這個遊戲。

passages.original: I remember now.”
passages.vernacular: 我而家想起嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在想起來了。」

passages.original: “Suppose you tell me, then.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你告訴我吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你告訴我吧。」

passages.original: And this time Pollyanna told him.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次,波莉安娜告訴咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次,波莉安娜告訴了他。

passages.original: She told him the whole thing from the very first--from the crutches that should have been a doll.
passages.vernacular: 佢把整件事從頭講起——從嗰副本該係洋娃娃嘅拐杖講起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她把整件事從頭講起——從那副本該是洋娃娃的拐杖講起。

passages.original: As she talked, she did not look at his face.
passages.vernacular: 佢一邊講,一邊冇睇佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一邊講,一邊沒有看他的臉。

passages.original: Her rapt eyes were still on the dancing flecks of color from the prism pendants swaying in the sunlit window.
passages.vernacular: 佢出神嘅眼睛始終望住窗前陽光下搖曳嘅棱鏡吊墜投下嘅嗰啲跳動嘅彩色斑點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她出神的眼睛始終望著窗前陽光下搖曳的棱鏡吊墜投下的那些跳動的彩色斑點。

passages.original: “And that's all,” she sighed, when she had finished.
passages.vernacular: 「就係咁樣,」講完後佢嘆咗口氣,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是這樣,」講完後她嘆了口氣,

passages.original: “And now you know why I said the sun was trying to play it--that game.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家你知道我點解講太陽喺玩嗰個遊戲喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你知道我為什麼說太陽在玩那個遊戲了。」

passages.original: For a moment there was silence.
passages.vernacular: 有咁一會兒,屋裡一片寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼一會兒,屋裡一片寂靜。

passages.original: Then a low voice from the bed said unsteadily:
passages.vernacular: 然後床上傳嚟一個低低嘅聲音,顫抖住講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後床上傳來一個低低的聲音,顫抖著說:

passages.original: “Perhaps; but I'm thinking that the very finest prism of them all is yourself, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 「或者係吧;不過我喺想,所有棱鏡裡最好嘅嗰一塊,就係你自己啊,波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許是吧;不過我在想,所有棱鏡裡最好的那一塊,就是你自己啊,波莉安娜。」

passages.original: “Oh, but I don't show beautiful red and green and purple when the sun shines through me, Mr. Pendleton!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過太陽照過我嘅時候,我唔會顯出美麗嘅紅色、綠色同紫色呀,潘德爾頓先生!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是太陽照過我的時候,我不會顯出美麗的紅色、綠色和紫色呀,潘德爾頓先生!」

passages.original: “Don't you?” smiled the man.
passages.vernacular: 「唔會嗎?」嗰人微笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會嗎?」那人微笑著說。

passages.original: And Pollyanna, looking into his face, wondered why there were tears in his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜望住佢嘅臉,不明白佢嘅眼裡點解含住淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜望著他的臉,不明白他的眼裡為什麼含著淚。

passages.original: “No,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「唔會嘅。」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會的。」她說。

passages.original: Then, after a minute she added mournfully: “I'm afraid, Mr. Pendleton, the sun doesn't make anything but freckles out of me.
passages.vernacular: 接住停咗一會兒,佢悲傷地補充道:「潘德爾頓先生,我恐怕太陽照喺我身上,只會弄出雀斑嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著停了一會兒,她悲傷地補充道:「潘德爾頓先生,我恐怕太陽照在我身上,只會弄出雀斑來。

passages.original: Aunt Polly says it DOES make them!”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽講佢真嘅會呢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽說它真的會呢!」

passages.original: The man laughed a little; and again Pollyanna looked at him: the laugh had sounded almost like a sob.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人輕輕笑咗笑;波莉安娜又睇咗佢一眼:嗰笑聲聽起嚟幾乎像係一聲抽泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人輕輕笑了笑;波莉安娜又看了他一眼:那笑聲聽起來幾乎像是一聲抽泣。

chapters.title: Ch. XIX Which Is Somewhat Surprising 第十九章:有點出人意料

passages.original: CH Pollyanna entered school in September.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜九月裡入學喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜九月裡入學了。

passages.original: Preliminary examinations showed that she was well advanced for a girl of her years, and she was soon a happy member of a class of girls and boys her own age.
passages.vernacular: 入學前嘅測驗表明,以佢呢個年紀嘅女孩來講,佢嘅程度相當超前,不久佢就快樂地成咗一個同佢同齡嘅男女同學班級中嘅一員。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 入學前的測驗表明,以她這個年紀的女孩來說,她的程度相當超前,不久她就快樂地成了一個與她同齡的男女同學班級中的一員。

passages.original: School, in some ways, was a surprise to Pollyanna; and Pollyanna, certainly, in many ways, was very much of a surprise to school.
passages.vernacular: 學校喺某些方面讓波莉安娜感到意外;而波莉安娜無疑喺許多方面都讓學校大食一驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 學校在某些方面讓波莉安娜感到意外;而波莉安娜無疑在許多方面也讓學校大吃一驚。

passages.original: They were soon on the best of terms, however, and to her aunt Pollyanna confessed that going to school WAS living, after all--though she had had her doubts before.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢哋好快就相處得極好,波莉安娜仲對姨媽承認,上學終究都算係生活——雖然佢以前對此有過懷疑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過他們很快就相處得極好,波莉安娜還對姨媽承認,上學終究也算是生活——雖然她以前對此有過懷疑。

passages.original: In spite of her delight in her new work, Pollyanna did not forget her old friends.
passages.vernacular: 盡管佢好鍾意新嘅功課,波莉安娜并冇忘記佢嘅老朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盡管她很喜歡新的功課,波莉安娜并沒有忘記她的老朋友。

passages.original: True, she could not give them quite so much time now, of course; but she gave them what time she could.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢而家冇法畀佢哋咁多時間喇;但佢會盡量擠出時間畀佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,她現在沒法給他們那麼多時間了;但她會盡量擠出時間給他們。

passages.original: Perhaps John Pendleton, of them all, however, was the most dissatisfied.
passages.vernacular: 不過喺佢哋所有人當中,約翰·潘德爾頓或者係最不滿意嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過在他們所有人當中,約翰·潘德爾頓也許是最不滿意的。

passages.original: One Saturday afternoon he spoke to her about it.
passages.vernacular: 一個星期六嘅下午,佢向佢提起咗呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個星期六的下午,他向她提起了這件事。

passages.original: “See here, Pollyanna, how would you like to come and live with me?” he asked, a little impatiently.
passages.vernacular: 「聽住,波莉安娜,你愿不愿意嚟跟我一起住?」佢有點不耐煩地問,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著,波莉安娜,你愿不愿意來跟我一起住?」他有點不耐煩地問,

passages.original: “I don't see anything of you, nowadays.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢幾天我都見唔到你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這幾天我都見不到你。」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed--Mr. Pendleton was such a funny man!
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜笑喇——潘德爾頓先生真係個有趣嘅人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜笑了——潘德爾頓先生真是個有趣的人!

passages.original: “I thought you didn't like to have folks 'round,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「我仲以為你不鍾意有人喺身邊呢。」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我還以為你不喜歡有人在身邊呢。」她說。

passages.original: He made a wry face.
passages.vernacular: 佢做咗個苦臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他做了個苦臉。

passages.original: “Oh, but that was before you taught me to play that wonderful game of yours.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰個係喺你教我玩你嗰個奇妙嘅遊戲之前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那是在你教我玩你那個奇妙的遊戲之前。

passages.original: Now I'm glad to be waited on, hand and foot!
passages.vernacular: 而家我好高興有人伺候,手腳都被人照顧住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我很高興有人伺候,手腳都被人照顧著!

passages.original: Never mind, I'll be on my own two feet yet, one of these days; then I'll see who steps around,” he finished, picking up one of the crutches at his side and shaking it playfully at the little girl.
passages.vernacular: 唔好緊,總有一天我會重新站起嚟;到時候我倒要睇睇邊個圍住邊個轉!」佢講完,攞起身邊嘅一根拐杖,逗趣地朝小姑娘晃咗晃。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要緊,總有一天我會重新站起來;到時候我倒要看看誰圍著誰轉!」他說完,拿起身邊的一根拐杖,逗趣地朝小姑娘晃了晃。

passages.original: They were sitting in the great library to-day.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋今日坐喺大書房裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們今天坐在大書房裡。

passages.original: “Oh, but you aren't really glad at all for things; you just SAY you are,” pouted Pollyanna, her eyes on the dog, dozing before the fire.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過你并唔係真嘅為各種事高興,你只係嘴上講講罷喇。」波莉安娜噘住嘴講,眼睛望住喺火爐前打盹嘅狗,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是你并不是真的為各種事高興,你只是嘴上說說罷了。」波莉安娜噘著嘴說,眼睛望著在火爐前打盹的狗,

passages.original: “You know you don't play the game right EVER, Mr. Pendleton--you know you don't!”
passages.vernacular: 「你知道你從來都冇把呢個遊戲玩對過,潘德爾頓先生——你知道你冇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道你從來都沒有把這個遊戲玩對過,潘德爾頓先生——你知道你沒有!」

passages.original: The man's face grew suddenly very grave.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人嘅臉色忽然變得好嚴肅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人的臉色忽然變得很嚴肅。

passages.original: “That's why I want you, little girl--to help me play it.
passages.vernacular: 「所以我才要你啊,小姑娘——幫我玩呢個遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以我才要你啊,小姑娘——幫我玩這個遊戲。

passages.original: Will you come?”
passages.vernacular: 你嚟不嚟?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你來不來?」

passages.original: Pollyanna turned in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜驚訝地轉過身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜驚訝地轉過身。

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton, you don't really mean--that?”
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓先生,你唔係真嘅——嗰個意思吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓先生,你不是真的——那個意思吧?」

passages.original: “But I do.
passages.vernacular: 「我係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是真的。

passages.original: I want you.
passages.vernacular: 我要你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要你。

passages.original: Will you come?”
passages.vernacular: 你嚟不嚟?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你來不來?」

passages.original: Pollyanna looked distressed.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜面露難色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜面露難色。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, I can't--you know I can't.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我唔能夠——你知道我唔能夠。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我不能——你知道我不能。

passages.original: Why, I'm--Aunt Polly's!”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,我係——波莉姨媽嘅人呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,我是——波莉姨媽的人呀!」

passages.original: A quick something crossed the man's face that Pollyanna could not quite understand.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人臉上飛快地掠過一種波莉安娜不太明白嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人臉上飛快地掠過一種波莉安娜不太明白的神情。

passages.original: His head came up almost fiercely.
passages.vernacular: 佢幾乎係兇狠地抬起咗頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他幾乎是兇狠地抬起了頭。

passages.original: “You're no more hers than--Perhaps she would let you come to me,” he finished more gently.
passages.vernacular: 「你并不比——或者佢會讓你到我呢度嚟。」佢講完,語氣溫和咗些,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你并不比——也許她會讓你到我這裡來。」他說完,語氣溫和了些,

passages.original: “Would you come--if she did?”
passages.vernacular: 「要係佢同意喇,你嚟嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「要是她同意了,你來嗎?」

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned in deep thought.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜皺起眉頭,陷入沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜皺起眉頭,陷入沉思。

passages.original: “But Aunt Polly has been so--good to me,” she began slowly; “and she took me when I didn't have anybody left but the Ladies' Aid, and--”
passages.vernacular: 「不過波莉姨媽對我一直咁——好,」佢慢慢地開口,「而且喺我除咗濟貧會嘅太太哋之外一個人都冇嘅時候,係佢收留咗我,仲有——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是波莉姨媽對我一直那麼——好,」她慢慢地開口,「而且在我除了濟貧會的太太們之外一個人也沒有的時候,是她收留了我,還有——」

passages.original: Again that spasm of something crossed the man's face; but this time, when he spoke, his voice was low and very sad.
passages.vernacular: 嗰陣唔知係乜嘢嘅抽動再次掠過嗰人嘅臉;不過呢一次,佢開口時聲音好低,而且好悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那陣不知是什麼的抽動再次掠過那人的臉;不過這一次,他開口時聲音很低,而且十分悲傷。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, long years ago I loved somebody very much.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,好多年以前,我曾深深愛過一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,很多年以前,我曾深深愛過一個人。

passages.original: I hoped to bring her, some day, to this house.
passages.vernacular: 我希望有一天能把佢帶到呢座房子裡嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望有一天能把她帶到這座房子裡來。

passages.original: I pictured how happy we'd be together in our home all the long years to come.”
passages.vernacular: 我想象住往後漫長嘅歲月裡,我哋喺自己嘅家裡會幾咁幸福。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想象著往後漫長的歲月裡,我們在自己的家裡會多麼幸福。」

passages.original: “Yes,” pitied Pollyanna, her eyes shining with sympathy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯。」波莉安娜同情地講,眼裡閃住同情嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯。」波莉安娜同情地說,眼裡閃著同情的光。

passages.original: “But--well, I didn't bring her here.
passages.vernacular: 「不過——我冇把佢帶到呢兒嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是——我沒有把她帶到這兒來。

passages.original: Never mind why.
passages.vernacular: 唔使問點解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不用問為什麼。

passages.original: I just didn't that's all.
passages.vernacular: 我就係冇,就咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是沒有,就這樣。

passages.original: And ever since then this great gray pile of stone has been a house--never a home.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰以後,呢座灰色嘅大石頭房子就一直只係一座房子——從來唔係一個家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那以後,這座灰色的大石頭房子就一直只是一座房子——從來不是一個家。

passages.original: It takes a woman's hand and heart, or a child's presence, to make a home, Pollyanna; and I have not had either.
passages.vernacular: 要有女人嘅手同心,或者細路嘅在場,才能造出一個家,波莉安娜;而呢兩樣我都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要有女人的手和心,或者孩子的在場,才能造出一個家,波莉安娜;而這兩樣我都沒有。

passages.original: Now will you come, my dear?”
passages.vernacular: 而家你嚟不嚟,親愛嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你來不來,親愛的?」

passages.original: Pollyanna sprang to her feet.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜一下子跳咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜一下子跳了起來。

passages.original: Her face was fairly illumined.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉簡直亮咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉簡直亮了起來。

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton, you--you mean that you wish you--you had had that woman's hand and heart all this time?”
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓先生,你——你係講,你希望你——咁多年嚟都能擁有嗰個女人嘅手同心嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓先生,你——你是說,你希望你——這麼多年來都能擁有那個女人的手和心嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, y-yes, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 「呃,係、係嘅,波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「呃,是、是的,波莉安娜。」

passages.original: “Oh, I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我太高興喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我太高興了!

passages.original: Then it's all right,” sighed the little girl.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就一切都好喇。」小姑娘嘆道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就一切都好了。」小姑娘嘆道,

passages.original: “Now you can take us both, and everything will be lovely.”
passages.vernacular: 「而家你可以把我哋倆都接去,一切就都美滿喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在你可以把我們倆都接去,一切就都美滿了。」

passages.original: “Take--you--both?” repeated the man, dazedly.
passages.vernacular: 「把——你哋——兩個?」嗰人茫然地重複道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「把——你們——兩個?」那人茫然地重複道。

passages.original: A faint doubt crossed Pollyanna's countenance.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜臉上掠過一絲淡淡嘅疑惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜臉上掠過一絲淡淡的疑惑。

passages.original: “Well, of course, Aunt Polly isn't won over, yet; but I'm sure she will be if you tell it to her just as you did to me, and then we'd both come, of course.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,當然,波莉姨媽而家仲冇被講服;不過我相信,只要你像對我講嘅嗰樣告訴佢,佢會同意嘅,嗰我哋倆當然就都嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,當然,波莉姨媽現在還沒被說服;不過我相信,只要你像對我說的那樣告訴她,她會同意的,那我們倆當然就都來了。」

passages.original: A look of actual terror leaped to the man's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人眼裡閃過一絲真正嘅恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人眼裡閃過一絲真正的恐懼。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly come--HERE!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽嚟——呢度!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽來——這裡!」

passages.original: Pollyanna's eyes widened a little.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅眼睛睜大咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的眼睛睜大了一點。

passages.original: “Would you rather go THERE?” she asked.
passages.vernacular: 「你更愿意去嗰邊嗎?」佢問,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你更愿意去那邊嗎?」她問,

passages.original: “Of course the house isn't quite so pretty, but it's nearer--”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,嗰座房子冇咁漂亮,不過佢離得近啲——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,那座房子沒有這麼漂亮,不過它離得近一些——」

passages.original: “Pollyanna, what ARE you talking about?” asked the man, very gently now.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,你到底喺講乜嘢?」嗰人問,呢陣語氣已經好溫和喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,你到底在說什麼?」那人問,這時語氣已經十分溫和了。

passages.original: “Why, about where we're going to live, of course,” rejoined Pollyanna, in obvious surprise.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,就係我哋要住喺邊兒呀。」波莉安娜明顯好詫異地回答,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,就是我們要住在哪兒呀。」波莉安娜明顯很詫異地回答,

passages.original: “I THOUGHT you meant here, at first.
passages.vernacular: 「我起先仲以為你講嘅係呢度呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我起先還以為你說的是這裡呢。

passages.original: You said it was here that you had wanted Aunt Polly's hand and heart all these years to make a home, and--”
passages.vernacular: 你講咁多年嚟,你一直想要波莉姨媽嘅手同心,嚟把呢度變成一個家,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說這麼多年來,你一直想要波莉姨媽的手和心,來把這裡變成一個家,而且——」

passages.original: An inarticulate cry came from the man's throat.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人喉嚨裡發出一聲含混不清嘅叫聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人喉嚨裡發出一聲含混不清的叫聲。

passages.original: He raised his hand and began to speak; but the next moment he dropped his hand nervelessly at his side.
passages.vernacular: 佢舉起手,想要講話;不過下一刻,佢嘅手無力地垂落喺身側。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他舉起手,想要說話;可是下一刻,他的手無力地垂落在身側。

passages.original: “The doctor, sir,” said the maid in the doorway.
passages.vernacular: 「醫生來喇,先生。」門口嘅女仆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「醫生來了,先生。」門口的女仆說。

passages.original: Pollyanna rose at once.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜即刻站咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜立刻站了起來。

passages.original: John Pendleton turned to her feverishly.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓激動地轉向佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓激動地轉向她。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, for Heaven's sake, say nothing of what I asked you--yet,” he begged, in a low voice.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,睇喺老天嘅份上,我問你嘅事先別對任何人講,」佢壓低聲音懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,看在老天的份上,我問你的事先別對任何人說,」他壓低聲音懇求道。

passages.original: Pollyanna dimpled into a sunny smile.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜露出咗甜甜嘅笑容,酒窩浮現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜露出了甜甜的笑容,酒窩浮現。

passages.original: “Of course not!
passages.vernacular: 「當然唔會!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不會!

passages.original: Just as if I didn't know you'd rather tell her yourself!” she called back merrily over her shoulder.
passages.vernacular: 好像我唔知道你寧愿自己告訴佢似嘅!」佢回頭快活地喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好像我不知道你寧愿自己告訴她似的!」她回頭快活地喊道。

passages.original: John Pendleton fell limply back in his chair.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓無力地癱回椅子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓無力地癱回椅子裡。

passages.original: “Why, what's up?” demanded the doctor, a minute later, his fingers on his patient's galloping pulse.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,點回事?」過咗一會兒醫生問道,手指按喺病人狂跳嘅脈搏上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,怎麼回事?」過了一會兒醫生問道,手指按在病人狂跳的脈搏上。

passages.original: A whimsical smile trembled on John Pendleton's lips.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓嘴角顫動住浮起一絲異想天開嘅笑意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓嘴角顫動著浮起一絲異想天開的笑意。

passages.original: “Overdose of your--tonic, I guess,” he laughed, as he noted the doctor's eyes following Pollyanna's little figure down the driveway.
passages.vernacular: 「大概係你嘅——補藥食多咗吧。」佢笑住講,睇到醫生嘅目光正追隨住波莉安娜嘅小身影沿車道遠去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「大概是你的——補藥吃多了吧。」他笑著說,看到醫生的目光正追隨著波莉安娜的小身影沿車道遠去。

chapters.title: Ch. XX Which Is More Surprising 第二十章:更加出人意料

passages.original: CH Sunday mornings Pollyanna usually attended church and Sunday school.
passages.vernacular: 星期天上午,波莉安娜通常去教堂同主日學校。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期天上午,波莉安娜通常去教堂和主日學校。

passages.original: Sunday afternoons she frequently went for a walk with Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 星期天下午,佢常同南希出去散步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 星期天下午,她常和南希出去散步。

passages.original: She had planned one for the day after her Saturday afternoon visit to Mr. John Pendleton; but on the way home from Sunday school Dr. Chilton overtook her in his gig, and brought his horse to a stop.
passages.vernacular: 佢本來計劃喺星期六下午拜訪約翰·潘德爾頓先生之後嘅第二天去散步;不過從主日學校回家嘅路上,奇爾頓醫生駕住雙輪馬車追上咗佢,勒住咗馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本來計劃在星期六下午拜訪約翰·潘德爾頓先生之後的第二天去散步;可是從主日學校回家的路上,奇爾頓醫生駕著雙輪馬車追上了她,勒住了馬。

passages.original: “Suppose you let me drive you home, Pollyanna,” he suggested.
passages.vernacular: 「讓我送你回家吧,波莉安娜,」佢提議道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我送你回家吧,波莉安娜,」他提議道,

passages.original: “I want to speak to you a minute.
passages.vernacular: 「我想跟你講幾句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想跟你說幾句話。

passages.original: I, was just driving out to your place to tell you,” he went on, as Pollyanna settled herself at his side.
passages.vernacular: 我正要去你家告訴你呢。」波莉安娜喺佢身旁坐好後,佢接住講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我正要去你家告訴你呢。」波莉安娜在他身旁坐好後,他接著說,

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton sent a special request for you to go to see him this afternoon, SURE.
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓先生特地捎話,要你今日下午務必去睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓先生特地捎話,要你今天下午務必去看他。

passages.original: He says it's very important.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講有好重要嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說有很重要的事。」

passages.original: Pollyanna nodded happily.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜高興地點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜高興地點點頭。

passages.original: “Yes, it is, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道好重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道很重要。

passages.original: I'll go.”
passages.vernacular: 我會去嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會去的。」

passages.original: The doctor eyed her with some surprise.
passages.vernacular: 醫生有些驚訝地打量佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生有些驚訝地打量她。

passages.original: “I'm not sure I shall let you, after all,” he declared, his eyes twinkling.
passages.vernacular: 「我倒不一定仲讓你去喇,」佢講,眼睛閃住光,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我倒不一定還讓你去了,」他說,眼睛閃著光,

passages.original: “You seemed more upsetting than soothing yesterday, young lady.”
passages.vernacular: 「尋日你畀佢嘅感覺,睇來係惹得佢心煩意亂,而唔係安撫佢,小姐。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「昨天你給他的感覺,看來是惹得他心煩意亂,而不是安撫他,小姐。」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜笑了。

passages.original: “Oh, it wasn't me, truly--not really, you know; not so much as it was Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,真嘅唔係我——其實唔係我,你知道;主要係因為波莉姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,真的不是我——其實不是我,你知道;主要是因為波莉姨媽。」

passages.original: The doctor turned with a quick start.
passages.vernacular: 醫生猛地轉過頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生猛地轉過頭。

passages.original: “Your--aunt!” he ejaculated.
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅——姨媽!」佢脫口而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的——姨媽!」他脫口而出。

passages.original: Pollyanna gave a happy little bounce in her seat.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜在座位上高興地蹦咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜在座位上高興地蹦了一下。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: And it's so exciting and lovely, just like a story, you know.
passages.vernacular: 呢事又刺激又美妙,就像故事一樣,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這事又刺激又美妙,就像故事一樣,你知道。

passages.original: I--I'm going to tell you,” she burst out, with sudden decision.
passages.vernacular: 我——我要告訴你,」佢突然下定決心,衝口而出,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我——我要告訴你,」她突然下定決心,衝口而出,

passages.original: “He said not to mention it; but he wouldn't mind your knowing, of course.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講唔好提嘅;不過當然佢唔會介意你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說不要提的;不過當然他不會介意你知道。

passages.original: He meant not to mention it to HER.”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅意思係唔好對佢提。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的意思是不要對她提。」

passages.original: “HER?”
“Yes; Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「對,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: And, of course he WOULD want to tell her himself instead of having me do it--lovers, so!”
passages.vernacular: 而且,佢當然想親自告訴佢,而唔係讓我來講——情人嘛,就係咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,他當然想親自告訴她,而不是讓我來說——情人嘛,就是這樣!」

passages.original: “Lovers!”
passages.vernacular: 「情人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「情人!」

passages.original: As the doctor said the word, the horse started violently, as if the hand that held the reins had given them a sharp jerk.
passages.vernacular: 醫生講出呢個詞嘅時候,馬猛地一驚,好像握住韁繩嘅手狠狠拽咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生說出這個詞的時候,馬猛地一驚,好像握著韁繩的手狠狠拽了一下。

passages.original: “Yes,” nodded Pollyanna, happily.
passages.vernacular: 「對,」波莉安娜高興地點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,」波莉安娜高興地點點頭。

passages.original: “That's the story-part, you see.
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係故事嘅部分,你瞧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是故事的部分,你瞧。

passages.original: I didn't know it till Nancy told me.
passages.vernacular: 我都係南希告訴我才知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也是南希告訴我才知道的。

passages.original: She said Aunt Polly had a lover years ago, and they quarrelled.
passages.vernacular: 佢講波莉姨媽多年前有過一個情人,佢哋吵咗架。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說波莉姨媽多年前有過一個情人,他們吵了架。

passages.original: She didn't know who it was at first.
passages.vernacular: 起先佢唔知道嗰個係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 起先她不知道那是誰。

passages.original: But we've found out now.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家我哋發現喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在我們發現了。

passages.original: It's Mr. Pendleton, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,就係潘德爾頓先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,就是潘德爾頓先生。」

passages.original: The doctor relaxed suddenly, The hand holding the reins fell limply to his lap.
passages.vernacular: 醫生忽然放鬆下嚟。握住韁繩嘅手無力地落喺膝上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生忽然放鬆下來。握著韁繩的手無力地落在膝上。

passages.original: “Oh!
No; I--didn't know,” he said quietly.
passages.vernacular: 不;我——唔知道。」佢平靜地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不;我——不知道。」他平靜地說。

passages.original: Pollyanna hurried on--they were nearing the Harrington homestead.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜急忙接住講——佢哋快到哈靈頓家嘅宅子喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜急忙接著說——他們快到哈靈頓家的宅子了。

passages.original: “Yes; and I'm so glad now.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;我而家可高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;我現在可高興了。

passages.original: It's come out lovely.
passages.vernacular: 結果好極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 結果好極了。

passages.original: Mr. Pendleton asked me to come and live with him, but of course I wouldn't leave Aunt Polly like that--after she'd been so good to me.
passages.vernacular: 潘德爾頓先生要我去跟佢住,但我當然唔能夠嗰樣離開波莉姨媽——佢對我咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潘德爾頓先生要我去跟他住,但我當然不能那樣離開波莉姨媽——她對我那麼好。

passages.original: Then he told me all about the woman's hand and heart that he used to want, and I found out that he wanted it now; and I was so glad!
passages.vernacular: 然後佢把佢從前想要嘅嗰個女人嘅手同心嘅事全告訴咗我,我發現佢而家仲想要;我真高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他把他從前想要的那個女人的手和心的事全告訴了我,我發現他現在還想要;我真高興!

passages.original: For of course if he wants to make up the quarrel, everything will be all right now, and Aunt Polly and I will both go to live there, or else he'll come to live with us.
passages.vernacular: 因為當然,要係佢想彌合呢場爭吵,而家一切就都會好起嚟嘅,我同波莉姨媽會一起去嗰度住,要不佢就搬嚟同我哋住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為當然,要是他想彌合這場爭吵,現在一切就都會好起來的,我和波莉姨媽會一起去那裡住,要不他就搬來和我們住。

passages.original: Of course Aunt Polly doesn't know yet, and we haven't got everything settled; so I suppose that is why he wanted to see me this afternoon, sure.”
passages.vernacular: 當然波莉姨媽仲唔知道,我哋都仲冇把一切談妥;所以我想呢個就係佢今日下午務必要見我嘅原因。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然波莉姨媽還不知道,我們也還沒把一切談妥;所以我想這就是他今天下午務必要見我的原因。」

passages.original: The doctor sat suddenly erect.
passages.vernacular: 醫生猛地坐直咗身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生猛地坐直了身子。

passages.original: There was an odd smile on his lips.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘴角掛住古怪嘅笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他嘴角掛著古怪的笑。

passages.original: “Yes; I can well imagine that Mr. John Pendleton does--want to see you, Pollyanna,” he nodded, as he pulled his horse to a stop before the door.
passages.vernacular: 「對;我完全可以想象,約翰·潘德爾頓先生確實——想見你,波莉安娜。」佢點點頭講住,把馬勒停喺門前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對;我完全可以想象,約翰·潘德爾頓先生確實——想見你,波莉安娜。」他點點頭說著,把馬勒停在門前。

passages.original: “There's Aunt Polly now in the window,” cried Pollyanna; then, a second later: “Why, no, she isn't--but I thought I saw her!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽喺窗口呢。」波莉安娜叫道;隨即一秒鐘後又講:「哎呀,不,佢不喺——可我頭先仲以為睇見佢喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽在窗口呢。」波莉安娜叫道;隨即一秒鐘後又說:「哎呀,不,她不在——可我剛才還以為看見她了!」

passages.original: “No; she isn't there--now,” said the doctor, His lips had suddenly lost their smile.
passages.vernacular: 「不,佢而家不喺嗰兒。」醫生講,佢嘅嘴角驟然失去咗笑意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,她現在不在那兒。」醫生說,他的嘴角驟然失去了笑意。

passages.original: Pollyanna found a very nervous John Pendleton waiting for her that afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天下午,波莉安娜發現一個好緊張嘅約翰·潘德爾頓喺等佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天下午,波莉安娜發現一個非常緊張的約翰·潘德爾頓在等她。

passages.original: “Pollyanna,” he began at once.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,」佢即刻開口講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,」他立刻開口說,

passages.original: “I've been trying all night to puzzle out what you meant by all that, yesterday--about my wanting your Aunt Polly's hand and heart here all those years.
passages.vernacular: 「我整晚都喺琢磨,你尋日嗰番話係乜嘢意思——講我呢啲年一直想要你波莉姨媽嘅手同心嚟到呢兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我整晚都在琢磨,你昨天那番話是什麼意思——說我這些年一直想要你波莉姨媽的手和心來到這兒。

passages.original: What did you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 你係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Why, because you were lovers, you know once; and I was so glad you still felt that way now.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,因為你哋曾經係情人呀,你知道;我好高興你而家仲嗰樣想。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,因為你們曾經是情人呀,你知道;我很高興你現在還那樣想。」

passages.original: “Lovers!--your Aunt Polly and I?”
passages.vernacular: 「情人!——你波莉姨媽同我?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「情人!——你波莉姨媽和我?」

passages.original: At the obvious surprise in the man's voice, Pollyanna opened wide her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 聽到嗰人聲音裡明顯嘅驚訝,波莉安娜睜大咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到那人聲音裡明顯的驚訝,波莉安娜睜大了眼睛。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, Nancy said you were!”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,南希講你哋係嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,南希說你們是的!」

passages.original: The man gave a short little laugh.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人短促地笑咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人短促地笑了一聲。

passages.original: “Indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的嗎!

passages.original: Well, I'm afraid I shall have to say that Nancy--didn't know.”
passages.vernacular: 嗯,恐怕我只好講,南希——唔知道內情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,恐怕我只好說,南希——不知道內情。」

passages.original: “Then you--weren't lovers?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你哋——唔係情人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你們——不是情人?」

passages.original: Pollyanna's voice was tragic with dismay.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅聲音因失望而顯得悲涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的聲音因失望而顯得悲涼。

passages.original: “Never!”
passages.vernacular: 「從來唔係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從來不是!」

passages.original: “And it ISN'T all coming out like a book?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁事情并唔係像書裡寫嘅嗰樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼事情并不是像書裡寫的那樣?」

passages.original: There was no answer.
passages.vernacular: 冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有回答。

passages.original: The man's eyes were moodily fixed out the window.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人憂鬱嘅目光凝固喺窗外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人憂鬱的目光凝固在窗外。

passages.original: “O dear!
passages.vernacular: 「哦天呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦天哪!

passages.original: And it was all going so splendidly,” almost sobbed Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 本來進行得咁好,」波莉安娜幾乎哭咗出嚟,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本來進行得那麼好,」波莉安娜幾乎哭了出來,

passages.original: “I'd have been so glad to come--with Aunt Polly.”
passages.vernacular: 「我本來會好高興去嘅——同波莉姨媽一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我本來會很高興去的——和波莉姨媽一起。」

passages.original: “And you won't--now?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰你而家——不去喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那你現在——不去了?」

passages.original: The man asked the question without turning his head.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人冇轉頭,問出咗呢個問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人沒有轉頭,問出了這個問題。

passages.original: “Of course not!
passages.vernacular: 「當然不去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然不去!

passages.original: I'm Aunt Polly's.”
passages.vernacular: 我係波莉姨媽嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是波莉姨媽的。」

passages.original: The man turned now, almost fiercely.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人呢陣轉過身嚟,幾乎係兇狠嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人這時轉過身來,幾乎是兇狠的。

passages.original: “Before you were hers, Pollyanna, you were--your mother's.
passages.vernacular: 「喺你屬于佢之前,波莉安娜,你係——你母親嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「在你屬于她之前,波莉安娜,你是——你母親的。

passages.original: And--it was your mother's hand and heart that I wanted long years ago.”
passages.vernacular: 而且——多年前我想要嘅,係你母親嘅手同心。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且——多年前我想要的,是你母親的手和心。」

passages.original: “My mother's!”
passages.vernacular: 「我母親嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我母親的!」

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: I had not meant to tell you, but perhaps it's better, after all, that I do--now.”
passages.vernacular: 我本不打算告訴你,不過或者,終究定係而家告訴你比較好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本不打算告訴你,可是也許,終究還是現在告訴你比較好。」

passages.original: John Pendleton's face had grown very white.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓嘅臉變得好蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓的臉變得非常蒼白。

passages.original: He was speaking with evident difficulty.
passages.vernacular: 佢講話顯然好食力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說話顯然很吃力。

passages.original: Pollyanna, her eyes wide and frightened, and her lips parted, was gazing at him fixedly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜睜大驚恐嘅眼睛,嘴唇微張,目不轉睛地望住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜睜大驚恐的眼睛,嘴唇微張,目不轉睛地望著他。

passages.original: “I loved your mother; but she--didn't love me.
passages.vernacular: 「我愛你母親;不過佢——不愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我愛你母親;可是她——不愛我。

passages.original: And after a time she went away with--your father.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一陣子,佢跟——你父親走喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一陣子,她跟——你父親走了。

passages.original: I did not know until then how much I did--care.
passages.vernacular: 直到嗰時我才知道自己有幾咁在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到那時我才知道自己有多麼在乎。

passages.original: The whole world suddenly seemed to turn black under my fingers, and--But, never mind.
passages.vernacular: 整個世界突然喺我嘅指間變成咗黑色,而且——不過,冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個世界突然在我的指間變成了黑色,而且——不過,沒關係。

passages.original: For long years I have been a cross, crabbed, unlovable, unloved old man--though I'm not nearly sixty, yet, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 多年嚟我一直係個脾氣壞、愛發牢騷、讓人無法鍾意、都冇人鍾意嘅老頭——雖然我仲唔到六十歲,波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多年來我一直是個脾氣壞、愛發牢騷、讓人無法喜歡、也沒人喜歡的老頭——雖然我還不到六十歲,波莉安娜。

passages.original: Then, One day, like one of the prisms that you love so well, little girl, you danced into my life, and flecked my dreary old world with dashes of the purple and gold and scarlet of your own bright cheeriness.
passages.vernacular: 後來,有一天,像你咁喜愛嘅棱鏡一樣,小姑娘,你跳舞般闖進咗我嘅生活,用你自己明亮歡快嘅紫色、金色同猩紅色,畀我嗰荒涼嘅舊世界點綴上咗斑斕嘅色彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來,有一天,像你那麼喜愛的棱鏡一樣,小姑娘,你跳舞般闖進了我的生活,用你自己明亮歡快的紫色、金色和猩紅色,給我那荒涼的舊世界點綴上了斑斕的色彩。

passages.original: I found out, after a time, who you were, and--and I thought then I never wanted to see you again.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一陣子,我發現咗你係邊個,而且——而且我當時想我再都唔想見你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一陣子,我發現了你是誰,而且——而且我當時想我再也不想見你。

passages.original: I didn't want to be reminded of--your mother.
passages.vernacular: 我唔想被提醒起——你母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不想被提醒起——你母親。

passages.original: But--you know how that came out.
passages.vernacular: 但係——你知道後來點樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是——你知道後來怎麼樣了。

passages.original: I just had to have you come.
passages.vernacular: 我就係非讓你嚟不可。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就是非讓你來不可。

passages.original: And now I want you always.
passages.vernacular: 而家我要你永遠喺我身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我要你永遠在我身邊。

passages.original: Pollyanna, won't you come NOW?”
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜,你而家嚟好不好?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜,你現在來好不好?」

passages.original: “But, Mr. Pendleton, I--There's Aunt Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,潘德爾頓先生,我——波莉姨媽喺嗰兒!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,潘德爾頓先生,我——波莉姨媽在那兒!」

passages.original: Pollyanna's eyes were blurred with tears.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅眼睛因淚水而模糊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的眼睛因淚水而模糊。

passages.original: The man made an impatient gesture.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人做咗個不耐煩嘅手勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人做了個不耐煩的手勢。

passages.original: “What about me?
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我呢?

passages.original: How do you suppose I'm going to be 'glad' about anything--without you?
passages.vernacular: 你以為冇你,我點能對任何事情『高興』得起嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你以為沒有你,我怎麼能對任何事情『高興』得起來?

passages.original: Why, Pollyanna, it's only since you came that I've been even half glad to live!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉安娜,自從你嚟咗以後,我才至少有一半嘅時候樂意活住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉安娜,自從你來了以後,我才至少有一半的時候樂意活著!

passages.original: But if I had you for my own little girl, I'd be glad for--anything; and I'd try to make you glad, too, my dear.
passages.vernacular: 不過如果我有你做我自己嘅小姑娘,我乜嘢事都會高興;而且我都會設法讓你高興,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是如果我有你做我自己的小姑娘,我什麼事都會高興;而且我也會設法讓你高興,親愛的。

passages.original: You shouldn't have a wish ungratified.
passages.vernacular: 你唔會有任何愿望得唔到滿足。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不會有任何愿望得不到滿足。

passages.original: All my money, to the last cent, should go to make you happy.”
passages.vernacular: 我所有嘅錢,一分不剩,都會用嚟讓你幸福。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我所有的錢,一分不剩,都會用來讓你幸福。」

passages.original: Pollyanna looked shocked.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜顯得好震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜顯得很震驚。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, as if I'd let you spend it on me--all that money you've saved for the heathen!”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我點會讓你把錢花喺我身上——嗰個係你為異教徒存下嚟嘅錢呀!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我怎麼會讓你把錢花在我身上——那是你為異教徒存下來的錢呀!」

passages.original: A dull red came to the man's face.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人臉上泛起一陣暗紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人臉上泛起一陣暗紅。

passages.original: He started to speak, but Pollyanna was still talking.
passages.vernacular: 佢想開口,不過波莉安娜仲喺講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想開口,可是波莉安娜還在說。

passages.original: “Besides, anybody with such a lot of money as you have doesn't need me to make you glad about things.
passages.vernacular: 「再講,有咁多錢嘅人,不需要我嚟讓你對事情高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再說,有這麼多錢的人,不需要我來讓你對事情高興。

passages.original: You're making other folks so glad giving them things that you just can't help being glad yourself!
passages.vernacular: 你畀別人嘢,讓別人咁高興,你自己都會忍不住高興嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你給別人東西,讓別人那麼高興,你自己也會忍不住高興的!

passages.original: Why, look at those prisms you gave Mrs. Snow and me, and the gold piece you gave Nancy on her birthday, and--”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,睇睇你畀斯諾太太同我嘅嗰啲棱鏡,仲有你喺南希生日時畀佢嘅金幣,仲有——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,看看你給斯諾太太和我的那些棱鏡,還有你在南希生日時給她的金幣,還有——」

passages.original: “Yes, yes--never mind about all that,” interrupted the man.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇——別提嗰啲喇。」嗰人打斷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了——別提那些了。」那人打斷道。

passages.original: His face was very, very red now--and no wonder, perhaps: it was not for “giving things” that John Pendleton had been best known in the past.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉而家紅得厲害——都難怪:過去嘅約翰·潘德爾頓,最出名嘅可唔係「送嘢」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的臉現在紅得厲害——也難怪:過去的約翰·潘德爾頓,最出名的可不是「送東西」。

passages.original: “That's all nonsense.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰都係胡講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那都是胡說。

passages.original: 'Twasn't much, anyhow--but what there was, was because of you.
passages.vernacular: 反正冇多少——就算有啲,都係因為你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正沒多少——就算有一點,也是因為你。

passages.original: YOU gave those things; not I!
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲嘢係你送嘅;唔係我!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些東西是你送的;不是我!

passages.original: Yes, you did,” he repeated, in answer to the shocked denial in her face.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,係你,」佢睇到佢臉上震驚否認嘅神情,又重複咗一遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,是你,」他看到她臉上震驚否認的神情,又重複了一遍。

passages.original: “And that only goes to prove all the more how I need you, little girl,” he added, his voice softening into tender pleading once more.
passages.vernacular: 「呢恰恰更證明了我幾咁需要你,小姑娘,」佢補充道,聲音又軟咗下嚟,變成溫柔嘅懇求。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這恰恰更證明了我多麼需要你,小姑娘,」他補充道,聲音又軟了下來,變成溫柔的懇求。

passages.original: “If ever, ever I am to play the 'glad game,' Pollyanna, you'll have to come and play it with me.”
passages.vernacular: 「如果我有一天真要玩『高興遊戲』,波莉安娜,你就得嚟同我一起玩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「如果我有一天真要玩『高興遊戲』,波莉安娜,你就得來和我一起玩。」

passages.original: The little girl's forehead puckered into a wistful frown.
passages.vernacular: 小姑娘嘅額頭皺成咗一個惆悵嘅愁容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姑娘的額頭皺成了一個惆悵的愁容。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly has been so good to me,” she began; but the man interrupted her sharply.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽對我一直咁好,」佢開口講;不過嗰人尖銳地打斷咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽對我一直那麼好,」她開口說;可是那人尖銳地打斷了她。

passages.original: The old irritability had come back to his face.
passages.vernacular: 往日嘅煩躁又回到咗佢嘅臉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 往日的煩躁又回到了他的臉上。

passages.original: Impatience which would brook no opposition had been a part of John Pendleton's nature too long to yield very easily now to restraint.
passages.vernacular: 唔容反對嘅急躁,已成為約翰·潘德爾頓天性嘅一部分太久,而家唔會輕易屈從于克制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不容反對的急躁,已成為約翰·潘德爾頓天性的一部分太久,現在不會輕易屈從于克制。

passages.original: “Of course she's been good to you!
passages.vernacular: 「佢當然對你好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她當然對你好!

passages.original: But she doesn't want you, I'll warrant, half so much as I do,” he contested.
passages.vernacular: 不過我敢保證,佢要你嘅心思,不及我嘅一半。」佢爭辯道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我敢保證,她要你的心思,不及我的一半。」他爭辯道。

passages.original: “Why, Mr. Pendleton, she's glad, I know, to have--”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我知道佢樂意有——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,潘德爾頓先生,我知道她樂意有——」

passages.original: “Glad!” interrupted the man, thoroughly losing his patience now.
passages.vernacular: 「樂意!」嗰人徹底失去耐心,打斷佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「樂意!」那人徹底失去耐心,打斷她。

passages.original: “I'll wager Miss Polly doesn't know how to be glad--for anything!
passages.vernacular: 「我敢打賭波莉小姐根本唔知道點樣為任何事情高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我敢打賭波莉小姐根本不知道怎樣為任何事情高興!

passages.original: Oh, she does her duty, I know.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我知道佢盡佢嘅責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我知道她盡她的責任。

passages.original: She's a very DUTIFUL woman.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個好盡職嘅女人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她是個非常盡職的女人。

passages.original: I've had experience with her 'duty,' before.
passages.vernacular: 我以前領教過佢嘅『責任』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前領教過她的『責任』。

passages.original: I'll acknowledge we haven't been the best of friends for the last fifteen or twenty years.
passages.vernacular: 我承認,過去十五年或二十年嚟,我哋唔係乜嘢好朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認,過去十五年或二十年來,我們不是什麼好朋友。

passages.original: But I know her.
passages.vernacular: 不過我了解佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我了解她。

passages.original: Every one knows her--and she isn't the 'glad' kind, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 每個人都了解佢——佢唔係嗰種『高興』嘅人,波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個人都了解她——她不是那種『高興』的人,波莉安娜。

passages.original: She doesn't know how to be.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔知道該點高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不知道該怎麼高興。

passages.original: As for your coming to me--you just ask her and see if she won't let you come.
passages.vernacular: 至于你到我呢度嚟嘅事——你就去問問佢,睇佢會唔會讓你嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至于你到我這裡來的事——你就去問問她,看她會不會讓你來。

passages.original: And, oh, little girl, little girl, I want you so!” he finished brokenly.
passages.vernacular: 哦,小姑娘,小姑娘,我幾咁想要你啊!」佢語不成聲地講完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,小姑娘,小姑娘,我多麼想要你啊!」他語不成聲地說完。

passages.original: Pollyanna rose to her feet with a long sigh.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜長嘆一聲,站咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜長嘆一聲,站了起來。

passages.original: “All right.
passages.vernacular: 「好吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧。

passages.original: I'll ask her,” she said wistfully.
passages.vernacular: 我去問佢。」佢惆悵地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我去問她。」她惆悵地說。

passages.original: “Of course I don't mean that I wouldn't like to live here with you, Mr. Pendleton, but--” She did not complete her sentence.
passages.vernacular: 「當然我唔係講我不愿意同你住喺呢度,潘德爾頓先生,不過——」佢冇把話講完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然我不是說我不愿意和你住在這裡,潘德爾頓先生,可是——」她沒有把話說完。

passages.original: There was a moment's silence, then she added: “Well, anyhow, I'm glad I didn't tell her yesterday;--'cause then I supposed SHE was wanted, too.”
passages.vernacular: 沉默咗片刻,然後佢補充道:「嗯,不管點樣,我好高興我尋日冇告訴佢;——因為嗰時我以為佢都被需要。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默了片刻,然後她補充道:「嗯,不管怎樣,我很高興我昨天沒告訴她;——因為那時我以為她也被需要。」

passages.original: John Pendleton smiled grimly.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓苦笑咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓苦笑了一下。

passages.original: “Well, yes, Pollyanna; I guess it is just as well you didn't mention it--yesterday.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係啊,波莉安娜;我想你尋日冇提,倒都正好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是啊,波莉安娜;我想你昨天沒提,倒也正好。」

passages.original: “I didn't--only to the doctor; and of course he doesn't count.”
passages.vernacular: 「我冇講——只跟醫生講過;當然佢不算數。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我沒說——只跟醫生說過;當然他不算數。」

passages.original: “The doctor!” cried John Pendleton, turning quickly.
passages.vernacular: 「醫生!」約翰·潘德爾頓猛地轉頭叫道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「醫生!」約翰·潘德爾頓猛地轉頭叫道,

passages.original: “Not--Dr.--Chilton?”
passages.vernacular: 「唔會係——奇爾頓——醫生吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會是——奇爾頓——醫生吧?」

passages.original: “Yes; when he came to tell me you wanted to see me to-day, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅;就係佢嚟告訴我你今日想見我嘅時候,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的;就是他來告訴我你今天想見我的時候,你知道。」

passages.original: “Well, of all the--” muttered the man, falling back in his chair.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,真係嘅——」嗰人喃喃道,往後癱喺椅子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,真是的——」那人喃喃道,往後癱在椅子裡。

passages.original: Then he sat up with sudden interest.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢突然嚟咗興趣,坐直咗身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後他突然來了興趣,坐直了身子。

passages.original: “And what did Dr. Chilton say?” he asked.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰奇爾頓醫生講乜嘢喇?」佢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那奇爾頓醫生說什麼了?」他問。

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned thoughtfully.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜若有所思地皺起眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜若有所思地皺起眉頭。

passages.original: “Why, I don't remember.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我不記得喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我不記得了。

passages.original: Not much, I reckon.
passages.vernacular: 我想冇講多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想沒說多少。

passages.original: Oh, he did say he could well imagine you did want to see me.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,佢係講佢完全能想象你確實想見我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,他是說他完全能想象你確實想見我。」

passages.original: “Oh, did he, indeed!” answered John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢真咁講喇!」約翰·潘德爾頓答道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他真這麼說了!」約翰·潘德爾頓答道。

passages.original: And Pollyanna wondered why he gave that sudden queer little laugh.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜納悶,佢點解突然發出嗰種古怪嘅小笑聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜納悶,他為什麼突然發出那種古怪的小笑聲。

chapters.title: Ch. XXI A Question Answered 第二十一章:問題有了答案

passages.original: CH The sky was darkening fast with what appeared to be an approaching thunder shower when Pollyanna hurried down the hill from John Pendleton's house.
passages.vernacular: 當波莉安娜匆匆從約翰·潘德爾頓嘅房子跑下山時,天色迅速暗咗下嚟,睇樣子係一場雷陣雨要嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當波莉安娜匆匆從約翰·潘德爾頓的房子跑下山時,天色迅速暗了下來,看樣子是一場雷陣雨要來了。

passages.original: Half-way home she met Nancy with an umbrella.
passages.vernacular: 走到半路,佢遇見咗攞住傘嘅南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走到半路,她遇見了拿著傘的南希。

passages.original: By that time, however, the clouds had shifted their position and the shower was not so imminent.
passages.vernacular: 可嗰時雲已經挪咗位置,雷雨都冇咁迫喺眉睫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可那時雲已經挪了位置,雷雨也沒那麼迫在眉睫了。

passages.original: “Guess it's goin' 'round ter the north,” announced Nancy, eyeing the sky critically.
passages.vernacular: 「睇來係往北邊去喇。」南希挑剔地打量住天空,宣布道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看來是往北邊去了。」南希挑剔地打量著天空,宣布道。

passages.original: “I thought 'twas, all the time, but Miss Polly wanted me ter come with this.
passages.vernacular: 「我一直覺得係,可波莉小姐非要我攞呢個嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一直覺得是,可波莉小姐非要我拿這個來。

passages.original: She was WORRIED about ye!”
passages.vernacular: 佢可擔心你喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她可擔心你了!」

passages.original: “Was she?” murmured Pollyanna abstractedly, eyeing the clouds in her turn.
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?」波莉安娜心不喺焉地喃喃道,輪到佢打量嗰啲雲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?」波莉安娜心不在焉地喃喃道,輪到她打量那些雲。

passages.original: Nancy sniffed a little.
passages.vernacular: 南希哼咗一聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希哼了一聲。

passages.original: “You don't seem ter notice what I said,” she observed aggrievedly.
passages.vernacular: 「你好像冇留意我講嘅話。」佢委屈地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你好像沒留意我說的話。」她委屈地說。

passages.original: “I said yer aunt was WORRIED about ye!”
passages.vernacular: 「我講你姨媽擔心你喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說你姨媽擔心你了!」

passages.original: “Oh,” sighed Pollyanna, remembering suddenly the question she was so soon to ask her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,」波莉安娜嘆咗口氣,突然想起自己不久就要問姨媽嘅嗰個問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,」波莉安娜嘆了口氣,突然想起自己不久就要問姨媽的那個問題。

passages.original: “I'm sorry.
passages.vernacular: 「對不起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對不起。

passages.original: I didn't mean to scare her.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔係故意嚇佢嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是故意嚇她的。」

passages.original: “Well, I'm glad,” retorted Nancy, unexpectedly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我倒高興。」南希出人意料地回嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我倒高興。」南希出人意料地回嘴。

passages.original: “I am, I am.”
passages.vernacular: 「我高興,我高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我高興,我高興。」

passages.original: Pollyanna stared.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜愣住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜愣住了。

passages.original: “GLAD that Aunt Polly was scared about me!
passages.vernacular: 「你高興波莉姨媽為我擔心害怕!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你高興波莉姨媽為我擔心害怕!

passages.original: Why, Nancy, THAT isn't the way to play the game--to be glad for things like that!” she objected.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,南希,為呢種事高興,可唔係玩嗰個遊戲嘅方式!」佢反對道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,南希,為這種事高興,可不是玩那個遊戲的方式!」她反對道。

passages.original: “There wa'n't no game in it,” retorted Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「呢度頭冇遊戲。」南希回嘴,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這裡頭沒有遊戲。」南希回嘴,

passages.original: “Never thought of it.
passages.vernacular: 「我壓根冇想過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我壓根沒想過。

passages.original: YOU don't seem ter sense what it means ter have Miss Polly WORRIED about ye, child!”
passages.vernacular: 你好像不明白,細路,波莉小姐替你擔心係乜嘢意思!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你好像不明白,孩子,波莉小姐替你擔心是什麼意思!」

passages.original: “Why, it means worried--and worried is horrid--to feel,” maintained Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,意思就係擔心——擔心嘅感覺好糟糕呀。」波莉安娜堅持講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,意思就是擔心——擔心的感覺很糟糕呀。」波莉安娜堅持說,

passages.original: “What else can it mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「仲能有乜嘢別嘅意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還能有什麼別的意思?」

passages.original: Nancy tossed her head.
passages.vernacular: 南希把頭一甩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希把頭一甩。

passages.original: “Well, I'll tell ye what it means.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我告訴你呢意思係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我告訴你這意思是什麼。

passages.original: It means she's at last gettin' down somewheres near human--like folks; an' that she ain't jest doin' her duty by ye all the time.”
passages.vernacular: 意思係佢終于變得有點像人喇——像別嘅人一樣;意思係佢不光係一直喺對你盡責任。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 意思是她終于變得有點像人了——像別的人一樣;意思是她不光是一直在對你盡責任。」

passages.original: “Why, Nancy,” demurred the scandalized Pollyanna, “Aunt Polly always does her duty.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,南希,」嚇咗一跳嘅波莉安娜反駁道,「波莉姨媽總是盡佢嘅責任嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,南希,」嚇了一跳的波莉安娜反駁道,「波莉姨媽總是盡她的責任的。

passages.original: She--she's a very dutiful woman!”
passages.vernacular: 佢——佢係個好盡職嘅女人!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她——她是個非常盡職的女人!」

passages.original: Unconsciously Pollyanna repeated John Pendleton's words of half an hour before.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜無意中重複咗半小時前約翰·潘德爾頓嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜無意中重複了半小時前約翰·潘德爾頓的話。

passages.original: Nancy chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 南希咯咯地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希咯咯地笑了。

passages.original: “You're right she is--and she always was, I guess!
passages.vernacular: 「你講得對,佢係——佢一向都係,我想!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你說得對,她是——她一向都是,我想!

passages.original: But she's somethin' more, now, since you came.”
passages.vernacular: 可自從你嚟咗以後,佢仲多咗點別嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可自從你來了以後,她還多了點別的。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's face changed.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅臉色變喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的臉色變了。

passages.original: Her brows drew into a troubled frown.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眉頭擰成咗煩惱嘅皺紋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眉頭擰成了煩惱的皺紋。

passages.original: “There, that's what I was going to ask you, Nancy,” she sighed.
passages.vernacular: 「對喇,呢正是我想問你嘅,南希,」佢嘆道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對了,這正是我想問你的,南希,」她嘆道,

passages.original: “Do you think Aunt Polly likes to have me here?
passages.vernacular: 「你覺得波莉姨媽鍾意我喺呢度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你覺得波莉姨媽喜歡我在這裡嗎?

passages.original: Would she mind--if if I wasn't here any more?”
passages.vernacular: 要係我不喺呢兒喇,佢會在意嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是我不在這兒了,她會在意嗎?」

passages.original: Nancy threw a quick look into the little girl's absorbed face.
passages.vernacular: 南希飛快地瞥咗一眼小姑娘專注嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希飛快地瞥了一眼小姑娘專注的臉。

passages.original: She had expected to be asked this question long before, and she had dreaded it.
passages.vernacular: 佢早就料到會被問呢個問題,并且一直害怕住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她早就料到會被問這個問題,并且一直害怕著。

passages.original: She had wondered how she should answer it--how she could answer it honestly without cruelly hurting the questioner.
passages.vernacular: 佢曾經苦苦思量該點回答——點才能既誠實又不殘忍地傷害提問嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她曾經苦苦思量該怎麼回答——怎麼才能既誠實又不殘忍地傷害提問的人。

passages.original: But now, NOW, in the face of the new suspicions that had become convictions by the afternoon's umbrella-sending--Nancy only welcomed the question with open arms.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家,而家,面對下午送傘呢件事讓佢嘅新懷疑變成咗確信——南希張開雙臂歡迎呢個問題。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是現在,現在,面對下午送傘這件事讓她的新懷疑變成了確信——南希張開雙臂歡迎這個問題。

passages.original: She was sure that, with a clean conscience to-day, she could set the love-hungry little girl's heart at rest.
passages.vernacular: 佢確信,今日佢可以問心無愧地讓呢個渴望愛嘅小姑娘嘅心安定下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她確信,今天她可以問心無愧地讓這個渴望愛的小姑娘的心安定下來。

passages.original: “Likes ter have ye here?
passages.vernacular: 「鍾意你喺呢兒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「喜歡你在這兒?

passages.original: Would she miss ye if ye wa'n't here?” cried Nancy, indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 你不喺咗佢會想你嗎?」南希憤憤地喊道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不在了她會想你嗎?」南希憤憤地喊道,

passages.original: “As if that wa'n't jest what I was tellin' of ye!
passages.vernacular: 「好像我頭先跟你講嘅不就係呢個似嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像我剛才跟你說的不就是這個似的!

passages.original: Didn't she send me posthaste with an umbrella 'cause she see a little cloud in the sky?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係因為睇見天上有一小朵雲,就急急忙忙差我攞傘去嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不是因為看見天上有一小朵雲,就急急忙忙差我拿傘去嗎?

passages.original: Didn't she make me tote yer things all down-stairs, so you could have the pretty room you wanted?
passages.vernacular: 佢唔係叫我把你嘅嘢全搬到樓下,好讓你住上你想要嘅漂亮房間嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她不是叫我把你的東西全搬到樓下,好讓你住上你想要的漂亮房間嗎?

passages.original: Why, Miss Pollyanna, when ye remember how at first she hated ter have--”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉安娜小姐,你想想,佢起先幾咁不愿意有——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉安娜小姐,你想想,她起先多麼不愿意有——」

passages.original: With a choking cough Nancy pulled herself up just in time.
passages.vernacular: 南希嗆咳咗一聲,及時剎住咗口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希嗆咳了一聲,及時剎住了口。

passages.original: “And it ain't jest things I can put my fingers on, neither,” rushed on Nancy, breathlessly.
passages.vernacular: 「而且都不光係我能指出嚟嘅嗰啲事,」南希氣喘吁吁地接住講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且也不光是我能指出來的那些事,」南希氣喘吁吁地接著說,

passages.original: “It's little ways she has, that shows how you've been softenin' her up an' mellerin' her down--the cat, and the dog, and the way she speaks ter me, and oh, lots o' things.
passages.vernacular: 「係佢嗰啲小小嘅表現,講明你一直喺讓佢軟下嚟、變溫和——貓啊,狗啊,仲有佢跟我講話嘅方式,哦,仲有好多好多事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是她那些小小的表現,說明你一直在讓她軟下來、變溫和——貓啊,狗啊,還有她跟我說話的方式,哦,還有好多好多事。

passages.original: Why, Miss Pollyanna, there ain't no tellin' how she'd miss ye--if ye wa'n't here,” finished Nancy, speaking with an enthusiastic certainty that was meant to hide the perilous admission she had almost made before.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉安娜小姐,要係你不喺呢兒,邊個都講不準佢會多想你,」南希滿懷熱情、好肯定地講完,係想要掩飾佢頭先差點講漏嘅嗰個危險嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉安娜小姐,要是你不在這兒,誰也說不準她會多想你,」南希滿懷熱情、十分肯定地說完,是想要掩飾她剛才差點說漏的那個危險的話。

passages.original: Even then she was not quite prepared for the sudden joy that illumined Pollyanna's face.
passages.vernacular: 即便如此,佢都冇料到波莉安娜臉上會驟然煥發出嗰樣嘅喜悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即便如此,她也沒有料到波莉安娜臉上會驟然煥發出那樣的喜悅。

passages.original: “Oh, Nancy, I'm so glad--glad--glad!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,南希,我真高興——高興——高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,南希,我真高興——高興——高興!

passages.original: You don't know how glad I am that Aunt Polly--wants me!”
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道我多高興,波莉姨媽——需要我!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道我多高興,波莉姨媽——需要我!」

passages.original: “As if I'd leave her now!” thought Pollyanna, as she climbed the stairs to her room a little later.
passages.vernacular: 「我點會而家就離開佢呢!」稍後爬上樓梯回房間時,波莉安娜想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我怎麼會現在就離開她呢!」稍後爬上樓梯回房間時,波莉安娜想。

passages.original: “I always knew I wanted to live with Aunt Polly--but I reckon maybe I didn't know quite how much I wanted Aunt Polly--to want to live with ME!”
