passages.vernacular: 「我一直知道我想同波莉姨媽住喺一起——可我想我以前并不太清楚,我有多希望波莉姨媽——都想同我住喺一起!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我一直知道我想和波莉姨媽住在一起——可我想我以前并不太清楚,我有多希望波莉姨媽——也想和我住在一起!」

passages.original: The task of telling John Pendleton of her decision would not be an easy one, Pollyanna knew, and she dreaded it.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜知道,把自己嘅決定告訴約翰·潘德爾頓并唔係件容易嘅事,佢好怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜知道,把自己的決定告訴約翰·潘德爾頓并不是件容易的事,她很怕。

passages.original: She was very fond of John Pendleton, and she was very sorry for him--because he seemed to be so sorry for himself.
passages.vernacular: 佢好鍾意約翰·潘德爾頓,都好同情佢——因為佢似乎對自己咁同情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她非常喜歡約翰·潘德爾頓,也很同情他——因為他似乎對自己那麼同情。

passages.original: She was sorry, too, for the long, lonely life that had made him so unhappy; and she was grieved that it had been because of her mother that he had spent those dreary years.
passages.vernacular: 佢都同情嗰漫長孤獨嘅歲月,係佢使佢如此不快樂;佢仲為佢係因為佢母親才度過嗰啲凄涼歲月而感到難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也同情那漫長孤獨的歲月,是它使他如此不快樂;她還為他是因為她母親才度過那些凄涼歲月而感到難過。

passages.original: She pictured the great gray house as it would be after its master was well again, with its silent rooms, its littered floors, its disordered desk; and her heart ached for his loneliness.
passages.vernacular: 佢想象住嗰座灰色嘅大房子喺主人康復以後嘅樣子,空蕩寂靜嘅房間、雜亂嘅地板、凌亂嘅書桌;佢嘅心為佢嘅孤單而疼痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想象著那座灰色的大房子在主人康復以後的樣子,空蕩寂靜的房間、雜亂的地板、凌亂的書桌;她的心為他的孤單而疼痛。

passages.original: She wished that somewhere, some one might be found who--And it was at this point that she sprang to her feet with a little cry of joy at the thought that had come to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢希望喺某個地方,能找到某個人,可以——就喺呢陣,佢想到咗乜嘢,高興地叫咗一聲,一下子跳咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她希望在某個地方,能找到某個人,可以——就在這時,她想到了什麼,高興地叫了一聲,一下子跳了起來。

passages.original: As soon as she could, after that, she hurried up the hill to John Pendleton's house; and in due time she found herself in the great dim library, with John Pendleton himself sitting near her, his long, thin hands lying idle on the arms of his chair, and his faithful little dog at his feet.
passages.vernacular: 此後佢一得空,就匆匆爬上山到約翰·潘德爾頓嘅房子去;不一會兒,佢就嚟到咗昏暗寬敞嘅大書房,約翰·潘德爾頓本人坐喺佢身邊,修長瘦削嘅雙手閑擱喺椅子扶手上,佢忠實嘅小狗伏喺佢腳邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此後她一得空,就匆匆爬上山到約翰·潘德爾頓的房子去;不一會兒,她就來到了昏暗寬敞的大書房,約翰·潘德爾頓本人坐在她身邊,修長瘦削的雙手閑擱在椅子扶手上,他忠實的小狗伏在他腳邊。

passages.original: “Well, Pollyanna, is it to be the 'glad game' with me, all the rest of my life?” asked the man, gently.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,波莉安娜,我呢後半輩子,係唔係都要同『高興遊戲』為伴喇?」嗰人溫和地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,波莉安娜,我這後半輩子,是不是都要和『高興遊戲』為伴了?」那人溫和地問。

passages.original: “Oh, yes,” cried Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」波莉安娜叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」波莉安娜叫道。

passages.original: “I've thought of the very gladdest kind of a thing for you to do, and--”
passages.vernacular: 「我想到一件最高興嘅事讓你做,而且——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想到一件最高興的事讓你做,而且——」

passages.original: “With--YOU?” asked John Pendleton, his mouth growing a little stern at the corners.
passages.vernacular: 「同——你?」約翰·潘德爾頓問,嘴角微微繃緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「和——你?」約翰·潘德爾頓問,嘴角微微繃緊。

passages.original: “N-no; but--”
passages.vernacular: 「不、唔係;不過——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不、不是;可是——」

passages.original: “Pollyanna, you aren't going to say no!” interrupted a voice deep with emotion.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,你唔會講不吧!」一個飽含感情嘅聲音打斷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,你不會說不吧!」一個飽含感情的聲音打斷道。

passages.original: “I--I've got to, Mr. Pendleton; truly I have.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我必須咁樣,潘德爾頓先生;真嘅必須。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我必須這樣,潘德爾頓先生;真的必須。

passages.original: Aunt Polly--”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽——」

passages.original: “Did she REFUSE--to let you--come?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢係唔係拒絕——讓你——嚟?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她是不是拒絕——讓你——來?」

passages.original: “I--I didn't ask her,” stammered the little girl, miserably.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我冇問佢,」小姑娘不安地結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我沒問她,」小姑娘不安地結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜!」

passages.original: Pollyanna turned away her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜轉開咗視線。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜轉開了視線。

passages.original: She could not meet the hurt, grieved gaze of her friend.
passages.vernacular: 佢無法面對朋友嗰受傷而悲傷嘅目光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她無法面對朋友那受傷而悲傷的目光。

passages.original: “So you didn't even ask her!”
passages.vernacular: 「咁講你連問都冇問佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說你連問都沒問她!」

passages.original: “I couldn't, sir--truly,” faltered Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠,先生——真嘅,」波莉安娜支支吾吾地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能,先生——真的,」波莉安娜支支吾吾地說。

passages.original: “You see, I found out--without asking.
passages.vernacular: 「你瞧,我發現喇——唔使問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你瞧,我發現了——不用問。

passages.original: Aunt Polly WANTS me with her, and--and I want to stay, too,” she confessed bravely.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽需要我留喺佢身邊,而且——而且我都想留下,」佢勇敢地坦白道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽需要我留在她身邊,而且——而且我也想留下,」她勇敢地坦白道。

passages.original: “You don't know how good she's been to me; and--and I think, really, sometimes she's beginning to be glad about things--lots of things.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔知道佢對我多好;而且——而且我真嘅覺得,有時候佢開始對啲事情高興喇——好多好多事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不知道她對我多好;而且——而且我真的覺得,有時候她開始對一些事情高興了——好多好多事。

passages.original: And you know she never used to be.
passages.vernacular: 而且你知道佢以前從來唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且你知道她以前從來不會。

passages.original: You said it yourself.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係你自己講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是你自己說的。

passages.original: Oh, Mr. Pendleton, I COULDN'T leave Aunt Polly--now!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,潘德爾頓先生,我而家唔能夠離開波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,潘德爾頓先生,我現在不能離開波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: There was a long pause.
passages.vernacular: 沉默咗好久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默了很久。

passages.original: Only the snapping of the wood fire in the grate broke the silence.
passages.vernacular: 只有爐柵裡木柴噼啪嘅燃燒聲打破寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有爐柵裡木柴噼啪的燃燒聲打破寂靜。

passages.original: At last, however, the man spoke.
passages.vernacular: 不過,嗰人終于開口喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,那人終于開口了。

passages.original: “No, Pollyanna; I see.
passages.vernacular: 「不,波莉安娜;我明白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,波莉安娜;我明白了。

passages.original: You couldn't leave her--now,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 你而家唔能夠離開佢,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在不能離開她,」他說。

passages.original: “I won't ask you--again.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔會再問你喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不會再問你了。」

passages.original: The last word was so low it was almost inaudible; but Pollyanna heard.
passages.vernacular: 最後一個詞低得幾乎聽唔見;不過波莉安娜聽到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一個詞低得幾乎聽不見;可是波莉安娜聽到了。

passages.original: “Oh, but you don't know about the rest of it,” she reminded him eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,不過你仲唔知道後面嘅事呢,」佢急切地提醒佢,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,可是你還不知道後面的事呢,」她急切地提醒他,

passages.original: “There's the very gladdest thing you CAN do--truly there is!”
passages.vernacular: 「你可以做一件最高興嘅事——真嘅有!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你可以做一件最高興的事——真的有!」

passages.original: “Not for me, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 「對我來講冇,波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對我來說沒有,波莉安娜。」

passages.original: “Yes, sir, for you.
passages.vernacular: 「有嘅,先生,對你來講有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有的,先生,對你來說有。

passages.original: You SAID it.
passages.vernacular: 係你講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是你說的。

passages.original: You said only a--a woman's hand and heart or a child's presence could make a home.
passages.vernacular: 你講只有女人嘅手同心,或者細路嘅在場,才能造出一個家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說只有女人的手和心,或者孩子的在場,才能造出一個家。

passages.original: And I can get it for you--a child's presence;--not me, you know, but another one.”
passages.vernacular: 而我可以畀你找到——一個細路嘅在場;——唔係我,你知道,係另一個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我可以給你找到——一個孩子的在場;——不是我,你知道,是另一個。」

passages.original: “As if I would have any but you!” resented an indignant voice.
passages.vernacular: 「好像我會要你以外嘅任何人似嘅!」一個憤憤不平嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像我會要你以外的任何人似的!」一個憤憤不平的聲音說。

passages.original: “But you will--when you know; you're so kind and good!
passages.vernacular: 「不過你會要嘅——等你知道喇;你咁善良!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是你會要的——等你知道了;你那麼善良!

passages.original: Why, think of the prisms and the gold pieces, and all that money you save for the heathen, and--”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,想想嗰啲棱鏡同金幣,仲有你為異教徒存嘅嗰啲錢,仲有——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,想想那些棱鏡和金幣,還有你為異教徒存的那些錢,還有——」

passages.original: “Pollyanna!” interrupted the man, savagely.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜!」嗰人兇狠地打斷道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜!」那人兇狠地打斷道,

passages.original: “Once for all let us end that nonsense!
passages.vernacular: 「讓我哋一勞永逸地結束呢種胡講!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓我們一勞永逸地結束這種胡說!

passages.original: I've tried to tell you half a dozen times before.
passages.vernacular: 我以前已經試住告訴過你五六次喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以前已經試著告訴過你五六次了。

passages.original: There is no money for the heathen.
passages.vernacular: 根本冇畀異教徒嘅錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 根本沒有給異教徒的錢。

passages.original: I never sent a penny to them in my life.
passages.vernacular: 我呢輩子從來冇畀佢哋寄過一分錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這輩子從來沒給他們寄過一分錢。

passages.original: There!”
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣!」

passages.original: He lifted his chin and braced himself to meet what he expected--the grieved disappointment of Pollyanna's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢抬起下巴,挺直身子,準備迎接佢預料中嘅——波莉安娜眼中嗰失望悲傷嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他抬起下巴,挺直身子,準備迎接他預料中的——波莉安娜眼中那失望悲傷的神情。

passages.original: To his amazement, however, there was neither grief nor disappointment in Pollyanna's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 可令佢驚訝嘅係,波莉安娜嘅眼中既冇悲傷,都冇失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可令他驚訝的是,波莉安娜的眼中既沒有悲傷,也沒有失望。

passages.original: There was only surprised joy.
passages.vernacular: 只有驚喜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只有驚喜。

passages.original: “Oh, oh!” she cried, clapping her hands.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,哦!」佢拍著手叫道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,哦!」她拍著手叫道,

passages.original: “I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 「我真高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真高興!

passages.original: That is,” she corrected, coloring distressfully, “I don't mean that I'm not sorry for the heathen, only just now I can't help being glad that you don't want the little India boys, because all the rest have wanted them.
passages.vernacular: 我係講,」佢窘迫地紅住臉更正道,「我唔係講我不為異教徒難過,只係而家我忍不住高興你唔想要嗰啲印度小男孩,因為別嘅人都想要佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是說,」她窘迫地紅著臉更正道,「我不是說我不為異教徒難過,只是現在我忍不住高興你不想要那些印度小男孩,因為別的人都想要他們。

passages.original: And so I'm glad you'd rather have Jimmy Bean.
passages.vernacular: 所以我高興你寧愿要吉米·比恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我高興你寧愿要吉米·比恩。

passages.original: Now I know you'll take him!”
passages.vernacular: 而家我知道你會收養佢喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我知道你會收養他了!」

passages.original: “Take--WHO?”
passages.vernacular: 「收養——邊個?」

passages.original: “Jimmy Bean.
passages.vernacular: 「吉米·比恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉米·比恩。

passages.original: He's the 'child's presence,' you know; and he'll be so glad to be it.
passages.vernacular: 佢就係嗰個『細路嘅在場』,你知道;佢會好高興當呢個人嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他就是那個『孩子的在場』,你知道;他會非常高興當這個人的。

passages.original: I had to tell him last week that even my Ladies' Aid out West wouldn't take him, and he was so disappointed.
passages.vernacular: 上星期我唔得不告訴佢,連我西部嗰邊嘅濟貧會太太哋都唔肯收養佢,佢好失望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期我不得不告訴他,連我西部那邊的濟貧會太太們都不肯收養他,他很失望。

passages.original: But now--when he hears of this--he'll be so glad!”
passages.vernacular: 不過而家——等佢聽到呢件事——佢會多高興啊!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是現在——等他聽到這件事——他會多高興啊!」

passages.original: “Will he?
passages.vernacular: 「佢會嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他會嗎?

passages.original: Well, I won't,” ejaculated the man, decisively.
passages.vernacular: 可我唔會。」嗰人斷然脫口而出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可我不會。」那人斷然脫口而出。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, this is sheer nonsense!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,呢完全係胡講八道!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,這完全是胡說八道!」

passages.original: “You don't mean--you won't take him?”
passages.vernacular: 「你唔係講——你唔會收養佢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不是說——你不會收養他?」

passages.original: “I certainly do mean just that.”
passages.vernacular: 「我正是呢個意思。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我正是這個意思。」

passages.original: “But he'd be a lovely child's presence,” faltered Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢會係一個好可愛嘅細路嘅在場,」波莉安娜支吾住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是他會是一個很可愛的孩子的在場,」波莉安娜支吾著說。

passages.original: She was almost crying now.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家幾乎要哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在幾乎要哭了。

passages.original: “And you COULDN'T be lonesome--with Jimmy 'round.”
passages.vernacular: 「而且有吉米喺身邊,你唔可能會寂寞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且有吉米在身邊,你不可能會寂寞。」

passages.original: “I don't doubt it,” rejoined the man; “but--I think I prefer the lonesomeness.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不懷疑,」嗰人回答,「不過——我想我寧愿要寂寞。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不懷疑,」那人回答,「可是——我想我寧愿要寂寞。」

passages.original: It was then that Pollyanna, for the first time in weeks, suddenly remembered something Nancy had once told her.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣,波莉安娜數星期嚟第一次突然想起咗南希曾經對佢講過嘅一件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時,波莉安娜數星期來第一次突然想起了南希曾經對她說過的一件事。

passages.original: She raised her chin aggrievedly.
passages.vernacular: 佢委屈地抬起下巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她委屈地抬起下巴。

passages.original: “Maybe you think a nice live little boy wouldn't be better than that old dead skeleton you keep somewhere; but I think it would!”
passages.vernacular: 「或者你覺得一個活潑可愛嘅小男孩比不上你藏喺乜嘢地方嘅嗰具死骷髏;可我覺得會比佢強!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許你覺得一個活潑可愛的小男孩比不上你藏在什麼地方的那具死骷髏;可我覺得會比它強!」

passages.original: “SKELETON?”
passages.vernacular: 「骷髏?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「骷髏?」

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: Nancy said you had one in your closet, somewhere.”
passages.vernacular: 南希講你喺壁櫥裡乜嘢地方藏住一具。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希說你在壁櫥裡什麼地方藏著一具。」

passages.original: “Why, what--” Suddenly the man threw back his head and laughed.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,乜嘢——」嗰人突然仰起頭大笑起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,什麼——」那人突然仰起頭大笑起來。

passages.original: He laughed very heartily indeed--so heartily that Pollyanna began to cry from pure nervousness.
passages.vernacular: 佢笑得真嘅好開懷——開懷得波莉安娜因為純粹嘅緊張而哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他笑得真的非常開懷——開懷得波莉安娜因為純粹的緊張而哭了起來。

passages.original: When he saw that, John Pendleton sat erect very promptly.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓見狀,即刻坐直咗身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓見狀,立刻坐直了身子。

passages.original: His face grew grave at once.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉頓時嚴肅起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的臉頓時嚴肅起來。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, I suspect you are right--more right than you know,” he said gently.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,我想你係對嘅——比你所知道嘅仲要對,」佢溫和地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,我想你是對的——比你所知道的還要對,」他溫和地說。

passages.original: “In fact, I KNOW that a 'nice live little boy' would be far better than--my skeleton in the closet; only--we aren't always willing to make the exchange.
passages.vernacular: 「其實,我知道『一個活潑可愛嘅小男孩』,要比我壁櫥裡嘅骷髏好得多;只係——我哋并不總是愿意做呢個交換。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「其實,我知道『一個活潑可愛的小男孩』,要比我壁櫥裡的骷髏好得多;只是——我們并不總是愿意做這個交換。

passages.original: We are apt to still cling to--our skeletons, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 我哋往往仍舊緊抱住——我哋嘅骷髏不放,波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們往往仍舊緊抱著——我們的骷髏不放,波莉安娜。

passages.original: However, suppose you tell me a little more about this nice little boy.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,你不如再多跟我講講呢個可愛嘅小男孩吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,你不如再多跟我講講這個可愛的小男孩吧。」

passages.original: And Pollyanna told him.
passages.vernacular: 于係波莉安娜講畀佢聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 于是波莉安娜講給他聽。

passages.original: Perhaps the laugh cleared the air; or perhaps the pathos of Jimmy Bean's story as told by Pollyanna's eager little lips touched a heart already strangely softened.
passages.vernacular: 或者係嗰陣笑聲凈化咗空氣;或者係波莉安娜用急切嘅小嘴講述嘅吉米·比恩嘅故事中嘅辛酸,觸動咗一顆已經奇妙地軟化咗嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許是那陣笑聲凈化了空氣;也許是波莉安娜用急切的小嘴講述的吉米·比恩的故事中的辛酸,觸動了一顆已經奇妙地軟化了的心。

passages.original: At all events, when Pollyanna went home that night she carried with her an invitation for Jimmy Bean himself to call at the great house with Pollyanna the next Saturday afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 總之,當波莉安娜嗰晚回家時,佢帶住一份邀請:請吉米·比恩本人下星期六下午跟波莉安娜一起到嗰座大房子去拜訪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,當波莉安娜那晚回家時,她帶著一份邀請:請吉米·比恩本人下星期六下午跟波莉安娜一起到那座大房子去拜訪。

passages.original: “And I'm so glad, and I'm sure you'll like him,” sighed Pollyanna, as she said good-by.
passages.vernacular: 「我真高興,而且我相信你會鍾意佢,」波莉安娜講住告別道,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真高興,而且我相信你會喜歡他,」波莉安娜說著告別道,

passages.original: “I do so want Jimmy Bean to have a home--and folks that care, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望吉米·比恩有個家——有在乎佢嘅人,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望吉米·比恩有個家——有在乎他的人,你知道。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXII Sermons and Woodboxes 第二十二章:講道與柴箱

passages.original: CH On the afternoon that Pollyanna told John Pendleton of Jimmy Bean, the Rev. Paul Ford climbed the hill and entered the Pendleton Woods, hoping that the hushed beauty of God's out-of-doors would still the tumult that His children of men had wrought.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜把吉米·比恩嘅事告訴約翰·潘德爾頓嘅嗰天下午,保羅·福特牧師爬上山,走進咗潘德爾頓樹林,希望上帝戶外世界嘅靜謐之美,能平息祂嘅世人造成嘅喧囂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜把吉米·比恩的事告訴約翰·潘德爾頓的那天下午,保羅·福特牧師爬上山,走進了潘德爾頓樹林,希望上帝戶外世界的靜謐之美,能平息祂的世人造成的喧囂。

passages.original: The Rev. Paul Ford was sick at heart.
passages.vernacular: 保羅·福特牧師心裡難受極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保羅·福特牧師心裡難受極了。

passages.original: Month by month, for a year past, conditions in the parish under him had been growing worse and worse; until it seemed that now, turn which way he would, he encountered only wrangling, backbiting, scandal, and jealousy.
passages.vernacular: 一年嚟,佢所牧養嘅教區狀況一個月比一個月糟;到如今,似乎無論佢轉向邊度,遇到嘅都只有爭吵、背後中傷、醜聞同嫉妒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一年來,他所牧養的教區狀況一個月比一個月糟;到如今,似乎無論他轉向哪裡,遇到的都只有爭吵、背後中傷、醜聞和嫉妒。

passages.original: He had argued, pleaded, rebuked, and ignored by turns; and always and through all he had prayed--earnestly, hopefully.
passages.vernacular: 佢輪番地勸講、懇求、責備、不理會;而且始終,喺呢一切之中,佢都喺祈禱——懇切地、滿懷希望地祈禱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他輪番地勸說、懇求、責備、不理會;而且始終,在這一切之中,他都在祈禱——懇切地、滿懷希望地祈禱。

passages.original: But to-day miserably he was forced to own that matters were no better, but rather worse.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日,佢痛苦地唔得不承認,情況并冇好轉,反而更糟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是今天,他痛苦地不得不承認,情況并沒有好轉,反而更糟了。

passages.original: Two of his deacons were at swords' points over a silly something that only endless brooding had made of any account.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅兩位執事為了一件愚蠢嘅小事針鋒相對,而嗰件事本來冇乜嘢要緊,全係冇完冇咗地琢磨才變得似乎重要起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的兩位執事為了一件愚蠢的小事針鋒相對,而那件事本來沒什麼要緊,全是沒完沒了地琢磨才變得似乎重要起來。

passages.original: Three of his most energetic women workers had withdrawn from the Ladies' Aid Society because a tiny spark of gossip had been fanned by wagging tongues into a devouring flame of scandal.
passages.vernacular: 佢最能幹嘅三位女工作者退出咗濟貧會,因為一星期裡一丁點兒閑話被長舌婦哋煽成咗吞噬一切嘅醜聞烈火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他最能幹的三位女工作者退出了濟貧會,因為一星期裡一丁點兒閑話被長舌婦們煽成了吞噬一切的醜聞烈火。

passages.original: The choir had split over the amount of solo work given to a fanciedly preferred singer.
passages.vernacular: 唱詩班因為分畀一位被認為受偏愛嘅歌手嘅獨唱太多而分裂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唱詩班因為分給一位被認為受偏愛的歌手的獨唱太多而分裂了。

passages.original: Even the Christian Endeavor Society was in a ferment of unrest owing to open criticism of two of its officers.
passages.vernacular: 就連基督徒奮進會都因公開批評兩位職員而陷入騷動不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就連基督徒奮進會也因公開批評兩位職員而陷入騷動不安。

passages.original: As to the Sunday school--it had been the resignation of its superintendent and two of its teachers that had been the last straw, and that had sent the harassed minister to the quiet woods for prayer and meditation.
passages.vernacular: 至于主日學校——佢嘅校長同兩位教師辭職,成咗壓垮駱駝嘅最後一根稻草,都把呢位焦頭爛額嘅牧師送進咗寧靜嘅樹林裡禱告沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至于主日學校——它的校長和兩位教師辭職,成了壓垮駱駝的最後一根稻草,也把這位焦頭爛額的牧師送進了寧靜的樹林裡禱告沉思。

passages.original: Under the green arch of the trees the Rev. Paul Ford faced the thing squarely.
passages.vernacular: 喺綠色嘅樹拱之下,保羅·福特牧師直面呢件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在綠色的樹拱之下,保羅·福特牧師直面這件事。

passages.original: To his mind, the crisis had come.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢睇來,危機已經到來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他看來,危機已經到來。

passages.original: Something must be done--and done at once.
passages.vernacular: 必須採取行動——而且要即刻採取。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 必須採取行動——而且要立刻採取。

passages.original: The entire work of the church was at a standstill.
passages.vernacular: 教會嘅整個事工都陷于停頓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 教會的整個事工都陷于停頓。

passages.original: The Sunday services, the week-day prayer meeting, the missionary teas, even the suppers and socials were becoming less and less well attended.
passages.vernacular: 禮拜日嘅聚會、平日嘅禱告會、傳教士茶會,甚至晚餐會同聯誼會,出席嘅人都越嚟越少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 禮拜日的聚會、平日的禱告會、傳教士茶會,甚至晚餐會和聯誼會,出席的人也越來越少。

passages.original: True, a few conscientious workers were still left.
passages.vernacular: 誠然,仲剩下幾位認真盡責嘅工作者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誠然,還剩下幾位認真盡責的工作者。

passages.original: But they pulled at cross purposes, usually; and always they showed themselves to be acutely aware of the critical eyes all about them, and of the tongues that had nothing to do but to talk about what the eyes saw.
passages.vernacular: 可佢哋通常各行其係;而且佢哋總是顯得敏銳地意識到周圍嗰啲挑剔嘅眼睛,以及嗰啲無事可做、只會議論眼睛所見嘅舌頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可他們通常各行其是;而且他們總是顯得敏銳地意識到周圍那些挑剔的眼睛,以及那些無事可做、只會議論眼睛所見的舌頭。

passages.original: And because of all this, the Rev. Paul Ford understood very well that he (God's minister), the church, the town, and even Christianity itself was suffering; and must suffer still more unless--
passages.vernacular: 正因如此,保羅·福特牧師好清楚,佢(上帝嘅牧師)、教會、小鎮,甚至基督教本身都喺受苦;而且仲會受更多嘅苦,除非——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正因如此,保羅·福特牧師非常清楚,他(上帝的牧師)、教會、小鎮,甚至基督教本身都在受苦;而且還會受更多的苦,除非——

passages.original: Clearly something must be done, and done at once.
passages.vernacular: 顯然必須做點乜嘢,而且要即刻做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 顯然必須做點什麼,而且要立刻做。

passages.original: But what?
passages.vernacular: 不過做乜嘢呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是做什麼呢?

passages.original: Slowly the minister took from his pocket the notes he had made for his next Sunday's sermon.
passages.vernacular: 牧師慢慢從口袋裡掏出為下個星期天講道所做嘅筆記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師慢慢從口袋裡掏出為下個星期天講道所做的筆記。

passages.original: Frowningly he looked at them.
passages.vernacular: 佢皺住眉頭睇住佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他皺著眉頭看著它們。

passages.original: His mouth settled into stern lines, as aloud, very impressively, he read the verses on which he had determined to speak:
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅嘴抿成嚴厲嘅線條,大聲、好有氣勢地念出佢已決定要講嘅經文:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的嘴抿成嚴厲的線條,大聲、很有氣勢地念出他已決定要講的經文:

passages.original: “'But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.'
passages.vernacular: 「『你哋呢啲假冒為善嘅文士同法利賽人有禍喇!因為你哋把天國嘅門關喇,自己不進去,正要進去嘅人,你哋都唔容佢哋進去。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你們這些假冒為善的文士和法利賽人有禍了!因為你們把天國的門關了,自己不進去,正要進去的人,你們也不容他們進去。』

passages.original: “'Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows' houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.'
passages.vernacular: 「『你哋呢啲假冒為善嘅文士同法利賽人有禍喇!因為你哋侵吞寡婦嘅家產,假意作好長嘅禱告,所以你哋要受更重嘅刑罰。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你們這些假冒為善的文士和法利賽人有禍了!因為你們侵吞寡婦的家產,假意作很長的禱告,所以你們要受更重的刑罰。』

passages.original: “'Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.'”
passages.vernacular: 「『你哋呢啲假冒為善嘅文士同法利賽人有禍喇!因為你哋將薄荷、茴香、孜然獻上十分之一,嗰律法上更重嘅事,就係公義、憐憫、信實,反倒不行喇。呢啲原係你哋當行嘅,嗰啲都不可不行。』」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『你們這些假冒為善的文士和法利賽人有禍了!因為你們將薄荷、茴香、孜然獻上十分之一,那律法上更重的事,就是公義、憐憫、信實,反倒不行了。這些原是你們當行的,那些也不可不行。』」

passages.original: It was a bitter denunciation.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一番尖刻嘅譴責。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一番尖刻的譴責。

passages.original: In the green aisles of the woods, the minister's deep voice rang out with scathing effect.
passages.vernacular: 喺綠蔭蔽天嘅林間過道裡,牧師低沉嘅聲音以嚴厲嘅效果響徹四方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在綠蔭蔽天的林間過道裡,牧師低沉的聲音以嚴厲的效果響徹四方。

passages.original: Even the birds and squirrels seemed hushed into awed silence.
passages.vernacular: 連鳥兒同松鼠似乎都被震懾得鴉雀無聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連鳥兒和松鼠似乎也被震懾得鴉雀無聲。

passages.original: It brought to the minister a vivid realization of how those words would sound the next Sunday when he should utter them before his people in the sacred hush of the church.
passages.vernacular: 呢讓牧師鮮明地意識到,下星期天佢喺教會神圣嘅寂靜中,當住會眾嘅面講出呢啲話時,會係乜嘢樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這讓牧師鮮明地意識到,下星期天他在教會神圣的寂靜中,當著會眾的面說出這些話時,會是什麼樣子。

passages.original: His people!--they WERE his people.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅會眾!——佢哋確實係佢嘅會眾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的會眾!——他們確實是他的會眾。

passages.original: Could he do it?
passages.vernacular: 佢能咁樣做嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他能這樣做嗎?

passages.original: Dare he do it?
passages.vernacular: 佢敢咁樣做嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他敢這樣做嗎?

passages.original: Dare he not do it?
passages.vernacular: 佢敢不咁樣做嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他敢不這樣做嗎?

passages.original: It was a fearful denunciation, even without the words that would follow--his own words.
passages.vernacular: 即使不算接下嚟佢自己要講嘅嗰啲話,呢都已經係一番可怕嘅譴責喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使不算接下來他自己要說的那些話,這也已經是一番可怕的譴責了。

passages.original: He had prayed and prayed.
passages.vernacular: 佢已經禱告咗又禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他已經禱告了又禱告。

passages.original: He had pleaded earnestly for help, for guidance.
passages.vernacular: 佢懇切地祈求幫助,祈求指引。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他懇切地祈求幫助,祈求指引。

passages.original: He longed--oh, how earnestly he longed!--to take now, in this crisis, the right step.
passages.vernacular: 佢渴望——哦,佢幾咁懇切地渴望!——喺呢危機時刻,邁出正確嘅一步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他渴望——哦,他多麼懇切地渴望!——在這危機時刻,邁出正確的一步。

passages.original: But was this--the right step?
passages.vernacular: 可呢——係正確嘅一步嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可這——是正確的一步嗎?

passages.original: Slowly the minister folded the papers and thrust them back into his pocket.
passages.vernacular: 牧師慢慢地把紙折好,塞回口袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師慢慢地把紙折好,塞回口袋。

passages.original: Then, with a sigh that was almost a moan, he flung himself down at the foot of a tree, and covered his face with his hands.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢發出一聲幾近呻吟嘅嘆息,倒喺一棵樹腳下,雙手掩面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,他發出一聲幾近呻吟的嘆息,倒在一棵樹腳下,雙手掩面。

passages.original: It was there that Pollyanna, on her way home from the Pendleton house, found him.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜從潘德爾頓家回嚟嘅路上,就係喺嗰度發現咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜從潘德爾頓家回來的路上,就是在那裡發現了他。

passages.original: With a little cry she ran forward.
passages.vernacular: 佢輕呼一聲,跑上前去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她輕呼一聲,跑上前去。

passages.original: “Oh, oh, Mr. Ford!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,哦,福特先生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,哦,福特先生!

passages.original: You--YOU haven't broken YOUR leg or--or anything, have you?” she gasped.
passages.vernacular: 你——你冇摔斷你嘅腿,或者——或者乜嘢吧?」佢喘住氣問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你——你沒有摔斷你的腿,或者——或者什麼吧?」她喘著氣問。

passages.original: The minister dropped his hands, and looked up quickly.
passages.vernacular: 牧師放下雙手,急忙抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師放下雙手,急忙抬起頭來。

passages.original: He tried to smile.
passages.vernacular: 佢勉強笑咗笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他勉強笑了笑。

passages.original: “No, dear--no, indeed!
passages.vernacular: 「冇,親愛嘅——真嘅冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有,親愛的——真的沒有!

passages.original: I'm just--resting.”
passages.vernacular: 我只係——喺休息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只是——在休息。」

passages.original: “Oh,” sighed Pollyanna, falling back a little.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,」波莉安娜嘆咗口氣,稍微退後咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,」波莉安娜嘆了口氣,稍微退後了一點。

passages.original: “That's all right, then.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰就冇事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就沒事了。

passages.original: You see, Mr. Pendleton HAD broken his leg when I found him--but he was lying down, though.
passages.vernacular: 你瞧,我發現潘德爾頓先生嘅時候,佢確實摔斷咗腿——不過佢係躺住嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瞧,我發現潘德爾頓先生的時候,他確實摔斷了腿——不過他是躺著的。

passages.original: And you are sitting up.”
passages.vernacular: 而你係坐住嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你是坐著的。」

passages.original: “Yes, I am sitting up; and I haven't broken anything--that doctors can mend.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我係坐住嘅;而且我乜嘢都冇摔斷——冇醫生能醫好嘅嘢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我是坐著的;而且我什麼也沒摔斷——沒有醫生能醫好的東西。」

passages.original: The last words were very low, but Pollyanna heard them.
passages.vernacular: 最後嘅話講得好低,不過波莉安娜聽見喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後的話說得很低,可是波莉安娜聽見了。

passages.original: A swift change crossed her face.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉上飛快地掠過一陣變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉上飛快地掠過一陣變化。

passages.original: Her eyes glowed with tender sympathy.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛閃住溫柔嘅同情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛閃著溫柔的同情。

passages.original: “I know what you mean--something plagues you.
passages.vernacular: 「我明白你嘅意思——有乜嘢事喺困擾你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明白你的意思——有什麼事在困擾你。

passages.original: Father used to feel like that, lots of times.
passages.vernacular: 爸爸以前都常常有咁樣嘅感覺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 爸爸以前也常常有這樣的感覺。

passages.original: I reckon ministers do--most generally.
passages.vernacular: 我想牧師哋大概都咁樣——大多數時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想牧師們大概都這樣——大多數時候。

passages.original: You see there's such a lot depends on 'em, somehow.”
passages.vernacular: 你瞧,唔知點嘅,有咁多事要靠佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瞧,不知怎麼的,有那麼多事要靠他們。」

passages.original: The Rev. Paul Ford turned a little wonderingly.
passages.vernacular: 保羅·福特牧師有些詫異地轉過身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保羅·福特牧師有些詫異地轉過身來。

passages.original: “Was YOUR father a minister, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅父親係牧師嗎,波莉安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的父親是牧師嗎,波莉安娜?」

passages.original: “Yes, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。

passages.original: Didn't you know?
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道嗎?

passages.original: I supposed everybody knew that.
passages.vernacular: 我仲以為人人都知道呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還以為人人都知道呢。

passages.original: He married Aunt Polly's sister, and she was my mother.”
passages.vernacular: 佢娶咗波莉姨媽嘅妹妹,佢就係我母親。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他娶了波莉姨媽的妹妹,她就是我母親。」

passages.original: “Oh, I understand.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我明白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我明白了。

passages.original: But, you see, I haven't been here many years, so I don't know all the family histories.”
passages.vernacular: 不過,你知道,我嚟呢兒冇幾年,所以不了解所有家族嘅歷史。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,你知道,我來這兒沒有幾年,所以不了解所有家族的歷史。」

passages.original: “Yes, sir--I mean, no, sir,” smiled Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生——我係講,唔係嘅,先生。」波莉安娜微笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生——我是說,不是的,先生。」波莉安娜微笑著說。

passages.original: There was a long pause.
passages.vernacular: 沉默咗好久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默了很久。

passages.original: The minister, still sitting at the foot of the tree, appeared to have forgotten Pollyanna's presence.
passages.vernacular: 牧師依然坐喺樹腳下,似乎已經忘咗波莉安娜在場。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師依然坐在樹腳下,似乎已經忘了波莉安娜在場。

passages.original: He had pulled some papers from his pocket and unfolded them; but he was not looking at them.
passages.vernacular: 佢從口袋裡抽出幾張紙展開,不過并冇喺睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他從口袋裡抽出幾張紙展開,可是并沒有在看。

passages.original: He was gazing, instead, at a leaf on the ground a little distance away--and it was not even a pretty leaf.
passages.vernacular: 佢凝視住稍遠處地上嘅一片葉子——而且嗰甚至唔係一片好睇嘅葉子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他凝視著稍遠處地上的一片葉子——而且那甚至不是一片好看的葉子。

passages.original: It was brown and dead.
passages.vernacular: 佢係褐色嘅,已經枯死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是褐色的,已經枯死。

passages.original: Pollyanna, looking at him, felt vaguely sorry for him.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜望住佢,隱隱地為佢難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜望著他,隱隱地為他難過。

passages.original: “It--it's a nice day,” she began hopefully.
passages.vernacular: 「今——今日天氣真好。」佢滿懷希望地開口喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「今——今天天氣真好。」她滿懷希望地開口了。

passages.original: For a moment there was no answer; then the minister looked up with a start.
passages.vernacular: 有一會兒冇人回答;然後牧師猛地抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一會兒沒人回答;然後牧師猛地抬起頭來。

passages.original: “What?
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼?

passages.original: Oh!--yes, it is a very nice day.”
passages.vernacular: 哦!——係嘅,今日天氣好好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦!——是的,今天天氣很好。」

passages.original: “And 'tisn't cold at all, either, even if 'tis October,” observed Pollyanna, still more hopefully.
passages.vernacular: 「而且啲都不冷,雖然而家係十月。」波莉安娜講,更加滿懷希望喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且一點也不冷,雖然現在是十月。」波莉安娜說,更加滿懷希望了。

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton had a fire, but he said he didn't need it.
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓先生生咗火,不過佢講不需要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓先生生了火,可是他說不需要。

passages.original: It was just to look at.
passages.vernacular: 只係用嚟睇嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是用來看的。

passages.original: I like to look at fires, don't you?”
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意睇火,你呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡看火,你呢?」

passages.original: There was no reply this time, though Pollyanna waited patiently, before she tried again--by a new route.
passages.vernacular: 呢次冇回答,波莉安娜耐心地等咗一會兒,又換咗個新嘅方式試咗試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次沒有回答,波莉安娜耐心地等了一會兒,又換了個新的方式試了試。

passages.original: “Do You like being a minister?”
passages.vernacular: 「你鍾意當牧師嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你喜歡當牧師嗎?」

passages.original: The Rev. Paul Ford looked up now, very quickly.
passages.vernacular: 保羅·福特牧師呢陣好快地抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保羅·福特牧師這時很快地抬起頭來。

passages.original: “Do I like--Why, what an odd question!
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意——哎呀,多奇怪嘅問題!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡——哎呀,多奇怪的問題!

passages.original: Why do you ask that, my dear?”
passages.vernacular: 你點解問呢個,親愛嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼問這個,親愛的?」

passages.original: “Nothing--only the way you looked.
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢——只係你頭先嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒什麼——只是你剛才的樣子。

passages.original: It made me think of my father.
passages.vernacular: 讓我想起咗我爸爸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我想起了我爸爸。

passages.original: He used to look like that--sometimes.”
passages.vernacular: 佢有時候都係嗰個樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有時候也是那個樣子。」

passages.original: “Did he?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?」

passages.original: The minister's voice was polite, but his eyes had gone back to the dried leaf on the ground.
passages.vernacular: 牧師嘅聲音好客氣,不過佢嘅目光又回到咗地上嗰片枯葉上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師的聲音很客氣,可是他的目光又回到了地上那片枯葉上。

passages.original: “Yes, and I used to ask him just as I did you if he was glad he was a minister.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我以前都像問你一樣,問過佢係唔係高興當牧師。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我以前也像問你一樣,問過他是不是高興當牧師。」

passages.original: The man under the tree smiled a little sadly.
passages.vernacular: 樹下嘅男人帶住一絲悲傷微微笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 樹下的男人帶著一絲悲傷微微笑了。

passages.original: “Well--what did he say?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯——佢點講?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯——他怎麼說?」

passages.original: “Oh, he always said he was, of course, but 'most always he said, too, that he wouldn't STAY a minister a minute if 'twasn't for the rejoicing texts.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢總是講高興,當然啦,不過佢幾乎總是仲講,要唔係有嗰啲『歡喜嘅經文』,佢連一分鐘牧師都唔會當下去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他總是說高興,當然啦,可是他幾乎總是還說,要不是有那些『歡喜的經文』,他連一分鐘牧師也不會當下去。」

passages.original: “The--WHAT?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰啲——乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那些——什麼?」

passages.original: The Rev. Paul Ford's eyes left the leaf and gazed wonderingly into Pollyanna's merry little face.
passages.vernacular: 保羅·福特牧師嘅目光離開咗嗰片葉子,驚奇地望住波莉安娜快樂嘅小臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 保羅·福特牧師的目光離開了那片葉子,驚奇地望著波莉安娜快樂的小臉。

passages.original: “Well, that's what father used to call 'em,” she laughed.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,爸爸就係咁叫佢哋嘅,」佢笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,爸爸就是這麼叫它們的,」她笑著說。

passages.original: “Of course the Bible didn't name 'em that.
passages.vernacular: 「當然圣經裡唔係咁稱呼佢哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然圣經裡不是這麼稱呼它們的。

passages.original: But it's all those that begin 'Be glad in the Lord,' or 'Rejoice greatly,' or 'Shout for joy,' and all that, you know--such a lot of 'em.
passages.vernacular: 但嗰都係嗰啲以『你哋要靠主歡喜』,或者『大大歡喜』,或者『歡呼』等等開頭嘅經文,你知道——咁樣嘅經文有好多好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但那都是那些以『你們要靠主歡喜』,或者『大大歡喜』,或者『歡呼』等等開頭的經文,你知道——這樣的經文有好多好多。

passages.original: Once, when father felt specially bad, he counted 'em.
passages.vernacular: 有一回,爸爸特別難受嘅時候,佢數咗數。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一回,爸爸特別難受的時候,他數了數。

passages.original: There were eight hundred of 'em.”
passages.vernacular: 一共有八百條呢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一共有八百條呢。」

passages.original: “Eight hundred!”
passages.vernacular: 「八百條!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「八百條!」

passages.original: “Yes--that told you to rejoice and be glad, you know; that's why father named 'em the 'rejoicing texts.'”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——就係吩咐你要歡喜快樂嘅,你知道;所以爸爸管佢哋叫『歡喜嘅經文』。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——就是吩咐你要歡喜快樂的,你知道;所以爸爸管它們叫『歡喜的經文』。」

passages.original: “Oh!”
There was an odd look on the minister's face.
passages.vernacular: 牧師嘅臉上露出一種奇特嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師的臉上露出一種奇特的神情。

passages.original: His eyes had fallen to the words on the top paper in his hands--“But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅目光落到咗手中最上面嗰張紙嘅字句上——「你哋呢啲假冒為善嘅文士同法利賽人有禍喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的目光落到了手中最上面那張紙的字句上——「你們這些假冒為善的文士和法利賽人有禍了!」

passages.original: “And so your father--liked those 'rejoicing texts,'” he murmured.
passages.vernacular: 「咁講你父親——鍾意嗰啲『歡喜嘅經文』。」佢喃喃地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說你父親——喜歡那些『歡喜的經文』。」他喃喃地說。

passages.original: “Oh, yes,” nodded Pollyanna, emphatically.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅,」波莉安娜用力地點點頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的,」波莉安娜用力地點點頭說。

passages.original: “He said he felt better right away, that first day he thought to count 'em.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講佢第一天想到去數佢哋嘅時候,即刻就覺得好多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說他第一天想到去數它們的時候,馬上就覺得好多了。

passages.original: He said if God took the trouble to tell us eight hundred times to be glad and rejoice, He must want us to do it--SOME.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,如果上帝不厭其煩地告訴我哋八百次要高興、要歡喜,祂一定希望我哋——多少做到啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,如果上帝不厭其煩地告訴我們八百次要高興、要歡喜,祂一定希望我們——多少做到一些。

passages.original: And father felt ashamed that he hadn't done it more.
passages.vernacular: 而爸爸為自己冇做得更多感到慚愧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而爸爸為自己沒做得更多感到慚愧。

passages.original: After that, they got to be such a comfort to him, you know, when things went wrong; when the Ladies' Aiders got to fight--I mean, when they DIDN'T AGREE about something,” corrected Pollyanna, hastily.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰以後,佢哋就成咗佢嘅極大安慰,你知道,喺事情不順嘅時候;喺濟貧會嘅太太哋吵起嚟嘅時候——我係講,喺佢哋對某件事意見不一致嘅時候。」波莉安娜趕忙更正道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那以後,它們就成了他的極大安慰,你知道,在事情不順的時候;在濟貧會的太太們吵起來的時候——我是說,在她們對某件事意見不一致的時候。」波莉安娜趕忙更正道。

passages.original: “Why, it was those texts, too, father said, that made HIM think of the game--he began with ME on the crutches--but he said 'twas the rejoicing texts that started him on it.”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,爸爸講,都係嗰啲經文讓佢想到咗嗰個遊戲——佢係從我攞拐杖嗰件事開始嘅——不過佢講係嗰啲歡喜嘅經文讓佢開始玩嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,爸爸說,也是那些經文讓他想到了那個遊戲——他是從我拿拐杖那件事開始的——不過他說是那些歡喜的經文讓他開始玩的。」

passages.original: “And what game might that be?” asked the minister.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係個乜嘢遊戲呢?」牧師問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是個什麼遊戲呢?」牧師問。

passages.original: “About finding something in everything to be glad about, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「就係喺每件事裡找出可以高興嘅地方,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是在每件事裡找出可以高興的地方,你知道。

passages.original: As I said, he began with me on the crutches.”
passages.vernacular: 就像我講嘅,佢係從我攞拐杖嗰件事開始嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像我說的,他是從我拿拐杖那件事開始的。」

passages.original: And once more Pollyanna told her story--this time to a man who listened with tender eyes and understanding ears.
passages.vernacular: 于係波莉安娜又一次講咗佢嘅故事——呢一次係講畀一個帶住溫柔目光、善解人意地傾聽嘅人聽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 于是波莉安娜又一次講了她的故事——這一次是講給一個帶著溫柔目光、善解人意地傾聽的人聽。

passages.original: A little later Pollyanna and the minister descended the hill, hand in hand.
passages.vernacular: 不久之後,波莉安娜同牧師手拉著手走下山。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不久之後,波莉安娜和牧師手拉著手走下山。

passages.original: Pollyanna's face was radiant.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅臉上洋溢住光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的臉上洋溢著光彩。

passages.original: Pollyanna loved to talk, and she had been talking now for some time: there seemed to be so many, many things about the game, her father, and the old home life that the minister wanted to know.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜愛講話,佢已經講咗好一陣子:關于嗰個遊戲、佢父親、以及老家嘅生活,牧師似乎想知道嘅事情有咁多、咁多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜愛說話,她已經說了好一陣子:關于那個遊戲、她父親、以及老家的生活,牧師似乎想知道的事情有那麼多、那麼多。

passages.original: At the foot of the hill their ways parted, and Pollyanna down one road, and the minister down another, walked on alone.
passages.vernacular: 喺山腳下佢哋分咗手,波莉安娜沿一條路,牧師沿另一條路,各自獨自走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在山腳下他們分了手,波莉安娜沿一條路,牧師沿另一條路,各自獨自走去。

passages.original: In the Rev. Paul Ford's study that evening the minister sat thinking.
passages.vernacular: 嗰天晚上,喺保羅·福特牧師嘅書房裡,牧師坐住沉思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那天晚上,在保羅·福特牧師的書房裡,牧師坐著沉思。

passages.original: Near him on the desk lay a few loose sheets of paper--his sermon notes.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢身旁嘅書桌上,散放住幾張紙——佢嘅講道筆記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他身旁的書桌上,散放著幾張紙——他的講道筆記。

passages.original: Under the suspended pencil in his fingers lay other sheets of paper, blank--his sermon to be.
passages.vernacular: 佢手指間懸住嘅鉛筆下,係另外幾張空白嘅紙——佢將要寫嘅講道稿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他手指間懸著的鉛筆下,是另外幾張空白的紙——他將要寫的講道稿。

passages.original: But the minister was not thinking either of what he had written, or of what he intended to write.
passages.vernacular: 不過牧師想嘅既唔係佢寫下嘅嘢,都唔係佢打算寫嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是牧師想的既不是他寫下的東西,也不是他打算寫的東西。

passages.original: In his imagination he was far away in a little Western town with a missionary minister who was poor, sick, worried, and almost alone in the world--but who was poring over the Bible to find how many times his Lord and Master had told him to “rejoice and be glad.”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅想象力遠遠飛到咗西部嘅一個小鎮,飛到一位貧窮、多病、憂心忡忡、幾乎舉目無親嘅傳教士牧師身邊——而佢卻喺仔細研讀圣經,要找出佢嘅主同師傅有多少次吩咐佢「要歡喜快樂」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的想象力遠遠飛到了西部的一個小鎮,飛到一位貧窮、多病、憂心忡忡、幾乎舉目無親的傳教士牧師身邊——而他卻在仔細研讀圣經,要找出他的主和師傅有多少次吩咐他「要歡喜快樂」。

passages.original: After a time, with a long sigh, the Rev. Paul Ford roused himself, came back from the far Western town, and adjusted the sheets of paper under his hand.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,保羅·福特牧師長嘆一聲,振作起嚟,從遙遠嘅西部小鎮回到現實,把手下嘅紙張整理好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,保羅·福特牧師長嘆一聲,振作起來,從遙遠的西部小鎮回到現實,把手下的紙張整理好。

passages.original: “Matthew twenty-third; 13--14 and 23,” he wrote; then, with a gesture of impatience, he dropped his pencil and pulled toward him a magazine left on the desk by his wife a few minutes before.
passages.vernacular: 「馬太福音二十三章;13—14節同23節,」佢寫下,隨即不耐煩地做咗個手勢,扔下鉛筆,拉過一本佢妻子幾分鐘前留喺書桌上嘅雜誌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「馬太福音二十三章;13—14節和23節,」他寫下,隨即不耐煩地做了個手勢,扔下鉛筆,拉過一本他妻子幾分鐘前留在書桌上的雜誌。

passages.original: Listlessly his tired eyes turned from paragraph to paragraph until these words arrested them:
passages.vernacular: 佢疲倦嘅眼睛無精打采地從一段睇到另一段,直到呢啲話吸引住咗佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他疲倦的眼睛無精打采地從一段看到另一段,直到這些話吸引住了他:

passages.original: “A father one day said to his son, Tom, who, he knew, had refused to fill his mother's woodbox that morning: 'Tom, I'm sure you'll be glad to go and bring in some wood for your mother.'
passages.vernacular: 「一天,一位父親對佢嘅兒子湯姆講——佢知道湯姆嗰天朝早拒絕畀佢母親嘅柴箱裝滿柴:『湯姆,我相信你會好樂意去畀你媽媽抱些柴進嚟。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「一天,一位父親對他的兒子湯姆說——他知道湯姆那天早上拒絕給他母親的柴箱裝滿柴:『湯姆,我相信你會很樂意去給你媽媽抱些柴進來。』

passages.original: And without a word Tom went.
passages.vernacular: 湯姆一句話都冇講就去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 湯姆一句話也沒說就去了。

passages.original: Why?
passages.vernacular: 點解?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼?

passages.original: Just because his father showed so plainly that he expected him to do the right thing.
passages.vernacular: 就因為佢父親嗰樣明顯地表現出,佢期待佢去做正確嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就因為他父親那樣明顯地表現出,他期待他去做正確的事。

passages.original: Suppose he had said: 'Tom, I overheard what you said to your mother this morning, and I'm ashamed of you.
passages.vernacular: 假如父親講嘅係:『湯姆,我聽到你今日朝早跟你媽媽講嘅話喇,我為你感到羞恥。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 假如父親說的是:『湯姆,我聽到你今天早上跟你媽媽說的話了,我為你感到羞恥。

passages.original: Go at once and fill that woodbox!'
passages.vernacular: 即刻去把嗰個柴箱裝滿!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬上去把那個柴箱裝滿!』

passages.original: I'll warrant that woodbox, would be empty yet, so far as Tom was concerned!”
passages.vernacular: 我敢保證,就湯姆而言,嗰個柴箱到而家定係空嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢保證,就湯姆而言,那個柴箱到現在還是空的!」

passages.original: On and on read the minister--a word here, a line there, a paragraph somewhere else:
passages.vernacular: 牧師不停地讀下去——呢度一個詞,嗰度一行,別處一段:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師不停地讀下去——這裡一個詞,那裡一行,別處一段:

passages.original: “What men and women need is encouragement.
passages.vernacular: 「男男女女需要嘅係鼓勵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「男男女女需要的是鼓勵。

passages.original: Their natural resisting powers should be strengthened, not weakened....
passages.vernacular: 應當增強佢哋天生嘅抵抗力,而唔係削弱佢……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 應當增強他們天生的抵抗力,而不是削弱它……

passages.original: Instead of always harping on a man's faults, tell him of his virtues.
passages.vernacular: 唔好總是抓住一個人嘅缺點不放,而要告訴佢佢嘅優點。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要總是抓著一個人的缺點不放,而要告訴他他的優點。

passages.original: Try to pull him out of his rut of bad habits.
passages.vernacular: 設法把佢從壞習慣嘅老套裡拉出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 設法把他從壞習慣的老套裡拉出來。

passages.original: Hold up to him his better self, his REAL self that can dare and do and win out!...
passages.vernacular: 向佢舉起佢更好嘅自己、佢嗰個敢作敢為又能取勝嘅真正自己!……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 向他舉起他更好的自己、他那個敢作敢為又能取勝的真正自己!……

passages.original: The influence of a beautiful, helpful, hopeful character is contagious, and may revolutionize a whole town....
passages.vernacular: 一個美好、肯幫忙、有希望嘅品格,其影響力係有感染性嘅,可以使整個小鎮煥然一新……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個美好、肯幫忙、有希望的品格,其影響力是有感染性的,可以使整個小鎮煥然一新……

passages.original: People radiate what is in their minds and in their hearts.
passages.vernacular: 人哋散發出嘅,係佢哋心裡同頭腦裡所想嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 人們散發出的,是他們心裡和頭腦裡所想的。

passages.original: If a man feels kindly and obliging, his neighbors will feel that way, too, before long.
passages.vernacular: 如果一個人覺得友善、樂于助人,佢嘅鄰居不久都會咁樣覺得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果一個人覺得友善、樂于助人,他的鄰居不久也會這樣覺得。

passages.original: But if he scolds and scowls and criticizes--his neighbors will return scowl for scowl, and add interest!...
passages.vernacular: 但如果佢責罵、皺眉、批評——佢嘅鄰居就會以皺眉仲皺眉,仲要加倍奉仲!……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果他責罵、皺眉、批評——他的鄰居就會以皺眉還皺眉,還要加倍奉還!……

passages.original: When you look for the bad, expecting it, you will get it.
passages.vernacular: 當你尋找壞處、期待壞處時,你就會得到壞處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你尋找壞處、期待壞處時,你就會得到壞處。

passages.original: When you know you will find the good--you will get that....
passages.vernacular: 當你知道你會找到好處時——你就會得到好處……
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當你知道你會找到好處時——你就會得到好處……

passages.original: Tell your son Tom you KNOW he'll be glad to fill that woodbox--then watch him start, alert and interested!”
passages.vernacular: 告訴你嘅兒子湯姆,你知道佢樂意把嗰個柴箱裝滿——然後睇住佢機靈、有興致地動手吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴你的兒子湯姆,你知道他樂意把那個柴箱裝滿——然後看著他機靈、有興致地動手吧!」

passages.original: The minister dropped the paper and lifted his chin.
passages.vernacular: 牧師放下報紙,抬起咗下巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 牧師放下報紙,抬起了下巴。

passages.original: In a moment he was on his feet, tramping the narrow room back and forth, back and forth.
passages.vernacular: 不一會兒,佢站咗起嚟,喺狹窄嘅房間裡嚟回踱步,嚟回踱步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不一會兒,他站了起來,在狹窄的房間裡來回踱步,來回踱步。

passages.original: Later, some time later, he drew a long breath, and dropped himself in the chair at his desk.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一陣,又過咗一陣,佢深深吸咗口氣,坐進書桌前嘅椅子裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一陣,又過了一陣,他深深吸了口氣,坐進書桌前的椅子裡。

passages.original: “God helping me, I'll do it!” he cried softly.
passages.vernacular: 「求上帝幫助我,我會做到嘅!」佢輕聲喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「求上帝幫助我,我會做到的!」他輕聲喊道。

passages.original: “I'll tell all my Toms I KNOW they'll be glad to fill that woodbox!
passages.vernacular: 「我要告訴我所有嘅湯姆哋,我知道佢哋樂意把嗰個柴箱裝滿!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我要告訴我所有的湯姆們,我知道他們樂意把那個柴箱裝滿!

passages.original: I'll give them work to do, and I'll make them so full of the very joy of doing it that they won't have TIME to look at their neighbors' woodboxes!”
passages.vernacular: 我要畀佢哋工作做,我要讓佢哋充滿做呢啲事嘅喜樂,以至于冇時間去睇鄰居嘅柴箱!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要給他們工作做,我要讓他們充滿做這些事的喜樂,以至于沒有時間去看鄰居的柴箱!」

passages.original: And he picked up his sermon notes, tore straight through the sheets, and cast them from him, so that on one side of his chair lay “But woe unto you,” and on the other, “scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites!” while across the smooth white paper before him his pencil fairly flew--after first drawing one black line through Matthew twenty-third; 13--14 and 23.
passages.vernacular: 于係佢攞起講道筆記,一把撕開嗰幾頁紙,扔到一邊,結果椅子嘅一邊躺住「你哋有禍咗」,另一邊躺住「文士同法利賽人,假冒為善嘅!」而佢面前嗰張平整嘅白紙上,鉛筆喺飛快地寫住——喺佢先喺馬太福音二十三章13—14節同23節上劃咗一道黑線之後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 于是他拿起講道筆記,一把撕開那幾頁紙,扔到一邊,結果椅子的一邊躺著「你們有禍了」,另一邊躺著「文士和法利賽人,假冒為善的!」而他面前那張平整的白紙上,鉛筆在飛快地寫著——在他先在馬太福音二十三章13—14節和23節上劃了一道黑線之後。

passages.original: Thus it happened that the Rev. Paul Ford's sermon the next Sunday was a veritable bugle-call to the best that was in every man and woman and child that heard it; and its text was one of Pollyanna's shining eight hundred:
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣,保羅·福特牧師下個星期天嘅講道,成咗對每一個聽到嘅男女老幼心中最美好嘅部分嘅一聲真正嘅號角;佢嘅經文係波莉安娜嗰八百條閃光嘅經文之一:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣,保羅·福特牧師下個星期天的講道,成了對每一個聽到的男女老幼心中最美好的部分的一聲真正的號角;它的經文是波莉安娜那八百條閃光的經文之一:

passages.original: “Be glad in the Lord and rejoice, ye righteous, and shout for joy all ye that are upright in heart.”
passages.vernacular: 「你哋義人應當靠耶同華歡喜,凡心裡正直嘅,都當歡呼。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你們義人應當靠耶和華歡喜,凡心裡正直的,都當歡呼。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXIII An Accident 第二十三章:意外

passages.original: CH At Mrs. Snow's request, Pollyanna went one day to Dr. Chilton's office to get the name of a medicine which Mrs. Snow had forgotten.
passages.vernacular: 應斯諾太太嘅請求,波莉安娜有一天去奇爾頓醫生嘅診所,要攞一種斯諾太太忘咗名字嘅藥嘅名稱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 應斯諾太太的請求,波莉安娜有一天去奇爾頓醫生的診所,要拿一種斯諾太太忘了名字的藥的名稱。

passages.original: As it chanced, Pollyanna had never before seen the inside of Dr. Chilton's office.
passages.vernacular: 碰巧,波莉安娜以前從來冇見過奇爾頓醫生診所嘅裡面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 碰巧,波莉安娜以前從來沒見過奇爾頓醫生診所的裡面。

passages.original: “I've never been to your home before!
passages.vernacular: 「我以前從冇到過你家!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我以前從沒到過你家!

passages.original: This IS your home, isn't it?” she said, looking interestedly about her.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係你嘅家,對不對?」佢饒有興致地環顧四周,講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是你的家,對不對?」她饒有興致地環顧四周,說。

passages.original: The doctor smiled a little sadly.
passages.vernacular: 醫生略帶憂傷地笑咗笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生略帶憂傷地笑了笑。

passages.original: “Yes--such as 'tis,” he answered, as he wrote something on the pad of paper in his hand; “but it's a pretty poor apology for a home, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅——就咁樣吧。」佢回答,同時喺手裡嘅便箋簿上寫住乜嘢,「不過佢只係個好差勁嘅家嘅替代品,波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的——就這樣吧。」他回答,同時在手裡的便箋簿上寫著什麼,「不過它只是個很差勁的家的替代品,波莉安娜。

passages.original: They're just rooms, that's all--not a home.”
passages.vernacular: 呢只係幾個房間,僅此而已——唔係個家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這只是幾個房間,僅此而已——不是個家。」

passages.original: Pollyanna nodded her head wisely.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜聰明地點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜聰明地點點頭。

passages.original: Her eyes glowed with sympathetic understanding.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼裡閃住同情同理解嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼裡閃著同情和理解的光。

passages.original: “I know.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道。

passages.original: It takes a woman's hand and heart, or a child's presence to make a home,” she said.
passages.vernacular: 要有女人嘅手同心,或者細路嘅在場,才能造出一個家。」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要有女人的手和心,或者孩子的在場,才能造出一個家。」她說。

passages.original: “Eh?”
The doctor wheeled about abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 醫生猛地轉過身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生猛地轉過身來。

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton told me,” nodded Pollyanna, again; “about the woman's hand and heart, or the child's presence, you know.
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓先生告訴我嘅,」波莉安娜又點點頭講,「關于女人嘅手同心,或者細路嘅在場,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓先生告訴我的,」波莉安娜又點點頭說,「關于女人的手和心,或者孩子的在場,你知道。

passages.original: Why don't you get a woman's hand and heart, Dr. Chilton?
passages.vernacular: 你點解不找一個女人嘅手同心呢,奇爾頓醫生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼不找一個女人的手和心呢,奇爾頓醫生?

passages.original: Or maybe you'd take Jimmy Bean--if Mr. Pendleton doesn't want him.”
passages.vernacular: 或者,要係潘德爾頓先生唔好吉米·比恩嘅話,或者你可以收養佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者,要是潘德爾頓先生不要吉米·比恩的話,也許你可以收養他。」

passages.original: Dr. Chilton laughed a little constrainedly.
passages.vernacular: 奇爾頓醫生有點不自然地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇爾頓醫生有點不自然地笑了。

passages.original: “So Mr. Pendleton says it takes a woman's hand and heart to make a home, does he?” he asked evasively.
passages.vernacular: 「咁講,潘德爾頓先生講要有女人嘅手同心才能造出一個家,係嗎?」佢回避地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說,潘德爾頓先生說要有女人的手和心才能造出一個家,是嗎?」他回避地問。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: He says his is just a house, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢嘅家都只係一座房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他的家也只是一座房子。

passages.original: Why don't you, Dr. Chilton?”
passages.vernacular: 你點解不呢,奇爾頓醫生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼不呢,奇爾頓醫生?」

passages.original: “Why don't I--what?”
passages.vernacular: 「我點解不——乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我為什麼不——什麼?」

passages.original: The doctor had turned back to his desk.
passages.vernacular: 醫生已經轉回身朝向佢嘅書桌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生已經轉回身朝向他的書桌。

passages.original: “Get a woman's hand and heart.
passages.vernacular: 「找一個女人嘅手同心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「找一個女人的手和心。

passages.original: Oh--and I forgot.”
passages.vernacular: 哦——我忘喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦——我忘了。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's face showed suddenly a painful color.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅臉上突然泛起一種痛苦嘅紅暈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的臉上突然泛起一種痛苦的紅暈。

passages.original: “I suppose I ought to tell you.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我應該告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我應該告訴你。

passages.original: It wasn't Aunt Polly that Mr. Pendleton loved long ago; and so we--we aren't going there to live.
passages.vernacular: 好久以前潘德爾頓先生愛嘅唔係波莉姨媽;所以我哋——我哋唔會搬去嗰度住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很久以前潘德爾頓先生愛的不是波莉姨媽;所以我們——我們不會搬去那裡住了。

passages.original: You see, I told you it was--but I made a mistake.
passages.vernacular: 你知道,我告訴過你係佢——但係我弄錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,我告訴過你是她——但是我弄錯了。

passages.original: I hope YOU didn't tell any one,” she finished anxiously.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你冇告訴任何人。」佢焦急地講完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你沒有告訴任何人。」她焦急地說完。

passages.original: “No--I didn't tell any one, Pollyanna,” replied the doctor, a little queerly.
passages.vernacular: 「冇——我冇告訴任何人,波莉安娜。」醫生有點古怪地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有——我沒有告訴任何人,波莉安娜。」醫生有點古怪地回答。

passages.original: “Oh, that's all right, then,” sighed Pollyanna in relief.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰就好喇。」波莉安娜如釋重負地嘆道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那就好了。」波莉安娜如釋重負地嘆道。

passages.original: “You see you're the only one I told, and I thought Mr. Pendleton looked sort of funny when I said I'd told YOU.”
passages.vernacular: 「你瞧,你係我唯一告訴嘅人,而且我講我告訴過你嘅時候,我覺得潘德爾頓先生有點怪怪嘅樣子。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你瞧,你是我唯一告訴的人,而且我說我告訴過你的時候,我覺得潘德爾頓先生有點怪怪的樣子。」

passages.original: “Did he?”
passages.vernacular: 「係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是嗎?」

passages.original: The doctor's lips twitched.
passages.vernacular: 醫生嘅嘴唇抽動咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生的嘴唇抽動了一下。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: And of course he wouldn't want many people to know it--when 'twasn't true.
passages.vernacular: 而且當然佢不愿意讓好多人知道——既然嗰唔係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且當然他不愿意讓很多人知道——既然那不是真的。

passages.original: But why don't you get a woman's hand and heart, Dr. Chilton?”
passages.vernacular: 不過你點解不找一個女人嘅手同心呢,奇爾頓醫生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是你為什麼不找一個女人的手和心呢,奇爾頓醫生?」

passages.original: There was a moment's silence; then very gravely the doctor said:
passages.vernacular: 沉默咗片刻;然後醫生好嚴肅地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沉默了片刻;然後醫生非常嚴肅地說:

passages.original: “They're not always to be had--for the asking, little girl.”
passages.vernacular: 「并唔係總能得到嘅——只要開口要,小姑娘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「并不是總能得到的——只要開口要,小姑娘。」

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned thoughtfully.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜若有所思地皺起眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜若有所思地皺起眉頭。

passages.original: “But I should think you could get 'em,” she argued.
passages.vernacular: 「可我覺得你能得到呀。」佢爭辯道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我覺得你能得到呀。」她爭辯道。

passages.original: The flattering emphasis was unmistakable.
passages.vernacular: 嗰恭維般嘅著重語氣再明顯不過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那恭維般的著重語氣再明顯不過了。

passages.original: “Thank you,” laughed the doctor, with uplifted eyebrows.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你。」醫生笑住講,揚起咗眉毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你。」醫生笑著說,揚起了眉毛。

passages.original: Then, gravely again: “I'm afraid some of your older sisters would not be quite so--confident.
passages.vernacular: 然後又嚴肅起嚟:「恐怕你嘅啲姐姐哋就唔會咁——有信心喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後又嚴肅起來:「恐怕你的一些姐姐們就不會這麼——有信心了。

passages.original: At least, they--they haven't shown themselves to be so--obliging,” he observed.
passages.vernacular: 至少,佢哋——佢哋冇表現得咁——樂意。」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至少,她們——她們沒有表現得這麼——樂意。」他說。

passages.original: Pollyanna frowned again.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜又皺起咗眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜又皺起了眉頭。

passages.original: Then her eyes widened in surprise.
passages.vernacular: 然後佢嘅眼睛驚訝地睜大喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後她的眼睛驚訝地睜大了。

passages.original: “Why, Dr. Chilton, you don't mean--you didn't try to get somebody's hand and heart once, like Mr. Pendleton, and--and couldn't, did you?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,奇爾頓醫生,你唔係講——你唔係曾經想要得到某個人嘅手同心,像潘德爾頓先生嗰樣,然後——然後冇得到,係唔係?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,奇爾頓醫生,你不是說——你不是曾經想要得到某個人的手和心,像潘德爾頓先生那樣,然後——然後沒得到,是不是?」

passages.original: The doctor got to his feet a little abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 醫生有點突然地站咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生有點突然地站了起來。

passages.original: “There, there, Pollyanna, never mind about that now.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,波莉安娜,而家別管嗰個喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,波莉安娜,現在別管那個了。

passages.original: Don't let other people's troubles worry your little head.
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀別人嘅煩惱困擾你嘅小腦袋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別讓別人的煩惱困擾你的小腦袋。

passages.original: Suppose you run back now to Mrs. Snow.
passages.vernacular: 你而家不如跑回斯諾太太嗰兒去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你現在不如跑回斯諾太太那兒去。

passages.original: I've written down the name of the medicine, and the directions how she is to take it.
passages.vernacular: 藥名我已經寫好喇,仲有佢該點服用嘅講明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 藥名我已經寫好了,還有她該怎麼服用的說明。

passages.original: Was there anything else?”
passages.vernacular: 仲有別嘅事嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有別的事嗎?」

passages.original: Pollyanna shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜搖搖頭。

passages.original: “No, Sir; thank you, Sir,” she murmured soberly, as she turned toward the door.
passages.vernacular: 「冇喇,先生;謝謝你,先生。」佢正經地喃喃講住,轉身朝門口走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒有了,先生;謝謝你,先生。」她正經地喃喃說著,轉身朝門口走去。

passages.original: From the little hallway she called back, her face suddenly alight: “Anyhow, I'm glad 'twasn't my mother's hand and heart that you wanted and couldn't get, Dr. Chilton.
passages.vernacular: 從小門廳裡佢回頭喊道,臉上忽然亮咗起嚟:「不管點樣,我好高興你想要卻冇得到嘅唔係我母親嘅手同心,奇爾頓醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從小門廳裡她回頭喊道,臉上忽然亮了起來:「不管怎樣,我很高興你想要卻沒得到的不是我母親的手和心,奇爾頓醫生。

passages.original: Good-by!”
passages.vernacular: 再見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見!」

passages.original: It was on the last day of October that the accident occurred.
passages.vernacular: 事故發生喺十月嘅最後一天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事故發生在十月的最後一天。

passages.original: Pollyanna, hurrying home from school, crossed the road at an apparently safe distance in front of a swiftly approaching motor car.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜放學匆匆回家,喺一輛疾馳而嚟嘅汽車前面一段睇似安全嘅距離處過馬路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜放學匆匆回家,在一輛疾馳而來的汽車前面一段看似安全的距離處過馬路。

passages.original: Just what happened, no one could seem to tell afterward.
passages.vernacular: 究竟發生咗乜嘢,事後似乎邊個都講不清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 究竟發生了什麼,事後似乎誰也說不清楚。

passages.original: Neither was there any one found who could tell why it happened or who was to blame that it did happen.
passages.vernacular: 都找唔到有邊個能講出點解會發生,或者該怪邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也找不到有誰能說出為什麼會發生,或者該怪誰。

passages.original: Pollyanna, however, at five o'clock, was borne, limp and unconscious, into the little room that was so dear to her.
passages.vernacular: 然而,下午五點鐘,波莉安娜軟綿綿、失去知覺地被抬進咗佢嗰間佢所鍾愛嘅小屋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,下午五點鐘,波莉安娜軟綿綿、失去知覺地被抬進了她那間她所鍾愛的小屋。

passages.original: There, by a white-faced Aunt Polly and a weeping Nancy she was undressed tenderly and put to bed, while from the village, hastily summoned by telephone, Dr. Warren was hurrying as fast as another motor car could bring him.
passages.vernacular: 喺嗰度,臉色蒼白嘅波莉姨媽同哭泣嘅南希溫柔地畀佢脫咗衣服,把佢安置喺床上,而沃倫醫生喺電話嘅緊急召喚下,正乘另一輛汽車以最快嘅速度從村裡趕嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在那裡,臉色蒼白的波莉姨媽和哭泣的南希溫柔地給她脫了衣服,把她安置在床上,而沃倫醫生在電話的緊急召喚下,正乘另一輛汽車以最快的速度從村裡趕來。

passages.original: “And ye didn't need ter more'n look at her aunt's face,” Nancy was sobbing to Old Tom in the garden, after the doctor had arrived and was closeted in the hushed room; “ye didn't need ter more'n look at her aunt's face ter see that 'twa'n't no duty that was eatin' her.
passages.vernacular: 「你只要睇一眼佢姨媽嘅臉,」醫生到咗、關喺寂靜嘅房間裡之後,南希喺花園裡對老湯姆抽泣住講,「你只要睇一眼佢姨媽嘅臉,就睇得出嚟,折磨佢嘅唔係乜嘢責任。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你只要看一眼她姨媽的臉,」醫生到了、關在寂靜的房間裡之後,南希在花園裡對老湯姆抽泣著說,「你只要看一眼她姨媽的臉,就看得出來,折磨她的不是什麼責任。

passages.original: Yer hands don't shake, and yer eyes don't look as if ye was tryin' ter hold back the Angel o' Death himself, when you're jest doin' yer DUTY, Mr. Tom they don't, they don't!”
passages.vernacular: 你只係喺盡你嘅責任嘅時候,手唔會發抖,眼睛都唔會像想要攔住死神本人似嘅——湯姆先生,唔會嘅,唔會嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只是在盡你的責任的時候,手不會發抖,眼睛也不會像想要攔住死神本人似的——湯姆先生,不會的,不會的!」

passages.original: “Is she hurt--bad?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢傷得——重嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她傷得——重嗎?」

passages.original: The old man's voice shook.
passages.vernacular: 老人嘅聲音顫抖住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人的聲音顫抖著。

passages.original: “There ain't no tellin',” sobbed Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「講不準,」南希抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「說不準,」南希抽泣著說。

passages.original: “She lay back that white an' still she might easy be dead; but Miss Polly said she wa'n't dead--an' Miss Polly had oughter know, if any one would--she kept up such a listenin' an' a feelin' for her heartbeats an' her breath!”
passages.vernacular: 「佢躺喺嗰兒又白又靜,好可能已經死喇;不過波莉小姐講佢冇死——而且波莉小姐最該知道喇,要係有邊個會知道嘅話——佢一直聽住、摸住,感覺佢嘅心跳同呼吸!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她躺在那兒又白又靜,很可能已經死了;可是波莉小姐說她沒死——而且波莉小姐最該知道了,要是有誰會知道的話——她一直聽著、摸著,感覺她的心跳和呼吸!」

passages.original: “Couldn't ye tell anythin' what it done to her?--that--that--” Old Tom's face worked convulsively.
passages.vernacular: 「你就講不出嗰嘢把佢點樣咗嗎?——嗰——嗰——」老湯姆嘅臉痛苦地抽搐住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你就說不出那東西把她怎麼樣了嗎?——那——那——」老湯姆的臉痛苦地抽搐著。

passages.original: Nancy's lips relaxed a little.
passages.vernacular: 南希嘅嘴唇微微鬆開咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希的嘴唇微微鬆開了一點。

passages.original: “I wish ye WOULD call it somethin', Mr. Tom an' somethin' good an' strong, too.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望你畀佢起個名字,湯姆先生,起個又重又狠嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望你給它起個名字,湯姆先生,起個又重又狠的名字。

passages.original: Drat it!
passages.vernacular: 該死嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 該死的!

passages.original: Ter think of its runnin' down our little girl!
passages.vernacular: 想想睇,佢居然把咱哋嘅小姑娘撞倒喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想看,它居然把咱們的小姑娘撞倒了!

passages.original: I always hated the evil-smellin' things, anyhow--I did, I did!”
passages.vernacular: 我一向就討厭嗰啲臭烘烘嘅嘢——我係,我係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一向就討厭那些臭烘烘的東西——我是,我是!」

passages.original: “But where is she hurt?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢傷喺邊兒?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她傷在哪兒?」

passages.original: “I don't know, I don't know,” moaned Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,我唔知道,」南希呻吟住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,我不知道,」南希呻吟著說。

passages.original: “There's a little cut on her blessed head, but 'tain't bad--that ain't--Miss Polly says.
passages.vernacular: 「佢嗰可愛嘅頭上有一道小口子,但不嚴重——唔好緊——波莉小姐咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她那可愛的頭上有一道小口子,但不嚴重——不要緊——波莉小姐這麼說。

passages.original: She says she's afraid it's infernally she's hurt.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢怕係傷喺地獄裡喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她怕是傷在地獄裡了。」

passages.original: A faint flicker came into Old Tom's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 一絲微弱嘅光閃而家老湯姆嘅眼裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一絲微弱的光閃現在老湯姆的眼裡。

passages.original: “I guess you mean internally, Nancy,” he said dryly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你係講內部,南希。」佢冷冷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你是說內部,南希。」他冷冷地說。

passages.original: “She's hurt infernally, all right--plague take that autymobile!--but I don't guess Miss Polly'd be usin' that word, all the same.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢傷得確實係喺地獄裡,冇錯——呢該死嘅汽車!——不過我猜波莉小姐可唔會用嗰個字。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她傷得確實是在地獄裡,沒錯——這該死的汽車!——不過我猜波莉小姐可不會用那個字。」

passages.original: “Eh?
Well, I don't know, I don't know,” moaned Nancy, with a shake of her head as she turned away.
passages.vernacular: 哎,我唔知道,我唔知道,」南希呻吟住,搖住頭轉身走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,我不知道,我不知道,」南希呻吟著,搖著頭轉身走開了。

passages.original: “Seems as if I jest couldn't stand it till that doctor gits out o' there.
passages.vernacular: 「睇來喺嗰位醫生出嚟之前,我就係忍不下去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看來在那位醫生出來之前,我就是忍不下去了。

passages.original: I wish I had a washin' ter do--the biggest washin' I ever see, I do, I do!” she wailed, wringing her hands helplessly.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望我有衣服要洗——我見過嘅最大嘅一堆衣服,我真希望啊,我真希望!」佢無助地絞著手,哀號道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望我有衣服要洗——我見過的最大的一堆衣服,我真希望啊,我真希望!」她無助地絞著手,哀號道。

passages.original: Even after the doctor was gone, however, there seemed to be little that Nancy could tell Mr. Tom.
passages.vernacular: 即便喺醫生走後,南希似乎都冇多少可以告訴湯姆先生嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即便在醫生走後,南希似乎也沒有多少可以告訴湯姆先生的。

passages.original: There appeared to be no bones broken, and the cut was of slight consequence; but the doctor had looked very grave, had shaken his head slowly, and had said that time alone could tell.
passages.vernacular: 睇起嚟冇骨頭折斷,傷口都無關緊要;不過醫生神情好嚴峻,慢慢地搖住頭,講只有時間才能講明一切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看起來沒有骨頭折斷,傷口也無關緊要;可是醫生神情非常嚴峻,慢慢地搖著頭,說只有時間才能說明一切。

passages.original: After he had gone, Miss Polly had shown a face even whiter and more drawn looking than before.
passages.vernacular: 佢走後,波莉小姐嘅臉色比先前更加蒼白憔悴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他走後,波莉小姐的臉色比先前更加蒼白憔悴。

passages.original: The patient had not fully recovered consciousness, but at present she seemed to be resting as comfortably as could be expected.
passages.vernacular: 病人仲冇完全恢復知覺,不過目前佢似乎正安穩地休息住,已係所能期望嘅最好狀況喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 病人還沒有完全恢復知覺,不過目前她似乎正安穩地休息著,已是所能期望的最好狀況了。

passages.original: A trained nurse had been sent for, and would come that night.
passages.vernacular: 已經派人去請一位受過訓練嘅護士,當晚就到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已經派人去請一位受過訓練的護士,當晚就到。

passages.original: That was all.
passages.vernacular: 就呢啲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這些了。

passages.original: And Nancy turned sobbingly, and went back to her kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 南希抽泣住轉過身,回佢嘅廚房去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希抽泣著轉過身,回她的廚房去了。

passages.original: It was sometime during the next forenoon that Pollyanna opened conscious eyes and realized where she was.
passages.vernacular: 第二天上午嘅某個時候,波莉安娜睜開咗清醒嘅眼睛,意識到咗自己喺邊度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二天上午的某個時候,波莉安娜睜開了清醒的眼睛,意識到了自己在哪裡。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, what's the matter?
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,點回事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,怎麼回事?

passages.original: Isn't it daytime?
passages.vernacular: 而家唔係白天嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在不是白天嗎?

passages.original: Why don't I get up?” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 我點解不起床?」佢叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為什麼不起床?」她叫道。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, I can't get up,” she moaned, falling back on the pillow, after an ineffectual attempt to lift herself.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,我起不嚟,」佢呻吟住,試圖撐起身子卻冇能成功,又倒回枕頭上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,我起不來,」她呻吟著,試圖撐起身子卻沒能成功,又倒回枕頭上。

passages.original: “No, dear, I wouldn't try--just yet,” soothed her aunt quickly, but very quietly.
passages.vernacular: 「不,親愛嘅,而家先別試——」佢姨媽即刻安撫道,聲音好輕好輕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不,親愛的,現在先別試——」她姨媽立刻安撫道,聲音很輕很輕。

passages.original: “But what is the matter?
passages.vernacular: 「不過點回事呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是怎麼回事呢?

passages.original: Why can't I get up?”
passages.vernacular: 我點解起不嚟?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為什麼起不來?」

passages.original: Miss Polly's eyes asked an agonized question of the white-capped young woman standing in the window, out of the range of Pollyanna's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅目光向站喺窗邊、喺波莉安娜視線之外嘅嗰位戴白帽嘅年輕女子投去痛苦嘅詢問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的目光向站在窗邊、在波莉安娜視線之外的那位戴白帽的年輕女子投去痛苦的詢問。

passages.original: The young woman nodded.
passages.vernacular: 嗰位年輕女子點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位年輕女子點點頭。

passages.original: “Tell her,” the lips said.
passages.vernacular: 「告訴佢。」嗰嘴唇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「告訴她。」那嘴唇說。

passages.original: Miss Polly cleared her throat, and tried to swallow the lump that would scarcely let her speak.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐清咗清嗓子,試圖咽下嗰塊讓佢幾乎講不出話嚟嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐清了清嗓子,試圖咽下那塊讓她幾乎說不出話來的東西。

passages.original: “You were hurt, dear, by the automobile last night.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅,尋日晚上你被汽車撞傷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的,昨天晚上你被汽車撞傷了。

passages.original: But never mind that now.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家先別管嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過現在先別管那個。

passages.original: Auntie wants you to rest and go to sleep again.”
passages.vernacular: 姨媽要你休息,再瞓一覺。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 姨媽要你休息,再睡一覺。」

passages.original: “Hurt?
passages.vernacular: 「撞傷喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「撞傷了?

passages.original: Oh, yes; I--I ran.”
passages.vernacular: 哦,係嘅;我——我跑過去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,是的;我——我跑過去。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's eyes were dazed.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅眼神茫然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的眼神茫然。

passages.original: She lifted her hand to her forehead.
passages.vernacular: 佢抬手摸咗摸前額。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她抬手摸了摸前額。

passages.original: “Why, it's--done up, and it--hurts!”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,佢——包扎住,而且——疼!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,它——包扎著,而且——疼!」

passages.original: “Yes, dear; but never mind.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,親愛嘅;不過冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,親愛的;不過沒關係。

passages.original: Just--just rest.”
passages.vernacular: 只管——只管休息。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只管——只管休息。」

passages.original: “But, Aunt Polly, I feel so funny, and so bad!
passages.vernacular: 「不過,波莉姨媽,我覺得好奇怪,好難受!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,波莉姨媽,我覺得好奇怪,好難受!

passages.original: My legs feel so--so queer--only they don't FEEL--at all!”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅腿覺得好——好怪——只不過佢哋根本冇感覺!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的腿覺得很——很怪——只不過它們根本沒有感覺!」

passages.original: With an imploring look into the nurse's face, Miss Polly struggled to her feet, and turned away.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐懇求地睇咗一眼護士嘅臉,掙扎住站起身,轉身走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐懇求地看了一眼護士的臉,掙扎著站起身,轉身走開了。

passages.original: The nurse came forward quickly.
passages.vernacular: 護士迅速走上前嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士迅速走上前來。

passages.original: “Suppose you let me talk to you now,” she began cheerily.
passages.vernacular: 「而家讓我跟你講話吧,」佢愉快地開口講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在讓我跟你說話吧,」她愉快地開口說。

passages.original: “I'm sure I think it's high time we were getting acquainted, and I'm going to introduce myself.
passages.vernacular: 「我想而家正是我哋該互相認識嘅時候喇,我來自我介紹一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想現在正是我們該互相認識的時候了,我來自我介紹一下。

passages.original: I am Miss Hunt, and I've come to help your aunt take care of you.
passages.vernacular: 我係亨特小姐,我係嚟幫你姨媽照顧你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是亨特小姐,我是來幫你姨媽照顧你的。

passages.original: And the very first thing I'm going to do is to ask you to swallow these little white pills for me.”
passages.vernacular: 而我要做嘅第一件事,就係請你替我把呢啲小白藥丸吞下去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我要做的第一件事,就是請你替我把這些小白藥丸吞下去。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's eyes grew a bit wild.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅眼神有點慌亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的眼神有點慌亂。

passages.original: “But I don't want to be taken care of--that is, not for long!
passages.vernacular: 「不過我唔想被照顧——至少唔想長久被照顧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我不想被照顧——至少不想長久被照顧!

passages.original: I want to get up.
passages.vernacular: 我想起床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想起床。

passages.original: You know I go to school.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我要上學嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我要上學的。

passages.original: Can't I go to school to-morrow?”
passages.vernacular: 我聽日能去上學嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明天能去上學嗎?」

passages.original: From the window where Aunt Polly stood now there came a half-stifled cry.
passages.vernacular: 從而家波莉姨媽站住嘅窗邊,傳嚟一聲半壓抑嘅驚呼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從現在波莉姨媽站著的窗邊,傳來一聲半壓抑的驚呼。

passages.original: “To-morrow?” smiled the nurse, brightly.
passages.vernacular: 「聽日?」護士明朗地笑住講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明天?」護士明朗地笑著說,

passages.original: “Well, I may not let you out quite so soon as that, Miss Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我可能唔會咁快就放你出去,波莉安娜小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我可能不會這麼快就放你出去,波莉安娜小姐。

passages.original: But just swallow these little pills for me, please, and we'll see what THEY'LL do.”
passages.vernacular: 不過請你替我把呢啲小藥丸吞下去,我哋睇睇佢哋會起乜嘢作用。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過請你替我把這些小藥丸吞下去,我們看看它們會起什麼作用。」

passages.original: “All right,” agreed Pollyanna, somewhat doubtfully; “but I MUST go to school day after to-morrow--there are examinations then, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,」波莉安娜有點疑惑地同意喇,「不過我後天一定得去上學——後天有考試,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,」波莉安娜有點疑惑地同意了,「不過我後天一定得去上學——後天有考試,你知道。」

passages.original: She spoke again, a minute later.
passages.vernacular: 一分鐘後佢又開口喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一分鐘後她又開口了。

passages.original: She spoke of school, and of the automobile, and of how her head ached; but very soon her voice trailed into silence under the blessed influence of the little white pills she had swallowed.
passages.vernacular: 佢談起咗學校,談起咗汽車,談起咗佢嘅頭幾咁疼;不過好快,佢嘅聲音就喺佢吞下嘅小白藥丸嘅神奇作用下逐漸消失,歸于寂靜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她談起了學校,談起了汽車,談起了她的頭多麼疼;可是很快,她的聲音就在她吞下的小白藥丸的神奇作用下逐漸消失,歸于寂靜。

chapters.title: Ch. XXIV John Pendleton 第二十四章:約翰·潘德爾頓

passages.original: CH Pollyanna did not go to school “to-morrow,” nor the “day after to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜「聽日」冇去上學,「後天」都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜「明天」沒有去上學,「後天」也沒有。

passages.original: Pollyanna, however, did not realize this, except momentarily when a brief period of full consciousness sent insistent questions to her lips.
passages.vernacular: 不過,波莉安娜自己并唔知道呢啲,只有喺短暫清醒嘅片刻,才會有迫切嘅問題涌到佢嘴邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,波莉安娜自己并不知道這一點,只有在短暫清醒的片刻,才會有迫切的問題涌到她嘴邊。

passages.original: Pollyanna did not realize anything, in fact, very clearly until a week had passed; then the fever subsided, the pain lessened somewhat, and her mind awoke to full consciousness.
passages.vernacular: 其實,直到一個星期過去,波莉安娜對乜嘢事都冇清楚嘅意識;然後燒退喇,疼痛稍減,佢嘅神志才完全清醒過嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其實,直到一個星期過去,波莉安娜對什麼事都沒有清楚的意識;然後燒退了,疼痛稍減,她的神志才完全清醒過來。

passages.original: She had then to be told all over again what had occurred.
passages.vernacular: 呢陣,佢唔得唔再一次被告知發生咗乜嘢事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這時,她不得不再一次被告知發生了什麼事。

passages.original: “And so it's hurt that I am, and not sick,” she sighed at last.
passages.vernacular: 「咁講我係受傷喇,唔係生病,」佢終于嘆咗口氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說我是受傷了,不是生病,」她終于嘆了口氣說。

passages.original: “Well, I'm glad of that.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,呢我好高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,這我很高興。」

passages.original: “G-glad, Pollyanna?” asked her aunt, who was sitting by the bed.
passages.vernacular: 「高——興,波莉安娜?」坐喺床邊嘅姨媽問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高——興,波莉安娜?」坐在床邊的姨媽問。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: I'd so much rather have broken legs like Mr. Pendleton's than life-long-invalids like Mrs. Snow, you know.
passages.vernacular: 我寧愿像潘德爾頓先生嗰樣斷咗腿,都不愿像斯諾太太嗰樣做一輩子嘅病人,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧愿像潘德爾頓先生那樣斷了腿,也不愿像斯諾太太那樣做一輩子的病人,你知道。

passages.original: Broken legs get well, and lifelong-invalids don't.”
passages.vernacular: 斷咗嘅腿會好,而一輩子嘅病人唔會。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 斷了的腿會好,而一輩子的病人不會。」

passages.original: Miss Polly--who had said nothing whatever about broken legs--got suddenly to her feet and walked to the little dressing table across the room.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐——佢根本冇提過乜嘢斷腿嘅話——忽地站起身,走到房間嗰頭嘅小梳妝檯前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐——她根本沒有提過什麼斷腿的話——忽地站起身,走到房間那頭的小梳妝檯前。

passages.original: She was picking up one object after another now, and putting each down, in an aimless fashion quite unlike her usual decisiveness.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家一件接一件地攞起嘢,又一件件放下,漫無目的,完全不像佢平日嘅果斷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在一件接一件地拿起東西,又一件件放下,漫無目的,完全不像她平日的果斷。

passages.original: Her face was not aimless-looking at all, however; it was white and drawn.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢嘅臉上卻絲毫冇漫無目的嘅神情;佢蒼白而憔悴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,她的臉上卻絲毫沒有漫無目的的神情;它蒼白而憔悴。

passages.original: On the bed Pollyanna lay blinking at the dancing band of colors on the ceiling, which came from one of the prisms in the window.
passages.vernacular: 床上,波莉安娜躺住,眨住眼睛望住天花板上嗰條跳動嘅彩帶,嗰個係窗上一塊棱鏡投下嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 床上,波莉安娜躺著,眨著眼睛望著天花板上那條跳動的彩帶,那是窗上一塊棱鏡投下的。

passages.original: “I'm glad it isn't smallpox that ails me, too,” she murmured contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 「我都好高興我得嘅唔係天花,」佢滿足地喃喃講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也很高興我得的不是天花,」她滿足地喃喃說。

passages.original: “That would be worse than freckles.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰比雀斑更糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那比雀斑更糟。

passages.original: And I'm glad 'tisn't whooping cough--I've had that, and it's horrid--and I'm glad 'tisn't appendicitis nor measles, 'cause they're catching--measles are, I mean--and they wouldn't let you stay here.”
passages.vernacular: 我都高興唔係百日咳——我得過,可怕極喇——都高興唔係闌尾炎或麻疹,因為佢哋會傳染——我係講麻疹——佢哋就唔會讓你待喺呢兒喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也高興不是百日咳——我得過,可怕極了——也高興不是闌尾炎或麻疹,因為它們會傳染——我是說麻疹——他們就不會讓你待在這兒了。」

passages.original: “You seem to--to be glad for a good many things, my dear,” faltered Aunt Polly, putting her hand to her throat as if her collar bound.
passages.vernacular: 「你似乎——為好多事情高興啊,親愛嘅。」姨媽結結巴巴地講,把手按喺喉嚨上,好像領子勒住佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你似乎——為很多事情高興啊,親愛的。」姨媽結結巴巴地說,把手按在喉嚨上,好像領子勒著她。

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed softly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜輕輕地笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜輕輕地笑了。

passages.original: “I am.
passages.vernacular: 「係呀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是呀。

passages.original: I've been thinking of 'em--lots of 'em--all the time I've been looking up at that rainbow.
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺想佢哋——好多好多——我一直睇住嗰道彩虹嘅時候,都喺想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在想它們——好多好多——我一直看著那道彩虹的時候,都在想。

passages.original: I love rainbows.
passages.vernacular: 我愛彩虹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛彩虹。

passages.original: I'm so glad Mr. Pendleton gave me those prisms!
passages.vernacular: 我真高興潘德爾頓先生送咗我嗰啲棱鏡!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真高興潘德爾頓先生送了我那些棱鏡!

passages.original: I'm glad of some things I haven't said yet.
passages.vernacular: 仲有些事我仲冇講呢,我都好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有些事我還沒說呢,我也很高興。

passages.original: I don't know but I'm 'most glad I was hurt.”
passages.vernacular: 我差不多覺得,我受傷咗仲幾乎係一件高興嘅事呢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我差不多覺得,我受傷了還幾乎是一件高興的事呢。」

passages.original: “Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜!」

passages.original: Pollyanna laughed softly again.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜又輕輕笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜又輕輕笑了。

passages.original: She turned luminous eyes on her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 佢用明亮嘅眼睛睇住姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她用明亮的眼睛看著姨媽。

passages.original: “Well, you see, since I have been hurt, you've called me 'dear' lots of times--and you didn't before.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,你瞧,自從我受傷以來,你叫咗我好多次『親愛嘅』——以前你冇叫過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,你瞧,自從我受傷以來,你叫了我好多次『親愛的』——以前你沒有叫過。

passages.original: I love to be called 'dear'--by folks that belong to you, I mean.
passages.vernacular: 我鍾意被叫『親愛嘅』——被屬于你嘅人叫,我係講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我喜歡被叫『親愛的』——被屬于你的人叫,我是說。
