passages.original: Some of the Ladies' Aiders did call me that; and of course that was pretty nice, but not so nice as if they had belonged to me, like you do.
passages.vernacular: 濟貧會嘅太太哋有些人確實咁樣叫過我;當然嗰都好好,不過不如係屬于我嘅人叫,像你咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 濟貧會的太太們有些人確實這樣叫過我;當然那也很好,可是不如是屬于我的人叫,像你這樣。

passages.original: Oh, Aunt Polly, I'm so glad you belong to me!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉姨媽,我真高興你係屬于我嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉姨媽,我真高興你是屬于我的!」

passages.original: Aunt Polly did not answer.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽沒有回答。

passages.original: Her hand was at her throat again.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅手又放到咗喉嚨上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的手又放到了喉嚨上。

passages.original: Her eyes were full of tears.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼裡充滿咗淚水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼裡充滿了淚水。

passages.original: She had turned away and was hurrying from the room through the door by which the nurse had just entered.
passages.vernacular: 佢轉過身,匆匆從護士頭先進嚟嘅嗰道門走出咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她轉過身,匆匆從護士剛才進來的那道門走出了房間。

passages.original: It was that afternoon that Nancy ran out to Old Tom, who was cleaning harnesses in the barn.
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰天下午,南希跑出去找正在穀倉裡擦馬具嘅老湯姆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那天下午,南希跑出去找正在穀倉裡擦馬具的老湯姆。

passages.original: Her eyes were wild.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼神狂亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼神狂亂。

passages.original: “Mr. Tom, Mr. Tom, guess what's happened,” she panted.
passages.vernacular: 「湯姆先生,湯姆先生,猜猜出咗乜嘢事,」佢喘住氣講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「湯姆先生,湯姆先生,猜猜出了什麼事,」她喘著氣說,

passages.original: “You couldn't guess in a thousand years--you couldn't, you couldn't!”
passages.vernacular: 「你一千年都猜不出嚟——猜不出嚟,猜不出嚟!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你一千年也猜不出來——猜不出來,猜不出來!」

passages.original: “Then I cal'late I won't try,” retorted the man, grimly, “specially as I hain't got more'n TEN ter live, anyhow, probably.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰我想我就不猜喇,」嗰人冷冷地回答,「尤其係我大概都活不過十年喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那我想我就不猜了,」那人冷冷地回答,「尤其是我大概也活不過十年了。

passages.original: You'd better tell me first off, Nancy.”
passages.vernacular: 南希,你最好一開始就告訴我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希,你最好一開始就告訴我。」

passages.original: “Well, listen, then.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,嗰你聽住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,那你聽著。

passages.original: Who do you s'pose is in the parlor now with the mistress?
passages.vernacular: 你猜而家邊個喺客廳裡跟女主人喺一起?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你猜現在誰在客廳裡跟女主人在一起?

passages.original: Who, I say?”
passages.vernacular: 我問你,邊個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我問你,誰?」

passages.original: Old Tom shook his head.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆搖搖頭。

passages.original: “There's no tellin',” he declared.
passages.vernacular: 「冇法猜,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒法猜,」他說。

passages.original: “Yes, there is.
passages.vernacular: 「有嘅,有嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有的,有的。

passages.original: I'm tellin'.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你。

passages.original: It's--John Pendleton!”
passages.vernacular: 係——約翰·潘德爾頓!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是——約翰·潘德爾頓!」

passages.original: “Sho, now!
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀!

passages.original: You're jokin', girl.”
passages.vernacular: 你開玩笑吧,姑娘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你開玩笑吧,姑娘。」

passages.original: “Not much I am--an' me a-lettin' him in myself--crutches an' all!
passages.vernacular: 「才唔係呢——定係我親自放佢進嚟嘅——連拐杖都帶住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「才不是呢——還是我親自放他進來的——連拐杖都帶著!

passages.original: An' the team he come in a-waitin' this minute at the door for him, jest as if he wa'n't the cranky old crosspatch he is, what never talks ter no one! jest think, Mr. Tom--HIM a-callin' on HER!”
passages.vernacular: 佢坐嚟嘅嗰輛馬車呢會兒仲喺門口等住佢呢,好像佢唔係嗰個性子古怪嘅老怪物,從不跟人講話嘅嗰個!你想想睇,湯姆先生——佢嚟拜訪佢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐來的那輛馬車這會兒還在門口等著他呢,好像他不是那個性子古怪的老怪物,從不跟人說話的那個!你想想看,湯姆先生——他來拜訪她!」

passages.original: “Well, why not?” demanded the old man, a little aggressively.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,點解不可以?」老人有些挑釁地問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,為什麼不可以?」老人有些挑釁地問。

passages.original: Nancy gave him a scornful glance.
passages.vernacular: 南希輕蔑地瞪咗佢一眼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希輕蔑地瞪了他一眼。

passages.original: “As if you didn't know better'n me!” she derided.
passages.vernacular: 「好像你比我仲不清楚似嘅!」佢嘲諷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像你比我還不清楚似的!」她嘲諷道。

passages.original: “Eh?”
“Oh, you needn't be so innercent,” she retorted with mock indignation; “--you what led me wildgoose chasin' in the first place!”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,你別裝得咁無辜,」佢假裝憤憤地回嘴,「——一開始就係你帶住我瞎忙亂嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,你別裝得那麼無辜,」她假裝憤憤地回嘴,「——一開始就是你帶著我瞎忙亂的!」

passages.original: “What do ye mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「你乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你什麼意思?」

passages.original: Nancy glanced through the open barn door toward the house, and came a step nearer to the old man.
passages.vernacular: 南希透過敞開嘅穀倉門瞥咗一眼房子,朝老人走近咗一步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希透過敞開的穀倉門瞥了一眼房子,朝老人走近了一步。

passages.original: “Listen!
passages.vernacular: 「聽住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「聽著!

passages.original: 'Twas you that was tellin' me Miss Polly had a lover in the first place, wa'n't it?
passages.vernacular: 最先告訴我波莉小姐有過情人嘅,不就係你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最先告訴我波莉小姐有過情人的,不就是你嗎?

passages.original: Well, one day I thinks I finds two and two, and I puts 'em tergether an' makes four.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,有一天我以為我找到咗兩個,把佢哋湊到一起,得出咗四個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,有一天我以為我找到了兩個,把它們湊到一起,得出了四個。

passages.original: But it turns out ter be five--an' no four at all, at all!”
passages.vernacular: 可結果係五個——根本唔係四個,根本唔係!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可結果是五個——根本不是四個,根本不是!」

passages.original: With a gesture of indifference Old Tom turned and fell to work.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆無所謂地擺咗擺手,轉身幹起活嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆無所謂地擺了擺手,轉身幹起活來。

passages.original: “If you're goin' ter talk ter me, you've got ter talk plain horse sense,” he declared testily.
passages.vernacular: 「你要係想跟我講話,就得講大白話,講實在話,」佢不耐煩地講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要是想跟我說話,就得說大白話,說實在話,」他不耐煩地說,

passages.original: “I never was no hand for figgers.”
passages.vernacular: 「我從來就不擅長算數。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我從來就不擅長算數。」

passages.original: Nancy laughed.
passages.vernacular: 南希笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希笑了。

passages.original: “Well, it's this,” she explained.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係咁樣嘅,」佢解釋道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是這樣的,」她解釋道。

passages.original: “I heard somethin' that made me think him an' Miss Polly was lovers.”
passages.vernacular: 「我聽到些事,讓我以為佢同波莉小姐係情人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我聽到些事,讓我以為他和波莉小姐是情人。」

passages.original: “MR.
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓

passages.original: PENDLETON!”
passages.vernacular: 先生!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生!」

passages.original: Old Tom straightened up.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆直起咗身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆直起了身子。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: Oh, I know now; he wasn't.
passages.vernacular: 哦,我而家知道喇;佢哋唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我現在知道了;他們不是。

passages.original: It was that blessed child's mother he was in love with, and that's why he wanted--but never mind that part,” she added hastily, remembering just in time her promise to Pollyanna not to tell that Mr. Pendleton had wished her to come and live with him.
passages.vernacular: 佢愛嘅係嗰個可愛細路嘅母親,所以佢想要——不過嗰部分就別提喇。」佢趕忙補充道,及時想起咗自己答應過波莉安娜,唔能夠講潘德爾頓先生希望佢去同佢同住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他愛的是那個可愛孩子的母親,所以他想要——不過那部分就別提了。」她趕忙補充道,及時想起了自己答應過波莉安娜,不能說潘德爾頓先生希望她去和他同住。

passages.original: “Well, I've been askin' folks about him some, since, and I've found out that him an' Miss Polly hain't been friends for years, an' that she's been hatin' him like pizen owin' ter the silly gossip that coupled their names tergether when she was eighteen or twenty.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我後來向人打聽咗佢啲事,發現佢同波莉小姐已經好多年唔係朋友喇,佢恨佢恨得像毒藥一樣,就係因為喺佢十八二十歲嘅時候,有人把佢哋嘅名字扯喺一起,傳咗些愚蠢嘅閑話。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我後來向人打聽了他一些事,發現他和波莉小姐已經好多年不是朋友了,她恨他恨得像毒藥一樣,就是因為在她十八二十歲的時候,有人把他們的名字扯在一起,傳了些愚蠢的閑話。」

passages.original: “Yes, I remember,” nodded Old Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我記得。」老湯姆點點頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我記得。」老湯姆點點頭說。

passages.original: “It was three or four years after Miss Jennie give him the mitten and went off with the other chap.
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個係詹妮小姐拒絕咗佢、跟另一個家伙走咗嘅三四年之後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那是詹妮小姐拒絕了他、跟另一個家伙走了的三四年之後。

passages.original: Miss Polly knew about it, of course, and was sorry for him.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐當然知道呢事,都為佢難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐當然知道這事,也為他難過。

passages.original: So she tried ter be nice to him.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢就想對佢好啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她就想對他好一點。

passages.original: Maybe she overdid it a little--she hated that minister chap so who had took off her sister.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢做得有點過頭——佢咁恨帶走佢妹妹嘅嗰個牧師。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許她做得有點過頭——她那麼恨帶走她妹妹的那個牧師。

passages.original: At any rate, somebody begun ter make trouble.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,有人就開始搬弄係非。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,有人就開始搬弄是非。

passages.original: They said she was runnin' after him.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋講佢喺追佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們說她在追他。」

passages.original: “Runnin' after any man--her!” interjected Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「追任何男人——佢!」南希插嘴道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「追任何男人——她!」南希插嘴道。

passages.original: “I know it; but they did,” declared Old Tom, “and of course no gal of any spunk'll stand that.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道;可佢哋就係咁講嘅,」老湯姆講,「而且當然,冇邊個有骨氣嘅姑娘受得咗呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道;可他們就是這麼說的,」老湯姆說,「而且當然,沒有哪個有骨氣的姑娘受得了這個。

passages.original: Then about that time come her own lover an' the trouble with HIM.
passages.vernacular: 然後差不多嗰時候,佢自己嘅情人出現喇,跟佢都出咗麻煩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後差不多那時候,她自己的情人出現了,跟他也出了麻煩。

passages.original: After that she shut up like an oyster an' wouldn't have nothin' ter do with nobody fur a spell.
passages.vernacular: 嗰以後,佢就像牡蠣一樣閉上喇,有一陣子不跟任何人來往。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那以後,她就像牡蠣一樣閉上了,有一陣子不跟任何人來往。

passages.original: Her heart jest seemed to turn bitter at the core.”
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅心似乎一下子從核心裡變苦喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的心似乎一下子從核心裡變苦了。」

passages.original: “Yes, I know.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道。

passages.original: I've heard about that now,” rejoined Nancy; “an' that's why you could 'a' knocked me down with a feather when I see HIM at the door--him, what she hain't spoke to for years!
passages.vernacular: 我而家聽講喇,」南希回答,「所以我睇見佢站喺門口嘅時候,你隨便攞根羽毛就能把我打倒——佢啊,佢好多年都冇跟佢講過話喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在聽說了,」南希回答,「所以我看見他站在門口的時候,你隨便拿根羽毛就能把我打倒——他啊,她好多年都沒跟他說過話了!

passages.original: But I let him in an' went an' told her.”
passages.vernacular: 不過我定係放佢進嚟,仲去告訴咗佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過我還是放他進來,還去告訴了她。」

passages.original: “What did she say?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講咗乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她說了什麼?」

passages.original: Old Tom held his breath suspended.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆屏住咗呼吸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆屏住了呼吸。

passages.original: “Nothin'--at first.
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢都冇講——起先。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼也沒說——起先。

passages.original: She was so still I thought she hadn't heard; and I was jest goin' ter say it over when she speaks up quiet like: 'Tell Mr. Pendleton I will be down at once.'
passages.vernacular: 佢咁安靜,我仲以為佢冇聽見;我正要重講一遍,佢就平靜地開口喇:『告訴潘德爾頓先生,我即刻就下去。』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她那麼安靜,我還以為她沒聽見;我正要重說一遍,她就平靜地開口了:『告訴潘德爾頓先生,我馬上就下去。』

passages.original: An' I come an' told him.
passages.vernacular: 我就去告訴佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就去告訴他了。

passages.original: Then I come out here an' told you,” finished Nancy, casting another backward glance toward the house.
passages.vernacular: 然後我就出嚟告訴你喇。」南希講完,又回頭瞥咗一眼房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我就出來告訴你了。」南希說完,又回頭瞥了一眼房子。

passages.original: “Humph!” grunted Old Tom; and fell to work again.
passages.vernacular: 「哼!」老湯姆哼咗一聲,又幹起活嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哼!」老湯姆哼了一聲,又幹起活來。

passages.original: In the ceremonious “parlor” of the Harrington homestead, Mr. John Pendleton did not have to wait long before a swift step warned him of Miss Polly's coming.
passages.vernacular: 喺哈靈頓家宅子嗰間講究禮節嘅「客廳」裡,約翰·潘德爾頓先生冇等多久,就聽到一陣急促嘅腳步聲,預告住波莉小姐嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在哈靈頓家宅子那間講究禮節的「客廳」裡,約翰·潘德爾頓先生沒有等多久,就聽到一陣急促的腳步聲,預告著波莉小姐來了。

passages.original: As he attempted to rise, she made a gesture of remonstrance.
passages.vernacular: 佢想起身,佢做咗個制止嘅手勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想起身,她做了個制止的手勢。

passages.original: She did not offer her hand, however, and her face was coldly reserved.
passages.vernacular: 不過,佢冇伸出手,臉上冷冰冰嘅,保持住距離。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,她沒有伸出手,臉上冷冰冰的,保持著距離。

passages.original: “I called to ask for--Pollyanna,” he began at once, a little brusquely.
passages.vernacular: 「我係嚟問——波莉安娜嘅情況,」佢一開口就講,語氣有點生硬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是來問——波莉安娜的情況,」他一開口就說,語氣有點生硬。

passages.original: “Thank you.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你。

passages.original: She is about the same,” said Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 佢差不多定係老樣子。」波莉小姐講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她差不多還是老樣子。」波莉小姐說。

passages.original: “And that is--won't you tell me HOW she is?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰個就係——你能唔能夠告訴我佢究竟點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那就是——你能不能告訴我她究竟怎麼樣?」

passages.original: His voice was not quite steady this time.
passages.vernacular: 呢次佢嘅聲音不太平穩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這次他的聲音不太平穩。

passages.original: A quick spasm of pain crossed the woman's face.
passages.vernacular: 一陣劇痛飛快地掠過女人嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣劇痛飛快地掠過女人的臉。

passages.original: “I can't, I wish I could!”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠,我真希望我能!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能,我真希望我能!」

passages.original: “You mean--you don't know?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係講——你唔知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是說——你不知道?」

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。」

passages.original: “But--the doctor?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過——醫生呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是——醫生呢?」

passages.original: “Dr. Warren himself seems--at sea.
passages.vernacular: 「沃倫醫生自己好像都——唔知所措。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沃倫醫生自己好像也——不知所措。

passages.original: He is in correspondence now with a New York specialist.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家正同一位紐約嘅專家通信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在正和一位紐約的專家通信。

passages.original: They have arranged for a consultation at once.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋已經安排即刻會診。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們已經安排馬上會診。」

passages.original: “But--but what WERE her injuries that you do know?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過——不過你所知道嘅佢嘅傷係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是——可是你所知道的她的傷是什麼?」

passages.original: “A slight cut on the head, one or two bruises, and--and an injury to the spine which has seemed to cause--paralysis from the hips down.”
passages.vernacular: 「頭上一道小口子,一兩處瘀傷,仲有——脊椎受傷,似乎造成喇——從臀部以下癱瘓。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「頭上一道小口子,一兩處瘀傷,還有——脊椎受傷,似乎造成了——從臀部以下癱瘓。」

passages.original: A low cry came from the man.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人發出一聲低低嘅驚叫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人發出一聲低低的驚叫。

passages.original: There was a brief silence; then, huskily, he asked:
passages.vernacular: 短暫嘅沉默;然後佢沙啞地問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 短暫的沉默;然後他沙啞地問:

passages.original: “And Pollyanna--how does she--take it?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗰波莉安娜——佢點——承受嘅?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那波莉安娜——她怎麼——承受的?」

passages.original: “She doesn't understand--at all--how things really are.
passages.vernacular: 「佢完全不明白——事情到底係點回事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她完全不明白——事情到底是怎麼回事。

passages.original: And I CAN'T tell her.”
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠告訴佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能告訴她。」

passages.original: “But she must know--something!”
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢總該知道——啲吧!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她總該知道——一些吧!」

passages.original: Miss Polly lifted her hand to the collar at her throat in the gesture that had become so common to her of late.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐抬手摸住喉嚨處嘅領子,嗰個係佢近來變得好常見嘅動作。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐抬手摸著喉嚨處的領子,那是她近來變得很常見的動作。

passages.original: “Oh, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的。

passages.original: She knows she can't--move; but she thinks her legs are--broken.
passages.vernacular: 佢知道自己動不喇;不過佢以為係佢嘅腿——斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她知道自己動不了;可是她以為是她的腿——斷了。

passages.original: She says she's glad it's broken legs like yours rather than 'lifelong-invalids' like Mrs. Snow's; because broken legs get well, and the other--doesn't.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢好高興係像你嗰樣嘅斷腿,而唔係像斯諾太太嗰樣嘅『一輩子嘅病人』;因為斷咗嘅腿會好,而另一種——唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她很高興是像你那樣的斷腿,而不是像斯諾太太那樣的『一輩子的病人』;因為斷了的腿會好,而另一種——不會。

passages.original: She talks like that all the time, until it--it seems as if I should--die!”
passages.vernacular: 佢一直咁樣講,講得我——我覺得我快要死喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一直這樣說,說得我——我覺得我快要死了!」

passages.original: Through the blur of tears in his own eyes, the man saw the drawn face opposite, twisted with emotion.
passages.vernacular: 透過自己眼中模糊嘅淚水,嗰人睇見咗對面嗰張憔悴嘅、因激動而扭曲嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 透過自己眼中模糊的淚水,那人看見了對面那張憔悴的、因激動而扭曲的臉。

passages.original: Involuntarily his thoughts went back to what Pollyanna had said when he had made his final plea for her presence: “Oh, I couldn't leave Aunt Polly--now!”
passages.vernacular: 佢不由得想起波莉安娜喺佢最後一次懇求佢嚟嘅時候講嘅話:「哦,我而家唔能夠離開波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不由得想起波莉安娜在他最後一次懇求她來的時候說的話:「哦,我現在不能離開波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: It was this thought that made him ask very gently, as soon as he could control his voice:
passages.vernacular: 正是呢個念頭,讓佢喺能控制住聲音時,好溫和地問道:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 正是這個念頭,讓他在能控制住聲音時,非常溫和地問道:

passages.original: “I wonder if you know, Miss Harrington, how hard I tried to get Pollyanna to come and live with me.”
passages.vernacular: 「唔知道你係咪知道,哈靈頓小姐,我曾經幾咁努力地想讓波莉安娜嚟同我一起住。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不知道你是否知道,哈靈頓小姐,我曾經多麼努力地想讓波莉安娜來和我一起住。」

passages.original: “With YOU!--Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「同你!——波莉安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「和你!——波莉安娜!」

passages.original: The man winced a little at the tone of her voice; but his own voice was still impersonally cool when he spoke again.
passages.vernacular: 聽到佢嘅語氣,嗰人微微畏縮咗一下;不過佢再次開口時,聲音依然係客觀冷靜嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到她的語氣,那人微微畏縮了一下;可是他再次開口時,聲音依然是客觀冷靜的。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: I wanted to adopt her--legally, you understand; making her my heir, of course.”
passages.vernacular: 我想收養佢——合法收養,你明白;當然,讓佢做我嘅繼承人。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想收養她——合法收養,你明白;當然,讓她做我的繼承人。」

passages.original: The woman in the opposite chair relaxed a little.
passages.vernacular: 對面椅子上嘅女人稍稍放鬆咗啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對面椅子上的女人稍稍放鬆了一點。

passages.original: It came to her, suddenly, what a brilliant future it would have meant for Pollyanna--this adoption; and she wondered if Pollyanna were old enough and mercenary enough--to be tempted by this man's money and position.
passages.vernacular: 佢忽然意識到,呢次收養對波莉安娜意味住幾咁輝煌嘅前程;佢不禁懷疑波莉安娜係咪年紀夠大、夠貪財——會被呢個男人嘅金錢同地位所誘惑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她忽然意識到,這次收養對波莉安娜意味著多麼輝煌的前程;她不禁懷疑波莉安娜是否年紀夠大、夠貪財——會被這個男人的金錢和地位所誘惑。

passages.original: “I am very fond of Pollyanna,” the man was continuing.
passages.vernacular: 「我好鍾意波莉安娜,」嗰人繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我非常喜歡波莉安娜,」那人繼續說。

passages.original: “I am fond of her both for her own sake, and for--her mother's.
passages.vernacular: 「我鍾意佢,既因為佢自己,都因為——佢嘅母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我喜歡她,既因為她自己,也因為——她的母親。

passages.original: I stood ready to give Pollyanna the love that had been twenty-five years in storage.”
passages.vernacular: 我本打算把儲存咗二十五年嘅愛畀波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本打算把儲存了二十五年的愛給波莉安娜。」

passages.original: “LOVE.”

Miss Polly remembered suddenly why SHE had taken this child in the first place--and with the recollection came the remembrance of Pollyanna's own words uttered that very morning: “I love to be called 'dear' by folks that belong to you!”
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐忽然想起咗自己當初點解要收留呢個細路——隨住呢個回憶,佢仲想起咗波莉安娜當天朝早講嘅話:「我鍾意被屬于你嘅人叫『親愛嘅』!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐忽然想起了自己當初為什麼要收留這個孩子——隨著這個回憶,她還想起了波莉安娜當天早上說的話:「我喜歡被屬于你的人叫『親愛的』!」

passages.original: And it was this love-hungry little girl that had been offered the stored-up affection of twenty-five years:--and she was old enough to be tempted by love!
passages.vernacular: 而呢個渴望愛嘅小姑娘,曾被人提議畀予二十五年積蓄嘅情感:——而佢嘅年紀,足以被愛所誘惑!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而這個渴望愛的小姑娘,曾被人提議給予二十五年積蓄的情感:——而她的年紀,足以被愛所誘惑!

passages.original: With a sinking heart Miss Polly realized that.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐沉住心意識到咗呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐沉著心意識到了這一點。

passages.original: With a sinking heart, too, she realized something else: the dreariness of her own future now without Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 佢同樣心頭一沉,仲意識到咗另一件事:冇波莉安娜,自己往後嘅日子將幾咁凄涼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她同樣心頭一沉,還意識到了另一件事:沒有波莉安娜,自己往後的日子將多麼凄涼。

passages.original: “Well?” she said.
passages.vernacular: 「咁?」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼?」她說。

passages.original: And the man, recognizing the self-control that vibrated through the harshness of the tone, smiled sadly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人聽出咗佢嚴厲語調中顫動嘅自制,悲傷地笑咗笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人聽出了她嚴厲語調中顫動的自制,悲傷地笑了笑。

passages.original: “She would not come,” he answered.
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔肯嚟,」佢回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她不肯來,」他回答。

passages.original: “Why?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」

passages.original: “She would not leave you.
passages.vernacular: 「佢唔肯離開你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她不肯離開你。

passages.original: She said you had been so good to her.
passages.vernacular: 佢講你對佢咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說你對她那麼好。

passages.original: She wanted to stay with you--and she said she THOUGHT you wanted her to stay,” he finished, as he pulled himself to his feet.
passages.vernacular: 佢想留喺你身邊——而且佢講佢認為你希望佢留下,」佢講住,站起身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她想留在你身邊——而且她說她認為你希望她留下,」他說著,站起身來。

passages.original: He did not look toward Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇睇波莉小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有看波莉小姐。

passages.original: He turned his face resolutely toward the door.
passages.vernacular: 佢堅決地把臉轉向門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他堅決地把臉轉向門口。

passages.original: But instantly he heard a swift step at his side, and found a shaking hand thrust toward him.
passages.vernacular: 不過即刻,佢聽到身旁響起一陣急促嘅腳步聲,發現一隻顫抖嘅手伸向咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是立刻,他聽到身旁響起一陣急促的腳步聲,發現一隻顫抖的手伸向了他。

passages.original: “When the specialist comes, and I know anything--definite about Pollyanna, I will let you hear from me,” said a trembling voice.
passages.vernacular: 「等專家嚟喇,我知道咗波莉安娜嘅任何確切情況,我會讓你知道嘅,」一個顫抖嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「等專家來了,我知道了波莉安娜的任何確切情況,我會讓你知道的,」一個顫抖的聲音說。

passages.original: “Good-by--and thank you for coming.
passages.vernacular: 「再見——謝謝你嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「再見——謝謝你來。

passages.original: Pollyanna will be pleased.”
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜會高興嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜會高興的。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXV A Waiting Game 第二十五章:等待的日子

passages.original: CH On the day after John Pendleton's call at the Harrington homestead, Miss Polly set herself to the task of preparing Pollyanna for the visit of the specialist.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓拜訪哈靈頓家宅子嘅第二天,波莉小姐著手讓波莉安娜為專家嘅嚟訪做準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓拜訪哈靈頓家宅子的第二天,波莉小姐著手讓波莉安娜為專家的來訪做準備。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, my dear,” she began gently, “we have decided that we want another doctor besides Dr. Warren to see you.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,親愛嘅,」佢溫和地開口,「我哋決定,除咗沃倫醫生,仲要請另一位醫生來畀你睇睇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,親愛的,」她溫和地開口,「我們決定,除了沃倫醫生,還要請另一位醫生來給你看看。

passages.original: Another one might tell us something new to do--to help you get well faster, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 另一位醫生或者會告訴我哋新嘅辦法——幫你更快好起嚟,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一位醫生也許會告訴我們新的辦法——幫你更快好起來,你知道。」

passages.original: A joyous light came to Pollyanna's face.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅臉上露出歡喜嘅光。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的臉上露出歡喜的光。

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton!
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生!

passages.original: Oh, Aunt Polly, I'd so love to have Dr. Chilton!
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉姨媽,我太想要奇爾頓醫生喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉姨媽,我太想要奇爾頓醫生了!

passages.original: I've wanted him all the time, but I was afraid you didn't, on account of his seeing you in the sun parlor that day, you know; so I didn't like to say anything.
passages.vernacular: 我一直都想要佢,不過我怕你唔想,因為嗰天佢喺日光室裡睇見你嘅緣故,你知道;所以我不好意思講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直都想要他,可是我怕你不想,因為那天他在日光室裡看見你的緣故,你知道;所以我不好意思說。

passages.original: But I'm so glad you do want him!”
passages.vernacular: 不過我太高興你都想要佢喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是我太高興你也想要他了!」

passages.original: Aunt Polly's face had turned white, then red, then back to white again.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嘅臉變白,又變紅,然後又變白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽的臉變白,又變紅,然後又變白。

passages.original: But when she answered, she showed very plainly that she was trying to speak lightly and cheerfully.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢回答時,明顯喺努力講得輕鬆愉快些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她回答時,明顯在努力說得輕鬆愉快些。

passages.original: “Oh, no, dear!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,唔係嘅,親愛嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,不是的,親愛的!

passages.original: It wasn't Dr. Chilton at all that I meant.
passages.vernacular: 我講嘅完全唔係奇爾頓醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說的完全不是奇爾頓醫生。

passages.original: It is a new doctor--a very famous doctor from New York, who--who knows a great deal about--about hurts like yours.”
passages.vernacular: 係一位新醫生——一位從紐約嚟嘅好有名嘅醫生,佢——佢好懂得——懂得像你咁樣嘅傷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是一位新醫生——一位從紐約來的很有名的醫生,他——他非常懂得——懂得像你這樣的傷。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's face fell.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅臉沉咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的臉沉了下來。

passages.original: “I don't believe he knows half so much as Dr. Chilton.”
passages.vernacular: 「我不相信佢懂嘅有奇爾頓醫生嘅一半多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不相信他懂的有奇爾頓醫生的一半多。」

passages.original: “Oh, yes, he does, I'm sure, dear.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢懂嘅,我敢肯定,親愛嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,他懂的,我敢肯定,親愛的。」

passages.original: “But it was Dr. Chilton who doctored Mr. Pendleton's broken leg, Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過畀潘德爾頓先生治斷腿嘅係奇爾頓醫生呀,波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是給潘德爾頓先生治斷腿的是奇爾頓醫生呀,波莉姨媽。

passages.original: If--if you don't mind VERY much, I WOULD LIKE to have Dr. Chilton--truly I would!”
passages.vernacular: 要係——要係你唔係好介意嘅話,我真想要奇爾頓醫生——真嘅想!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要是——要是你不是非常介意的話,我真想要奇爾頓醫生——真的想!」

passages.original: A distressed color suffused Miss Polly's face.
passages.vernacular: 一陣為難嘅紅暈漫上波莉小姐嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一陣為難的紅暈漫上波莉小姐的臉。

passages.original: For a moment she did not speak at all; then she said gently--though yet with a touch of her old stern decisiveness:
passages.vernacular: 有一會兒佢乜嘢都冇講;然後佢溫和地講——雖然仍帶住往日嗰種嚴厲嘅果斷:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一會兒她什麼也沒說;然後她溫和地說——雖然仍帶著往日那種嚴厲的果斷:

passages.original: “But I do mind, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「不過我介意,波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我介意,波莉安娜。

passages.original: I mind very much.
passages.vernacular: 我好介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常介意。

passages.original: I would do anything--almost anything for you, my dear; but I--for reasons which I do not care to speak of now, I don't wish Dr. Chilton called in on--on this case.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅,我乜嘢事都愿意為你做——幾乎乜嘢事;不過,因為啲我而家唔想講嘅原因,我不希望請奇爾頓醫生來睇——睇呢個病例。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的,我什麼事都愿意為你做——幾乎什麼事;可是,因為一些我現在不想說的原因,我不希望請奇爾頓醫生來看——看這個病例。

passages.original: And believe me, he can NOT know so much about--about your trouble, as this great doctor does, who will come from New York to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 而且相信我,佢唔可能像聽日從紐約嚟嘅呢位大醫生嗰樣懂得——懂得你嘅病情。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且相信我,他不可能像明天從紐約來的這位大醫生那樣懂得——懂得你的病情。」

passages.original: Pollyanna still looked unconvinced.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜依然一臉不信服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜依然一臉不信服。

passages.original: “But, Aunt Polly, if you LOVED Dr. Chilton--”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,波莉姨媽,要係你愛奇爾頓醫生——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,波莉姨媽,要是你愛奇爾頓醫生——」

passages.original: “WHAT, Pollyanna?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢,波莉安娜?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼,波莉安娜?」

passages.original: Aunt Polly's voice was very sharp now.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嘅聲音而家好尖銳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽的聲音現在非常尖銳。

passages.original: Her cheeks were very red, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅雙頰都漲得通紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的雙頰也漲得通紅。

passages.original: “I say, if you loved Dr. Chilton, and didn't love the other one,” sighed Pollyanna, “seems to me that would make some difference in the good he would do; and I love Dr. Chilton.”
passages.vernacular: 「我係講,要係你愛奇爾頓醫生,不愛另外嗰位,」波莉安娜嘆道,「我覺得呢對佢能起嘅作用係會有些不同嘅;而我愛奇爾頓醫生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是說,要是你愛奇爾頓醫生,不愛另外那位,」波莉安娜嘆道,「我覺得這對他能起的作用是會有些不同的;而我愛奇爾頓醫生。」

passages.original: The nurse entered the room at that moment, and Aunt Polly rose to her feet abruptly, a look of relief on her face.
passages.vernacular: 就喺呢陣護士走進咗房間,波莉姨媽猛地站起身嚟,臉上帶住如釋重負嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在這時護士走進了房間,波莉姨媽猛地站起身來,臉上帶著如釋重負的神情。

passages.original: “I am very sorry, Pollyanna,” she said, a little stiffly; “but I'm afraid you'll have to let me be the judge, this time.
passages.vernacular: 「我好抱歉,波莉安娜,」佢有點生硬地講;「不過恐怕呢次你得讓我嚟做主。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我很抱歉,波莉安娜,」她有點生硬地說;「不過恐怕這次你得讓我來做主。

passages.original: Besides, it's already arranged.
passages.vernacular: 而且,已經安排好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,已經安排好了。

passages.original: The New York doctor is coming to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 紐約嘅醫生聽日就嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 紐約的醫生明天就來。」

passages.original: As it happened, however, the New York doctor did not come “to-morrow.”
passages.vernacular: 然而,碰巧嘅係,紐約嘅醫生并冇喺「聽日」到來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,碰巧的是,紐約的醫生并沒有在「明天」到來。

passages.original: At the last moment a telegram told of an unavoidable delay owing to the sudden illness of the specialist himself.
passages.vernacular: 最後一刻,一封電報通知講,因專家本人突然生病,不可避免地要推遲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最後一刻,一封電報通知說,因專家本人突然生病,不可避免地要推遲。

passages.original: This led Pollyanna into a renewed pleading for the substitution of Dr. Chilton--“which would be so easy now, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 呢使得波莉安娜重新懇求換成奇爾頓醫生——「而家換起嚟好容易嘅,你知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使得波莉安娜重新懇求換成奇爾頓醫生——「現在換起來很容易的,你知道。」

passages.original: But as before, Aunt Polly shook her head and said “no, dear,” very decisively, yet with a still more anxious assurance that she would do anything--anything but that--to please her dear Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 不過同之前一樣,波莉姨媽搖搖頭,好堅決地講「不行,親愛嘅」,同時更加焦急地保證,佢愿意為親愛嘅波莉安娜做任何事——除咗呢件事以外嘅任何事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是和之前一樣,波莉姨媽搖搖頭,非常堅決地說「不行,親愛的」,同時更加焦急地保證,她愿意為親愛的波莉安娜做任何事——除了這件事以外的任何事。

passages.original: As the days of waiting passed, one by one, it did indeed, seem that Aunt Polly was doing everything (but that) that she could do to please her niece.
passages.vernacular: 等待嘅日子一天天過去,波莉姨媽確實似乎喺竭盡所能(除咗嗰件事)去討外甥女嘅歡心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等待的日子一天天過去,波莉姨媽確實似乎在竭盡所能(除了那件事)去討外甥女的歡心。

passages.original: “I wouldn't 'a' believed it--you couldn't 'a' made me believe it,” Nancy said to Old Tom one morning.
passages.vernacular: 「我真唔會相信嘅——你點講我都唔會相信嘅,」一天朝早南希對老湯姆講,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真不會相信的——你怎麼說我也不會相信的,」一天早上南希對老湯姆說,

passages.original: “There don't seem ter be a minute in the day that Miss Polly ain't jest hangin' 'round waitin' ter do somethin' for that blessed lamb if 'tain't more than ter let in the cat--an' her what wouldn't let Fluff nor Buff up-stairs for love nor money a week ago; an' now she lets 'em tumble all over the bed jest 'cause it pleases Miss Pollyanna!
passages.vernacular: 「好像一天裡冇一分鐘,波莉小姐不喺嗰兒轉嚟轉去,等住畀嗰可愛嘅小羊羔做點乜嘢,邊怕只係放進嚟一隻貓——呢個人一星期前,再點好話歹話都唔肯讓弗拉夫同巴夫上樓;而家卻讓佢哋喺床上到處打滾,就因為波莉安娜小姐高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好像一天裡沒有一分鐘,波莉小姐不在那兒轉來轉去,等著給那可愛的小羊羔做點什麼,哪怕只是放進來一隻貓——這個人一星期前,再怎麼好話歹話也不肯讓弗拉夫和巴夫上樓;現在卻讓它們在床上到處打滾,就因為波莉安娜小姐高興!

passages.original: “An' when she ain't doin' nothin' else, she's movin' them little glass danglers 'round ter diff'rent winders in the room so the sun'll make the 'rainbows dance,' as that blessed child calls it.
passages.vernacular: 「而且佢不做別嘅事嘅時候,就把嗰啲小玻璃吊墜挪到房間裡不同嘅窗子上,讓太陽照出『跳舞嘅彩虹』,嗰個可愛嘅細路係咁叫嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且她不做別的事的時候,就把那些小玻璃吊墜挪到房間裡不同的窗子上,讓太陽照出『跳舞的彩虹』,那個可愛的孩子是這麼叫的。

passages.original: She's sent Timothy down ter Cobb's greenhouse three times for fresh flowers--an' that besides all the posies fetched in ter her, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢三次派蒂莫西去科布嘅溫室買新鮮嘅花——呢仲不算別人送畀佢嘅嗰啲花。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她三次派蒂莫西去科布的溫室買新鮮的花——這還不算別人送給她的那些花。

passages.original: An' the other day, if I didn't find her sittin' 'fore the bed with the nurse actually doin' her hair, an' Miss Pollyanna lookin' on an' bossin' from the bed, her eyes all shinin' an' happy.
passages.vernacular: 前幾天,我竟睇見佢坐喺床前,護士喺畀佢梳頭,而波莉安娜小姐躺喺床上睇住,發號施令,眼睛閃閃發亮,開心極喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 前幾天,我竟看見她坐在床前,護士在給她梳頭,而波莉安娜小姐躺在床上看著,發號施令,眼睛閃閃發亮,開心極了。

passages.original: An' I declare ter goodness, if Miss Polly hain't wore her hair like that every day now--jest ter please that blessed child!”
passages.vernacular: 我老天爺,波莉小姐而家每天都嗰樣梳頭——就為了讓嗰個可愛嘅細路高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我老天爺,波莉小姐現在每天都那樣梳頭——就為了讓那個可愛的孩子高興!」

passages.original: Old Tom chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆咯咯笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆咯咯笑了。

passages.original: “Well, it strikes me Miss Polly herself ain't lookin' none the worse--for wearin' them 'ere curls 'round her forehead,” he observed dryly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我睇波莉小姐自己都冇因為額頭前面垂住嗰啲捲髮就顯得更糟,」佢冷冷地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我看波莉小姐自己也沒有因為額頭前面垂著那些捲髮就顯得更糟,」他冷冷地說。

passages.original: “'Course she ain't,” retorted Nancy, indignantly.
passages.vernacular: 「當然冇,」南希憤憤地回嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然沒有,」南希憤憤地回嘴。

passages.original: “She looks like FOLKS, now.
passages.vernacular: 「佢而家睇起嚟像個正常人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她現在看起來像個正常人。

passages.original: She's actually almost--”
passages.vernacular: 佢簡直幾乎——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她簡直幾乎——」

passages.original: “Keerful, now, Nancy!” interrupted the old man, with a slow grin.
passages.vernacular: 「小心點,南希!」老人慢吞吞地咧嘴笑住打斷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小心點,南希!」老人慢吞吞地咧嘴笑著打斷道。

passages.original: “You know what you said when I told ye she was handsome once.”
passages.vernacular: 「你記得我告訴你佢年輕時漂亮嘅時候,你係點講嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你記得我告訴你她年輕時漂亮的時候,你是怎麼說的。」

passages.original: Nancy shrugged her shoulders.
passages.vernacular: 南希聳聳肩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希聳聳肩。

passages.original: “Oh, she ain't handsome, of course; but I will own up she don't look like the same woman, what with the ribbons an' lace jiggers Miss Pollyanna makes her wear 'round her neck.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢當然不漂亮;不過我得承認,佢睇起嚟不像同一個人喇,波莉安娜小姐讓佢喺脖子上戴上絲帶同花邊飾物嘛。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她當然不漂亮;不過我得承認,她看起來不像同一個人了,波莉安娜小姐讓她在脖子上戴上絲帶和花邊飾物嘛。」

passages.original: “I told ye so,” nodded the man.
passages.vernacular: 「我跟你講過嘅,」老人點點頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我跟你說過的,」老人點點頭說。

passages.original: “I told ye she wa'n't--old.”
passages.vernacular: 「我跟你講過佢不——老。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我跟你說過她不——老。」

passages.original: Nancy laughed.
passages.vernacular: 南希笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希笑了。

passages.original: “Well, I'll own up she HAIN'T got quite so good an imitation of it--as she did have, 'fore Miss Pollyanna come.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我承認佢而家冇咁像老太太喇——比波莉安娜小姐嚟之前好多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我承認她現在沒那麼像老太太了——比波莉安娜小姐來之前好多了。

passages.original: Say, Mr. Tom, who WAS her A lover?
passages.vernacular: 哎,湯姆先生,佢嘅嗰個情人到底係邊個啊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,湯姆先生,她的那個情人到底是誰啊?

passages.original: I hain't found that out, yet; I hain't, I hain't!”
passages.vernacular: 我仲冇打聽出嚟;仲冇,仲冇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還沒打聽出來;還沒有,還沒有!」

passages.original: “Hain't ye?” asked the old man, with an odd look on his face.
passages.vernacular: 「仲冇?」老人臉上帶住古怪嘅神情問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還沒有?」老人臉上帶著古怪的神情問。

passages.original: “Well, I guess ye won't then from me.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我睇你從我呢兒係打聽唔到嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我看你從我這兒是打聽不到的。」

passages.original: “Oh, Mr. Tom, come on, now,” wheedled the girl.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,湯姆先生,嚟嘛,」姑娘哄住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,湯姆先生,來嘛,」姑娘哄著說。

passages.original: “Ye see, there ain't many folks here that I CAN ask.”
passages.vernacular: 「你睇,呢兒我能問嘅人不多。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看,這兒我能問的人不多。」

passages.original: “Maybe not.
passages.vernacular: 「或者吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許吧。

passages.original: But there's one, anyhow, that ain't answerin',” grinned Old Tom.
passages.vernacular: 不過有一個,反正是唔會回答你嘅,」老湯姆咧嘴笑道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過有一個,反正是不會回答你的,」老湯姆咧嘴笑道。

passages.original: Then, abruptly, the light died from his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢眼裡嘅光驟然熄滅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,他眼裡的光驟然熄滅了。

passages.original: “How is she, ter-day--the little gal?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢今日點樣——嗰個小姑娘?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她今天怎麼樣——那個小姑娘?」

passages.original: Nancy shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 南希搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希搖搖頭。

passages.original: Her face, too, had sobered.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉都嚴肅起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉也嚴肅起來。

passages.original: “Just the same, Mr. Tom.
passages.vernacular: 「定係老樣子,湯姆先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「還是老樣子,湯姆先生。

passages.original: There ain't no special diff'rence, as I can see--or anybody, I guess.
passages.vernacular: 冇乜嘢特別嘅變化,就我所見——或者任何人所見,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒什麼特別的變化,就我所見——或者任何人所見,我想。

passages.original: She jest lays there an' sleeps an' talks some, an' tries ter smile an' be 'glad' 'cause the sun sets or the moon rises, or some other such thing, till it's enough ter make yer heart break with achin'.”
passages.vernacular: 佢就躺喺嗰兒瞓覺,講講話,努力微笑住,為太陽落咗、月亮升咗或者別嘅乜嘢事而『高興』,讓人心都碎喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就躺在那兒睡覺,說說話,努力微笑著,為太陽落了、月亮升了或者別的什麼事而『高興』,讓人心都碎了。」

passages.original: “I know; it's the 'game'--bless her sweet heart!” nodded Old Tom, blinking a little.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道;呢個就係嗰個『遊戲』——真係個好心腸嘅細路!」老湯姆點點頭,眨咗眨眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道;這就是那個『遊戲』——真是個好心腸的孩子!」老湯姆點點頭,眨了眨眼睛。

passages.original: “She told YOU, then, too, about that 'ere--game?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁講佢都跟你講過嗰個——遊戲?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這麼說她也跟你講過那個——遊戲?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的。

passages.original: She told me long ago.”
passages.vernacular: 佢好久以前就告訴我喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她很久以前就告訴我了。」

passages.original: The old man hesitated, then went on, his lips twitching a little.
passages.vernacular: 老人猶豫咗一下,然後接住講,嘴唇微微抽動住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人猶豫了一下,然後接著說,嘴唇微微抽動著。

passages.original: “I was growlin' one day 'cause I was so bent up and crooked; an' what do ye s'pose the little thing said?”
passages.vernacular: 「有一天我因為自己彎腰駝背而發牢騷;你猜嗰小嘢點講?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「有一天我因為自己彎腰駝背而發牢騷;你猜那小東西怎麼說?」

passages.original: “I couldn't guess.
passages.vernacular: 「我猜不出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我猜不出來。

passages.original: I wouldn't think she could find ANYTHIN' about THAT ter be glad about!”
passages.vernacular: 我想佢唔可能喺嗰件事裡找出乜嘢值得高興嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想她不可能在那件事裡找出什麼值得高興的!」

passages.original: “She did.
passages.vernacular: 「佢找到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她找到了。

passages.original: She said I could be glad, anyhow, that I didn't have ter STOOP SO FAR TER DO MY WEEDIN' 'cause I was already bent part way over.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講,不管點樣我可以高興,因為我唔使彎咁低去除草,我本來就已經彎咗一半喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說,不管怎樣我可以高興,因為我不必彎那麼低去除草,我本來就已經彎了一半了。」

passages.original: Nancy gave a wistful laugh.
passages.vernacular: 南希發出一聲惆悵嘅笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希發出一聲惆悵的笑。

passages.original: “Well, I ain't surprised, after all.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我啲都不奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我一點也不奇怪。

passages.original: You might know she'd find somethin'.
passages.vernacular: 你該知道佢總能找出點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你該知道她總能找出點什麼。

passages.original: We've been playin' it--that game--since almost the first, 'cause there wa'n't no one else she could play it with--though she did speak of--her aunt.”
passages.vernacular: 我哋一直喺玩——嗰個遊戲——幾乎從一開始,因為佢冇別人可以一起玩——雖然佢提過——佢姨媽。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一直在玩——那個遊戲——幾乎從一開始,因為她沒有別人可以一起玩——雖然她提過——她姨媽。」

passages.original: “MISS POLLY!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉小姐!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉小姐!」

passages.original: Nancy chuckled.
passages.vernacular: 南希咯咯笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希咯咯笑了。

passages.original: “I guess you hain't got such an awful diff'rent opinion o' the mistress than I have,” she bridled.
passages.vernacular: 「我想你對女主人嘅睇法,同我嘅睇法都冇多大不同吧,」佢昂住頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想你對女主人的看法,和我的看法也沒有多大不同吧,」她昂著頭說。

passages.original: Old Tom stiffened.
passages.vernacular: 老湯姆僵咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老湯姆僵了一下。

passages.original: “I was only thinkin' 'twould be--some of a surprise--to her,” he explained with dignity.
passages.vernacular: 「我只係喺想嗰會讓佢——有些食驚,」佢莊重地解釋道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我只是在想那會讓她——有些吃驚,」他莊重地解釋道。

passages.original: “Well, yes, I guess 'twould be--THEN,” retorted Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,係啊,我想嗰時候會——」南希回嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,是啊,我想那時候會——」南希回嘴。

passages.original: “I ain't sayin' what 'twould be NOW.
passages.vernacular: 「我而家可唔敢講會點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我現在可不敢說會怎麼樣。

passages.original: I'd believe anythin' o' the mistress now--even that she'd take ter playin' it herself!”
passages.vernacular: 我而家對女主人乜嘢事都相信——甚至相信佢自己都會開始玩呢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在對女主人什麼事都相信——甚至相信她自己也會開始玩呢!」

passages.original: “But hain't the little gal told her--ever?
passages.vernacular: 「不過嗰小姑娘從來冇告訴過佢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是那小姑娘從來沒告訴過她嗎?

passages.original: She's told ev'ry one else, I guess.
passages.vernacular: 佢大概告訴咗所有人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她大概告訴了所有人。

passages.original: I'm hearin' of it ev'rywhere, now, since she was hurted,” said Tom.
passages.vernacular: 自從佢受傷後,我到處都聽講喇,」湯姆講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從她受傷後,我到處都聽說了,」湯姆說。

passages.original: “Well, she didn't tell Miss Polly,” rejoined Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢冇告訴波莉小姐,」南希回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她沒告訴波莉小姐,」南希回答。

passages.original: “Miss Pollyanna told me long ago that she couldn't tell her, 'cause her aunt didn't like ter have her talk about her father; an' 'twas her father's game, an' she'd have ter talk about him if she did tell it.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜小姐好久以前告訴我,佢冇法告訴佢,因為佢姨媽不鍾意佢談佢父親;而呢個係佢父親嘅遊戲,佢要講就得談到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜小姐很久以前告訴我,她沒法告訴她,因為她姨媽不喜歡她談她父親;而這是她父親的遊戲,她要講就得談到他。

passages.original: So she never told her.”
passages.vernacular: 所以佢從來冇講過。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以她從來沒講過。」

passages.original: “Oh, I see, I see.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我明白喇,我明白喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我明白了,我明白了。」

passages.original: The old man nodded his head slowly.
passages.vernacular: 老人慢慢地點住頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老人慢慢地點著頭。

passages.original: “They was always bitter against the minister chap--all of 'em, 'cause he took Miss Jennie away from 'em.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋一直都恨嗰個牧師——所有嘅人,因為佢帶走咗詹妮小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們一直都恨那個牧師——所有的人,因為他帶走了詹妮小姐。

passages.original: An' Miss Polly--young as she was--couldn't never forgive him; she was that fond of Miss Jennie--in them days.
passages.vernacular: 而波莉小姐——咁年輕——始終冇法原諒佢;嗰時候佢咁鍾意詹妮小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而波莉小姐——那麼年輕——始終沒法原諒他;那時候她那麼喜歡詹妮小姐。

passages.original: I see, I see.
passages.vernacular: 我明白喇,我明白喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明白了,我明白了。

passages.original: 'Twas a bad mess,” he sighed, as he turned away.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係一團糟,」佢嘆道,轉身走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是一團糟,」他嘆道,轉身走開了。

passages.original: “Yes, 'twas--all 'round, all 'round,” sighed Nancy in her turn, as she went back to her kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,係嘅——各方面都係,各方面都係,」南希都嘆息道,回到咗佢嘅廚房。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,是的——各方面都是,各方面都是,」南希也嘆息道,回到了她的廚房。

passages.original: For no one were those days of waiting easy.
passages.vernacular: 對邊個來講,呢啲等待嘅日子都不輕鬆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對誰來說,這些等待的日子都不輕鬆。

passages.original: The nurse tried to look cheerful, but her eyes were troubled.
passages.vernacular: 護士努力顯得愉快,不過佢嘅眼裡有憂慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士努力顯得愉快,可是她的眼裡有憂慮。

passages.original: The doctor was openly nervous and impatient.
passages.vernacular: 醫生明顯地緊張而急躁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生明顯地緊張而急躁。

passages.original: Miss Polly said little; but even the softening waves of hair about her face, and the becoming laces at her throat, could not hide the fact that she was growing thin and pale.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐話好少;不過即使係佢臉旁嗰柔和嘅捲髮,同頸上嗰好睇嘅花邊,都掩蓋不咗佢日漸消瘦蒼白嘅事實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐話很少;可是即使是她臉旁那柔和的捲髮,和頸上那好看的花邊,也掩蓋不了她日漸消瘦蒼白的事實。

passages.original: As to Pollyanna--Pollyanna petted the dog, smoothed the cat's sleek head, admired the flowers and ate the fruits and jellies that were sent in to her; and returned innumerable cheery answers to the many messages of love and inquiry that were brought to her bedside.
passages.vernacular: 至于波莉安娜——波莉安娜撫摸住狗,撫平貓光滑嘅頭,欣賞住送到佢身邊嘅花,食住送畀佢嘅水果同果凍;并對許多送到床頭嘅關愛同問候嘅口信,畀出無數歡快嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至于波莉安娜——波莉安娜撫摸著狗,撫平貓光滑的頭,欣賞著送到她身邊的花,吃著送給她的水果和果凍;并對許多送到床頭的關愛和問候的口信,給出無數歡快的回答。

passages.original: But she, too, grew pale and thin; and the nervous activity of the poor little hands and arms only emphasized the pitiful motionlessness of the once active little feet and legs now lying so woefully quiet under the blankets.
passages.vernacular: 但係佢都變得蒼白消瘦;嗰雙可憐嘅小手同手臂神經質嘅忙碌,只係更凸顯咗嗰曾經活躍嘅小腳同小腿,如今喺毯子下悲哀地靜止不動嘅可憐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是她也變得蒼白消瘦;那雙可憐的小手和手臂神經質的忙碌,只是更凸顯了那曾經活躍的小腳和小腿,如今在毯子下悲哀地靜止不動的可憐。

passages.original: As to the game--Pollyanna told Nancy these days how glad she was going to be when she could go to school again, go to see Mrs. Snow, go to call on Mr. Pendleton, and go to ride with Dr. Chilton nor did she seem to realize that all this “gladness” was in the future, not the present.
passages.vernacular: 至于遊戲——呢幾天波莉安娜告訴南希,等佢又能去上學、去睇斯諾太太、去拜訪潘德爾頓先生、同奇爾頓醫生一起去兜風嘅時候,佢會有多高興——佢似乎冇意識到,所有呢啲「高興」都喺將來,而唔係而家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至于遊戲——這幾天波莉安娜告訴南希,等她又能去上學、去看斯諾太太、去拜訪潘德爾頓先生、和奇爾頓醫生一起去兜風的時候,她會有多高興——她似乎沒有意識到,所有這些「高興」都在將來,而不是現在。

passages.original: Nancy, however, did realize it--and cry about it, when she was alone.
passages.vernacular: 不過南希意識到喇——而且一個人嘅時候就為此哭泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過南希意識到了——而且一個人的時候就為此哭泣。

chapters.title: Ch. XXVI A Door Ajar 第二十六章:虛掩的門

passages.original: CH Just a week from the time Dr. Mead, the specialist, was first expected, he came.
passages.vernacular: 就喺原本預定專家米德醫生到來嘅整整一週之後,佢嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在原本預定專家米德醫生到來的整整一週之後,他來了。

passages.original: He was a tall, broad-shouldered man with kind gray eyes, and a cheerful smile.
passages.vernacular: 佢係個高個子、寬肩膀嘅男人,有一雙和藹嘅灰眼睛同一個開朗嘅笑容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個高個子、寬肩膀的男人,有一雙和藹的灰眼睛和一個開朗的笑容。

passages.original: Pollyanna liked him at once, and told him so.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜一下子就鍾意上咗佢,并且告訴咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜一下子就喜歡上了他,并且告訴了他。

passages.original: “You look quite a lot like MY doctor, you see,” she added engagingly.
passages.vernacular: 「你睇上去好像我嘅醫生,你知道,」佢討人鍾意地補充道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你看上去很像我的醫生,你知道,」她討人喜歡地補充道。

passages.original: “YOUR doctor?”
passages.vernacular: 「你嘅醫生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你的醫生?」

passages.original: Dr. Mead glanced in evident surprise at Dr. Warren, talking with the nurse a few feet away.
passages.vernacular: 米德醫生明顯驚訝地瞥咗一眼幾步遠處正同護士講話嘅沃倫醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 米德醫生明顯驚訝地瞥了一眼幾步遠處正和護士說話的沃倫醫生。

passages.original: Dr. Warren was a small, brown-eyed man with a pointed brown beard.
passages.vernacular: 沃倫醫生係個矮小嘅男人,棕色嘅眼睛,留住尖尖嘅棕色鬍鬚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃倫醫生是個矮小的男人,棕色的眼睛,留著尖尖的棕色鬍鬚。

passages.original: “Oh, THAT isn't my doctor,” smiled Pollyanna, divining his thought.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,嗰唔係我嘅醫生,」波莉安娜猜到咗佢嘅想法,微笑住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,那不是我的醫生,」波莉安娜猜到了他的想法,微笑著說。

passages.original: “Dr. Warren is Aunt Polly's doctor.
passages.vernacular: 「沃倫醫生係波莉姨媽嘅醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沃倫醫生是波莉姨媽的醫生。

passages.original: My doctor is Dr. Chilton.”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅醫生係奇爾頓醫生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的醫生是奇爾頓醫生。」

passages.original: “Oh-h!” said Dr. Mead, a little oddly, his eyes resting on Miss Polly, who, with a vivid blush, had turned hastily away.
passages.vernacular: 「哦——!」米德醫生講,語氣有點奇怪,目光落喺波莉小姐身上,佢臉頰緋紅,急忙轉過身去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——!」米德醫生說,語氣有點奇怪,目光落在波莉小姐身上,她臉頰緋紅,急忙轉過身去。

passages.original: “Yes.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。」

passages.original: Pollyanna hesitated, then continued with her usual truthfulness.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜猶豫咗一下,然後照例誠實地繼續講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜猶豫了一下,然後照例誠實地繼續說。

passages.original: “You see, I wanted Dr. Chilton all the time, but Aunt Polly wanted you.
passages.vernacular: 「你瞧,我一直想要奇爾頓醫生,可波莉姨媽想要你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你瞧,我一直想要奇爾頓醫生,可波莉姨媽想要你。

passages.original: She said you knew more than Dr. Chilton, anyway about--about broken legs like mine.
passages.vernacular: 佢講你懂得比奇爾頓醫生多,不管點樣,關于——關于像我咁樣嘅斷腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說你懂得比奇爾頓醫生多,不管怎樣,關于——關于像我這樣的斷腿。

passages.original: And of course if you do, I can be glad for that.
passages.vernacular: 當然,如果你真嘅懂得多,我就可以為此高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,如果你真的懂得多,我就可以為此高興了。

passages.original: Do you?”
passages.vernacular: 你係嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是嗎?」

passages.original: A swift something crossed the doctor's face that Pollyanna could not quite translate.
passages.vernacular: 一種波莉安娜不太能解讀嘅神情飛快地掠過醫生嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一種波莉安娜不太能解讀的神情飛快地掠過醫生的臉。

passages.original: “Only time can tell that, little girl,” he said gently; then he turned a grave face toward Dr. Warren, who had just come to the bedside.
passages.vernacular: 「呢只有時間才能講明,小姑娘。」佢溫和地講;然後佢把一張嚴肅嘅臉轉向剛走到床邊嘅沃倫醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這只有時間才能說明,小姑娘。」他溫和地說;然後他把一張嚴肅的臉轉向剛走到床邊的沃倫醫生。

passages.original: Every one said afterward that it was the cat that did it.
passages.vernacular: 後來每個人都講,係嗰隻貓惹嘅禍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後來每個人都說,是那隻貓惹的禍。

passages.original: Certainly, if Fluffy had not poked an insistent paw and nose against Pollyanna's unlatched door, the door would not have swung noiselessly open on its hinges until it stood perhaps a foot ajar; and if the door had not been open, Pollyanna would not have heard her aunt's words.
passages.vernacular: 當然,要唔係弗拉菲用爪子同鼻子執拗地頂住波莉安娜冇插上門閂嘅門,嗰扇門就唔會無聲地喺合頁上轉開,直到半開住大約一英尺;而如果門唔係開住嘅,波莉安娜就唔會聽到姨媽嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,要不是弗拉菲用爪子和鼻子執拗地頂著波莉安娜沒有插上門閂的門,那扇門就不會無聲地在合頁上轉開,直到半開著大約一英尺;而如果門不是開著的,波莉安娜就不會聽到姨媽的話。

passages.original: In the hall the two doctors, the nurse, and Miss Polly stood talking.
passages.vernacular: 喺走廊裡,兩位醫生、護士同波莉小姐站住交談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在走廊裡,兩位醫生、護士和波莉小姐站著交談。

passages.original: In Pollyanna's room Fluffy had just jumped to the bed with a little purring “meow” of joy when through the open door sounded clearly and sharply Aunt Polly's agonized exclamation.
passages.vernacular: 喺波莉安娜嘅房間裡,弗拉菲剛帶住一聲歡喜嘅「喵」呼嚕住跳到床上,呢陣從敞開嘅門裡清晰而尖銳地傳嚟咗波莉姨媽痛苦嘅呼喊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在波莉安娜的房間裡,弗拉菲剛帶著一聲歡喜的「喵」呼嚕著跳到床上,這時從敞開的門裡清晰而尖銳地傳來了波莉姨媽痛苦的呼喊。

passages.original: “Not that!
passages.vernacular: 「唔會吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不會吧!

passages.original: Doctor, not that!
passages.vernacular: 醫生,唔會吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生,不會吧!

passages.original: You don't mean--the child--will NEVER WALK again!”
passages.vernacular: 你唔係講——呢細路——再都唔能夠走路喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是說——這孩子——再也不能走路了!」

passages.original: It was all confusion then.
passages.vernacular: 接住一片混亂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 接著一片混亂。

passages.original: First, from the bedroom came Pollyanna's terrified “Aunt Polly Aunt Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 首先,臥室裡傳嚟波莉安娜驚恐嘅呼喊:「波莉姨媽!波莉姨媽!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先,臥室裡傳來波莉安娜驚恐的呼喊:「波莉姨媽!波莉姨媽!」

passages.original: Then Miss Polly, seeing the open door and realizing that her words had been heard, gave a low little moan and--for the first time in her life--fainted dead away.
passages.vernacular: 然後波莉小姐睇到咗敞開嘅門,意識到自己嘅話被聽到喇,發出一聲低低嘅呻吟,并且——生平第一次——昏咗過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後波莉小姐看到了敞開的門,意識到自己的話被聽到了,發出一聲低低的呻吟,并且——生平第一次——昏了過去。

passages.original: The nurse, with a choking “She heard!” stumbled toward the open door.
passages.vernacular: 護士哽咽住講咗一聲「佢聽到喇!」,跌跌撞撞地朝敞開嘅門走去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士哽咽著說了一聲「她聽到了!」,跌跌撞撞地朝敞開的門走去。

passages.original: The two doctors stayed with Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 兩位醫生留下嚟照顧波莉小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩位醫生留下來照顧波莉小姐。

passages.original: Dr. Mead had to stay--he had caught Miss Polly as she fell.
passages.vernacular: 米德醫生唔得不留下——波莉小姐倒下時係佢接住嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 米德醫生不得不留下——波莉小姐倒下時是他接住的。

passages.original: Dr. Warren stood by, helplessly.
passages.vernacular: 沃倫醫生無助地站喺一旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沃倫醫生無助地站在一旁。

passages.original: It was not until Pollyanna cried out again sharply and the nurse closed the door, that the two men, with a despairing glance into each other's eyes, awoke to the immediate duty of bringing the woman in Dr. Mead's arms back to unhappy consciousness.
passages.vernacular: 直到波莉安娜又一次尖叫起嚟,護士把門關上,呢兩個男人才喺絕望地對視一眼之後,醒悟到眼前嘅責任:要把米德醫生懷裡嘅呢個女人喚回到不幸嘅意識中嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到波莉安娜又一次尖叫起來,護士把門關上,這兩個男人才在絕望地對視一眼之後,醒悟到眼前的責任:要把米德醫生懷裡的這個女人喚回到不幸的意識中來。

passages.original: In Pollyanna's room, the nurse had found a purring gray cat on the bed vainly trying to attract the attention of a white-faced, wild-eyed little girl.
passages.vernacular: 喺波莉安娜嘅房間裡,護士發現一隻呼嚕住嘅灰貓喺床上,徒勞地想引起一個臉色蒼白、眼神狂亂嘅小姑娘嘅注意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在波莉安娜的房間裡,護士發現一隻呼嚕著的灰貓在床上,徒勞地想引起一個臉色蒼白、眼神狂亂的小姑娘的注意。

passages.original: “Miss Hunt, please, I want Aunt Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「亨特小姐,求你喇,我要波莉姨媽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「亨特小姐,求你了,我要波莉姨媽。

passages.original: I want her right away, quick, please!”
passages.vernacular: 我即刻就要見佢,快,求你喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我馬上就要見她,快,求你了!」

passages.original: The nurse closed the door and came forward hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 護士關上門,急忙走上前嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士關上門,急忙走上前來。

passages.original: Her face was very pale.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉色好蒼白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的臉色非常蒼白。

passages.original: “She--she can't come just this minute, dear.
passages.vernacular: 「佢——佢呢一刻唔能夠過嚟,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她——她這一刻不能過來,親愛的。

passages.original: She will--a little later.
passages.vernacular: 佢會嘅——過一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她會的——過一會兒。

passages.original: What is it?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼事?

passages.original: Can't I--get it?”
passages.vernacular: 我能唔能夠——幫你攞?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能不能——幫你拿?」

passages.original: Pollyanna shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜搖搖頭。

passages.original: “But I want to know what she said--just now.
passages.vernacular: 「可我想知道佢頭先講咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我想知道她剛才說了什麼。

passages.original: Did you hear her?
passages.vernacular: 你聽到佢講咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽到她說了嗎?

passages.original: I want Aunt Polly--she said something.
passages.vernacular: 我要波莉姨媽——佢講咗點乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要波莉姨媽——她說了點什麼。

passages.original: I want her to tell me 'tisn't true--'tisn't true!”
passages.vernacular: 我要佢告訴我嗰唔係真嘅——唔係真嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要她告訴我那不是真的——不是真的!」

passages.original: The nurse tried to speak, but no words came.
passages.vernacular: 護士想開口,卻講不出話嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士想開口,卻說不出話來。

passages.original: Something in her face sent an added terror to Pollyanna's eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢臉上嘅某種神情使波莉安娜嘅眼裡更添咗幾分恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她臉上的某種神情使波莉安娜的眼裡更添了幾分恐懼。

passages.original: “Miss Hunt, you DID hear her!
passages.vernacular: 「亨特小姐,你確實聽到佢講喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「亨特小姐,你確實聽到她說了!

passages.original: It is true!
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真的!

passages.original: Oh, it isn't true!
passages.vernacular: 哦,呢唔係真嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,這不是真的!

passages.original: You don't mean I can't ever--walk again?”
passages.vernacular: 你唔係講我再都唔能夠——走路咗吧?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不是說我再也不能——走路了吧?」

passages.original: “There, there, dear--don't, don't!” choked the nurse.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,親愛嘅——別咁樣,別咁樣!」護士哽咽住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,親愛的——別這樣,別這樣!」護士哽咽著說。

passages.original: “Perhaps he didn't know.
passages.vernacular: 「或者佢唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許他不知道。

passages.original: Perhaps he was mistaken.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢弄錯喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許他弄錯了。

passages.original: There's lots of things that could happen, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,有好多事情係可能發生嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,有很多事情是可能發生的。」

passages.original: “But Aunt Polly said he did know!
passages.vernacular: 「可波莉姨媽講佢知道!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可波莉姨媽說他知道!

passages.original: She said he knew more than anybody else about--about broken legs like mine!”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢比任何人都懂得——懂得像我咁樣嘅斷腿!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說他比任何人都懂得——懂得像我這樣的斷腿!」

passages.original: “Yes, yes, I know, dear; but all doctors make mistakes sometimes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,係嘅,我知道,親愛嘅;不過醫生有時都會出錯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,是的,我知道,親愛的;不過醫生有時也會出錯。

passages.original: Just--just don't think any more about it now--please don't, dear.”
passages.vernacular: 只係——只係而家唔好再想呢件事喇——請別想喇,親愛嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 只是——只是現在別再想這件事了——請別想了,親愛的。」

passages.original: Pollyanna flung out her arms wildly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜狂亂地伸出雙臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜狂亂地伸出雙臂。

passages.original: “But I can't help thinking about it,” she sobbed.
passages.vernacular: 「可我忍不住要想,」佢抽泣住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可我忍不住要想,」她抽泣著說。

passages.original: “It's all there is now to think about.
passages.vernacular: 「而家只有呢件事好想喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「現在只有這件事好想了。

passages.original: Why, Miss Hunt, how am I going to school, or to see Mr. Pendleton, or Mrs. Snow, or--or anybody?”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,亨特小姐,我點上學,點去睇潘德爾頓先生或者斯諾太太,或者——或者任何人?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,亨特小姐,我怎麼上學,怎麼去看潘德爾頓先生或者斯諾太太,或者——或者任何人?」

passages.original: She caught her breath and sobbed wildly for a moment.
passages.vernacular: 佢喘不過氣嚟,狂亂地哭咗一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她喘不過氣來,狂亂地哭了一會兒。

passages.original: Suddenly she stopped and looked up, a new terror in her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 忽然佢停住喇,抬起頭嚟,眼裡帶住一種新嘅恐懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 忽然她停住了,抬起頭來,眼裡帶著一種新的恐懼。

passages.original: “Why, Miss Hunt, if I can't walk, how am I ever going to be glad for--ANYTHING?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,亨特小姐,如果我唔能夠走路,我仲點能為——任何事情高興?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,亨特小姐,如果我不能走路,我還怎麼能為——任何事情高興?」

passages.original: Miss Hunt did not know “the game;” but she did know that her patient must be quieted, and that at once.
passages.vernacular: 亨特小姐唔知道「嗰個遊戲」;但佢知道必須讓病人安靜下嚟,而且要即刻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 亨特小姐不知道「那個遊戲」;但她知道必須讓病人安靜下來,而且要馬上。

passages.original: In spite of her own perturbation and heartache, her hands had not been idle, and she stood now at the bedside with the quieting powder ready.
passages.vernacular: 盡管佢自己心神不寧、心裡難受,佢嘅手卻一直冇閑住,此刻佢站喺床邊,鎮靜嘅藥粉已經準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盡管她自己心神不寧、心裡難受,她的手卻一直沒閑著,此刻她站在床邊,鎮靜的藥粉已經準備好了。

passages.original: “There, there, dear, just take this,” she soothed; “and by and by we'll be more rested, and we'll see what can be done then.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,親愛嘅,把呢個食喇,」佢安撫道;「過一會兒我哋就休息得好些喇,到時候再睇能點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,親愛的,把這個吃了,」她安撫道;「過一會兒我們就休息得好些了,到時候再看能怎麼辦。

passages.original: Things aren't half as bad as they seem, dear, lots of times, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,親愛嘅,好多時候事情并冇睇上去咁糟嘅一半。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,親愛的,很多時候事情并沒有看上去那麼糟的一半。」

passages.original: Obediently Pollyanna took the medicine, and sipped the water from the glass in Miss Hunt's hand.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜順從地食咗藥,啜飲住亨特小姐手裡杯子裡嘅水。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜順從地吃了藥,啜飲著亨特小姐手裡杯子裡的水。

passages.original: “I know; that sounds like things father used to say,” faltered Pollyanna, blinking off the tears.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道;呢聽起嚟像爸爸以前講過嘅話。」波莉安娜眨住眼睛忍住淚水,支支吾吾地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道;這聽起來像爸爸以前說過的話。」波莉安娜眨著眼睛忍住淚水,支支吾吾地說。

passages.original: “He said there was always something about everything that might be worse; but I reckon he'd never just heard he couldn't ever walk again.
passages.vernacular: 「佢講,每件事裡總有些事情可能更糟;不過我想佢從來冇啱啱聽講自己再都唔能夠走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說,每件事裡總有些事情可能更糟;不過我想他從來沒有剛剛聽說自己再也不能走路。

passages.original: I don't see how there CAN be anything about that, that could be worse--do you?”
passages.vernacular: 我真不明白呢度面仲能有乜嘢更糟嘅——你講呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真不明白這裡面還能有什麼更糟的——你說呢?」

passages.original: Miss Hunt did not reply.
passages.vernacular: 亨特小姐冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 亨特小姐沒有回答。

passages.original: She could not trust herself to speak just then.
passages.vernacular: 佢呢陣無法相信自己能開口講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她這時無法相信自己能開口說話。

chapters.title: Ch. XXVII Two Visits 第二十七章:兩次拜訪

passages.original: CH It was Nancy who was sent to tell Mr. John Pendleton of Dr. Mead's verdict.
passages.vernacular: 被派去把米德醫生嘅診斷告訴約翰·潘德爾頓先生嘅係南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 被派去把米德醫生的診斷告訴約翰·潘德爾頓先生的是南希。

passages.original: Miss Polly had remembered her promise to let him have direct information from the house.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐記得自己答應過讓佢直接得到家裡嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐記得自己答應過讓他直接得到家裡的消息。

passages.original: To go herself, or to write a letter, she felt to be almost equally out of the question.
passages.vernacular: 要親自去,或者寫信,佢覺得幾乎同樣唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要親自去,或者寫信,她覺得幾乎同樣不可能。

passages.original: It occurred to her then to send Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 于係佢想到咗派南希去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 于是她想到了派南希去。

passages.original: There had been a time when Nancy would have rejoiced greatly at this extraordinary opportunity to see something of the House of Mystery and its master.
passages.vernacular: 曾經有一段時間,南希會為呢個難得嘅機會——能一睹神秘之屋及其主人——而興高采烈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 曾經有一段時間,南希會為這個難得的機會——能一睹神秘之屋及其主人——而興高采烈。

passages.original: But to-day her heart was too heavy to, rejoice at anything.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日佢嘅心太沉重喇,對乜嘢都高興不起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是今天她的心太沉重了,對什麼都高興不起來。

passages.original: She scarcely even looked about her at all, indeed, during the few minutes, she waited for Mr. John Pendleton to appear.
passages.vernacular: 喺等約翰·潘德爾頓先生出嚟嘅嗰幾分鐘裡,佢簡直連四下睇一眼都冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在等約翰·潘德爾頓先生出來的那幾分鐘裡,她簡直連四下看一眼都沒有。

passages.original: “I'm Nancy, sir,” she said respectfully, in response to the surprised questioning of his eyes, when he came into the room.
passages.vernacular: 「我係南希,先生。」當佢走進房間,用驚訝嘅目光詢問佢時,佢恭敬地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我是南希,先生。」當他走進房間,用驚訝的目光詢問她時,她恭敬地說。

passages.original: “Miss Harrington sent me to tell you about--Miss Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 「哈靈頓小姐派我嚟告訴你——波莉安娜小姐嘅事。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈靈頓小姐派我來告訴你——波莉安娜小姐的事。」

passages.original: “Well?”
passages.vernacular: 「點樣?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼樣?」

passages.original: In spite of the curt terseness of the word, Nancy quite understood the anxiety that lay behind that short “well?”
passages.vernacular: 盡管呢個詞簡短生硬,南希定係完全明白咗嗰聲簡短嘅「點樣?」背後嘅焦慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 盡管這個詞簡短生硬,南希還是完全明白了那聲簡短的「怎麼樣?」背後的焦慮。

passages.original: “It ain't well, Mr. Pendleton,” she choked.
passages.vernacular: 「不好,潘德爾頓先生。」佢哽咽住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不好,潘德爾頓先生。」她哽咽著說。

passages.original: “You don't mean--” He paused, and she bowed her head miserably.
passages.vernacular: 「你唔係講——」佢頓住喇,佢痛苦地低下咗頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你不是說——」他頓住了,她痛苦地低下了頭。

passages.original: “Yes, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。

passages.original: He says--she can't walk again--never.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講——佢再都唔能夠走路喇——永遠唔能夠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說——她再也不能走路了——永遠不能。」

passages.original: For a moment there was absolute silence in the room; then the man spoke, in a voice shaken with emotion.
passages.vernacular: 屋裡一陣絕對嘅寂靜;然後嗰人開口喇,聲音因激動而顫抖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 屋裡一陣絕對的寂靜;然後那人開口了,聲音因激動而顫抖。

passages.original: “Poor--little--girl!
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅——小——姑娘!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的——小——姑娘!

passages.original: Poor--little--girl!”
passages.vernacular: 可憐嘅——小——姑娘!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可憐的——小——姑娘!」

passages.original: Nancy glanced at him, but dropped her eyes at once.
passages.vernacular: 南希瞥咗佢一眼,又即刻垂下咗眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希瞥了他一眼,又立刻垂下了眼睛。

passages.original: She had not supposed that sour, cross, stern John Pendleton could look like that.
passages.vernacular: 佢從冇想到刻薄、暴躁、嚴厲嘅約翰·潘德爾頓會露出嗰樣嘅神情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從沒想到刻薄、暴躁、嚴厲的約翰·潘德爾頓會露出那樣的神情。

passages.original: In a moment he spoke again, still in the low, unsteady voice.
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒佢又開口喇,聲音依然低沉不穩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒他又開口了,聲音依然低沉不穩。

passages.original: “It seems cruel--never to dance in the sunshine again!
passages.vernacular: 「多殘酷啊——再都唔能夠喺陽光裡跳舞喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「多殘酷啊——再也不能在陽光裡跳舞了!

passages.original: My little prism girl!”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅小棱鏡姑娘!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的小棱鏡姑娘!」

passages.original: There was another silence; then, abruptly, the man asked:
passages.vernacular: 又係一陣沉默;然後嗰人突然問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又是一陣沉默;然後那人突然問:

passages.original: “She herself doesn't know yet--of course--does she?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢自己仲唔知道——當然——對嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她自己還不知道——當然——對嗎?」

passages.original: “But she does, sir.” sobbed Nancy, “an' that's what makes it all the harder.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢知道喇,先生。」南希抽泣住講,「呢才讓一切更加難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她知道了,先生。」南希抽泣著說,「這才讓一切更加難受。

passages.original: She found out--drat that cat!
passages.vernacular: 佢發現喇——該死嘅貓!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她發現了——該死的貓!

passages.original: I begs yer pardon,” apologized the girl, hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,」姑娘連忙道歉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,」姑娘連忙道歉。

passages.original: “It's only that the cat pushed open the door an' Miss Pollyanna overheard 'em talkin'.
passages.vernacular: 「只係嗰隻貓頂開咗門,波莉安娜小姐偷聽到咗佢哋嘅談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「只是那隻貓頂開了門,波莉安娜小姐偷聽到了他們的談話。

passages.original: She found out--that way.”
passages.vernacular: 佢就係嗰樣發現嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她就是那樣發現的。」

passages.original: “Poor--little--girl!” sighed the man again.
passages.vernacular: 「可憐嘅——小——姑娘!」嗰人又嘆息道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可憐的——小——姑娘!」那人又嘆息道。

passages.original: “Yes, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,先生。

passages.original: You'd say so, sir, if you could see her,” choked Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 你要係睇見佢,都會咁講嘅,先生。」南希哽咽住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要是看見她,也會這麼說的,先生。」南希哽咽著說。

passages.original: “I hain't seen her but twice since she knew about it, an' it done me up both times.
passages.vernacular: 「佢知道以後我只見過佢兩次,兩次都讓我心都碎喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她知道以後我只見過她兩次,兩次都讓我心都碎了。

passages.original: Ye see it's all so fresh an' new to her, an' she keeps thinkin' all the time of new things she can't do--NOW.
passages.vernacular: 你瞧,呢一切對佢來講都咁新鮮、咁突然,佢一直喺想佢而家做不咗嘅新事情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瞧,這一切對她來說都那麼新鮮、那麼突然,她一直在想她現在做不了的新事情。

passages.original: It worries her, too, 'cause she can't seem ter be glad--maybe you don't know about her game, though,” broke off Nancy, apologetically.
passages.vernacular: 呢都讓佢發愁,因為佢似乎高興不起嚟喇——不過或者你唔知道佢嘅遊戲,」南希抱歉地打住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這也讓她發愁,因為她似乎高興不起來了——不過也許你不知道她的遊戲,」南希抱歉地打住了。

passages.original: “The 'glad game'?” asked the man.
passages.vernacular: 「『高興遊戲』?」嗰人問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「『高興遊戲』?」那人問。

passages.original: “Oh, yes; she told me of that.”
passages.vernacular: 「哦,係嘅;佢告訴過我呢個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,是的;她告訴過我這個。」

passages.original: “Oh, she did!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,佢告訴你喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,她告訴你了!

passages.original: Well, I guess she has told it generally ter most folks.
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我想佢大概告訴咗大多數人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我想她大概告訴了大多數人。

passages.original: But ye see, now she--she can't play it herself, an' it worries her.
passages.vernacular: 不過你瞧,而家佢——佢自己冇法玩喇,呢讓佢發愁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是你瞧,現在她——她自己沒法玩了,這讓她發愁。

passages.original: She says she can't think of a thing--not a thing about this not walkin' again, ter be glad about.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講,關于再都唔能夠走路呢件事,佢想不出一件事——一件事可以高興嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說,關于再也不能走路這件事,她想不出一件事——一件事可以高興的。」

passages.original: “Well, why should she?” retorted the man, almost savagely.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,佢點解要想得出?」嗰人幾乎兇狠地回嘴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,她為什麼要想得出?」那人幾乎兇狠地回嘴。

passages.original: Nancy shifted her feet uneasily.
passages.vernacular: 南希不安地挪動住腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希不安地挪動著腳。

passages.original: “That's the way I felt, too--till I happened ter think--it WOULD be easier if she could find somethin', ye know.
passages.vernacular: 「我都係咁覺得嘅——直到我碰巧想到——如果佢能找到點乜嘢,會容易些嘅,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我也是這麼覺得的——直到我碰巧想到——如果她能找到點什麼,會容易些的,你知道。

passages.original: So I tried to--to remind her.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我就試住——提醒佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我就試著——提醒她。」

passages.original: “To remind her!
passages.vernacular: 「提醒佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「提醒她!

passages.original: Of what?”
passages.vernacular: 提醒乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提醒什麼?」

passages.original: John Pendleton's voice was still angrily impatient.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓嘅聲音依然惱怒而急躁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓的聲音依然惱怒而急躁。

passages.original: “Of--of how she told others ter play it Mis' Snow, and the rest, ye know--and what she said for them ter do.
passages.vernacular: 「提醒佢——佢點樣叫別人玩呢個遊戲,斯諾太太同其他人,你知道——仲有佢叫佢哋點做嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「提醒她——她怎樣叫別人玩這個遊戲,斯諾太太和其他人,你知道——還有她叫他們怎麼做的。

passages.original: But the poor little lamb just cries, an' says it don't seem the same, somehow.
passages.vernacular: 不過嗰可憐嘅小羊羔只係哭,講唔知點感覺不一樣喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是那可憐的小羊羔只是哭,說不知怎麼感覺不一樣了。

passages.original: She says it's easy ter TELL lifelong invalids how ter be glad, but 'tain't the same thing when you're the lifelong invalid yerself, an' have ter try ter do it.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,告訴一輩子嘅病人點樣高興好容易,不過等你自己成咗一輩子嘅病人,仲得努力去做,就唔係一回事喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說,告訴一輩子的病人怎樣高興很容易,可是等你自己成了一輩子的病人,還得努力去做,就不是一回事了。

passages.original: She says she's told herself over an' over again how glad she is that other folks ain't like her; but that all the time she's sayin' it, she ain't really THINKIN' of anythin' only how she can't ever walk again.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢一遍又一遍地對自己講,佢幾咁高興別人不像佢咁樣;不過佢嘴上講住嘅時候,腦子裡其實乜嘢都冇想,只想住佢再都唔能夠走路喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她一遍又一遍地對自己說,她多麼高興別人不像她這樣;可是她嘴上說著的時候,腦子裡其實什麼也沒想,只想著她再也不能走路了。」

passages.original: Nancy paused, but the man did not speak.
passages.vernacular: 南希停咗下嚟,嗰人冇講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希停了下來,那人沒有說話。

passages.original: He sat with his hand over his eyes.
passages.vernacular: 佢坐住,一隻手捂住眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他坐著,一隻手捂著眼睛。

passages.original: “Then I tried ter remind her how she used ter say the game was all the nicer ter play when--when it was hard,” resumed Nancy, in a dull voice.
passages.vernacular: 「然後我試住提醒佢,佢以前常講呢個遊戲越係難玩,就越好玩,」南希用沉悶嘅聲音接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「然後我試著提醒她,她以前常說這個遊戲越是難玩,就越好玩,」南希用沉悶的聲音接著說。

passages.original: “But she says that, too, is diff'rent--when it really IS hard.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢講嗰都不一樣——當佢真嘅好難嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她說那也不一樣——當它真的很難的時候。

passages.original: An' I must be goin', now, sir,” she broke off abruptly.
passages.vernacular: 我得走喇,先生,」佢突然打住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得走了,先生,」她突然打住說。

passages.original: At the door she hesitated, turned, and asked timidly:
passages.vernacular: 到咗門口,佢猶豫咗一下,轉過身,怯生生地問:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了門口,她猶豫了一下,轉過身,怯生生地問:

passages.original: “I couldn't be tellin' Miss Pollyanna that--that you'd seen Jimmy Bean again, I s'pose, sir, could I?”
passages.vernacular: 「我想我唔能夠告訴波莉安娜小姐,講你又見過吉米·比恩咗吧,先生,可以嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我不能告訴波莉安娜小姐,說你又見過吉米·比恩了吧,先生,可以嗎?」

passages.original: “I don't see how you could--as I haven't seen him,” observed the man a little shortly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白你點能咁講——我又冇見過佢,」嗰人有點生硬地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白你怎麼能這麼說——我又沒見過他,」那人有點生硬地說。

passages.original: “Why?”
passages.vernacular: 「點解?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為什麼?」

passages.original: “Nothin', sir, only--well, ye see, that's one of the things that she was feelin' bad about, that she couldn't take him ter see you, now.
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢,先生,只係——嗯,你瞧,嗰個係佢難過嘅事情之一,佢而家唔能夠帶佢嚟睇你喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒什麼,先生,只是——嗯,你瞧,那是她難過的事情之一,她現在不能帶他來看你了。

passages.original: She said she'd taken him once, but she didn't think he showed off very well that day, and that she was afraid you didn't think he would make a very nice child's presence, after all.
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢帶佢嚟過一次,可佢覺得嗰天佢表現得不太好,佢怕你覺得佢終究唔會係個好好嘅『細路嘅在場』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說她帶他來過一次,可她覺得那天他表現得不太好,她怕你覺得他終究不會是個很好的『孩子的在場』。

passages.original: Maybe you know what she means by that; but I didn't, sir.”
passages.vernacular: 或者你知道佢呢話係乜嘢意思;我可唔知道,先生。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你知道她這話是什麼意思;我可不知道,先生。」

passages.original: “Yes, I know--what she means.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我知道——佢嘅意思。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我知道——她的意思。」

passages.original: “All right, sir.
passages.vernacular: 「好嘅,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好的,先生。

passages.original: It was only that she was wantin' ter take him again, she said, so's ter show ye he really was a lovely child's presence.
passages.vernacular: 佢只係講佢想再帶佢嚟,好讓你睇睇佢真嘅係個可愛嘅『細路嘅在場』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她只是說她想再帶他來,好讓你看看他真的是個可愛的『孩子的在場』。

passages.original: And now she--can't--drat that autymobile!
passages.vernacular: 不過而家佢——唔能夠喇——該死嘅汽車!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是現在她——不能了——該死的汽車!

passages.original: I begs yer pardon, sir.
passages.vernacular: 請原諒,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請原諒,先生。

passages.original: Good-by!”
passages.vernacular: 再見!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再見!」

passages.original: And Nancy fled precipitately.
passages.vernacular: 南希倉促地跑開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希倉促地跑開了。

passages.original: It did not take long for the entire town of Beldingsville to learn that the great New York doctor had said Pollyanna Whittier would never walk again; and certainly never before had the town been so stirred.
passages.vernacular: 冇過多久,整個貝爾丁斯維爾鎮都知道喇:嗰位紐約嘅大醫生講波莉安娜·惠蒂爾再都唔能夠走路喇;而呢鎮子從來冇咁樣震動過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒過多久,整個貝爾丁斯維爾鎮都知道了:那位紐約的大醫生說波莉安娜·惠蒂爾再也不能走路了;而這鎮子從來沒有這樣震動過。

passages.original: Everybody knew by sight now the piquant little freckled face that had always a smile of greeting; and almost everybody knew of the “game” that Pollyanna was playing.
passages.vernacular: 而家每個人都認得嗰張俏皮嘅、長住雀斑嘅小臉,佢總是笑住打招呼;幾乎每個人都知道波莉安娜正在玩嘅嗰個「遊戲」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在每個人都認得那張俏皮的、長著雀斑的小臉,她總是笑著打招呼;幾乎每個人都知道波莉安娜正在玩的那個「遊戲」。

passages.original: To think that now never again would that smiling face be seen on their streets--never again would that cheery little voice proclaim the gladness of some everyday experience!
passages.vernacular: 想到從今以後,喺佢哋嘅街上再都睇唔到嗰張微笑嘅臉——再都聽唔到嗰個歡快嘅小聲音宣告某件日常小事嘅喜悅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想到從今以後,在他們的街上再也看不到那張微笑的臉——再也聽不到那個歡快的小聲音宣告某件日常小事的喜悅!

passages.original: It seemed unbelievable, impossible, cruel.
passages.vernacular: 呢似乎難以置信,唔可能,太殘酷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這似乎難以置信,不可能,太殘酷。

passages.original: In kitchens and sitting rooms, and over back-yard fences women talked of it, and wept openly.
passages.vernacular: 喺廚房裡同起居室裡,喺後院嘅籬笆旁,女人哋議論住呢件事,公然落淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在廚房裡和起居室裡,在後院的籬笆旁,女人們議論著這件事,公然落淚。

passages.original: On street corners and in store lounging-places the men talked, too, and wept--though not so openly.
passages.vernacular: 喺街角同商店嘅閑談處,男人哋都談住,都落淚——雖然冇咁公開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在街角和商店的閑談處,男人們也談著,也落淚——雖然沒那麼公開。

passages.original: And neither the talking nor the weeping grew less when fast on the heels of the news itself, came Nancy's pitiful story that Pollyanna, face to face with what had come to her, was bemoaning most of all the fact that she could not play the game; that she could not now be glad over--anything.
passages.vernacular: 消息剛傳開,緊接住又傳嚟咗南希嗰可憐嘅故事:波莉安娜面對降臨喺佢身上嘅一切,最痛苦嘅係佢唔能夠玩嗰個遊戲喇;佢而家唔能夠為——任何事情高興喇。咁樣一來,議論同眼淚啲都冇減少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 消息剛傳開,緊接著又傳來了南希那可憐的故事:波莉安娜面對降臨在她身上的一切,最痛苦的是她不能玩那個遊戲了;她現在不能為——任何事情高興了。這樣一來,議論和眼淚一點也沒有減少。

passages.original: It was then that the same thought must have, in some way, come to Pollyanna's friends.
passages.vernacular: 就喺嗰時,波莉安娜嘅朋友哋心中想必唔知點都產生咗同一個念頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就在那時,波莉安娜的朋友們心中想必不知怎麼都產生了同一個念頭。

passages.original: At all events, almost at once, the mistress of the Harrington homestead, greatly to her surprise, began to receive calls: calls from people she knew, and people she did not know; calls from men, women, and children--many of whom Miss Polly had not supposed that her niece knew at all.
passages.vernacular: 總之,幾乎即刻,哈靈頓家宅子嘅女主人驚訝地發現,開始有人嚟拜訪:有佢認識嘅人,都有佢不認識嘅人;有男人、女人同細路——其中許多人波莉小姐根本冇想到佢外甥女竟然認識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,幾乎立刻,哈靈頓家宅子的女主人驚訝地發現,開始有人來拜訪:有她認識的人,也有她不認識的人;有男人、女人和孩子——其中許多人波莉小姐根本沒想到她外甥女竟然認識。

passages.original: Some came in and sat down for a stiff five or ten minutes.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅人進嚟,僵硬地坐上五到好鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的人進來,僵硬地坐上五到十分鐘。

passages.original: Some stood awkwardly on the porch steps, fumbling with hats or hand-bags, according to their sex.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅人笨拙地站喺門廊臺階上,按性別擺弄住帽子或手提包。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的人笨拙地站在門廊臺階上,按性別擺弄著帽子或手提包。

passages.original: Some brought a book, a bunch of flowers, or a dainty to tempt the palate.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅人帶嚟一本書、一束花,或係引誘味覺嘅精致小點心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的人帶來一本書、一束花,或是引誘味覺的精致小點心。

passages.original: Some cried frankly.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅人坦率地哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的人坦率地哭了。

passages.original: Some turned their backs and blew their noses furiously.
passages.vernacular: 有嘅人轉過身去,使勁擤鼻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有的人轉過身去,使勁擤鼻子。

passages.original: But all inquired very anxiously for the little injured girl; and all sent to her some message--and it was these messages which, after a time, stirred Miss Polly to action.
passages.vernacular: 但每個人都好焦急地詢問呢個受傷嘅小姑娘;每個人都托帶畀佢某個口信——而正是呢啲口信,過咗一陣子,促使波莉小姐行動咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但每個人都非常焦急地詢問這個受傷的小姑娘;每個人都托帶給她某個口信——而正是這些口信,過了一陣子,促使波莉小姐行動了起來。

passages.original: First came Mr. John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 首先嚟嘅係約翰·潘德爾頓先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先來的是約翰·潘德爾頓先生。

passages.original: He came without his crutches to-day.
passages.vernacular: 佢今日冇拄拐杖就嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他今天沒有拄拐杖就來了。

passages.original: “I don't need to tell you how shocked I am,” he began almost harshly.
passages.vernacular: 「我不需要告訴你我有多震驚,」佢幾乎粗暴地開口講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不需要告訴你我有多震驚,」他幾乎粗暴地開口說。

passages.original: “But can--nothing be done?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,難道——就冇辦法咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,難道——就沒有辦法了嗎?」

passages.original: Miss Polly gave a gesture of despair.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐做咗個絕望嘅手勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐做了個絕望的手勢。

passages.original: “Oh, we're 'doing,' of course, all the time.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我哋當然一直喺『想辦法』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我們當然一直在『想辦法』。

passages.original: Dr. Mead prescribed certain treatments and medicines that might help, and Dr. Warren is carrying them out to the letter, of course.
passages.vernacular: 米德醫生開咗某些可能有幫助嘅治療同藥物,沃倫醫生當然嚴格照辦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 米德醫生開了某些可能有幫助的治療和藥物,沃倫醫生當然嚴格照辦。

passages.original: But--Dr. Mead held out almost no hope.”
passages.vernacular: 不過——米德醫生幾乎不抱乜嘢希望。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是——米德醫生幾乎不抱什麼希望。」

passages.original: John Pendleton rose abruptly--though he had but just come.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓突然站起嚟——雖然佢才剛坐下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓突然站起來——雖然他才剛坐下。

passages.original: His face was white, and his mouth was set into stern lines.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅臉色蒼白,嘴唇繃成嚴厲嘅線條。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的臉色蒼白,嘴唇繃成嚴厲的線條。

passages.original: Miss Polly, looking at him, knew very well why he felt that he could not stay longer in her presence.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐睇住佢,好清楚佢點解覺得自己唔能夠喺佢面前多待。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐看著他,很清楚他為什麼覺得自己不能在她面前多待。

passages.original: At the door he turned.
passages.vernacular: 到咗門口,佢轉過身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到了門口,他轉過身來。

passages.original: “I have a message for Pollyanna,” he said.
passages.vernacular: 「我有一個口信要帶畀波莉安娜,」佢講。
