passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我有一個口信要帶給波莉安娜,」他說。

passages.original: “Will you tell her, please, that I have seen Jimmy Bean and--that he's going to be my boy hereafter.
passages.vernacular: 「請你告訴佢,我見過吉米·比恩喇,而且——今後佢就係我嘅細路喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請你告訴她,我見過吉米·比恩了,而且——今後他就是我的孩子了。

passages.original: Tell her I thought she would be--GLAD to know.
passages.vernacular: 告訴佢,我想佢會——高興知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴她,我想她會——高興知道的。

passages.original: I shall adopt him, probably.”
passages.vernacular: 我大概會收養佢。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我大概會收養他。」

passages.original: For a brief moment Miss Polly lost her usual well-bred self-control.
passages.vernacular: 有咁短暫嘅一刻,波莉小姐失去咗佢一貫嘅教養良好嘅自制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有那麼短暫的一刻,波莉小姐失去了她一貫的教養良好的自制。

passages.original: “You will adopt Jimmy Bean!” she gasped.
passages.vernacular: 「你要收養吉米·比恩!」佢喘住氣講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要收養吉米·比恩!」她喘著氣說。

passages.original: The man lifted his chin a little.
passages.vernacular: 嗰人微微抬起咗下巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那人微微抬起了下巴。

passages.original: “Yes.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的。

passages.original: I think Pollyanna will understand.
passages.vernacular: 我想波莉安娜會明白嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想波莉安娜會明白的。

passages.original: You will tell her I thought she would be--GLAD!”
passages.vernacular: 你告訴佢,我想佢會——高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你告訴她,我想她會——高興!」

passages.original: “Why, of--of course,” faltered Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「當——當然,」波莉小姐支支吾吾地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當——當然,」波莉小姐支支吾吾地說。

passages.original: “Thank you,” bowed John Pendleton, as he turned to go.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你。」約翰·潘德爾頓鞠咗一躬,轉身離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你。」約翰·潘德爾頓鞠了一躬,轉身離去。

passages.original: In the middle of the floor Miss Polly stood, silent and amazed, still looking after the man who had just left her.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐站喺房間中央,沉默而驚愕,仍舊望住嗰個啱啱離開佢嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐站在房間中央,沉默而驚愕,仍舊望著那個剛剛離開她的人。

passages.original: Even yet she could scarcely believe what her ears had heard.
passages.vernacular: 直到而家,佢幾乎仲唔敢相信自己嘅耳朵聽到咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直到現在,她幾乎還不敢相信自己的耳朵聽到了什麼。

passages.original: John Pendleton ADOPT Jimmy Bean?
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓收養吉米·比恩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓收養吉米·比恩?

passages.original: John Pendleton, wealthy, independent, morose, reputed to be miserly and supremely selfish, to adopt a little boy--and such a little boy?
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓,富有、獨立、陰鬱、素以吝嗇同極端自私著稱,要收養一個小男孩——而且係嗰樣一個小男孩?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓,富有、獨立、陰鬱、素以吝嗇和極端自私著稱,要收養一個小男孩——而且是那樣一個小男孩?

passages.original: With a somewhat dazed face Miss Polly went up-stairs to Pollyanna's room.
passages.vernacular: 帶住有些茫然嘅神情,波莉小姐上樓嚟到波莉安娜嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 帶著有些茫然的神情,波莉小姐上樓來到波莉安娜的房間。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, I have a message for you from Mr. John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,我有一個約翰·潘德爾頓先生畀你嘅口信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,我有一個約翰·潘德爾頓先生給你的口信。

passages.original: He has just been here.
passages.vernacular: 佢剛嚟過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他剛來過。

passages.original: He says to tell you he has taken Jimmy Bean for his little boy.
passages.vernacular: 佢講讓我告訴你,佢收養咗吉米·比恩做佢嘅小男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說讓我告訴你,他收養了吉米·比恩做他的小男孩。

passages.original: He said he thought you'd be glad to know it.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講佢想你會高興知道嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說他想你會高興知道的。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's wistful little face flamed into sudden joy.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜惆悵嘅小臉驟然煥發出喜悅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜惆悵的小臉驟然煥發出喜悅。

passages.original: “Glad?
passages.vernacular: 「高興?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興?

passages.original: GLAD?
passages.vernacular: 高興嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 高興嗎?

passages.original: Well, I reckon I am glad!
passages.vernacular: 嗯,我當然高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗯,我當然高興!

passages.original: Oh, Aunt Polly, I've so wanted to find a place for Jimmy--and that's such a lovely place!
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉姨媽,我一直咁想畀吉米找個地方——嗰個係個多可愛嘅地方啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉姨媽,我一直那麼想給吉米找個地方——那是個多可愛的地方啊!

passages.original: Besides, I'm so glad for Mr. Pendleton, too.
passages.vernacular: 而且,我都為潘德爾頓先生高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,我也為潘德爾頓先生高興。

passages.original: You see, now he'll have the child's presence.”
passages.vernacular: 你瞧,而家佢有嗰個『細路嘅在場』喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你瞧,現在他有那個『孩子的在場』了。」

passages.original: “The--what?”
Pollyanna colored painfully.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜痛苦地紅咗臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜痛苦地紅了臉。

passages.original: She had forgotten that she had never told her aunt of Mr. Pendleton's desire to adopt her--and certainly she would not wish to tell her now that she had ever thought for a minute of leaving her--this dear Aunt Polly!
passages.vernacular: 佢忘咗自己從冇告訴過姨媽潘德爾頓先生想收養佢嘅事——而且佢當然不愿而家告訴佢,佢曾有一分鐘想過離開佢——離開呢位親愛嘅波莉姨媽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她忘了自己從沒告訴過姨媽潘德爾頓先生想收養她的事——而且她當然不愿現在告訴她,她曾有一分鐘想過離開她——離開這位親愛的波莉姨媽!

passages.original: “The child's presence,” stammered Pollyanna, hastily.
passages.vernacular: 「細路嘅在場,」波莉安娜慌忙結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「孩子的在場,」波莉安娜慌忙結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “Mr. Pendleton told me once, you see, that only a woman's hand and heart or a child's presence could make a--a home.
passages.vernacular: 「你瞧,潘德爾頓先生有一次告訴我,只有女人嘅手同心或者細路嘅在場,才能造出一個——一個家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你瞧,潘德爾頓先生有一次告訴我,只有女人的手和心或者孩子的在場,才能造出一個——一個家。

passages.original: And now he's got it--the child's presence.”
passages.vernacular: 而家佢有喇——細路嘅在場。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他有了——孩子的在場。」

passages.original: “Oh, I--see,” said Miss Polly very gently; and she did see--more than Pollyanna realized.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我——明白喇。」波莉小姐好溫和地講;而且佢確實明白喇——比波莉安娜意識到嘅更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我——明白了。」波莉小姐非常溫和地說;而且她確實明白了——比波莉安娜意識到的更多。

passages.original: She saw something of the pressure that was probably brought to bear on Pollyanna herself at the time John Pendleton was asking HER to be the “child's presence,” which was to transform his great pile of gray stone into a home.
passages.vernacular: 佢多少睇出咗當年約翰·潘德爾頓請波莉安娜去做嗰個「細路嘅在場」,要把佢嗰座灰色巨石大宅變成一個家嘅時候,波莉安娜自己好可能承受嘅壓力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她多少看出了當年約翰·潘德爾頓請波莉安娜去做那個「孩子的在場」,要把他那座灰色巨石大宅變成一個家的時候,波莉安娜自己很可能承受的壓力。

passages.original: “I see,” she finished, her eyes stinging with sudden tears.
passages.vernacular: 「我明白喇,」佢講完,眼睛因突然涌出嘅淚水而刺痛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我明白了,」她說完,眼睛因突然涌出的淚水而刺痛。

passages.original: Pollyanna, fearful that her aunt might ask further embarrassing questions, hastened to lead the conversation away from the Pendleton house and its master.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜生怕姨媽再問些尷尬嘅問題,連忙把話題從潘德爾頓嘅房子同佢嘅主人身上引開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜生怕姨媽再問些尷尬的問題,連忙把話題從潘德爾頓的房子和它的主人身上引開。

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton says so, too--that it takes a woman's hand and heart, or a child's presence, to make a home, you know,” she remarked.
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生都咁講——要有女人嘅手同心,或者細路嘅在場,才能造出一個家,你知道,」佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生也這麼說——要有女人的手和心,或者孩子的在場,才能造出一個家,你知道,」她說。

passages.original: Miss Polly turned with a start.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嚇咗一跳,轉過身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐嚇了一跳,轉過身來。

passages.original: “DR.
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓

passages.original: CHILTON!
passages.vernacular: 醫生!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生!

passages.original: How do you know--that?”
passages.vernacular: 你點知道——嗰個?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼知道——那個?」

passages.original: “He told me so.
passages.vernacular: 「佢告訴我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他告訴我的。

passages.original: 'Twas when he said he lived in just rooms, you know--not a home.”
passages.vernacular: 係佢講佢住嘅只係幾個房間,你知道——唔係家嘅時候。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是他說他住的只是幾個房間,你知道——不是家的時候。」

passages.original: Miss Polly did not answer.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐冇回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐沒有回答。

passages.original: Her eyes were out the window.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛望住窗外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛望著窗外。

passages.original: “So I asked him why he didn't get 'em--a woman's hand and heart, and have a home.”
passages.vernacular: 「所以我問佢點解不去找一個——女人嘅手同心,有個家。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以我問他為什麼不去找一個——女人的手和心,有個家。」

passages.original: “Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜!」

passages.original: Miss Polly had turned sharply.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐猛地轉過身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐猛地轉過身來。

passages.original: Her cheeks showed a sudden color.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅雙頰突然泛起咗紅暈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的雙頰突然泛起了紅暈。

passages.original: “Well, I did.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我問喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我問了。

passages.original: He looked so--so sorrowful.”
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟咁——咁悲傷。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來那麼——那麼悲傷。」

passages.original: “What did he--say?”
passages.vernacular: 「佢講喇——乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他說了——什麼?」

passages.original: Miss Polly asked the question as if in spite of some force within her that was urging her not to ask it.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐問呢個問題,仿佛係違背咗心裡某種力量,佢喺催促佢唔好問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐問這個問題,仿佛是違背了心裡某種力量,它在催促她不要問。

passages.original: “He didn't say anything for a minute; then he said very low that you couldn't always get 'em for the asking.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢有一會兒乜嘢都冇講;然後佢好低聲地講,唔係想要就總能得到嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他有一會兒什麼也沒說;然後他很低聲地說,不是想要就總能得到的。」

passages.original: There was a brief silence.
passages.vernacular: 短暫嘅沉默。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 短暫的沉默。

passages.original: Miss Polly's eyes had turned again to the window.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅目光又轉向咗窗外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的目光又轉向了窗外。

passages.original: Her cheeks were still unnaturally pink.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅雙頰依舊紅得不自然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的雙頰依舊紅得不自然。

passages.original: Pollyanna sighed.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “He wants one, anyhow, I know, and I wish he could have one.”
passages.vernacular: 「不管點樣,我知道佢想要一個,我真希望佢能有一個。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不管怎樣,我知道他想要一個,我真希望他能有一個。」

passages.original: “Why, Pollyanna, HOW do you know?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,波莉安娜,你點知道?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,波莉安娜,你怎麼知道?」

passages.original: “Because, afterwards, on another day, he said something else.
passages.vernacular: 「因為後來有一天佢仲講咗別嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「因為後來有一天他還說了別的話。

passages.original: He said that low, too, but I heard him.
passages.vernacular: 佢都係低聲講嘅,不過我聽到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他也是低聲說的,可是我聽到了。

passages.original: He said that he'd give all the world if he did have one woman's hand and heart.
passages.vernacular: 佢講,如果佢能有一個女人嘅手同心,佢愿意用全世界嚟換。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說,如果他能有一個女人的手和心,他愿意用全世界來換。

passages.original: Why, Aunt Polly, what's the matter?”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉姨媽,你點喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉姨媽,你怎麼了?」

passages.original: Aunt Polly had risen hurriedly and gone to the window.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽已經急忙站起嚟,走到咗窗邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽已經急忙站起來,走到了窗邊。

passages.original: “Nothing, dear.
passages.vernacular: 「冇乜嘢,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒什麼,親愛的。

passages.original: I was changing the position of this prism,” said Aunt Polly, whose whole face now was aflame.
passages.vernacular: 我喺調整呢塊棱鏡嘅位置,」波莉姨媽講,整張臉而家都燒得通紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在調整這塊棱鏡的位置,」波莉姨媽說,整張臉現在都燒得通紅。

chapters.title: Ch. XXVIII The Game and Its Players 第二十八章:遊戲與玩家

passages.original: CH It was not long after John Pendleton's second visit that Milly Snow called one afternoon.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓第二次嚟訪後不久,有一天下午米莉·斯諾嚟訪喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓第二次來訪後不久,有一天下午米莉·斯諾來訪了。

passages.original: Milly Snow had never before been to the Harrington homestead.
passages.vernacular: 米莉·斯諾以前從冇到過哈靈頓家嘅宅子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 米莉·斯諾以前從沒到過哈靈頓家的宅子。

passages.original: She blushed and looked very embarrassed when Miss Polly entered the room.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐走進房間時,佢臉紅喇,顯得好窘迫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐走進房間時,她臉紅了,顯得十分窘迫。

passages.original: “I--I came to inquire for the little girl,” she stammered.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我係嚟問候嗰個小姑娘嘅,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我是來問候那個小姑娘的,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “You are very kind.
passages.vernacular: 「你真好心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真好心。

passages.original: She is about the same.
passages.vernacular: 佢差不多定係老樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她差不多還是老樣子。

passages.original: How is your mother?” rejoined Miss Polly, wearily.
passages.vernacular: 你母親好嗎?」波莉小姐疲倦地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你母親好嗎?」波莉小姐疲倦地回答。

passages.original: “That is what I came to tell you--that is, to ask you to tell Miss Pollyanna,” hurried on the girl, breathlessly and incoherently.
passages.vernacular: 「我就係嚟告訴你呢個嘅——都就係講,嚟請你轉告波莉安娜小姐,」姑娘氣喘吁吁、語無倫次地急忙講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我就是來告訴你這個的——也就是說,來請你轉告波莉安娜小姐,」姑娘氣喘吁吁、語無倫次地急忙說。

passages.original: “We think it's--so awful--so perfectly awful that the little thing can't ever walk again; and after all she's done for us, too--for mother, you know, teaching her to play the game, and all that.
passages.vernacular: 「我哋覺得——太可怕喇——實在太可怕喇,嗰個小嘢再都唔能夠走路喇;而且佢為我哋做咗咁多,為媽媽,你知道,教佢玩嗰個遊戲,仲有呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我們覺得——太可怕了——實在太可怕了,那個小東西再也不能走路了;而且她為我們做了那麼多,為媽媽,你知道,教她玩那個遊戲,還有這些。

passages.original: And when we heard how now she couldn't play it herself--poor little dear!
passages.vernacular: 當我哋聽講佢而家自己反而玩不咗喇——可憐嘅小寶貝!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我們聽說她現在自己反而玩不了了——可憐的小寶貝!

passages.original: I'm sure I don't see how she CAN, either, in her condition!--but when we remembered all the things she'd said to us, we thought if she could only know what she HAD done for us, that it would HELP, you know, in her own case, about the game, because she could be glad--that is, a little glad--” Milly stopped helplessly, and seemed to be waiting for Miss Polly to speak.
passages.vernacular: 我都實在睇不出,喺佢呢種情形下,佢點可能玩得喇!——但係我哋想起佢對我哋講過嘅所有話,我哋想,要係佢能知道佢為我哋做咗乜嘢,或者會對佢自己有幫助,關于嗰個遊戲嘅,因為佢就可以高興喇——就係講,稍微高興啲——」米莉無助地停住喇,似乎喺等波莉小姐開口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也實在看不出,在她這種情形下,她怎麼可能玩得了!——但是我們想起她對我們說過的所有話,我們想,要是她能知道她為我們做了什麼,也許會對她自己有幫助,關于那個遊戲的,因為她就可以高興了——就是說,稍微高興一點——」米莉無助地停住了,似乎在等波莉小姐開口。

passages.original: Miss Polly had sat politely listening, but with a puzzled questioning in her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐一直禮貌地坐住聽,但眼裡帶住困惑嘅疑問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐一直禮貌地坐著聽,但眼裡帶著困惑的疑問。

passages.original: Only about half of what had been said, had she understood.
passages.vernacular: 頭先講嘅話,佢只聽懂咗大約一半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛才說的話,她只聽懂了大約一半。

passages.original: She was thinking now that she always had known that Milly Snow was “queer,” but she had not supposed she was crazy.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家心想,佢一直知道米莉·斯諾有點「古怪」,但冇想到佢係瘋喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她現在心想,她一直知道米莉·斯諾有點「古怪」,但沒想到她是瘋了。

passages.original: In no other way, however, could she account for this incoherent, illogical, unmeaning rush of words.
passages.vernacular: 不過,除此之外,佢無法解釋呢一連串語無倫次、冇邏輯、毫無意義嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,除此之外,她無法解釋這一連串語無倫次、沒有邏輯、毫無意義的話。

passages.original: When the pause came she filled it with a quiet:
passages.vernacular: 等對方停下嚟嘅時候,佢用平靜嘅一句話填補咗空白:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等對方停下來的時候,她用平靜的一句話填補了空白:

passages.original: “I don't think I quite understand, Milly.
passages.vernacular: 「我想我不太明白,米莉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我想我不太明白,米莉。

passages.original: Just what is it that you want me to tell my niece?”
passages.vernacular: 你到底要我告訴我外甥女乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你到底要我告訴我外甥女什麼?」

passages.original: “Yes, that's it; I want you to tell her,” answered the girl, feverishly.
passages.vernacular: 「對,就係咁樣;我要你告訴佢,」姑娘狂熱地回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「對,就是這樣;我要你告訴她,」姑娘狂熱地回答。

passages.original: “Make her see what she's done for us.
passages.vernacular: 「讓佢明白佢為我哋做咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「讓她明白她為我們做了什麼。

passages.original: Of course she's SEEN some things, because she's been there, and she's known mother is different; but I want her to know HOW different she is--and me, too.
passages.vernacular: 當然有些事佢係睇到咗嘅,因為佢去過嗰度,知道媽媽變喇;但我要佢知道佢變得有多大——仲有我都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然有些事她是看到了的,因為她去過那裡,知道媽媽變了;但我要她知道她變得有多大——還有我也是。

passages.original: I'm different.
passages.vernacular: 我都變喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也變了。

passages.original: I've been trying to play it--the game--a little.”
passages.vernacular: 我一直喺試住玩——嗰個遊戲——啲點。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直在試著玩——那個遊戲——一點點。」

passages.original: Miss Polly frowned.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐皺起眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐皺起眉頭。

passages.original: She would have asked what Milly meant by this “game,” but there was no opportunity.
passages.vernacular: 佢本想問米莉講嘅呢個「遊戲」係乜嘢意思,但冇機會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她本想問米莉說的這個「遊戲」是什麼意思,但沒有機會。

passages.original: Milly was rushing on again with nervous volubility.
passages.vernacular: 米莉又神經質地滔滔不絕地沖咗出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 米莉又神經質地滔滔不絕地沖了出來。

passages.original: “You know nothing was ever right before--for mother.
passages.vernacular: 「你知道,以前對媽媽來講,乜嘢都不對勁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你知道,以前對媽媽來說,什麼都不對勁。

passages.original: She was always wanting 'em different.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是想要不一樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她總是想要不一樣的。

passages.original: And, really, I don't know as one could blame her much--under the circumstances.
passages.vernacular: 而且,講真嘅,喺嗰種情況下,我覺得都唔能夠點怪佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且,說真的,在那種情況下,我覺得也不能怎麼怪她。

passages.original: But now she lets me keep the shades up, and she takes interest in things--how she looks, and her nightdress, and all that.
passages.vernacular: 不過而家佢讓我把窗簾拉起嚟,佢對事情有咗興趣——佢嘅樣子啦,佢嘅瞓衣啦,呢啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是現在她讓我把窗簾拉起來,她對事情有了興趣——她的樣子啦,她的睡衣啦,這些。

passages.original: And she's actually begun to knit little things--reins and baby blankets for fairs and hospitals.
passages.vernacular: 佢仲真嘅開始編織啲小嘢喇——馬韁繩同嬰兒毯,畀義賣會同醫院嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她還真的開始編織一些小東西了——馬韁繩和嬰兒毯,給義賣會和醫院的。

passages.original: And she's so interested, and so GLAD to think she can do it!--and that was all Miss Pollyanna's doings, you know, 'cause she told mother she could be glad she'd got her hands and arms, anyway; and that made mother wonder right away why she didn't DO something with her hands and arms.
passages.vernacular: 佢咁感興趣,想到自己能做到而咁高興!——呢全係波莉安娜小姐嘅功勞,你知道,因為佢告訴媽媽,不管點樣佢至少仲有手同手臂可以高興;呢讓媽媽即刻想到,點解唔使佢嘅手同手臂做點乜嘢呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她那麼感興趣,想到自己能做到而那麼高興!——這全是波莉安娜小姐的功勞,你知道,因為她告訴媽媽,不管怎樣她至少還有手和手臂可以高興;這讓媽媽馬上想到,為什麼不用她的手和手臂做點什麼呢。

passages.original: And so she began to do something--to knit, you know.
passages.vernacular: 于係佢就開始做點乜嘢——織嘢,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 于是她就開始做點什麼——織東西,你知道。

passages.original: And you can't think what a different room it is now, what with the red and blue and yellow worsteds, and the prisms in the window that SHE gave her--why, it actually makes you feel BETTER just to go in there now; and before I used to dread it awfully, it was so dark and gloomy, and mother was so--so unhappy, you know.
passages.vernacular: 你想唔到嗰房間而家變成咗幾咁不一樣嘅樣子,有咗紅嘅、藍嘅、黃嘅毛線,仲有窗子上佢送嘅棱鏡——哎呀,而家光係走進嗰間屋子,就讓你覺得好些喇;以前我真怕進去,咁黑、咁陰沉,媽媽咁——咁不快樂,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想不到那房間現在變成了多麼不一樣的樣子,有了紅的、藍的、黃的毛線,還有窗子上她送的棱鏡——哎呀,現在光是走進那間屋子,就讓你覺得好些了;以前我真怕進去,那麼黑、那麼陰沉,媽媽那麼——那麼不快樂,你知道。

passages.original: “And so we want you to please tell Miss Pollyanna that we understand it's all because of her.
passages.vernacular: 「所以我哋想請你告訴波莉安娜小姐,我哋知道呢全都係因為佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所以我們想請你告訴波莉安娜小姐,我們知道這全都是因為她。

passages.original: And please say we're so glad we know her, that we thought, maybe if she knew it, it would make her a little glad that she knew us.
passages.vernacular: 請告訴佢我哋多高興認識佢,我哋想,或者佢要係知道喇,會因為認識我哋而稍微高興啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請告訴她我們多高興認識她,我們想,也許她要是知道了,會因為認識我們而稍微高興一點。

passages.original: And--and that's all,” sighed Milly, rising hurriedly to her feet.
passages.vernacular: 仲有——仲有就呢啲喇,」米莉嘆息住,匆忙站起身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有——還有就這些了,」米莉嘆息著,匆忙站起身來。

passages.original: “You'll tell her?”
passages.vernacular: 「你會告訴佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你會告訴她嗎?」

passages.original: “Why, of course,” murmured Miss Polly, wondering just how much of this remarkable discourse she could remember to tell.
passages.vernacular: 「當然會,」波莉小姐喃喃講,心裡琢磨住呢番非同尋常嘅講話,自己到底能記住多少去轉述。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然會,」波莉小姐喃喃說,心裡琢磨著這番非同尋常的講話,自己到底能記住多少去轉述。

passages.original: These visits of John Pendleton and Milly Snow were only the first of many; and always there were the messages--the messages which were in some ways so curious that they caused Miss Polly more and more to puzzle over them.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓同米莉·斯諾嘅呢啲拜訪,只係許多拜訪嘅開始;而且總是帶住口信——呢啲口信有些方面咁奇怪,使得波莉小姐越嚟越想不通。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓和米莉·斯諾的這些拜訪,只是許多拜訪的開始;而且總是帶著口信——這些口信有些方面那麼奇怪,使得波莉小姐越來越想不通。

passages.original: One day there was the little Widow Benton.
passages.vernacular: 有一天嚟嘅係小個子嘅本頓寡婦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一天來的是小個子的本頓寡婦。

passages.original: Miss Polly knew her well, though they had never called upon each other.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐認識佢,雖然佢哋從冇互相拜訪過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐認識她,雖然她們從沒互相拜訪過。

passages.original: By reputation she knew her as the saddest little woman in town--one who was always in black.
passages.vernacular: 據名聲所知,佢係鎮上最悲傷嘅小個子女人——總是一身黑衣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據名聲所知,她是鎮上最悲傷的小個子女人——總是一身黑衣。

passages.original: To-day, however, Mrs. Benton wore a knot of pale blue at the throat, though there were tears in her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 不過今日,本頓太太喺喉嚨處別咗一個淡藍色嘅結,盡管佢眼裡含住淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過今天,本頓太太在喉嚨處別了一個淡藍色的結,盡管她眼裡含著淚。

passages.original: She spoke of her grief and horror at the accident; then she asked diffidently if she might see Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 佢談起對呢次事故嘅悲痛同驚駭;然後羞怯地問能否見一見波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她談起對這次事故的悲痛和驚駭;然後羞怯地問能否見一見波莉安娜。

passages.original: Miss Polly shook her head.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐搖搖頭。

passages.original: “I am sorry, but she sees no one yet.
passages.vernacular: 「好抱歉,佢而家仲唔見任何人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「很抱歉,她現在還不見任何人。

passages.original: A little later--perhaps.”
passages.vernacular: 或者稍後吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許稍後吧。」

passages.original: Mrs. Benton wiped her eyes, rose, and turned to go.
passages.vernacular: 本頓太太擦咗擦眼睛,站起身嚟,轉身要走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 本頓太太擦了擦眼睛,站起身來,轉身要走。

passages.original: But after she had almost reached the hall door she came back hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 但係幾乎走到咗門廳嘅門口,佢又匆匆折咗回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是幾乎走到了門廳的門口,她又匆匆折了回來。

passages.original: “Miss Harrington, perhaps, you'd give her--a message,” she stammered.
passages.vernacular: 「哈靈頓小姐,或者你可以帶畀佢一個——口信,」佢結結巴巴地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哈靈頓小姐,也許你可以帶給她一個——口信,」她結結巴巴地說。

passages.original: “Certainly, Mrs. Benton; I shall be very glad to.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然,本頓太太;我好樂意。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然,本頓太太;我很樂意。」

passages.original: Still the little woman hesitated; then she spoke.
passages.vernacular: 呢個小個子女人仍然猶豫住;然後佢開口喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個小個子女人仍然猶豫著;然後她開口了。

passages.original: “Will you tell her, please, that--that I've put on THIS,” she said, just touching the blue bow at her throat.
passages.vernacular: 「請你告訴佢,我戴上咗呢個,」佢講住,輕輕碰咗碰喉嚨處嘅藍色蝴蝶結。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請你告訴她,我戴上了這個,」她說著,輕輕碰了碰喉嚨處的藍色蝴蝶結。

passages.original: Then, at Miss Polly's ill-concealed look of surprise, she added: “The little girl has been trying for so long to make me wear--some color, that I thought she'd be--glad to know I'd begun.
passages.vernacular: 然後,睇到波莉小姐掩飾不住嘅驚訝神色,佢補充道:「呢個小姑娘勸咗我咁久,要我穿戴——啲顏色,我想佢會——高興知道我已經開始喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,看到波莉小姐掩飾不住的驚訝神色,她補充道:「這個小姑娘勸了我那麼久,要我穿戴——一點顏色,我想她會——高興知道我已經開始了。

passages.original: She said that Freddy would be so glad to see it, if I would.
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果我戴喇,弗雷迪會好高興睇到嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說如果我戴了,弗雷迪會很高興看到的。

passages.original: You know Freddy's ALL I have now.
passages.vernacular: 你知道弗雷迪係我而家僅有嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道弗雷迪是我現在僅有的了。

passages.original: The others have all--” Mrs. Benton shook her head and turned away.
passages.vernacular: 其他嘅都已經——」本頓太太搖搖頭,轉身走開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他的都已經——」本頓太太搖搖頭,轉身走開了。

passages.original: “If you'll just tell Pollyanna--SHE'LL understand.”
passages.vernacular: 「你只要告訴波莉安娜——佢會明白嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你只要告訴波莉安娜——她會明白的。」

passages.original: And the door closed after her.
passages.vernacular: 門喺佢身後關上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門在她身後關上了。

passages.original: A little later, that same day, there was the other widow--at least, she wore widow's garments.
passages.vernacular: 稍後,同一天,又嚟咗另一位寡婦——至少,佢穿住寡婦嘅衣服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後,同一天,又來了另一位寡婦——至少,她穿著寡婦的衣服。

passages.original: Miss Polly did not know her at all.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐完全不認識佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐完全不認識她。

passages.original: She wondered vaguely how Pollyanna could have known her.
passages.vernacular: 佢隱約納悶波莉安娜點會認識佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她隱約納悶波莉安娜怎麼會認識她。

passages.original: The lady gave her name as “Mrs. Tarbell.”
passages.vernacular: 呢位女士自報姓名係「塔貝爾太太」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這位女士自報姓名是「塔貝爾太太」。

passages.original: “I'm a stranger to you, of course,” she began at once.
passages.vernacular: 「我對你來講當然係陌生人,」佢一開口就講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我對你來說當然是陌生人,」她一開口就說。

passages.original: “But I'm not a stranger to your little niece, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「但我對你嘅小外甥女波莉安娜可唔係陌生人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「但我對你的小外甥女波莉安娜可不是陌生人。

passages.original: I've been at the hotel all summer, and every day I've had to take long walks for my health.
passages.vernacular: 我整個夏天都住喺旅館裡,每天為了健康都要出去長時間散步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我整個夏天都住在旅館裡,每天為了健康都要出去長時間散步。

passages.original: It was on these walks that I've met your niece--she's such a dear little girl!
passages.vernacular: 就係喺呢啲散步途中我遇見咗你嘅外甥女——佢係個幾咁可愛嘅小姑娘啊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就是在這些散步途中我遇見了你的外甥女——她是個多麼可愛的小姑娘啊!

passages.original: I wish I could make you understand what she's been to me.
passages.vernacular: 我多希望能讓你明白,佢對我意味住乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我多希望能讓你明白,她對我意味著什麼。

passages.original: I was very sad when I came up here; and her bright face and cheery ways reminded me of--my own little girl that I lost years ago.
passages.vernacular: 我嚟呢度嘅時候好悲傷;而佢明亮嘅臉龐同歡快嘅樣子,讓我想起喇——我多年前失去嘅小女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來這裡的時候非常悲傷;而她明亮的臉龐和歡快的樣子,讓我想起了——我多年前失去的小女兒。

passages.original: I was so shocked to hear of the accident; and then when I learned that the poor child would never walk again, and that she was so unhappy because she couldn't be glad any longer--the dear child!--I just had to come to you.”
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢次事故,我好震驚;然後當我得知呢可憐嘅細路再都唔能夠走路,而且佢因為再都唔能夠高興而咁不快樂——親愛嘅細路!——我就唔得不嚟找你喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這次事故,我非常震驚;然後當我得知這可憐的孩子再也不能走路,而且她因為再也不能高興而那麼不快樂——親愛的孩子!——我就不得不來找你了。」

passages.original: “You are very kind,” murmured Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「你真好心,」波莉小姐喃喃講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你真好心,」波莉小姐喃喃說。

passages.original: “But it is you who are to be kind,” demurred the other.
passages.vernacular: 「不過該好心嘅係你,」對方反駁道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不過該好心的是你,」對方反駁道。

passages.original: “I--I want you to give her a message from me.
passages.vernacular: 「我——我想請你替我畀佢帶個口信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我——我想請你替我給她帶個口信。

passages.original: Will you?”
passages.vernacular: 你愿意嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你愿意嗎?」

passages.original: “Certainly.”
passages.vernacular: 「當然。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「當然。」

passages.original: “Will you just tell her, then, that Mrs. Tarbell is glad now.
passages.vernacular: 「咁請你告訴佢,塔貝爾太太而家高興喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼請你告訴她,塔貝爾太太現在高興了。

passages.original: Yes, I know it sounds odd, and you don't understand.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,我知道呢聽起嚟好怪,你不明白。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,我知道這聽起來很怪,你不明白。

passages.original: But--if you'll pardon me I'd rather not explain.”
passages.vernacular: 不過——請原諒,我寧愿不解釋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過——請原諒,我寧愿不解釋。」

passages.original: Sad lines came to the lady's mouth, and the smile left her eyes.
passages.vernacular: 悲傷嘅線條出而家呢位女士嘅嘴角,笑意從佢嘅眼中消失喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 悲傷的線條出現在這位女士的嘴角,笑意從她的眼中消失了。

passages.original: “Your niece will know just what I mean; and I felt that I must tell--her.
passages.vernacular: 「你外甥女會明白我嘅意思;我覺得我必須告訴——佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你外甥女會明白我的意思;我覺得我必須告訴——她。

passages.original: Thank you; and pardon me, please, for any seeming rudeness in my call,” she begged, as she took her leave.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝你;請原諒我呢次拜訪中任何睇似無禮之處,」佢告辭時懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝你;請原諒我這次拜訪中任何看似無禮之處,」她告辭時懇求道。

passages.original: Thoroughly mystified now, Miss Polly hurried up-stairs to Pollyanna's room.
passages.vernacular: 而家波莉小姐徹底糊涂喇,佢匆匆上樓嚟到波莉安娜嘅房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在波莉小姐徹底糊涂了,她匆匆上樓來到波莉安娜的房間。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, do you know a Mrs. Tarbell?”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,你認識一位塔貝爾太太嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,你認識一位塔貝爾太太嗎?」

passages.original: “Oh, yes.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,認識。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,認識。

passages.original: I love Mrs. Tarbell.
passages.vernacular: 我愛塔貝爾太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我愛塔貝爾太太。

passages.original: She's sick, and awfully sad; and she's at the hotel, and takes long walks.
passages.vernacular: 佢生住病,好悲傷;佢住喺旅館裡,常常長時間散步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她生著病,非常悲傷;她住在旅館裡,常常長時間散步。

passages.original: We go together.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一起去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一起去。

passages.original: I mean--we used to.”
passages.vernacular: 我係講——我哋以前一起去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是說——我們以前一起去。」

passages.original: Pollyanna's voice broke, and two big tears rolled down her cheeks.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅聲音哽住喇,兩大顆淚珠滾下臉頰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的聲音哽住了,兩大顆淚珠滾下臉頰。

passages.original: Miss Polly cleared her throat hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐急忙清咗清嗓子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐急忙清了清嗓子。

passages.original: “We'll, she's just been here, dear.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,佢頭先嚟過,親愛嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,她剛才來過,親愛的。

passages.original: She left a message for you--but she wouldn't tell me what it meant.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀你留咗個口信——不過唔肯告訴我係乜嘢意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她給你留了個口信——可是不肯告訴我是什麼意思。

passages.original: She said to tell you that Mrs. Tarbell is glad now.”
passages.vernacular: 佢講讓我告訴你,塔貝爾太太而家高興喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說讓我告訴你,塔貝爾太太現在高興了。」

passages.original: Pollyanna clapped her hands softly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜輕輕拍著手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜輕輕拍著手。

passages.original: “Did she say that--really?
passages.vernacular: 「佢真嘅咁講咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她真的這麼說了嗎?

passages.original: Oh, I'm so glad!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我真高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我真高興!」

passages.original: “But, Pollyanna, what did she mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,波莉安娜,佢係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,波莉安娜,她是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “Why, it's the game, and--” Pollyanna stopped short, her fingers to her lips.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,呢個係遊戲,而且——」波莉安娜突然停住,手指按喺嘴唇上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,這是遊戲,而且——」波莉安娜突然停住,手指按在嘴唇上。

passages.original: “What game?”
passages.vernacular: 「乜嘢遊戲?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什麼遊戲?」

passages.original: “N-nothing much, Aunt Polly; that is--I can't tell it unless I tell other things that--that I'm not to speak of.”
passages.vernacular: 「冇、冇乜嘢,波莉姨媽;就係——我唔能夠講,除非講到別嘅事,而嗰啲——我唔能夠講。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒、沒什麼,波莉姨媽;就是——我不能講,除非講到別的事,而那些——我不能說。」

passages.original: It was on Miss Polly's tongue to question her niece further; but the obvious distress on the little girl's face stayed the words before they were uttered.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐話到嘴邊,正要進一步追問外甥女;不過小姑娘臉上明顯嘅苦惱,使話喺講出口之前就咽咗回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐話到嘴邊,正要進一步追問外甥女;可是小姑娘臉上明顯的苦惱,使話在說出口之前就咽了回去。

passages.original: Not long after Mrs. Tarbell's visit, the climax came.
passages.vernacular: 塔貝爾太太嚟訪後不久,高潮嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 塔貝爾太太來訪後不久,高潮來了。

passages.original: It came in the shape of a call from a certain young woman with unnaturally pink cheeks and abnormally yellow hair; a young woman who wore high heels and cheap jewelry; a young woman whom Miss Polly knew very well by reputation--but whom she was angrily amazed to meet beneath the roof of the Harrington homestead.
passages.vernacular: 佢以一位年輕女子嚟訪嘅形式出現:呢位女子雙頰紅得不自然,頭髮黃得反常;穿住高跟鞋,戴住廉價首飾;波莉小姐對佢嘅名聲咗如指掌——但係喺哈靈頓家嘅屋檐下遇見佢,卻令佢憤怒地震驚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它以一位年輕女子來訪的形式出現:這位女子雙頰紅得不自然,頭髮黃得反常;穿著高跟鞋,戴著廉價首飾;波莉小姐對她的名聲了如指掌——但是在哈靈頓家的屋檐下遇見她,卻令她憤怒地震驚。

passages.original: Miss Polly did not offer her hand.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐冇伸出手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐沒有伸出手。

passages.original: She drew back, indeed, as she entered the room.
passages.vernacular: 事實上,佢走進房間時仲向後退咗一步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 事實上,她走進房間時還向後退了一步。

passages.original: The woman rose at once.
passages.vernacular: 嗰女人即刻站咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那女人立刻站了起來。

passages.original: Her eyes were very red, as if she had been crying.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅眼睛紅紅嘅,好像哭過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的眼睛紅紅的,好像哭過。

passages.original: Half defiantly she asked if she might, for a moment, see the little girl, Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 佢半帶挑釁地問係咪可以見一見嗰個小姑娘波莉安娜,邊怕一會兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她半帶挑釁地問是否可以見一見那個小姑娘波莉安娜,哪怕一會兒。

passages.original: Miss Polly said no.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐講不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐說不行。

passages.original: She began to say it very sternly; but something in the woman's pleading eyes made her add the civil explanation that no one was allowed yet to see Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 佢開始講得好嚴厲;不過嗰女人懇求嘅眼神中有乜嘢嘢,使佢又加上一句禮貌嘅解釋:而家邊個都不許見波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她開始說得很嚴厲;可是那女人懇求的眼神中有什麼東西,使她又加上一句禮貌的解釋:現在誰也不許見波莉安娜。

passages.original: The woman hesitated; then a little brusquely she spoke.
passages.vernacular: 嗰女人猶豫咗一下;然後有點生硬地開口喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那女人猶豫了一下;然後有點生硬地開口了。

passages.original: Her chin was still at a slightly defiant tilt.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅下巴仍帶住啲挑釁嘅翹起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的下巴仍帶著一點挑釁的翹起。

passages.original: “My name is Mrs. Payson--Mrs. Tom Payson.
passages.vernacular: 「我叫佩森太太——湯姆·佩森太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我叫佩森太太——湯姆·佩森太太。

passages.original: I presume you've heard of me--most of the good people in the town have--and maybe some of the things you've heard ain't true.
passages.vernacular: 我想你聽講過我——鎮上大多數好人都聽講過——而且你聽到嘅某些事或者唔係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你聽說過我——鎮上大多數好人都聽說過——而且你聽到的某些事也許不是真的。

passages.original: But never mind that.
passages.vernacular: 不過冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過沒關係。

passages.original: It's about the little girl I came.
passages.vernacular: 我係為了嗰個小姑娘嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是為了那個小姑娘來的。

passages.original: I heard about the accident, and--and it broke me all up.
passages.vernacular: 我聽講咗嗰次事故,然後——我整個人都崩潰喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽說了那次事故,然後——我整個人都崩潰了。

passages.original: Last week I heard how she couldn't ever walk again, and--and I wished I could give up my two uselessly well legs for hers.
passages.vernacular: 上星期我聽講佢再都唔能夠走路喇,然後——我真希望我能把我呢兩條冇用嘅好腿換畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上星期我聽說她再也不能走路了,然後——我真希望我能把我這兩條沒用的好腿換給她。

passages.original: She'd do more good trotting around on 'em one hour than I could in a hundred years.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺上面蹦跳一個鐘頭,都比我一百年做嘅好事仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在上面蹦跳一個鐘頭,也比我一百年做的好事還多。

passages.original: But never mind that.
passages.vernacular: 不過冇關係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過沒關係。

passages.original: Legs ain't always given to the one who can make the best use of 'em, I notice.”
passages.vernacular: 我發現,腿并不總是長喺最能好好利用佢哋嘅人身上。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我發現,腿并不總是長在最能好好利用它們的人身上。」

passages.original: She paused, and cleared her throat; but when she resumed her voice was still husky.
passages.vernacular: 佢停咗下嚟,清咗清嗓子;不過佢再次開口時,聲音仍然沙啞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她停了下來,清了清嗓子;可是她再次開口時,聲音仍然沙啞。

passages.original: “Maybe you don't know it, but I've seen a good deal of that little girl of yours.
passages.vernacular: 「或者你唔知道,你嗰個小姑娘我見過不少次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許你不知道,你那個小姑娘我見過不少次。

passages.original: We live on the Pendleton Hill road, and she used to go by often--only she didn't always GO BY.
passages.vernacular: 我哋住喺潘德爾頓山路上,佢以前常經過——只係佢并不總是只係經過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們住在潘德爾頓山路上,她以前常經過——只是她并不總是只是經過。

passages.original: She came in and played with the kids and talked to me--and my man, when he was home.
passages.vernacular: 佢進嚟同細路哋玩,跟我講話——我男人喺家嘅時候都跟佢講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她進來和孩子們玩,跟我說話——我男人在家的時候也跟他說。

passages.original: She seemed to like it, and to like us.
passages.vernacular: 佢似乎鍾意咁樣,都鍾意我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她似乎喜歡這樣,也喜歡我們。

passages.original: She didn't know, I suspect, that her kind of folks don't generally call on my kind.
passages.vernacular: 我猜佢唔知道,佢嗰一類嘅人通常唔會拜訪我呢一類嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我猜她不知道,她那一類的人通常不會拜訪我這一類的人。

passages.original: Maybe if they DID call more, Miss Harrington, there wouldn't be so many--of my kind,” she added, with sudden bitterness.
passages.vernacular: 或者佢哋要係多去拜訪,哈靈頓小姐,就唔會有咁多——我呢一類嘅人喇,」佢突然帶住苦澀補充道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許他們要是多去拜訪,哈靈頓小姐,就不會有那麼多——我這一類的人了,」她突然帶著苦澀補充道。

passages.original: “Be that as it may, she came; and she didn't do herself no harm, and she did do us good--a lot o' good.
passages.vernacular: 「不管點講,佢嚟喇;佢對自己冇害處,對我哋卻有好處——好大嘅好處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不管怎麼說,她來了;她對自己沒有害處,對我們卻有好處——很大的好處。

passages.original: How much she won't know--nor can't know, I hope; 'cause if she did, she'd know other things--that I don't want her to know.
passages.vernacular: 有多大佢唔會知道——都唔能夠知道,我希望;因為要係佢知道喇,佢就會知道別嘅事——嗰啲我唔想讓佢知道嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有多大她不會知道——也不能知道,我希望;因為要是她知道了,她就會知道別的事——那些我不想讓她知道的事。

passages.original: “But it's just this.
passages.vernacular: 「不過情況係咁樣嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是情況是這樣的。

passages.original: It's been hard times with us this year, in more ways than one.
passages.vernacular: 今年我哋過得好艱難,不止一個方面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今年我們過得很艱難,不止一個方面。

passages.original: We've been blue and discouraged--my man and me, and ready for--'most anything.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一直好沮喪、灰心——我男人同我,準備好喇——幾乎乜嘢都做得出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一直很沮喪、灰心——我男人和我,準備好了——幾乎什麼都做得出來。

passages.original: We was reckoning on getting a divorce about now, and letting the kids well, we didn't know what we would do with the kids.
passages.vernacular: 我哋正打算大約呢個時候離婚,讓細路哋——嗯,我哋唔知道該攞細路哋點算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們正打算大約這個時候離婚,讓孩子們——嗯,我們不知道該拿孩子們怎麼辦。

passages.original: Then came the accident, and what we heard about the little girl's never walking again.
passages.vernacular: 然後出咗呢次事故,我哋聽講嗰個小姑娘再都唔能夠走路喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後出了這次事故,我們聽說那個小姑娘再也不能走路了。

passages.original: And we got to thinking how she used to come and sit on our doorstep and train with the kids, and laugh, and--and just be glad.
passages.vernacular: 我哋就開始想,佢以前點樣過嚟坐喺我哋嘅門階上,跟細路哋一起操練,笑住,而且——就係高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們就開始想,她以前怎樣過來坐在我們的門階上,跟孩子們一起操練,笑著,而且——就是高興。

passages.original: She was always being glad about something; and then, one day, she told us why, and about the game, you know; and tried to coax us to play it.
passages.vernacular: 佢總是為某件事高興;然後有一天,佢告訴咗我哋點解,仲有嗰個遊戲,你知道;并想哄我哋玩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她總是為某件事高興;然後有一天,她告訴了我們為什麼,還有那個遊戲,你知道;并想哄我們玩。

passages.original: “Well, we've heard now that she's fretting her poor little life out of her, because she can't play it no more--that there's nothing to be glad about.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我哋而家聽講佢為了再都玩不咗而煩惱得要命——講係冇乜嘢值得高興嘅喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我們現在聽說她為了再也玩不了而煩惱得要命——說是沒有什麼值得高興的了。

passages.original: And that's what I came to tell her to-day--that maybe she can be a little glad for us, 'cause we've decided to stick to each other, and play the game ourselves.
passages.vernacular: 所以我今日嚟就係要告訴佢呢個——或者佢可以為我哋稍微高興啲,因為我哋決定廝守喺一起,自己嚟玩呢個遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我今天來就是要告訴她這個——也許她可以為我們稍微高興一點,因為我們決定廝守在一起,自己來玩這個遊戲。

passages.original: I knew she would be glad, because she used to feel kind of bad--at things we said, sometimes.
passages.vernacular: 我知道佢會高興嘅,因為佢以前有時對我哋講嘅話感到有點難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道她會高興的,因為她以前有時對我們說的話感到有點難過。

passages.original: Just how the game is going to help us, I can't say that I exactly see, yet; but maybe 'twill.
passages.vernacular: 呢個遊戲到底點幫我哋,我仲唔能夠講我完全睇得出嚟;但或者會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個遊戲到底怎麼幫我們,我還不能說我完全看得出來;但也許會的。

passages.original: Anyhow, we're going to try--'cause she wanted us to.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,我哋要試一試——因為佢希望我哋咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,我們要試一試——因為她希望我們這樣。

passages.original: Will you tell her?”
passages.vernacular: 你會告訴佢嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會告訴她嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, I will tell her,” promised Miss Polly, a little faintly.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,我會告訴佢,」波莉小姐有些微弱地許諾道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,我會告訴她,」波莉小姐有些微弱地許諾道。

passages.original: Then, with sudden impulse, she stepped forward and held out her hand.
passages.vernacular: 然後,佢突然衝動地走上前去,伸出咗手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,她突然衝動地走上前去,伸出了手。

passages.original: “And thank you for coming, Mrs. Payson,” she said simply.
passages.vernacular: 「謝謝你嚟,佩森太太,」佢簡單地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「謝謝你來,佩森太太,」她簡單地說。

passages.original: The defiant chin fell.
passages.vernacular: 嗰挑釁嘅下巴垂咗下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那挑釁的下巴垂了下來。

passages.original: The lips above it trembled visibly.
passages.vernacular: 下巴上面嘅嘴唇明顯地顫抖住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下巴上面的嘴唇明顯地顫抖著。

passages.original: With an incoherently mumbled something, Mrs. Payson blindly clutched at the outstretched hand, turned, and fled.
passages.vernacular: 佩森太太含糊不清地嘟噥咗點乜嘢,盲目地抓住咗伸出嘅手,轉身跑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 佩森太太含糊不清地嘟噥了點什麼,盲目地抓住了伸出的手,轉身跑了。

passages.original: The door had scarcely closed behind her before Miss Polly was confronting Nancy in the kitchen.
passages.vernacular: 門喺佢身後剛關上,波莉小姐就喺廚房裡面對南希喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 門在她身後剛關上,波莉小姐就在廚房裡面對南希了。

passages.original: “Nancy!”
passages.vernacular: 「南希!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希!」

passages.original: Miss Polly spoke sharply.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐厲聲講道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐厲聲說道。

passages.original: The series of puzzling, disconcerting visits of the last few days, culminating as they had in the extraordinary experience of the afternoon, had strained her nerves to the snapping point.
passages.vernacular: 最近幾天一連串令人困惑、令人不安嘅嚟訪,喺今日下午嗰次非同尋常嘅經歷中達到頂點,已使佢嘅神經繃到了斷裂嘅邊緣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最近幾天一連串令人困惑、令人不安的來訪,在今天下午那次非同尋常的經歷中達到頂點,已使她的神經繃到了斷裂的邊緣。

passages.original: Not since Miss Pollyanna's accident had Nancy heard her mistress speak so sternly.
passages.vernacular: 自從波莉安娜小姐出事以來,南希仲冇聽女主人咁樣嚴厲地講過話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 自從波莉安娜小姐出事以來,南希還沒聽女主人這樣嚴厲地說過話。

passages.original: “Nancy, WILL you tell me what this absurd 'game' is that the whole town seems to be babbling about?
passages.vernacular: 「南希,你能唔能夠告訴我,呢個荒唐嘅『遊戲』到底係乜嘢,全鎮嘅人好像都喺念叨佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希,你能不能告訴我,這個荒唐的『遊戲』到底是什麼,全鎮的人好像都在念叨它?

passages.original: And what, please, has my niece to do with it?
passages.vernacular: 仲有,我嘅外甥女同佢有乜嘢關係?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,我的外甥女和它有什麼關係?

passages.original: WHY does everybody, from Milly Snow to Mrs. Tom Payson, send word to her that they're 'playing it'?
passages.vernacular: 點解從米莉·斯諾到湯姆·佩森太太,每個人都畀佢捎口信講佢哋喺『玩佢』?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼從米莉·斯諾到湯姆·佩森太太,每個人都給她捎口信說他們在『玩它』?

passages.original: As near as I can judge, half the town are putting on blue ribbons, or stopping family quarrels, or learning to like something they never liked before, and all because of Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 據我所能判斷嘅,鎮上有一半嘅人喺戴藍絲帶,或者唔再吵架,或者學住鍾意以前從不鍾意嘅嘢,而呢一切都係因為波莉安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 據我所能判斷的,鎮上有一半的人在戴藍絲帶,或者不再吵架,或者學著喜歡以前從不喜歡的東西,而這一切都是因為波莉安娜。

passages.original: I tried to ask the child herself about it, but I can't seem to make much headway, and of course I don't like to worry her--now.
passages.vernacular: 我試住問嗰細路本人,不過好像問不出乜嘢名堂,而且我當然不愿意喺呢個時候讓佢煩惱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我試著問那孩子本人,可是好像問不出什麼名堂,而且我當然不愿意在這個時候讓她煩惱。

passages.original: But from something I heard her say to you last night, I should judge you were one of them, too.
passages.vernacular: 不過從琴晚我聽到佢對你講嘅話嚟判斷,我想你都係其中一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過從昨晚我聽到她對你說的話來判斷,我想你也是其中一個。

passages.original: Now WILL you tell me what it all means?”
passages.vernacular: 而家你能唔能夠告訴我,呢到底係點回事?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在你能不能告訴我,這到底是怎麼回事?」

passages.original: To Miss Polly's surprise and dismay, Nancy burst into tears.
passages.vernacular: 令波莉小姐驚訝同沮喪嘅係,南希突然哭咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 令波莉小姐驚訝和沮喪的是,南希突然哭了起來。

passages.original: “It means that ever since last June that blessed child has jest been makin' the whole town glad, an' now they're turnin' 'round an' tryin' ter make her a little glad, too.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢個就係講,從去年六月起,嗰個可愛嘅細路就一直喺讓整個小鎮高興,而而家大家反過嚟,都想讓佢稍微高興啲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這就是說,從去年六月起,那個可愛的孩子就一直在讓整個小鎮高興,而現在大家反過來,也想讓她稍微高興一點。」

passages.original: “Glad of what?”
passages.vernacular: 「高興乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興什麼?」

passages.original: “Just glad!
passages.vernacular: 「就係高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「就是高興!

passages.original: That's the game.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰個遊戲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那個遊戲。」

passages.original: Miss Polly actually stamped her foot.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐竟然跺咗一下腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐竟然跺了一下腳。

passages.original: “There you go like all the rest, Nancy.
passages.vernacular: 「你都同其他人一樣,南希。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你也和其他人一樣,南希。

passages.original: What game?”
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢遊戲?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼遊戲?」

passages.original: Nancy lifted her chin.
passages.vernacular: 南希抬起下巴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希抬起下巴。

passages.original: She faced her mistress and looked her squarely in the eye.
passages.vernacular: 佢面對女主人,直直地睇住佢嘅眼睛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她面對女主人,直直地看著她的眼睛。

passages.original: “I'll tell ye, ma'am.
passages.vernacular: 「我告訴你,太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我告訴你,太太。

passages.original: It's a game Miss Pollyanna's father learned her ter play.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係波莉安娜小姐嘅父親教佢玩嘅遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是波莉安娜小姐的父親教她玩的遊戲。

passages.original: She got a pair of crutches once in a missionary barrel when she was wantin' a doll; an' she cried, of course, like any child would.
passages.vernacular: 有一次佢喺傳教士嘅桶裡得到咗一副拐杖,而當時佢想要嘅係洋娃娃;佢當然像任何細路一樣哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一次她在傳教士的桶裡得到了一副拐杖,而當時她想要的是洋娃娃;她當然像任何孩子一樣哭了。

passages.original: It seems 'twas then her father told her that there wasn't ever anythin' but what there was somethin' about it that you could be glad about; an' that she could be glad about them crutches.”
passages.vernacular: 似乎就係嗰時佢父親告訴佢,世上冇邊件事,裡面唔係有可以高興嘅地方嘅;而且佢可以為嗰副拐杖高興。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 似乎就是那時她父親告訴她,世上沒有哪件事,裡面不是有可以高興的地方的;而且她可以為那副拐杖高興。」

passages.original: “Glad for--CRUTCHES!”
passages.vernacular: 「為——拐杖高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為——拐杖高興!」

passages.original: Miss Polly choked back a sob--she was thinking of the helpless little legs on the bed up-stairs.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐強咽下一聲啜泣——佢想到咗樓上床上嗰雙無助嘅小腿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐強咽下一聲啜泣——她想到了樓上床上那雙無助的小腿。

passages.original: “Yes'm.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,太太。

passages.original: That's what I said, an' Miss Pollyanna said that's what she said, too.
passages.vernacular: 我都係咁講嘅,波莉安娜小姐講佢當時都係咁講嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也是這麼說的,波莉安娜小姐說她當時也是這麼說的。

passages.original: But he told her she COULD be glad--'cause she DIDN'T NEED 'EM.”
passages.vernacular: 不過佢告訴佢,佢可以高興——因為佢不需要佢哋。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是他告訴她,她可以高興——因為她不需要它們。」

passages.original: “Oh-h!” cried Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦——!」波莉小姐叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦——!」波莉小姐叫道。

passages.original: “And after that she said he made a regular game of it--findin' somethin' in everythin' ter be glad about.
passages.vernacular: 「從嗰以後,佢講佢把佢變成咗一個正式嘅遊戲——喺每件事裡找出可以高興嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「從那以後,她說他把它變成了一個正式的遊戲——在每件事裡找出可以高興的地方。

passages.original: An' she said ye could do it, too, and that ye didn't seem ter mind not havin' the doll so much, 'cause ye was so glad ye DIDN'T need the crutches.
passages.vernacular: 佢講你都能做到,而且你似乎都冇咁在意冇得到洋娃娃,因為你咁高興自己不需要拐杖。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說你也能做到,而且你似乎也沒那麼在意沒得到洋娃娃,因為你那麼高興自己不需要拐杖。

passages.original: An' they called it the 'jest bein' glad' game.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋把佢叫做『只管高興』遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們把它叫做『只管高興』遊戲。

passages.original: That's the game, ma'am.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰個遊戲,太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那個遊戲,太太。

passages.original: She's played it ever since.”
passages.vernacular: 佢從嗰以後就一直喺玩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她從那以後就一直在玩。」

passages.original: “But, how--how--” Miss Polly came to a helpless pause.
passages.vernacular: 「不過,點——點——」波莉小姐無助地停住喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,怎麼——怎麼——」波莉小姐無助地停住了。

passages.original: “An' you'd be surprised ter find how cute it works, ma'am, too,” maintained Nancy, with almost the eagerness of Pollyanna herself.
passages.vernacular: 「你要係知道佢多靈驗,會食驚嘅,太太,」南希堅持講,幾乎帶住波莉安娜本人嗰樣嘅熱切。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你要是知道它多靈驗,會吃驚的,太太,」南希堅持說,幾乎帶著波莉安娜本人那樣的熱切。

passages.original: “I wish I could tell ye what a lot she's done for mother an' the folks out home.
passages.vernacular: 「我真希望能告訴你,佢為我媽媽同老家嘅人做咗多少事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我真希望能告訴你,她為我媽媽和老家的人做了多少事。

passages.original: She's been ter see 'em, ye know, twice, with me.
passages.vernacular: 你知道,佢跟我一起去睇過佢哋兩次。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,她跟我一起去看過他們兩次。

passages.original: She's made me glad, too, on such a lot o' things--little things, an' big things; an' it's made 'em so much easier.
passages.vernacular: 佢都讓我對好多事情高興起嚟——小事,大事;讓一切容易多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她也讓我對很多事情高興起來——小事,大事;讓一切容易多了。

passages.original: For instance, I don't mind 'Nancy' for a name half as much since she told me I could be glad 'twa'n't 'Hephzibah.'
passages.vernacular: 比方講,自從佢告訴我可以高興我嘅名字唔係『赫夫齊芭』之後,我就不咁介意『南希』呢個名字喇,連一半都不介意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 比方說,自從她告訴我可以高興我的名字不是『赫夫齊芭』之後,我就不那麼介意『南希』這個名字了,連一半都不介意。

passages.original: An' there's Monday mornin's, too, that I used ter hate so.
passages.vernacular: 仲有星期一嘅早晨,我以前最討厭嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有星期一的早晨,我以前最討厭的。

passages.original: She's actually made me glad for Monday mornin's.”
passages.vernacular: 佢竟然讓我對星期一嘅早晨都高興起嚟喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她竟然讓我對星期一的早晨也高興起來了。」

passages.original: “Glad--for Monday mornings!”
passages.vernacular: 「高興——星期一早晨!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「高興——星期一早晨!」

passages.original: Nancy laughed.
passages.vernacular: 南希笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希笑了。

passages.original: “I know it does sound nutty, ma'am.
passages.vernacular: 「我知道呢聽起嚟好瘋,太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我知道這聽起來很瘋,太太。

passages.original: But let me tell ye.
passages.vernacular: 不過讓我告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是讓我告訴你。

passages.original: That blessed lamb found out I hated Monday mornin's somethin' awful; an' what does she up an' tell me one day but this: 'Well, anyhow, Nancy, I should think you could be gladder on Monday mornin' than on any other day in the week, because 'twould be a whole WEEK before you'd have another one!'
passages.vernacular: 嗰個可愛嘅小羊羔發現我特別恨星期一嘅早晨;有一天佢竟對我講:『嗯,不管點樣,南希,我想星期一早晨你該比一週裡任何一天都更高興才對,因為要整整一個星期才會再碰到下一個呢!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個可愛的小羊羔發現我特別恨星期一的早晨;有一天她竟對我說:『嗯,不管怎樣,南希,我想星期一早晨你該比一週裡任何一天都更高興才對,因為要整整一個星期才會再碰到下一個呢!』

passages.original: An' I'm blest if I hain't thought of it ev'ry Monday mornin' since--an' it HAS helped, ma'am.
passages.vernacular: 我敢講,從嗰以後每個星期一早晨我都會想到呢句話——而且確實有幫助,太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢說,從那以後每個星期一早晨我都會想到這句話——而且確實有幫助,太太。

passages.original: It made me laugh, anyhow, ev'ry time I thought of it; an' laughin' helps, ye know--it does, it does!”
passages.vernacular: 無論如何,每次想到佢我都會笑;笑係有幫助嘅,你知道——係嘅,係嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無論如何,每次想到它我都會笑;笑是有幫助的,你知道——是的,是的!」

passages.original: “But why hasn't--she told me--the game?” faltered Miss Polly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢點解冇告訴我——呢個遊戲?」波莉小姐支吾地講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她為什麼沒有告訴我——這個遊戲?」波莉小姐支吾地說。

passages.original: “Why has she made such a mystery of it, when I asked her?”
passages.vernacular: 「我問佢嘅時候,佢點解要把佢弄得咁神秘?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我問她的時候,她為什麼要把它弄得那麼神秘?」

passages.original: Nancy hesitated.
passages.vernacular: 南希猶豫喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 南希猶豫了。

passages.original: “Beggin' yer pardon, ma'am, you told her not ter speak of--her father; so she couldn't tell ye.
passages.vernacular: 「請恕我直言,太太,你告訴過佢唔好提——佢父親;所以佢冇法告訴你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「請恕我直言,太太,你告訴過她不要提——她父親;所以她沒法告訴你。

passages.original: 'Twas her father's game, ye see.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,呢個係佢父親嘅遊戲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,這是她父親的遊戲。」

passages.original: Miss Polly bit her lip.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐咬住咗嘴唇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐咬住了嘴唇。

passages.original: “She wanted ter tell ye, first off,” continued Nancy, a little unsteadily.
passages.vernacular: 「佢一開始就想告訴你嘅,」南希有點不穩地接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她一開始就想告訴你的,」南希有點不穩地接著說。

passages.original: “She wanted somebody ter play it with, ye know.
passages.vernacular: 「佢想找個人一起玩,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她想找個人一起玩,你知道。

passages.original: That's why I begun it, so she could have some one.”
passages.vernacular: 所以我才開始玩嘅,好讓佢有個伴。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我才開始玩的,好讓她有個伴。」

passages.original: “And--and--these others?”
passages.vernacular: 「咁——咁——其他呢啲人呢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼——那麼——其他這些人呢?」

passages.original: Miss Polly's voice shook now.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅聲音而家顫抖喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的聲音現在顫抖了。

passages.original: “Oh, ev'rybody, 'most, knows it now, I guess.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我想,而家差不多人人都知道喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我想,現在差不多人人都知道了。

passages.original: Anyhow, I should think they did from the way I'm hearin' of it ev'rywhere I go.
passages.vernacular: 不管點樣,從我走到邊兒都聽到嘅情形嚟睇,我想係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不管怎樣,從我走到哪兒都聽到的情形來看,我想是這樣。

passages.original: Of course she told a lot, and they told the rest.
passages.vernacular: 當然,佢告訴咗不少人,佢哋又告訴咗其他人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當然,她告訴了不少人,他們又告訴了其他人。

passages.original: Them things go, ye know, when they gets started.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲事情一旦傳開咗就係咁樣,你知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些事情一旦傳開了就是這樣,你知道。

passages.original: An' she was always so smilin' an' pleasant ter ev'ry one, an' so--so jest glad herself all the time, that they couldn't help knowin' it, anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 而且佢對每個人都總是咁笑瞇瞇、咁和藹,佢自己又總是咁——咁只管高興,所以佢哋無論如何都唔可能唔知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且她對每個人都總是那麼笑瞇瞇、那麼和藹,她自己又總是那麼——那麼只管高興,所以他們無論如何都不可能不知道的。

passages.original: Now, since she's hurt, ev'rybody feels so bad--specially when they heard how bad SHE feels 'cause she can't find anythin' ter be glad about.
passages.vernacular: 而家,自從佢受傷以後,人人都咁難受——特別係聽講佢自己因為找唔到任何可以高興嘅事而幾咁難受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,自從她受傷以後,人人都那麼難受——特別是聽說她自己因為找不到任何可以高興的事而多麼難受。

passages.original: An' so they've been comin' ev'ry day ter tell her how glad she's made THEM, hopin' that'll help some.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢哋每天都嚟,告訴佢佢讓佢哋幾咁高興,希望呢會有點幫助。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他們每天都來,告訴她她讓他們多麼高興,希望這會有點幫助。

passages.original: Ye see, she's always wanted ev'rybody ter play the game with her.”
passages.vernacular: 你睇,佢一直希望人人都跟佢一起玩呢個遊戲。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看,她一直希望人人都跟她一起玩這個遊戲。」

passages.original: “Well, I know somebody who'll play it--now,” choked Miss Polly, as she turned and sped through the kitchen doorway.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我知道有一個人會玩——而家,」波莉小姐哽咽住講,轉身快步穿過廚房嘅門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我知道有一個人會玩——現在,」波莉小姐哽咽著說,轉身快步穿過廚房的門口。

passages.original: Behind her, Nancy stood staring amazedly.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢身後,南希食驚地呆呆望住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她身後,南希吃驚地呆呆望著。

passages.original: “Well, I'll believe anythin'--anythin' now,” she muttered to herself.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,我而家乜嘢都信喇——乜嘢都信喇,」佢喃喃自語。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,我現在什麼都信了——什麼都信了,」她喃喃自語。

passages.original: “Ye can't stump me with anythin' I wouldn't believe, now--o' Miss Polly!”
passages.vernacular: 「你而家講乜嘢我都唔會覺得不可信喇——哦,波莉小姐!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你現在說什麼我都不會覺得不可信了——哦,波莉小姐!」

passages.original: A little later, in Pollyanna's room, the nurse left Miss Polly and Pollyanna alone together.
passages.vernacular: 稍後,喺波莉安娜嘅房間裡,護士離開喇,留下波莉小姐同波莉安娜單獨喺一起。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後,在波莉安娜的房間裡,護士離開了,留下波莉小姐和波莉安娜單獨在一起。

passages.original: “And you've had still another caller to-day, my dear,” announced Miss Polly, in a voice she vainly tried to steady.
passages.vernacular: 「你今日仲有另一位訪客,親愛嘅,」波莉小姐宣布道,聲音徒勞地想保持平穩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你今天還有另一位訪客,親愛的,」波莉小姐宣布道,聲音徒勞地想保持平穩。

passages.original: “Do you remember Mrs. Payson?”
passages.vernacular: 「你仲記得佩森太太嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你還記得佩森太太嗎?」

passages.original: “Mrs. Payson?
passages.vernacular: 「佩森太太?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「佩森太太?

passages.original: Why, I reckon I do!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,我當然記得!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,我當然記得!

passages.original: She lives on the way to Mr. Pendleton's, and she's got the prettiest little girl baby three years old, and a boy 'most five.
passages.vernacular: 佢住喺去潘德爾頓先生家嘅路上,佢有個最漂亮嘅三歲小女娃,仲有個快五歲嘅男孩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她住在去潘德爾頓先生家的路上,她有個最漂亮的三歲小女娃,還有個快五歲的男孩。

passages.original: She's awfully nice, and so's her husband--only they don't seem to know how nice each other is.
passages.vernacular: 佢人好好,佢丈夫都係——只係佢哋好像唔知道對方有多好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她人非常好,她丈夫也是——只是他們好像不知道對方有多好。

passages.original: Sometimes they fight--I mean, they don't quite agree.
passages.vernacular: 有時佢哋打架——我係講,佢哋意見不太一致。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時他們打架——我是說,他們意見不太一致。

passages.original: They're poor, too, they say, and of course they don't ever have barrels, 'cause he isn't a missionary minister, you know, like--well, he isn't.”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋仲好窮,佢哋講,當然佢哋從來冇傳教士嘅桶,因為佢唔係傳教士牧師,你知道,像——嗯,佢唔係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們還很窮,他們說,當然他們從來沒有傳教士的桶,因為他不是傳教士牧師,你知道,像——嗯,他不是。」

passages.original: A faint color stole into Pollyanna's cheeks which was duplicated suddenly in those of her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜嘅臉頰泛起淡淡嘅紅暈,佢姨媽嘅臉頰都突然現出同樣嘅紅暈。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜的臉頰泛起淡淡的紅暈,她姨媽的臉頰也突然現出同樣的紅暈。

passages.original: “But she wears real pretty clothes, sometimes, in spite of their being so poor,” resumed Pollyanna, in some haste.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢有時候穿住真漂亮嘅衣服,盡管佢哋咁窮,」波莉安娜有點急忙地接住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是她有時候穿著真漂亮的衣服,盡管他們那麼窮,」波莉安娜有點急忙地接著說。

passages.original: “And she's got perfectly beautiful rings with diamonds and rubies and emeralds in them; but she says she's got one ring too many, and that she's going to throw it away and get a divorce instead.
passages.vernacular: 「佢仲有特別漂亮嘅戒指,上面鑲住鉆石、紅寶石同綠寶石;不過佢講佢多咗一枚戒指,佢要把佢扔掉,改去離婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「她還有特別漂亮的戒指,上面鑲著鉆石、紅寶石和綠寶石;可是她說她多了一枚戒指,她要把它扔掉,改去離婚。

passages.original: What is a divorce, Aunt Polly?
passages.vernacular: 離婚係乜嘢,波莉姨媽?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 離婚是什麼,波莉姨媽?

passages.original: I'm afraid it isn't very nice, because she didn't look happy when she talked about it.
passages.vernacular: 我怕不太好,因為佢談到佢嘅時候睇起嚟不高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕不太好,因為她談到它的時候看起來不高興。

passages.original: And she said if she did get it, they wouldn't live there any more, and that Mr. Payson would go 'way off, and maybe the children, too.
passages.vernacular: 佢講如果真離喇,佢哋就唔會再住喺嗰兒喇,佩森先生會遠遠地走掉,或者細路哋都係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她說如果真離了,他們就不會再住在那兒了,佩森先生會遠遠地走掉,也許孩子們也是。

passages.original: But I should think they'd rather keep the ring, even if they did have so many more.
passages.vernacular: 但係我覺得佢哋寧愿留住戒指,即使佢哋已經有咁多喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是我覺得他們寧愿留著戒指,即使他們已經有那麼多了。

passages.original: Shouldn't you?
passages.vernacular: 你講呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說呢?

passages.original: Aunt Polly, what is a divorce?”
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽,離婚到底係乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽,離婚到底是什麼?」

passages.original: “But they aren't going 'way off, dear,” evaded Aunt Polly, hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 「不過佢哋唔會遠遠地走掉嘅,親愛嘅,」波莉姨媽連忙回避道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是他們不會遠遠地走掉的,親愛的,」波莉姨媽連忙回避道。

passages.original: “They're going to stay right there together.”
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋會留喺嗰度,喺一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們會留在那裡,在一起。」

passages.original: “Oh, I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我真高興!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我真高興!

passages.original: Then they'll be there when I go up to see--O dear!” broke off the little girl, miserably.
passages.vernacular: 嗰樣等我去睇——哎呀!」小姑娘痛苦地突然打住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那樣等我去看——哎呀!」小姑娘痛苦地突然打住。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, why CAN'T I remember that my legs don't go any more, and that I won't ever, ever go up to see Mr. Pendleton again?”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,我點就係記不住我嘅腿再都唔能夠動喇,我再都永遠唔能夠上去睇潘德爾頓先生喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,我怎麼就是記不住我的腿再也不能動了,我再也永遠不能上去看潘德爾頓先生了?」

passages.original: “There, there, don't,” choked her aunt.
passages.vernacular: 「好喇,好喇,別咁樣,」佢姨媽哽咽住講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好了,好了,別這樣,」她姨媽哽咽著說。

passages.original: “Perhaps you'll drive up sometime.
passages.vernacular: 「或者你有一天能坐馬車上去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許你有一天能坐馬車上去。

passages.original: But listen!
passages.vernacular: 不過聽住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是聽著!

passages.original: I haven't told you, yet, all that Mrs. Payson said.
passages.vernacular: 我仲冇把佩森太太講嘅話全告訴你呢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還沒把佩森太太說的話全告訴你呢。

passages.original: She wanted me to tell you that they--they were going to stay together and to play the game, just as you wanted them to.”
passages.vernacular: 佢要我告訴你,佢哋——佢哋打算留喺一起,玩嗰個遊戲,就像你希望嘅嗰樣。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她要我告訴你,他們——他們打算留在一起,玩那個遊戲,就像你希望的那樣。」

passages.original: Pollyanna smiled through tear-wet eyes.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜含住淚微笑喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜含著淚微笑了。

passages.original: “Did they?
passages.vernacular: 「真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「真的嗎?

passages.original: Did they, really?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋真嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們真的嗎?

passages.original: Oh, I am glad of that!”
passages.vernacular: 哦,我真為此高興!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我真為此高興!」

passages.original: “Yes, she said she hoped you'd be.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,佢講佢希望你會高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,她說她希望你會高興。

passages.original: That's why she told you, to make you--GLAD, Pollyanna.”
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係佢告訴你嘅原因,為了讓你——高興,波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是她告訴你的原因,為了讓你——高興,波莉安娜。」

passages.original: Pollyanna looked up quickly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜好快地抬起頭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜很快地抬起頭來。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, you--you spoke just as if you knew--DO you know about the game, Aunt Polly?”
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,你——你講得好像你知道似嘅——你知道嗰個遊戲嗎,波莉姨媽?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,你——你說得好像你知道似的——你知道那個遊戲嗎,波莉姨媽?」

passages.original: “Yes, dear.”
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,親愛嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,親愛的。」

passages.original: Miss Polly sternly forced her voice to be cheerfully matter-of-fact.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嚴厲地迫使自己嘅聲音保持愉快嘅平實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐嚴厲地迫使自己的聲音保持愉快的平實。

passages.original: “Nancy told me.
passages.vernacular: 「南希告訴我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「南希告訴我的。

passages.original: I think it's a beautiful game.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得嗰個係個好美嘅遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得那是個很美的遊戲。

passages.original: I'm going to play it now--with you.”
passages.vernacular: 我而家要玩佢喇——同你一起。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在要玩它了——和你一起。」

passages.original: “Oh, Aunt Polly--YOU?
passages.vernacular: 「哦,波莉姨媽——你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,波莉姨媽——你?

passages.original: I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 我太高興喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興了!

passages.original: You see, I've really wanted you most of anybody, all the time.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,我一直最想要嘅就係你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,我一直最想要的就是你。」

passages.original: Aunt Polly caught her breath a little sharply.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽嘅呼吸微微一滯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽的呼吸微微一滯。

passages.original: It was even harder this time to keep her voice steady; but she did it.
passages.vernacular: 呢一次要保持聲音平穩更難喇;但佢做到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一次要保持聲音平穩更難了;但她做到了。

passages.original: “Yes, dear; and there are all those others, too.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,親愛嘅;仲有所有嗰啲其他人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,親愛的;還有所有那些其他人。

passages.original: Why, Pollyanna, I think all the town is playing that game now with you--even to the minister!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉安娜,我想全鎮嘅人而家都喺跟你玩嗰個遊戲——連牧師都係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉安娜,我想全鎮的人現在都在跟你玩那個遊戲——連牧師也是!

passages.original: I haven't had a chance to tell you, yet, but this morning I met Mr. Ford when I was down to the village, and he told me to say to you that just as soon as you could see him, he was coming to tell you that he hadn't stopped being glad over those eight hundred rejoicing texts that you told him about.
passages.vernacular: 我仲冇嚟得及告訴你,今日朝早我到村裡去嘅時候遇見咗福特先生,佢讓我告訴你,只要你一能見佢,佢就嚟告訴你,佢對你告訴佢嘅嗰八百條歡喜嘅經文,一直冇停止高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還沒來得及告訴你,今天早上我到村裡去的時候遇見了福特先生,他讓我告訴你,只要你一能見他,他就來告訴你,他對你告訴他的那八百條歡喜的經文,一直沒有停止高興。

passages.original: So you see, dear, it's just you that have done it.
passages.vernacular: 所以你睇,親愛嘅,呢都係你做成嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你看,親愛的,這都是你做成的。

passages.original: The whole town is playing the game, and the whole town is wonderfully happier--and all because of one little girl who taught the people a new game, and how to play it.”
passages.vernacular: 整個小鎮都喺玩呢個遊戲,整個小鎮都變得好幸福——呢一切都係因為一個小姑娘,佢教咗人哋一個新遊戲,仲教會咗佢哋點玩。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 整個小鎮都在玩這個遊戲,整個小鎮都變得好幸福——這一切都是因為一個小姑娘,她教了人們一個新遊戲,還教會了他們怎麼玩。」

passages.original: Pollyanna clapped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜拍著手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜拍著手。

passages.original: “Oh, I'm so glad,” she cried.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,我真高興,」佢叫道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,我真高興,」她叫道。

passages.original: Then, suddenly, a wonderful light illumined her face.
passages.vernacular: 然後,忽然,一道奇妙嘅光芒照亮咗佢嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後,忽然,一道奇妙的光芒照亮了她的臉。

passages.original: “Why, Aunt Polly, there IS something I can be glad about, after all.
passages.vernacular: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,畢竟定係有一件事我可以高興嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哎呀,波莉姨媽,畢竟還是有一件事我可以高興的。

passages.original: I can be glad I've HAD my legs, anyway--else I couldn't have done--that!”
passages.vernacular: 我可以高興我曾經擁有過我嘅腿,不管點樣——不然我就做不成——嗰啲事喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以高興我曾經擁有過我的腿,不管怎樣——不然我就做不成——那些事了!」

chapters.title: Ch. XXIX Through an Open Window 第二十九章:穿過敞開的窗

passages.original: CH One by one the short winter days came and went--but they were not short to Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 冬天短短嘅日子一天天嚟咗又去——但對波莉安娜來講,佢哋并不短。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冬天短短的日子一天天來了又去——但對波莉安娜來說,它們并不短。

passages.original: They were long, and sometimes full of pain.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋好長,有時充滿痛苦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它們很長,有時充滿痛苦。

passages.original: Very resolutely, these days, however, Pollyanna was turning a cheerful face toward whatever came.
passages.vernacular: 不過呢啲日子裡,波莉安娜好堅決地,對無論降臨乜嘢,都轉向佢哋一張愉快嘅臉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過這些日子裡,波莉安娜非常堅決地,對無論降臨什麼,都轉向它們一張愉快的臉。

passages.original: Was she not specially bound to play the game, now that Aunt Polly was playing it, too?
passages.vernacular: 既然波莉姨媽都喺玩呢個遊戲,佢唔係更有責任玩下去嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然波莉姨媽也在玩這個遊戲,她不是更有責任玩下去嗎?

passages.original: And Aunt Polly found so many things to be glad about!
passages.vernacular: 而且波莉姨媽發現咗咁多值得高興嘅事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且波莉姨媽發現了那麼多值得高興的事!

passages.original: It was Aunt Polly, too, who discovered the story one day about the two poor little waifs in a snow-storm who found a blown-down door to crawl under, and who wondered what poor folks did that didn't have any door!
passages.vernacular: 都係波莉姨媽有一天發現咗嗰個故事:兩個可憐嘅小流浪兒喺暴風雪裡,找到一扇被吹倒嘅門,爬到下面躲住,仲納悶冇門嘅窮人該點算!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也是波莉姨媽有一天發現了那個故事:兩個可憐的小流浪兒在暴風雪裡,找到一扇被吹倒的門,爬到下面躲著,還納悶沒有門的窮人該怎麼辦!

passages.original: And it was Aunt Polly who brought home the other story that she had heard about the poor old lady who had only two teeth, but who was so glad that those two teeth “hit”!
passages.vernacular: 都係波莉姨媽把另一個故事帶回家,係佢聽嚟嘅:一位可憐嘅老太太只剩兩顆牙,卻咁高興嗰兩顆牙剛好「對得上」!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也是波莉姨媽把另一個故事帶回家,是她聽來的:一位可憐的老太太只剩兩顆牙,卻那麼高興那兩顆牙剛好「對得上」!

passages.original: Pollyanna now, like Mrs. Snow, was knitting wonderful things out of bright colored worsteds that trailed their cheery lengths across the white spread, and made Pollyanna--again like Mrs. Snow--so glad she had her hands and arms, anyway.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜而家像斯諾太太一樣,用鮮艷嘅毛線織住奇妙嘅嘢,嗰啲毛線把佢哋歡快嘅長度拖喺白色嘅床罩上,使得波莉安娜——又像斯諾太太一樣——好高興不管點樣自己仲有手同手臂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜現在像斯諾太太一樣,用鮮艷的毛線織著奇妙的東西,那些毛線把它們歡快的長度拖在白色的床罩上,使得波莉安娜——又像斯諾太太一樣——很高興不管怎樣自己還有手和手臂。

passages.original: Pollyanna saw people now, occasionally, and always there were the loving messages from those she could not see; and always they brought her something new to think about--and Pollyanna needed new things to think about.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜而家偶爾能見見人喇,而且總有嗰啲佢見唔到嘅人帶嚟嘅充滿愛嘅口信;呢啲口信總是畀佢帶嚟新嘅嘢去想——而波莉安娜需要新嘅嘢去想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜現在偶爾能見見人了,而且總有那些她見不到的人帶來的充滿愛的口信;這些口信總是給她帶來新的東西去想——而波莉安娜需要新的東西去想。

passages.original: Once she had seen John Pendleton, and twice she had seen Jimmy Bean.
passages.vernacular: 佢見過一次約翰·潘德爾頓,見過兩次吉米·比恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她見過一次約翰·潘德爾頓,見過兩次吉米·比恩。

passages.original: John Pendleton had told her what a fine boy Jimmy was getting to be, and how well he was doing.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓告訴佢吉米越嚟越棒喇,表現得幾咁好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓告訴她吉米越來越棒了,表現得多麼好。

passages.original: Jimmy had told her what a first-rate home he had, and what bang-up “folks” Mr. Pendleton made; and both had said that it was all owing to her.
passages.vernacular: 吉米告訴佢佢有一個幾咁一流嘅家,潘德爾頓先生係幾咁了不起嘅「人」;兩人都講呢全都多虧咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米告訴她他有一個多麼一流的家,潘德爾頓先生是多麼了不起的「人」;兩人都說這全都多虧了她。

passages.original: “Which makes me all the gladder, you know, that I HAVE had my legs,” Pollyanna confided to her aunt afterwards.
passages.vernacular: 「呢讓我更高興喇,你知道,高興我曾經擁有過我嘅腿。」波莉安娜事後對姨媽吐露道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這讓我更高興了,你知道,高興我曾經擁有過我的腿。」波莉安娜事後對姨媽吐露道。

passages.original: The winter passed, and spring came.
passages.vernacular: 冬天過去喇,春天嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 冬天過去了,春天來了。

passages.original: The anxious watchers over Pollyanna's condition could see little change wrought by the prescribed treatment.
passages.vernacular: 焦急地守望住波莉安娜病情嘅人哋,睇不出規定嘅治療帶嚟咗多少變化。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 焦急地守望著波莉安娜病情的人們,看不出規定的治療帶來了多少變化。

passages.original: There seemed every reason to believe, indeed, that Dr. Mead's worst fears would be realized--that Pollyanna would never walk again.
passages.vernacular: 確實,似乎有充分嘅理由相信,米德醫生最糟嘅擔心會成真——波莉安娜將永遠唔能夠再走路喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 確實,似乎有充分的理由相信,米德醫生最糟的擔心會成真——波莉安娜將永遠不能再走路了。

passages.original: Beldingsville, of course, kept itself informed concerning Pollyanna; and of Beldingsville, one man in particular fumed and fretted himself into a fever of anxiety over the daily bulletins which he managed in some way to procure from the bed of suffering.
passages.vernacular: 貝爾丁斯維爾當然一直喺了解波莉安娜嘅情況;而喺貝爾丁斯維爾,有一個人特別地,對佢設法從病床邊弄到嘅每日消息焦慮得發咗燒,坐立不安。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝爾丁斯維爾當然一直在了解波莉安娜的情況;而在貝爾丁斯維爾,有一個人特別地,對他設法從病床邊弄到的每日消息焦慮得發了燒,坐立不安。

passages.original: As the days passed, however, and the news came to be no better, but rather worse, something besides anxiety began to show in the man's face: despair, and a very dogged determination, each fighting for the mastery.
passages.vernacular: 不過隨住日子一天天過去,消息并冇好轉,反而更糟,嗰人嘅臉上開始顯現出焦慮以外嘅嘢:絕望,同一種好頑強嘅決心,兩者喺爭奪主導。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是隨著日子一天天過去,消息并沒有好轉,反而更糟,那人的臉上開始顯現出焦慮以外的東西:絕望,和一種非常頑強的決心,兩者在爭奪主導。

passages.original: In the end, the dogged determination won; and it was then that Mr. John Pendleton, somewhat to his surprise, received one Saturday morning a call from Dr. Thomas Chilton.
passages.vernacular: 最終,頑強嘅決心獲勝;就喺嗰時,約翰·潘德爾頓先生有些意外地,喺一個星期六嘅上午,迎嚟咗托馬斯·奇爾頓醫生嘅拜訪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最終,頑強的決心獲勝;就在那時,約翰·潘德爾頓先生有些意外地,在一個星期六的上午,迎來了托馬斯·奇爾頓醫生的拜訪。

passages.original: “Pendleton,” began the doctor, abruptly, “I've come to you because you, better than any one else in town, know something of my relations with Miss Polly Harrington.”
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓,」醫生突兀地開口講,「我嚟找你,係因為你比鎮上任何人都更了解我同波莉·哈靈頓小姐之間嘅啲關係。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓,」醫生突兀地開口說,「我來找你,是因為你比鎮上任何人都更了解我和波莉·哈靈頓小姐之間的一些關係。」

passages.original: John Pendleton was conscious that he must have started visibly--he did know something of the affair between Polly Harrington and Thomas Chilton, but the matter had not been mentioned between them for fifteen years, or more.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓意識到自己一定明顯地一驚——佢確實知道波莉·哈靈頓同托馬斯·奇爾頓之間嘅啲事,但呢事佢哋之間已有十五年或更久冇提起過喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓意識到自己一定明顯地一驚——他確實知道波莉·哈靈頓和托馬斯·奇爾頓之間的一些事,但這事他們之間已有十五年或更久沒有提起過了。

passages.original: “Yes,” he said, trying to make his voice sound concerned enough for sympathy, and not eager enough for curiosity.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,」佢講,努力讓自己嘅聲音聽起嚟足夠關切以示同情,又不至于急切得顯出好奇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,」他說,努力讓自己的聲音聽起來足夠關切以示同情,又不至于急切得顯出好奇。

passages.original: In a moment he saw that he need not have worried, however: the doctor was quite too intent on his errand to notice how that errand was received.
passages.vernacular: 不過轉眼佢就明白自己唔使擔心喇:醫生太專注于佢此行嘅目的,根本冇注意呢個目的被點樣接受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過轉眼他就明白自己不必擔心了:醫生太專注于他此行的目的,根本沒注意這個目的被怎樣接受。

passages.original: “Pendleton, I want to see that child.
passages.vernacular: 「潘德爾頓,我想見見嗰個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「潘德爾頓,我想見見那個孩子。

passages.original: I want to make an examination.
passages.vernacular: 我想做個檢查。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想做個檢查。

passages.original: I MUST make an examination.”
passages.vernacular: 我必須做檢查。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我必須做檢查。」

passages.original: “Well--can't you?”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯——你唔能夠嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯——你不能嗎?」

passages.original: “CAN'T I!
passages.vernacular: 「我唔能夠嗎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不能嗎!

passages.original: Pendleton, you know very well I haven't been inside that door for more than fifteen years.
passages.vernacular: 潘德爾頓,你好清楚我已經有十五年多冇踏進過嗰扇門喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潘德爾頓,你很清楚我已經有十五年多沒踏進過那扇門了。

passages.original: You don't know--but I will tell you--that the mistress of that house told me that the NEXT time she ASKED me to enter it, I might take it that she was begging my pardon, and that all would be as before--which meant that she'd marry me.
passages.vernacular: 你唔知道——但我告訴你——嗰座房子嘅女主人曾對我講,下一次佢請我進去,我就可以當作佢喺向我道歉,一切將像從前一樣——嗰意味住佢會嫁畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不知道——但我告訴你——那座房子的女主人曾對我說,下一次她請我進去,我就可以當作她在向我道歉,一切將像從前一樣——那意味著她會嫁給我。

passages.original: Perhaps you see her summoning me now--but I don't!”
passages.vernacular: 或者你睇到佢而家召我去喇——可我冇睇到!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也許你看到她現在召我去了——可我沒看到!」

passages.original: “But couldn't you go--without a summons?”
passages.vernacular: 「不過你唔能夠不等召喚就去嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是你不能不等召喚就去嗎?」

passages.original: The doctor frowned.
passages.vernacular: 醫生皺起眉頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生皺起眉頭。

passages.original: “Well, hardly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,幾乎唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,幾乎不可能。

passages.original: I have some pride, you know.”
passages.vernacular: 你知道,我都有點自尊。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道,我也有點自尊。」

passages.original: “But if you're so anxious--couldn't you swallow your pride and forget the quarrel--”
passages.vernacular: 「不過如果你咁焦急——難道你唔能夠咽下自尊,忘掉嗰場爭吵嗎——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是如果你這麼焦急——難道你不能咽下自尊,忘掉那場爭吵嗎——」

passages.original: “Forget the quarrel!” interrupted the doctor, savagely.
passages.vernacular: 「忘掉嗰場爭吵!」醫生兇狠地打斷道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「忘掉那場爭吵!」醫生兇狠地打斷道。

passages.original: “I'm not talking of that kind of pride.
passages.vernacular: 「我講嘅唔係嗰種自尊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我說的不是那種自尊。

passages.original: So far as THAT is concerned, I'd go from here there on my knees--or on my head--if that would do any good.
passages.vernacular: 就嗰個而言,只要有用,我可以跪住——或者倒立住——從呢兒爬過去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就那個而言,只要有用,我可以跪著——或者倒立著——從這兒爬過去。

passages.original: It's PROFESSIONAL pride I'm talking about.
passages.vernacular: 我講嘅係職業上嘅自尊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說的是職業上的自尊。

passages.original: It's a case of sickness, and I'm a doctor.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個病例,而我係個醫生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個病例,而我是個醫生。

passages.original: I can't butt in and say, 'Here, take me! can I?”
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠硬闖進去講:『喂,讓我嚟!』能嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能硬闖進去說:『喂,讓我來!』能嗎?」

passages.original: “Chilton, what was the quarrel?” demanded Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓,你哋嗰場爭吵係為了乜嘢?」潘德爾頓追問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓,你們那場爭吵是為了什麼?」潘德爾頓追問。

passages.original: The doctor made an impatient gesture, and got to his feet.
passages.vernacular: 醫生做咗個不耐煩嘅手勢,站起身嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醫生做了個不耐煩的手勢,站起身來。

passages.original: “What was it?
passages.vernacular: 「為了乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「為了什麼?

passages.original: What's any lovers' quarrel after it's over?” he snarled, pacing the room angrily.
passages.vernacular: 情人間嘅爭吵事後又算乜嘢呢?」佢咆哮住,憤怒地喺房間裡踱步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 情人間的爭吵事後又算什麼呢?」他咆哮著,憤怒地在房間裡踱步。

passages.original: “A silly wrangle over the size of the moon or the depth of a river, maybe--it might as well be, so far as its having any real significance compared to the years of misery that follow them!
passages.vernacular: 「或者係為月亮大小或河水深淺嘅一場愚蠢爭論——同隨之而嚟嘅多年痛苦相比,佢哋本就可能係嗰樣,冇任何真正嘅意義!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許是為月亮大小或河水深淺的一場愚蠢爭論——與隨之而來的多年痛苦相比,它們本就可能是那樣,沒有任何真正的意義!

passages.original: Never mind the quarrel!
passages.vernacular: 別提嗰場爭吵喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別提那場爭吵了!

passages.original: So far as I am concerned, I am willing to say there was no quarrel.
passages.vernacular: 就我而言,我愿意講根本冇乜嘢爭吵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就我而言,我愿意說根本沒有什麼爭吵。

passages.original: Pendleton, I must see that child.
passages.vernacular: 潘德爾頓,我必須見嗰個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 潘德爾頓,我必須見那個孩子。

passages.original: It may mean life or death.
passages.vernacular: 呢可能關乎生死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這可能關乎生死。

passages.original: It will mean--I honestly believe--nine chances out of ten that Pollyanna Whittier will walk again!”
passages.vernacular: 我真心相信,呢意味住波莉安娜·惠蒂爾有九成嘅機會能再走路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真心相信,這意味著波莉安娜·惠蒂爾有九成的機會能再走路!」

passages.original: The words were spoken clearly, impressively; and they were spoken just as the one who uttered them had almost reached the open window near John Pendleton's chair.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲話講得清晰而有力;而且就喺講話嘅人幾乎走到約翰·潘德爾頓椅子旁邊嘅敞開窗戶時講出嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些話說得清晰而有力;而且就在說話的人幾乎走到約翰·潘德爾頓椅子旁邊的敞開窗戶時說出的。

passages.original: Thus it happened that very distinctly they reached the ears of a small boy kneeling beneath the window on the ground outside.
passages.vernacular: 于係,呢啲話好清楚地傳到咗一個跪喺窗外地上嘅小男孩耳朵裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 于是,這些話非常清楚地傳到了一個跪在窗外地上的小男孩耳朵裡。

passages.original: Jimmy Bean, at his Saturday morning task of pulling up the first little green weeds of the flowerbeds, sat up with ears and eyes wide open.
passages.vernacular: 吉米·比恩正在做佢星期六上午嘅活兒,拔花壇裡最初冒出嘅小綠草,呢陣佢坐直咗身子,耳朵同眼睛都睜得大大嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米·比恩正在做他星期六上午的活兒,拔花壇裡最初冒出的小綠草,這時他坐直了身子,耳朵和眼睛都睜得大大的。

passages.original: “Walk!
passages.vernacular: 「走路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「走路!

passages.original: Pollyanna!”
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜!」

passages.original: John Pendleton was saying.
passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓說。

passages.original: “What do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「你係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你是什麼意思?」

passages.original: “I mean that from what I can hear and learn--a mile from her bedside--that her case is very much like one that a college friend of mine has just helped.
passages.vernacular: 「我嘅意思係,從我所能聽到同了解到嘅——離佢床邊一英里遠——佢嘅病例同我一位大學朋友啱啱幫助治好嘅一個病例好相似。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我的意思是,從我所能聽到和了解到的——離她床邊一英里遠——她的病例和我一位大學朋友剛剛幫助治好的一個病例非常相似。

passages.original: For years he's been making this sort of thing a special study.
passages.vernacular: 多年嚟佢一直把呢類病作為專門研究。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多年來他一直把這類病作為專門研究。

passages.original: I've kept in touch with him, and studied, too, in a way.
passages.vernacular: 我一直跟佢保持聯繫,自己都有所研究。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一直跟他保持聯繫,自己也有所研究。

passages.original: And from what I hear--but I want to SEE the girl!”
passages.vernacular: 而根據我所聽講嘅——不過我要親眼睇見呢個女孩!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而根據我所聽說的——可是我要親眼看見這個女孩!」

passages.original: John Pendleton came erect in his chair.
