passages.vernacular: 約翰·潘德爾頓喺椅子上坐直咗身子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 約翰·潘德爾頓在椅子上坐直了身子。

passages.original: “You must see her, man!
passages.vernacular: 「你必須見佢,老兄!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你必須見她,老兄!

passages.original: Couldn't you--say, through Dr. Warren?”
passages.vernacular: 你能唔能夠——比如講,通過沃倫醫生?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能不能——比如說,通過沃倫醫生?」

passages.original: The other shook his head.
passages.vernacular: 對方搖搖頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對方搖搖頭。

passages.original: “I'm afraid not.
passages.vernacular: 「恐怕不行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「恐怕不行。

passages.original: Warren has been very decent, though.
passages.vernacular: 不過沃倫一直好得體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過沃倫一直很得體。

passages.original: He told me himself that he suggested consultation with me at the first, but--Miss Harrington said no so decisively that he didn't dare venture it again, even though he knew of my desire to see the child.
passages.vernacular: 佢親口告訴我,佢一開始就建議過同我會診,不過——哈靈頓小姐斷然講不,佢就再都唔敢提喇,盡管佢知道我想見呢個細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他親口告訴我,他一開始就建議過和我會診,可是——哈靈頓小姐斷然說不,他就再也不敢提了,盡管他知道我想見這個孩子。

passages.original: Lately, some of his best patients have come over to me--so of course that ties my hands still more effectually.
passages.vernacular: 最近,佢嘅啲最好嘅病人轉到咗我呢邊——所以呢當然更有效地束縛咗我嘅手腳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最近,他的一些最好的病人轉到了我這邊——所以這當然更有效地束縛了我的手腳。

passages.original: But, Pendleton, I've got to see that child!
passages.vernacular: 不過,潘德爾頓,我一定得見呢個細路!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是,潘德爾頓,我一定得見這個孩子!

passages.original: Think of what it may mean to her--if I do!”
passages.vernacular: 想想如果我見到喇,呢對佢可能意味住乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 想想如果我見到了,這對她可能意味著什麼!」

passages.original: “Yes, and think of what it will mean--if you don't!” retorted Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,都想想如果你見唔到,又意味住乜嘢!」潘德爾頓回嘴道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,也想想如果你見不到,又意味著什麼!」潘德爾頓回嘴道。

passages.original: “But how can I--without a direct request from her aunt?--which I'll never get!”
passages.vernacular: 「不過我點能——冇佢姨媽嘅直接請求呢?——嗰我係永遠等唔到嘅!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是我怎麼能——沒有她姨媽的直接請求呢?——那我是永遠等不到的!」

passages.original: “She must be made to ask you!”
passages.vernacular: 「必須讓佢嚟請你!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「必須讓她來請你!」

passages.original: “How?”
passages.vernacular: 「點讓?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「怎麼讓?」

passages.original: “I don't know.”
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道。」

passages.original: “No, I guess you don't--nor anybody else.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,我想你唔知道——邊個都唔知道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,我想你不知道——誰也不知道。

passages.original: She's too proud and too angry to ask me--after what she said years ago it would mean if she did ask me.
passages.vernacular: 佢太驕傲、太生氣喇,唔會嚟請我——因為多年前佢講過,如果佢嚟請我,嗰意味住乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她太驕傲、太生氣了,不會來請我——因為多年前她說過,如果她來請我,那意味著什麼。

passages.original: But when I think of that child, doomed to lifelong misery, and when I think that maybe in my hands lies a chance of escape, but for that confounded nonsense we call pride and professional etiquette, I--” He did not finish his sentence, but with his hands thrust deep into his pockets, he turned and began to tramp up and down the room again, angrily.
passages.vernacular: 不過一想到嗰個細路,注定要一輩子受苦,一想到或者喺我手裡就有一線逃脫嘅機會,卻因為我哋稱之為自尊同職業禮節嘅嗰種該死嘅廢話而作罷,我——」佢冇講完呢句話,雙手深深插進口袋,轉身又開始憤怒地喺房間裡嚟回踱步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是一想到那個孩子,注定要一輩子受苦,一想到也許在我手裡就有一線逃脫的機會,卻因為我們稱之為自尊和職業禮節的那種該死的廢話而作罷,我——」他沒有說完這句話,雙手深深插進口袋,轉身又開始憤怒地在房間裡來回踱步。

passages.original: “But if she could be made to see--to understand,” urged John Pendleton.
passages.vernacular: 「不過如果能讓佢明白——理解就好喇,」約翰·潘德爾頓催促道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是如果能讓她明白——理解就好了,」約翰·潘德爾頓催促道。

passages.original: “Yes; and who's going to do it?” demanded the doctor, with a savage turn.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊;邊個嚟做呢?」醫生兇狠地轉身質問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊;誰來做呢?」醫生兇狠地轉身質問。

passages.original: “I don't know, I don't know,” groaned the other, miserably.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道,我唔知道,」另一個人痛苦地呻吟道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道,我不知道,」另一個人痛苦地呻吟道。

passages.original: Outside the window Jimmy Bean stirred suddenly.
passages.vernacular: 窗外,吉米·比恩忽然動咗一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗外,吉米·比恩忽然動了一下。

passages.original: Up to now he had scarcely breathed, so intently had he listened to every word.
passages.vernacular: 到此為止佢幾乎冇敢呼吸,如此專注地聽住每一個字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 到此為止他幾乎沒敢呼吸,如此專注地聽著每一個字。

passages.original: “Well, by Jinks, I know!” he whispered, exultingly.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,天呀,我知道喇!」佢興奮地低聲講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,天哪,我知道了!」他興奮地低聲說。

passages.original: “I'M a-goin' ter do it!”
passages.vernacular: 「我去做!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我去做!」

passages.original: And forthwith he rose to his feet, crept stealthily around the corner of the house, and ran with all his might down Pendleton Hill.
passages.vernacular: 佢即刻站起身嚟,躡手躡腳地繞過房子嘅拐角,拼盡全力沿住潘德爾頓山飛奔而下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他立刻站起身來,躡手躡腳地繞過房子的拐角,拼盡全力沿著潘德爾頓山飛奔而下。

chapters.title: Ch. XXX Jimmy Takes the Helm 第三十章:吉米掌舵

passages.original: CH “It's Jimmy Bean.
passages.vernacular: 「係吉米·比恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是吉米·比恩。

passages.original: He wants ter see ye, ma'am,” announced Nancy in the doorway.
passages.vernacular: 佢想見你,太太,」南希喺門口宣布道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他想見你,太太,」南希在門口宣布道。

passages.original: “Me?” rejoined Miss Polly, plainly surprised.
passages.vernacular: 「見我?」波莉小姐回答,顯然好驚訝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「見我?」波莉小姐回答,顯然很驚訝。

passages.original: “Are you sure he did not mean Miss Pollyanna?
passages.vernacular: 「你確定佢唔係想見波莉安娜小姐嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「你確定他不是想見波莉安娜小姐嗎?

passages.original: He may see her a few minutes to-day, if he likes.”
passages.vernacular: 如果佢愿意,今日佢可以見佢幾分鐘。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他愿意,今天他可以見她幾分鐘。」

passages.original: “Yes'm.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,太太。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,太太。

passages.original: I told him.
passages.vernacular: 我告訴過佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴過他了。

passages.original: But he said it was you he wanted.”
passages.vernacular: 不過佢講佢要見嘅係你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是他說他要見的是你。」

passages.original: “Very well, I'll come down.”
passages.vernacular: 「好吧,我下去。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好吧,我下去。」

passages.original: And Miss Polly arose from her chair a little wearily.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐有點疲倦地從椅子上站咗起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐有點疲倦地從椅子上站了起來。

passages.original: In the sitting room she found waiting for her a round-eyed, flushed-faced boy, who began to speak at once.
passages.vernacular: 喺起居室裡,佢睇到一個睜大眼睛、滿臉通紅嘅男孩喺等佢,佢即刻開口講話喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在起居室裡,她看到一個睜大眼睛、滿臉通紅的男孩在等她,他立刻開口說話了。

passages.original: “Ma'am, I s'pose it's dreadful--what I'm doin', an' what I'm sayin'; but I can't help it.
passages.vernacular: 「太太,我想我做嘅事、講嘅話都好糟糕;不過我冇辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「太太,我想我做的事、說的話都很糟糕;可是我沒辦法。

passages.original: It's for Pollyanna, and I'd walk over hot coals for her, or face you, or--or anythin' like that, any time.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係為了波莉安娜,為了佢,我可以走過燒紅嘅煤炭,或者面對你,或者——或者隨時做任何嗰樣嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是為了波莉安娜,為了她,我可以走過燒紅的煤炭,或者面對你,或者——或者隨時做任何那樣的事。

passages.original: An' I think you would, too, if you thought there was a chance for her ter walk again.
passages.vernacular: 我想你都會嘅,要係你知道有機會讓佢再走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想你也會的,要是你知道有機會讓她再走路。

passages.original: An' so that's why I come ter tell ye that as long as it's only pride an' et--et-somethin' that's keepin' Pollyanna from walkin', why I knew you WOULD ask Dr. Chilton here if you understood--”
passages.vernacular: 所以我嚟告訴你,只要係自尊啦、仲有——仲有乜嘢嘅喺阻礙波莉安娜走路,我就知道你要係明白喇,係會請奇爾頓醫生到呢兒嚟嘅——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我來告訴你,只要是自尊啦、還有——還有什麼的在阻礙波莉安娜走路,我就知道你要是明白了,是會請奇爾頓醫生到這兒來的——」

passages.original: “Wh-at?” interrupted Miss Polly, the look of stupefaction on her face changing to one of angry indignation.
passages.vernacular: 「什——麼?」波莉小姐打斷道,臉上嘅驚愕轉成咗憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「什——麼?」波莉小姐打斷道,臉上的驚愕轉成了憤怒。

passages.original: Jimmy sighed despairingly.
passages.vernacular: 吉米絕望地嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米絕望地嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “There, I didn't mean ter make ye mad.
passages.vernacular: 「糟喇,我唔係想惹你生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「糟了,我不是想惹你生氣。

passages.original: That's why I begun by tellin' ye about her walkin' again.
passages.vernacular: 所以我才一開始就講佢能再走路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我才一開始就說她能再走路。

passages.original: I thought you'd listen ter that.”
passages.vernacular: 我以為你會聽呢個嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以為你會聽這個的。」

passages.original: “Jimmy, what are you talking about?”
passages.vernacular: 「吉米,你喺講乜嘢?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉米,你在說什麼?」

passages.original: Jimmy sighed again.
passages.vernacular: 吉米又嘆咗口氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米又嘆了口氣。

passages.original: “That's what I'm tryin' ter tell ye.”
passages.vernacular: 「呢正是我想告訴你嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「這正是我想告訴你的。」

passages.original: “Well, then tell me.
passages.vernacular: 「咁就告訴我吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「那麼就告訴我吧。

passages.original: But begin at the beginning, and be sure I understand each thing as you go.
passages.vernacular: 但要從頭講起,而且要讓我聽明白你講嘅每一件事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但要從頭說起,而且要讓我聽明白你說的每一件事。

passages.original: Don't plunge into the middle of it as you did before--and mix everything all up!”
passages.vernacular: 別像上次嗰樣一頭扎到中間——把一切都攪成一團!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別像上次那樣一頭扎到中間——把一切都攪成一團!」

passages.original: Jimmy wet his lips determinedly.
passages.vernacular: 吉米下定決心地舔咗舔嘴唇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米下定決心地舔了舔嘴唇。

passages.original: “Well, ter begin with, Dr. Chilton come ter see Mr. Pendleton, an' they talked in the library.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,先講,奇爾頓醫生來睇潘德爾頓先生,佢哋喺書房裡講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,先說,奇爾頓醫生來看潘德爾頓先生,他們在書房裡說話。

passages.original: Do you understand that?”
passages.vernacular: 你明白嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你明白嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes, Jimmy.”
passages.vernacular: 「明白,吉米。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明白,吉米。」

passages.original: Miss Polly's voice was rather faint.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅聲音相當微弱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的聲音相當微弱。

passages.original: “Well, the window was open, and I was weedin' the flower-bed under it; an' I heard 'em talk.”
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,窗子開住,我正在窗下嘅花壇裡拔草;我聽見佢哋講話喇。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,窗子開著,我正在窗下的花壇裡拔草;我聽見他們說話了。」

passages.original: “Oh, Jimmy!
passages.vernacular: 「哦,吉米!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,吉米!

passages.original: LISTENING?”
passages.vernacular: 偷聽?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偷聽?」

passages.original: “'Twa'n't about me, an' 'twa'n't sneak listenin',” bridled Jimmy.
passages.vernacular: 「唔係關于我嘅,都唔係偷偷摸摸地聽,」吉米昂住頭講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「不是關于我的,也不是偷偷摸摸地聽,」吉米昂著頭說。

passages.original: “And I'm glad I listened.
passages.vernacular: 「而且我好高興我聽喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「而且我很高興我聽了。

passages.original: You will be when I tell ye.
passages.vernacular: 等我告訴你,你都會高興嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等我告訴你,你也會高興的。

passages.original: Why, it may make Pollyanna--walk!”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,呢或者能讓波莉安娜——走路!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,這也許能讓波莉安娜——走路!」

passages.original: “Jimmy, what do you mean?”
passages.vernacular: 「吉米,你係乜嘢意思?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「吉米,你是什麼意思?」

passages.original: Miss Polly was leaning forward eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐急切地探身向前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐急切地探身向前。

passages.original: “There, I told ye so,” nodded Jimmy, contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 「瞧,我就知道,」吉米滿意地點點頭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「瞧,我就知道,」吉米滿意地點點頭。

passages.original: “Well, Dr. Chilton knows some doctor somewhere that can cure Pollyanna, he thinks--make her walk, ye know; but he can't tell sure till he SEES her.
passages.vernacular: 「嗯,奇爾頓醫生認識某個地方嘅某個醫生,佢認為能治好波莉安娜——讓佢走路,你知道;不過佢得親眼睇見佢才能確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「嗯,奇爾頓醫生認識某個地方的某個醫生,他認為能治好波莉安娜——讓她走路,你知道;不過他得親眼看見她才能確定。

passages.original: And he wants ter see her somethin' awful, but he told Mr. Pendleton that you wouldn't let him.”
passages.vernacular: 佢好想見佢,不過佢對潘德爾頓先生講,你唔肯讓佢見。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他非常想見她,可是他對潘德爾頓先生說,你不肯讓他見。」

passages.original: Miss Polly's face turned very red.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐嘅臉漲得通紅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐的臉漲得通紅。

passages.original: “But, Jimmy, I--I can't--I couldn't!
passages.vernacular: 「不過,吉米,我——我唔能夠——我冇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,吉米,我——我不能——我沒有!

passages.original: That is, I didn't know!”
passages.vernacular: 都就係講,我唔知道!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也就是說,我不知道!」

passages.original: Miss Polly was twisting her fingers together helplessly.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐無助地絞著手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐無助地絞著手指。

passages.original: “Yes, an' that's what I come ter tell ye, so you WOULD know,” asserted Jimmy, eagerly.
passages.vernacular: 「係啊,所以我才嚟告訴你,讓你知道,」吉米急切地斷言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是啊,所以我才來告訴你,讓你知道,」吉米急切地斷言。

passages.original: “They said that for some reason--I didn't rightly catch what--you wouldn't let Dr. Chilton come, an' you told Dr. Warren so; an' Dr. Chilton couldn't come himself, without you asked him, on account of pride an' professional et--et--well, et-somethin anyway.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋講,唔知點解原因——我冇聽清楚——你唔肯讓奇爾頓醫生來,你仲咁跟沃倫醫生講喇;而奇爾頓醫生自己唔能夠嚟,除非你請佢,因為自尊同職業上嘅乜嘢——乜嘢——嗯,反正是乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們說,不知為什麼原因——我沒聽清楚——你不肯讓奇爾頓醫生來,你還這麼跟沃倫醫生說了;而奇爾頓醫生自己不能來,除非你請他,因為自尊和職業上的什麼——什麼——嗯,反正是什麼。

passages.original: An' they was wishin' somebody could make you understand, only they didn't know who could; an' I was outside the winder, an' I says ter myself right away, 'By Jinks, I'll do it!'
passages.vernacular: 佢哋希望有邊個能讓你明白,只係唔知道邊個能;我就喺窗外,我即刻對自己講:『天呀,我去做!』
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們希望有誰能讓你明白,只是不知道誰能;我就在窗外,我馬上對自己說:『天哪,我去做!』

passages.original: An' I come--an' have I made ye understand?”
passages.vernacular: 我就嚟喇——我讓你明白咗嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我就來了——我讓你明白了嗎?」

passages.original: “Yes; but, Jimmy, about that doctor,” implored Miss Polly, feverishly.
passages.vernacular: 「明白喇;不過,吉米,嗰位醫生嘅事呢?」波莉小姐狂熱地懇求道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「明白了;可是,吉米,那位醫生的事呢?」波莉小姐狂熱地懇求道。

passages.original: “Who was he?
passages.vernacular: 「佢係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他是誰?

passages.original: What did he do?
passages.vernacular: 佢做咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他做了什麼?

passages.original: Are they SURE he could make Pollyanna walk?”
passages.vernacular: 佢哋確定佢能讓波莉安娜走路嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們確定他能讓波莉安娜走路嗎?」

passages.original: “I don't know who he was.
passages.vernacular: 「我唔知道佢係邊個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不知道他是誰。

passages.original: They didn't say.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋冇講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們沒說。

passages.original: Dr. Chilton knows him, an' he's just cured somebody just like her, Dr. Chilton thinks.
passages.vernacular: 奇爾頓醫生認識佢,奇爾頓醫生認為佢啱啱治好咗一個同佢一模一樣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇爾頓醫生認識他,奇爾頓醫生認為他剛剛治好了一個和她一模一樣的人。

passages.original: Anyhow, they didn't seem ter be doin' no worryin' about HIM.
passages.vernacular: 反正佢哋似乎并不擔心佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 反正他們似乎并不擔心他。

passages.original: 'Twas YOU they was worryin' about, 'cause you wouldn't let Dr. Chilton see her.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋擔心嘅係你,因為你唔肯讓奇爾頓醫生見佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們擔心的是你,因為你不肯讓奇爾頓醫生見她。

passages.original: An' say--you will let him come, won't you?--now you understand?”
passages.vernacular: 仲有,你會讓佢嚟嘅,係唔係?——而家你明白喇?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有,你會讓他來的,是不是?——現在你明白了?」

passages.original: Miss Polly turned her head from side to side.
passages.vernacular: 波莉小姐把頭轉嚟轉去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉小姐把頭轉來轉去。

passages.original: Her breath was coming in little uneven, rapid gasps.
passages.vernacular: 佢呼吸短促、不均勻,急促地喘住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她呼吸短促、不均勻,急促地喘著。

passages.original: Jimmy, watching her with anxious eyes, thought she was going to cry.
passages.vernacular: 吉米焦急地注視住佢,以為佢要哭喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吉米焦急地注視著她,以為她要哭了。

passages.original: But she did not cry.
passages.vernacular: 不過佢冇哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可是她沒有哭。

passages.original: After a minute she said brokenly:
passages.vernacular: 過咗一會兒,佢斷斷續續地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過了一會兒,她斷斷續續地說:

passages.original: “Yes--I'll let--Dr. Chilton--see her.
passages.vernacular: 「好——我會讓——奇爾頓醫生——嚟睇佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好——我會讓——奇爾頓醫生——來看她。

passages.original: Now run home, Jimmy--quick!
passages.vernacular: 而家快回家,吉米——快!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在快回家,吉米——快!

passages.original: I've got to speak to Dr. Warren.
passages.vernacular: 我得去跟沃倫醫生講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得去跟沃倫醫生說。

passages.original: He's up-stairs now.
passages.vernacular: 佢而家喺樓上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他現在在樓上。

passages.original: I saw him drive in a few minutes ago.”
passages.vernacular: 我幾分鐘前睇見佢駕車進嚟。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我幾分鐘前看見他駕車進來。」

passages.original: A little later Dr. Warren was surprised to meet an agitated, flushed-faced Miss Polly in the hall.
passages.vernacular: 稍後,沃倫醫生喺走廊裡遇到一位激動、滿臉通紅嘅波莉小姐,感到好意外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍後,沃倫醫生在走廊裡遇到一位激動、滿臉通紅的波莉小姐,感到很意外。

passages.original: He was still more surprised to hear the lady say, a little breathlessly:
passages.vernacular: 聽到呢位女士有點氣喘地講話,佢更食驚喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到這位女士有點氣喘地說話,他更吃驚了:

passages.original: “Dr. Warren, you asked me once to allow Dr. Chilton to be called in consultation, and--I refused.
passages.vernacular: 「沃倫醫生,你曾經請求我允許請奇爾頓醫生來會診,而我——拒絕喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沃倫醫生,你曾經請求我允許請奇爾頓醫生來會診,而我——拒絕了。

passages.original: Since then I have reconsidered.
passages.vernacular: 從嗰以後我重新考慮喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從那以後我重新考慮了。

passages.original: I very much desire that you SHOULD call in Dr. Chilton.
passages.vernacular: 我好希望你去請奇爾頓醫生來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常希望你去請奇爾頓醫生來。

passages.original: Will you not ask him at once--please?
passages.vernacular: 你能唔能夠即刻去請佢——拜托喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能不能馬上去請他——拜托了?

passages.original: Thank you.”
passages.vernacular: 謝謝你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝你。」

chapters.title: Ch. XXXI A New Uncle 第三十一章:新姨丈

passages.original: CH The next time Dr. Warren entered the chamber where Pollyanna lay watching the dancing shimmer of color on the ceiling, a tall, broad-shouldered man followed close behind him.
passages.vernacular: 下一次沃倫醫生走進波莉安娜躺住、望住天花板上跳動閃爍嘅色彩嘅房間時,一個高個子、寬肩膀嘅男人緊隨其後。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 下一次沃倫醫生走進波莉安娜躺著、望著天花板上跳動閃爍的色彩的房間時,一個高個子、寬肩膀的男人緊隨其後。

passages.original: “Dr. Chilton!--oh, Dr. Chilton, how glad I am to see YOU!” cried Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 「奇爾頓醫生!——哦,奇爾頓醫生,睇到你我多高興啊!」波莉安娜喊道。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「奇爾頓醫生!——哦,奇爾頓醫生,看到你我多高興啊!」波莉安娜喊道。

passages.original: And at the joyous rapture of the voice, more than one pair of eyes in the room brimmed hot with sudden tears.
passages.vernacular: 聽到嗰聲音裡歡喜嘅狂喜,屋裡不止一雙眼睛突然涌上熱淚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽到那聲音裡歡喜的狂喜,屋裡不止一雙眼睛突然涌上熱淚。

passages.original: “But, of course, if Aunt Polly doesn't want--”
passages.vernacular: 「不過,當然,如果波莉姨媽唔想要——」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「可是,當然,如果波莉姨媽不想要——」

passages.original: “It is all right, my dear; don't worry,” soothed Miss Polly, agitatedly, hurrying forward.
passages.vernacular: 「冇關係,親愛嘅,別擔心,」波莉小姐激動地安慰道,急忙走上前嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「沒關係,親愛的,別擔心,」波莉小姐激動地安慰道,急忙走上前來。

passages.original: “I have told Dr. Chilton that--that I want him to look you over--with Dr. Warren, this morning.”
passages.vernacular: 「我已經對奇爾頓醫生講喇——講我希望佢今日上午同沃倫醫生一起畀你檢查一下。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我已經對奇爾頓醫生說了——說我希望他今天上午和沃倫醫生一起給你檢查一下。」

passages.original: “Oh, then you asked him to come,” murmured Pollyanna, contentedly.
passages.vernacular: 「哦,咁講係你請佢嚟嘅,」波莉安娜滿足地喃喃講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「哦,這麼說是你請他來的,」波莉安娜滿足地喃喃說。

passages.original: “Yes, dear, I asked him.
passages.vernacular: 「係嘅,親愛嘅,係我請嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「是的,親愛的,是我請的。

passages.original: That is--” But it was too late.
passages.vernacular: 都就係講——」不過已經太遲喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也就是說——」可是已經太遲了。

passages.original: The adoring happiness that had leaped to Dr. Chilton's eyes was unmistakable and Miss Polly had seen it.
passages.vernacular: 奇爾頓醫生眼裡一下子迸發出嚟嘅愛慕嘅幸福,明明白白,波莉小姐睇到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇爾頓醫生眼裡一下子迸發出來的愛慕的幸福,明明白白,波莉小姐看到了。

passages.original: With very pink cheeks she turned and left the room hurriedly.
passages.vernacular: 佢兩頰緋紅,轉身匆匆離開咗房間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她兩頰緋紅,轉身匆匆離開了房間。

passages.original: Over in the window the nurse and Dr. Warren were talking earnestly.
passages.vernacular: 窗邊,護士同沃倫醫生正在認真交談。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 窗邊,護士和沃倫醫生正在認真交談。

passages.original: Dr. Chilton held out both his hands to Pollyanna.
passages.vernacular: 奇爾頓醫生向波莉安娜伸出雙手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奇爾頓醫生向波莉安娜伸出雙手。

passages.original: “Little girl, I'm thinking that one of the very gladdest jobs you ever did has been done to-day,” he said in a voice shaken with emotion.
passages.vernacular: 「小姑娘,我想,你做過嘅最高興嘅事之一,今日已經做成喇,」佢用激動顫抖嘅聲音講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「小姑娘,我想,你做過的最高興的事之一,今天已經做成了,」他用激動顫抖的聲音說。

passages.original: At twilight a wonderfully tremulous, wonderfully different Aunt Polly crept to Pollyanna's bedside.
passages.vernacular: 暮色降臨時,一個奇妙地顫抖住、奇妙地變咗樣嘅波莉姨媽,悄悄嚟到波莉安娜嘅床邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暮色降臨時,一個奇妙地顫抖著、奇妙地變了樣的波莉姨媽,悄悄來到波莉安娜的床邊。

passages.original: The nurse was at supper.
passages.vernacular: 護士喺食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 護士在吃晚飯。

passages.original: They had the room to themselves.
passages.vernacular: 房間裡只剩佢哋兩個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 房間裡只剩她們兩個。

passages.original: “Pollyanna, dear, I'm going to tell you--the very first one of all.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,親愛嘅,我要告訴你——你係第一個知道嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,親愛的,我要告訴你——你是第一個知道的。

passages.original: Some day I'm going to give Dr. Chilton to you for your--uncle.
passages.vernacular: 總有一天,我要把奇爾頓醫生送畀你,做你嘅——姨父。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總有一天,我要把奇爾頓醫生送給你,做你的——姨父。

passages.original: And it's you that have done it all.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切都係你做成嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切都是你做成的。

passages.original: Oh, Pollyanna, I'm so--happy!
passages.vernacular: 哦,波莉安娜,我好——幸福!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,波莉安娜,我好——幸福!

passages.original: And so--glad!--darling!”
passages.vernacular: 好——高興!——寶貝!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好——高興!——寶貝!」

passages.original: Pollyanna began to clap her hands; but even as she brought her small palms together the first time, she stopped, and held them suspended.
passages.vernacular: 波莉安娜開始拍手;不過就喺佢嘅小手掌第一次合攏嘅時候,佢停住喇,把手懸喺半空。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉安娜開始拍手;可是就在她的小手掌第一次合攏的時候,她停住了,把手懸在半空。

passages.original: “Aunt Polly, Aunt Polly, WERE you the woman's hand and heart he wanted so long ago?
passages.vernacular: 「波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,你係佢好久以前想要嘅嗰個女人嘅手同心嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉姨媽,波莉姨媽,你是他很久以前想要的那個女人的手和心嗎?

passages.original: You were--I know you were!
passages.vernacular: 你係——我知道你係!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是——我知道你是!

passages.original: And that's what he meant by saying I'd done the gladdest job of all--to-day.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係佢講我今日做咗最高興嘅事嘅意思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是他說我今天做了最高興的事的意思。

passages.original: I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 我太高興喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我太高興了!

passages.original: Why, Aunt Polly, I don't know but I'm so glad that I don't mind--even my legs, now!”
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,波莉姨媽,我真係高興極喇,而家連我嘅腿都不在乎喇!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,波莉姨媽,我真是高興極了,現在連我的腿都不在乎了!」

passages.original: Aunt Polly swallowed a sob.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽咽下一聲啜泣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽咽下一聲啜泣。

passages.original: “Perhaps, some day, dear--” But Aunt Polly did not finish.
passages.vernacular: 「或者,總有一天,親愛嘅——」不過波莉姨媽冇講完。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「也許,總有一天,親愛的——」可是波莉姨媽沒有說完。

passages.original: Aunt Polly did not dare to tell, yet, the great hope that Dr. Chilton had put into her heart.
passages.vernacular: 波莉姨媽仲唔敢講出奇爾頓醫生放進佢心裡嘅嗰個巨大嘅希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波莉姨媽還不敢說出奇爾頓醫生放進她心裡的那個巨大的希望。

passages.original: But she did say this--and surely this was quite wonderful enough--to Pollyanna's mind:
passages.vernacular: 不過佢講咗呢個——而呢喺波莉安娜睇來,當然已經足夠奇妙喇:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過她說了這個——而這在波莉安娜看來,當然已經足夠奇妙了:

passages.original: “Pollyanna, next week you're going to take a journey.
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜,下個星期你要去旅行。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜,下個星期你要去旅行。

passages.original: On a nice comfortable little bed you're going to be carried in cars and carriages to a great doctor who has a big house many miles from here made on purpose for just such people as you are.
passages.vernacular: 你將躺喺一張舒適嘅小床上,乘火車同馬車,被送到一位大醫生嗰度,佢喺離呢度好多英里嘅地方有一座大房子,專門為像你咁樣嘅人建造嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你將躺在一張舒適的小床上,乘火車和馬車,被送到一位大醫生那裡,他在離這裡很多英里的地方有一座大房子,專門為像你這樣的人建造的。

passages.original: He's a dear friend of Dr. Chilton's, and we're going to see what he can do for you!”
passages.vernacular: 佢係奇爾頓醫生嘅好朋友,我哋要睇睇佢能為你做些乜嘢!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是奇爾頓醫生的好朋友,我們要看看他能為你做些什麼!」

chapters.title: Ch. XXXII A Letter from Pollyanna 第三十二章:波麗安娜的來信

passages.original: CH “Dear Aunt Polly and Uncle Tom:--Oh, I can--I can--I CAN walk!
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅波莉姨媽同湯姆姨父:——哦,我能——我能——我能走路喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的波莉姨媽和湯姆姨父:——哦,我能——我能——我能走路了!

passages.original: I did to-day all the way from my bed to the window!
passages.vernacular: 今日我從床邊一路走到咗窗邊!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 今天我從床邊一路走到了窗邊!

passages.original: It was six steps.
passages.vernacular: 一共六步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一共六步。

passages.original: My, how good it was to be on legs again!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,重新用腿站住真好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,重新用腿站著真好!

passages.original: “All the doctors stood around and smiled, and all the nurses stood beside of them and cried.
passages.vernacular: 「所有嘅醫生站喺周圍微笑,所有嘅護士站喺佢哋旁邊哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「所有的醫生站在周圍微笑,所有的護士站在他們旁邊哭。

passages.original: A lady in the next ward who walked last week first, peeked into the door, and another one who hopes she can walk next month, was invited in to the party, and she laid on my nurse's bed and clapped her hands.
passages.vernacular: 隔壁病房一位上星期第一個學會走路嘅女士,從門口探頭睇,另一位希望下個月能走路嘅女士,被請進嚟參加聚會,佢躺喺我護士嘅床上拍手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隔壁病房一位上星期第一個學會走路的女士,從門口探頭看,另一位希望下個月能走路的女士,被請進來參加聚會,她躺在我護士的床上拍手。

passages.original: Even Black Tilly who washes the floor, looked through the piazza window and called me 'Honey, child' when she wasn't crying too much to call me anything.
passages.vernacular: 連洗地板嘅黑人蒂莉都從走廊嘅窗戶往裡睇,佢哭得太厲害叫不出別嘅話時,就叫我『寶貝細路』。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 連洗地板的黑人蒂莉也從走廊的窗戶往裡看,她哭得太厲害叫不出別的話時,就叫我『寶貝孩子』。

passages.original: “I don't see why they cried.
passages.vernacular: 「我不明白佢哋點解哭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「我不明白他們為什麼哭。

passages.original: I wanted to sing and shout and yell!
passages.vernacular: 我只想唱歌、喊叫、大叫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我只想唱歌、喊叫、大叫!

passages.original: Oh--oh--oh! just think, I can walk--walk--WALK!
passages.vernacular: 哦——哦——哦!你想想,我能走路——走路——走路喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦——哦——哦!你想想,我能走路——走路——走路了!

passages.original: Now I don't mind being here almost ten months, and I didn't miss the wedding, anyhow.
passages.vernacular: 而家我不介意喺呢度待咗快十個月喇,而且不管點樣我冇錯過婚禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我不介意在這裡待了快十個月了,而且不管怎樣我沒有錯過婚禮。

passages.original: Wasn't that just like you, Aunt Polly, to come on here and get married right beside my bed, so I could see you.
passages.vernacular: 呢不正像你嗎,波莉姨媽,特地跑到呢兒嚟,就喺我嘅床邊結婚,好讓我睇見你哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不正像你嗎,波莉姨媽,特地跑到這兒來,就在我的床邊結婚,好讓我看見你們。

passages.original: You always do think of the gladdest things!
passages.vernacular: 你總是想到最讓人高興嘅事!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你總是想到最讓人高興的事!

passages.original: “Pretty soon, they say, I shall go home.
passages.vernacular: 「佢哋講,好快我就能回家喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「他們說,很快我就能回家了。

passages.original: I wish I could walk all the way there.
passages.vernacular: 我真希望能一路走回去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我真希望能一路走回去。

passages.original: I do.
passages.vernacular: 真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真的。

passages.original: I don't think I shall ever want to ride anywhere any more.
passages.vernacular: 我想我以後再都唔想坐車去任何地方喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我以後再也不想坐車去任何地方了。

passages.original: It will be so good just to walk.
passages.vernacular: 光係走路就太好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 光是走路就太好了。

passages.original: Oh, I'm so glad!
passages.vernacular: 哦,我太高興喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哦,我太高興了!

passages.original: I'm glad for everything.
passages.vernacular: 我為一切高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為一切高興。

passages.original: Why, I'm glad now I lost my legs for a while, for you never, never know how perfectly lovely legs are till you haven't got them--that go, I mean.
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,我而家甚至高興我曾有一陣子失去咗我嘅腿,因為你永遠永遠唔會知道腿有幾咁可愛,除非你冇佢哋——能走嘅,我係講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,我現在甚至高興我曾有一陣子失去了我的腿,因為你永遠永遠不會知道腿有多麼可愛,除非你沒有它們——能走的,我是說。

passages.original: I'm going to walk eight steps to-morrow.
passages.vernacular: 聽日我要走八步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 明天我要走八步。

passages.original: “With heaps of love to everybody,
passages.vernacular: 「送畀大家滿滿嘅愛,
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「送給大家滿滿的愛,

passages.original: “POLLYANNA.”
passages.vernacular: 「波莉安娜。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「波莉安娜。」
